title: fix(mcp): prefer structured tool results
body:
Modern MCP servers can return the required `content`, and the newer but optional [`structuredContent`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#structured-content).

The big reason that `structuredContent` was added to the spec is that, if the tool declares an `outputSchema`,
`structuredContent` has to conform to it. For backward compatibility, the MCP spec recommends also returning the structured result serialized in a `TextContent` block, and many MCP servers indeed do that.

Before this PR, `fx` sent both representations to the model. For MCPs that contain both forms, this duplicates the tool response, using more input tokens than it needed.

This PR makes it so that if the MCP server returned both forms, it'll prefer keeping only `structuredContent`. Truncation is then applied only to the selected representation.

For reference, that's also what Codex does ([source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8b8ee28a9b0df8188fec8d4e3855a7b3af3ed8a2/codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs#L2270-L2291)), and OpenCode's upcoming code-mode does that too ([source](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b578b7261fc9ec4917fe272df5cc4bd8a056cd5d/packages/opencode/src/tool/code-mode.ts#L109-L109)).

## Verification

- Unit and runtime tests cover:
  - preferring non-null `structuredContent`
  - falling back when it is absent or null
  - excluding the duplicate `content` representation
  - Updates `mcp-http.test.ts` to assert the `structuredContent` preference

title: Bug: Codex OAuth login reaches callback but token exchange returns HTTP 400 on macOS
body:
### Issue details

## Summary

`fx login codex` completes the OpenAI account and workspace consent flow and receives the authorization callback on localhost, but the callback page displays `Authorization failed` and fx exits with a generic error. No credential is saved.

## Environment

- fx: 0.0.7
- build revision: `cef08aa0f178`
- OS: macOS 15.7.7, arm64
- ChatGPT workspace: personal
- official Codex CLI on the same machine: 0.152.0, already logged in using ChatGPT
- standard HTTP/HTTPS proxy environment variables and macOS system proxy are configured

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `fx login codex`.
2. Select the ChatGPT account and personal workspace.
3. Continue from the consent page.
4. Observe the localhost callback and CLI output.

## Expected behavior

The callback succeeds and fx saves a refreshable Codex credential.

## Actual behavior

The browser reaches `http://localhost:1455/auth/callback`, then displays:

```
Authorization failed
Return to fx for details.
```

The CLI only reports:

```
fx login: failed to sign in with Codex
```

`fx status --json` remains `"auth":"missing"` and `"auth_refreshable":false`.

## Diagnostic result

I built the exact 0.0.7 revision with temporary, local-only instrumentation around `OAuthHttpOperation.run`.

I also called Zig's `client.initDefaultProxies(...)` before the request. The diagnostic output was:

```
fx oauth diagnostic: proxy http=true https=true
fx oauth diagnostic: response status=400
fx login: failed to sign in with Codex
```

The result was reproduced on three fresh OAuth attempts. This confirms that:

- the localhost callback listener receives the authorization code;
- the patched client recognizes both proxy settings;
- the OpenAI token endpoint responds, but rejects the exchange with HTTP 400;
- fx currently collapses the underlying rejection to `ChatGptOAuthRequestFailed`, so the actionable OAuth error is not visible.

The instrumentation logged only proxy presence and status code, not authorization codes, tokens, response bodies, or proxy values.

## Possible next diagnostic

It may help to expose a sanitized OAuth error code/description for rejected token responses. I have not identified the protocol-level cause of the 400 and do not want to claim that the proxy is the root cause.

### Trace

_No response_

### Sensitive information

- [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

title: Route Codex requests through macOS HTTPS proxies
body:
## Summary

- route affected Codex HTTPS requests through the system `curl` on macOS when `HTTPS_PROXY` or `ALL_PROXY` is configured
- cover the OAuth token exchange, Codex model catalog, and Codex Responses request paths
- stream Codex SSE events incrementally through the existing reducer
- keep credentials and request payloads out of process arguments by passing a bounded curl config through stdin
- preserve the existing `std.http` transport on other platforms and when no HTTPS proxy is configured

Fixes #611.

## Root cause

With Zig 0.16, `std.http.Client` establishes an HTTP CONNECT tunnel through the configured proxy but the resulting proxied connection is not wrapped in TLS for the HTTPS target. The proxy therefore receives a plaintext HTTP request on the target's port 443 and returns HTTP 400 (`The plain HTTP request was sent to HTTPS port`).

The browser authorization succeeds because it uses a working proxy stack, but fx then fails during the token exchange. The same transport issue also affects the authenticated model catalog and Responses requests after login.

## Implementation notes

The fallback is intentionally limited to macOS HTTPS requests with an active HTTPS or ALL proxy. macOS provides `/usr/bin/curl`, while unaffected requests continue to use the native Zig transport. Response sizes, stderr, timeouts, and cancellation remain bounded. The curl config is escaped and sent over stdin so bearer tokens and JSON bodies do not appear in `argv`.

Streaming responses include curl's HTTP headers so the transport can skip the proxy CONNECT response, preserve final HTTP status mapping, and pass the SSE body to the existing reducer as bytes arrive. The request stops at the protocol's completion event instead of waiting for the proxy connection to close.

## Verification

- `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe`
- focused transport tests: 11 passed
- fresh repository binary: `./zig-out/bin/fx status --json` loaded the Codex subscription and model catalog through the configured proxy
- fresh repository binary: a two-turn request ran `pwd` through the terminal tool and returned `STREAM_FIX_OK` with exit code 0 using `gpt-5.6-sol`
- initial full `zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe` run: 8312 passed, 2 skipped, 1 failed

The one full-suite failure is `core.agent.runtime.assistant_stream.test.streamed presentation preserves ANSI OSC 8 code fence and table spans`. It is unrelated to the gateway changes and was also reproduced before this PR's changes on the released source revision. After the streaming follow-up, the ReleaseSafe build, focused tests, and live multi-turn verification all passed again.

## Summary

MCP startup and reload coupled unrelated servers, and discovery, authentication, menus, and SDK calls did not share consistent contracts. Rebuild ownership around independent server connections and use MCP v1 by default while retaining the existing CLI, slash commands, menus, and SDK integration.

- Connect servers independently with per-server startup limits. Activate optional servers on demand for headless calls, reuse healthy connections on reload, and retain the previous configuration when a required replacement fails.

- Print a manual authorization URL and continue waiting when a headless CLI cannot launch a browser.
- Load bounded complete schemas through capability search, retain explicit selection, and let servers validate tool argument semantics. Bind calls to their advertised server, schema, and authority without replaying uncertain calls.
- Preserve typed images, structured results, cancellation, and saved history across native and SDK execution. Match the official MCP TypeScript SDK v1 call signature and accept normal MCP descriptions within the existing metadata and frame budgets.
- Keep saved MCP images through conversation replay, legacy import, compaction, and recovery copying. Store image bytes in the existing artifact store and keep references in conversation events.
- Run MCP menu tests without a live Gateway key, including HTTP add/remove, bulk project trust/reset, and resource/prompt insertion without submission.

- Measure PGSO command duration at process completion while retaining timeout, cancellation, and bounded output handling. Exclude supervisor polling and log-drain delay from heavy-workload comparisons.

## Validation

Earlier fresh Linux builds in Vercel Sandbox exercised Plain, Datadog, Context7, is-agentic, and chrome-devtools through real authentication, tool calls, reload, process restart, and logout. Headless and ACP runs called all five servers. The SDK used the official MCP client with all five servers; a browser SDK run used a real MCP-backed host client. Screenshot results and cancellation were exercised end to end.

Focused native, TUI/CLI, authentication, transport, ACP, SDK native/Wasm, and browser checks passed locally. The pinned conformance runner passed its modern and MCP v1 suites. The merged source passed MCP discovery, complete skill loading, image-resume, cancellation, ACP, TUI and SDK checks. Full CI passed on Linux and macOS for both x86_64 and arm64 at `a748a2f4ef7a36691580fe38fd2dd0d693b85884`. title: Bug: Long-running tasks exhaust tens of GiB and trigger OOM kills
body:
### Issue details

**During actual development work, a single task running for several hours consumed tens of GiB, triggered the Linux OOM killer, and left my working environment unusable. I consider this a severe stability bug and ask that it be prioritized.** This was a real task, not a stress test.

### Environment and incident

- Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, x86_64; approximately 64 GB host RAM, 40 GB allocated to the Ubuntu environment, and 10 GiB swap.
- On 2026-09-05, fx alone reached approximately **35.3 GiB anonymous RSS plus 8.1 GiB swap**. Free swap reached zero and the kernel killed fx. Other services subsequently failed.
- The recovered turn contained 1,171 tool steps and 3,735 distinct tool calls, but its complete recovery snapshot was only about 13.2 MiB.

The original incident occurred on my fork. I then independently reproduced the memory-growth defect on **unmodified upstream `478960a8ab9315507e0a40d4434df71898fadf13`**.

### Deterministic upstream reproduction

Build with Zig 0.16.0 using `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe -j2`. Run the built `./zig-out/bin/fx ask --json --yolo` against a local Gateway SSE fixture, in an isolated HOME/workspace. Have the fixture request one `read_file` per step with a unique call ID, changing the roughly 1 KiB file before every read, and supply a final response after 1,000 steps. No paid model is needed.

The test capped fx address space at **2 GiB**, imposed a **600-second timeout**, disabled core dumps, and sampled only fx RSS every 100 ms. The fixture discarded request bodies.

| Model request | fx RSS |
| --- | ---: |
| 100 | 81.06 MiB |
| 200 | 268.11 MiB |
| 400 | 1,002.24 MiB |
| 480 | 1,425.74 MiB |

After **490 successful reads**, fx returned `OutOfMemory` and exited with code 1. Peak sampled RSS was **1,483.49 MiB**, while the retained execution record was only **1.37 MiB**, including about **0.50 MiB of tool output**. This bounded reproduction failed through the allocator; the real incident above triggered the OS OOM killer.

### Confirmed allocation path

- [The turn arena](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/478960a8ab9315507e0a40d4434df71898fadf13/src/core/agent/runtime/orchestrator.zig#L4115-L4117) survives until the entire user turn ends.
- [`persistRecoveryCheckpoint`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/478960a8ab9315507e0a40d4434df71898fadf13/src/core/agent/runtime/orchestrator.zig#L3282-L3295) repeatedly rebuilds the accumulated execution history into that arena. Earlier temporary copies remain allocated, producing approximately quadratic cumulative growth. [Successful responses also trigger these saves](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/478960a8ab9315507e0a40d4434df71898fadf13/src/core/agent/runtime/orchestrator.zig#L6458-L6487).
- [The persistence sink](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/478960a8ab9315507e0a40d4434df71898fadf13/src/core/session/session_log.zig#L2315-L2335) synchronously copies the incoming checkpoint and frees its previous owned copy, but this does not release the caller's temporary reconstruction.

**Expected:** memory may grow with retained history, but obsolete checkpoint copies must be released after each save. Use an independent temporary allocator with correct copy-out ownership; do not reset the whole turn arena while messages or callbacks still borrow it. Lowering the step limit alone does not fix this defect.

The step limit is unlimited by default. A separate fixture also completed 160 unchanged inspection batches without a no-progress stop. However, the OOM reproduction above uses changing evidence, so useful long-running tasks are affected too.

Related: #483 and the still-unmerged #484. This report adds the Ubuntu incident and a reproduction on the current tested upstream revision. I have not tested #484, and without a heap snapshot cannot attribute every byte of the original incident to this one allocation path.

### Sensitive information

- [x] Reviewed and removed secrets and private session content. Only aggregate measurements and synthetic test details are included.

title: Bound temporary memory during long agent turns
body:
Long saved turns retain each full recovery-checkpoint reconstruction, plus provider HTTP/parser scratch, in the turn arena until the turn ends. Rebuilding a growing history repeatedly therefore accumulates obsolete copies and can exhaust memory during an otherwise ordinary task.

Give checkpoint reconstruction and each provider attempt their own temporary arena. Persistence sinks synchronously copy or serialize the checkpoint; owned provider results are deep-copied before request storage is released, including deferred usage references and failure diagnostics. Existing history, retry behavior, and step limits are preserved.

The included deterministic benchmark uses a local Gateway fixture with changing 1 KiB file reads, a 2 GiB address-space cap, and a 600-second deadline. On Ubuntu x86_64 with Zig 0.16 ReleaseSafe:

| Version | Successful tool steps | Peak fx RSS | Retained tool output |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Upstream `478960a8` | 482, then `OutOfMemory` | 1433.7 MiB | 0.50 MiB |
| This fix | 1000, completed | 82.2 MiB | 1.03 MiB |

Validation includes 1000 growing checkpoint saves, 1000 provider attempts covering success, cancellation and failures, allocation-failure injection for result copies, and runtime CLI/ACP/TUI checks for recovery, retry, cancellation, streaming and persistent child turns. Full CI passed on all four native platforms for `21fd1b6d`: [full run](https://github.com/acking-you/fx/actions/runs/33961697797).

Required classification: `type: bug` .

Fixes #686

title: Preserve Gateway v3 reasoning parts through tool continuation and resume
body:
## Summary

On the `/v3/ai/language-model` endpoint, fx forwarded reasoning text to the display but dropped it from the conversation: reasoning blocks, their provider metadata (signatures, redacted or encrypted state, item IDs, thought signatures), and part ordering were lost after tool calls, on later user turns, and across save/resume. fx also sent specification header `4` to the v3 route and emitted a top-level `reasoning` field that the v3 call-options schema discards.

This change preserves supported assistant reasoning parts, their order, and their replay metadata through the v3 stream, the owned completion, the next tool-loop request, durable history, and resumed sessions.

## What changed

- **Decode:** the shared SSE decoder accumulates text/reasoning blocks by stream ID with latest-snapshot metadata semantics — including metadata-only blocks and signatures carried on empty deltas — and captures tool-call and final-result metadata at their own scopes. Retained state is bounded; oversized or unattributable capture discards the sequence explicitly rather than truncating signed content.
- **Serialize:** assistant messages emit the ordered parts with per-part `providerOptions` when present, and keep the existing text/tool projection otherwise. References to tool calls are validated against the surviving calls.
- **Runtime:** parts flow through tool loops, steering, stop-hook and silent continuations, and the final answer. Call filtering remaps ordered references with the selected calls in the same pass, and projections that rewrite calls or text detach signed state instead of replaying altered content. Response-language rejection clears parts with content. Failed, interrupted, or length-limited attempts do not retain partial replay state.
- **Persistence:** the conversation event log carries parts on assistant events (omitted when absent) and call/result metadata on their own events; the shared session codec, recovery checkpoints, kernel checkpoints, and the JS host store round-trip them as optional fields with no schema bump. Old records load with replay state absent; unknown envelope keys stay rejected; stale references fail strictly.
- **Retention policy:** provider signatures and ciphertext are opaque protocol state — retained exactly, never logged, never normalized. Any transform that would alter part content (secret masking, argument rewrites, compaction) marks the replay unit unavailable and the message falls back to the legacy projection.
- **Protocol:** native and host streaming and the retained non-streaming helper send specification header `3` on the v3 route; the unsupported top-level `reasoning` field is no longer emitted. Effort preferences are unchanged and remain available through supported provider options. Direct Codex/Grok paths are unchanged.

## Test plan

- New unit/integration coverage: a decode-to-replay fixture; decoder tests for metadata-only blocks, end-event metadata, malformed and unattributable lifecycle events, capture bounds, and allocation-failure cleanup; serializer tests for ordered replay, per-part option scopes, and stale/duplicate reference rejection; a runtime tool-loop test inspecting the continuation request body; redaction-collision policy tests; conversation-log and shared-codec round trips including old shapes; kernel-checkpoint round trip.
- New e2e in `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` (inherits the file's existing PGSO classification): a tool loop whose continuation request carries the exact retained parts, followed by a fresh-process resume that sends them again.
- Updated header/effort assertions in `cli.test.ts`, `config-persistence.test.ts`, and `web-search-fake-gateway.test.ts`.
- Verified locally: focused `zig build test` scopes in Debug and ReleaseSafe, `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe`, `scripts/check-public-surface.sh`, and the lifecycle/CLI/web-search e2e files against the built binary.

title: Add durable journal execution to libfx
body:
Persist model decisions, tool outcomes and turn completion before dependent work proceeds, so interrupted sessions recover acknowledged work without blindly repeating an uncertain effect.

- Add one journal and replay contract across the native and Wasm SDKs, with stable request, message and tool identities; derive transcripts and recorded request outcomes from the journal.
- Use the same authority in CLI, interactive, ACP and persistent child sessions. Convert eligible completed legacy sessions under their writer lock while preserving original files; keep uncertain legacy work read-only until compatible recovery resolves it.
- Preserve compaction, images, permissions and steering. Restart through an acknowledged one-use handoff; ordinary reopening leaves unfinished work paused. Remember an interactive session when its first journal request is durably admitted.
- Retain request outcomes through checkpoint pruning, refuse capacity before model/tool I/O, fence uncertain writes, and preserve ESM/CommonJS loading, asynchronous Wasm assets and deployment tracing.

title: Add native DeepSeek provider via the Responses API
body:
## Summary

Adds **DeepSeek** as a native model provider that fx talks to directly. Requests route straight from fx to the DeepSeek API (`api.deepseek.com`) over the OpenAI Responses protocol with your own key, never through Vercel AI Gateway, OpenAI, or xAI.

## Registering DeepSeek with `fx login deepseek`

DeepSeek is pay-as-you-go and key-based, so there is no OAuth browser sign-in. Configure it from the terminal:

```bash
export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-...   # create a key in the DeepSeek Platform console
fx login deepseek                # validates the key and selects DeepSeek
fx
```

Notes on how this flow behaves, so the docs and copy stay honest:

- `fx login deepseek` checks the `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` environment variable, fetches the authenticated DeepSeek model catalog with it, and persists only the provider/model selection (profile settings under `~/.fx`).
- The key itself is read from the environment on every request. fx saves no DeepSeek login session, does not write the key to the macOS Keychain or to any `~/.fx` file, and never sends it to Vercel, OpenAI, or xAI.
- `fx logout deepseek` prints that nothing is stored.
- `fx login deepseek` reports `fx needs a DeepSeek API key for this model. Set DEEPSEEK_API_KEY.` when the variable is missing or empty, and `fx provider deepseek` and `/provider` can select DeepSeek the same way.

## What changes

- New `deepseek` provider id wired into the CLI, TUI provider menu, model catalog, credential resolution, and permission review.
- `src/gateway/deepseek.zig`: DeepSeek transport over the Responses API, including streaming, tool use, and image input; `src/gateway/deepseek_models.zig`: authenticated model catalog; `src/gateway/deepseek_permission_reviewer.zig`: permission review for direct DeepSeek traffic.
- Thinking-mode chain of thought is stored with your sessions so continued tool use can pass it back to the API.
- README usage docs for the new provider.

## Verification

- `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe` succeeds on this head; the built binary reports `0.0.8` and runs.
- Local unit/e2e suites and Full CI have not been run yet for this head; this PR is a draft pending the Full CI run on all four native runners.

title: Saturate OAuth refresh deadline subtraction
body:
## Why
Corrupt or hand-edited Grok/ChatGPT auth files can store an out-of-range `expires_at_ms`. `refreshDeadlineMs` used an unchecked `-` for the one-minute skew, so values near `i64.min` overflowed and aborted fx. Other parse failures on the same file degrade to a re-login. This one field crashed instead.

## Scope
- `src/core/auth/subscription_session.zig`: `refreshDeadlineMs` uses saturating subtraction (`-|`), matching `oauth_session.zig`. Grok and ChatGPT sessions both use this shared helper now, so one change covers both.
- Four new cases in the existing refresh-deadline test: `0`, `-1`, `i64.min` and `i64.max`.

## Blast radius
Only the refresh-deadline helper. Healthy token write paths already use checked math and are unchanged.

## Verification
- `zig build test` with Zig 0.17.0: the refresh-deadline test passes. 10 other tests fail or crash locally (git worktree, session, subagent and catalog tests). None of them touch auth, and this PR doesn't change them.

title: Resolve inline emphasis with a delimiter stack
body:
## Summary

- A `**`, `*`, `__`, `_`, or `~~` with no matching partner on the line renders as the literal characters instead of styling everything to the end of the line, and a lone backtick renders literally instead of turning the rest of the line into code.
- Emphasis is resolved with the CommonMark delimiter stack: runs are classified once from their neighbours, `***both***` nests bold inside italic, `****` and `~~~~` stay literal, `*italic**` closes italic and leaves one literal star, intraword `snake_case` never delimits, and `**a __b__ c**` keeps the outer bold after the inner span closes.
- Emphasis pairs correctly across code spans, links, images, autolinks, and bare URLs because those are single tokens before matching; a backtick inside link text or a star inside a code span never affects pairing.
- Bare URLs no longer depend on which styles are active. Like GFM autolinks they run to the next whitespace and leave trailing punctuation, including `*`, `_`, and `~`, outside the link, so `**https://example.com** tail` and `*see https://example.com/a* next` both pair.
- Headings resolve emphasis the same way with bold suppressed, so an unmatched `**` inside a heading stays visible instead of being stripped.
- Rendering is linear in the line length: 96 KB of unmatched openers or closers, 64 K stars in one run, and URL heavy lines all render in a few milliseconds with no lookahead budget.

Behavior that changes on purpose: an unclosed opener no longer styles to the end of the line; a URL followed by mismatched underscores (`_https://example.com/path__`) now trims the trailing underscores from the link and pairs on the shared run length, matching GitHub.

title: Bug: Empty grep_files path can make a compacted session unresumable
body:
### Issue details

### Description

A successful `grep_files` call with an explicitly empty optional `path` can add invalid file evidence to the active turn. The search itself succeeds because the tool decoder normalizes an empty path to `"."`, but the durable execution-memory projection copies the raw empty string into `FileEvidence.path`.

The invalid evidence remains latent while the turn is active. If context compaction checkpoints that turn, later turn finalization or recovery materialization rejects the empty path with `InvalidConversationEvent`. Shutdown can retry the same persistence path and report a second error:

```text
fx: InvalidConversationEvent
fx: session save failed: InvalidConversationEvent
```

The conversation event log and compaction checkpoint can still be valid, so `fx doctor` and `fx session --id <id> --json` may both succeed even though continuing or finalizing the recovered turn fails.

Observed with fx 0.0.8 on Arch Linux.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a saved session and keep one turn active.
2. Execute a successful root-scoped search whose raw arguments contain an empty path:

   ```json
   {"pattern":"needle","path":""}
   ```

3. Trigger context compaction while that turn is active.
4. Let the turn finish, interrupt it, or resume it and submit a fresh prompt.
5. Observe `InvalidConversationEvent` while fx persists the completed or interrupted turn. On shutdown, observe `session save failed: InvalidConversationEvent` as the same state is retried.

### Expected behavior

Root-scoped searches should store a valid effective path, matching the path used by the tool. Compaction and recovery should not make the session impossible to finalize or resume.

### Actual behavior

`grep_files` execution treats `"path":""` as `"."`, while `appendFileEvidenceForTool` stores the raw empty string. `validateConversationPath` later rejects that value because conversation paths must be non-empty.

### Root cause

The producer and validator disagree:

- `src/tools/filesystem/grep_files.zig` normalizes an omitted or empty search path to `"."` for execution.
- `src/core/agent/execution_memory.zig` derives file evidence from the raw tool-call arguments and accepts an empty string.
- `src/core/session/session_event.zig` rejects empty `FileEvidence.path` values when finalizing the conversation event.

In the affected session, the final saved event was a valid context checkpoint. The invalid values existed only in the recovery checkpoint's execution file evidence, which explains why ordinary session inspection did not detect the failure.

### Suggested fix

Normalize missing and empty search roots to `"."` when creating file evidence, and add regression coverage for both explicit empty paths and omitted paths.

Existing affected sessions may still require recovery-file repair or a dedicated normalization path; preventing new invalid evidence does not retroactively change saved recovery checkpoints.

### Trace

No trace is attached because it may contain private conversation and workspace data. The diagnosis above was reproduced from structural session metadata without including prompt, output, or file contents.

### Sensitive information

- [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

title: Normalize root search paths in file evidence
body:
**Issue:** Fixes #779

## Summary

- Treat empty search-path fields as absent when projecting tool calls into durable file evidence.
- Record `"."` when a `grep_files` or `glob_files` call omits its search root or supplies an empty root.
- Add regression coverage for explicit empty and omitted search paths.

## Problem

The search tools execute an omitted or empty path against the current workspace by normalizing it to `"."`. File-evidence projection previously read the raw tool-call arguments instead and persisted `FileEvidence.path = ""`.

That empty path is rejected later by conversation-event validation. The failure can remain hidden during an active turn, become part of a recovery checkpoint after compaction, and then surface as `InvalidConversationEvent` when the completed or interrupted turn is persisted. Shutdown can retry the same invalid state and emit `session save failed: InvalidConversationEvent`.

## Changes

`appendFileEvidenceForTool` now:

1. Ignores empty `path`, `directory`, and `query` string candidates.
2. Uses the first non-empty search root when one is present.
3. Falls back to `"."` for root-scoped `grep_files` and `glob_files` calls.
4. Continues to omit file evidence for non-search tools whose required path is missing or empty.

The focused unit test covers:

- `grep_files` with `"path":""`.
- `glob_files` with no `path` field.

Both cases must produce non-empty file evidence with path `"."`.

## Scope

This change prevents new invalid file-evidence records. It does not migrate recovery checkpoints already containing an empty path. The reported local session was repaired separately by changing only the affected empty search paths to `"."` after first creating a full backup.

## Verification

Passed locally:

```text
zig fmt --check src/core/agent/execution_memory.zig
```

```text
zig test -target x86_64-linux-musl -lc -ODebug \
  --dep build_options -Mroot=src/main.zig \
  -Mbuild_options=<generated-options.zig> \
  --test-filter 'search file evidence normalizes missing and empty roots'
```

Result after merging the latest `main`: 14 filtered test roots passed, exit 0.

A patched static debug binary was built successfully for `x86_64-linux-musl`. With the separately repaired recovery file, that binary:

- inspected the affected original session with exit 0 and empty stderr;
- resumed the exact original session ID;
- displayed the preserved paused recovery at attempt 1/10;
- exited cleanly with exit 0 without making a model request.

`git diff --check` also passed with exit 0.

## Local verification limitations

The post-merge local musl Debug command below completed with exit 1 after 8,770 tests passed and 20 were skipped:

```text
zig build test -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-musl
```

The ANSI-span test launches a nested native `zig test` and failed because this Arch Linux host's GCC 16 `.sframe` startup object uses `R_X86_64_PC64` relocations that Zig 0.16's linker does not handle. Two process-disappearance timing tests also failed during the broad local run; both live in `command_runner.zig`, outside the PR's one-file diff:

- `foreground session owner loss kills the target and descendant before delayed effects`
- `timeout terminates foreground process group descendants`

The previous canonical `main` commit, `cce01969`, passed the repository's native Ubuntu ReleaseSafe CI run 34414854124. The branch now also includes current canonical `main` at `4f9b152f`; no Actions run for that commit was indexed at update time. Full CI has not yet run for the PR's exact commit, `210e529b`, and remains required on the repository's native Linux and macOS matrix.

## Privacy

No private transcript, prompt text, model output, trace, terminal recording, credential, session identifier, or unrelated workspace content is included in this PR.

title: Resolve hostnames on Termux
body:
On Termux, `/etc` is a symlink to the read-only Android `/system/etc`, so `/etc/resolv.conf` does not exist. fx's DNS resolver only reads that path and otherwise falls back to `127.0.0.1:53`, which has no listener on Android. Every hostname lookup therefore timed out, which broke OAuth discovery, the device-token poll, and model and credit requests, so sign-in failed on Termux.

This change adds a Termux-aware `netLookup` override behind the existing `process_io_for` host selection in `io.zig`. When `/etc/resolv.conf` is absent but Termux's `/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/etc/resolv.conf` exists, fx resolves A and AAAA records directly against the configured nameservers, with IP-literal and localhost handling preserved. On ordinary Linux the original resolver is used unchanged, so there is no behavior change elsewhere.

Unit tests cover the DNS query builder.

## Alternative considered

Instead of a runtime override, we could patch the Zig toolchain in CI with the one-line fallback the Termux `zig` package already ships in `std/Io/net/HostName.zig`:

```zig
Io.Dir.openFileAbsolute(io, "/etc/resolv.conf", .{})
    catch Io.Dir.openFileAbsolute(io, "/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/etc/resolv.conf", .{})
```

That drops the new source file, but it pins releases to a patched toolchain and fails silently when Zig reshapes that resolver. The runtime override was chosen because it is toolchain-independent and produces a single `aarch64-linux` binary that works on both Termux and ordinary Linux.

## Summary

Shrinks the compact ReleaseSmall surface back under 5 MiB on aarch64-macos (4.966 MiB) with no feature changes, recovering the ~140 KiB that recent main added since the original 4.987 MiB reference, via three size levers.

Strictness is preserved: `ConversationInterruption` gains a `jsonParseFromValue` mirror of its custom hook, and the recovery checkpoint frame keeps its strict two-field shape checks. The image-measurement site in `prompt_context.zig` intentionally keeps typed parsing to borrow multi-MB payload strings from the request body.

title: Bug: Transcript history transitions can leave gaps or hide follow-up output
body: ### Description Long-running interactive sessions can desynchronize the visible transcript from terminal-native scrollback during two related contraction paths: 1. Closing an expanded footer surface, such as a question prompt or picker, can leave the compact footer detached from the terminal bottom with unused rows in the transcript viewport. 2. Replacing a mutable assistant or tool-status row with shorter content after part of that row has already entered native scrollback can make the next assistant output disappear, repeat, or render against an invalid history position until a resize rebuilds the projection. Observed with fx 0.0.8 on Arch Linux. ### Current investigation status PR #816 addresses two deterministic transcript transition failures reproduced in tests and makes the footer gap occur less often, but the original symptom remains intermittently reproducible in real sessions. The mechanisms below are confirmed contributing failure paths, not yet a complete root-cause explanation. Help from maintainers reproducing and tracing the remaining path would be greatly appreciated. ### Screenshots Recommended upload order and captions: 1. `1-bug.png` — Transcript rows disappear after a history contraction. 2. `1-normal.png` — The same transcript region after a resize rebuilds the projection and restores the missing rows. 3. `2-bug.png` — The active footer remains stranded near the middle of the terminal, leaving a large empty region below it. 4. `3.png` — A long-running active session retains its footer but loses the visible transcript entirely. The solid red regions are intentional privacy redactions. ### Steps to reproduce #### Footer reservation contraction 1. Start an interactive fx session with enough transcript content to fill the viewport. 2. Open a footer surface that reserves additional rows, such as an `ask_user_question` prompt or a picker. 3. Continue producing transcript content while the expanded footer is visible. 4. Close the footer surface. 5. Observe that the compact footer can remain above the terminal bottom instead of allowing the transcript to refill the released rows. #### Mutable source contraction 1. Fill the transcript viewport and append a replaceable assistant or tool-status row that wraps across multiple visual rows. 2. Allow part of that mutable row to move into terminal-native scrollback. 3. Replace it with shorter settled content. 4. Append more assistant output. 5. Observe that the logical viewport can attempt to rewind behind rows already committed to native scrollback, causing missing or duplicate follow-up output. Resizing the terminal rebuilds the projection and restores the expected content. These two transition failures are timing-sensitive in ordinary use but become deterministic when committed visual and history offsets are modeled directly. They do not yet account for every occurrence of the footer-gap symptom. ### Expected behavior When footer reservation contracts, fx should reclaim the released viewport rows and keep the footer anchored to the terminal bottom. When mutable transcript content contracts after entering native scrollback, fx should preserve the immutable native-history floor, repaint the valid on-screen suffix, and render later assistant output exactly once without requiring a resize. ### Actual behavior The renderer previously treated contraction paths as if one history rule applied to both: - Footer shrink retained the old displaced projection even though additional viewport rows had become available. - Mutable source shrink could invalidate or rewind the committed anchor even though terminal-native history cannot be rewritten. - Later growth could release rows already present in native history a second time. ### Confirmed contributing mechanisms Footer direction was represented by independent booleans rather than one coherent transition. The transcript pipeline therefore could not consistently distinguish rows displaced by footer growth from rows reclaimed after footer shrink. Source reconciliation also treated replaceable-tail and ordinary turn-finalization rewrites too strictly. Once mutable rows had physically entered native scrollback, invalidating the same-epoch anchor lost the only record of the immutable history floor. ### Partial fix under evaluation - Represent footer history movement as one typed transition: unchanged, displaced, or reclaimed. - During footer reclamation, bypass stable projection preservation so the natural transcript tail can refill the expanded viewport. - Preserve the native-history floor across same-epoch mutable source contractions when the source still contains rows at that floor. - If a deep contraction removes every remaining row at or beyond the floor, avoid staging an unpaintable EOF projection and repaint the natural visible tail behind immutable history. - Preserve the normal-buffer anchor for ordinary tool lifecycle finalization and replaceable-tail rewrites when geometry is compatible. - Compute later semantic release from the greater of the visual and history offsets so previously committed history rows are not released twice. - Add deterministic regressions for footer closure, repeated stable frames, mutable contraction, and subsequent assistant growth. ### Trace No trace is attached because it may contain private conversation and workspace data. The diagnosis above was reproduced from structural session metadata without including prompt, output, or file contents. ### Sensitive information - [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

title: Reduce transcript gaps across footer and source contractions
body:
**Issue:** Related to #815

## Current status

This PR addresses two deterministic transcript transition failures reproduced in tests and makes the footer gap from #815 occur less often, but it does not fully resolve the original field symptom. The footer can still become detached from the terminal bottom intermittently in real sessions.

The mechanisms and changes below should therefore be read as confirmed contributing failure paths and partial fixes, not as the complete root cause or resolution. Help from maintainers tracing the remaining path would be greatly appreciated.

Redacted screenshots of the observed failures are available in #815.

## Summary

- Refill transcript viewport rows when an expanded footer closes.
- Preserve terminal-native history when mutable assistant or tool-status content contracts after scrolling.
- Prevent later content growth from releasing already committed history rows a second time.
- Add deterministic coverage for footer reclamation, stable follow-up frames, lifecycle reconciliation, and subsequent assistant output.

## Problem

Two opposite contraction paths could leave the logical transcript projection inconsistent with terminal-native history.

When a question prompt, picker, or other expanded footer closed, fx could preserve the old displaced projection instead of using the newly available transcript rows. This left the compact footer detached from the terminal bottom or retained an empty viewport band.

Separately, a replaceable assistant or tool-status row could physically enter native scrollback and then contract when its settled content replaced a longer provisional row. Invalidating or rewinding the anchor at that point is impossible because native scrollback is immutable. Follow-up assistant content could disappear, repeat, or render incorrectly until a resize rebuilt the projection.

## Changes

### Typed footer history transitions

Footer reservation direction now flows through frame preparation and scroll planning as one `FooterHistoryTransition` value:

- `unchanged`
- `displaced`
- `reclaimed`

This replaces independent booleans that could express contradictory states and gives transcript preparation and scroll planning one shared transition contract.

### Footer viewport reclamation

During a reclaimed footer transition, transcript preparation bypasses stable projection and history-floor preservation. The renderer can select the natural tail that fits the expanded transcript area while keeping the footer anchored to the terminal bottom.

Displaced footer rows retain their existing replay behavior when the footer grows.

### Mutable-source history preservation

Same-epoch replaceable-tail rewrites preserve the committed transcript anchor instead of forcing a rebase. Ordinary tool lifecycle finalization now uses the same normal-buffer anchor-preserving policy, while incompatible terminal geometry still invalidates the anchor.

When a contracted source leaves the logical viewport behind the native-history offset, transition resolution preserves the history floor while the source still contains rows at that floor. If a deeper contraction moves EOF below the floor, the renderer avoids staging an unpaintable EOF projection and repaints the natural visible tail behind immutable history. Later growth starts semantic release from the greater of the visual and history offsets, preventing duplicate terminal-history release.

### Regression coverage

The tests cover:

- Closing a filtered picker and returning the footer to the terminal bottom.
- Closing a question prompt after concurrent transcript progress and refilling the transcript area.
- Four identical follow-up frames with no planned, committed, or unplanned scroll and no document append.
- Contracting a source while preserving its existing native-history floor.
- Contracting a source below that floor without staging an EOF projection.
- Replacing a wrapped mutable row with shorter settled content after it has scrolled.
- Rendering settled status and follow-up assistant output exactly once.
- Applying turn-finalization anchor preservation by default while retaining the geometry-change fallback.
- Subsequent source growth producing no duplicate semantic or terminal-history release.

## Verification

Passed locally while developing this branch:

```text
zig fmt --check src/
git diff --check main
```

Result: exit 0.

```text
zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe
```

Result: exit 0.

Focused x86_64 Linux musl ReleaseSafe tests:

```text
zig test -target x86_64-linux-musl -lc -OReleaseSafe \
  --dep build_options -Mroot=src/main.zig -Mbuild_options=<generated-options.zig> \
  --test-filter 'question modal replays displaced transcript rows into history'
```

Result: 16 tests passed, exit 0.

The same command shape also passed these focused filters:

- `long transcript picker filtering keeps footer anchored and close releases reservation`: 16 tests passed.
- `contracted transcript source preserves the native history floor`: 15 tests passed in ReleaseSafe and Debug, including the deep-contraction EOF boundary.
- `mutable transcript contraction preserves the native history floor`: 16 tests passed.
- `turn finished anchor preservation applies by default and falls back for geometry blocker`: 15 tests passed.

Freshly built binary smoke verification:

```text
./zig-out/bin/fx --version
./zig-out/bin/fx replay <private-recording> --json
```

Result: fx reported `0.0.8`; replay exited 0 with empty stderr. The private recording is not included in the branch.

An earlier full x86_64 Linux musl ReleaseSafe test run before the final deep-contraction guard completed with 8,723 passed, 20 skipped, and 87 failed. The directly affected tests passed. Most failures required configured product executables or unsupported cross-target and process fixtures in the local environment. The final guard was then covered by the focused contraction test above.

## Local verification limitations

The native Debug build remains blocked on this Arch Linux host because GCC 16's `.sframe` startup object uses `R_X86_64_PC64` relocations that Zig 0.16's linker does not handle. ReleaseSafe and musl-focused verification succeeded.

The branch is pushed and this PR remains in draft while the intermittent footer-gap path is investigated. Full CI results must be evaluated for the exact current PR commit before review.

## Privacy

No private transcript, prompt text, model output, trace, terminal recording, credential, session identifier, or unrelated workspace content is included in this PR.

title: Deliver tool output verbatim to the model
body:
## Summary

Tool results, tool arguments, and saved session history now reach the model verbatim (still encoding-sanitized and capped). Previously, secret-shaped spans were replaced with a redaction marker at ingestion, and the masked copy was the only one kept — so when a task needed the value, the model could only pass the literal marker text and the receiving tool rejected it.

Human-facing surfaces keep masking: status lines, failure details, ACP client replay, URL display, diagnostics, and traces. `maskSecrets` and the credential-key argument projection remain in use for those display paths. The permission pipeline is unchanged.

This matches how other coding agents handle tool output: the model sees what the tool returned, display stays masked.

## Behavior change worth noting in review

This intentionally relaxes "secrets never persist in session state" to "secrets persist locally, display stays masked, provider sees tool output as-is" — the same posture as mainstream harnesses. Anything the pattern detector previously caught in tool output now flows like everything it never caught. The command-replay tape already stored raw output before this change.

## What was removed

- The model-path masking composition (`redactModelText`, `prepareRedactedOutput`)
- The `read_tool_result` unmasked special case (the general path is now unmasked, so the branch collapsed into it)

title: Bug: Crash after completed responses with InvalidConversationEvent
body:
### Issue details

fx can render a completed assistant response then fail during final session persistence:

```text
fx: InvalidConversationEvent
fx: session save failed: InvalidConversationEvent
```

The process exits and the completed turn is not saved.

## Expected behavior

A completed response should persist normally. If persistence fails, fx should preserve the rendered response and report the rejected event and invariant.

## Observed behavior

- fx version: `0.0.9`
- Environment: interactive macOS session
- A fresh session completed a multi-step agent turn with local file reads, shell commands and web fetches.
- The final assistant response rendered successfully.
- Immediately after `prompt_finish`, final persistence failed with `InvalidConversationEvent`.
- The session had no prior history, so this was not caused by corrupt resumed history.

A separate noninteractive run of the same private task completed and saved successfully. The failing interactive run had seven model steps and the successful run had six. This is correlation only.

## Findings

The error occurs after model execution, rendering and tool completion while fx serializes the in-memory completed turn into durable conversation events.

The current validation path returns only `InvalidConversationEvent`. It does not record the event kind, rejected field or failed invariant. It is therefore impossible to determine whether the bad value is in assistant text, provider replay, a tool call, a tool result or file evidence from the public error and normal trace alone.

## Suggested fix

Add safe persistence diagnostics at the conversation-event validation boundary:

- event ordinal and kind
- validator rule or field name
- byte lengths and boolean presence flags only
- no prompt, tool output, paths, arguments or provider-replay contents

Then add a regression test from the captured event shape and ensure persistence failure does not terminate fx after a response has already rendered.


### Trace

Unfortunately I cannot share the original prompt, repository and full trace because they contain private project content, paths and tool activity. 

However I ran fx with traces and here is the relevant trace sequence:

```text

[agent] event=prompt_finish ... outcome_kind=assistant
[session] shutdown finished prompt persistence failed err=InvalidConversationEvent
```

title: Bug: fx spins at 100% CPU or aborts after terminal revocation on macOS
body:
### Issue details

## Problem

On macOS, fx can consume 100% CPU indefinitely after its terminal is revoked. Depending on timing, it can instead abort during terminal cleanup.

## Cause

There are two failures in `src/ui/shell_runtime.zig`:

1. `TerminalState.pollInput` ignores `POLLNVAL`. A revoked descriptor makes `poll()` return immediately, but the event loop does not recognize the input as closed. It keeps polling without waiting.
2. `TerminalState.disableRawMode` calls `std.posix.tcsetattr` on the revoked descriptor. Zig treats the resulting `EBADF` as `unreachable`, so cleanup aborts. The surrounding `catch {}` cannot catch this panic.

## Reproduction

1. Launch a Debug build of fx on a fresh PTY, draining output from the master.
2. Use LLDB to pause immediately before the `std.posix.poll` call in `TerminalState.pollInput`, after startup.
3. Call macOS `revoke()` on the test PTY slave path.
4. Disable the breakpoint and continue.

This reproduced sustained 97–100% CPU usage in 3/3 runs.

Without controlling the timing, revocation reproduced the cleanup abort in 4/4 runs:

```text
std.posix.tcsetattr: .BADF => unreachable
TerminalState.disableRawMode
finishLeavingInteractiveMode
shutdownInteractiveShell
App.releaseTerminal
```

## Expected behavior

fx should exit without spinning or aborting when its terminal becomes invalid.

Both paths need handling: recognize `POLLNVAL` as closed input, and tolerate a revoked descriptor during terminal cleanup.

### Trace

_No response_

title: Exit cleanly when the terminal is revoked
body:
Closes #852.

When macOS revokes the terminal before the next poll, `poll()` returns `POLLNVAL` immediately. `TerminalState.pollInput` ignored that flag, so the event loop kept running at 100% CPU. Treat it as an input error and use the existing input-closure exit path.

Terminal cleanup also calls `tcsetattr` after revocation. Zig's POSIX wrapper treats `EBADF` as unreachable, so `catch {}` cannot prevent an abort. Call the underlying syscall during best-effort restoration and retain retries for `EINTR`.

Add regression tests for invalid descriptors, actual macOS PTY revocation, normal termios restoration, and event-loop exit on an input error. No event-loop behavior or public interface changes beyond handling the lost terminal.

Verification on macOS arm64 with Zig 0.16.0:

- Before the fix, both poll regression tests failed and the cleanup regression test aborted at `std.posix.tcsetattr`.
- After the fix, all 31 focused tests passed in both Debug and ReleaseSafe.
- `zig build`, `zig fmt --check src/`, `git diff --check`, and the public-surface audit passed.
- The freshly built binary exited with status 0 after LLDB-controlled revocation immediately before polling, with empty stderr.
- Four additional PTY revocations and a normal `/exit` interaction also exited with status 0 and empty stderr. Each run used an isolated HOME.

Full CI is pending. This PR remains a draft until the required checks pass.

Required classification: `type: bug`.

title: Remove struct fields that are written but never read
body:
## Summary

- Remove twenty struct fields whose values are recorded and never consumed, found by a field-flow analysis over the Zig AST (writes via literals and assignments versus reads in any position, with whole-struct hazards like `std.meta.eql` and `expectEqualDeep` excluded): layout records nobody reads back (`SkillsMenuLayout.description_row_count`, `Geometry.activity_reserved_rows`, `Row.prefix_cell_width`, `Row.first_cursor_offset`, `PaintPlan.footer_reservation_source` with its `FooterReservationSource` enum, `FooterFramePlan.banner_activity`/`overlay_suppressed`), shimmer/paint diagnostics with no consumer (`PaintTraceState` shimmer fields, `TranscriptRuntime.shimmer_row`, the inert `paint_test_mode` scaffolding with its `PaintTestMode` enum), `Styles.cancelled_text_style`, `Match.clear_match`, `Ranked.secondary_hits`, `CreatedParentResidue.created_identity`, `EventReplay.gap_through`, record_tape `start_ms`, `ParentTurnDeliveryAck.end_offset`, and `FakeSubagents.childPresentationView` whose view struct was never consumed. `FileMutationActionIdentity` hashes (compared via `std.meta.eql`), `Decision.stale_reason` (pinned by `expectEqualDeep` tests), extern syscall layouts, and terminal-contract model fields were excluded by construction. No user-facing behavior change.

title: Move profile usage ledger writes off the turn path
body:
## Summary

- Responses render as soon as the model finishes instead of waiting for usage accounting: turn completion lands 5-8ms after the model's final byte, down from 610-937ms on profiles with large usage ledgers (measured against a 14MB, 57k-record usage.jsonl). That is roughly 100x faster on the post-stream stage (737ms to 6ms on average).

title: Reclip truncated command statuses to the live terminal width
body:
## Summary

- Show the full command in collapsed tool groups for tty runs and terminal-session actions (Observed, Sent input to, Stopped) whenever it fits the terminal width, instead of stopping at a fixed cap with trailing dots
- Reclip truncated command statuses to the live width after terminal resizes and in the expanded full-transcript view

title: Skip redundant credential reloads on the request path
body:
## Summary

- Request steps no longer re-read the OS secret store when the credential was just verified: step begin to request sent is 30-33ms, down from 80-92ms per step (measured with fx ask, ReleaseSafe, macOS keychain-backed fx_login), about 2.5x faster on the pre-send stage of every step.
- Turns with multiple steps (tool loops) skip the repeated reload between steps; a step that lands past the 30 second freshness window still performs a real reload, verified live on a 76 second multi-step turn.
- Auth behavior is unchanged: a stale skip costs one unauthorized response, which the existing force-refresh replay recovers; the freshness stamp is set on every successful credential load and preparation.

title: Add retry guidance for shell parse and usage errors
body:
## Summary

- Shell tool results for commands the shell could not parse (unmatched quote or syntax error) now include retry guidance directing the agent to rewrite the command with corrected quoting instead of rerunning it.
- Shell tool results for usage errors (missing or empty arguments) now include retry guidance directing the agent to rebuild the command with explicit arguments instead of rerunning it unchanged.
- Ordinary command failures and successful commands return no retry guidance, unchanged from before.

title: Reclip resumed session rows to the live terminal width
body:
## Summary

- Reclip resumed Observed, Sent input to, and Stopped rows to the live terminal width instead of keeping the frozen 120-column text
- Show the launch command instead of the raw session id for resumed tty-launched session rows
- Skip command reprojection when the frozen row does not start with the stored action label

Stacked on #860.

title: List only resumable sessions and expand the selected one
body:
## Summary

- The resume picker lists only sessions that can actually be resumed: the session you are inside no longer appears, and sessions held by another live fx process are left out until they are freed.
- Right expands the selected session with its full workspace path, recorded model, and creation age; Left collapses it.
- Rows keep their existing look: title first, metadata clustered on the right, brightness marking the selection.

Was stacked on #833, which has merged.

title: Notify when Fast mode drops because model support is unconfirmed
body:
**Summary**
---
- Emit a one-time per-turn notice when Fast mode is on but the model catalog is known to be failed or unreachable, so the request silently runs at standard speed: "Fast mode is unavailable for this model right now; continuing at standard speed."
- A reachable catalog that simply lacks fast metadata for the model stays quiet; the notice is reserved for the divergent case where the UI shows Fast mode while the wire cannot confirm it
- The request stays fail-closed; only the user-facing notice is new

title: Add --model, --effort, and --fast flags to fx ask
body:
**Summary**
---
- fx ask --model <id> overrides the model for one run without changing saved preferences
- fx ask --effort <level> overrides the reasoning effort for the run
- fx ask --fast and --no-fast turn Fast mode on or off for the run
- Overriding the model without --fast drops the default-enabled Fast mode, which only ever applied to the default model
- Flag overrides win over resumed session preferences and are never written back to the session

- Add the approved v0.0.10 release notes.

title: Preserve transcript rows across retention rewrites
body:
## Summary

- Keep finalized conversation rows and their blank separators when command-output retention trims older entries.
- Stop newer output from overwriting older rows before those rows reach native scrollback.
- Preserve pending transcript publication while the full-transcript viewer is open and across terminal resizes.
- Complete pending replacement notices after a partial bounded release instead of failing the transcript transition.
- Keep live tool-status updates editable and explicit clear and resume behavior unchanged.

title: Tiered transcript collapse (Marionette-style) with live terminal hotkeys
body:
## Summary

fx today offers a global **Collapse tool calls** setting: one summary header per tool group in the main transcript, with full detail behind `Ctrl+O`. That is useful but blunt.

This issue proposes **Marionette-style tiered collapse**: one mega umbrella per turn, nested collapsible groups underneath, **per-node** expand/collapse, and **hotkeys that work mid-turn** in the TUI (no mouse required).

## Motivation

Long turns produce dozens of tool lines. Operators need to:

1. Keep the live transcript scannable under a single turn umbrella (e.g. “Worked for …”).
2. Expand one batch (`Ran N commands`) without dumping every group.
3. Collapse/expand while the agent is still running.

Global on/off + full-transcript escape hatch does not cover (2) or (3).

## Proposed model

| Tier | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| T0 | Turn umbrella — one node from user send → turn done |
| T1 | Tool / thought batches (today’s tool groups + thought blocks) |
| T2 | Individual tool rows (and nested thoughts inside a batch) |

Default live view: T0 open (or collapsed to umbrella only via hotkey), T1 headers visible, T2 collapsed. Expand is per-node.

## Proposed hotkeys (live mid-turn)

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `←` / `h` | Collapse focused node |
| `→` / `l` | Expand focused node one level |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Toggle focused node |
| `[` | Collapse all to T0 umbrella only |
| `]` | Expand T0; keep T1 headers, T2 collapsed |
| `Ctrl+[` | Collapse subtree under focus |
| `Ctrl+]` | Expand one level under focus |
| `Ctrl+O` | Keep as full unfiltered transcript escape hatch |

Focus = transcript row cursor (`j`/`k` or arrows). New tools append into the open leaf group; T0 duration updates live.

## Implementation notes (non-binding)

- Spine: `src/ui/transcript/tool_group_projection.zig` already owns T1 grouping.
- Replace global `collapse_tool_calls: bool` as the sole UX with per-node expand state (`node_id → open|closed`); keep the setting as **default policy for new nodes** if useful.
- Keys first; mouse later.
- Preserve retention / full-transcript correctness (see related work on transcript gaps / retention).

## Out of scope (for the first PR)

- Mouse click targets
- Redesigning full-transcript (`Ctrl+O`) itself
- Durable journal / Redis swarm (separate track)

## Acceptance (P0)

- [ ] T0 turn umbrella in the main transcript
- [ ] T1 groups toggle independently while a turn is live
- [ ] `[` / `]` / Enter (or documented equivalents) work mid-run
- [ ] `zig build` + focused UI tests; verify with `./zig-out/bin/fx` (not PATH)

Happy to take a first PR on this.

title: Stop re-parsing and rewriting the usage ledger on every append
body:
## Summary

- Usage ledger writes no longer stall behind full-file work: the store keeps a resident record index and reads only newly appended bytes, so steady-state appends drop from hundreds of milliseconds to under 1ms on a 16MB, 66k-record profile.
- Turns no longer trigger a full-ledger compaction rewrite: the after-append trigger previously counted a turn's just-resolved pending marker as expired, so every turn rewrote the whole file; it now requires records aged past the 35-day retention.
- Concurrent fx sessions stop serializing behind the ledger lock for hundreds of milliseconds per turn; fx ask runs use about half the CPU (0.49-0.53s vs 0.84-1.03s) with wall time steady at 1.8-2.0s instead of a lock-contended 2.1-8.0s.
- Incident records in the ledger are capped at 4096, bounding parse cost for profiles with long billing-incomplete history.
- Ledger contents, dedupe, and durability are unchanged; a tail-sample guard forces a full re-parse whenever another process replaced the file.

title: Add --model, --effort, and --fast flags to interactive launch
body:

title: Add --no-mcp and FX_DISABLE_MCP launch suppression
body:
## What and why

A launch spawned by another agent inherits the operator's MCP profile. When fx
runs as a Puppetmaster worker, the worker can reach the `puppetmaster` MCP
server and start more workers. The recursion fix belongs at the source, not only
in a downstream depth counter.

This adds two ways to turn MCP loading off for a launch:

- `fx --no-mcp <command>`: a global launch modifier, accepted before
  interactive, resume, ask, ACP, PR, and issue launches.
- `FX_DISABLE_MCP=1`: the same policy for wrappers that cannot add argv flags.

`--no-mcp` replaces the configured MCP loader with one that loads nothing, so
the policy holds for the first load and for every later reload or authority
rebuild. `fx acp --no-mcp` also drops ACP project MCP sources, so a host cannot
reintroduce servers through the ACP request.

`FX_DISABLE_MCP` is a blunt, silent switch, so it only suppresses launches that
can own the policy. It never turns another command into an argv-style usage
error.

## Verification

Built and driven locally (`./zig-out/bin/fx`, macOS arm64).

Interactive, isolated `HOME` with one profile MCP fixture that appends its pid
to a launch log:

| launch | fixture launches | `/mcp list` |
|---|---|---|
| `fx --no-mcp` | 0 | `No MCP servers configured.` |
| `fx` (control) | 8 (fixture exits, retried) | `MCP health (1 server): fixture ...` |

Both sessions exited cleanly with `/exit` (exit 0). CLI surface checked with the
built binary: `fx help` lists the flag, `--no-mcp --no-mcp` fails with
`--no-mcp may only be specified once`, and `fx --no-mcp mcp list` fails with the
launch-suppression usage line. Both exit 1.

`tests/e2e/mcp-stdio.test.ts` gained three tests: suppression on `ask`,
suppression through `FX_DISABLE_MCP`, and a control that still loads the server
(65 pass / 0 fail for the file). Unit tests cover parsing, the env switch, and
the App loader.

`zig build test`: 8925 pass, 2 skip, 5 fail. The 5 failures are pre-existing on
the base commit in this checkout (`tool_runtime.run_command` and
`command_runner` shell-sandbox tests); the base commit shows the identical 5
failures with 8919 pass. Neither module is touched here.

TUI-driven suites could not run in this environment: `tmux` is not installed, so
the tmux-based scenarios skipped. Full CI covers those on all four runners.

## Docs

`CONTRIBUTING.md` MCP section documents both switches and their purpose.

## Label

`type: feature`.

title: Add a /swarm command for Puppetmaster swarm status
body:
## What this does

Adds a `/swarm` slash command that shows Puppetmaster swarm state inside the fx transcript. It is read-only and one-shot.

```
/swarm                 # this workspace's latest job
/swarm <job-id>        # one job by id
/swarm findings        # artifacts only
```

Output shape:

```
* swarm: swarm job_01054acb05c0 · complete
    kernel analyze request
    goal: Role: analysis
    tasks: 3 total · 1 complete · 2 queued · 4 artifacts
    delivery: delivered · quality ok · trustworthy
    findings: 1
    recent:
      finding · artifact.saved
      patch · artifact.saved
```

## How it reads Puppetmaster

Through the CLI, not the state directory: `status <job>` and `feed <job> --json`. The raw JSON in Puppetmaster's state dir is private layout, and hardcoding it would couple fx to something that changes without notice.

Both reads are bounded (512 KiB stdout, 8 KiB stderr, 15s deadline), so a missing binary, a slow caller, or a runaway worker cannot turn a read-only view into a hang. Every field is optional on read, because Puppetmaster adds keys over time and a schema addition must not break the view.

`PUPPETMASTER_COMMAND` overrides the binary name, defaulting to `puppetmaster` on PATH.

## Behavior on failure

Each of these is a short notice, verified against the built binary:

| State | Notice |
| --- | --- |
| Binary absent | `Puppetmaster is not installed or not on PATH` |
| No job in this workspace | `No Puppetmaster swarm found for this workspace...` |
| Read exceeds the deadline | `Puppetmaster did not answer in time` |
| Non-zero exit | `Puppetmaster could not read that job` |

A missing binary stays distinct from an empty workspace, which a single "nothing found" string would have conflated.

## Design

New module dir `src/core/swarm/`:

- `snapshot.zig` - pure parse and render. No process, no filesystem, no app state.
- `provider.zig` - the bounded CLI read, injected as a function pointer so the App and tests can substitute it.

Rendering goes through the same `writeDomainNotice` path as `/mcp` and `/skills`, so there is no second rendering path. A long-lived artifact follower was considered and deliberately left out of this change; it would need a background thread and a cancellation path, turning a read-only view into a live subsystem. The provider seam is where it would attach later.

`docs/swarm-command-design.md` records the captured data contract (including that `status` has no `--json` flag and `feed` returns an array) and the rejected alternatives.

## Verification

- `zig build`: clean.
- `zig build test`: 8940 pass, 2 skip, 5 fail. The 5 failures are pre-existing on `main` in `tool_runtime.run_command` and `command_runner` (unrelated shell tests); the branch adds 21 passing tests over the `main` baseline of 8919.
- Real binary, `./zig-out/bin/fx`: drove `/swarm`, `/swarm findings`, and `/swarm <job-id>` against a fake `puppetmaster`; drove all four failure rows above; confirmed `/swarm` appears in the `/help` catalog under Agents.
- E2E: the slash catalog grew from 35 to 36 commands, so this updates the count assertions in 7 tmux-driven files. All of them run green locally: 237 tests, 0 failures (3 skipped for a missing API key).
- `python3 -m unittest scripts.pgso.tests.test_corpus`: OK. No new e2e file, so no corpus classification change.
- `zig fmt --check src/`: clean.

## Note for the reviewer

The catalog count is hardcoded in 7 e2e files (`Commands 35` and `waitForHelpMenu(session, 35)`). Adding any command requires touching all of them. I updated them here rather than changing the helper, but deriving the count once would make the next command a one-line change.

title: Bound PGSO IR outlining memory
body:
## Summary

- Apply the production profile-use pipeline before a deterministic two-way IR split.
- Outline each balanced partition sequentially, relink it, and restore the original private symbol surface.
- Cluster generated IR helpers by hottest profiled caller to preserve startup code-page locality.
- Verify the final IR and fail if outlining changes the binary’s external symbols.

## Why

LLVM 21 crashes during teardown when its IR outliner processes the current fx module as one unit. Splitting the already optimized module keeps each outliner pass below the standard runner’s memory limit while retaining the size optimization. Dense profile-ranked helper placement prevents outlined code from being scattered across cold pages. The training corpus, benchmark candidates, measurement hardware, runtime features, and release safety mode are unchanged.

title: Bug: MCP optional arguments become required, breaking Linear comment tools
body:
## Issue details

fx can connect to the Linear MCP server and read issues, but it cannot call the server's issue-comment tools. The callable schema exposed inside fx causes unrelated optional arguments to be included in the request. Linear then rejects the request before reading or writing a comment.

### Environment

- fx: `0.0.10`
- fx build revision: `1210c2756ea8`
- OS: macOS / Darwin 25.6.0
- Linear server: `Linear MCP` version `1.0.0`
- Negotiated MCP protocol: `2025-11-25`
- Linear tools discovered: `74`
- Transport: HTTP
- Authentication: ready and authenticated

`fx mcp list --connect` reports Linear as healthy:

```text
linear source=profile scope=profile policy=optional transport=http state=ready auth=authenticated
  negotiated_name=Linear MCP negotiated_version=1.0.0 protocol=2025-11-25
  tools=74 resources=0 templates=0 prompts=0 cache=fresh subscription=active
```

### What works

Issue reads work through `mcp_linear_get_issue`. For example, fx successfully retrieved a Linear issue by its human identifier and returned its title, project, status, assignee, description, and linked child issues.

### Reproduction: read issue comments

Run fx with a configured and authenticated Linear MCP server:

```bash
fx ask --auto --json --no-save \
  'Use only the configured Linear MCP. Read-only test: list comments for Linear issue GTMS-5222. Do not create or update anything. If the MCP tool fails, return its exact error and tool name.'
```

fx discovers and calls `mcp_linear_list_comments`, but the call fails:

```text
mcp_linear_list_comments failed.

Error: statusUpdateType is only valid together with statusUpdateId
```

A direct attempt scoped to an issue produces the same server error. The request includes an issue parent plus `statusUpdateType`, even though no status-update parent is being used.

### Reproduction: create an issue comment

The valid Linear request should need only:

```json
{
  "issueId": "GTMS-5222",
  "body": "Test comment from fx — confirming that the fx Linear MCP can create issue comments. Safe to delete."
}
```

Calling `mcp_linear_save_comment` through fx fails before creating the comment:

```text
Error: statusUpdateType is only valid together with statusUpdateId
```

No comment is created.

### Working comparison

Claude Code can call the same Linear MCP server successfully after loading the tool schema. It sends only the relevant fields:

```json
{
  "issueId": "GTMS-5222",
  "body": "Test comment from Claude Code — checking that I can write comments to Linear via MCP. Safe to delete."
}
```

Linear returns a server-assigned comment ID and `createdAt` timestamp. This shows that the server, OAuth identity, issue identifier, and comment operation are valid.

### Expected behavior

fx should preserve optional fields from the MCP tool's JSON Schema. For an issue comment:

- `list_comments` should allow `issueId` without `statusUpdateType` or `statusUpdateId`.
- `save_comment` should allow `issueId` plus `body` without unrelated parent fields.
- Mutually exclusive parent references should not become required together.

### Actual behavior

The executable tool shape presented in fx causes optional sibling fields to be supplied. In particular, `statusUpdateType` is sent without `statusUpdateId`. Linear correctly rejects that invalid combination.

### Impact

Agents running through fx can read Linear issue descriptions but cannot reliably:

- read issue comments;
- create milestone or completion comments;
- use comments as shared context across coordinated worktrees.

This blocks a Linear-first multi-agent workflow even though the MCP connection itself is healthy.

### Sensitive information

- [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.
- No access tokens, server URLs, customer data, or private comment content are included.

title: fix: tolerate finish_reason-less terminal usage trailer in Chat Completions reducer
body:
Some OpenAI-compatible proxies send the trailing usage-only SSE frame as a populated `choices[0]` with an empty `delta` and no `finish_reason` key, instead of an empty `choices: []` array. The reducer's strict `InconsistentFinishReason` check for repeated terminal choices rejected this, breaking plain responses and tool-call turns for configured Chat Completions connections against those proxies.

This tolerates a missing `finish_reason` on an already-finished stream's trailing frame, while still requiring an exact match when it's present, and still rejecting any unexpected delta content on that frame.

Includes a regression test covering both cases.

Example trailer that currently fails (redacted):
```
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":6,"prompt_tokens":8,"total_tokens":14,...}}

data: [DONE]
```

The prior frame already carried `finish_reason:"stop"`; this trailer omits it entirely.

title: qwen-3-32b via Bedrock streams truncated tool-call input, tripping the malformed-arguments limit
body:
## Summary

`alibaba/qwen-3-32b` (routed to `bedrock`) frequently streams tool-call input that is missing its leading `{"`. fx correctly rejects each as malformed, but after three strikes it aborts the turn with exit code 1, so a flaky upstream becomes a hard failure for the user.

## Observed

`fx ask --json --auto --model alibaba/qwen-3-32b --resume-id <sid> "Read note.txt and reply with its contents."`, fx 0.0.10 (main `aef66909` and the #892 branch behave the same). Captured Gateway SSE parts across two runs, six `read_file` attempts:

```
"type":"tool-call","toolCallId":"tooluse_1pnowwnXa4VbWYY35Vpopb","toolName":"read_file","input":"path\": \"note.txt\"}
"type":"tool-call","toolCallId":"tooluse_Bvpum6ewmtlyL7a4O3xTEf","toolName":"read_file","input":"path\": \"note.txt\"}
"type":"tool-call","toolCallId":"tooluse_cVUCYyKY6glm4kfhvIVSKq","toolName":"read_file","input":"path\": \"note.txt\"}
"type":"tool-call","toolCallId":"tooluse_mz7khEoxB9lnjsFk6sN2Fh","toolName":"read_file","input":"path\": \"note.txt\"}
"type":"tool-call","toolCallId":"tooluse_ZgB58WVeo6fqJhHMcrEHel","toolName":"read_file","input":"path\": \"note.txt\"}
"type":"tool-call","toolCallId":"tooluse_gksvuyisahSQYBjlGV9Z9M","toolName":"read_file","input":"{\"path\": \"note.txt\"}
```

Five of six arrive truncated; the matching `tool-input-delta` parts are truncated the same way, so the corruption is upstream of fx (Bedrock or the Gateway's conversion), not in fx's parser. One run recovered on the fourth attempt; the other hit the limit:

```
Repeated malformed tool arguments stopped the agent loop. The invalid calls were not executed. Continue with a follow-up prompt if needed.
```

## Why it matters

The failure is nondeterministic and the model otherwise works, so users see intermittent hard stops on tool turns. Not caused by the system-message layout: it reproduces with both one and seven leading system messages.

## Possible directions

- Report upstream (Gateway routing for `alibaba/qwen-3-32b` via bedrock) with the captured parts.
- Consider whether fx's malformed-argument handling should tolerate more retries for this class of error, or attempt a conservative repair when the payload is valid JSON after prepending `{"`.

Found while investigating #892; raw captures available on request.
