title: deepseek-v3.2 via Bedrock leaks a partial DSML tool-call marker into visible text
body:
## Summary

`deepseek/deepseek-v3.2` (routed to `bedrock`) leaks a partial DeepSeek tool-call marker into the visible assistant text before the actual tool call. The tool call itself works.

## Observed

`fx ask --json --auto --model deepseek/deepseek-v3.2 --resume-id <sid> "Read note.txt and reply with its contents."`, fx 0.0.10 (main `aef66909`). The `output` field of the JSON result:

```
I'll read the note.txt file and reply with its contents.

<｜DSML｜function_calls

The note says: PINEAPPLE-42
```

The Gateway SSE stream carries the marker as ordinary `text-delta` parts, followed by a well-formed `tool-call` part for `read_file`. So the upstream conversion recognises the call but lets the opening fragment of DeepSeek's native `<｜DSML｜function_calls>` wrapper through as text.

## Why it matters

Users see a stray control token in the transcript on every tool turn with this model. Harmless to execution, but it looks like a bug and pollutes saved session history that is replayed on later turns.

## Possible directions

- Report upstream (Gateway conversion for deepseek via bedrock).
- Consider stripping known unbalanced tool-call wrapper fragments (`<｜DSML｜function_calls`, `<tool_call>` without a close) from visible text when a tool call follows in the same step.

Found while investigating #892; raw captures available on request.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: llama-4-maverick via Bedrock rejects every fx request: no tool use in streaming mode
body:
## Summary

`meta/llama-4-maverick` (routed to `bedrock`) rejects every fx request with HTTP 400 because fx always streams and always sends tools. The model is unusable from fx even for a plain text turn.

## Observed

`fx ask --json --auto --model meta/llama-4-maverick "Reply with the single word OK."`, fx 0.0.10 (main `aef66909`). All three turns of a three-turn script (text, tool call, text) fail identically:

```
"error":{"message":"undefined: This model doesn't support tool use in streaming mode.","type":"AI_APICallError","statusCode":400}
```

Routing metadata: `"provider":"bedrock","statusCode":400,"error":"undefined: This model doesn't support tool use in streaming mode."`. The catalog entry for this id advertises the `tool-use` tag.

## Why it matters

The model appears in the picker and looks supported, but every turn fails with an opaque provider error. Not related to the system-message layout.

## Possible directions

- Report upstream: the Gateway could fall back to a non-streaming call for this route, or the catalog should not advertise `tool-use` for routes that cannot stream tool calls.
- In fx, surface this class of error with a clearer message, or hide models whose only route rejects streaming tool use.

Found while investigating #892; raw captures available on request.

title: Add a live Gateway compatibility matrix harness
body:
## Summary

Adds `scripts/gateway_matrix`, a manual investigation tool that drives a built `fx` binary through the same multi-turn `fx ask --json --auto` conversation against a list of Gateway model ids, with a loopback logging proxy between fx and the Gateway. Per request it records the prompt role sequence, the number of leading system messages, the upstream HTTP status, the route the Gateway chose (`providerMetadata.gateway.routing.finalProvider`) and any error body, then prints a per-turn table.

This is the harness that produced the wire evidence in the #892 investigation (Qwen 3.5+ on Fireworks rejecting fx's multi-system layout once assistant history carries reasoning, other routes accepting it). Committing it so the next provider-compatibility question can be answered the same way instead of rebuilt from scratch.

## Scope

- `scripts/gateway_matrix/proxy.py`: threaded loopback proxy. Forwards to the real Gateway unchanged, streams the response back, captures bodies, extracts routing from the finish event. Forwards `Authorization` but never writes it to disk.
- `scripts/gateway_matrix/runner.py`: runs the turns per model, resumes sessions with `--resume-id`, excludes fx's title side-requests from the summary by matching the `ai-language-model-id` header.
- `scripts/gateway_matrix/__main__.py`: CLI. Default output under `zig-out/gateway-matrix/`, which is already gitignored.
- `scripts/gateway_matrix/README.md`: usage, cost warning, how to read results.
- `scripts/tests/test_gateway_matrix.py`: unit tests for the summarisers and table formatting, no network.

Not wired into `zig build test` or CI. Every turn costs real Gateway requests billed to the signed-in account, which is why it stays manual.

## Verification

- `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_gateway_matrix -v`: 7 passed.
- `./scripts/check-public-surface.sh`: clean.
- Live smoke: one turn against `moonshotai/kimi-k3` through the harness produced the expected row (7 leading systems, route `fireworks`, 200, exit 0) and the capture files.
- Live use against the single-system-message fix branch: 3-turn runs for `alibaba/qwen3.8-max`, `moonshotai/kimi-k3` (1 system each, all 200) and `openai/gpt-5.5` (7 systems kept, all 200).

## Draft gates

Required classification: **type: maintenance**. The author has read-only upstream permissions; a maintainer must approve fork workflows.

title: Custom connections: first request to a cold local model always hits the 120s timeout; recovery depends on the server's prompt cache
body:
## Summary

When fx uses a custom model connection pointing at a local Ollama server, the first request after a cold model start always fails with a 120-second timeout. fx retries the identical request, and the retry succeeds only because Ollama's prompt cache, warmed by the failed attempts, makes the next prefill fast enough. On slower hardware, a larger model, or a server without cross-request prompt caching, all 10 attempts would fail and the request would error out after roughly 20 minutes.

## Environment

- fx 0.0.10, dev channel, build `dd0757b5f686`
- macOS on Apple Silicon, Ollama 0.34.0 running on `http://localhost:11434`
- Model: `qwen3.8:27b-mlx`

## Configuration

Connection defined in `~/.fx/settings.json` per the custom model connections guide:

```json
{
  "provider": "ollama",
  "providers": {
    "ollama": {
      "protocol": "openai-chat-completions",
      "base_url": "http://localhost:11434/v1",
      "auth": { "type": "none" },
      "model_metadata": {
        "qwen3.8:27b-mlx": {
          "context_window": 262144,
          "max_output_tokens": 16384,
          "supports_tool_use": true
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "models": { "ollama": "qwen3.8:27b-mlx" }
}
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an Ollama custom connection as above.
2. Unload the model so the next request is cold: `ollama stop qwen3.8:27b-mlx`.
3. Run `fx ask "Reply with only the word pong."`.

## Expected

fx waits for the local server to load the model and read the prompt, then prints the answer.

## Actual

- Attempt 1 times out after exactly 120,012 ms with zero bytes received. Trace: `stream_error err=Timeout cancel_requested=false provider_attempts=1/10 saw_content=false recovery=retry_request`.
- The user sees `Network interrupted · Timeout · retrying request`, which misdiagnoses a healthy loopback server.
- Attempt 2 times out the same way.
- Attempt 3 succeeds, because Ollama's prompt cache, warmed by the failed attempts, makes prefill fast enough to start streaming inside the 120-second window.
- Total wall time: 3m11s for a one-word answer.

## Root cause

- fx sends about 56 KB / 15,000 estimated tokens even for a trivial prompt. Trace: `request_bytes=56805 estimated_tokens=14888`.
- fx's per-attempt wait for the first response content is 120 seconds.
- A cold 27B local model needs about 177 seconds before its first token on this machine. Measured directly with curl using a same-size request: `time_starttransfer=177.1s`, after which the server streams a fully compliant SSE response (`finish_reason: "stop"`, then `data: [DONE]`).
- Once the model is warm, the same fx request completes in 2.2 seconds, so the connection configuration itself is correct.

## Why recovery is fragile

Each retry resends the same 15,000-token prompt, and recovery depends entirely on the server remembering prompts across requests. A server without cross-request prompt caching would fail all 10 attempts and then fail the request outright.

## Suggestions

Any one of these would fix it:

- Add a per-connection timeout field (for example `request_timeout_ms`) to the connection definition.
- Treat "no bytes yet from a loopback server" as the server still working, rather than `transport_interrupted`.
- Document a warm-up requirement for local servers in the custom model connections guide.

## Workaround

Keep the model loaded so the first request stays under 120 seconds: run `ollama run <model>` once before using fx, or start the server with `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1`.

I can share the full fx trace privately if useful.

title: Pool gateway HTTP connections and warm them at launch
body:
## Summary

- Reuse warm keep-alive connections for gateway chat requests instead of opening a fresh connection per request.
- Pre-connect to the AI Gateway in the background at launch, so the first message skips DNS, TCP, and TLS setup entirely.
- Expire pooled connections after 30 s idle and redial transparently; stale connections never surface as request failures.
- Return only cleanly completed streams to the pool; cancelled or failed requests close their connection.
- Cover the interactive shell and fx ask. Codex, Grok, and custom providers are unchanged.
- Add gateway trace events for pool warm, borrow, drain, and stale expiry (FX_TRACE=1 FX_TRACE_SCOPES=gateway).

## Measured impact

Same machine, network, and endpoint (iad1), traced before and after this change:

| path | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| first request after launch | 45-48 ms connect | 0-1 ms (pre-warmed) |
| every later message in a session | 45-48 ms per request | 0-1 ms |
| 10-message session, total handshake time | ~470 ms | ~50 ms (one dial) |
| fx ask "hi" (title + main, 2 requests) | ~92 ms of connect setup | ~44 ms |
| connect outliers on slower networks | up to 1.29 s once observed | 0 ms on pool hits |

The gateway edge confirmed receipt of every request within 14-120 ms of send on both sides of this change, so the saving is entirely the removed per-request handshake. Server-side latency is unchanged and unaffected.

Verified live: scripted interactive sessions show the launch warm completing in 47-60 ms in the background, message 2+ connecting in 0-1 ms, a mid-stream cancellation correctly keeping its connection out of the pool, and a 30+ s idle gap draining and redialing with no user-visible error.

title: Accept provider totals above itemized token counts
body:
## Problem

Some Chat Completions providers report `total_tokens` larger than
`prompt_tokens + completion_tokens`, because they bill template, cache, and
reasoning tokens that the itemized counts do not include.

`accept_usage` required exact equality (`tokens != sum` when both itemized
counts were present), so such a response failed the entire stream with
`InvalidChunk` after content had already been delivered. The turn died with no
usable output even though the response was otherwise well formed.

## Observed

Against a provider on this shape, a plain completion reports:

```
prompt_tokens=26  completion_tokens=2  total_tokens=87
```

The itemized counts are correct for the text; the extra 59 tokens are billed
template/cache overhead the response does not itemize. The equality check
rejected it.

## Change

Treat a reported total as a lower bound: only a total **below** the itemized sum
is a contradiction, which is still rejected.

The carried-progress branch is untouched, so a later itemized sum that overtakes
an already observed total is still rejected, and totals that decrease are still
rejected.

## Tests

- Added a case for a total above the itemized sum being accepted end to end
  (usage preserved, stream finishes).
- Three existing cases that asserted the exact-equality rule were updated to use
  genuinely impossible totals (a total below the itemized sum), so they still
  cover the contradiction they were written for.

Focused suite for the changed file passes.

Required label: `type: bug`

title: Retry a provider stream that violates the wire contract
body:
## Problem

A provider stream that violates the wire contract could not be parsed, a
malformed chunk, an unusable finish reason, or tool arguments that are not a
JSON object, produced no network failure evidence. Model recovery therefore
treated it as a local error and stopped the turn fatally.

The request was sound and the transport was healthy: the fault is transient
provider behavior, and replaying the identical request is the correct recovery.
This matters most on long agent turns, where one bad frame ends a run that had
already done a dozen successful tool calls.

## Change

- `NetworkFailureCause.provider_stream_malformed` is a new cause, distinct from
  `transport_interrupted`.
- `isMalformedProviderStreamError` classifies the protocol errors that mean the
  stream could not be trusted: `InvalidChunk`, `InconsistentFinishReason`,
  `InvalidFinishReason`, `IncompleteStream`, `ConflictingIdentity`,
  `UnexpectedToolCall`, and `InvalidToolCallId` / `InvalidToolName` /
  `InvalidToolArguments`.
- `decide` replays the request from the beginning for this cause rather than
  continuing, because a partial response produced by a malformed stream is not
  trustworthy enough to continue.

## Recovery still refuses to rerun work

- A tool that may have executed reconciles instead of replaying.
- An exhausted attempt budget pauses instead of looping.
- Cancellation always stops.
- Terminal outcomes stay non-retryable by design: `OutputTruncated`,
  `ContentFiltered`, `Refused`, `RequiredToolMissing`, `InvalidToolHistory`.

Both properties are covered by tests added in this change.

## Verification

Beyond the unit tests, this was verified by fault injection rather than by
waiting for a real glitch: a logging proxy in front of the provider injected one
malformed chunk mid-stream, then the same task was run end to end.

Before:

```
err=InvalidChunk recovery=stop replay_safe=false retry=false
```

After:

```
err=InvalidChunk recovery=retry_request replay_safe=true retry=true
cause=provider_stream_malformed  attempts 1/10 -> 2/10
```

The run completed and the tool call succeeded. Reproducing the fault by hammering
the provider did not work (roughly 150 clean turns), which is consistent with an
intermittent fault.

Required label: `type: improvement`

title: Skip the pending prompt preview over the transcript endpoint row
body:
## Summary

- Submitting a long pasted message with a full screen no longer leaves a truncated duplicate of the message's last line in native scrollback.
- Keep the previous turn's summary line through the submit instead of dropping it.
- Keep showing the pending submission preview when there is room below the transcript; defer it only for the one frame where it would overwrite the transcript's last line.

title: Read only top-level frontmatter keys
body:
## Problem

The frontmatter reader scanned every line for a colon and treated the text
before it as a skill key, ignoring indentation. A skill whose frontmatter
carries a nested block was therefore rejected.

A real installed skill demonstrates it. Its frontmatter is:

```yaml
---
name: cua-driver
description: Drive a native GUI app ...
version: 0.22.2
metadata:
  openclaw:
    requires:
      bins:
        - cua-driver
      envVars:
        - name: CUA_DRIVER_EMBEDDED
          required: false
          description: Set to 1 when a macOS host app launches the driver in embedded mode.
        # ... five more entries, each with a nested description
---
```

Every nested `description:` was read as a top-level key, so the skill reported
`duplicate_recognized_key` and silently never loaded. Nothing about the skill is
wrong: YAML top-level keys start at column zero, and those keys are nested inside
`metadata.openclaw.requires.envVars`.

## Change

A top-level YAML key starts at column zero, so treat an indented line as part of
a nested mapping or sequence and skip it instead of reading a key from it.

The existing `unsupported_multiline` diagnostic for an indented continuation
after a recognized key is unchanged, and description blocks (`>`, `>-`, `|`) are
still consumed by the block reader before the line loop sees them.

## Tests

Added a case with a nested `metadata` block containing both a nested
`description:` and a nested `name:`; the skill must load with the top-level name
and description intact.

## Verification

Against the real installed skill, before this change a run reported:

```
candidate ".../skills/cua-driver" was skipped because its metadata is invalid
(duplicate_recognized_key)
```

After this change, the skill loads and appears in the skill list, and the run
reports no discovery diagnostics.

Required label: `type: bug`

title: Persist the workspace file index for instant completion
body:
## Summary

- **6–40x faster to usable @ completions.** On a 907 GB workspace with 972 nested checkouts, `@` results appear about 1.5 s after launch (painted from the persisted index) instead of after a 9–64 s full indexing walk on every launch.
- @-file completion paints from a per-workspace persisted index at launch and is searchable immediately; a background rescan always follows and replaces it.
- The index is written under ~/.fx/file-index/ after each successful scan and is integrity-checked on load; a mismatched or corrupt file falls back to a normal scan.
- A failed rescan keeps the persisted results instead of showing Files unavailable.

title: Add gateway stream timing stats and a reasoning display toggle
body:
## Summary

- Log per-request stream milestones (head_ms, first_reasoning_ms, first_text_ms, first_tool_call_ms), the gateway generation id, and edge correlation headers (x-vercel-id, Date, x-matched-path) in the FX_TRACE gateway and stream scopes.
- Report the last model call's stream milestones and generation id under `stream` in `fx ask --json` output.
- Add `/reasoning [on|off]` and a "Reasoning text" settings entry to show streamed model reasoning as a dim transcript block; hidden by default.

title: Trace the failing provider error at the send site
body:
## Problem

When a provider stream violates the wire contract fx retries it, but the retry
loop records only `cause=network_interrupted`. Once the attempt budget is
exhausted the user sees:

```
⚠ Response ended early · recovery paused after 10/10 attempts
```

with no record of which error the provider actually produced. The failing
session is gone, so the failure is undiagnosable after the fact: the raw stream
that caused it was never written anywhere.

This makes a malformed-stream report impossible to act on. A user can say only
"it failed", not which contract rule the provider broke, so the fix is guesswork
against a provider that cannot be made to reproduce on demand.

## Change

Log the failing error name, whether it is retryable, and the recovery evidence
cause at the request send site, where the error is already being classified for
recovery:

```
[gateway] provider_failure err=InvalidChunk retryable=true evidence=provider_stream_malformed
```

The error name is the only evidence of what the provider actually sent, and the
retry loop otherwise discards it.

## Verification

Driving a real turn through a loopback proxy that injects one malformed chunk
into an otherwise valid stream, with `FX_TRACE=1`:

```
[notice] ⚠ Response ended early · InvalidChunk · retrying request · attempt 1/10
[notice] ⚠ Response ended early · InvalidChunk · retrying request · attempt 2/10
[notice] ✓ recovered · succeeded on attempt 2/10

1789564301449 [gateway] provider_failure err=InvalidChunk retryable=true evidence=provider_stream_malformed
```

Before this change the same run produced no trace line naming the error.

Required label: `type: improvement`

title: Accept a trailing delta after the terminal frame
body:
## Problem

A provider may emit the assistant's trailing text **after** it has already declared
`finish_reason`, in a frame that carries no `finish_reason` field of its own.
This is **deterministic** for a given request — the same bytes produce the same
frame every time.

The reducer rejected it with `InconsistentFinishReason` at line 610:

```zig
const reason = try string(non_null(choice, "finish_reason") orelse
    return error.InconsistentFinishReason);
```

so the missing field on an otherwise-complete response killed the turn. A retry
then reproduced the identical offending frame and exhausted the attempt budget
with the same error — the turn could never succeed.

## Root cause captured

The `fp_fusion_deepseek_v4_1_flash` backend on Surplus emits a trailing content
frame without a `finish_reason`:

```
[28] {"finish_reason":"tool_calls"}         -> phase = .finished
[29] {"choices":[],"usage":{...}}            -> usage frame
[30] {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Found it..."}}]}   <- NO finish_reason field
[31] {"choices":[],"usage":{...}}
[32] [DONE]
```

Frame [30] is not a contradiction — it is a late delta.

## Change

A post-finish frame **without** a `finish_reason` is a late delta: accept its
content and reasoning and let the turn complete. A post-finish frame that
**does** carry a `finish_reason` is still validated, and a mismatched one
still produces `InconsistentFinishReason`.

## Proof

Byte-for-byte replay of the captured stream that previously failed (all five
runs on the unpatched build):

```
unpatched:  InconsistentFinishReason ×2  → "recovered on attempt 2/10"  (needed retry)
patched:    exit 0, InconsistentFinishReason ×0 → completed first try, text kept
```

Required label: `type: bug`

title: Add custom TUI themes from ~/.fx/themes with VS Code theme support
body:
## Summary

- Load custom TUI themes from `~/.fx/themes/<name>.json` with `FX_THEME=<name>`.
- Accept the VS Code theme format (`colors` and `tokenColors`), so editor themes like Cursor Dark or GitHub Dark apply directly, including TextMate scope syntax colors with bold and italic.

title: Add Labs status badges to README
body:
## Summary - Add **LABS PRODUCT** using Shields for-the-badge styling and fixed black labels. - Keep the badges inline in a single HTML paragraph: category, version/release, license, then monthly npm downloads where verified. Small screens wrap naturally; no forced line breaks. - Preserve the existing README content and useful badges. No code, package, release, or repository-archive changes. ## Preview

` breaks. - Browser layout: badges share one horizontal row at 1000px; 390px mobile layout wraps without viewport overflow. title: Escalate repeated identical tool failures
body:
## Summary

- A zero-occurrence `edit_file` failure now tells the agent to re-read the file and not retry when the change is already applied, instead of returning a bare not-found message.
- The second and later identical failing tool calls in one turn append an explicit do-not-retry-unchanged escalation to the model-visible result, so a model cannot loop on an already-applied edit for dozens of steps without being told to stop.
- Malformed-argument rejections keep their existing hard-stop path and never escalate through the new tracker.
- `/trace` and `fx ask --json` record tool failures that ran the tool's preflight or content checks, including permission-stage prepare failures, as `tool_failed` instead of `rejected`; genuine denials keep the `rejected` label.

title: Submit small MCP select-one forms directly
body:
MCP forms with one select-one field and at most three options now submit directly from the terminal prompt. Text inputs, numbers, booleans, multi-selects, and larger forms retain a separate Submit/Edit review step. Decline, Cancel, defaults, and optional-field skipping remain available.

Validation: ReleaseSafe build, all 28 focused form-handler tests, and six deterministic terminal tests passed using the freshly built `./zig-out/bin/fx`. The terminal checks cover direct choice submission, short-input review, boolean review, operation timeouts, resource/prompt continuation, and HTTP transport. Formatting, the public-surface audit, and PGSO corpus classification checks passed.

Full CI and the final ship gate must pass for the current commit before this PR is marked ready.

title: Make the auto-mode reviewer model configurable
body:
## Summary

- Add a profile-owned `review_model` setting (`~/.fx/settings.json`) with `FX_REVIEW_MODEL` as the process override, selecting the model behind automatic auto-mode permission reviews. Default reviewer is unchanged when unset.
- `review_model: "typesafeai/jev"` (or the gateway spelling `typesafe-ai/jev`) routes each review to TypeSafe's Jev evaluation model, which returns a typed clear/caution decision with calibrated probabilities and a confidence score recorded in the rationale and trace.
- Jev is reached through the gateway's `/v4/ai/evaluation-model` endpoint with the session's gateway credential; setting `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` talks to TypeSafe's API directly instead.
- Any other value keeps the gateway chat review path and sends that model id, so reviews can run on any AI Gateway chat model.
- Hold actions unexecuted when the selected reviewer is unavailable (missing credentials, endpoint failure), matching existing unavailable-reviewer behavior.

The override resolves through normal config layering (env > profile settings; project `.fx.json` rejects it as profile-owned) and flows through interactive, ask, ACP, and subagent review paths via the shared tool context.

## Test plan

- `zig build test`: settings parse/merge/env-override coverage, project-config rejection, gateway transport model-override test, Jev model-id matching, route resolution (direct vs gateway, derived evaluation URL), loopback gateway transport asserting path, auth, and protocol headers.
- `tests/e2e/review-model-override.test.ts`: env override to Jev direct, settings override to Jev, gateway evaluation path when no direct key (asserts endpoint, model id, auth), generic chat-model override, default unchanged, failing-endpoint hold.
- Live binary: `fx ask --auto` with the env override and with settings-only override both reached Jev (direct) and executed a cleared action; a settings override to another gateway chat model reviewed through that model; default run used the unchanged default reviewer; TUI session via tmux routed its review to Jev. The gateway evaluation path is covered by loopback unit tests and fake-gateway e2e; live verification needs a gateway account with the typesafe-ai provider enabled.

title: Restore themed inline code across streamed blocks and unify tool labels
body:
## Summary

- Keep theme-supplied inline-code colors intact across streamed blocks: the pacer now recognizes the active theme's inline-code open instead of only the two builtin grays, so an interleaved reset no longer drops the rest of a code span to default text.
- Render every tool activity label (Ran, Searching, Fetching, Converting, and similar) from one themed tool-text slot, restoring the exact pre-theme default grays on light terminals.
- Pin the variant rules with deterministic e2e coverage: sibling swap on a mismatched terminal, builtin fallback when no sibling file exists, and rejection of a sibling whose declared variant also mismatches.

title: Install the Slack workspace bot through the CLI
body:
Install the fx Slack workspace bot from the CLI while retaining Slack's required HTTPS redirect and PKCE. `fx slack install` generates state and a verifier in memory, receives the HTTPS bridge's loopback form POST, exchanges the code directly with Slack, and validates the configured app/workspace, exact bot scope, and `auth.test` identity before saving credentials.

The installer owns an atomic, owner-only local credential file. `fx slack status [--json]` reports metadata; `fx slack refresh` rotates credentials under the same local lock. Refresh accepts omitted response metadata only when the refreshed bot identity still matches. No Redis service, shared installation endpoint, maintainer password, or background refresh service is introduced. Existing employee MCP user authorization and credentials remain separate.

Requires the stateless bridge in [fx-web #108](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx-web/pull/108). Keep the existing localhost redirect for employee MCP login. The bridge must be deployed and configured before this command works with Slack. Live installation, mentionability, and hoverable “Sent using @fx” attribution are still unverified; test attribution with the existing user-token MCP connection before rollout.

Validation: local build and formatting, 8 deterministic CLI E2E tests, focused Zig callback/runtime tests, 2 existing MCP callback regressions, and a separate fresh-binary happy-path run against local mocked Slack endpoints. The companion bridge was exercised in Chrome through an HTTPS redirect chain and HTTP loopback POST. The new E2E owner is classified as verification-only in the PGSO corpus. Full CI for this commit is pending.

title: Close recovery follow-ups on cancel clears, labels, and draft safety
body:
## Summary

- Cancelling a turn during recovery now clears its durable checkpoint on every cancel path, so the next resume no longer revives a turn the user stopped.
- Recovery labels drop the removed attempt budget: terminal stops read "stopped after 3 attempts" instead of "stopped after 3/10 attempts", with the same sweep across paused and recovered banners.
- A stall-stopped turn no longer replaces a draft typed into the composer mid-retry; a new end-to-end test pins the occupied-composer case.
- Internal tidy-up: one shared NTP-safe elapsed-time helper replaces three copies, paused and terminal labels share one cause display-name mapping, and a dead attempt helper is removed.

Stacked on #879.

title: Add a persisted theme key to settings.json
body:
## Summary

- Select a TUI theme persistently with the `theme` key in `~/.fx/settings.json` (for example `"cursor-dark"`, matching a file in `~/.fx/themes/`); no environment variable needed.
- Accept `"light"` and `"dark"` in the key to pin a built-in variant; `FX_THEME` still wins when set.
- The key is profile-owned: project `.fx.json` ignores it with a diagnostic.
- Settings-selected custom themes follow the terminal's light or dark mode with the same sibling swap, built-in fallback, and live re-resolution as env-selected themes.

Stacked on #917.

title: Speed up session resume with a binary replay cache
body:
## Summary

- Resuming a session now replays a per-session binary cache of its event log instead of parsing the full JSONL twice, cutting a 266MB session's writable resume from about 2.7s to about 1.1s.
- The cache builds during the first writable resume and extends at each open; a corrupt, torn, or stale cache degrades to a prefix splice or a full log replay.
- Legacy sessions gain a cache at migration; fresh sessions keep the minimal durable footprint until their first resume.

title: Slim README into a starter guide
body:
## Summary

- Add a highlights list so the top of the page carries the key product points.
- Keep install, sign-in, and first-request steps as the starter path.
- Replace in-README reference material for custom model connections, themes, compaction, and automatic tool review with a one-line pointer to the fx.sh documentation, matching the shape of Vercel's other open-source READMEs.
- Point agents at the Markdown mirror of every docs page and the combined llms-full.txt file.
- Add a security disclosure note.
- Drop the exact binary size from the intro; it drifted with every release.

title: Say esc to pause during connectivity waits
body:
## Summary

- The connectivity-wait hint now reads "esc to pause", matching what the key does: it parks the turn and the checkpoint auto-continues on the next resume. Previously it read "esc to stop" while doing neither.

Stacked on #919.

title: Make Ctrl+C exit immediate during background work
body:
## Summary

- Exit promptly on double Ctrl+C while an auto-upgrade check or download is in flight, instead of waiting on the network transfer.
- Exit promptly when a local MCP server ignores shutdown, instead of waiting out per-server grace timeouts.
- Exit promptly while MCP servers are still connecting during startup.
- Keep the single-press cancel and double-press exit gestures unchanged.

title: Connect subagent statusline continuation with vertical pipe
body:
When subagents run inside a grouped tool call, their secondary statusline row was always being indented with two plain spaces. For intermediate rows (`├`), this left a gap in the tree instead of continuing the branch down with a `│` pipe.

Now, non-terminal rows use `│ ` so the tree connects properly, while the last row (`└`) continues to use `  ` indentation.

#### Before

```text
● 4 tool calls · 4 subagent
├ Subagent working · Run task
  glm-5.3-flash · max
├ Subagent working · Run task
  glm-5.3-flash · max
├ Subagent working · Run task
  glm-5.3-flash · max · 15k/1000k 1%
└ Subagent working · Run task
  glm-5.3-flash · max · 15k/1000k 1%
```

#### After

```text
● 4 tool calls · 4 subagent
├ Subagent working · Run task
│ glm-5.3-flash · max
├ Subagent working · Run task
│ glm-5.3-flash · max
├ Subagent working · Run task
│ glm-5.3-flash · max · 15k/1000k 1%
└ Subagent working · Run task
  glm-5.3-flash · max · 15k/1000k 1%
```

title: Name the unresolved path in tool preflight failures
body:
## Summary

- Permission preflight failures for unresolvable tool paths now name the exact path argument with a plain reason, such as "Path not found: fx/src/core/tool_specs.zig", instead of "Permission target resolution failed for <tool>: <error>".
- Missing-path, not-a-directory, access-denied, and outside-workspace failures each get specific wording; other resolution errors keep the precise error name.
- The same text is returned to the model as the tool result and shown in the transcript, so agents can fix the path and retry without user help.

title: Surface model catalog failures in /trace reports
body:
## Summary

- The /trace report gains a Model Catalog section with catalog cache state, the selected model's resolved capabilities, and recent catalog load, capability lookup, and image rejection events, captured without FX_TRACE.
- Failed catalog loads, capability lookup misses, and rejected image submissions now appear under Problems instead of "no obvious errors captured".

title: Use GitHub theme names in theme documentation examples
body:
## Summary

- README and theme module docs now reference `github-dark` and `github-light`, the canonical VS Code theme pair, instead of other editor theme names.

title: Retry permission review on transport failure
body:
## Summary

- Safety reviews in auto mode now retry once when the reviewer call fails with a transport timeout, a transient transport error, or a failed connection, using a fresh 30-second deadline for the retry.
- Actions are held with Review unavailable only after the retry also fails; a recovered review clears the action normally.
- Permanent transport failures and cancellations still never retry, and each exact action still spends at most one unavailable review opportunity per turn.

title: Keep the native-clear probe off while an alternate screen is active
body:
## Summary

Typing any printable character while the ctrl+o full transcript (or any alternate-screen surface) is open started the native-clear probe with the main-grid footer row as the expected cursor position. The terminal answers the cursor query from the alternate screen, so the row never matched, and fx treated it as a native terminal clear (Cmd+K): the visible transcript reset to the welcome banner, making the chat look wiped until the session was resumed.

The probe now refuses to begin while an alternate-screen owner is active.

## Root cause

`nativeClearProbeEligible` gated on prompts, paste, pending actions, and resize lifecycle, but not on alternate-screen ownership. Keystrokes typed inside ctrl+o fall through to the composer, so they pass through probe eligibility first; with the alt screen owning the cursor, the expected row (main-grid footer) and the observed row (alt screen) never match.

## Reproduction

1. Run fx in a real terminal (not tmux, which disables the probe).
2. Complete a turn, then open ctrl+o.
3. Type any letter (it falls through to the composer while browsing).
4. Close ctrl+o: the transcript has reset to the welcome banner. Session data is intact; resume restores it.

## Tests

- New E2E in `tui-native-clear-recovery.test.ts`: typing inside ctrl+o issues no new probe request, no mismatch, no recovery, and the byte still lands in the composer. Verified it fails without the fix.
- Existing native-clear recovery tests unchanged and passing.

title: Reduce binary overhead in MCP and compaction diagnostics
body:
## Summary

- Reduce the ordinary macOS arm64 ReleaseSafe binary by 16,416 bytes.
- Preserve MCP elicitation behavior while using fewer temporary allocations.
- Preserve compaction `/trace` output while lowering diagnostic stack use.

title: Syntax-highlight shell commands in tool call rows
body:
## Summary

- Shell commands in tool call rows (Running, Ran, Timed out, Cancelled) highlight quoted strings, numbers, comments, and shell keywords using the active theme's syntax palette.
- The action label, connector, and untokenized text keep the row's ambient color; commands without highlightable tokens render byte-identical to before.
- The syntax highlighter moved from ui/render_engine to core/agent/presentation so the transcript projection and the tool-action composer share it.

title: Normalize root search paths in file evidence
body:
## Summary

- Root-scoped `grep_files` and `glob_files` calls with an omitted or empty search path now record `.` in the turn's file evidence instead of an empty path, which failed conversation-event validation and exited fx when the completed turn was saved.
- `read_file`, `write_file`, and `edit_file` calls with an empty path no longer record file evidence.

Closes #779. Carries the patch from #781 unchanged; that branch could not merge because its commit is unsigned.

title: Keep the session alive when a finished turn fails to save
body:
## Summary

- A completed turn that fails session persistence no longer exits fx after the response renders: the turn stays in memory, a session notice names the failure, and the error is latched for shutdown reporting.
- Conversation-event validation rejections now log the exact rejected rule (for example `file-path`) to the trace log, so diagnostic reports identify the failing invariant without including contents.

Fixes #849.

title: Trace per-stage shutdown timing in FX_TRACE_LOG
body:
## Summary

- Log each interactive shutdown stage with step and total milliseconds under the shutdown trace scope, so a slow exit names the stage that caused it.
- Log when the double Ctrl+C exit gesture activates.

title: Give every model the ten-minute stream stall window
body:
## Summary

- Give every model the same ten-minute mid-stream stall window before a gateway stream is declared dead.
- Remove the model-name stall classification, so newer long-thinking models (for example gpt-6-astra at high effort) no longer get killed after sixty seconds of post-header silence and retried into the same stall in a loop.

title: Show session totals and window coverage in /trace reports
body:
## Summary

- The /trace network section now prints session-wide call totals (count, ok, errors, total model time) alongside the existing recent-window stats, which previously described only the last 32 calls while reading as session-wide.
- The /trace network section gains a per-turn rollup listing calls, errors, model time, subagent calls, and start time per turn.
- The /trace tool section now prints session-wide outcome totals and total tool time alongside the existing last-64 window.
- Both sections now state whether the retained window covers the whole session or only its tail, pointing at the session directory for earlier history.

title: Reduce diagnostic event storage
body:
## Summary

- Preserve compaction and model-catalog diagnostic output with typed event names.
- Reduce always-on diagnostic storage and generated release code.

title: Add opt-in Jev extractive compaction
body:
Jev provides an opt-in extractive compaction path for older fx tool results. With `FX_EXPERIMENT_JEV_COMPACTION=1`, fx retains selected results verbatim, preserves user text and retrievable originals, and falls back to the existing summarizer when evaluation or handoff validation fails. Normal model selection is unchanged.

This PR contains only the native evaluation transport, compaction behavior, documentation and deterministic tests. Native routing at prompt and subagent assignment boundaries is a separate PR. Harbor adapters, policies and benchmark binaries have been removed from this PR's diff.

Validation: local ReleaseSafe build; focused native Jev/compaction tests; three built-binary E2E cases, including terminal compaction and continuation with retrievable originals (92 assertions); Linux x86_64 musl cross-build; formatting and public-surface checks. Exact-current-commit Full CI is required before readiness.

Live Jev testing remains blocked by HTTP 403. Read-only inspection found TypeSafe AI disabled in the Vercel team's provider allowlist; the current account cannot change it. No quality, latency or cost improvement is claimed. Evaluation usage is logged separately and billing can remain incomplete when no generation identity is returned.

title: Add Jev routing for prompts and subagent assignments
body:
Add native Jev routing for each new user prompt and each assignment to an idle automatic subagent. With `--model jev/auto`, the shared fx runtime classifies the current assignment using bounded role, objective and recent-conversation context, then selects an eligible model. The selected model stays fixed through tool calls, normal retries and busy-child steering. CLI, interactive and ACP sessions use the same path.

`FX_EXPERIMENT_JEV_SUBAGENT_ROUTING=1` enables automatic creation defaults for unspecified child models independently of the parent. Concrete model choices bypass classification. Persistent automatic children reroute on their next idle assignment; pinned children remain pinned. Recovery, resumed-session fallback and manual compaction preserve the selected model. Chosen models also reach model-specific prompts, replay projection and delegated search.

The frozen policy selects Luna, Kimi or Sol using a 12-family taxonomy and a routine/general/demanding rubric. Live capabilities and an optional model allowlist constrain selection. Uncertainty, invalid answers or evaluator failure retain the previous eligible routed model, otherwise Kimi; no eligible fallback fails the assignment. The bounded evaluation transport uses the current Gateway credential/team and respects cancellation. This is an unvalidated requirements heuristic, not a learned model-success predictor or managed Gateway router.

Each routing boundary records origin, model, policy, probabilities, latency, usage and fallback reason. Saved routing metadata supports continuity after restart; those experimental sessions require a build that understands it. The standalone JavaScript Gateway example remains available, while native fx requires no Node runtime. Compaction and hosted benchmark infrastructure are separate diffs.

Validation: local ReleaseSafe build and focused native routing, session-codec and manual-compaction tests; deterministic built-binary CLI, terminal, ACP, child-assignment, explicit-model, fallback and restart tests; standalone JavaScript tests; Linux x86_64 musl cross-build; formatting, public-surface and PGSO classification checks. The combined experiment also tests long tool history, extractive compaction and subsequent rerouting. Exact-current-commit Full CI and the final ship gate remain required before readiness.

Live Jev testing remains blocked by HTTP 403; TypeSafe AI is disabled in the Vercel team's provider allowlist and needs an authorized team owner to enable access. No benchmark improvement is claimed. Evaluation billing remains incomplete when no normal generation identity is returned.

title: Read image files with read_file
body:
## Summary

- read_file attaches PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP images up to the 3.9MB attach limit to its result so vision-capable models receive the pixels inline, and larger images report the limit instead of a generic binary omission.
- Custom Chat Completions providers whose connection declares supports_vision: true now receive tool images and user-attached images as image_url content parts; images from denied tool calls are never sent.
- Models without inline image input keep receiving no pixels, but the withheld notice now explains why and what to do instead: the vision tool for non-native models, or a retry or user attachment when support is unconfirmed.
- A one-time notice tells the user when tool images are withheld because the model catalog is unavailable.
- read_tool_result now states that stored images are sent only when the model accepts image input instead of implying they were delivered.
- The read_file tool description no longer tells models it reads only UTF-8 text.

title: Show the last shutdown breakdown in /trace
body:
## Summary

- Record each interactive exit's per-stage timing to a small diagnostics file, so a slow shutdown is visible without enabling the trace log.
- Render a Last Shutdown section in the /trace report with the total and per-stage milliseconds from the previous exit.

title: Reduce trace rollup sorting overhead
body:
## Summary

- Preserve /trace network turn ordering and recent-window selection.
- Reduce binary size and speed up bounded turn-rollup snapshots.

title: Color shell operators and variables in command rows
body:
## What

Extends the shell profile in the syntax highlighter so `&`, `|`, `;`, `<`, `>` runs and `$name`-style variables take the keyword color. Compound commands in tool rows now read at their seams: `cd /tmp && echo $HOME | head -2` colors the verbs, `&&`, `|`, and `$HOME` in the theme's keyword color while paths and labels stay in the row base.

The operator set and the `$` variable rule live on the language profile, so only `sh` picks them up; other languages are byte-identical. Themes that set `syntax: false` still pass everything through, and the four `syntax` slots keep controlling the colors.

## Verification

- `zig build test` — 9210 tests green locally.
- New unit coverage: operator runs, `$HOME`/`$?`, bare `$` stays plain, `$` inside quotes keeps the string color, non-shell languages untouched.
- Existing styled-byte tests re-pinned for the operator color.
- Live tmux run against a custom theme: `cd`, `&&`, `echo`, `|`, `head` in the theme keyword color, `2` in the number color, row base intact.

title: Resolve subagent model overrides against the model catalog
body:
## Summary

- Subagent `model` overrides are matched against the gateway model catalog before a child session is created, in the TUI, `fx ask`, and ACP sessions: exact and unambiguous partial names (for example `terra-fast`) resolve to the canonical catalog ID.
- Unknown or ambiguous override names are rejected immediately with `unknown_model` or `ambiguous_model` and the closest catalog candidate IDs, instead of spawning a child session that fails after a wasted gateway request.
- Only substring-level matches resolve; weaker token or subsequence paraphrases surface as suggestions, and overrides for configured non-gateway providers pass through unchanged.
- The subagent tool schema documents that `model` expects a catalog model ID.

title: Color dash flags as units in shell commands
body:
## What

Extends the shell highlighter so a dash at a word boundary opens a flag token — `-8`, `--json`, `-q` — colored as a single unit in the number color. Previously `tail -8` rendered a plain dash with a colored `8`.

Dashes inside words (path date suffixes like `build-20260918`) stay plain, a lone `-` stdin marker stays plain, and the rule is gated on the shell profile so other languages are byte-identical. `syntax: false` themes still pass everything through.

## Verification

- `zig build test` — 9235 tests green locally.
- New unit coverage: single/double-dash flags, flags after pipes, lone dash, non-shell languages.
- Existing styled-byte tests re-pinned (`-80`, `-C`, `--short`, `-c` now color as units).
- Live tmux run: `ls README.md | tail -8 && echo --json ok` shows `-8` and `--json` as single colored units, verbs and operators in the keyword color, paths plain.

title: Reduce permission migration sort overhead
body:
## Summary

- Preserve schema-1 permission migration ordering and idempotence.
- Reduce binary size, migration time, and peak stack use.

title: Match the bash grammar's command scoping in tool rows
body:
## What

Aligns shell command highlighting with the bash grammar's scoping (verified against syntect's bundled grammar, the same one codex's TUI uses):

- **Command position colors any command word.** `gh`, `bun`, `sleep`, `rg` — every first word after the start, `&&`/`||`/`|`/`;`/`&`, `$(`, a backtick, or a control keyword takes the keyword color. Argument-position words stay plain (`xargs echo` leaves `echo` plain), as do redirect targets.
- **Bare number arguments no longer color.** `sleep 5` and run ids like `35397045604` stay plain; the grammar scopes only file descriptors glued to a redirect (`2>&1`), and so do we. Flags (`-8`, `--json`) keep the number color.
- **Grammar-shaped expansions:** `${VAR}` braced variables, `~` home paths, glob `*`, `$(` opening command position for its contents, backtick spans parsed as code instead of one flat string, and `$VAR`/`${VAR}` interpolated inside double quotes.
- The fixed verb list is gone from the shell profile; command position covers it.
- Rows without a recorded action label (legacy sessions, denials, timeouts) fall back to known multi-word status labels before the first-space split, so "Denied by auto agent zig build" highlights `zig`, not `by`.

Other languages are untouched; `syntax: false` themes still pass through.

## Verification

- `zig build test` — 9239 tests green locally, including 4 new parity tests (command position, fd-only numbers, expansions, quote interpolation) and re-pinned byte fixtures across the transcript suite.
- Live tmux proof under a custom theme: `gh run watch 35397045604 --exit-status 60 > /tmp/x.log 2>&1; echo "bye $USER" | head -2` — verbs/operators teal, flags and fds yellow, the run id and `60` plain, paths plain.

title: Fix tool image delivery crashes and gateway visibility
body:
## Summary

- Fix a crash when a model reads two or more images in one turn; the process could segfault while building the next request.
- Deliver images that tools read so vision models actually receive them through the gateway; previously the pixels were silently dropped, so models reported an attached image they could not see.
- Subagents now recognize image-capable gateway models instead of reporting that image support could not be confirmed.

title: Cover markdown, text, and diff fences plus more common languages
body:
## What

- **Markdown fences** color inline code spans (string slot) and `<!-- -->` comments; prose numbers stay plain.
- **Text fences** (`text`, `txt`, `plain`, `plaintext`) get an explicit plain profile, so they render byte-identical instead of falling through.
- **Diff and patch fences** paint line-wise with the theme's own added/removed marker colors: `+` lines green, `-` lines red, `@@` hunks in the keyword color, file headers in the comment color. Bare fences whose content looks like a unified diff (`diff --git`, `---`/`+++`, `@@`) are detected as patches. The theme's `syntax: false` switch disables this like everything else.
- **New profiles:** make, ini/conf, dotenv, graphql, dart, scala, elixir, haskell, perl, r, groovy/gradle, and nginx, with tight keyword lists in the existing style. Existing profiles pick up `shellscript` (sh), `m`/`mm` (c), and `vue`/`svelte` (html) aliases.

## Size

+16,528 bytes ReleaseSafe against current main (10,835,248 → 10,851,776), well under the binary-size warning threshold.

## Verification

- `zig build test` — 9244 tests green, including new coverage for the diff painter, text byte-identity, markdown inline code, alias resolution, and diff detection.
- Live tmux proof: a `diff` fence renders `- old` in the theme removed color and `+ new` in the added color; a markdown fence colors `inline code`; a haskell fence colors strings.

title: Share arena teardown across runtime paths
body:
## Summary

- Preserve arena lifetimes and release ordering while sharing teardown code across runtime paths.
- Reduce generated code without changing features, output, or persisted formats.

title: Harden tool result memory copies against partial allocation failure
body:
## Summary

- Fix a failure path in the tool result memory deep copy where a mid-copy allocation failure would free memory still owned by the caller's source value.
- Parallel tool execution now keeps review feedback and file presentations when duplicating tool result memory, and frees copied file presentations during attempt teardown.
- Add an allocation-failure sweep test covering every failure point of the copy.

title: Add a theme link color and split function, variable, operator slots
body:
## What

**Link colors.** Markdown links render in the theme's link color on top of the existing underline and OSC 8 clickability. Native themes set `colors.link`; VS Code themes map `textLink.foreground`; the builtins default to a link blue (`38;5;75` dark, `38;5;25` light).

**Finer syntax slots.** The syntax palette splits `function`, `variable`, and `operator` out of `keyword`: command words read the function slot, `$VAR`/`${VAR}`/`~` read variable, and `&&`/`|`/redirects/globs read operator, while control keywords keep keyword. Native themes set them under `syntax`; VS Code themes map `entity.name.function`, `variable`, and `keyword.operator` scopes. Builtin defaults equal the keyword color, so default rendering is byte-identical to before.

**Row-start fix.** A link that opens an answer row lost its color at the row-start restore: pre-content escapes are not copied verbatim into guttered rows, and the SGR tracker only knew attributes and the inline-code color. It now tracks the themed link color the same way, so a leading link keeps its color. (Found via a live repro where a one-line link answer rendered underline-only.)

## Verification

- `zig build test` — 9255 green, including new coverage: native and VS Code mapping of `link` plus the three split slots, builtin byte pins, a custom-theme slot-split highlighter test, pacer link tracking, and a guttered-row link test.
- New deterministic e2e in the classified gateway-stream file: a markdown link that opens the answer row keeps `38;5;75` and the underline.
- Live tmux proof under a custom theme: the answer link renders in the theme's `textLink.foreground`.

title: Reduce session codec cleanup overhead
body:
## Summary

- Preserve session decoding and recovery behavior while sharing typed cleanup paths.
- Reduce generated code without changing session schemas or persisted data.

title: Generate session titles after resuming an untitled session
body:
## Summary

- Resuming a session with no committed history no longer caches the "Untitled session" placeholder as a real title, so the first prompt after an upgrade relaunch generates a session title.
- The first committed turn no longer persists the fallback placeholder as the session title when the turn has no usable prompt text.

title: Remove never-wired diagnosticsDir path helper
body:
## Summary

- Remove `diagnosticsDir` from profile_paths.zig. The /trace last-shutdown breakdown added it alongside the diagnostics directory constant, but no caller ever arrived: the helper has had exactly one reference since introduction, its own declaration. The live paths use `diagnostics_dir_name` and `lastShutdownReportPath` directly. No user-facing behavior change.

title: Tell the model when MCP server availability changes mid-session
body:
## Summary

- Show the model an explicit note when an MCP server's availability changes mid-session, so answers stop repeating earlier claims that a server is unauthenticated or unavailable after the user authenticates it.
- List each changed server with its previous and current availability and tool count.
- Cover availability changes from reloads, recoveries, and failures, not only authentication.
- Stay silent during startup discovery and on turns where nothing changed.

title: Fix recovery checkpoint races on cancel and unclean exit
body:
## Summary

- Sending a message right after interrupting a response no longer fails with InvalidRecoveryCheckpoint; fx waits for the interrupted turn to finish closing, then sends.
- Resuming a session after a crash or kill no longer restarts a recovering turn on its own; fx explains the state and waits for the user to retry with "continue" or move on.

title: Classify MCP server status once for every surface
body:
## Summary

- Servers that need authentication now show `status=needs_auth` with the real server name in the `/mcp auth` hint across `/mcp list`, the menu, and trace reports, replacing the literal `<name>` placeholder that shipped before.
- Trace reports separate "needs authentication" from "failed" in the Problems section instead of listing every unauthenticated server as failed.
- The health summary, startup gating, model catalog, and capability search now classify servers with one shared rule, so the model and the UI stop disagreeing about the same server.
- Capability search offers its authentication guidance whenever an auth challenge is on record, even if the connection state is no longer marked failed.
- A disabled server that also needs authentication now reports as disabled until it is enabled, instead of asking for credentials first.

Stacked on #960.

title: Announce MCP servers that need attention when startup settles
body:
## Summary

- Post one summary notice after startup discovery settles when any server needs authentication or failed to connect, so broken MCP setup is visible immediately instead of only inside /mcp or a trace report.
- Name the first actionable command, such as `Run /mcp auth linear --open`, using the shared status classification.
- Show nothing on healthy startups, and fire once per process rather than on every health refresh.

Stacked on #962.

title: Fix phantom compaction from tool image request estimates
body:
## Summary

Retained tool images were priced as text by the pre-flight request estimator, causing automatic compaction to fire at a fraction of the real context window. A session carrying ~3.4MB of retained tool images measured ~943k estimated input tokens against ~105k provider-reported tokens and compacted at a tenth of the window.

Two root causes, both fixed:

1. **Estimator gate was blind to tool images.** `measureProviderRequest` only detected user-pasted attachments (`message.images`, `verified_images`), but retained tool images serialize through `tool_result_memory.tool_images` — as follow-up user-message `file` parts on the vercel protocol and as `input_image` parts inside `function_call_output` items on the responses protocol family. The gate now reads the same field the serializers read, the parser covers both envelopes, and unrecognized envelopes degrade to the conservative text estimate instead of failing the request.
2. **Usage calibration reset every turn.** `request_token_calibration` was a per-turn local, so the first request of every turn fell back to the raw byte estimate. It now lives on the agent (model-keyed, cleared on compaction install and history clear), so turn-start requests calibrate from the previous turn's exact provider usage.

## Verification

- `zig fmt --check src/` clean; `zig build` clean; `zig build test` green on the final tree.
- New regression tests: tool images priced as image input (vercel envelope), responses-protocol `function_call_output` payloads excluded, unknown-envelope degradation, calibration surviving `startTurn` and dying with cleared history, plus a gateway-flow test that measures a real serialized body carrying retained tool images.
- Mutation checks: removing the gate fails all three estimator tests; clearing calibration in `startTurn` fails the agent test; removing the `function_call_output` parse branch fails the responses test.
- Runtime repro pair on the assembled binary (same fixture, same model): base build compacted with `estimated_tokens=1179738` at ~28k real tokens; this build measured the same body at 29,892 tokens, no compaction, and turn 2 calibrated from prior usage (`prior_input_tokens=28324`).

title: Mark rejected MCP credentials as needing re-authentication
body:
## Summary

- A server whose stored OAuth credentials are rejected at refresh now reports `status=needs_auth` / `auth=required` with the `/mcp auth <name> --open` hint, instead of showing `failed` while still claiming `auth=authenticated`.
- The same marking applies when credentials expire with no refresh token.
- The startup notice, `/mcp list`, the menu, the trace report, capability search, and the model's server catalog all pick up the re-authentication state through the shared classifier.

title: Keep per-step runtime context at the message tail for prompt cache stability
body:
## Why

Provider prompt caching reuses the longest unchanged leading span of a request. fx rebuilds its per-step runtime context (turn environment, permission mode, stale-shell and subagent delivery notes) on every model step, and it can change mid-turn — most commonly when fx's own first edit flips the bounded git worktree probe to `dirty` in small repositories. That overlay was serialized at the end of the system instruction prefix, so a one-word change invalidated the cached prefix in front of the **entire conversation history**, and every later step reprocessed it. Subagent deliveries additionally appeared in and disappeared from that prefix, breaking it twice per completion.

## Measured impact

Real binary against a fake gateway: `fx ask` accumulates ~112KB of conversation history across 10 file reads, then fx's own `write_file` flips `git_worktree: unknown → dirty` mid-turn. Message-level shared prefix across the flip step:

| flip step (112KB history) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cached prefix reused | **6.0%** (6.7KB) | **99.0%** (110.9KB) |
| History reprocessed | **105,216 B (~26K tokens)** | **1,068 B (~270 tokens)** |

≈**98× less reprocessing** per mid-turn context change. The after-cost is the ~1KB overlay itself, regardless of history length; the before-cost grew linearly with the conversation. Steps without a context change were already append-only and keep 100% prefix reuse in both layouts.

Per-session triggers that previously each forced a full-history re-read: fx's first edit in a small repo, every subagent completion (twice), every explicit `$skill` invocation (twice), permission-mode changes, UTC-day rollover, and the post-restart stale-shell note clearing.

## What changed

- The volatile overlay now rides the **tail of the message list as user-role context** (the same pattern compaction handoffs and interruption notes already use). A mid-turn change now discards only the trailing note (~0.5KB) instead of the full history; unchanged steps keep their exact append-only prefix.
- The session-constant response-language control moves into the stable instruction prefix.
- The post-Vision prefill-rejection classifier now judges the conversation tail instead of the literal request tail (the overlay occupies it now); covered by a hardened unit test with the overlay present.
- The context-contract layout doc and golden snapshot reflect the new ordering.

## Regression proof

New `tests/e2e/prompt-cache-stability.test.ts` drives a real mid-turn dirty flip through a fake gateway and asserts:

- every request advertises `providerOptions.gateway.caching = "auto"`
- tool advertisements stay byte-identical across steps
- the flip actually happens (otherwise the test is vacuous)
- the full pre-overlay prompt — stable prefix plus the entire conversation history — survives byte-identically into the next request

The test fails on the old layout and passes on the new one. Registered in the PGSO corpus (`verification_scenarios`) and E2E shard weights. Gateway, ACP, and TUI lifecycle helpers now locate conversation user messages past the trailing overlay.

## Verification

- `zig fmt --check src/` clean; `zig build test` — full unit suite green
- `zig build`; the freshly built binary exercised end to end against a fake gateway, with message-level prefix reuse measured before (break in front of history) and after (break at the volatile tail)
- Full CI green on the head commit across all four native runners, all E2E shards, Benchmarks, Binary Size, and the macOS arm64 PGSO candidate

Why: Responses endpoints such as Meta's Model API (https://api.meta.ai/v1, serving Muse Spark) need the Responses wire format with `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` replay to keep reasoning coherent across agentic tool loops. Chat Completions drops that continuity.

title: ACP: a second session/prompt during a running turn fails with -32600 "Prompt already in progress" instead of queueing
body:
## Summary

When an ACP client sends a second `session/prompt` while a turn is still running, `fx acp` rejects it immediately with JSON-RPC `-32600 Invalid request: "Prompt already in progress"`. The message is dropped rather than queued as the next turn or folded into the running one.

## Repro

fx 0.0.10 (Homebrew), macOS arm64. Driven over `fx acp` stdio with the ACP Rust SDK:

1. `initialize` → `session/new` → `session/set_mode` (`code`)
2. `session/prompt`: "run `sleep 8`, then reply FIRST DONE"
3. Once the `tool_call` update for the sleep arrives (turn unambiguously live), send a second `session/prompt`

Timestamped wire log:

```
  5312ms  session/update tool_call "Running"
  5371ms  → session/prompt #2 sent
  5371ms  ← error -32600 "Prompt already in progress"
 19949ms  ← session/prompt #1 ok, stopReason "end_turn"
```

The running turn is unaffected — it completes normally after the rejection.

## Expected

Either behavior would let embedding clients offer "send while running":

- **Queue**: accept the request and settle it after the current turn, running the message as the next turn (what several other ACP agents do), or
- **Steer/fold**: deliver it into the running turn.

Failing that, the rejection is at least clean — but clients currently have to special-case this exact error to distinguish "fx refused because a turn is live" from a real protocol failure, and a user-typed follow-up is silently lost unless the client requeues it itself.

Related: #783 (`/btw`) covers interactive side questions; this is about the ACP transport contract for concurrent prompts.

title: Accept the 2024-11-05 protocol revision on streamable HTTP
body:
## Problem

Servers deployed against the original streamable-HTTP revision (for example hosted zread endpoints) complete the HTTP initialize handshake and echo `protocolVersion: 2024-11-05` in the result. The negotiation ladder in `protocol_negotiation` can already settle on that revision (`LegacyStdioVersion.v2024_11_05`), but the streamable-HTTP transport `Version` enum only committed to `2025-03-26` and newer, so `initializedVersion` rejected the echoed version with `McpUnsupportedProtocolVersion` before the ladder could run. Every such server shows up as Failed with `Protocol: unavailable`.

## Change

- Commit `v2024_11_05` to `legacy_streamable_http.Version`:
  - `sendsProtocolHeader` is false for it (the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header postdates the revision), matching the `2025-03-26` behavior.
  - `legacyWireForHttpVersion` maps it to no elicitation wire, same as `2025-03-26`.
- Update the initialization test: `2024-11-05` is accepted as `v2024_11_05`; a fabricated revision (`2023-09-30`) is still rejected.

## Verification

Live handshake against a deployed endpoint that only speaks the old revision:

```
POST /mcp initialize (protocolVersion 2024-11-05)
<- 200 OK, Mcp-Session-Id: ..., result.protocolVersion = 2024-11-05
POST tools/list
<- 200 OK, full tool listing
```

Before this change fx marks the server Failed with `McpUnsupportedProtocolVersion`; after it, the server reaches Ready with tools/resources discovered.

title: Accept 200 and 204 responses to streamable HTTP notifications
body:
## Problem

The transport requires exactly `202 Accepted` for notification posts. Deployed streamable-HTTP servers also answer `notifications/initialized` with `200 OK` (and some with `204 No Content`), so fx disconnects with `UnexpectedHttpStatus` immediately after a successful initialize handshake — the server then shows as Failed even though every request actually succeeded.

## Change

For requests sent with `expected_notification`, treat `accepted`, `ok`, and `no_content` alike. The spec says servers SHOULD return 202; accepting the other two status codes is strictly more permissive and cannot mask an error response, since those carry no body to misparse.

## Verification

Against the same deployed endpoint that motivates #994:

```
POST notifications/initialized
<- 200 OK            # fx previously failed here
POST tools/list
<- 200 OK, full tool listing
```

After this change the connection proceeds to Ready with tools discovered.

title: Use HTTPS callbacks for Slack authorization
body:
## Summary

Completing `fx slack install` now returns the browser to a persistent fx.sh confirmation page after the CLI saves credentials. Refreshing after the CLI exits no longer produces a localhost connection error. Authorization and credential-storage failures lead to a generic failure page.

Personal Slack MCP login for the fx app uses the HTTPS callback through the same bridge. Employees run `/mcp auth slack --open` or `fx mcp auth slack`; PKCE, token exchange, and credential storage remain in the CLI. Browser binding, replay protection, cancellation, and token refresh are preserved. The CLI recognizes Fx by its pinned public Slack Client ID before contacting fx.sh. Other MCP providers and different Slack app Client IDs retain their direct callback behavior without depending on fx.sh.

For the matching fx Slack client, first login and reauthorization request the full personal scope list published by fx.sh. When local `scopes` are configured, they must include every shared scope; extra local permissions are not requested. Narrower or explicitly empty scope lists stop authorization before opening the browser and explain how to opt into the full shared set, without rewriting the configuration or stored credentials. Per-user read-only subsets are not supported for this app. Missing local configuration, broader saved scopes, server scope challenges, and Slack's general capability metadata cannot expand the request. Missing or invalid shared scope metadata, including a mismatched Client ID, stops authorization. Existing tokens are not revoked or downscoped by this change.

Bot installation output uses a plain-language confirmation without Slack IDs and displays expiration as a readable UTC date and time. JSON output retains IDs and Unix timestamps for scripts.

## Rollout

Deploy [fx-web #130](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx-web/pull/130), including `/api/slack/install/config?flow=auth` and its `user_scopes`, before releasing this CLI. New Fx personal logins and reauthorization depend on fx.sh being available; an unavailable metadata endpoint returns `SlackBridgeUnavailable`. There is no localhost fallback for Fx. Keep the registered localhost callback for older clients. Changing the Fx Slack Client ID also requires a CLI update. The shared list contains the nine personal scopes configured for fx and advertised by Slack MCP; later additions still require any necessary Slack approval.

## Validation

Built and exercised `zig-out/bin/fx` locally. Focused tests cover fresh login without configured scopes, broader local and saved scopes, in-session server challenges, malformed or missing shared metadata, and unrelated Slack clients with both healthy and unavailable fx.sh metadata. Regression tests confirm those clients never contact fx.sh, while Fx fails closed on unavailable or mismatched metadata. Tests also cover read-only and empty local scopes, narrower lists with unrelated extras, unchanged saved credentials, preservation of explicit empty scopes across profile edits, and the in-session explanation without opening a browser. All 26 focused authentication tests pass locally. A separate local exercise connects the built CLI to both web handlers with mocked Slack, checks the exact nine-scope request and successful persistence for first login and reauthorization, and verifies exit 0 with empty stderr. Formatting and public-surface checks pass.

Existing coverage includes success, denied consent, manual browser handoff, credential-storage failure, and refreshing confirmation pages after the CLI exits. Live Slack authorization and message attribution still require rollout verification.

title: Improve subagent batch cancellation and partial-result recovery
body:
## Summary

fx can run multiple subagents in parallel, and recent work improves how their statuses are refreshed as they finish. However, a batch still needs clearer lifecycle behavior when children finish, fail, hang, or are cancelled.

## Problem

If a batch contains several subagents:

- One child may fail while others have already completed
- The user may want to cancel the remaining children
- A stuck child may keep the batch open indefinitely
- Completed child results should not be lost because another child failed
- It may be unclear whether the batch can be resumed safely

## Proposal

Improve subagent batch lifecycle handling by:

- Showing clear states such as running, completed, failed, cancelled, and timed out
- Preserving completed child results when another child fails
- Supporting cancellation of the remaining batch
- Ensuring child shutdown has a bounded timeout
- Showing a final batch summary
- Making interrupted batch state recoverable where practical

## Scope suggestion

This should be designed separately from ACP prompt queueing. The first step could be a design and test change for deterministic child states, cancellation, and partial results before adding a larger resume workflow.

I did not find an existing fx issue specifically covering this complete subagent batch lifecycle.

title: Grok catalog fails when the subscription lists a model the modality endpoint does not
body:
## Summary

With a Grok subscription (`fx login grok`), `fx provider grok` fails, so no Grok model is ever saved and Grok requests cannot start:

```
$ fx provider grok
fx provider: could not load the target model catalog (malformed_response)

$ FX_PROVIDER=grok FX_MODEL=grok-4.7 fx ask "hi"
fx: GrokModelNotSelected
```

Build: `e094531` (v0.0.11), macOS arm64. Observed on 2026-09-23.

If a Grok model is already saved in settings, `fx ask` still works, but the catalog load fails in the trace (`model_catalog_load ... outcome=failed failure_category=malformed_response http_status=200`).

## Cause

`parseCatalog` in `src/gateway/xai_grok_models.zig` joins two independently published lists:

- `https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/models` (subscription models)
- `https://api.x.ai/v1/language-models` (modalities)

Both requests return 200. Today the subscription list contains a model the modality list does not:

| Source | Models |
| --- | --- |
| `cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/models` | `grok-4.7`, `grok-4.7-build-fast`, `grok-4.6`, `grok-4.5` |
| `api.x.ai/v1/language-models` | 8 models, including `grok-4.7`, `grok-4.6`, `grok-4.5`, but not `grok-4.7-build-fast` |

When a subscription model has no modality entry, the parser returns `error.InvalidGrokModelCatalog` for the whole catalog:

```zig
const modality_object = try findModalityModel(modality_models.array.items, raw_id) orelse
    return error.InvalidGrokModelCatalog;
```

That error is reported as `malformed_response`, so one newly launched model makes every Grok model unavailable until the modality endpoint catches up.

## Expected

A subscription model without modality metadata is omitted, and the rest of the catalog loads. The parser already omits entries it cannot serve (`api_backend` other than `responses`, no `text` output modality), so this would follow the same rule. Malformed entries and missing required fields would still reject the catalog.

title: Omit Grok subscription models missing modality metadata
body:
Fixes #1014

## Problem

The Grok catalog joins the subscription list (`cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/models`) with the modality list (`api.x.ai/v1/language-models`). The two endpoints publish independently. Today the subscription list includes `grok-4.7-build-fast`, which the modality list does not include yet. `parseCatalog` rejects the whole catalog when any subscription model has no modality entry. As a result, `fx provider grok` reports `malformed_response` and saves no Grok model, so Grok requests then fail with `GrokModelNotSelected`, and `grok-4.7`, `grok-4.6` and `grok-4.5` all become unavailable.

## Change

A subscription model with no modality entry is now omitted and logged to the trace (`grok_model_omitted reason=missing_modalities`). Other entries still load. The parser already omits entries it cannot serve (non-`responses` backends and models without text output), and this change applies the same rule. Malformed entries, invalid ids and missing required fields still reject the catalog.

This reverses one assertion in `Grok catalog rejects missing provider-owned capability metadata`, which treated a missing modality entry as fatal. That case moves to a new test, `Grok catalog omits subscription models the modality endpoint does not list yet`, which asserts that the model is omitted and the rest of the catalog loads.

## Verification

- `zig build test --summary failures` passes locally (macOS arm64), and `zig fmt --check src/gateway/xai_grok_models.zig` is clean.
- Against the live catalogs on 2026-09-23, with a real Grok subscription and a fresh settings file (isolated `HOME`):
  - `main` (`e094531`): `fx provider grok` exits 1 with `could not load the target model catalog (malformed_response)` and leaves settings empty. `FX_PROVIDER=grok FX_MODEL=grok-4.7 fx ask "reply with only: ok"` then fails with `GrokModelNotSelected`. With a Grok model already saved, `ask` still runs, but the trace shows `model_catalog_load ... outcome=failed failure_category=malformed_response http_status=200`.
  - This branch: `fx provider grok` prints `Provider set to Grok.` and saves `grok-4.7`. The same `ask` command replies `ok`. The trace shows `[model_catalog] grok_model_omitted reason=missing_modalities model=grok-4.7-build-fast` followed by `model_catalog_load ... outcome=loaded`.
