title: Bug: ACP operational notices cannot be distinguished from assistant messages
body:
### Issue details

**Summary**

In fx 0.0.10, `fx acp` sends both assistant reply text and operational notices as `session/update` `agent_message_chunk` events. Their `messageId` values differ, but the update does not identify which message is a notice. A client can separate the messages, but cannot classify them while they stream.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Start `fx acp`, initialize it, and create a session in a workspace where fx emits a context or skill notice.
2. Send a short `session/prompt`, such as `hi`, and inspect the `session/update` notifications.
3. Compare the live text with `fx session --id <id> --json` after the turn ends.

In our ACP client, a context notice and `default` appeared alongside `Hi! What can I help you with?`. The saved assistant reply contained only `Hi! What can I help you with?`. This is an observed client symptom; I have not attached a raw ACP trace.

**Expected behavior**

The live ACP stream identifies operational notices separately from assistant reply text. A client can show notices as activity and stream the reply into the answer. Model reasoning remains separate as `agent_thought_chunk`.

**Actual behavior and impact**

fx gives operational and assistant text different message IDs, but sends both through `agent_message_chunk` without a kind field. A client must show notices as assistant messages, delay the answer until it can read the saved session, or guess from message order or text. A different ID indicates a different message, not its purpose.

The distinction exists inside fx: [`assistant_source` uses `assistantMessageId()`, while `operational` uses `operationalMessageId()`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/v0.0.10/src/acp/prompt.zig#L2165-L2186). Both paths call `sendAgentText()`, which writes an `agent_message_chunk`. [`pushReasoningDelta()` already writes `agent_thought_chunk`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/v0.0.10/src/acp/prompt.zig#L2181-L2186).

Could fx send operational notices through a distinct, documented ACP-compatible signal, while reserving `agent_message_chunk` for assistant reply text? An advertised extension notification is one possible approach. This differs from #207, which addressed terminal-rendered text versus raw Markdown; the reply text streams here, but has no reliable notice discriminator.

### Trace

Not attached. The example above contains no credentials or private paths.

title: Speed up session resume and listing with one session index
body:
## Summary

- `fx sessions`, `fx session last`, ACP session listing, the resume picker, and `fx --resume last` read one fingerprint-checked session index instead of scanning every session directory, so unchanged sessions are never reopened. On a 14.6k-session store, `fx sessions` drops from 95 s to 0.17 s, `fx --resume last` from 33 s to 0.5 s, and the picker catalog from 3 to 6 s to under 0.7 s.
- `fx sessions` and ACP listing stay read-only. The picker and `fx --resume last` save refreshed index rows.
- Resume renders saved edits from their inline previews. Full diffs are built after the first frame, only for the newest transcript page (so Ctrl+O opens at once) and for pages you open. A 189 MB session reaches its first frame in 0.36 s instead of 1.3 to 1.5 s.
- Closing or switching away from an interactive session that never received a message or a title removes it instead of leaving an empty session behind.
- `fx --resume last` retries a session that disappears mid-open once, then moves to the next newest, up to three sessions.
- Legacy sessions without an event log, and legacy sessions behind an interrupted upgrade, appear in the picker and every listing. Opening a fenced one runs the same recovery or reports the same error as before.
- `fx --resume last` skips a session it cannot read instead of failing on it: the sessions every listing skips, and an older session whose event log can no longer be replayed. That older session stays listed, and `fx doctor` reports it. When this workspace has no readable session and some saved sessions are unreadable, it says both and points to `fx doctor`, like `fx session last`.
- Like `fx session last`, `fx --resume last` considers only sessions that recorded a workspace, so a very old session saved without one is resumed by ID or from the picker rather than from whichever workspace asks.
- Subagent child sessions stay out of every listing, the picker, `fx session last`, and `fx --resume last`, including older children marked only in their first event, which listing reads within a fixed 16 KiB so a large log is never scanned. A session whose child marker or first event can't be checked stays listed, and resuming a real child is still refused.
- An older session whose saved summary lags its event log, or was lost or damaged, is listed and ranked by its committed log, so `fx --resume last` finds it in the workspace it moved to.
- A session index path that isn't a regular file, such as a FIFO, is ignored instead of blocking listing, the picker, or `fx --resume last`. The session files that listing, `fx --resume last`, and `fx doctor` read (the manifest, event log, commit watermark, authority files, and display file) are opened the same way, so a FIFO in place of one makes that session unreadable, or is ignored for a display file, instead of hanging.
- The shared regular-file open accepts a read-only file that another process is atomically replacing, as its check after the open already did, so a listing that races a save of the session index keeps using the index instead of rescanning every session.
- A session whose summary the index can't store, such as one updated before it was created after a clock change, is listed without being cached, so it can't disable the index for every other session.
- The first model request after resume starts with exactly the bytes the live session last sent, so provider prompt caching keeps working.

title: Treat empty provider responses as failures
body:
## Summary

- Retry a response that finishes with no text and no tool calls up to two more times, showing "Provider unavailable · empty response" while it retries.
- Complete the turn normally when one of those retries returns an answer.
- End the turn with an empty-response notice after the third empty response instead of showing "Done." as the reply. `fx ask` exits 1 and its JSON output has an empty `final_output`.
- Stop right away with an output-limit notice when a response hits the length limit before producing any answer, such as after a long hidden reasoning run. ACP still reports `max_output_tokens` for these turns.
- Treat whitespace-only responses as empty.
- Apply the same handling when the model stays silent after fx asks it to summarize its tool work.
- Wait for a running subagent's result when the model replies with nothing, instead of retrying and cancelling the subagent.
- Complete the turn with the answer already given when a stop hook continuation comes back empty.
- Continue with queued steering when empty retries run out.
- Report token usage for empty attempts, so the context meter and session totals stay current.
- Stop saving "Done." to session history as the model's reply. A failed turn records its notice instead, like other failed turns.

title: Bug: all numpad keys (digits and operators) are swallowed in kitty-protocol terminals
body:
### Issue details

All numpad keys do nothing in the composer: digits 0-9, operators `/ - * +`, `.`, and keypad Enter. (An earlier version of this report claimed digits work; they do not.)

fx enables the kitty keyboard protocol disambiguate flag at startup (`\x1b[>1u` in `src/ui/terminal/terminal.zig`). Keypad keys then arrive as CSI u function codes instead of plain bytes: KP_0..KP_9 = 57399-57408, KP_DECIMAL = 57409, KP_DIVIDE = 57410, KP_MULTIPLY = 57411, KP_SUBTRACT = 57412, KP_ADD = 57413, KP_ENTER = 57414, KP_EQUAL = 57415. `kittyUnicodeKeyAction` (`src/ui/input/escape_parser.zig`) maps none of 57399-57416 (no reference to these codes exists anywhere in `src/`), so every numpad keystroke falls through to `.ignore` and is silently dropped.

The legacy application-keypad SS3 encodings hit the same wall: parser stage 4 maps only arrows/Home/End and discards everything else, including `ESC O p`-`ESC O y` (digits), `ESC O n` (decimal), `ESC O j/k/m/o` (operators), and `ESC O M` (keypad Enter).

Fix: map the KP_* keycodes to their characters in `kittyUnicodeKeyAction`, and the SS3 application-keypad sequences in stage 4.

Related: #196 / #202 (same kitty-protocol swallow pattern, fixed for Esc).

### Environment

- Terminal: any kitty-keyboard-protocol terminal (Ghostty, Kitty, WezTerm, ...) or a terminal in application keypad mode
- tmux: unaffected for the kitty path — fx omits `\x1b[>1u` inside tmux

## Summary

- Show herdr "blocked" only while fx waits on an approval or an answer, with "Waiting for approval" or "Waiting for an answer" as the reason.

title: Show why stdio MCP servers fail to start
body:
## Summary

- When a stdio MCP server closes its connection before answering `initialize`, for example because its process exited, report its exit code or signal and an excerpt of its stderr instead of `McpInitFailed`.
- Limit that excerpt to one line of at most 400 bytes covering the first and latest output, with secrets masked, terminal escape sequences removed, and other control characters escaped.
- When the middle of a long stderr is dropped, also drop the partial words on each side of the gap, so a secret cut there is never shown in part.
- When startup times out, name the limit that ran out, the `startup_timeout_ms` key when that setting set the limit, and the exit of an earlier launch if there was one. A crash-recovery relaunch that hangs reports `startup_timeout_ms`, and one that uses up the tool call's deadline reports that span instead.
- When a server writes a stdout line that is not an MCP message, such as a banner, quote the start of that line instead of reporting a bare error name, on every stdio startup path including crash recovery. fx still restarts it once.
- Stop restarting a stdio server during startup once it has closed its connection at every offered protocol version or its startup deadline has passed.
- Show that same reason when a required MCP server fails to start and fx refuses to continue.
- Keep that reason in `/mcp list` when a crash-recovery relaunch or a deferred `fx ask` connection fails, instead of replacing it with an error name.
- Give the model that reason when its search names a server that is down, including a deferred server in `fx ask`. Searches that only mention the server in their query keep their normal results.
- Give the model that reason when a tool call finds its server stopped and its own relaunch fails. Other recovery errors keep their existing guidance.

title: Subagent result and status reads retain full session scratch in the parent turn
body:
While using fx (my BYOK fork) with **gpt-6-astra**, the model automatically started a subagent. Memory kept growing during execution and exceeded **60 GB**, leading to OOM. That is the observed incident, not a claim that the reduced reproduction uses 60 GB.

The corresponding allocation-lifetime bug is still present in upstream `c95fcc66`, after #687:

| Path | Current behavior | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `subagent.run` / `subagent.message` result observation | `managedResultText` loads the full child session using the parent tool/turn allocator, then returns only one matching assistant result | Decoded history and replay scratch can remain allocated until the parent turn ends |
| Progress initialization | `startStatusPublisher` loads the full child session just to obtain model and effort | Another unnecessary history load with the same lifetime problem |
| Repeated calls during a long parent turn | `state.deinit()` runs, but the caller is an arena | Individual frees do not generally reclaim arena backing; temporary session reads accumulate |

Expected: release session-read scratch when each read finishes, retain only the returned result/status fields, and read metadata without reconstructing history when possible.

This is a remaining subagent read path related to #483; #687 addressed checkpoint reconstruction and provider-request scratch. The trigger is not specific to GPT-6-Astra. A focused fix and bounded reproduction will follow.

title: Fix memory growth when reading subagent sessions
body:
Subagent result and progress reads load child-session history into the parent's turn arena. Repeated reads retain temporary data until the parent turn ends, contributing to the OOM reported in #1031.

Release read and capability-resolution scratch after each operation, copying only returned text/model fields into the caller allocator. Progress now reads saved preferences without replaying canonical history; older session formats retain their existing read behavior.

Linux x86_64, Zig 0.16 ReleaseSafe; medians of three fresh processes. The fixture has a 1 MiB old turn and a 12-byte selected result, read 16 times alongside 16 status initializations:

| Version | Retained caller arena | Peak process RSS | Result reads | Status reads |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before (`c95fcc66`) | 1.96 GiB | 376.6 MiB | 180.3 ms | 180.0 ms |
| Scratch lifetime fixed (`c6ebf4e9`) | 282 B | 21.0 MiB | 192.3 ms | 191.3 ms |
| Plus metadata-only status reads | 282 B | 20.9 MiB | 178.5 ms | 0.94 ms |

Arena capacity is not RSS. Timings cover the 16 helper calls per column, excluding fixture setup and model execution. This bounded reproduction does not allocate 60 GB. Reproduce with [`benchmarks/subagent_session_reads.md`](https://github.com/acking-you/fx/blob/7ce4e5a17b21f2aa13a8fcd7cc0eeb44f5b6d21b/benchmarks/subagent_session_reads.md).

Validation: focused ownership, allocation-failure, metadata and legacy tests; fresh-binary CLI persistent/one-off subagents, failure/replay handling, and TUI steering. [Full CI](https://github.com/acking-you/fx/actions/runs/35963528251) is running for `7ce4e5a1`.

Required classification: `type: bug`.

Fixes #1031

title: Bug: Codex subscription catalog validation times out behind an HTTP proxy on VPN, while completions succeed
body:
### Issue details

I am using fx 0.0.10 on Arch Linux behind a corporate VPN. All outbound HTTP(S) traffic must traverse a corporate forward proxy.

Proxy configuration:
```
http_proxy=http://<corporate-proxy>:80
https_proxy=http://<corporate-proxy>:80
no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1,<internal CIDRs and corporate domains>
```
I also tested with uppercase and generic proxy variables:
```
HTTP_PROXY="$http_proxy" \
HTTPS_PROXY="$https_proxy" \
ALL_PROXY="$https_proxy" \
NO_PROXY="$no_proxy" \
FX_TRACE=1 \
FX_TRACE_STDERR=1 \
FX_TRACE_LOG=/tmp/fx-codex.trace \
fx ask "where is Prague?"
```

fx login codex completes browser OAuth successfully. However, /setup codex waits several minutes and then reports:

```
provider: Subscription sign-in completed, but its model catalog could not be validated. The current provider is unchanged.
```

The official Codex CLI and OpenCode work through the same VPN/proxy configuration. fx also works correctly when disconnected from the VPN, which bypasses the corporate proxy path.

title: Update Slack auth test for the MCP server menu
body:
## Summary

- No user-facing change. The personal Slack reconnect test now checks the `/mcp list` server menu for a Ready server instead of the old text listing, so it passes again on every platform.

title: Preserve tmux pane modes during resize cleanup
body:
## Summary

- Keep tmux's session switcher and copy mode open when fx processes a terminal resize.
- Guard history clearing inside tmux using its current pane mode and explicit server-owned pane ID.
- Add isolated PTY regressions using real Ctrl+A prefix input, plus focused command-contract coverage and a README note.

## Cause

Opening `choose-tree -Zs` zooms a split pane and triggers fx's resize reset. The reset previously invoked `tmux clear-history` unconditionally, which also dismisses tmux pane modes. Ordinary terminal output and ANSI screen clearing did not cause the dismissal.

## Verification

Local macOS arm64, Zig 0.16.0, Bun 1.4.2, tmux 3.5a:

- `zig build`: passed, exit 0.
- `zig fmt --check src/`: passed, exit 0.
- `git diff --check`: passed, exit 0.
- Focused Zig tests for `tmux history clear`, using a temporary test root importing `ui/shell_runtime.zig`: 4 passed, exit 0; temporary root removed.
- `bun test ./tests/e2e/tui-resize.test.ts -t 'tmux (choose-tree|copy-mode) survives settled resize without auto closing'`: both regressions failed on the original binary because the pane mode disappeared, then both passed with the rebuilt `./zig-out/bin/fx`, exit 0.
- `bun test ./tests/e2e/tui-resize.test.ts -t 'settled resize replays a long assistant transcript from the header'`: passed on an isolated clean-config tmux server, exit 0.
- Real PTY interactions verified mode preservation, intentional dismissal, usable composer input, process survival, and clean stderr. The reporter also confirmed the fix works.

The existing `tui-resize.test.ts` PGSO training classification remains appropriate for common resize behavior; no new E2E owner was added.

Full CI for this commit is pending. Keep this PR in draft until all four platform aggregates and the final ship gate pass.

title: Deduplicate OAuth browser flow primitives
body:
## Summary

- Preserve Codex, Grok, and MCP OAuth behavior while sharing their form, PKCE, token, and prepared-login paths.
- Pass Slack MCP authorization values as typed state instead of rebuilding and reparsing the authorization URL.
- Share Slack callback parsing between MCP authorization and workspace installation while preserving each flow's validation and error behavior.
- Reduce non-PGSO macOS arm64 ReleaseSafe `__TEXT` by 13,449 bytes and file size by 16,416 bytes on current main.
- Remove 5,140 bytes of PGSO machine code; linker padding keeps the signed candidate file unchanged at 6.475082 MiB.

title: Keep resume and exit from blocking on the usage ledger
body:
## Summary

- Resume a session without waiting on the profile usage ledger. Queued usage publishes in the background.
- Exit the interactive shell without waiting on another fx process that holds the usage ledger lock. Unpublished usage stays with the session and publishes on the next resume.
- Stop re-reading the whole usage ledger on every usage write in release builds.
- Stop a usage publish at the first busy ledger lock instead of waiting on the lock once per record.
- Rewrite the usage ledger to drop expired records at most about once a day instead of on every write.

title: Accept the Slack OAuth resource origin in personal authorization
body:
## Summary

Personal Slack authorization failed with `InvalidSlackAuthorizationResource` before opening the browser because the HTTPS bridge expected the MCP transport URL as the OAuth resource. Slack advertises `https://mcp.slack.com`, which fx canonicalizes to `https://mcp.slack.com/`.

Validate that root resource while keeping the transport endpoint at `https://mcp.slack.com/mcp`. The bridge still rejects other resources before browser launch. The authentication fixture now advertises the same origin-level resource as Slack, and checks that authorization, token exchange, and saved credentials agree. Existing scope, client identity, PKCE, and callback checks are preserved.

## Validation

- Reproduced the pre-fix failure with the built CLI and corrected metadata fixture.
- `zig build`, formatting, and public-surface checks pass.
- All 27 focused authentication tests pass (594 assertions), including actual in-session login, reauthorization, wrong-resource rejection, and unrelated Slack clients.
- Exercised the built CLI with the actual web handlers and mocked Slack for first login and reauthorization: credentials saved, exit 0, empty stderr.
- The built CLI accepted Slack's live public metadata and reached the HTTPS bridge in an isolated profile. Stopped before consent; live token exchange remains to be verified after deployment.

## Rollout

Deploy [fx-web #135](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx-web/pull/135), which sends `resource=https://mcp.slack.com/`, before testing the updated CLI against production. No Slack app settings or bot reinstall are needed. Full CI on this commit must pass before marking this PR ready.

title: Keep detached daemons alive between shell calls
body:
## Summary

- Leave a daemon running after its shell command finishes when it moved to its own session, so CLIs such as agent-browser, tmux, and ssh-agent keep their server between calls on macOS and Linux.
- Leave that daemon's own children, such as the browser it launched, running with it.
- Keep stopping background jobs that stay in the command's session, such as `cmd &` and `nohup cmd &`, when the command finishes.
- Return from a shell call about a second after its command finishes when a detached process keeps the command's output open. If the reader is slow, live output stops ten seconds after the command finishes, and the result still includes the rest.
- Keep stopping detached daemons when a command times out, is cancelled, or fx exits while it runs.

title: Merge leading system messages into one provider request message
body:
## Summary

- Send one system message per provider request instead of one per context section, preserving section order and content.
- Fix intermittent HTTP 400 "System message must be at the beginning" failures from providers that render strict server-side chat templates, such as alibaba/qwen3.8-max, including mid-turn after tool calls.
- Apply the same merge to configured OpenAI-compatible providers.

title: Give compaction summaries a guaranteed share of the handoff
body:
## Summary

- Compaction summaries always get at least 40% of the handoff budget, and the summarizer is told its token target.
- User messages over about 2,000 tokens, like pasted logs, show up in the handoff as a placeholder that points to the saved original. The summary keeps their facts and instructions.
- Short user messages such as standing rules stay verbatim. When space runs out, the largest messages become placeholders first, and short ones are saved together only as a last resort.
- When compaction runs partway through a turn, that turn's prompt follows the same placeholder rules, so a large paste in it no longer fails the turn.
- The request after compaction still carries the current prompt verbatim, and a large prompt is sent once instead of twice.
- Placeholders stay placeholders in later compactions and are not expanded again.
- Steering messages follow the same rules as other user messages.
- A summary over its target gets one rewrite from the summary alone, then a section trim with a visible marker. Compaction no longer regenerates from the full history or fails the turn because a summary ran long.
- The section trim also cuts text written on a label's own line, keeping the bare label and a trim marker.
- A summary that stops at the model's output limit, or runs past the handoff size limit, keeps its complete lines with a visible cut-off marker instead of failing the turn or dropping later sections silently. Trimming never removes that marker.
- Summaries use labeled sections for standing rules, decisions, key facts, work done, work remaining, and saved files, and later compactions carry each section forward.
- Empty steering entries no longer add a blank note to the summarizer input.

title: Stop the skill walk at the repository when HOME is not above it
body:
## Summary

The workspace skill walk climbs from the workspace toward `/` and stops at HOME. That stop only works when HOME is one of the workspace's ancestors. When it is not, the walk never meets it: it scans every directory up to `/` and advertises whatever skills it finds there to the model.

This happens for any repository outside HOME (`/srv`, `/opt`, `/tmp`, a container's `/workspace`), and for any process that runs fx with a separate HOME, such as an orchestrator giving each worker its own profile.

- When HOME is not an ancestor of the workspace, the walk now ends at the nearest repository root: the first directory holding a `.git` directory or a linked-worktree `.git` file. That root is still scanned, so a repository's own skills keep loading.
- A workspace inside HOME keeps today's behavior, including skill directories in ancestors above the repository.
- Outside a repository the walk is unchanged.
- The discovery error set stays out-of-memory only: a `.git` entry that cannot be inspected counts as absent.

## Evidence

A linked worktree under a scratch directory in my HOME, with a canary skill one directory above the repository, running `fx ask` with a separate HOME against a local logging proxy in front of the DeepSeek API:

- `fx` 0.0.11: the first request carried the canary and 28 personal skills from `~/.codex/skills` and `~/skills`, and was 40,066 bytes.
- this branch: none of them, and the same request was 25,014 bytes.

## Verification

- Two new `skill_runtime` tests: a workspace outside HOME stops at the repository root while still loading that root's skills, and a workspace inside HOME keeps loading ancestors above the repository. The first test fails without the change.
- `loadVisibleSkills` tests: 23/23.
- `zig fmt --check` clean; `zig build` succeeds.
- Full CI on the fork: pending.

Suggested label: `type: bug`.

title: Downscale images over 2000 pixels before sending them
body:
## Problem

Once a conversation holds more than 20 images, some model providers reject any image wider or taller than 2000 pixels, and every provider rejects a side over 8000 pixels. fx only checked encoded size, so one large screenshot (for example a 3420x2224 PNG, or a 390x9000 full-page capture, read with `read_file`) failed the request. Tool images stay in history and are sent again on every request, so the session stayed stuck and every retry failed with the same error.

## Fix

- Every image in a chat request is at most 2000 pixels per side. Larger images shrink to fit and keep their aspect ratio.
- The model sees a note with the original size, the new size, and the factor that maps coordinates back to original pixels.
- PNGs over the pixel limit are decoded, downscaled, and re-encoded in process on every platform (`src/core/images/png_downscale.zig`, standard library only). This covers tool results (`read_file`, MCP, and other tools) and attached, pasted, ACP, and libfx in-memory images.
- PNGs that are also over the 5 MiB byte limit are downscaled for `read_file`, file attachments, ACP, and libfx. MCP and host tool images keep their existing 5 MiB per-image cap, which is part of their result framing.
- Every path that adds a tool result to history fits its images: parallel batches, single calls, and cancelled batches. A downscaled copy that would take a result past the stored image limit is withheld with a note.
- Other formats: attachments keep the existing macOS `sips` path. Oversized tool images in those formats are withheld with a note naming the format.
- If `sips` fails, runs past its 5-second limit, or writes output that still cannot be sent, an attachment that is only over the pixel limit is kept and left out of the request with the note below, and one also over the byte limit is rejected with a notice. Previously a hanging `sips` while attaching an image in the interactive shell ended the session with `fx: TimedOut`.
- Attachments still over the limit after capture (for example a large JPEG on Linux, or one saved before this change) are left out of the request. The model sees the format, the size, and the saved snapshot path, and is asked to save a smaller copy to a new file without changing the original. libfx in-memory attachments have no snapshot, so their note asks for a smaller copy instead. When an image attached in the current turn is withheld, fx tells the user once per turn.
- Sessions saved before this change: oversized stored tool images and attachments are left out when a request is built, so stuck sessions recover on resume.

## Verification

- Focused Zig tests for `png_downscale`, `image_data`, `image_attachments`, `execution_memory`, and `read_file`: 154 passed, including fixed-seed mutation tests for the PNG decoder and header parser, and a JPEG whose frame header sits behind 390 KB of metadata.
- Resizer failures: tests replace `sips` with scripts that fail, hang past the time limit, write garbage, or copy the oversized source. Pixel-only images are kept, byte-oversized ones are rejected, and a capture deadline that passes still fails the capture. Palette PNGs whose downscaled copy is over the byte limit keep the original, both on disk and in memory. The image test root passes 375 tests.
- E2E: `vision-route-fake-gateway` 49 passed (including an oversized JPEG attachment that no resizer can convert, left out with its saved path and a user notice on every platform), `file-tool-paths` 21 passed, `mcp-stdio` image tests 6 passed, `acp` image tests 10 passed (including a 6 MB, 3420x2224 PNG prompt that reaches the model at 2000x1301).
- Fake Gateway enforcing both provider limits: the original failing session shapes (3420x2224 frame after 21 images; 1440x5200 and 390x9000 headless Chrome screenshots) fail and stay stuck on the previous build, and complete or recover on this build. A 6 MB, 3420x2224 PNG reaches the request at 2000x1301 through both `read_file` and `--image`.
- Fault injection on macOS against a fake Gateway, compared with the previous commit: a fake `sips` that hangs, exits with an error, writes garbage, or writes a copy still over the limit; disk-full and I/O errors on capture files and when reading saved snapshots; Escape, Ctrl+C, and a kill during capture; resuming sessions saved by an older build. Every run through `fx ask`, the interactive shell, ACP, and a subagent kept each image at 2000 pixels or less, and the next turn and resume worked. The hanging and bad-output `sips` cases fail on the previous commit and pass here.
- Live Gateway on this build: the interactive shell with 24 attached images (21 small, a 3420x2224 PNG, a 390x9000 PNG, and a 4032x3024 JPEG) and a follow-up turn, ACP with a PNG and a JPEG, and a subagent that reads both large PNGs. Every image reached the model at 2000 pixels or less, and the model described each one correctly.
- Live Gateway: both failing traces reproduce on the previous build and succeed on this build, including resuming the sessions they broke. Resuming a session with an oversized saved attachment leads the model to write a smaller copy to a new file and describe it correctly, with the saved snapshot unchanged.

## Follow-ups

- The vision tool route has no pixel check of its own. It sends at most 8 images per request and keeps none in history, so only the provider's 8000-pixel limit applies there. Images it reads from `paths` go through the same capture step, so PNGs over 2000 pixels arrive downscaled and, on macOS, other formats arrive converted by `sips`. A non-PNG image over 8000 pixels (on Linux, or when `sips` fails) still fails that vision call.
- ACP rejects a JPEG over the 5 MiB byte limit before trying `sips`, while `fx ask` and the interactive shell convert the same file.
- A `sips` process that runs past its time limit is not stopped, as before this change. It keeps running in the background and can later leave an unused file in the session's image folder.

title: Keep diff markers monochrome until a theme is selected

## Summary

- Show edit counts and diff markers in monochrome when no theme is selected.
- Use the selected theme's marker colors for named themes and explicit light/dark variants.

title: Reduce MCP and search state overhead
body:
## Summary

- Keep MCP startup diagnostics unchanged while avoiding unused 4 KiB snapshots.

title: Handle Anthropic prompt-too-long errors and full-window output limits
body:
## Summary

- Compact and retry once when Anthropic rejects a request with "prompt is too long", instead of failing the turn.
- For models whose catalog output limit fills the whole context window, request at most 32,768 output tokens, or an eighth of the window when that is smaller, instead of leaving the limit unset. GLM 5.3 and Inkling replies no longer stop at 4,096 tokens.
- Reserve that same output amount when sizing input for those models, so automatic compaction starts slightly earlier.

title: Fix session listing, resume, and doctor gaps after the index change
body:
Follow-up to #1021. It closes the gaps left in listing, resume, and doctor after the session index change.

## What changes

**Stale logs are replayed once, not on every listing.** Read-only listings (`fx sessions`, `fx session last`, and ACP) now save the session index after they replay a stale or lost schema-v3 manifest. Before, they never saved, so every listing replayed every stale log again. Replays in one process now run one at a time, so a listing holds at most one replayed session state in memory.

**Lost manifests are handled the same everywhere.** Recovery from the committed log moved into the shared read-only classifier. `fx session <id>` now shows a session whose `session.json` is invalid (before: `SessionNotFound`). `fx doctor` reports a missing or invalid manifest as a warning ("from its workspace, run fx --resume <id> once") instead of failing it as `canonical_state_invalid`, because resuming rebuilds the summary from the log. A managed subagent child with a lost manifest, marked in its first event or, from older releases, only by `subagent/owner.json` or `subagent/control.json`, is still reported as invalid, since resume refuses it.

**`--resume last` passes over a fresh session open elsewhere.** When the newest session has nothing to resume yet (its summary shows no resumable content) and another process holds it, such as a fresh `fx` in another terminal, `--resume last` tries its lock once, without the usual two-second wait, and moves on to the next session. Before, it waited two seconds and failed with `SessionBusy`. Such a session that nobody holds, such as a first turn cut off by a crash, is still resumed, and a busy session with resumable content still waits and reports `SessionBusy`. When the only candidates are busy sessions with nothing to resume, it still reports `SessionBusy` with its hint to return to that process, now without the wait.

**No more hangs on special files at resume time.** The history cache, usage recovery marker, usage file, and remembered session pointer open without blocking. A FIFO in their place now fails fast instead of hanging resume, `fx session <id>`, or `fx doctor`.

**Cleanups.** The subagent child identity read reuses `readLineAt`, the concurrent replacement io test now checks that its renaming thread actually ran during the opens, and a stale doc comment above `listSubagentControlSessionIds` is removed.

## Measurements

Four stale schema-v3 sessions of about 100 MB each, `fx sessions`, ReleaseSafe:

| Build | Run | Time | Peak memory | Index saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | every run | ~0.57 s | ~470 MB | no |
| this branch | first run | 2.20 s | 119 MB | yes |
| this branch | later runs | ~0.00 s | 4 MB | yes |

The first listing is slower because replays now run one at a time. That keeps memory bounded to one session state no matter how many stale logs there are, and the cost is paid once.

Other real-binary checks against main:

- `--resume last` with a fresh session open in another terminal: main exits 1 with `SessionBusy` after 2.06 s; this branch resumes the real conversation in 0.09 s.
- `--resume last` when that fresh session is the only one: both report `SessionBusy`, main after 2.09 s and this branch in 0.03 s. The TUI prints the busy message with its `fg` hint.
- A FIFO as `history-cache.bin`: main hangs resume by id, session detail, and doctor; this branch finishes each one.
- A FIFO as the usage recovery marker: main hangs resume by id; this branch fails fast with `InvalidUsageRecoveryIndex`.
- Invalid manifest: `fx session <id>` works, the session is listed, doctor warns, and following the advice resumes it with full history; doctor is clean afterward.

## Tests

- New unit tests cover saving the index only after a replay and reusing it on the next listing, latest resume passing over a busy session with nothing to resume (quickly), reporting it busy when nothing else remains, and resuming it once it is free, the doctor warning for a lost summary and its exception for a managed child (first-event flag, `owner.json`, or legacy `control.json`), and the history cache FIFO.
- The lost-manifest test now expects the doctor warning kinds and checks that detail views open a recovered session.
- Two existing tests that expect `SessionBusy` from latest resume now give their busy session a turn.
- `zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe` passes.

title: Accept the Slack OAuth resource origin in personal authorization

title: Fix crash after clearing the screen in conversations with tool calls

title: Show effort and Fast mode choices after picking a model with Ctrl+P
body:
## Summary

- Picking a model from the Ctrl+P picker continues to the same effort and Fast mode choices as `/model` instead of applying the model with the current settings.
- The draft stays set aside through those choices and returns, with its cursor, once the model is applied.
- Esc or Ctrl+P during the effort or Fast mode choice returns to the draft without changing the model.
- Removing the `/model` text during those choices also returns to the draft.
- Enter on a model query that matches nothing during those choices keeps the picker open instead of running `/model` as a command.
- Ctrl+V skips image attach while those choices are open.
- Pasting an image path into the model picker keeps it as text instead of attaching an image.

title: Link standalone code URLs across terminal wraps
body:
## Summary

- Make standalone URLs in inline code clickable across wrapped terminal rows.
- Keep both rows of a wrapped URL under the same hyperlink identity so the terminal can highlight them as one link.
- Keep inline-code styling and leave a sentence-final period outside the link without dropping literal URI punctuation.

title: Replace context compaction with a turn-by-turn ledger
body:
## Summary

- Keep every user message and final reply of the turns a compaction covers word for word.
- Leave up to the four newest turns unchanged, as long as they fit in 40 percent of the room the compacted conversation gets.
- Note what the assistant did between each compacted turn's message and final reply, written by the conversation's own model.
- List every compacted tool call on a line fx writes from the call itself, such as `shell zig build test (failed, exit 1, 3120 bytes)`, followed by the model's note on why it ran and what it showed.
- Keep numbered entries for the user's rules, quoted word for word, and for facts, decisions, status, and open questions, plus the skills and MCP tools used.
- Save the previous compaction whole as `L<n>` at each later compaction, and show in its place one short summary of all earlier compactions, written by the model, plus their rules, status, and open entries still in force, word for word, so the turns of earlier compactions leave the view however many compactions a session has.
- Keep earlier compactions in view in sessions that are not saved, since they cannot be stored.
- Never rewrite an entry; a newer entry that replaces one marks it with the newer entry's ID.
- Keep an entry whose ID is already taken under the next free ID instead of dropping it, and keep the entry that held the ID.
- Renumber an entry whose ID is far above the highest of its kind.
- Leave out an entry line copied with its `(replaced by <ID>)` mark.
- Leave out rule candidates that a saved rule already quotes, so a long turn in progress is not filed again at every compaction.
- Keep a saved entry with an unreadable ID only in its saved compaction instead of failing every later compaction.
- Mark, without removing, a note or entry that names no source, quotes words the user did not write, states a path, number, version, or quoted text found in no compacted turn or tool call, names an unknown ID, or calls a failed tool call a success.
- Ask the model once more for compacted turns with work that it left without a note.
- Ask the model once more for the summary of earlier compactions when its notes leave it out, and take a reply to that request without its heading as the summary.
- Keep the previous summary and finish the compaction when only that summary needed the model and the request fails.
- Ask for the notes during automatic compaction right after the conversation, with the agent's own instructions, tools, and reasoning setting, so the provider reuses its cache.
- Keep fx's own notes request out of the rules, decisions, and status saved during automatic compaction.
- Cite rules from the turn still in progress as `(turn in progress)`, since that turn has no ID yet, and rules in sessions without saved records as `(turn <n>)`.
- Save entries written with a bold or checked ID, like `- [x] **F1** (T3):`, from the ID on.
- Write the turns out in a separate request at the model's lowest reasoning setting for `/compact`, and when the request after the conversation fails or does not fit.
- Retry a failed or empty separate request once on AI Gateway with Claude Sonnet 5, or with GPT-6 Sol when the conversation uses an Anthropic model, keeping the configured provider routing.
- Split turns too large for one separate request into several requests, oldest first.
- Skip the model request when no compacted turn has work between its message and final reply, no message may set a rule, and no earlier compaction needs its summary.
- Shorten the longest texts to their start and end only when the compacted conversation would outgrow its room, naming the saved turn that keeps each one whole; texts of 256 bytes or less are never shortened.
- Save each compacted turn as `M<n>`, each compacted tool call as `T<n>`, as the model saw it plus the handle of any full output saved separately, and each earlier compaction as `L<n>`, which the agent can open by ID with `read_tool_result`.
- Rank `read_tool_result` text searches across saved turns, tool calls, earlier compactions, and older result archives, favoring exact phrase matches, and report how many saved records hold all the words, with the first and last of them.
- Number new saved turns, tool calls, and compactions after the ones already saved when a checkpoint cannot be read, instead of replacing them.
- Add `auto_compact_percent` (10 to 80, default 80) to `~/.fx/settings.json` and `FX_AUTO_COMPACT_PERCENT` to choose when automatic compaction starts, in the app, `fx ask`, `fx acp`, and subagents.
- Resume a sessions v2 session from the first turn its latest compaction kept, so a compacted turn does not come back after a second compaction.
- Keep reading checkpoints saved by the previous compactor, including their exact user messages.
- Show the cancellation notice when compaction is cancelled right after it starts.
- Report the actual compaction decision in `/trace`, including compactions that find nothing to compact.

title: Reduce session test-control overhead

title: Stop gateway request timers from interrupting other connections
body:
## Summary

- `fx ask` and interactive turns no longer abort at random right after startup with "programmer bug caused syscall error: ISCONN" in Debug builds.
- Release builds no longer fail a gateway request at random with an unexpected connect error.
- Esc and request deadlines still cancel an in-flight gateway request.

## Same pattern elsewhere

Each gateway request used to race cancel and deadline sleeper tasks and cancel them when the request won. In Zig 0.16 that cancel can signal a worker thread after it has already started its next task, and an interrupted connect then fails with EISCONN. This PR fixes the gateway client. These files use the same sleeper-and-cancel pattern and should move to the same watcher next:

- `src/core/mcp/streamable_http.zig`
- `src/core/mcp/legacy_streamable_http.zig`
- `src/core/mcp/legacy_http_sse.zig`
- `src/core/mcp/mcp_auth.zig`
- `src/core/mcp/stdio_dispatcher.zig`
- `src/tools/web/http_fetch.zig`
- `src/core/cli/cli_ask.zig`
- `src/acp/prompt.zig`
- `src/core/hosts/native_keychain.zig`

Upstream Zig issue for the connect bug: https://codeberg.org/ziglang/zig/issues/31391

title: Enforce eval time budgets
body:
## Summary

- An eval that runs past its `timeoutSec` now stops `fx ask` and fails with "fx ask did not finish within Ns" instead of waiting for the Bun test timeout.
- A timed-out eval still removes its temporary home directory.
- `runEval` passes `fx ask --timeout` in seconds, so fx's default shell command limit matches the eval budget instead of about 41 hours.

title: Keep progress text out of published PR and issue titles
body:
## Summary

- `fx pr --create` and `fx issue --create` publish the model's final response, so text written before a tool call no longer becomes the title.
- The published body keeps its Markdown, including bold and inline code.
- A draft without a body, including an empty final reply, fails with the existing parse error instead of being published.
- A leading heading marker or `**` bold wrapping the whole title line is removed before publishing. Inline code in titles is kept.

title: Compact the session catalog cache
body:
## Summary

- Store the derived session catalog in a compact binary format that uses less disk space and memory during listing.
- Rebuild missing, corrupt, or older catalog caches from canonical saved sessions without changing listing or resume behavior.

title: Preserve terminal scrollback on fresh session commands
body:
## Summary

- Keep visible conversation output in terminal scrollback when `/new`, `/clear`, or `/reset` starts a fresh session.
- Leave composer and command picker rows out of the preserved history.
- Wait for a resize to settle before switching sessions, then deliver input typed during the wait to the new session.
- Cancel an active turn before a resize-deferred session switch. Keep queued work until the scrollback handoff and buffered input replay finish.
- If a partial handoff is interrupted by resize, keep the old session. If the active turn or terminal size does not settle, cancel the switch and deliver buffered input to the old session so commands like `/quit` still work.

title: Add an experimental v2 session store to fx ask
body:
## Summary

- Add `--sessions-v2` to `fx ask` (before or after `ask`) and `FX_SESSIONS_V2=1`. With either, `fx ask` saves the session as an append-only log in `~/.fx/sessions/v2/<id>/`.
- Resume those sessions with `--resume last` and `--resume-id`; they are only visible with the flag on. `--no-save` still writes nothing.
- Save each finished exchange while the turn runs. After a crash, the prompt and finished tool calls are kept, and the next resume marks that turn interrupted.
- Store tool output side files in `~/.fx/session-files/<id>/`, owner-only like the log.
- On resume, cut a half-written last line. A damaged line elsewhere stops the resume with `InvalidSessionFormat` and leaves the file unchanged. A session another process holds fails with `SessionBusy`.
- Report a missing session with the current store's errors, `NoSavedSessions` and `SessionNotFound`.
- Recover profile usage from v2 sessions after a crash, as for current sessions.
- Leave subagents off in `fx ask` while the flag is on.
- Keep the current store as the default; it now ignores the `v2` folder.
- Keep the session manager in `src/core/session_manager/`. It imports only `std` and its build options, and only `src/core/session/session_adapter.zig` imports it, which a unit test checks. `storage_fault.zig` and `trace.zig` compile only with the module's test hooks, which fx's build leaves off, so no fx binary or test step includes them. They are kept so the module stays identical to its standalone source.

title: Add the experimental v2 session store to interactive fx
body:

- Keep images, fetched pages and command output for v2 sessions in `~/.fx/session-files/<id>/`.
- Show `fx --sessions-v2 --resume <id>` in the exit hint, and keep the flag when fx relaunches after an upgrade.
- Leave subagents off in interactive fx while the flag is on.
- List `--sessions-v2` in `fx --help`.

title: Keep running tool calls and OS error names in v2 sessions
body:
## Summary

- With `--sessions-v2`, a tool call is saved before it runs, so killing fx while a tool runs no longer loses that call.
- On resume, a call that was still running when fx stopped comes back with a failed result telling the model the tool may have partly run.
- A tool that finished before the crash keeps its real result, and a turn fx cancelled itself comes back as before.
- When a v2 session can't be saved, fx reports the OS cause (`NoSpaceLeft`, `AccessDenied`, `ReadOnlyFileSystem` or `FileTooBig`) instead of `Io`. Every later call on that session reports the same first cause, even when a background sync was the one that failed.
- On v2, when the app can't open or save a session at startup, it says why instead of printing the bare error name. For example: "fx: this session cannot be saved: the disk is full. Free some space, then resume again." v1's messages are unchanged.
- On a full disk, a v2 turn now says the disk is full (`NoSpaceLeft` in `fx ask`, "Session could not be saved: the disk is full" in ACP). Before each model request a v2 session writes a small usage marker, and that write used to fail as `DurableReplacePreRenameFailed`, which names no cause. A durable replace can now record what stopped it, and only the marker asks.
- A new v2 session that can't be saved, for example in a read-only sessions folder, reports the cause (`AccessDenied`) instead of `Io`.

title: Pack syntax highlighting word lists
body:
## Summary

title: Harden fx-owned git reads against repository-configured programs
body:
## Summary

- Opening fx in a copied repository no longer runs a configured fsmonitor program while building the `@` file index.
- `grep_files` and `glob_files` use the same Git guards when searching inside a repository.
- Direct `git status` and `git diff` disable filter drivers supplied by the repository. The direct route continues to ignore user-level Git config.
- Direct `git log` pins a format that cannot request signature verification from a repository-configured `gpg.program`.
- `fx pr` and `fx issue` snapshots suppress repository filters and hooks, omit unsafe worktree details when filters cannot be verified, and run Git from a fixed path.
- fx-owned Git reads block lazy-fetch transports, nested submodule diff programs, and implicit adoption of bare repositories inside a checkout.

title: Store ACP sessions in sessions v2
body:
## Summary

- With `FX_SESSIONS_V2=1`, `fx acp` creates, loads, resumes and lists sessions in the v2 session log. The wasm build stays on v1.
- A new ACP session is written to disk only after its first prompt.
- `session/list` keeps v1's order, page size, cursor format and `cwd` matching.
- `session/load` replays the whole conversation, including turns from before a compaction, without the compaction handoff.
- Model, effort and provider changes, the generated title and token usage are saved with the session and restored on load.
- The ACP client system prompt, the MCP tool identities that load replays and the `cwd` of `session/new` and `session/load` work on v2 as they do on v1.
- A v2 session resumed or loaded from another folder lists under that folder right away, not only after it closes.
- A session killed during a prompt loads with that turn interrupted, and a tool that was still running is reported as failed and possibly partly run.
- Loading a session that another process has open returns "Session is busy".
- A load that hits a permission, read-only or full-disk fault answers "Session could not be loaded: permission denied" (or the matching cause) instead of "Session not found". A prompt that can't be saved answers "Session could not be saved: the disk is full" (or the matching cause) instead of "Io".
- ACP image prompts are saved with the session and replayed on load. A deleted image loads as "Image #1 unavailable".
- Images on a new v2 session no longer fail with `ImageSnapshotPathUnsafe` in `fx ask`, the app or ACP.
- The managed TTY shell works in v2 sessions.
- Listing or reading v2 sessions on an empty home creates nothing.
- Loading the full history of a 10K-turn session takes 34 ms, against 39 ms on v1.
- Subagents stay off on v2 sessions.
- A paused model response is not resumed on v2 sessions.

title: Run subagents on sessions v2

## Summary

- Each subagent is its own v2 session that names its parent and stays out of session lists.
- The parent's session log records when each subagent's work starts and finishes. No `children.json`, `owner.json` or `children.lock` is written.
- A named subagent keeps its history and instructions across fx runs.
- Work that a crash lost before the subagent started is reported as `child_lost`, and the next message to that name starts the subagent fresh.
- Subagent work left unfinished by a crash is recorded as interrupted when the parent session reopens.
- ACP load replays subagent calls with their results.
- A subagent keeps no paused-response checkpoint on v2 sessions.

- `fx session recover <id>` copies a damaged v2 session up to its last complete turn, side files included, into a new session. The source is left as it was, and a session with no complete turn is refused.

title: Run more end-to-end tests against sessions v2
body:
## Summary

- `FX_SESSIONS_V2=1` now reaches fx in every tmux test. Panes on the shared tmux server took that server's environment, so with the switch set the interactive suites still ran on v1. When the switch is unset, the pane has it unset too.
- With the switch set, `tui-resume` finds sessions under `~/.fx/sessions/v2` and expects the resume hint and the Ctrl+G relaunch to keep `--sessions-v2`. 47 of its 67 tests now pass on v2; the other 20 read or write v1 session files directly.
- New v2 tests for flows that had none: a resumed `fx ask` turn keeps the session's language; `fx ask` compacts on its own and resumes from the summary; a piece over 256 KB is kept as a blob and sent whole on resume; the app resumes a compacted session; text typed while the app answers steers that turn and is saved inside it; a cancelled reply is saved as cancelled; the app talks to the user while a child runs; a parent killed while a named child runs a tool records that work interrupted; a named child keeps its history after the app is killed; and a hosted terminal keeps running through an app crash, and the resumed app reaches it and stops it.
- Fault tests for the app, ACP and subagents: killed between turns, killed while a tool runs, a torn last line, a flipped byte, a missing blob, a read-only session, a second process on the same session, and a full disk. Each checks what the host says, that the log is left as it was, and that the session resumes afterwards. A damaged child log fails that message and the parent turn goes on.
- A fault grid crosses every way a run can leave a session (committed, cancelled, killed mid-reply, killed mid-tool) with every fault (none, a torn last line, a flipped byte, a missing blob, a read-only folder, a full disk, a second process) and every way back in (`fx ask` by id and by last, the app by id and with `-c`, ACP load and resume), plus a new session in each host. A refusal must name its cause and leave the log as it was, a fault that clears must give way, and a session that comes back must show the model the history the run left. On macOS the full disk is a real disk image filled to the last byte; elsewhere a file-size limit stands in.
- With `FX_TRACE_SCOPES=wiring`, v2 writes one trace line for each session step a host takes: the store opening and closing, a session opening and closing, a turn starting and ending, and a child starting and finishing. Each line names its session and process, so a run's session steps can be checked in order.
- The full-disk tests now size their limit from the shell's own block. Bash, which is `/bin/sh` on macOS, counts 1024-byte blocks and dash counts 512, so the old `fx ask` limit left twice the room it meant to on macOS.
- Running the suites this way found two bugs, fixed in the PRs that own the code: the picker froze for two seconds on a session open in another fx (#1073), and resuming an interactive session with a shell result hung (#1079).

Nothing changes when `FX_SESSIONS_V2` is unset.

title: Keep steering typed after a tool result when a turn is cancelled
body:
## Summary

- Cancelling a turn dropped any steering the user had typed right after a tool result, such as a message sent while a subagent was still running. The saved turn lost it, so a resume and the model never saw it again.

title: Close ACP gaps for embedded clients
body:
## Summary

- Keep tools from MCP servers the client supplies loaded on every turn. A server entry can opt out with `_meta.fx.alwaysLoaded: false`.
- Run a model call to a live MCP tool that is not loaded yet through the normal MCP permission path instead of rejecting it.

- Fail `session/load` and `session/resume` when a stored client system prompt cannot be read, keeping a different active session in place.

- Mark discovery calls such as `capability_search`, `mcp_select_tool`, and `read_tool_result` with `_meta.fx.toolCall.internal`, and add the MCP server, original tool name, and server title to MCP tool calls.

- Use the `cwd` on `session/new`, `session/load`, and `session/resume` as the session workspace, and start project MCP servers in it.

## Summary

- Preserve pasted, file-backed, and libfx image originals instead of resizing them during capture.
- Keep ACP image prompts usable when an image cannot be sent, with a saved source path instead of an early size error.

title: Allow skill symlink authorities in profile settings
body:
Adds a profile setting, `skill_symlink_authorities`, that does what `FX_SKILL_SYMLINK_AUTHORITIES` does today: symlinked skills may resolve into the listed absolute directories instead of being skipped with "authorize its external location". This lets tools that install skills as links into their own bundle, such as Codiff linking `~/.agents/skills/codiff` into `/Applications/Codiff.app/...`, work through `~/.fx/settings.json` without exporting an environment variable to every shell.

```json
{ "skill_symlink_authorities": ["/Applications/Codiff.app/Contents/Resources/app/codex/skills"] }
```

- The key is profile-only, so a committed project `.fx.json` can never grant filesystem authority. A workspace override replaces the global list.
- Entries must be absolute paths without `..` components, with at most 32 entries. An invalid value reports a specific `skill_symlink_authorities` config diagnostic instead of a generic malformed-settings error.
- The configured list is combined with the env var, which keeps working unchanged. Paths are canonicalized once at startup, so entries such as `/tmp/...` also match on macOS.

Authority checks run deep in skill discovery, refresh, and the skill tool, well away from any settings object. So startup installs the resolved list process-wide in `skill_runtime`, guarded by a mutex, following the pattern `debug_trace` uses for its startup configuration. That mirrors the env var's existing process-wide scope instead of threading a new parameter through every discovery caller. A workspace switch re-runs startup and replaces the list.

title: Add the technical-writer skill for repository prose
body:
## Summary

- Add the `technical-writer` skill in [`.fx/skills/technical-writer/`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/b/technical-writer-skill/.fx/skills/technical-writer/SKILL.md). It sets a voice for developer documentation, lists patterns to cut such as filler and hype, and asks writers to check technical claims against the source. The same skill was added to vercel/chat in [vercel/chat#976](https://github.com/vercel/chat/pull/976).

title: Keep the FIFO test's reader open until its writer joins
body:
## Summary

- The linked metadata FIFO test in `skill_runtime.zig` could hang the whole unit run. Its helper thread blocks opening the FIFO to write, and the test's cleanup released it by opening the read end and closing it right away.
- Under load the writer could miss that window: it went back to sleep with no reader left, and the `join` never returned. A stack sample of a hung run showed the main thread in `join` and the helper in `openat`, at 0% CPU for 36 minutes.
- The read end now stays open until the `join` returns, so the writer always gets a reader.

Test-only change. The full unit suite passes locally (9550 of 9552, 2 skipped).

title: Add one-command Slack MCP setup
body:
## Summary

Slack setup currently requires an MCP URL, a Client ID, and a separate authorization command. Add `/mcp add slack` and `fx mcp add slack` to save the fx preset, open the existing HTTPS PKCE flow, and connect Slack. The `/mcp` Servers tab also provides an **Add Slack** action with the `s` key.

- Read the personal scope set from the existing fx.sh configuration.
- Repair a missing fx Client ID and preserve other servers, timeouts, and explicit scope overrides. Stop with guidance if an existing Slack configuration conflicts with the preset.
- Reuse working credentials, including after removing and re-adding the preset. Keep an authorization already in progress intact.
- Make Slack tools available in the current session and show success only after the connection succeeds. Explain declined consent and authorization timeouts.

Workspace bot installation and the fx-web OAuth bridge are unchanged. Slack workspace approval can still be required.

- Built with Zig 0.16.0 and exercised the fresh binary through the CLI and a real tmux TTY with local OAuth/MCP fixtures.

[Full CI](https://github.com/samcx/fx/actions/runs/36642982436) passed on Linux x86_64, Linux ARM64, macOS Intel, and macOS Apple Silicon for commit `75abbef2`. Live Slack consent has not been repeated for this shortcut.

title: Navigate lists with Emacs-style Ctrl+N and Ctrl+P
body:
The composer follows Emacs and readline editing keys (Ctrl+A, Ctrl+E, Ctrl+K, and others), but lists did not. After typing `/`, Ctrl+N stepped through prompt history and Ctrl+P opened the model catalog.

**Behavior**
- Ctrl+N and Ctrl+P move down and up in any visible list, like the arrow keys. Ctrl+J and Ctrl+K remain aliases.
