title: Report fx lifecycle states to Otty
body:
## Summary

- Report fx activity to Otty automatically.
- Support processing, input waits, completion, and error badges.

## Problem

- Otty cannot observe individual fx turns or approval prompts.

## Solution

- Connect interactive lifecycle events to Otty’s custom-agent integration.
- Keep reporting asynchronous with bounded shutdown and an opt-out.
- Add focused lifecycle and hung-reporter coverage.

title: Reuse model catalogs across libfx agents
body:
## Summary

- Reuse scoped model catalogs across discovery and fresh agents while keeping every discovered model selectable.
- Give native and Wasm agents selected-model metadata to avoid parsing the full catalog on warm turns.
- Refresh stale catalogs after first text and register background work with the serverless host.
- Refresh stale catalogs after rejected agent creation so later attempts can use updated capabilities.
- Keep custom-fetch catalogs private by default, with explicit sharing for stable connections.
- Reject repeated catalog fetches, oversized metadata and catalog-size latency regressions in Node and Bun CI.

title: Make the compactor independent of the session module
body:
## Summary

- Move the saved-turn count and history range helpers unchanged from the session module into `src/core/shared/history_range.zig`, used by the session, session log, CLI, ACP, subagents, agent loop and compactor.
- Hand the session's projection of saved turns into chat messages to the compactor through `compactor.Request`, like the model caller and record store.
- Remove the session module exception from the compactor boundary check.
- Behavior is unchanged.

title: Load all Grok subscription models
body:
## Summary

- Discover all supported Grok subscription models from the live provider catalog.
- Keep subscription models available when optional public modality metadata is missing or unavailable.
- Use provider-supplied reasoning options and context limits for subscription-only models.

title: Share sessions v2 history replay
body:
## Summary

- Share one sessions v2 history walker across restore, session detail, TUI and ACP replay, and subagent results.
- CI confirms ReleaseSafe file reductions of 16,416 bytes on macOS arm64, 32,776 on macOS x86_64, 22,144 on Linux arm64, and 30,432 on Linux x86_64. Production PGSO savings and replay-specific performance and memory qualification are pending.

title: Add opt-in Ultrafast mode
body:
## Summary

- Request Ultrafast only for OpenAI models with priced Gateway catalog support, using an OpenAI-only route.
- Enable, disable, and inspect the requested mode with `/ultrafast` in the interactive shell.
- Select Ultrafast through Settings and the model picker's speed choices.
- Set profile defaults with `ultrafast_mode` and use process-only `FX_ULTRAFAST` overrides.
- Accept `--ultrafast` and `--no-ultrafast` in interactive launches, `ask`, and ACP; reject conflicting flags before sending a request.
- Keep Fast and Ultrafast independent and mutually exclusive.
- Preserve saved preferences across resume without persisting CLI or environment opt-ins.
- Advertise a per-session ACP Ultrafast option for eligible models and persist explicit changes across both session backends.
- Carry the request into temporary and named subagents while honoring child preferences and an explicit parent disable.
- Accept Ultrafast options in native and WebAssembly libfx and reject unsupported options on older native addons.
- Verify priced catalog support before the first embedded-terminal Ultrafast request without requiring the model menu or adding catalog I/O to normal startup.
- Show one bright yellow lightning marker for Ultrafast in light and dark themes, while Fast keeps its plain marker.
- Include the selected effort and speed in model-switch notices.
- Warn when Gateway does not confirm that a requested Ultrafast response used that tier.
- Keep titles, permission reviews, and compaction outside Ultrafast mode.
- Preserve default-off saved-session compatibility and the existing normal and Fast request paths.

title: Send libfx images as raw bytes
body:
## Summary

- Accept image prompts as `Uint8Array`, `Buffer`, `ArrayBuffer`, or another typed array with a `mimeType`, in addition to `Blob`, `File`, and base64.
- Send prompt image bytes to the agent core as raw bytes beside the prompt message, so base64 appears only in the model request.
- Pass native model requests to `fetch` as a raw body instead of base64 encoding the whole request across the addon boundary.
- Add a `resizeImage` option to `createFxAgent()` that receives and returns `{ bytes, mimeType }`. Size limits apply to its output, and the returned bytes are copied so the hook can reuse its buffer.
- Store prompt images in checkpoints as raw bytes and move checkpoints between JavaScript and the core without base64. Existing checkpoints still restore, but older libfx versions cannot restore the new format.
- Reject a restore checkpoint that references a stored image more than once, out of order, or not at all.
- Run concurrent `checkpoint()` calls one at a time. A call queued behind another fails like a direct call if a prompt starts before it runs.
- Throw a `TypeError` from `prompt()` for base64 image data that is not canonical, instead of failing the turn later.
- Measure image limits in raw bytes: 3.75 MiB per image and 6 MiB per prompt, matching the previous 5 MiB and 8 MiB of base64. A prompt's text and encoded images still share one 8 MiB limit.

title: Gate CI on Linux and run macOS only when a change needs it
body:
## Summary

- Run the full deterministic E2E suite on Linux in four shards on every pull request, plus the MCP conformance baseline, all against one shared build of fx.
- Run macOS arm64 unit tests and platform E2E files only when a change touches a Zig file with a macOS, BSD, or Linux code path, `build.zig`, macOS signing, the native SDK addon, a listed platform E2E file, or a shared E2E helper that reads the platform, or carries the `ci:macos` label. A manual dispatch of the macOS workflow also runs them. Otherwise the `macOS arm64` check passes without a macOS runner. The check fails when the detector cannot read the change.
- Run the macOS platform E2E files in two weighted shards that share one macOS build.
- Remove the four-platform Full CI workflow and the separate cross-target compile jobs.
- Smoke-test every Binary Size target, and reuse the base build for later pushes to the same pull request.
- Build the SDK WASM surfaces and Node-API addons once and share them across the SDK test jobs. `Build & Test` requires every SDK job.
- Restore Linux Zig caches from `main` on pull requests, and save them only from `main`, keyed by the Zig version and build files.
- Run PGSO on pull requests only when the PGSO pipeline changes, and keep release PGSO evidence for 90 days.
- Run the long-turn memory, libfx runtime, and live ACP jobs only on request, without cancelling the push run on `main`.
- Limit libfx publishing to an archive check, an install smoke test, and a registry byte comparison.
- Add a warning when an E2E file passes only on retry.
- Remove the unused Prepare Release workflow and document the new CI rules.

title: Restore the session replay code footprint
body:
## Summary

- Restore specialized sessions v2 history replay. The shared walker saved 16,416 PGSO file bytes but increased peak RSS by 162–172 KiB on 64-turn histories in both measurement orders.
- Keep the existing history format, recovery, compaction, and replay outputs. Footprint verification of this correction is pending.

title: Move sessions v2 bodies to blobs and terminal state to its own folder
body:
## Summary

- Behind `--sessions-v2`, fx no longer creates `~/.fx/session-files/{id}/`. A session is its folder under `~/.fx/sessions/v2/`, holding its log and read-only blobs.
- Large tool results, tool images and command output are kept as blobs of the session, and `read_tool_result` reads them after a resume.
- A long command's output streams to a temporary file outside the session while it runs, then is kept as one blob.
- Prompt images are saved inside the turn, so a resumed session sends them again even after the original file is gone.
- A web-fetch download is a read-only blob, and the model gets that file's path.
- Hosted terminal state lives in `~/.fx/terminal/{id}/`. A terminal outlives an app crash, and the resumed app can reach and stop it.
- An ACP client's system prompt and MCP tool identities are saved as session settings.
- Compaction records are kept as blobs, so `read_tool_result` on M12 or T12 still works after a restart.
- A sessions v2 session from an earlier build moves off `~/.fx/session-files/{id}/` on its first open, and its old handles and images keep working.
- `fx doctor` removes leftover terminal and session-files folders whose session is gone.
- A subagent's turn is saved when its work starts, so a crash after that records the work as interrupted instead of lost.

title: Avoid sorting ordered compaction records
body:
## Summary

- Keep compaction records in the same order without sorting completed turns again.
- Preserve fact validation for completed turns when the last turn is still running.

title: Replace the byte-at-a-time memset in the fx executable
body:
## Summary

- Run `fx sessions --json` 16% faster on Linux with 8 saved sessions and 46% faster with 64. This is the command that exceeded the 2 ms Startup Latency budget on slower CI runners.
- Run `fx status --json` 13% faster and `fx doctor --json` 21% faster on Linux. `fx help` and plain startup do not change.
- Fill memory 32 bytes at a time in Linux executables instead of one byte at a time. Zig 0.16's compiler_rt memset stores one byte per iteration, and safe builds call it for every `undefined` buffer.
- Leave macOS unchanged. Wall time there did not move with the new memset, and the macOS arm64 PGSO build links compiler_rt's object, where a second memset is a duplicate symbol. The macOS binary is byte-identical to main's. The WASM surfaces and the Node-API addon also keep the toolchain's memset.
- Give the late tool settlement E2E test a 120,000-file corpus on Linux. Searches there now finish before the test's second Escape, so the tool settled before the cancel and the test saw a second gateway request. The test also asserts that the cancel came first.

title: Fix compaction note retries, entry checks and damaged checkpoints
body:
## Summary

- Ask once more for the notes of every compacted turn with work that a reply left without notes, including replies with only entries.
- Keep a plain-text reply as the notes of the newest turn, and ask once more only for the other turns with work.
- Mark a decision, status or open-question entry that names no turn or tool call with `[check: no source]`, as rules and facts already are.
- Mark an entry about one failed tool call that calls it a success with `[check: T<n> failed]`.
- Read a checkpoint whose turn, tool call or compaction count no session reaches as damaged, so the next compaction numbers new records after the saved ones instead of crashing.
- Leave saved record files numbered past that count out of the numbering.

title: Avoid redundant Base64 decoding buffers
body:
## Summary

- Decode prompt images, saved binary data, and recovery chunks without a second Base64 buffer.
- Preserve canonical Base64 validation, exact payload bytes, and existing format limits.

title: Raise the CI unit test timeout
body:
## Summary

- Give the ReleaseSafe unit test step in CI 1500 seconds instead of 900, so normal runs on main no longer time out before the tests finish.

title: Raise the unit test timeout to 25 minutes
body:
## Summary

- Raise the ReleaseSafe unit test timeout in CI from 900 to 1500 seconds.
- The test step now takes 820 to 900 seconds on pull requests and on main. Main's last two pushes, 7e39bf1 and 88e6658, failed with `Unit tests elapsed: 900s` and exit code 124, not on a failing test.
- The limit still stops a hung test run well before the job's default timeout.

title: Keep a running step's text when fx crashes on sessions v2
body:
## Summary

- With `--sessions-v2`, when fx crashes or is killed while a tool runs, the text that came with that tool call shows again on resume, above the call's failed result. This holds in the interactive app, `fx ask` and ACP `session/load`.
- The first request after such a crash includes that text, so the model sees its own plan for the interrupted command.
- Text from an earlier step that already finished is not repeated on a later step that was still running.

title: Decode saved identifiers without hex round trips
body:
## Summary

- Read saved session identifiers and digests in one pass, retaining exact-length lowercase validation and existing errors.

title: Report fx state to the cmux sidebar
body:
Stacks on PR #1106

When fx runs inside [cmux](https://cmux.com), it shows its state as an `fx` status pill in the workspace sidebar: **Running** while it works, **Needs input** while a permission prompt or question waits, **Error** when a turn fails, and **Idle** when a turn finishes. A waiting prompt also posts a cmux notification. fx removes the pill when it exits. Reports carry only the state and the kind of prompt, never prompts or tool output. `FX_CMUX=0` turns it off.

fx detects cmux from `CMUX_SOCKET_PATH` and `CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID`, and writes one line per report to cmux's control socket using the same commands the `cmux` CLI sends: `set_status`, `clear_status`, and `notification.create_for_caller`, prefixed with `CMUX_SOCKET_CAPABILITY` when present. Like herdr, each report uses a short-lived connection with a 250 ms reply timeout, so an unavailable cmux never blocks the session. Pill icons and colors match cmux's own Claude Code and Codex pills.

**Shared foreground observer**

This builds on the `WorkerRuntime.foreground_observer` added in #1106. The worker has one observer slot, so the shared terminal status provider in `builtins/hooks.zig` now owns it and fans resume and settle events out to herdr, cmux, and Otty. Otty's `Hooks(App).configure` no longer installs the observer itself; it exposes `foreground_working` and `foreground_settled`, and `configureNotifications` runs Otty's configuration first so the shared provider knows whether to include it. Otty's behavior is unchanged.

As a result, herdr and cmux now return to working state after a permission or question is answered, instead of staying blocked until the turn ends.

**Not included**

- cmux rejects `fx` as an agent lifecycle key, so fx appears as a status pill rather than a first-class cmux agent.
- cmux does not reap statuses for dead agent PIDs, so fx does not register its PID; a crash can leave a stale pill, as with herdr.
- Session restore through `surface.resume.set` is left for a follow-up.

title: Draw the first frame before slow startup work
body:
## Summary

- Show the first frame before reading a Keychain-backed fx login or stored key on macOS. A prompt sent before the login loads waits for it, then sends.
- Load skills after the first frame. Skill menus fill in when the catalog lands, and skill discovery issues are reported then.
- Check the other sign-in sources after the first frame when a credential is already active, so a launch with an environment key no longer loads Security.framework before drawing.
- Wait at most 1 ms for input before drawing the first frame, instead of 8 ms.
- Stop waiting up to 200 ms for terminals that ignore the background color query. The startup probe now ends at the device attributes reply.
- Show "skills: loading" in the full-transcript session details while skills are still loading.
- Add benchmarks/first_frame.py to measure time to the first frame and compare builds under the same load.

title: Add durable session journals to libfx
body:
## Summary

- Record each libfx session in a journal the host supplies (`createFxAgent({ journal })`, with `append` and `load`), and restore the session from it on either backend.
- Store a turn's prompt before the model sees it, and a `replay: "never"` tool call before the tool runs. Other appends don't hold up the turn.
- Stop the turn at once when an append fails: no further model requests or tool calls, and the turn fails with `FX_JOURNAL_APPEND_FAILED`.
- Continue a turn that a crash left open with `agent.resume()`. A call that was running runs again, under the same call id, when its tool is `replay: "safe"`, and comes back answered as possibly run otherwise, so a `replay: "never"` tool doesn't run again. A turn that fails or is cancelled ends in the journal as it ends in the agent, and is not resumed.
- Require `replay: "safe"` or `replay: "never"` on host tools when a journal is set, and pass the model's `toolCallId` to `execute`.
- Accept host tools as an object keyed by tool name, as well as an array.
- Report a host tool that fails with an empty error as `Tool <name> failed without a message`, since providers reject an empty error result.
- Run host tools in parallel on the native backend, up to 16 at a time, except a tool marked `writes: true`, which runs alone.
- Stop an agent once another agent has appended to its journal: `createMemoryJournal` and World sessions reject its next append with `FxFencedError`, and the turn stops.
- Keep the AI Gateway session id across restores with `sessionId`, or the id `load()` returns.
- Return an id from `turn.steer()` that resolves once the steer is stored, take back an unplaced steer with `turn.withdraw(id)`, and deliver a stored steer when its turn resumes after a crash.
- Queue a turn to run after the current one with `agent.followUp()`. Follow-ups survive a crash; after a restore, each held follow-up waits for a `resume()` call, without holding up follow-ups the new agent queues.
- Read only the newest progress of an open turn on load, so long tool-heavy turns still restore within the 4 MiB load limit.
- Call the journal's optional `close()` when the agent closes or its core exits.
- Refuse to resume a turn that started under different instructions, tools, or model, with `FxConfigMismatchError`. `prompt()` still works.
- Reject journals written by a newer libfx with `FxJournalVersionError`, and journals that are too large or do not fold with the codes `FX_JOURNAL_TOO_LARGE` and `FX_JOURNAL_INVALID`.
- Name the request's model in the journal event written before each model request.
- Hand a running turn to another process with `turn.cancel({ reason: "handoff" })`: the turn stops without ending, and the next agent resumes it.
- Accept AI Gateway model metadata through `modelCatalog`, so the agent makes no catalog request and image prompts work behind a proxy that refuses it.
- Store a session in a Workflow World with `createFxAgent({ world, sessionId })`, using the World the app already has, such as `createWorld()` from `@workflow/world-vercel`. Each journal append is one event in the session's run, the run id becomes `agent.sessionId`, and libfx imports no Workflow package. `worldHandler({ world, createAgent })` is the queue route that resumes a session without a caller once its process stops. A handed-off turn resumes once its agent closes, and a wake for a session that can't open or resume, after a config change or with a journal that is too large or invalid, is answered with the reason instead of retried. Checked against a real world-vercel project as well as world-local: restore, fencing, and a route takeover that does not rerun a `replay: "never"` tool. When the World cannot queue a wake, as outside a deployment, the turn goes on and the agent emits `journal.wake_failed`.
- Deprecate `checkpoint()` and the `checkpoint` option. Both still work and emit a `deprecated` event.

title: Title a v2 session whose first turn crashed
body:
## Summary

- With `--sessions-v2`, a session whose first turn was cut off by a crash or kill is titled from its first prompt when its next turn ends, instead of staying "Untitled session" in the `fx -r` picker and `fx sessions`. This holds in the interactive app, `fx ask` and ACP.
- A resumed session that already has a title keeps it; later turns don't change it.

title: Add a pool of hidden terminals for child programs
body:
## Summary

- Add a `sub_engine` module that starts programs on their own pseudo-terminals, so fx can write to them, resize them and close them the way a terminal multiplexer does.
- Run up to ten of those terminals from one reader thread, which hands each child's output, report lines and exit to its owner in order.
- Give each child a report channel, a Unix socket pair named in its environment, for lines meant for the owner instead of the screen. The owner can reply on it, and a child that exits first can't kill fx with SIGPIPE.
- Queue a reply the report channel can't take at once and send the rest when it has room, so a long reply reaches the child whole.
- Report how many report lines were dropped when a terminal closes.
- Hang up every child before waiting on any when the pool shuts down, so they exit within one grace period.
- Leave fx's behavior unchanged: nothing uses the module yet. It is the base for experimental subagents behind `--subagents-v2`.

title: Report a child fx's state to the fx that launched it
body:
## Summary

- When fx starts in a sub-engine terminal whose environment names a report channel, report its session ID, whether it is idle or working, each message it takes, each turn's final reply and any open permission or question prompt, one JSON line per event.
- Apply answers the parent sends back on that channel to the prompt they were meant for, once, through the same paths as answering on the child's own screen.
- Write a question answered by the parent into the child's transcript, and cancel the child's turn when the parent cancels a question, as Esc does.
- Claim the report channel before fx starts any other program, so MCP servers and other subprocesses don't inherit it.
- Report `pasted` once a paste lands in the composer, so a parent presses Enter only after its text arrived.
- Pass a completed turn's final reply to post-turn-end hooks.
- Change nothing when fx runs on its own: without a valid report channel in the environment, reporting stays off.

Stacked on #1130.

title: Add an experimental subagent tool that runs each child as a full fx
body:
## Summary

- Add `--subagents-v2` and `FX_SUBAGENTS_V2=1`, which replace the `subagent` tool in the TUI, `fx ask` and ACP with one that runs each child as a full fx in its own hidden terminal, up to ten at once.
- Let the agent `launch` a named child with a task, `send` it a message, `wait` until children settle, `read` a child's final reply, messages or screen, `list` the children and `stop` one. A stopped child's session stays saved.
- Give children the main fx's provider, model, effort, permission mode and folder, and no subagent tool of their own.
- Send each child the main fx's user requests before its task and each message. A child runs its turns as a subagent's, so in auto mode its actions are reviewed against what the user asked, not against text the main agent wrote.
- In the TUI, show a child's permission and question prompts on main, labeled with the child's name, and send the user's answer to that child. Esc denies or cancels only that prompt.
- In the TUI, keep `wait` waiting while the user answers a blocked child's prompt.
- In `fx ask` and ACP, a child's prompts don't reach the user yet: a blocked child ends `wait` and stays blocked until it is stopped.
- Refuse a `send` to a child that is waiting on a prompt, so only the user answers it.
- Clear a child's draft when a message can't be delivered, and stop a child whose launch is cancelled before it takes its task.
- Stop every child when the main fx exits, after any subagent call in progress has stopped.
- List `--subagents-v2` in `--help`.

Stacked on #1131.

title: Add a live view of subagents behind Ctrl+T
body:
## Summary

- With `--subagents-v2`, open a picker of the main fx's children with Ctrl+T, listing each child's name and whether it is starting, working, idle, waiting on a prompt or exited.
- Show the chosen child's own fx at full size, with a status line naming it, and send every key straight to that child until Ctrl+T returns to main.
- Recognize Ctrl+T and Esc in the view and picker while Caps Lock or Num Lock is on.
- Keep every child at the terminal's size as it is resized, and repair main's screen on return when the terminal was resized meanwhile.
- Return to main when the viewed child exits.
- Hold main's own prompts while a view is open, with "main needs you" on the status line, so a key meant for the child never answers them. Ctrl+T then shows the prompt.
- Count the other children waiting on a prompt on the status line, since their prompts can't show while a view is open.
- Show a viewed child's permission and question prompts on its own screen instead of on main.
- Ignore Ctrl+T while the full transcript or another screen holds the alternate screen.
- Leave Ctrl+T unbound without `--subagents-v2`.

Stacked on #1132.

title: Preserve MCP credential refresh failure details
body:
## Summary

When saved MCP OAuth credentials fail to refresh, `/trace` reports a generic failure, and authentication classification can replace even that message with sign-in advice. Preserve the error name, request or response stage, HTTP status, and recognized OAuth error code in server health and trace reports, including when `FX_TRACE` is off.

Only typed, allowlisted response details enter the diagnostic. Raw response bodies, error descriptions, and credentials stay out of output. Recovery and unrelated failures clear the saved refresh diagnostic.

## Validation

- ReleaseSafe build and four focused Zig unit tests passed.
- Ten focused MCP E2E cases passed, including a TTY `/trace` interaction with tracing off and a successful login, refresh, and logout lifecycle. Stderr was clean.
- Zig formatting, public-surface audit, compactor boundary check, and PGSO corpus tests passed. The existing `mcp-auth.test.ts` training classification still covers the file's common OAuth lifecycle behavior.
- Regression cases cover oversized refresh responses and recognized OAuth errors returned with HTTP 200. Both cases failed before the fixes and pass afterward.
- Full CI passed all four native platform aggregates and all 16 E2E shards for `48060701`. Startup Latency and the manual final ship audit also passed.

## Tracking

Required classification: `type: improvement`.

Linear: [AX-5122](https://linear.app/vercel/issue/AX-5122/preserve-mcp-credential-refresh-failure-details)

title: Fix false compaction check marks and close finished open entries
body:
## Summary

- Count the user's answers to questions as their words when checking that a rule quotes the user. The questions themselves still do not count.
- Look for an entry's values in the conversation that stays after the compaction too, including the rest of a turn in progress, so a value read there is no longer marked as found nowhere.
- Tell the model that a status entry can close an open entry it answers or finishes, so finished next steps stop staying in force.
- Say in the README that only long numbers are checked.

title: Allow larger MCP OAuth scope requests
body:
## Summary

- Support MCP OAuth requests with larger scope lists.

## Problem

- The 64-scope cap blocks authorization before browser consent.
- The scope source in the reported Datadog failure remains unconfirmed.

## Solution

- Allow up to 1,024 unique scopes without truncating requests.
- Preserve scope validation and Slack's 64-scope bridge cap.
- Add boundary tests and end-to-end authorization coverage.
- Verify built-binary authorization with 129 scopes locally.

title: Load shell startup files once per fx process
body:
## Summary

- Commands that use the `user` profile run the login shell's startup files (zsh or bash) once per fx process. fx captures the resulting `PATH`, environment, aliases, functions, and shell options, then restores them for every later command. Subagents share the same capture.
- fx captures again on the next command after a watched startup file changes: `.zshenv`, `.zprofile`, `.zshrc`, and `.zlogin` in `ZDOTDIR` and `HOME`, their `/etc` and `/etc/zsh` copies, `.bash_profile`, `.bash_login`, `.profile`, `.bashrc`, `/etc/profile`, `/etc/bash.bashrc`, and `/etc/bashrc`.
- `/shell reload` makes the next command run the startup files again. The model can do the same with `reload: true` on `shell.run`.
- A reload clears the session's remembered command approvals. Cleared approvals no longer show in the approvals list or the status count. Other kinds of approvals stay.
- When a capture fails, exceeds 8 MiB, or takes longer than 10 seconds, fx runs the startup files for every command, as it does today, and says so once: a notice in the interactive shell, a warning on stderr in `fx ask`, and the first line of the ACP `tool_call_update` for the command that hit it.
- When restoring a capture fails inside a command, fx reruns that command with full startup.
- In auto mode, a routine command that uses a captured alias or function goes to the safety review. While captures are failing, routine commands go to the review instead of running right away.
- The shell tool description tells the model that startup files apply, that `cd`, `export`, and alias changes do not carry over between calls, and how zsh treats unquoted globs and words that start with `=`.
- The terminal host daemon (`--fx-internal-terminal-host`) and the tmux backend are removed, along with the `FX_TERMINAL_HOST_*` environment variables. `tty: true` terminals still run a full login shell, now inside the fx process, and end when fx exits. On resume they show as ended, and recovery reads only the resuming session's terminal records.

## Benchmarks

Measured with ReleaseSafe builds of `main` (d3c28f3d9) and this branch, using a fake model so only fx and the shell are timed. The macOS runs are on macOS arm64.

### Synthetic heavy startup files, macOS

`benchmarks/shell_command_overhead.py`, which also runs as a new CI job, sends N sequential `ls` calls and one `printenv PATH` through a local fake gateway. The isolated HOME has startup files with 400 aliases, 300 functions, 40 `PATH` edits, and a 200 ms sleep per load. Login shell: zsh. Per-call time is the gap between gateway requests.

| Metric | main, 10 calls | this branch, 10 calls | main, 100 calls | this branch, 100 calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Startup file loads | 10 | 1 | 100 | 1 |
| Total time | 2,994 ms | 774 ms | 26,720 ms | 4,603 ms |
| Median per call | 258.8 ms | 41.1 ms | 264.0 ms | 40.5 ms |
| Mean per call | 260.8 ms | 64.9 ms | 263.8 ms | 44.7 ms |
| p95 per call | 273.8 ms | 277.2 ms | 274.7 ms | 54.6 ms |
| Fastest call | 251.4 ms | 36.5 ms | 248.9 ms | 35.0 ms |
| Slowest call | 273.8 ms | 277.2 ms | 280.6 ms | 286.8 ms |
| `printenv PATH` call | 305.8 ms | 39.7 ms | 273.4 ms | 43.1 ms |
| `PATH` from startup files | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| CI budget check | fails | passes | fails | passes |

Over 100 calls, total time drops 5.8x and the median call 6.5x. The slowest call on this branch is the first one, which pays for the single capture. With only 10 calls that one call is also the p95.

### Synthetic heavy startup files, Linux

Same benchmark on a Linux arm64 VM (Debian, bash login shell), ReleaseSafe builds of the same two commits:

| Metric | main, 10 calls | this branch, 10 calls | main, 100 calls | this branch, 100 calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Startup file loads | 10 | 1 | 100 | 1 |
| Total time | 2,880 ms | 881 ms | 24,819 ms | 3,134 ms |
| Median per call | 254.5 ms | 53.0 ms | 238.8 ms | 27.9 ms |

| `PATH` from startup files | yes | yes | yes | yes |

Over 100 calls, total time drops 7.9x and the median call 8.6x.

The new CI job on this PR (GitHub's Linux x86_64 runner, bash, 100 calls): 1 startup file load, 2,718 ms total, 21.9 ms median, 34.2 ms p95, within its 60 ms median budget.

### Real startup files

My own zsh setup: 1,149 captured names, a 35,539-byte replay, captured in 105 ms. Ten `echo $PATH` calls:

| Metric | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Total time | 1,189 ms | 499 ms |
| Median per call | 116 ms | 40 ms |
| First call | 122 ms | 141 ms, including the capture |

A bare `zsh -l -i` takes 80 ms (median) on the same machine. `PATH` (20 entries), all 30 aliases, all 94 functions, and every environment variable name matched `main` exactly. The only differences are interactive-only shell options such as `autocd` and the history settings.

### Real model

`tests/evals/shell-path-ab.test.ts` asks the model to run `echo $PATH` in 10 separate calls, 3 trials per binary. Both binaries passed 3/3 trials with the startup-file `PATH` in 10/10 outputs. Wall time is dominated by model latency (28.7 s to 72.3 s per trial on either side; medians 33.6 s on `main`, 40.4 s here), so this eval checks correctness, not speed.

### Terminals after exit

`fx ask` starting a `tty: true` terminal running `sleep 6.43`, 3 runs per binary:

| Metric | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Terminal after fx exits | keeps running until its command ends, 6.3 s later | already ended when fx exits |
| Host daemon | still running 15 s after fx exits | none |

### Startup latency and size

`benchmarks/startup.sh --quick` (hyperfine means), two interleaved rounds shown as round 1 / round 2:

| Command | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `fx` | 1.9 / 1.7 ms | 1.9 / 1.9 ms |
| `fx help` | 1.9 / 2.0 ms | 1.8 / 1.9 ms |
| `fx status --json` | 2.2 / 2.2 ms | 2.3 / 2.2 ms |
| `fx doctor --json` | 2.3 / 2.2 ms | 2.3 / 2.3 ms |
| `fx sessions --json` | 3.0 / 3.0 ms | 3.0 / 2.9 ms |
| Bare process baseline | 1.3 / 1.3 ms | 1.5 / 1.2 ms |

Every difference is within 0.2 ms, which is run-to-run noise here.

Linux CI enforces the 2 ms budget. On this PR it measured 0.5 ms for `fx`, 0.6 ms for `fx help`, 0.9 ms for `fx status --json`, 1.0 ms for `fx doctor --json`, and 1.6 ms for `fx sessions --json`.

Stripped ReleaseSafe binary size from the Binary Size check, against `main`:

| Platform | main | this branch | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linux x86_64 | 13,444,216 bytes | 13,176,096 bytes | -268,120 bytes (-1.99%) |
| Linux arm64 | 11,383,880 bytes | 11,147,792 bytes | -236,088 bytes (-2.07%) |
| macOS x86_64 | 13,898,761 bytes | 13,619,917 bytes | -278,844 bytes (-2.01%) |
| macOS arm64 | 11,705,504 bytes | 11,459,184 bytes | -246,320 bytes (-2.10%) |

## Notes

- The capture and each command reach the shell over stdin.
- The CI job's 60 ms median budget is provisional. Linux CI runners use bash as the login shell, so that job measures bash.
- The benchmark's fake gateway turns off Nagle. With it on, Linux delayed ACKs added about 40 ms to every reply in the fixture itself; the Linux numbers above use the fixed fixture for both binaries.
- `src/core/execution/command_runner.zig` was never imported by the test root, so its tests never ran. They run now.
- Before this change, the terminal host had no config file setting. Its only knobs were the `FX_TERMINAL_HOST_IDLE_MS` and `FX_TERMINAL_HOST_PROTOCOL_*` environment variables, which this removes.
- A session's first command is approved before the capture exists, so the alias check does not apply to it.
- Partial restore failures and the approval reset are covered by unit tests only.
- `tui-resume.test.ts` "streaming scroll stays inline while Ctrl-O preserves native selection and ignores horizontal arrows" is flaky on `main` too: 2 of 10 local runs at d3c28f3d9 fail with the same 5-row shift after the command output is consolidated. It failed on one macOS x86_64 shard here and passed on rerun.
- The macOS arm64 PGSO candidate needed two reruns: `tui-permissions.test.ts` in a training shard (different tests per attempt; the same scenario fails PGSO on other branches, and the file passes 25/25 locally) and one `ui-activity-progress-bench` round out of 43 (the bench passes 500/500 locally on this branch and on `main`).
- fx does not detect edits to files that the startup files source; `/shell reload` covers that. Tools that switch the environment by directory, such as direnv or mise hooks, apply the environment of the directory where fx captured.

title: Retry gateway connections after an interrupted connect
body:
## Summary

- Retry a model request when opening its connection fails with an unexpected system error before anything was sent, such as a connect on macOS that a signal interrupted and that then finished in the background. The request used to fail the turn.

title: Exit without waiting on MCP servers or the usage ledger
body:
## Summary

- Exit kills every stdio MCP server at once instead of one at a time, so closing fx with Ctrl+C is 2.8x faster on macOS (20.6 ms to 7.4 ms).
- Quitting right after a reply no longer waits for the first usage ledger read, so that exit is 36x faster on macOS (303 ms to 8.4 ms) and 44x faster on Linux (1,003 ms to 23 ms). That usage stays with the session and is recorded when the session resumes.
- Pending MCP authentication and menu operations are still cancelled and logged at exit.
- An MCP server that is still launching is waited for, up to 1 s, and docker-backed servers keep the full teardown.

## Benchmarks

Median time from the second Ctrl+C, `main` at `d3c28f3` against this branch, builds interleaved. macOS runs used a real zsh and profile with 2 local and 3 remote MCP servers and a 33.5 MB `usage.jsonl`. Linux runs used a 4 vCPU Vercel Sandbox with a synthetic ledger of the same size.

| Case | Rounds | `main` | This PR | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| macOS, quit 0.67 s after launch, fx gone | 25 | 20.6 ms | 7.4 ms | 2.8x |
| macOS, quit 0.67 s after launch, shell prompt back | 25 | 26.2 ms | 13.3 ms | 2.0x |
| macOS, quit right after the first reply | 4 | 303 ms | 8.4 ms | 36x |
| Linux, two stdio MCP servers, quit at 10 s | 18 | 7.2 ms | 5.5 ms | 1.3x |
| Linux, quit right after the first reply | 10 | 1,003 ms | 23 ms | 44x |

title: Route terminal host status through one publisher
body:
Stacks on PR #1126

herdr, cmux, and Otty each kept their own copy of fx's foreground state, driven by different event sources, so they drifted: only Otty restored "working" after a subagent approval, herdr kept its startup session forever, and nothing settled after `/compact`. This replaces the three per-host state machines with one status model and one publisher.

**Shape**

- `status.zig` derives the only status hosts see (`idle`, `working`, `waiting` with the kind of prompt, `failed`, plus the session) from lifecycle events through a pure `next(state, event, session)`. The subagent approval overlay and session-change reset live here, covered by table tests.
- `terminal_status.zig` is the front door. `publish(event, session)` applies `next` and queues the status only when something visible changed. One publisher thread renders queued statuses in order to every detected host, so host I/O never runs on the UI or worker threads, and every visible transition is delivered (Otty's E2E contract) with overflow keeping the latest.
- `hosts/herdr.zig`, `hosts/cmux.zig`, and `hosts/otty.zig` translate `Status` values into each host's wire format and skip changes they cannot show. Wire formats and Otty's bounded child-process transport are unchanged.
- `Hooks(App, activeSessionId)` connects PostTurnEnd, AttentionRequired, the worker's foreground observer, and approval-prompt observations to `publish`.

**Removed**

Otty's event queue, `foreground_state`, `sync_child_approval`, and its separate hook registrations; cmux's `last_state`; the shared provider in `builtins/hooks.zig`; the Otty-first configuration ordering; the `@hasField(App, "otty")` checks; the three `reportWorking` calls in `main.zig`; and three differently placed shutdown calls, now one `terminal_status.deinit()` after the foreground worker stops.

**Behavior changes**

- herdr and cmux return to working when a subagent approval resolves, matching Otty.
- The worker loop reports start and outcome for every work item, so manual compaction settles instead of staying "working".
- herdr receives the new session after `/new` or `/resume`.
- herdr shows route-recovery pauses as blocked instead of idle.

**Boundary**

`scripts/check-terminal-status-boundary.sh` runs in CI next to the compactor check. It rejects deep imports into `builtins/terminal_status`, direct `app.herdr`/`app.cmux`/`app.otty` access, and host imports beyond the status model, socket transport, and shared basics. `AGENTS.md` records the rule.

title: Return unknown model tools as failed calls
body:
## Summary

Return well formed but unadvertised Chat Completions tool names to fx's tool dispatcher. The dispatcher reports them as unsupported tools without executing them, so the model can continue instead of ending the request with `InvalidToolName`.

## Verification

- `zig test` for the Chat Completions protocol: 60 tests passed on the clean branch.
- `zig fmt --check src/` passed.
- Built the current commit on Termux and ran `./zig-out/bin/fx` against a local Chat Completions fixture. The fixture emitted `unknown_tool`; fx returned `Unsupported tool: unknown_tool` and completed the follow-up response.

Missing arguments and malformed history remain rejected.\n\nVerification: 60 protocol tests pass, formatting passes, and the fresh Termux binary was rebuilt. Both commits on this branch are SSH-signed.

title: Preserve completed native HTTP responses
body:
## Summary

- Let successfully consumed native model responses reach HTTP EOF so later requests can reuse their connections.
- Keep streamed text and model results independent of HTTP tail cleanup.
- Abort pending requests immediately on cancellation or failure.
- Bound successful tail cleanup to 100 ms and 64 KiB so stalled or oversized responses cannot hold close indefinitely.

title: Custom providers: an undeclared model id is sent anyway, and fx reports the requested model rather than the serving one
body:
## Summary

With a custom (BYOK) `openai-chat-completions` connection, fx writes any requested model id to the socket without checking it against that provider's `model_metadata`, then reports back **the id that was requested** instead of the one the endpoint actually served. Plenty of OpenAI-compatible servers treat `model` as a display label rather than a selector — llama.cpp-derived servers, halogen, ollama's default, llama-swap peers — so the engine answers with whatever it happens to be running.

The user-visible result: exit 0, a normal completion, and a session record naming a model that never ran. Nothing in fx, the terminal, or the JSON says a different engine answered.

## Environment

fx 0.0.12 (built from tag `v0.0.12`), Linux x86_64, NixOS. No AI Gateway involved:

```json
{
  "provider": "host1",
  "providers": {
    "host1": {
      "protocol": "openai-chat-completions",
      "base_url": "https://host1.lan/v1",
      "auth": { "type": "none" },
      "model_metadata": {
        "Qwen3.8-125B-A6B": {
          "context_window": 262144,
          "max_output_tokens": 32768,
          "supports_tool_use": true,
          "supports_vision": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Only `Qwen3.8-125B-A6B` is declared. A second model, `Qwen3.8-27B`, runs on host2 — that is what the request was for.

## Reproduction

```
fx ask --model Qwen3.8-27B --json "When will the AI financial bubble pop?"
```

- exits 0, returns a completion
- the JSON reports `"model": "Qwen3.8-27B"`
- the 27B host's server journal recorded **zero** requests during the call
- the engine on host1 answered

Control run, same command with the declared id: 1 request in host1's engine log, 0 on the 27B host2. The only way to find out which model answered was to watch the engines from outside fx.

The same shape hits the `subagent` tool's `model` override, which is where it actually bit: children asked for the 27B were recorded under `"provider": {"name": "host1"}`, ran on the 125B, and the tool returned `ok: true`. Routing a subagent to a cheaper model is exactly the case where silent substitution is expensive — the bill looks right and the provenance is wrong.

## Cause, as far as v0.0.12 source goes

1. `src/core/config/configured_provider.zig:229` (`parse_metadata`) validates the *shape* of `model_metadata` — entry count, `max_output_tokens < context_window`, boolean types — and nothing downstream ever requires a requested id to appear in that list.
2. The subagent path does have a validator: `src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig:391-429` rejects with `ambiguous_model` / `unknown_model`. But the app-side resolver at `src/core/app/app_callbacks.zig:911-927` returns `.no_catalog` the moment `snapshotCachedModelIds()` is null, and `src/core/app/model_cache_runtime.zig:567-571` returns null unless the cache reached `.ready` with a non-empty catalog — that cache is `/v1/models`-shaped and AI-Gateway-oriented. `.no_catalog` is an explicit pass-through (`src/core/subagent/model_contract.zig:17-18`, skipped at `src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig:392-394`), so on a custom connection an arbitrary model string reaches the wire. `FX_TRACE=1 FX_TRACE_SCOPES=subagent` logs it as `model override resolution skipped … reason=no_catalog`.
3. The response's own identity is discarded. `src/gateway/chat_completions_protocol.zig:723` parses the response `model` into `response_model`; the only other mentions in the tree are the field declaration (`:653`) and its `free` (`:693`). It is never compared to the requested id and never surfaced, so `fx ask --json`'s `model` field is a restatement of the request.

## Expected

Either, and the second is the stronger fix:

- **Validate the request.** For a custom connection, hard-error when the requested id is not in `model_metadata`, listing the declared ids. `model_metadata` is the only truth fx has about a BYOK endpoint; right now it is treated as decoration.
- **Validate the response.** Compare `response_model` against the requested id and error (or at minimum warn) on mismatch. This also catches servers that answer with a *different* model even when the requested id is perfectly legal: quant swaps, router fallbacks, OOM degradation, an engine restarted under a new `--served-model-name`.

The silence is the bug. A mismatch that announces itself is a one-line fix for the user; a mismatch that reports the requested name corrupts session provenance permanently, and the user has no reason to suspect it.

## Repro with no GPU

`fake-llm.py` — an OpenAI-compatible server that ignores the requested model, like some of the real ones do:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Answers every /v1/chat/completions with the same model id."""
import json
import threading
import urllib.request
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

HOST, PORT = "127.0.0.1", 8799
SERVING = "served-model-AAA"


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        req = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
        body = json.dumps(
            {
                "id": "cmpl-1",
                "object": "chat.completion",
                "created": 0,
                "model": SERVING,  # ignores req["model"]
                "choices": [
                    {
                        "index": 0,
                        "message": {
                            "role": "assistant",
                            "content": f"asked={req.get('model')} answered={SERVING}",
                        },
                        "finish_reason": "stop",
                    }
                ],
                "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 1, "completion_tokens": 1, "total_tokens": 2},
            }
        ).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass


if __name__ == "__main__":
    HTTPServer((HOST, PORT), Handler).serve_forever()
```

Point a custom connection at `http://127.0.0.1:8799/v1`, declare only `served-model-AAA` in `model_metadata`, then ask for anything else: fx reports the name you asked for while the server answers `served-model-AAA`.

(The server's own mismatch behaviour is verified; the fx leg needs a settings.json entry to run, so treat it as a recipe rather than a captured transcript.)

title: Load AGENTS.md in the browser terminal from its workspace
body:
## Summary

- The browser terminal (`createFxTerminal`) sends AGENTS.md project instructions to the model on every turn when its workspace adapter provides `readFile`, reading `<home>/.fx/AGENTS.md` and `<root>/AGENTS.md` the way the CLI reads them from disk.
- A browser terminal whose workspace adapter has no `readFile` tells the model that `<root>/AGENTS.md` was omitted and adds a `[context]` notice to the full transcript instead of dropping the instructions silently.
- Workspace adapters accept an optional `readFile({ path, signal })` that returns a string, UTF-8 bytes, or `null`. fx calls it only for `AGENTS.md` paths inside the workspace root or home, with a 10-second deadline, and the interrupt key cancels it.
- AGENTS.md files read through the host follow the CLI's size limits, and unreadable or non-UTF-8 files are reported as omitted.
- Browser agent turns use the host workspace root, the same root their tools already use, instead of the WebAssembly process root `/`.

title: Persist libfx sessions through a store the host supplies
body:
## Summary

- Persist a libfx session through a store the host supplies, `createFxAgent({ persistence })`, with `load()`, `append({ expected, idempotencyKey, data })` and an optional `saveCheckpoint({ through, data })`, and restore it on either backend. Records and checkpoints are opaque bytes, and the store picks the cursors that order them.
- Send one append at a time, each naming the cursor of the record before it, so a store can refuse a write that does not continue its head. A refused append fails with `FxFencedError`, and the agent stops.
- Save a checkpoint after a turn once the records stored since the last one reach `checkpointAfterBytes` (1 MiB by default), and restore from the latest checkpoint plus only the records after it. A failed save emits `checkpoint.error` and changes nothing.
- Store a turn's prompt before the model sees it, and a response's tool calls before any of them runs. Other appends don't hold up the turn.
- Stop the turn at once when an append fails: no further model requests or tool calls, and the turn fails with `FX_JOURNAL_APPEND_FAILED`.
- Continue a turn that a stopped process left open with `agent.resume()`. Calls that were running come back to the model as possibly run, and the model decides what to do. A turn that fails or is cancelled is not resumed.
- Run a call again on resume when the host knows it never ran: `resume({ onAmbiguous })` asks about each running call, and a call it returns `"rerun"` for runs again under the same call id.
- Make a retried prompt the same turn with `prompt(input, { turnId })`: it continues the open turn with that id, or returns at once when that turn already ended. `turn.id` is the turn's id.
- Pass `{ signal, turnId, callId }` to each host tool's `execute`, so a tool can key its own retries on the turn and call.
- Accept host tools as an object keyed by tool name, as well as an array.
- Report a host tool that fails with an empty error as `Tool <name> failed without a message`, since providers reject an empty error result.
- Run host tools in parallel on the native backend, up to 16 at a time, except a tool marked `writes: true`, which runs alone.
- Keep the AI Gateway session id across restores with `sessionId`.
- Return an id from `turn.steer()` that resolves once the steer is stored, take back an unplaced steer with `turn.withdraw(id)`, and deliver a stored steer when its turn resumes.
- Queue a turn to run after the current one with `agent.followUp()`. Follow-ups survive a crash; after a restore, each held follow-up waits for a `resume()` call.
- Hand a running turn to another process with `turn.cancel({ reason: "handoff" })`: the turn stops without ending, and the next agent resumes it.
- Read only the newest progress of an open turn on load, so long tool-heavy turns still restore within the 4 MiB load limit.
- Reject records written by a newer libfx with `FxJournalVersionError`, and records that are too large or do not fold with `FX_JOURNAL_TOO_LARGE` and `FX_JOURNAL_INVALID`.
- Accept AI Gateway model metadata through `modelCatalog`, so the agent makes no catalog request and image prompts work behind a proxy that refuses it.
- Add `createMemoryPersistence()`, a store that keeps records and the latest checkpoint in memory.

An alternative to #1128: the same durability through a generic store, with the Workflow World binding outside libfx.

title: Anthropic model usage never recorded: stream billing rejected without response-metadata timestamp, /v1/generation fallback 401s for fx login
body:
## Summary

When using Anthropic models through AI Gateway (e.g. `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`) with an `fx login` credential, usage and spend never appear in `fx usage` / `/usage`. The requests are billed by Gateway, but fx never records them. OpenAI models in the same session record correctly.

Two issues combine:

1. **Stream billing is discarded when `response-metadata` has no `timestamp`.** Gateway's Anthropic stream omits `timestamp` from the `response-metadata` event, so `parseSseBilling` rejects otherwise valid billing data in the `finish` chunk and fx falls back to a deferred `/v1/generation` lookup.
2. **The deferred lookup always returns 401 for `fx login` credentials**, and a 401 is classified as `preserve_pending`, so these requests stay pending forever and never settle.

## Environment

- fx `0.0.12`, `dev` update channel, macOS (Darwin 25.6.0)
- Provider: `gateway`, `credential_source: fx_login`
- Source checked at `6bdd497`

## Reproduction

```sh
FX_TRACE=1 fx ask --json --model anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 "Reply with just: ok"
FX_TRACE=1 fx ask --json --model openai/gpt-6.1-sol "Reply with just: ok"
```

Opus trace:

```
[sse] stream billing ignored reason=invalid_terminal_metadata
[session] usage generation queued sequence=1 id=gen_...
[gateway] generation usage lookup status=401 outcome=preserve_pending
[session] usage generation lookup preserved attempt=1
```

`~/.fx/usage.jsonl` then gets only a `pending` record for the Opus request, never a `generation` record.

GPT trace:

```
[session] usage exact generation settled sequence=1 id=gen_...
```

## Evidence

The SSE stream was captured via a loopback proxy using `FX_GATEWAY_BASE_URL` / `FX_GATEWAY_CHAT_URL`. No headers were logged.

`response-metadata` events:

```
Opus: {"type":"response-metadata","id":"msg_...","modelId":"claude-opus-5-5"}
GPT:  {"type":"response-metadata","id":"resp_...","timestamp":"2026-10-03T23:06:10.000Z","modelId":"gpt-6.1-sol"}
```

The Opus `finish` chunk does contain valid billing data:

- `usage`: `inputTokens {total: 21507, noCache: 4, cacheRead: 21503, cacheWrite: 0}`, `outputTokens {total: 4, text: 4, reasoning: 0}`
- `providerMetadata.gateway.cost`: `"0.0043966"`
- `providerMetadata.gateway.routing.canonicalSlug`: `"anthropic/claude-opus-5.5"`
- `providerMetadata.gateway.generationId` present

`GET /v1/generation?id=...` sent with the `fx login` credential:

```
401 {"error":{"message":"Authentication failed. Create an API key and set in AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY environment variable: ...","type":"authentication_error"}}
```

## Code paths

- `src/gateway/client.zig`, `parseSseBilling`: `const timestamp = created_at_ms orelse return error.InvalidSseBilling;`. `created_at_ms` only comes from `response-metadata.timestamp`, so a missing timestamp discards all stream billing.
- `src/gateway/host_stream_provider.zig`, `gatewayUsageOutcome`: falls back to `.deferred` when `completion.billing == null`.
- `src/gateway/generation_usage.zig`, `classifyStatus`: 401/403 → `.preserve_pending`, retried indefinitely with no path to settle.

## Impact

In one day of heavy Opus use, none of it appears in `fx usage` (30d report lists only OpenAI/Moonshot/DeepSeek models, `completeness: incomplete`). `~/.fx/usage.jsonl` holds 0 Opus `generation` records, with 58 unresolved `pending` IDs and 216 `incident` records for that day. The only way to see the spend is the Gateway dashboard.

Possibly related: during several long interactive Opus sessions, almost no `pending` records were written at all (only `incident` records), so some requests may not even be retained for later recovery. I have not isolated that path.

## Suggested fixes

1. In `parseSseBilling`, accept a missing `response-metadata.timestamp` and fall back to the local receive time (or the `finish` event time) instead of rejecting the billing data.
2. Make the `/v1/generation` lookup work for `fx login` credentials, or treat a 401 for that credential type as terminal (marked unrecoverable) instead of `preserve_pending`.
3. Gateway side: emit `timestamp` in `response-metadata` for Anthropic streams, as it does for OpenAI.

title: Keep stream billing when the response timestamp is missing
body:
Anthropic routes send `response-metadata` without a `timestamp`, so `parseSseBilling` discards the terminal cost and the request falls back to a `/v1/generation` lookup. For `fx login` credentials that lookup returns 401, and the usage stays pending forever.

Terminal billing now uses the local receive time when the timestamp is missing. A malformed or conflicting timestamp is still rejected.

The 401 on `/v1/generation` is a separate issue and not fixed here.

title: Claude/trusting allen eh3evy
Accept a nested tool request object sent as JSON text
body:
Fixes #1150.

## Problem

Tools that advertise one nested `request` object, `shell` and `read_tool_result`, read that object only when it arrives as a JSON object. Some providers, reported with `mimo-v2.6-flash` over `openai-chat-completions`, send the same object as its JSON text:

```json
{"request": "{\"action\": \"run\", \"command\": \"echo repro-hi\"}"}
```

`shell` could not decode the call, so the correction path answered `invalid_shell_request`, the model repeated byte-identical arguments, and the run aborted after five retries with `Repeated shell validation failures stopped the tool loop`. `read_tool_result` rejected the same shape outright. Flat-parameter tools were unaffected.

## Fix

`tool_args.requestObject` resolves the wrapper in one place. It returns the nested `request` object when the call has one, the arguments object when it does not, and decodes `request` when the value is its JSON text, bounded at 64 KiB. Text that does not decode to a bounded object returns null, so each tool keeps reporting its own shape problem.

`shell` decodes through that helper when `request` is the only top-level member. Fields beside `request` stay unresolved, so the correction path still reports a conflicting call. Terminal argument normalization accepts the same text, so admission, labels, and projection see the canonical flat object. `read_tool_result` decodes through the helper too.

## Verification

* `zig fmt --check src/` passes
* `zig build` produces `./zig-out/bin/fx`
* Focused Zig unit tests cover the object, encoded, nested-composite, and rejection forms in `tool_args`, `shell`, `read_tool_result`, and terminal normalization
* `zig build test` reports the same failure set as `main` in a local environment, so this branch adds no new failures
* New E2E owner in `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` runs the command once through the built binary
* Live reproduction against the reported configuration, with `mimo-v2.6-flash` as the model:

```text
# main
$ ./zig-out/bin/fx ask --no-save --yolo 'Use shell once to run: echo repro-base'
[notice] Repeated shell validation failures stopped the tool loop. The invalid shell calls were not executed and produced no shell effect.

# this branch
$ ./zig-out/bin/fx ask --no-save --yolo 'Use shell once to run: echo repro-hi'
Running `echo repro-hi` via shell.
repro-hi
`echo repro-hi` completed with exit code 0, output: `repro-hi`
```

The E2E file keeps its existing PGSO classification, so `scripts/pgso/corpus.json` needs no change.

Full CI has not run on this commit yet, so this stays draft until all four platform jobs and the ship gate pass.

title: Bug: ACP emits invalid StopReason values
body:
### Issue details

**Summary**

`fx acp` can return stop-reason values that are not members of the ACP `StopReason` enum. ACP clients that validate the response may reject the completed prompt as a protocol error.

**Observed in v0.0.13**

The native ACP serializer emits `refused`, `max_output_tokens`, and `max_model_turns`, which are not ACP `StopReason` values. This remains in the official v0.0.13 source: [src/acp/types.zig](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/v0.0.13/src/acp/types.zig#L89-L103).

**Specification references**

- The [ACP v1 Prompt Turn specification](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/prompt-turn#stop-reasons) defines `end_turn`, `max_tokens`, `max_turn_requests`, `refusal`, and `cancelled`; in v1, `session/prompt` returns the `stopReason`.
- The [ACP v1 schema](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/schema) is the machine-readable schema reference.
- The [ACP v2 migration guide](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v2/migration) says these stop-reason values are unchanged in v2, but completion moves to an idle `state_update`. It also notes the v2 surface remains draft and should be negotiated explicitly.

The installed fx v0.0.13 responds with `protocolVersion: 1` when the client offers version 2, so the v1 response behavior applies to this report.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Start `fx acp`, initialize it, and create a session.
2. Cause a prompt to end with a refusal, output-token limit, or model-turn limit.
3. Inspect the `session/prompt` result's `stopReason`.

The response contains `refused`, `max_output_tokens`, or `max_model_turns` instead of valid ACP values. A serializer-level test can verify each mapping without depending on a live model.

**Expected behavior**

Map `refused` to `refusal`, `max_output_tokens` to `max_tokens`, and `max_model_turns` to `max_turn_requests` at the ACP boundary. Internal fx reason names can remain distinct if needed.

### Trace

Not attached; no runtime trace was collected.

### Sensitive information

- [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

title: Add opt-in remote reporting
body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in remote reporting plus a minimal receiving API.

- **fx:** when `FX_REPORT_URL` is set to an `http(s)://` URL, fx POSTs one JSON report on process exit (`fx ask` and interactive). `FX_REPORT_TOKEN` is sent as a bearer token. Off by default; with the variable unset nothing is buffered or sent.
- **Contents:** fx version, commit, OS, arch, plus one entry per model call (model, status, duration, tokens, error name, stop reason) and per tool call (name, outcome, duration). Prompts, tool arguments, tool output, file paths, and command output are never copied into the reporter, so they cannot be sent.
- **Safety:** delivery runs on a short-lived thread; exit waits at most 3s. Nothing is written to stdout/stderr; failures go to the `FX_TRACE` log under `remote_report`. Queues are bounded at 256 model calls and 256 tool calls with dropped counts.
- **Receiver:** `apps/report-server/server.ts` (Bun) with `POST /v1/reports`, `GET /v1/reports`, `GET /v1/summary` (per-version, per-platform, per-model, per-tool counts, failures, avg/p50/p95/max), `GET /health`, optional `REPORT_TOKEN`.

Hook point: `src/core/workspace/diagnostics.zig` already receives every gateway and tool call, so the reporter taps it there. Exit flushes are in `src/main.zig`.

## Testing

- `zig build`, `zig fmt --check src/`: pass
- `remote_report.zig` unit tests (5): pass, including a redaction test that asserts tool args/results never appear in the payload
- `bun test ./remote-report.test.ts` (3): built fx against a fake gateway and the real receiver; secret prompt/file content/path absent from the report; unreachable endpoint does not fail or stall; wrong token gets 401
- `bun test ./ci-shards.test.ts`, `python3 -m scripts.pgso.corpus --list`: pass (new test registered as verification-only)
- Manual: interactive `./zig-out/bin/fx` in tmux with `FX_REPORT_URL`, one prompt, `/quit`: one report received, stderr empty

Full CI pending.

title: Flatten the shell tool's arguments
body:
## Summary

- Models call `shell` with flat fields: `command` starts a command, and `session_id` checks on it, types into it with `input`, or ends it with `stop: true`. There is no `request` wrapper or `action` field.
- Calls in the old shapes still run when fx can read them exactly: the `request` wrapper, a wrapper sent as a JSON string, and `action` with the old field names (`yield_time_ms`, `timeout_ms`, `tty`, `chars`).
- `wait` and `timeout` take seconds. Out-of-range waits are clamped instead of rejected, and a `timeout` of zero or less means no deadline.
- Fields that don't apply to a call are ignored instead of failing it.
- A call with both `command` and `session_id`, but no `input` or `stop`, is rejected with a message that says which form to send.
- `shell` accepts bash, zsh, sh, dash, ksh or an absolute path to one of them, with or without `interactive`.
- A non-interactive run in a shell other than the login shell starts without that shell's startup files and keeps the current environment.
- Model commands in zsh run with `equals` and `nomatch` off and `ksh_zero_subscript` on, so `=====`, unmatched globs and `${arr[0]}` behave as they do in bash. Interactive zsh sessions are unchanged.
- History replays accepted calls in the flat form and rejected calls exactly as sent. Arguments that are not JSON replay as `{}`.
- The advertised schema drops `profile`, `force` and `reload`; calls that still send them keep working.
- The tool description is shorter and points file changes to `edit_file` and `write_file`.
- A remembered approval no longer covers a shell call that asks to reload startup files.
- A shell call without an `action` no longer fails the whole turn.

title: Upgrade to Zig 0.17
body:
## Summary

- Build fx with Zig 0.17.0. `build.zig.zon` requires it, and every CI, release, benchmark, and libfx workflow installs it.
- Require macOS 15 or later for the macOS release binaries, which is Zig 0.17's default minimum. Binaries built with Zig 0.16 ran on macOS 13.
- Accept MCP authorization documents, gateway generation responses, and provider error bodies that are exactly at their size limit, because Zig 0.17's `allocRemaining` treats the limit as inclusive. `readFileToEnd` still rejects a file of exactly `max_bytes`.
- Use Zig's `memset` in Linux binaries in place of fx's replacement, now that Zig's version stores a full vector per iteration.
- Qualify PGSO builds with LLVM 22.1.8, the LLVM version in Zig 0.17.
- Run allocation-failure sweeps and allocation-count tests on an allocator that never resizes in place, so they make the same allocations on every run under Zig 0.17's `SafeAllocator`.
- Read and set terminal attributes with the kernel ioctls on Linux. Zig 0.17 sizes `std.posix.termios` to the kernel struct, but `std.posix.tcgetattr` calls glibc when libc is linked, and glibc writes its larger struct past the end of it. ReleaseSafe Linux builds crashed in the terminal launcher and on interactive startup.
- Build the MCP stdio dispatcher driver once before its E2E tests. Zig 0.17 spends about 50 seconds compiling its build runner against an empty cache, which is longer than the first test's timeout in the uncached macOS platform job.
- Stop using every standard library declaration that Zig 0.17 deprecates, such as `std.fmt.allocPrint`, the `std.mem.indexOf` family, `std.fs.path`, and `@import("builtin").os`. Most are exact renames. `std.mem.copyForwards` became `@memmove`, with each destination sliced to its source's length where it was longer, and the trace report maps `builtin.optimize` back to the `ReleaseSafe` style labels it printed before. The one deprecated call left is `b.addTranslateC`, because its replacement is the external translate-c package.
- Decode single UTF-8 sequences with a helper that checks the lead byte against the slice length. The deprecated `std.unicode.utf8Decode` reached an assertion when they disagreed, so inline rendering crashed when a truncated sequence preceded an emphasis delimiter.

- Profile the seed's verified bitcode in the distributed PGSO candidate job instead of rebuilding it. Zig 0.17 can number anonymous symbols differently on another runner, so a rebuild of the same commit no longer matches byte for byte.
- Link the PGSO candidate against a copy of Zig's macOS 27 `libSystem.tbd` without its `arm64e.x1` targets. The Xcode 16.4 linker on the macos-15 runners rejects that architecture, and the arm64 link never uses it.
- Unroll and fold constant-trip loops before PGSO instrumentation and profile use. Zig 0.17 emits array bitcasts as per-element loops, so the training profile counted every element and `mem.eqlBytes` dominated it, which pushed nearly all other code below the cold cutoff.

- Pressing Enter on a prompt starts a new session holding the conversation before that prompt and switches to it.
- The chosen prompt is put back in the composer, ready to edit or send.
- The new session gets its own id and is titled `<title> (fork)`; forking a fork keeps a single `(fork)`.
- The transcript shows the command that resumes the original session, which the fork leaves unchanged.
- `/fork` waits while a turn is running, and says there is nothing to fork in a session with no prompts.
- Without `--sessions-v2`, `/fork` says forking needs it.
- Esc, or typing in the composer, closes the menu.

title: Bug: requests hang forever when IPv6 is routed but unreachable (no fallback to IPv4)
body:
### Issue details

fx hangs forever, with no output and no error, on a network where the router hands out IPv6 addresses and an IPv6 default route but IPv6 traffic never leaves the LAN. Other clients on the same machine work, because they fall back to IPv4. fx does not fall back.

**Environment:** fx 0.0.13 (stable, build `4d966e272cfc`), macOS 26.6.2 on Apple silicon, Codex subscription provider. `fx doctor` reports `ok=8 warn=1 fail=0`, auth configured and refreshable.

**The network:** `en0` has global IPv6 addresses from SLAAC and a default route via the router's link-local address, but no IPv6 packet gets out:

```
$ curl -6 -m 8 https://chatgpt.com/   # Connection timed out after 8006 ms
$ curl -4 -m 8 https://chatgpt.com/   # HTTP 403 in 0.08 s
$ curl    -m 8 https://chatgpt.com/   # HTTP 403 in 0.18 s (falls back to IPv4)
```

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Be on a network whose IPv6 is advertised but broken. Without such a router, the same state comes from adding an IPv6 default route to a black hole.
2. Run `fx ask "reply with just ok"`, or `fx` interactively, or `fx acp` from an ACP client.

**Expected:** fx tries IPv6, sees it fail, and uses the IPv4 connection that is already open, as curl and browsers do (RFC 8305 Happy Eyeballs). At worst it fails with a timeout error.

**Actual:** fx never sends the request and never returns. Sampling the process's sockets with `lsof -i` during `fx ask`:

```
t=2s   IPv4 → chatgpt.com:443  ESTABLISHED  (four sockets, two Cloudflare addresses)
       IPv6 → chatgpt.com:443  SYN_SENT     (two sockets)
t=12s  same
t=20s  IPv4 sockets in CLOSE_WAIT  (the server closed them after sitting idle)
       IPv6 sockets still SYN_SENT
```

The IPv4 connections open within milliseconds but sit idle until the server drops them. fx appears to wait on the IPv6 attempts, which never finish. I killed it after several minutes. The same pattern happens earlier at startup with the provider version lookup to `registry.npmjs.org` (five IPv4 sockets ESTABLISHED, then CLOSE_WAIT). An older trace from the same machine on 2026-09-08 ends in `[models] provider version lookup failed provider=codex err=Timeout`.

Turning IPv6 off on the interface (`networksetup -setv6off Wi-Fi`) should work around it, but fx is the only tool on this machine that would need that.

This may be related to #439 (startup blocking on auth reachability) and #1034 (catalog validation timing out behind a proxy while completions succeed). In both of those, a request that never completes blocks fx with nothing on screen.

### Trace

`FX_TRACE=1 FX_TRACE_LOG=… fx ask "reply with just ok"`. Skill discovery lines are omitted, and the timestamps are cut:

```
[agent] event=prompt_start turn_id=1 prompt_bytes=18 model=gpt-6-astra
[agent] event=provider_admitted model=gpt-5.6-luna
```

Nothing else is written. I killed the process after 25 s, and it had made no further progress after several minutes in earlier attempts. Pointing `FX_E2E_CODEX_VERSION_URL` at a local server that answers at once does not change this, so the version lookup is not the only request affected.

### Sensitive information

- [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

title: Bug: openai-chat-completions fails with InvalidChunk against gateways that stream model:"" (Bifrost)
Keep image-heavy chat-completions sessions within request limits
body:
Follow-up to #964, which fixed tool image pricing for `prompt` and `input` request bodies but left chat-completions `messages` bodies priced as text.

## Problem

With an `openai-chat-completions` provider, retained tool images serialize as `image_url` data URLs and the request estimator counts their base64 as text. While usage calibration applies, the estimate looks fine. Once compaction drops the calibration, a few 1 MB images estimate at over 1M tokens and the turn fails with `ContextCapacityExceeded`. Later prompts in the same session fail the same way.

A 413 on a request carrying tool images also goes through context overflow recovery. Compaction keeps recent tool images, so the request barely shrinks and the retry fails again.

## Change

- Measure chat-completions `image_url` parts as image input, like the other request shapes.
- After a 413 on a request with tool images, retry once without compacting and send only the newest tool result's images from then on. Older images get a notice and stay reloadable through `read_tool_result`.
