title: Make libfx sessions durable
body:
## Summary

- `createFxAgent()` returns the agent at once instead of a promise, and does no I/O until a session runs a turn.
- `agent.session(id)` opens a session, and `session.prompt()` returns a turn view with `accepted`, `result`, async iteration over its events, and an NDJSON `readable`.
- `agent.newSessionId()` gives an id before the first prompt, every tool call receives `sessionId`, and `session(null)` throws like any other invalid id.
- Sessions are durable by default: `vercel()` on Vercel, `local()` files in Node.js elsewhere, and `memory()` in browsers. The `durability` option picks one.
- `libfx/durable-local` and `libfx/durable-vercel` bundle their World, so an app installs no other package.
- `world()` from `libfx/durable-world` keeps sessions in a World the app creates, such as Workflow's Postgres World. `local()` and `vercel()` are built on it. libfx never starts or closes a World it was given, and agents that share one take its deliveries in turn.
- A turn whose process crashes, redeploys, or reaches its function deadline continues from its last record in the next process that gets work for the session.
- On Vercel, a turn stops at its next model request 30 seconds before the function deadline and continues in a new invocation from the same queue message.
- A model request or tool call still running 2 seconds before the deadline is cut off, and `onEvent` receives `session.deadline`.
- A step the deadline cuts off 3 times in a row is not run again: a cut-off call is answered as possibly run, and a model request cancels its turn. `session.deadline` reports `cutoffs`, the times in a row the same step was cut off.
- One process runs a session's turns at a time, and a prompt for a busy session queues behind the running turn.
- On a session with no turn in progress, the first model request goes out while the worker writes the prompt and its lease. The turn writes, shows, and runs nothing until that claim lands, and a claim that lands after another worker's write counts for nothing: its model request is cancelled.
- A process that froze and was replaced stops at its next write and never starts a tool with effects, and `onEvent` receives `session.fenced`. A process that started a new turn on an idle session and was replaced while still claiming the session runs nothing for that turn and reads the session's log again instead, so the prompt it brought is not lost.
- A write that fails for any other reason emits `session.error`, and the queue delivers the message again.
- A harness that stops between turns, such as an fx engine whose kernel exited, is replaced on the next delivery, and the prompts queued behind it still run.
- Each turn runs with the `context` of the `session()` call whose prompt or steer started it.
- A started turn whose engine stops 3 times is cancelled, and the prompts behind it run; a prompt whose engine stops 3 times before its turn starts ends with an error. If the engine stops twice more, even to cancel, the session ends that turn and later prompts with an error without starting an engine, so a failing engine never retries a model request forever.
- A turn whose engine stops after storing its end resolves with stop reason `unknown`.
- After an interruption, a call to an `idempotent: true` tool runs again. Any other call never reruns, and the model gets an error saying it may have partly run.
- `executionId` is the same each time a call runs, including after a crash.
- A prompt sent again with the same `messageId` starts nothing new: its view follows the original turn, or resolves at once to that turn's outcome with `repeated: true`. A failed turn whose end never reached the stream resolves with the error the session's log recorded.
- A turn view's `readable` closes as soon as its turn ends, without waiting for the World to cancel its stream read.
- A prompt's `signal` cancels only that prompt's turn, whether it runs or still waits.
- A prompt the harness refuses, or a turn cancelled before it starts, ends once and never blocks the session's later prompts.
- `session.stream(cursor)` replays a session's events from any cursor on any server, with `turn_start`, `turn_end`, `turn_resume`, and `turn_yield` lines.
- Every reader of a session's stream shows the same lines, because lines a replaced worker lands late are hidden.
- A worker writes each stream line as soon as no write is in flight, without a batch timer.
- `session.steer()` and `session.cancel()` reach the session's running turn, and `session.resume()` continues a turn a stopped process left open.
- Every turn end and yield saves a checkpoint, so continuing a session reads one checkpoint and the records after it.
- Checkpoints record the libfx version, tool set, and model. A session or checkpoint saved under different ones still loads, and `onEvent` receives `checkpoint.mismatch`.
- `session.checkpoint()` exports a session's history, and the `checkpoint` option starts a new agent's session from it.
- `agent.wakeHandler()` is the queue delivery route an app mounts on Vercel and subscribes to `__libfx_wkf_workflow_session` in `vercel.json`.
- On Vercel, libfx authenticates to the AI Gateway with the deployment's OIDC token when neither `apiKey` nor `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` is set.
- `createFxEngine()` accepts a `persistence` store, and `createMemoryPersistence()` provides one in memory. A store that rejects a stale append with `FxFencedError` stops a second writer.
- A turn whose store append fails stops at once with `FX_JOURNAL_APPEND_FAILED`, and the agent refuses later prompts.
- When one model response calls several host tools, the native backend runs them at the same time and returns their results in call order. A tool marked `writes: true` runs alone. WebAssembly still runs calls one at a time.
- `createFxEngine()` agents gain `followUp(input)`, which queues text to run as its own turn after the current one and, with `persistence`, survives a crash.
- `turn.withdraw(id)` takes back a steer the model has not seen yet.
- The `modelCatalog` option supplies the AI Gateway model catalog, so the agent makes no catalog request.
- `tools` may be an object keyed by tool name.
- A tool error with no message reaches the model as `Tool <name> failed without a message` instead of an empty error, which providers reject.
- libfx ships TypeScript declarations for every entry point.
- `createFxEngine()` names itself in its option errors, and the README lists what code written for libfx 0.0.12 does differently now that `createFxAgent()` is durable.

## Known limitations

- A call that runs again after a crash skips the kernel's permission check. libfx allows every host tool call there today, so a rerun skips no decision, but the rerun path would need the check if libfx adds permission rules for host tools.
- A steer is dropped when it arrives while a stuck or cancelled turn is being cancelled, including after a failed engine open, or in a session that runs no more turns.
- After an engine outage, a started turn that ended with an error can end a second time when the next prompt's engine continues or cancels it.
- A `session.resume()` view of a session that runs no more turns can stay unsettled.
- A process whose clock froze can still land writes after its replacement takes over, until the World rejects stale writes.
- On `local()`, a live reader can occasionally see two adjacent stream lines in swapped order, which comes from the bundled World; the stored stream is in order.
- Cancelling a `session.stream()` read before its first read of the World connects leaves that read open.

title: Report interactive shell status with OSC 7501
body:
## Summary

- Report `idle` to the terminal with the [Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501)](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status) when the interactive shell starts.
- Report `working` while a turn or `/compact` runs.
- Report `done` when a turn completes.
- Report `blocked` with `kind=permission` and the request label while an approval prompt is open.
- Report `blocked` with `kind=question` and the question text while a question or recovery prompt is open.
- Report `idle` after a cancelled or paused turn.
- Report `error` after a failed turn or request.
- Report `done` when `/compact` succeeds and `error` when it fails.
- Report a second failure in a row again.
- Report `idle` instead of repeating the last result after other work that reports no result, such as a `/permissions remember` confirmation.
- Clear the terminal's status records when fx exits or receives SIGTERM or SIGHUP.
- Clear the terminal's status records on Ctrl+Z and report the current state again on resume, with an already reported result shown as `idle`.
- Send reports without a support query. Terminals without OSC 7501 support ignore them.

title: Report the default reasoning effort in fx status
body:
## Summary

- `fx status` and `fx status --json` report `effort`: the reasoning effort a new session in that workspace starts with, read from the same settings a session uses, workspace overrides first.
- `effort` is `auto` when no effort is set.
- Interactive `/status` output is unchanged.

title: Bind the remaining test servers to loopback
body:
## Summary

- E2E and eval test servers now bind `127.0.0.1` instead of the wildcard address. On machines running other loopback servers, their connections can no longer reach another process on the same port.
- Covers 25 servers in 17 files: the file-local fake gateways, the shared MCP fixtures, the servers inside the MCP, ACP and eval tests, and the two logout request catchers, which bound `0.0.0.0`. #1179 makes the same change to the shared fake gateway in `tmux-helpers.ts`.

title: Bug: web_fetch rejects every URL on IPv6-only (DNS64/NAT64) networks with NonPublicDnsAnswer
body:
### Issue details

`web_fetch` fails on every URL when the Mac is on an IPv6-only network with DNS64/NAT64 (common on phone hotspots and some carrier and enterprise Wi-Fi). The tool returns:

```
web_fetch transport failed … "error":"NonPublicDnsAnswer"
```

`curl` to the same URL from the same machine succeeds.

**Environment:** fx 0.0.13 (stable, build `4d966e272cfc`), macOS 26.6.2 on Apple silicon.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Join a network that synthesizes NAT64 addresses. On such a network, `fx.sh` resolves to its public IPv4 addresses plus DNS64 answers:
   ```
   $ dscacheutil -q host -a name fx.sh
   ipv6_address: 64:ff9b::40ef:6d41
   ipv6_address: 64:ff9b::40ef:7b41
   ip_address: 64.239.123.65
   ip_address: 64.239.109.65
   ```
2. Ask fx to fetch any page, for example "Call web_fetch on https://fx.sh/llms.txt".
3. The call fails with `NonPublicDnsAnswer`.

**Expected:** the fetch succeeds. `64:ff9b::40ef:7b41` is the RFC 6052 well-known NAT64 prefix wrapping `64.239.123.65`, a public address.

**Cause**

- [`isPublicIpv6`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/699910ecc09160414369a6adc16c69d6259b82b2/src/tools/web/url_policy.zig#L542-L554) admits only `2000::/3`, so `64:ff9b::/96` is treated as non-public.
- [`fetch`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/699910ecc09160414369a6adc16c69d6259b82b2/src/tools/web/http_fetch.zig#L149-L152) rejects the whole request if any resolved address is non-public, so the DNS64 answers fail the fetch even though the A records are public.

**Suggested fix**

Judge `64:ff9b::/96` by its embedded IPv4 address with the existing IPv4 policy. Private and loopback targets stay blocked (`64:ff9b::7f00:1` → `127.0.0.1` is still rejected before dialing), and the local-use prefix `64:ff9b:1::/48` (RFC 8215) is unchanged.

```zig
fn isPublicIpv6(bytes: [16]u8) bool {
    // NAT64 (RFC 6052 well-known prefix 64:ff9b::/96): judge the embedded IPv4 address.
    if (isNat64WellKnown(bytes)) return isPublicIpv4(bytes[12..16].*);
    // … existing checks unchanged …
}

fn isNat64WellKnown(bytes: [16]u8) bool {
    const prefix = [_]u8{ 0x00, 0x64, 0xff, 0x9b, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 };
    return std.mem.eql(u8, bytes[0..12], &prefix);
}
```

**Validation** (Zig 0.16.0, against `main` at `699910e` and the `v0.0.13` tag)

- New fixtures in `url_policy.zig`: `64:ff9b::7f00:1`, `64:ff9b::a00:1`, `64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe` and `64:ff9b:1::5db8:d822` are rejected; `64:ff9b::5db8:d822` and `64:ff9b::40ef:7b41` are admitted.
- New fetch-level test in `http_fetch.zig`: a fake resolver returning `64.239.123.65` plus `64:ff9b::40ef:7b41` succeeds with both addresses admitted, and `64:ff9b::7f00:1` fails with `NonPublicDnsAnswer` without dialing.
- Without the fix, both new tests fail (the fetch-level one with `NonPublicDnsAnswer`). With it, all 72 `web_fetch` tests pass.
- `zig build test`: 9,773 pass. The one failure, `assistant_stream … preserves ANSI OSC 8 code fence and table spans`, also fails on unmodified `main` here.
- A `v0.0.13` build with the patch fetches `https://fx.sh/llms.txt` normally.

The change is about 20 lines plus tests. Happy to open a PR if that's useful.

Related but different: #1172 (requests hang when IPv6 is routed but unreachable).

### Trace

_No response_

### Sensitive information

- [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

title: Add trusted local providers and OpenCode Go support
body:
Allow trusted local executables to supply model catalogs and streaming through native fx sessions. Bundle the user's 13 selected OpenCode Go models across Chat Completions, Responses and Messages, preserving built-in Vercel Gateway, Codex and Grok catalogs and preferences.

### Changes

- Validate manifests and cached catalogs without starting executables; require native consent and provider-owned credentials before activation.
- Support CLI, TTY, ACP, resumed sessions and persistent children with native tools, image snapshots, structured output and bounded reasoning replay.
- Keep one `deepseek-flash` selection mapped to `deepseek-v4.1-flash`. Admit effort from pinned per-model metadata and advertise schemas only for documented APIs.

- Default the Bun harness to `FX_SOUND=0`, retaining the notification suite's explicit opt-out.
- Restore compact help and deferred missing-auth admission; synchronize statusline checks with saved settings.

### Validation

- 153 focused native E2E cases pass, including all 13 model tool loops, six directed saved-session API switches, picker and held-child cancellation. Process polling: 698 snapshots, zero observed `afplay` launches, despite an ambient `FX_SOUND=1`.
- Personally driven CLI and private TTY tool continuations pass through all three APIs, with clean exits and empty TTY stderr. Offline fetched-source ReleaseSafe build passes. Existing focused help tests and CI-regression owners pass.

### Pending gates

- Required `type: feature` label needs a maintainer; contributor access is READ.

title: Report the permission mode that ACP sessions enforce
body:
## Why

A new `fx acp` session reported mode `ask` while it enforced the configured permission mode, which is `auto` by default. An ACP client that trusted the report, such as T3 Code's Supervised threads, ran writes without approval prompts. The cause was two fields for one fact. `ActiveSessionState` took its mode id from the registry default and its permission mode from configuration, and both session responses reported the registry default.

The session now holds one `*const ModeSpec`. New, loaded, and resumed sessions start in the registered mode that grants no more than the configured permission mode, and the responses report that mode. With the default configuration, `session/new` reports `code`. With `FX_PERMISSION_MODE=ask`, it reports `ask` and requests permission before each write.

Fixes AGE-24.

## Scope

- `Registry.startingMode` in `src/core/modes/mode_registry.zig` picks the starting mode: `auto` starts in `code`, `ask` starts in `ask`, and `full-access` starts in `code`.
- `ActiveSessionState.mode` and `ActivePrompt.captured_mode` in `src/acp/server.zig` replace the separate `mode` and `permission_mode` fields.
- Every activation path in `src/acp/sessions.zig` and both session response writers use the session's mode.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` documents the starting mode under ACP Embedding.
- Out of scope: `runSubagentChild` still pairs the live session mode id with the admission permission snapshot. That pairing predates this change.

## Tradeoffs

- Starting every ACP session in `ask` would also make the report honest, but it would ignore `FX_PERMISSION_MODE` and the `permission_mode` setting for every ACP user who configured `auto`.
- ACP has no full-access mode, so a `full-access` configuration now starts in `code` and runs with `auto` permissions. Reporting `code` while bypassing permission policy would repeat this bug. A full-access ACP mode is a separate product decision.

## Blast Radius

ACP, libfx, and WASM sessions change the mode they report at start. Enforcement changes only for `full-access`, which now gets `auto` reviews instead of a bypass. Clients that write the mode explicitly see no change.

## Verification

- New e2e tests in `tests/e2e/acp.test.ts` fail on `main`, where `session/new` reports `ask` for unset, `auto`, and `full-access` configurations. They pass with the fix on both session backends. They cover the reported mode for four configurations, an `ask` session that requests permission before a write, and a default session that writes without a request, reports `code` after a cold load in a second process, and requests permission after a switch to `ask`.
- The issue's steps against `./zig-out/bin/fx`: on `main`, the session reports `ask`, sends 0 permission requests, and writes the file. With the fix, the same session reports `code`, the mode it enforces.
- 139 focused Zig tests in the touched files pass. `zig build`, `zig fmt --check src/`, and the wasm `core`, wasm `term`, and napi `core` builds pass.
- Local runs of `acp.test.ts`, `ultrafast-fake-gateway.test.ts`, `web-fetch-fake-network.test.ts`, and `web-search-fake-gateway.test.ts` pass. `sessions-v2.test.ts` passes except one `fx ask` doctor test that passes on rerun and on `main`.

title: Choose models across authenticated providers
body:
The model picker currently shows only the active provider, even though each provider login is stored separately. Show models from every connected provider in `/model` and Ctrl+P, and switch the selected model together with its credential authority. Qualify models from other connections with their provider name so duplicate model IDs stay distinct.

Use the existing provider preparation flow to validate authentication and the exact selected model before switching. Preserve provider logins, model preferences, reasoning and speed settings, and custom model IDs containing colons. Refresh the connected catalog after switching or signing out of an inactive subscription.

Validation:
- `zig build` and `zig fmt --check src/` pass on macOS arm64.
- 36 focused unit checks pass for the model cache, provider selection, and model settings.
- A tmux test runs `./zig-out/bin/fx`, selects Gateway, Codex, and Grok models, checks request credentials and model IDs, verifies saved logins, and reopens the catalog after restart. The process exits normally with empty stderr.
- Public surface, compactor boundary, and PGSO corpus checks pass. The auth E2E owner remains verification-only because it covers credential correctness and recovery.

Further provider recovery checks are running. Keep this PR in draft until CI, including `macOS arm64`, passes for the current commit and the final ship gate passes.

title: Make path, status, and word splitting work like bash in zsh model commands
body:
## Summary

- Keep `PATH` intact when a zsh model command assigns `path`, such as `for path in a b`, so later commands in the same call still run.
- Let a zsh model command assign `status` instead of stopping at a read-only variable error.
- Split unquoted variables into words in zsh model commands, as bash does, so `$cmd args` and `for f in $files` work.
- Label zsh errors in model commands `(anon):N:` instead of `(eval):N:` or `zsh:N:`, with the same line numbers.
- Stop telling models that zsh leaves unquoted variables unsplit.
- Leave interactive zsh sessions unchanged.

Stacked on #1160.

title: Match ACP session modes to the CLI's permission modes
body:
## Summary

- ACP sessions offer the CLI's permission modes, `auto`, `ask`, and `full-access`, named Auto, Ask, and Full access, in both the `mode` config option and the `modes` field. The `code` mode is removed.
- A session starts in the saved `permission_mode`, or `auto` when none is saved, and reports the mode it enforces. Sessions previously reported `ask` while enforcing the saved mode.
- Choosing a mode with `session/set_config_option` or `session/set_mode` saves it as the default permission mode, like `/permissions`, so new sessions and the CLI start in it.
- A session reads the saved mode when it starts, so a long-running ACP process follows a mode another fx process saved. Open sessions keep their own mode.
- In `full-access`, tool calls run without a permission request or an automatic review.
- An unknown mode, including `code`, returns an `Unknown mode` error and changes nothing. `session/set_mode` without a `modeId`, and a mode change without an active session, also return errors.
- Mode option values report their permission mode in `_meta.fx.permissionMode` instead of a top-level field outside ACP's schema.
- libfx host config saves modes as `auto`, `ask`, and `full-access`, and ignores a saved `code` when restoring.

title: List session modes in fx status --json
body:
## Summary

- `fx status --json` reports `mode`, the ACP session mode a new session in the workspace starts in, such as `full-access` when Full access is saved.
- `fx status --json` lists `modes`, each with its `id`, `name`, and `description`, in the order ACP offers them.

title: Keep queue deliveries from choosing what a durable turn runs
body:
Fixes the High finding from the security review of #1180, "Forged queue deliveries bypass session authorization". This targets `fazxes/libfx-durability` at `eb1b898`.

## Problem

On Vercel, queue deliveries reach the app's `wakeHandler()` route, which is a public URL. `@workflow/world-vercel` 5.1.0's `createQueueHandler` is a plain `@vercel/queue` `handleCallback`. For a binary callback (`ce-vqsreceipthandle` present), `@vercel/queue` 0.8.0 runs the request body as the message before anything is verified or acknowledged. `SessionWorker.consume()` then wrote that message's `input` and `context` to the session log. So anyone who could name a session could add prompts to it and run its tools with another caller's `context`, skipping the app's own authorization.

`@vercel/queue` 0.8.0 has no provenance check for binary callbacks to reuse. Workflow's own handler goes through the same path, but its message is only a pointer (`runId`) into an event log that only the deployment can write.

## Change

This applies the same model to libfx sessions:

- `prompt()`, `steer()`, `cancel()` and `resume()` write the input, the caller's `context` and the restore seed to the session log before they send. This now happens on every World, not only when `!queueDurable`.
- The queue message is only `{ type, messageId, sessionId }`, and the delivery listener reads nothing else from a delivery.
- A worker acts only on a message its session's log already holds. It drops any other delivery before writing anything, so no lease, engine or stream line, with the same result whether or not the session exists.
- A resume request is recorded as a log input that is spent once it is read, so its deliveries are recognized like any other message.

This changes the design described for #1180. `prompt()` is now one log append plus one queue send, and the message no longer carries the input. On Vercel this adds one World round trip before `accepted`. There's no new configuration, and `vercel.json` and `wakeHandler()` are unchanged. `sdk/README.md` documents that the wake route never trusts a delivery's body.

The Medium finding, "Resumed turns inherit another caller's tool identity", is already fixed in this branch by `0be65b17`. This change keeps that behavior.

## Tests

New `local`-mode tests in `sdk/tests/test-durable-core.mjs` use a world-local store with no in-process handler, delivering through `wakeHandler()` and running the request body as binary callbacks do:

- Forged prompt, steer, cancel and resume deliveries, plus one to a session nobody created, cause no World writes, steps, turns or engine opens, and no harness sees the forged `context`.
- Queued messages are exactly `{ messageId, sessionId, type }`. A delivery naming another session's message, or a replay with a rewritten input and `context`, runs nothing.
- A long turn still continues across deliveries, and a redelivery runs it once.

The first two fail on `eb1b898`.

Passed locally:

- `test-durable-core.mjs` memory and local on Node 24, Node 26 and Bun
- `test-durable.mjs` memory and local, native and wasm, on Node and Bun
- `test-durable-harness.mjs` on Bun
- `test-world-persistence.mjs` native and wasm on Node and Bun

Not run locally:

- `sdk/tests/model/check.sh` and `drive.mjs`: no Java on this machine.
- The packaged Next and example tests: they need all four platform addons.
- `test-durable.mjs vercel native` and `drive.mjs --durability vercel`: these need a live World, and are worth running to confirm that a delivery always sees the sender's append.

## Follow-up

`handleCallback` running binary-mode bodies before verification affects any route mounted that way, not just libfx. It's worth raising with the Queues and Workflow owners.

title: Show a submitted prompt immediately on a full screen
body:
## Summary

- When the transcript fills the screen, a submitted prompt appears in the same frame that clears the composer, instead of after the whole transcript is rendered again.
- The prompt keeps its row when the written card replaces the preview, one blank line below the previous turn.
- A multi-line prompt on a full screen previews its last line until the full card is written.
- Queued steering messages on a full screen paint below the previous turn's summary instead of over it.
- In long sessions that are still under the transcript retention limit, the request reaches the model sooner after Enter, because the frame that shows the card reuses the transcript render made while writing it.

title: Silence host audio for fx runs spawned by the test harness
body:
## What

`runFx` now defaults `FX_SOUND` to `0` for every spawned fx process. A test that exercises sound passes its own value, which `notifications.test.ts` already does through `notificationEnv`.

## Why

On macOS `fx ask` plays host audio through `/usr/bin/afplay` even when stdout and stderr are pipes. The tmux harness already defaults `FX_SOUND` to `0` (tests/e2e/tmux-helpers.ts), so TUI tests are silent, but the non-TTY spawn path was not covered. Running an e2e file that spawns fx through `runFx` rings the developer's speakers on every turn.

## Evidence

Watching for the player while running one existing test on `main`:

```
bun test mcp-auth.test.ts -t "fx ask reports an actionable auth requirement for broad search without opening a browser"
/usr/bin/afplay /var/folders/.../T/fx-success.m4a
/usr/bin/afplay /var/folders/.../T/fx-success.m4a
```

Same test on this branch: zero `afplay` processes.

## Verification

- `cd tests/e2e && bun test mcp-auth.test.ts -t "fx ask reports an actionable auth requirement for broad search without opening a browser"` passes, with no `afplay` spawn.
- `cd tests/e2e && bun test notifications.test.ts` passes (5 pass, 0 fail). That file opts back into sound on purpose, because it asserts bell counts and sound handler traces.

## Known ceiling

`notifications.test.ts` still plays audio by design. A fully silent full-suite run needs a switch that overrides the sound tests too; I did not add one.

title: Fix MCP re-authorization for grants larger than the scope budget
body:
## Root cause

`/mcp auth datadog --open` failed with `TooManyOAuthScopes` before the browser opened.

1. fx stores the granted scope in the credential. On macOS that is the keychain item `FX_MCP_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS_V1`; this account's Datadog credential holds 166 scope tokens (3628 characters).
2. `authorizeWithRedirect` seeds every authorization request with that stored scope through `requestedScope` (src/core/mcp/mcp_auth.zig).
3. `appendUnique` caps the union at `max_scope_tokens = 64` and returns `error.TooManyOAuthScopes` on the 65th distinct token.
4. Scope resolution runs before `request_authorization`, so the request dies before the browser opens. Re-authorization is unrecoverable from the UI for any server that grants more than 64 scopes.

Datadog's protected-resource metadata advertises no scopes and its authorization-server metadata advertises only `mcp_all`, so the stored grant was the only large input.

## Fix

Carry the stored scope only when the challenge is `insufficient_scope`, which is the RFC 6750 incremental authorization case where the server states it needs more scope. A fresh authorization no longer re-requests a grant the server already issued, and the 64-token budget keeps bounding untrusted server-supplied scope lists.

## Verification

Reproduced with the built binary in tmux against the real Datadog endpoint:

- `main`: `/mcp auth datadog --open` prints `MCP authentication for 'datadog' failed: TooManyOAuthScopes.`
- This branch: the flow opens `https://app.datadoghq.com/oauth2/v1/authorize` with `resource` set and no `scope` parameter, then waits for the browser callback.

Regression test, red on `main` and green here:

```
cd tests/e2e && bun test mcp-auth.test.ts -t "re-authorization survives a stored grant larger than the scope budget"

main:  Received: "fx mcp auth failed: TooManyOAuthScopes.\n"
branch: 1 pass, 0 fail
```

Full file and formatting:

- `cd tests/e2e && bun test mcp-auth.test.ts` gives 78 pass, 0 fail.
- `zig fmt --check src/` passes.

## Unverified

The browser consent step needs real Datadog credentials, so I did not complete the OAuth exchange. The token request now omits `scope`; Datadog applies its default grant, which is the set it issued before.

## Workaround for an affected profile

`/mcp logout datadog` removes the stored credential, so the next authorization starts without a previous scope. I did not run it here because it deletes the working credential. Refresh keeps working either way, because the refresh request never sends scope.

title: Fix missing and undercounted usage costs
body:
## Summary

- Record the cost of streamed responses whose final metadata has no timestamp from their receipt, instead of waiting on a generation lookup.
- Record the amount AI Gateway charged, including surcharges, instead of the inference-only cost.
- Keep recording costs while generation lookups are waiting. A response with a receipt no longer needs a free lookup slot.
- Hold a generation lookup that AI Gateway refuses for the current credential and retry it when the credential changes, instead of retrying it forever.
- Look up the cost of failed or interrupted responses that already reported a generation ID, instead of marking them incomplete.
- Wait for a generation lookup when a call has no credential source yet, instead of marking it incomplete.
- Use the current credential for lookups queued under an earlier one.
- Retry a failed usage save at the end of a turn instead of marking the session's costs or code changes incomplete.
- Keep an ACP session open with its usage when releasing it fails.
- Publish usage for a model beyond a session's 32-model limit to the profile ledger and mark the session totals incomplete, instead of failing the save.
- Count subagent model calls in the parent session's usage in the interactive shell.
- Count session title generation and Gateway-routed TypeSafe permission reviews in usage.
- Show `/usage` as a compact table of cost, tokens, and requests per model, with a total row when it lists more than one model.
- Open `/usage` on the current session, with periods ordered session, 24h, 7d, 30d. Tab and Shift+Tab wrap through them.
- Show costs under $1 with up to four decimals instead of rounding to cents.
- Say what the totals leave out: calls waiting for a cost, calls the sign-in can't price, calls that may be billed with no cost, and calls still in progress.
- Load the 24h, 7d, and 30d views several times faster on large usage histories.
- Move Left and Right on the `/usage` tabs in their on-screen direction.
- Quit right after a reply without waiting on usage ledger cleanup, even with a large `usage.jsonl`.

title: Index and search workspace files without running git
body:
## Summary

- Open a repository without starting git, so programs named by its own config, such as `core.fsmonitor`, hooks, filters, diff drivers and the pager, no longer run at startup.
- List `@`-completion candidates from a native index that reads `.gitignore` rules, `.git/index` and git config as files.
- Fill `@`-completion from the saved listing right away, then rescan only the roots that changed.
- Follow a symlinked `~/.gitconfig`, its includes and the excludes file it names, as git does, so globally ignored files stay out of `glob_files` and `grep_files`. Paths a repository names still refuse symlinks.
- Rebuild the saved listing when the git config location changes through HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME or the GIT_CONFIG_* variables.
- Press Enter on a folder in the `@` menu to mention that folder; Tab still opens the folder to browse inside.
- Show an opened folder as the first `@` row, above its contents, so it can be selected from inside.
- Paint a folder's rows in the same frame as the keystroke that lists it, instead of first flashing an empty "indexing files..." list.
- Run `glob_files` and `grep_files` on the same listing, so a search sees a file created a moment earlier, including untracked files in subfolders.
- Apply `.gitignore` when `glob_files` or `grep_files` searches a subfolder of a repository.
- Search file contents on several threads, with the same results and the same cut at the match cap as before.
- Run the agent's direct read-only `git status`, `git diff` and `git log`, when the command does not use the user's own shell environment, and the `fx pr` and `fx issue` snapshot with every repository-configured program turned off, and skip git when it would use a different repository than the one fx read.
- In auto mode, hold a git command that this safe path refuses and tell the agent why, instead of running plain git. Ask mode still prompts.
- Allow git 2.25 and later on the safe path. Its flags turn off every repository-configured program on 2.25 and 2.34 as on current git.
- Look up git helper programs for those commands only in `/usr/bin` and `/bin`, so a Git LFS installed elsewhere is not found there.
- List hidden files such as `.env` in `glob_files` results outside a repository unless they sit in a hidden folder.
- Count only files toward the 100,000-file candidate cap of `glob_files` and `grep_files`, so folders no longer push files out of a search. The `@` menu still shows at most 100,000 files and folders.
- Scan a folder fresh instead of reusing a saved listing that was cut at the candidate cap.
- Scan a folder fresh when a folder above it changed, so a `.gitignore` added above the searched folder applies at once.
- Free the memory of each `glob_files` and `grep_files` search when it ends, so a turn with many searches no longer keeps a full scan for every one.
- Hold less memory while scanning a folder and in the listing the `@` menu keeps. On the Linux kernel a scan peaks at about half its previous size, and the kept listing is about a sixth.
- Leave malformed paths out of a saved listing for added roots too, as for the workspace root.
- Say whether a `glob_files` or `grep_files` listing was cut short by the candidate cap or by folders and git files that could not be read.
- Stop parallel grep at the match cap even while an earlier batch is still running, and fail for running out of memory only when it happens before the cut.
- Treat a `.gitignore` pattern that would take too long to match against a path as not matching, so a crafted pattern lists the file instead of hanging fx.
- Git run as an ordinary shell command, in the shell tool's default `user` environment or as one of auto mode's routine commands such as `git fetch`, still uses the repository's full config. AGENTS.md now says so.

title: Convert v1 sessions to v2 when they are opened
body:
## Summary

- With `--sessions-v2`, opening a v1 session converts it to the v2 store first, with its subagent children, through every way of opening: `--resume`, `-c`, `-r`, `/resume`, `fx ask --resume-id` and ACP `session/load`.
- After a conversion the v1 copy is deleted. A v1 folder left behind by a crash or a refused delete is removed on a later open, but only while it is unchanged since it was copied.
- A converted session keeps its saved permission rules, ACP system prompt and tool identities, hosted terminal state, side files and their handles, and an unfinished reply when v1 would show one. It carries no usage, which fx no longer keeps per session.
- `-c` reopens the session v1 remembers when v2 has none.
- Sessions in older on-disk formats, and session folders an old release left world-readable, convert too.
- `fx sessions`, the picker and `--resume last` include v1 sessions not converted yet, and `--resume last` picks the newest of both stores.
- `fx session <id>` shows an unconverted v1 session without converting it.
- `fx sessions convert` converts every v1 session, prints `converted N, busy N, unreadable N` and a line per skipped session, and exits 1 when any was skipped. It needs `--sessions-v2`.
- A session that can't be converted is refused with the file and the reason in the app, `fx ask` and ACP, and its v1 files stay as they were. A session another fx has open is refused as busy.
- A side file larger than the v2 store keeps in one file is left out and named; the rest of the session converts.
- A conversion that takes longer than about 150 ms shows a notice in the app, on `fx ask` stderr and to ACP clients.
- A stored tool result from an earlier turn reaches the model as its preview with the handle to read it, as v1 shows it, in converted and native v2 sessions alike.
- Listing sessions stays fast with thousands of v2 sessions.
- `tests/tla/session_manager/V1Conversion.tla` drops its usage marker steps to match.

title: Keep image-heavy requests under provider size limits
body:
## Summary

- Leave the oldest images out of a request that would exceed 30 MiB or 100 images, keeping the newest ones.
- Replace each left-out tool image with a note naming the `read_tool_result` handle that loads it again.
- Replace each left-out attachment with a note naming its saved file.
- Keep the saved conversation unchanged; only the request sent to the provider drops images.
- Treat an AI Gateway 400 whose routing metadata shows a provider 413 as a request-size rejection.
- Retry a size rejection with a lower limit for that model instead of compacting the conversation.
- Fall back to compaction when the rejected request carried no images or after two size retries in one turn.
- Forget the learned limit when the conversation is cleared or replaced.
- Count chat-completions image parts as images instead of base64 text when estimating request size.

Supersedes #1174 and includes its chat-completions measurement fix.

title: Let a durable session choose its own model and instructions
body:
A durable libfx agent has one model and one set of instructions for every session. An app whose conversations each pick a model, or carry their own system context, such as a design style per chat, cannot express that today: every message goes to the same queue topic, so one agent per configuration would hand sessions to the wrong one.

`agent.session(id, { model, instructions })` now runs the turns that session object starts with that model choice and those instructions instead of the agent's:

```js
const session = agent.session(chatId, {
  model: { id: "anthropic/claude-opus-5.5-fast", effort: "low" },
  instructions: [baseInstructions, designMd],
});
```

- The settings follow the rule `context` follows: they are stored with each prompt, and a turn keeps the settings of the `session()` call that started it, also when another process continues it. A call without them runs with the agent's.
- A session's `model` replaces the agent's whole model choice, its effort and fast options included. `instructions` replace the agent's.
- They are checked when the session object is made, by the same rules `createFxEngine()` applies, so a bad model option throws there instead of failing a later turn.
- When the settings change between turns, the worker reopens the engine for the next turn. A checkpoint saved under another model still loads and reports `checkpoint.mismatch`.

The harness contract gains an optional `settings(sessionOptions)`, and `open()` receives the turn's `settings` beside its `context`. The core stores them without knowing what they mean.

## Validation

- New core test: each prompt's turn runs with its session object's settings, through resumes at every step, and a harness's refusal reaches the caller. New fx test: a session's model and instructions reach its model requests, the agent's apply without them, and bad settings throw when the session object is made. Each fails when its part of the change is removed: settings dropped from the log entry, settings ignored when the engine is reopened, settings ignored by the fx harness.
- The SDK set CI runs, 59 commands, passes: the Node and Bun lanes on N-API and Wasm, the durable and core suites on memory, local and an app's World, the TLA+ check, the send, lookup and cutoff walks, packaging and types.

title: Show usage history from AI Gateway reports
body:
## Summary

- Send `providerOptions.gateway.user` on every AI Gateway request made with an API key: `fx_` and a one-way hash of the key, the same on every install that uses it.
- Send no user tag on requests made with fx login, a deployment token, or a subscription.
- Show Today, 7d, and 30d in `/usage` and `fx usage` from AI Gateway's usage reports for the API key's fx user, counting fx requests from every machine that uses the key.
- Keep AI Gateway's last answer in `~/.fx/usage-gateway.json`, and ask again when it is more than 15 minutes old or from an earlier UTC day, or when `r` is pressed, at most every 30 seconds.
- Open the usage dashboard on the stored answer without waiting on the network, and show when AI Gateway sent it.
- Say why history is unavailable without an API key, with a subscription, or when AI Gateway refuses usage reports for the key.
- Replace the `24h` period with `today`, one whole UTC day, in the dashboard and in `fx usage --period`.
- Add `source`, `as_of_ms`, `refresh_failed`, and `unavailable` to `fx usage --json`.
- Stop writing `~/.fx/usage.jsonl`, its lock, and usage-recovery markers, and stop rebuilding usage history from saved sessions. Existing files stay in place and are no longer read.
- Settle each call's usage straight into its session's totals. An older session that still holds usage staged for the profile settles it when it reopens.

Stacked on #1195.

title: Take over a crashed durable session after a short lease
body:
## Summary

- On Vercel and any World that can't tell whether a worker still runs, a turn whose function dies continues once that worker's lease runs out, 15 seconds after its last renewal, instead of at the function's deadline.
- A running worker renews its lease every third of the lease (5 seconds by default), so a turn that outlasts the lease keeps its session.
- A worker whose session was taken over after its lease ran out stops its turn at its next renewal, a model request still in flight included.
- `vercel({ leaseMs })` and `world({ leaseMs })` set the lease, at least 1000 ms.

Stacked on #1200.

title: Support trailer-only usage for custom model connections
body:
Endpoints such as Cloudflare Workers AI emit per-chunk token deltas before a cumulative usage trailer. fx treats those deltas as cumulative counts and stops with `ConflictingIdentity`, preventing a configured connection from returning a response.

Add the typed provider setting `"usage_mode": "trailer-only"` to read counts from the final trailer. The default remains `"cumulative"`. The adapter passes the mode to the shared stream parser, so the setting works through any endpoint, including custom domains and proxies. There is no URL matching or Cloudflare-specific parser entry point. If the trailer is absent, trailer-only mode leaves usage unknown.

Tests cover default and explicit modes, invalid configuration values, and both empty-choice and repeated-finish trailers. Two CLI regression cases use a local endpoint to verify that defaults still reject decreasing usage and the opt-in setting produces the correct final counts. The README documents the setting.

Validation:
- Zig 0.16.0 ReleaseSafe build succeeded; 92 focused unit tests passed.
- Both new CLI regression tests and 11 CI shard tests passed.
- Formatting, diff, public-surface, compactor-boundary, and PGSO corpus checks passed.
- The built binary completed a live Cloudflare request using DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731), including a successful `read_file` tool call and its follow-up response.

This PR remains a draft pending upstream CI.

title: Broad deny rules do not prevent web_fetch in auto mode
body:
## Observation

With fx 0.0.13 (status build_revision 4d966e272cfc), Linux aarch64/glibc 2.31, an OpenAI-compatible custom connection, and permission_mode=auto, the following private-profile rules are reported by `fx permissions --json` but do not prevent builtin web_fetch:

```json
{
  "permission_mode": "auto",
  "permission": {
    "*": "deny",
    "web_fetch": "deny"
  }
}
```

During an MCP deployment smoke test which explicitly forbade unrelated tools, fx executed web_fetch against https://example.com/. The model subsequently acknowledged the unrelated fetch. No mail content or secrets were involved in the smoke test.

The actual `fx ask --auto --json --no-save` result contained:

```json
{"exit_code":0,"steps":1,"tool_calls":[{"name":"web_fetch","status":"success","web_fetch":{"url":"https://example.com/","bytes":175,"status":200,"duration_ms":154,"cache_hit":false,"artifact":"none"}}]}
```

`fx permissions --json` reported both `{permission:"*",pattern:"*",action:"deny"}` and `{permission:"web_fetch",pattern:"*",action:"deny"}`. No interactive grant or full-access flag was used.

## Why it matters

A service profile intended to expose only narrow MCP tools cannot safely rely on the documented last-match permission/default-deny model to prevent general URL retrieval. Permission inspection makes these rules look effective. This blocks activation of an unattended mail agent even though its MCP mutation boundaries are independently enforced.

## Where to look

In the current public source (1eed0348b40f8a96b18cd3ebe57f72735b323f2d), inspect `src/core/permissions/permissions.zig` symbols `evaluateRulesetForTool`, `evaluateWebFetchRuleset`, `rulesDenyAllTargetsForTool`, and `webFetchRuleWarningCount`, plus builtin tool projection/admission. `evaluateWebFetchRuleset` accepts only exact canonical domain patterns, bypassing both catch-all permission rules and wildcard web_fetch rules. This may explain the behavior; the installed build revision differs from public HEAD.

## Expected state / acceptance

- Global `"*":"deny"` and `"web_fetch":"deny"` prevent web_fetch before network execution, or unsupported broad-deny rules fail configuration clearly before the agent starts.
- Permission inspection must not imply an unsupported rule is effective.
- Exact per-domain web_fetch allow/deny rules continue to work.
- Add a regression test covering broad deny in auto/noninteractive mode.

## Evidence

Verified 2026-10-10 using the official https://fx.sh/setup.sh Linux aarch64 installer. Local evidence is the deployment transcript and private profile inspection; the sanitized reproducer and returned tool metadata above contain everything needed to reproduce without mailbox access.

title: Add MCP-v2 as an opt-in MCP engine
body:
## Summary

- `FX_MCP_ENGINE=v2` runs MCP servers through MCP-v2, a new MCP client. Without it, fx keeps using the current engine.
- MCP-v2 speaks MCP 2026-07-28 and 2025-03-26 through 2025-11-25 over stdio and Streamable HTTP.
- MCP-v2 starts a server the first time something needs it, such as a matching tool search, instead of at launch.
- `fx mcp list`, `show`, `add`, `remove`, `login`, `logout`, `approve`, and `reject` manage servers. `list` and `show` accept `--json`.
- `/mcp` opens a menu of servers with their status, tools, and actions, and `/mcp <command>` runs the same commands in the shell.
- At startup, fx names project servers that are waiting for approval.
- `fx mcp login` signs in through the browser, or with `--no-browser` by pasting the address the browser ends on.
- `fx mcp logout` revokes the token when the server supports revocation.
- MCP-v2 keeps its logins apart from the current engine's, in the macOS Keychain when it's available and otherwise under `~/.fx/mcp-credentials/`.
- Quitting fx sends each running stdio server SIGTERM and exits without waiting for it.
- For 2025 servers, a call's idle timeout pauses while the user answers the server's question. The overall limit still applies.
- Server instructions reach the model with that server's tools.
- A server that doesn't register fx as a client shows a hint to set `oauth.client_id` in `mcp.json`.
- Over ACP with MCP-v2, fx advertises stdio and HTTP servers only, and refuses `"type": "acp"` servers with a reason.
- Over ACP with MCP-v2, editor-supplied servers marked always-loaded keep their tools in every turn.
- Over ACP with MCP-v2, editors receive `elicitation/complete` for URL questions, including a completion that arrives before the user accepts the URL.
- Editors that advertise `session.notices` receive fx's notices as ACP Session Notices instead of assistant text, with either engine.

title: Take provider credentials through one callback
body:
## Summary

- Pass refreshed credentials to `onCredentials` with the provider and session, replacing `onChatgptCredentials`.

title: Run libfx agents on a Grok plan
body:
## Summary

- Run a libfx agent on Grok with `provider: "grok"`: model requests and the model list go to xAI's Grok endpoints through the host's `fetch` instead of AI Gateway.
- Supply Grok credentials through the shared `credentials({ provider, sessionId })` callback. libfx adds the token and account id only to Grok requests, so they never reach the engine or a saved session.
- Refresh Grok tokens five minutes before they expire and once after a 401, refuse a refreshed token for a different account, and pass new tokens to `onCredentials`.
- Continue a durable Grok session in a new process, which asks `credentials` for that session's credentials.
- Sign in with a Grok plan from `libfx/grok` with device code, or by pasting the callback address, and refresh tokens from there.
- Share token refreshes between a durable agent's sessions, so sessions on one account never redeem the same refresh token twice. This also applies to Codex.
- Retry a request that was rejected after another request refreshed on the newer token, instead of spending the old refresh token again.
- Pass refreshed credentials to `onCredentials` once for each session that uses them, so a host that keeps credentials per session saves every rotation.
- Accept an optional `refreshLock` so an app with several servers refreshes an account on one at a time. Inside the lock, libfx asks `credentials()` again and uses what another server already saved.

Stacked on #1210.

title: Run libfx agents on a custom OpenAI-compatible provider
body:
## Summary

- Run a libfx agent on any server that speaks OpenAI Chat Completions by passing `provider: { name, baseUrl, models }`. Requests go to `{baseUrl}/chat/completions` through the host's `fetch`, with the CLI's own request and reply handling.
- Supply the provider's API key through the shared `credentials({ provider, sessionId })` callback, or omit it for a server that needs none. libfx adds the key only to that chat URL, so it never reaches the engine or a saved session.
- Check a custom provider's name, base URL and model details when the agent is created, require a `model`, and reject `onCredentials` and `refreshLock`, since a key is never refreshed.
- Continue a durable session on a custom provider in a new process. The crash test now covers Codex, Grok and a custom provider.
- Mask the API key or token in a failed response's body, so a server that quotes it back cannot put it in the turn, `onEvent` diagnostics, or a saved session. This covers Codex and Grok too.

Stacked on #1211.

title: Coerce a stringified request object before tool decode
body:
## Summary

A model that serializes the shell tool's nested `request` object as a JSON
string could not run any shell command. The request never reached execution,
fx returned a correction the model could not act on, and the tool loop was
cut off after repeated identical failures.

`normalized_terminal_request_arguments` now parses a string-valued `request`
into an object before the existing object check, so the same call decodes and
runs on the first attempt.

## Problem

The `shell` tool advertises its input as a single required object field:

```json
{ "request": { "action": "run", "command": "..." } }
```

Some reasoning models emit that nested object as a JSON string instead:

```json
{ "request": "{\"action\": \"run\", \"command\": \"...\"}" }
```

The normalization step returned `null` on a string value, so the raw
arguments passed through unchanged to `decode_input`, which reads a top-level
`action` and fails. fx then returned an `invalid_shell_request` correction
with a `retry_with` object but did not execute anything. The model received
the corrected shape, could not reproduce it, and repeated the same stringified
call until the loop was stopped.

Tools with flat parameters, such as `web_fetch` with its `url` field, were
unaffected. Only tools that advertise a nested `request` object hit this path.

## Change

In `normalized_terminal_request_arguments`, when `request` is a string, parse
it into a JSON value in the same arena and continue with the existing object
path. An unparseable string or one that parses to a non-object returns
`null`, which is the same behavior the function already has for malformed
input, so the advisory correction still applies when there is nothing to
recover.

The coercion mirrors what `request_correction` in the shell tool already does
for its advisory path; this brings the executable path to parity.

## Testing

- Added `terminal request normalization coerces a stringified request object`,
  which asserts that a stringified `run` request normalizes to the flattened
  executable form.
- `zig build` succeeds.
- Ran the focused test for the changed path.
- Drove the built binary against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint served by a
  model that serializes the nested object, and confirmed a `shell` call
  executes on the first attempt.

title: Bug: a tool call whose input JSON contains line breaks crashes the host process
body:
**libfx:** 0.0.12, 0.0.13, and 0.0.13-dev.1432.g1df91f0b4ebf (`createFxEngine`), native backend, on Node 22.23 and 25.8 (macOS arm64). The `wasm` backend handles the same input correctly.

## What happens

When the gateway streams a `tool-call` part whose `input` string is pretty-printed JSON (it contains line breaks), the SDK throws an uncaught exception from its output reader, and the Node process exits:

```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"libfx/tool_call","params":{"sessionId":"2vNM-8fbbEmP","name":"todo","input":{

SyntaxError: Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 111 (line 1 column 112)
    at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
    at consume (libfx/core-output.js:41:45)
    at CoreOutput.write (libfx/core-output.js:46:12)
    at drainOutput (libfx/node.js:477:32)
```

`CoreOutput` in `core-output.js` splits the native core's output on line-break bytes, one JSON-RPC message per line. The core writes the call's `input` into the `libfx/tool_call` message as raw JSON, keeping the model's whitespace, so a pretty-printed input splits the message in two and the first half fails `JSON.parse` (the first line of the output above). Re-serializing the input (or escaping it) before framing would fix it. A frame that fails to parse probably shouldn't take down the process either.

The same input without line breaks works.

## Seen with real traffic

With no `fetch` override, a real AI Gateway key, and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` on the native backend, a prompt that makes the model call a tool with an array of objects crashed the process in each of our runs (0.0.13 and 0.0.13-dev.1432), here with `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input`. The same run on `backend: "wasm"` completes.

The Gateway streams that model's `input` pretty-printed:

```
{"items": [
  {"text": "Finalize website design and content", "priority": "high", "done": true},
  {"text": "Set up hosting and domain configuration", "priority": "high", "done": false},
  ...
```

Across the 16 models we ran through the Gateway (one or two calls each), `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` and `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` sent line breaks. Opus 4.6, the Claude 5.5 models, GPT-5/5.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro/3.5 Flash, Grok 4.7, GLM 5.2, Kimi K3, Qwen3 Coder, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and Mistral Large 4 sent single-line input.

## Repro without a key

This is a fake gateway that sends one tool call whose `input` has line breaks; the SSE event itself is a single line of valid JSON.

```js
import { createFxAgent } from "libfx"

const sse = (parts) => new Response(new ReadableStream({ start(c) {
  for (const p of parts) c.enqueue(new TextEncoder().encode(`data: ${JSON.stringify(p)}\n\n`)); c.close() } }),
  { headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" } })
const usage = { inputTokens: { total: 1, noCache: 1, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 }, outputTokens: { total: 1, text: 1, reasoning: 0 } }
let step = 0
const fetch = async (url) => {
  if (!String(url).endsWith("/ai/language-model")) return new Response(JSON.stringify({ data: [] }))
  return step++ === 0
    ? sse([{ type: "stream-start", warnings: [] },
        { type: "tool-call", toolCallId: "call_1", toolName: "todo", input: '{\n  "items": [\n    {"text": "a"}\n  ]\n}' },
        { type: "finish", finishReason: { unified: "tool-calls", raw: "tool_use" }, usage }])
    : sse([{ type: "stream-start", warnings: [] }, { type: "text-start", id: "t" }, { type: "text-delta", id: "t", delta: "done" },
        { type: "text-end", id: "t" }, { type: "finish", finishReason: { unified: "stop", raw: "end_turn" }, usage }])
}

// On 0.0.13-dev, use createFxEngine: createFxAgent is now the durable agent.
const agent = await createFxAgent({ apiKey: "k", model: "anthropic/m", fetch, tools: [{
  name: "todo", description: "t",
  inputSchema: { type: "object", properties: { items: { type: "array", items: { type: "object" } } } },
  execute: async (input) => ({ got: input }) }] })
const turn = agent.prompt("go")
for await (const _ of turn);
await turn.result // never settles: the process dies with the SyntaxError above
```

## Expected

The input is valid JSON, so the tool should run with `{ items: [{ text: "a" }] }`.

## Workaround

We re-serialize `tool-call` inputs compactly in a `fetch` wrapper before libfx sees them.

title: Fix MCP-v2 issues from the first dogfood round
body:
## Summary

- Ctrl+C closes the `/mcp` menu from any screen.
- Typing on a server's screen filters its tools.
- Remove and Reject confirm in place, without resizing the menu.
- The server list shows only whether each server is running, and a stale error clears once the server is ready.
- While a sign-in waits for the browser, the server's screen shows the full sign-in address.
- MCP status moves from the transcript to the status line: sign-in results, servers that need a login or approval, failures, and config problems. A typed `/mcp login NAME` still reports in the transcript.
- When nothing needs attention, the status line shows `mcp R/N`, ready servers out of enabled ones.
- Servers start in the background after the first frame, and come back on their own after `/mcp add`, `remove`, `approve`, or `reject`.
- The page shown after a browser sign-in is fx's styled page again.
- A sign-in the server refuses shows the server's reason instead of garbled text.
- Logins saved by the previous MCP engine carry over once, and a later logout stays signed out.
- `/trace` reports MCP-v2's engine, its servers, and their states.
- Slack signs in with fx's Slack app through fx.sh, and `/mcp add slack` fills in Slack's server URL.
- Token responses with `token_type` "user" are accepted, and token errors returned with HTTP 200 show the server's error code.
- `fx ask` on a terminal asks a server's form or URL question instead of declining it.
- `fx ask` points to `fx mcp approve` for unapproved project servers.
- `"type": "streamable-http"` in an MCP config is read as an HTTP server.
- Project stdio servers in an editor session start in the session's project directory.

title: Reject host HTTP statuses outside 100 to 599
body:
A host that embeds fx through the SDK reports each response's HTTP status to fx as a number. fx converted that number to `std.http.Status` without checking it, and that type only holds values up to 1023. A host that reported 1024 or more crashed fx: in the Node SDK the whole process exits with `panic: invalid enum value`, and in the ReleaseSmall WASM core the conversion is undefined behavior.

The status now goes through one check, `httpStatus` in `host_stream_provider.zig`, at the three places it enters: the native and JS model catalogs and the host stream. A status outside 100 to 599 fails that request as a transport failure, the same range the web fetch tool accepts.

This also changes statuses 0 to 99 and 600 to 1023, which fit in `std.http.Status` and never crashed. A turn used to fail with the response body as the error detail, and a catalog request as an HTTP status failure; both now fail as transport failures. A browser host reports 0 for an opaque response, so such a host now gets the generic failure. Statuses 100 to 599 behave as before.

## Testing

- New unit tests cover the check's boundaries, the catalog GET, and the host stream with statuses such as 0, 99, 600, 1024, and 65535. Without the fix they fail.
- A Node SDK script whose `fetch` reports 1024 crashed `main` with exit 134 for both the model catalog and a turn. With this change the process stays up and the request fails.
- `node sdk/tests/test-node-napi.mjs`, `test-core.mjs`, and `test-core-cancel.mjs` pass, and the WASM core builds.

title: Bug: Inconsistent MCP configuration behavior
Replace the remaining catch unreachable with error handling
body:
Twenty-one `catch unreachable` lines assume a fallible call cannot fail. If that assumption is ever wrong, a safe build panics and an unsafe build has undefined behavior. This handles each error instead. The six that #1163 rewrites as part of the Zig 0.17 upgrade are left to it.

| Where | Change |
|---|---|
| `image_commands.zig`, `mcp_host/login.zig` (2), `mcp/protocol/subscriptions.zig` (3) | `try`; each function already returns errors |
| `session_manager/session.zig` (2) | a line that fails its own check fails the write, as the code beside it does |
| `session_manager/log.zig` | the batch check becomes `seqsMatch`, asserted with `std.debug.assert` |
| `mcp/protocol/elicitation.zig` | `Options.init` returns its error; an unreadable option list matches no answer |
| `gateway/client.zig` | `BoundedRequestWatch.finish` still waits for the watch's own event before releasing the select, and treats a closed queue, which only `Select.cancel` causes, as nothing left to wait for |
| `mcp/server.zig` (2) | a stored elicitation that no longer parses refuses the answer with the function's own rejection error |
| Test fakes in `input_completion_runtime.zig`, `login_flow.zig` (2), `openai_codex.zig` (2), `xai_grok.zig` (2), `terminal/store.zig` | record or return the error, so a failure fails that test rather than the test binary |

No behavior changes when the calls succeed.

## Testing

- `zig build test` after merging main at 29fc20147: 10074 passed. The 12 failures are all in `command_runner.zig` and are the same 12 that plain main fails on this machine; main's CI and macOS unit tests pass them, so they are local to this machine. Earlier, before main moved, the suite passed in full.
- E2E: sessions-v2 98/98, session-recovery 39/39, mcp-verbs 13/13, mcp-auth 97/97, mcp-stdio 131/131, mcp-http 41/41, tui-composer-edit-contracts 31/31, vision-route-fake-gateway 50/50. One session-recovery run failed a fixture setup step once under load; the test passed in isolation on this branch and on main, and in two further full runs.
- The built binary resumed a v2 session and appended to it, and `fx mcp show` loaded an MCP-v2 server.

title: Mask the gateway key in libfx error details
body:
## Summary

- Mask the gateway key in the failure detail of a libfx gateway request. A server that quoted the key in an error response put it in the turn, its `onEvent` diagnostics and the saved session, because the libfx gateway path passed error bodies through unchanged.
- Use the same masking configured providers already use: the body is normalized as JSON, then the raw and JSON-escaped key are replaced with `*`.
- Classify a provider's size rejection from the original body before masking, so `request_too_large` still works for large error bodies.
- Host-managed requests are unchanged. Their credentials never reach the engine, and the host masks them before the body arrives.

The CLI is unaffected: it uses its own gateway client, which already redacts this detail.

## Testing

- `zig fmt --check src/`
- `zig build test`: the new host provider test passes. It covers a raw key, an escaped key, a plain-text body and a host-managed request.
- A fake gateway that echoes the key in a 403, on memory, local and World storage with the native and Wasm engines: the key reached the turn stream, `onEvent` and the saved session in all 6 combinations before this change, and in none after it. The rejection still reaches the turn with the key masked.

All 10 checks passed.

title: Wrap Ctrl+O tool rows instead of clipping them
body:
## Summary

- Wrap long tool rows in Ctrl+O instead of cutting them off with `…`, so full shell commands stay visible at every terminal width.
- Show the full launch command on terminal session rows such as `Observed` and `Stopped` in Ctrl+O. These calls have no command argument, so the row is the only place the command appears.

title: Read /usage from provider usage reports
body:
## Summary

- `/usage` and `fx usage` show the provider's own usage numbers instead of counting locally.
- With AI Gateway and fx login, they show your spend on the team and your user budget. With an API key, they show that key's spend.
- AI Gateway usage covers today, the last 7 days and the calendar month (UTC), with a table per model and a details screen for each model.
- With Codex, they show the ChatGPT plan's limits, token activity, and usage by model and surface.
- With Grok, they show the plan's allowance, usage by product, bought credits, and pay-as-you-go spending.
- Opening `/usage` shows cached numbers right away and refreshes in the background, then every 15 minutes while open. Opening it again within a minute of the last refresh for that sign-in doesn't refresh.
- `r` refreshes every time, unless a refresh is already running.
- After switching provider, opening `/usage` refreshes the new sign-in's numbers right away.
- With an empty or relative `HOME`, `fx usage` reports that HOME isn't set, and `/usage` shows numbers without caching them.
- Finished days are cached in `~/.fx/usage-cache`, which every fx process on the machine shares, and are read only when the cache doesn't already hold them for the current UTC day.
- After the clock is corrected backward, the next refresh is shown and saved, and finished days are read again once.
- Finished days stay on screen when the cache file becomes unreadable, and a refresh is still shown when the cache can't be written.
- A report with totals too large to add up counts as a bad response and leaves the cache unchanged.
- Provider names can't put control, bidi or zero-width characters on the terminal.
- `fx usage` takes `--period today`, `7d` or `month` and prints the same tables, and `--json` includes every provider's view. `24h` and `30d` are no longer accepted.
- The `/cost` alias is removed.
- fx no longer keeps session or profile usage ledgers, the per-session usage file, or AI Gateway generation lookups. Saved sessions with old usage data still load and resume.
- A model response's tool calls still don't run after another process takes over the session.
- ACP `usage_update` reports context use from each response's token counts and no longer includes a cost.
- A usage fetch creates a missing `~/.fx` with owner-only access, and an existing `~/.fx` is made private when a session reopens.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#160.

title: Read a durable turn's stream only once its view is used
body:
A durable prompt's view (`session.prompt()`, `session.resume()`) no longer opens a read of the session stream the moment the prompt is sent. It starts reading the first time its events, `readable` or `result` are used.

## Why

Every view started a background reader on the session's UI stream as soon as it was created, and buffered the turn's events until `turn_end`, whether or not anything read the view. Dropping the view cancels nothing, so the reader stayed open for the length of the turn.

Code that only sends, such as a route that returns once the prompt is `accepted`, or the README's own `agent.session(sessionId).prompt("Start with the schema.")`, held one World stream read open per prompt. On Vercel that is a connection to the World's stream for as long as the turn runs.

## What changed

- `turnView` still runs `start()` at once: the prompt is stored or queued, and `accepted` resolves as before. `start()` also records the stream position the view follows from, before the message goes out.
- The stream read starts on first use: iterating the view, reading `readable`, or reading `result`. A reader that comes later reads from that recorded position, so it still sees every event of the turn, even one that has already ended.
- A prompt with a `signal` reads `result` to remove its abort listener when the turn ends, so it still follows the stream, as today.
- `FxTurnView`'s declaration and the README's Sessions section say when a view reads.

## Measurements

The new test counts `world.streams.get` calls for a prompt that runs to its end with nobody reading its view, on `local()` and on an app-built World: 0 reads with this change; on `main` the view's background reader makes one as soon as the prompt is sent and keeps it open until the turn ends. The same view, read after the turn ended, then yields all of its events.

## Tests

- `sdk/tests/test-durable-core.mjs`: new test, "a prompt nobody reads holds no read of the session stream, and a later reader still sees its turn" (local and world). It fails on `main` with "nothing read the session stream".
- Passing locally on macOS arm64, Node 24 (and Bun 1.4.2 for the suites CI runs on Bun): `test-durable-core.mjs` memory, local and world (memory and local on Bun too); `test-durable.mjs` memory, local and world on native, and local on Wasm; `test-durable-harness.mjs` on Bun; `test-types.mjs`.

title: End a call a crash left running for the turn's viewers too
body:
When a resumed turn answers a call as possibly run, its events now start with a `tool_end` for that call: `isError: true`, with the same text the model gets as the call's result.

## Why

After a crash, a call with effects is not run again. The kernel answers it with "fx stopped while this tool was running, so it may have partly run…", and the model decides what to do. The host never heard that answer: the call's `tool_start`, written before the crash, had no matching `tool_end`, neither from `createFxEngine().resume()` nor on a durable session's stream. A page that draws tool calls from the stream showed the call running forever, and had to close it itself when it saw `turn_resume`.

Seen on Vercel with libfx 0.0.13-dev.1432: in 12 of 12 crash drills (a non-idempotent tool whose function exits mid-call), the session stream held the call's `tool_start` and no `tool_end`, while the model was told the call may have partly run.

## What changed

- `resume()`, and `prompt()` with the open turn's `turnId`, ask `onAmbiguous` about the calls the crash left running, as before, and now also keep the calls it did not choose to run again. The turn they return yields a `tool_end` for each of those first, before anything the kernel streams.
- A call `onAmbiguous` reran (an idempotent tool in a durable session) gets no extra event: its rerun streams its own `tool_start` and `tool_end`, as before.
- The text is the kernel's `unfinished_tool_output` (`session_adapter.zig`), repeated as a constant in `fx-sdk.js`; the tests check it against the tool result in the model request, so the two cannot drift apart unnoticed.
- The README's "Tools with side effects" says the turn's events end the call with that error.
- `DurableSession.tla`: a worker that continues a turn whose call is answered as possibly run writes `turn_resume` and then the call's `tool_end`, as a rerun writes `turn_resume` and `tool_start`. `drive.mjs` compares the code's UI lines with the model's, so the send graph needs it (send 95,299 states, leased 204,165; lookup and cutoff unchanged; every witness still reached).

## Tests

- `sdk/tests/test-journal.mjs`, "a resumed turn answers a call a crash left running instead of running it again": the resumed turn's first event is the call's `tool_end`, with `isError: true` and the model's answer, and the call has no other event. Passes native → Wasm and Wasm → native.
- `sdk/tests/test-durable.mjs`, "a crash during send never sends twice, and the turn goes on": the session stream holds one `tool_end` for the crashed call, after `turn_resume`, naming the call the model heard about. It does not assert the dead worker's `tool_start`, which may not have landed before the kill. Fails on `main` with "the call ended once" (0 ends).
- Passing locally on macOS arm64, Node 24: `test-durable.mjs` memory, local and world on native and local on Wasm; `test-durable-provider-crash.mjs` native; `test-world-persistence.mjs` native and Wasm; `test-checkpoint.mjs` native → Wasm; `check.sh`; and, on Bun 1.4.2, `drive.mjs` send (40 walks), lookup (40, seed 7), send and lookup on world (20, seeds 3 and 9), cutoff (20, seed 5) and leased (40, seed 12).
