title: Hold durable sessions on Vercel by their queue message
body:
On Vercel, a durable session's worker no longer renews its lease in the session's log while a turn runs. The queue already knows whether the function holding a turn is alive, so libfx uses that: a lease names the queue delivery that took it, and the next delivery of that message takes the session over. A function that crashes mid-turn now loses its session in about 1.3 s instead of about 15 s, and a running turn writes nothing to show it is alive.

## Why

`vercel()` holds a 15 s lease that each worker renews every 5 s. Each renewal is an `fx.log` event in the session's run, about 12 writes a minute per running turn, read back by every fold of the log. And a function that crashes keeps its session for the rest of its lease: a crash 1.5 s into a tool call was taken over 14.9 s and 15.1 s later.

Vercel Queues already tracks this. A delivery keeps its message from every other delivery while the function handles it (`@vercel/queue` extends the visibility while the handler runs), and hands the message on only once that delivery let it go without acknowledging it. And when a function's process exits mid-delivery, Vercel runs the same delivery again in a new instance about a second later, with the same message id and delivery count (in our drills, 1.0 to 1.1 s after the exit).

## What changed

Two commits, then a README wording fix and a merge of `main` (the README rewrite).

**Take a session over when its holder's queue message comes back.**

- Each lease records `delivery: { messageId, attempt }`, from the metadata every World's queue handler receives (world-vercel passes the Vercel Queues message id and delivery count, world-local its own). Renewals and checkpoints carry it too.
- A delivery of that same message in another process, at that attempt or a later one, treats the lease as dead and claims the session at once, whatever the lease's expiry. A worker still running in this process (`liveHolders`) is never taken over this way.
- This applies on any World that reports message ids, `vercel({ leaseMs })` included: it is what turns the 15 s takeover above into about 1.2 s.

**Hold sessions on Vercel by their queue message, without lease renewals.**

- `world()` takes `queueLeases: true` for a World whose queue holds and redelivers messages this way. A worker on such a World holds its lease to its deadline (`getRuntimeDeadline()` or `maxDurationMs`) and renews nothing. One with no deadline still renews, as today.
- `vercel()` sets it, unless the app passes `leaseMs`, which keeps today's renewed lease.
- A worker whose write fails under a queue-held lease has the queue deliver its own message again (the handler throws, and world-vercel retries the same message) instead of returning `{ timeoutSeconds: 1 }`, which world-vercel sends on as a new message. Otherwise a release that failed would leave the lease standing until the function's deadline.
- A message that finds the session held comes back once the lease would run out, as today; with a queue-held lease that is the holder's deadline (capped at 300 s, as today), not every 15 s.

**What it costs.** A function that stops without its process exiting, for example an instance that is lost or frozen, keeps the message until the queue's hold on it lapses. world-vercel's handler uses `@vercel/queue`'s default 300 s visibility, so that case takes up to five minutes (or the function's deadline, when another message for the session arrives first), against about 15 s with renewals. `vercel({ leaseMs: 15_000 })` keeps the old bound for apps that want it. A shorter bound without renewals needs world-vercel to let a queue handler set its visibility timeout.

## Model

`DurableSession.tla` gets `QueueHeld`: a freeze is the queue giving up on the holder's delivery, and only the worker the queue hands that message to may take the session over; every other worker still finds the lease held (`lapse`). `check.sh` checks a new `queue` graph (send, 91,835 states, every invariant), and the existing graphs are unchanged (same state counts). `drive.mjs queue` walks the real code along it on a World whose queue delivers as Vercel Queues does (`sdk/tests/queue-world.mjs`); the Start that finds a frozen holder delivers that holder's message to the other agent. CI runs it with `--walks 40 --seed 4`.

## Measurements

A small Next.js app on Vercel built on `createFxAgent` (libfx 0.0.13-dev.1432 with this branch's `durable.js` and durability bundles), its wake route at `maxDuration: 60`, Node.js 24. Times come from the session log's own `createdAt` timestamps.

Crash drill: the model calls a non-idempotent tool whose function `process.exit(1)`s 1.5 s into the call. Recovery is the crash to the takeover's lease.

| | Recovery after the crash | Prompt to the turn's end |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Renewed 15 s lease, no delivery check (as published today) | 14.9 s, 15.1 s | 20.6 s, 21.2 s |
| Queue-held lease, takeover only on a later attempt | 57.8 to 59.4 s (n=3), at the 60 s deadline | 64.9 to 65.9 s |
| This PR, `vercel()` | 1.24, 1.31, 1.38, 1.41 s | 6.8 to 7.5 s |
| This PR, `vercel({ leaseMs: 15_000 })` | 0.99, 1.24, 1.40 s | 7.1 to 7.8 s |

The second row is why a delivery at the same attempt counts: the one that takes over after a process exit is Vercel running the same delivery again, at the same delivery count. In every drill the payment did not run again, and the model said it may have partly run.

Writes: a session with one short turn, then a turn that waits 40 s in a tool and continues once after a yield, holds 3 `lease` entries with this PR (one per claim) against 11 with renewals (8 renewals during the 40 s).

## Tests

- `test-durable-core.mjs` runs on a fourth durability, `queue`: an app-built World on world-local's store whose queue holds and redelivers as Vercel Queues does (`queueLeases: true`, a 10 minute deadline). All 29 core tests pass on it, plus:
  - a later delivery of the holder's message, and the same delivery run again, each take over a session whose lease would stand for another minute (also on `world`);
  - a held session writes one lease and no renewals while a renewed one writes at least 6 in 2.5 s;
  - a worker whose release failed gets its own message back and lets the session go (fails on the first commit alone: the next prompt waits for the deadline).
- `world()` validates `queueLeases`; `types/durable-world.d.ts`, `types/durable-vercel.d.ts` and the type fixture cover it.
- Passing locally on macOS arm64 (Node 24; Bun 1.4.2 where CI uses Bun): `test-durable-core.mjs` memory, local, world and queue; `test-durable.mjs` memory, local and world on native, local on Wasm; `test-durable-provider-crash.mjs`; `test-durable-harness.mjs`; `test-types.mjs`; `check.sh` (all graphs and witnesses); `drive.mjs` queue (40 walks, seeds 4 and 21), send, lookup, send and lookup on world, cutoff and leased with the walks and seeds CI uses.
- Not run: `test-durable.mjs vercel` and `drive.mjs --durability vercel`, which need a Vercel access token configured as `sdk/tests/vercel-storage.mjs` describes.

title: Exit with 2 when the command line is wrong
body:
## Summary

- An unknown command, an unknown or invalid flag, or a missing or bad argument now exits with 2 instead of 1, on every command.
- `fx ask` exits 2 for a missing prompt, an unknown flag, or `--no-save` with `--resume`, including in `--json` mode, where the JSON error body is unchanged.
- `fx replay` exits 2 for argument errors and still exits 1 when a tape is missing or malformed.
- Work that fails after the command line is accepted still exits 1.

Docs to update on fx.sh: the exit codes on `using-fx/cli` and `using-fx/fx-ask`.

title: Parse fx ask flags with one shared parser
body:
## Summary

- `fx ask` accepts `--flag=value` for every flag that takes a value.
- When `fx ask` flags repeat or conflict, the last one wins: `--fast --no-fast` runs with Fast mode off, and `--auto --full-access` runs with full access.
- `fx ask --permission-mode ask|auto|full-access` and `fx ask --ask` set the permission mode for one request.
- A bad `fx ask` flag prints what's wrong before the usage line: an unknown flag with the closest match when one is near, a missing value, a value on a flag that takes none, or an invalid value.
- `fx ask --timeout` rejects a value that isn't a whole number of seconds instead of ignoring it.
- `fx ask --resume-id` is removed and fails with a hint to use `--resume <id>`.
- `fx ask --help` is rendered from the same option list the parser reads.

Docs to update on fx.sh: `using-fx/fx-ask` (`--permission-mode`, `--ask`, `=value`, last flag wins, `--resume-id` removed). vercel-labs/fx-web#193 adds the permission-mode flags. vercel-labs/fx-web#166 covers `=value` and last flag wins on the CLI page, and fx.sh never documented `--resume-id`.

Stacked on #1232.

title: Cut resume down to seven spellings
body:
## Summary

Resume now has one spelling per job: `fx -c`, `fx --continue`, `fx -r`, `fx --resume [last|<id>]`, `fx session resume [last|<id>]`, `fx ask --resume`, and `/resume`.

The other spellings fail with exit code 2 and name the replacement:

- `fx --resume-last` points to `fx --resume last`.
- `fx --resume-<id>` points to `fx --resume <id>`.
- `fx resume [last|<id>]` and `fx resume --id <id>` point to `fx --resume` and `fx session resume`.
- `fx session resume --id <id>` points to `fx session resume <id>`.
- `fx session resume --resume --last` points to `fx session resume last`.

`fx resume <id> --upgrade-relaunch` still works, because an older fx restarts the new version that way after an upgrade. `fx --help` and the resume usage line list only the kept spellings.

Docs to update on fx.sh: `using-fx/cli` and `using-fx/sessions` wherever they show `--resume-last`, `--resume-<id>`, `fx resume`, or `--id`.

title: Stop request watches instead of cancelling them
body:
## Summary

- MCP requests over HTTP, legacy HTTP with SSE, and stdio no longer leave a cancellation signal that can break a connect starting at the same time on macOS. That connect used to fail with an unexpected error, or crash a Debug build.
- MCP OAuth refreshes, Keychain credential reads and writes, MCP requests to ACP-hosted servers, ACP elicitation replies, MCP questions answered in `fx ask`, and `web_fetch` host name lookups no longer leave that signal either.
- Cancelling or timing out a Keychain credential write now kills and reaps the `osascript` helper instead of leaving it running.
- Keychain read output that arrives after a cancel is zeroed before it is freed.
- A `web_fetch` host name lookup no longer keeps running against freed memory when its deadline watch fails to start or the task running the fetch is cancelled.
- An ACP elicitation that fx abandons because its own task was cancelled now tells the client to cancel the request.

title: Bug: ACP `provider` config option uses `category: "model"`, so spec-following clients pick it as the model selector
body:
### Issue details

`fx acp` tags more than one session config option with `category: "model"`, and the first of them is the `provider` selector rather than the model selector. ACP clients that follow the spec end up using `provider` as the model picker, so they can't select a model and session setup fails.

**Where it happens** (main @ `2c7a4f8`, `src/acp/sessions.zig`):

- `writeProviderConfigOption` → `{"id":"provider","name":"Provider","category":"model",...}`. It is written **first** in `configOptions` on native builds (around line 642, and again around line 1314).
- `writeModelConfigOption` → `{"id":"model","name":"Model","category":"model",...}`, written second.
- `writeFastConfigOption` / `writeUltrafastConfigOption` → also `"category":"model"`.

**What the spec says** ([Session Config Options → Option Categories](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/session-config-options)):

- `model`: *Model selector*
- `model_config`: *Model-related parameter, such as context size or speed/quality trade-off*
- Category names that begin with `_` are free for custom use.
- *When multiple options share the same category, Clients SHOULD use the array ordering to resolve ties, preferring earlier options in the list.*

Because `provider` comes first, a client that follows that rule treats `provider` as the model selector.

**Repro** with v0.0.13 and a configured custom provider:

1. `fx acp`, then `initialize`, then `session/new`. The result contains:
   ```json
   [
     {"id":"provider","category":"model","currentValue":"pi","options":[{"value":"gateway"},{"value":"codex"},{"value":"grok"},{"value":"pi"}]},
     {"id":"model","category":"model","currentValue":"claude-opus-5.5","options":[...]},
     {"id":"mode","category":"mode",...}
   ]
   ```
2. The client (T3 Code in my case) picks the first `category: "model"` option and sends the chosen model to it:
   ```text
   session/set_config_option {configId:"provider", value:"claude-haiku-5.5"} -> {"code":-32602,"message":"Invalid provider"}
   session/set_config_option {configId:"model",    value:"claude-haiku-5.5"} -> ok
   ```
3. The session never opens. T3 shows `Failed to open acpRegistry provider session ...`.

The T3 maintainers traced the problem to this tagging. See [pingdotgg/t3code#18586](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/18586#issuecomment-6120752625). T3 is also tracking its own picker inconsistency there, but there's no client-side workaround.

**Expected:** only the real model selector uses `category: "model"`. Suggested change:

- `provider` → a custom category such as `_provider`. A provider switch isn't a model parameter, so `model_config` doesn't seem right either.
- `fast` / `ultrafast` → `model_config`. They're speed/quality trade-offs, which is the spec's own example for that category.

`model` would then be the only `category: "model"` option, and its position in the array would no longer matter.

### Trace

Not applicable. This is an ACP payload shape issue; the JSON-RPC exchange above is the relevant part.

### Sensitive information

- [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

title: Parse global fx flags with the shared parser
body:
## Summary

- The flags before a command or an interactive launch (`--model`, `--provider`, `--effort`, `--fast`, `--add-dir`, and the rest) now go through the same parser as `fx ask`, so every flag that takes a value accepts `--flag=value`.
- When those flags repeat or conflict, the last one wins. `fx --fast --no-fast` and `fx --no-additional-dirs --no-additional-dirs` no longer fail.
- `fx --permission-mode ask|auto|full-access`, `--ask`, `--auto`, `--full-access`, and `--yolo` set the permission mode for one interactive session. The flag wins over `FX_PERMISSION_MODE` and is never saved.
- A missing value or a value on a flag that takes none prints the flag's name, such as `fx: --model needs a value`.
- Putting a session-only flag before a subcommand, such as `fx --auto status`, and using `--add-dir` outside a launch are usage errors and exit 2.
- `fx --help` lists the permission flags, and a test checks that every global flag the parser reads is listed there.

Docs to update on fx.sh: `using-fx/cli` (permission flags, `=value`, last flag wins).

Stacked on #1234.

title: Parse every command's flags with the shared parser
body:
## Summary

- Every remaining command reads its flags through the shared parser, from the same option lists its help shows: `fx sessions`, `fx session` (and `migrate`, `recover`), `fx usage`, `fx upgrade`, `fx workspace`, `fx status`, `fx doctor`, `fx models`, `fx permissions`, `fx mcp list`, `fx acp`, `fx pr`, `fx issue`, and `fx replay`.
- Every flag that takes a value accepts `--flag=value`, and when a flag repeats the last one wins. `fx sessions --limit=5 --limit 2` lists two sessions, `fx session --id=a --id b` opens `b`, and `fx acp --ultrafast --no-ultrafast` starts with Ultra mode off.
- A bad flag names the problem before the usage line: `fx status: unknown flag --jsno (did you mean --json?)`, `fx sessions: --limit needs a value`, `fx acp: --log-file needs a value`, or `fx workspace: --json doesn't take a value`.
- `fx usage` follows the parser's rule for a repeated flag, as every other command does: the last one wins. Its new parser on `main` rejected `--period` or `--json` given twice.
- A session still takes one target. Two targets, or a target together with `--id`, print the usage line.
- A session ID that starts with `-`, which fx can generate, still works as that target: `fx session -_u88j00skyI` looks the session up instead of reporting an unknown flag.
- `fx pr --auto=yes` and `fx issue --create=1` are usage errors that exit 2. Before, the text was passed to the agent as part of the context.

title: Fail CI when CLI code parses a flag by hand
body:
## Summary

- `scripts/check_cli_shape.py` now fails when code in `src/core/cli/` compares an argument with a flag literal outside a test. Each remaining comparison, such as help and version detection or the fixed resume grammar, is listed in `hand_parsed_flags` with its reason, and a listed flag that nothing compares any more is reported as stale.
- The check no longer compares `fx ask` and the global flags against help text, because every command now parses from the option lists help renders, and the build fails when a parser and its list disagree.

title: Search large files in grep, skip FIFOs, and treat a relative HOME as unset
body:
## Summary

- `grep_files` searches files of any size. A file over 200 KiB no longer answers "no matches" for text it contains.
- A match on a line longer than 64 KiB shows the line's first 64 KiB.
- `grep_files` skips a FIFO, including one reached through a symlink, instead of hanging until a writer appears.
- With `path` set to one file, an `include` pattern with a slash, such as `src/*.zig`, matches the file's path relative to the workspace, as in folder searches.
- A relative or empty `HOME` is treated as unset. fx no longer aborts, writes nothing under the current folder, and commands that need `HOME` say it is not set. Child processes still get `HOME` unchanged.

title: Keep the ui-activity benchmark's output in PGSO round logs
body:
## Summary

- The PGSO `Heavy ui-activity` job keeps the benchmark's own stdout and stderr in each round's log, so a failed round shows the timing ratios and the error instead of only hyperfine's "non-zero exit code 1".
- A passing round adds two short lines per benchmark to its log. Both binaries in a round are measured the same way.

title: Require idempotent on libfx tools and speed up durable turns
body:
## Summary

- `createFxAgent` refuses a tool that doesn't set `idempotent`, and the error names both choices. MCP tools are `idempotent: false`.
- A tool with `idempotent: true` that doesn't write starts as soon as the model calls it, without waiting for the call to be saved.
- `writes` defaults to the opposite of `idempotent`, so only tools that are safe to repeat run in parallel.
- When a crash lands between a model response and the save of its tool calls, the resumed turn asks the model again with its tools instead of going on without their results.
- Each tool call's result is saved as soon as that call finishes, so a crash leaves no finished call in doubt.
- Events that arrive while a save is in flight go out together in the next record, and `append()` says with `barrier` whether the engine waits for it.
- Each progress record holds only what's new since the previous one.
- A session saves a checkpoint at a turn's end or yield only after 64 KiB of new records, instead of at every turn's end.
- The next prompt starts as soon as the previous turn ends, instead of waiting up to a second for the old worker to notice.
- On Vercel, `prompt()` runs the turn in the request that called it when no other invocation holds the session. Vercel Queues keeps the prompt until after that request's time limit and continues the turn if the request dies. `world()` takes `runInRequest` and `waitUntil`.
- On a World with Workflow's in-band writer fence, the World refuses a claim or record from a worker another has replaced, so none of it is stored.
- `libfx/durable-local` and `libfx/durable-vercel` bundle world-local 5.1.1 and world-vercel 5.2.1, whose Worlds have that fence.
- `stream(cursor)` starts reading at the cursor's line instead of the stream's start.
- A `checkpoint` option written by a newer libfx throws `FxJournalVersionError`.
- `libfxApiVersion` is 3.
- The SDK README explains when to set `idempotent: false`, and documents `yieldAt`, `load()`'s `head` and `retryAfterSeconds` in the Vercel trigger.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#162

Includes #1227, with its merge against #1230 resolved.

Also fixes the ACP unit test that fails on main since the Gateway's model catalog grew past what it read.

title: Check model flags against the model catalog
body:
## Summary

- `fx ask` stops before sending a request when `--model` names no catalog model, and points to `fx models`.
- `fx ask` stops when `--model` matches several catalog models, and lists them.
- `fx ask --model` with a unique partial name, such as `sonnet-4.5`, runs on its full catalog ID.
- `fx ask` stops before sending a request when the model doesn't offer `--fast`, `--ultrafast`, or the `--effort` level, and names the model. `--json` reports `UnsupportedFast`, `UnsupportedEffort`, or the existing `UltrafastUnavailable` code.
- A rejected `fx ask` run no longer leaves an empty saved session.
- Interactive `fx` checks the same flags when the model catalog loads. An unknown model falls back to the configured model, and an unsupported speed or effort is turned off, each with a notice. The footer shows what the next request uses.
- Without an authenticated catalog, such as when the catalog fails to load or only the public catalog is available, model names pass through as before.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#163

title: Add -m as the short form of --model
body:
## Summary

- `-m <id>` selects the model the same way as `--model <id>` for interactive `fx`, `fx ask`, and `fx acp`.
- Help and usage text show `-m, --model <id>`.
- A missing model value now reports `-m/--model requires a model id`.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#163

title: Steer libfx turns the way the fx CLI does
body:
## Summary

- A libfx steer sent while the model streams a reply cuts the reply short, and the turn continues with the steer and the text written so far, on the native addon and on WebAssembly.
- A steer sent once the model has started a tool call, or while a tool runs, waits for the tool, then joins the same turn.
- A durable steer sent while a turn waits to start joins that turn instead of running after it.
- Cancelling a turn keeps the steers it never placed, and a steer that arrives as a turn ends is refused instead of dropped. A durable session runs either as the next turn.
- `session.steer()` takes a `messageId`. A retry with the same id adds nothing. A steer that reuses a prompt's id is rejected with `FX_MESSAGE_ID_IN_USE`, or reported as a `session.error` with that code on a queue that outlives the process.
- `session.steer()` resolves with `{ messageId }`, and the `user_message` event carries the steer's id. It is sent when a model request carries the steer, not when the steer is queued.
- A durable steer with images ends the running turn at its next safe point and runs as the next turn. Steers sent after it join its turn.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#164

title: Durable sessions: a queued turn doesn't say which agent it's for, so an app can have only one durable agent
body:
## What happens

Every durable agent queues its turns on one topic, `__libfx_wkf_workflow_session` (`queueName` in `sdk/durable.js`), and a queued message carries the session id and the prompt, not the agent. So an app with two durable agents (say a support agent and a coding agent, with different models, instructions and tools) can't tell their turns apart:

- **In one process** (a World with `registerHandler`, such as the local World): `listen()` hands each delivery to the agents on that World in turn (`handlers[listeners.turn++ % handlers.length]`), so a session's turns can alternate between the two agents.
- **On Vercel:** one wake route can mount only one agent's `wakeHandler()`, and that agent runs every queued turn with its own model and tools. Two wake routes subscribed to the topic are two consumers, so each gets every turn.

Either way a session can run a turn with an agent that didn't create it. Today the safe rule is one durable agent per app. (From reading `sdk/durable.js` at 31ddc74d64.)

## Proposal

- **A name per agent:** `createFxAgent({ name: 'support', ... })`, defaulting to `'default'`, recorded on the session when it's created and in each queued message.
- **Delivery by name:** `listen()` keeps handlers by name, and a delivery goes to the agent named in the message (or, for a message without one, the name the session recorded). A name no agent in the process has is left for the queue to deliver again, or fails with an error that names it.
- **One wake route for every agent:** a module-level handler (for example `import { wakeHandler } from 'libfx'`) that dispatches to whichever agent in the process has the message's name. A deployment then mounts one route and one `vercel.json` trigger however many agents it has; `agent.wakeHandler()` keeps working for single-agent apps.
- **One topic,** so the existing `vercel.json` trigger doesn't change.

Happy to send a PR if this direction works for you.

title: Leave out old images to fit native libfx requests
body:
## Summary

- On the native libfx backend, a request whose images would pass the 8 MiB fetch bridge leaves out its oldest images, each with a note, instead of failing with `HostStreamBackpressure`.
- Native libfx conversations keep working after their images add up to more than about 6 MiB.
- Codex, Grok and configured providers on the native backend fit their requests the same way.
- The WebAssembly backend and the fx CLI keep their current request limits.

title: Measure ui-activity growth in one paired window
body:
## Summary

- The ui-activity benchmark's growth gate now times a fresh fixture and a grown one in alternation within one window, instead of timing one fixture in two separate windows. A CPU slowdown between the windows no longer reads as growth.
- The PGSO `Heavy ui-activity` job failed this way on recent runs: per-batch p95 times flipped between about 1.0 and 2.5 microseconds while the work stayed the same, on both the candidate and the control.
- A new test simulates a 2.5 times slowdown halfway through the window and checks that the paired ratio stays at 1.0.
- On the macOS arm64 PGSO runners, 102 benchmark runs each: the old growth ratio ranged from 0.490x to 1.966x (standard deviation 0.162), against a 2.0x limit. With this change it ranged from 0.960x to 1.033x (standard deviation 0.014).

title: Start a session with a first prompt from the command line
body:
## Summary

- `fx "<prompt>"` starts an interactive session and sends the prompt as the first message once the first frame is on screen. Launch flags can go before or after the prompt, and `fx -- "<prompt>"` takes a prompt that starts with a dash.
- Several unquoted words, such as `fx fix the login bug`, exit 2 with `fx: put the prompt in quotes: fx "fix the login bug"`. An empty prompt exits 2.
- A first word one or two edits from a command name, such as `fx stauts`, exits 2 with `fx: unknown command stauts (did you mean status?)`, and `fx version` suggests `--version`. Any other word that isn't a command is now a first prompt, where it used to print "unknown subcommand" and the full help.
- An unknown launch flag, such as `fx --modle x`, exits 2 with `fx: unknown flag --modle (did you mean --model?)`, before or after a prompt.
- `fx -p` and `fx --print` exit 2 and say to use `fx ask "<prompt>"`, repeating the prompt when one follows.
- `fx -c "<prompt>"` and `fx -r <id|last> "<prompt>"` (also `--resume` and `--resume=`) resume that session and send the prompt as its next message.
- `-r` is the short form of `--resume`: `fx -r last` and `fx -r <id>` resume that session, and a bare `fx --resume` opens the session picker instead of the newest session. `fx --resume=<id>` works too.
- `fx --help` shows `fx [flags] "<prompt>"`, an example, and one `-r, --resume [last|<id>]` row.
- The `fx-cli-shape` skill describes the first prompt, the `-p` hint, and the single `-r`/`--resume` flag.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#166 updates `using-fx/cli` and `using-fx/sessions`.

Stacked on #1239.

title: Save session images once
body:
## Summary

- A durable session saves each prompt image once, named by the SHA-256 of its bytes, and its log, records and checkpoints refer to that name. Sessions no longer stop working once their images pass 4 MiB.
- Sending the same image again in a session stores it once.
- A session keeps its newest 4,096 images, up to 512 MiB. Once a turn is recorded, an older image leaves the conversation and keeps only its name, and the model sees a note in its place. An open loads those images and a resumed turn's own, so a session never saves more than it can open again, and a turn that fails drops nothing.
- A durable session keeps its images in streams of its own World run. The image store stays internal: durable sessions hand it to the engines they run, and `createFxEngine()` persistence is unchanged, so an engine's own store keeps images inline as before. The README now says so and points conversations with many images to durable sessions.
- A durable prompt still takes image data as a base64 string, as on main. A prompt whose image can't be stored is rejected with the store's error before anything is recorded.
- A durable prompt libfx would refuse now throws from `prompt()`, by the same rules as an engine's `prompt()`, instead of being stored and ending as an error turn: an empty prompt, base64 that isn't canonical, an image whose bytes aren't its type, more than 8 images, or more than 6 MiB of them. An engine's `prompt()` now refuses mislabeled image bytes and empty prompts too, and the core refuses a libfx prompt over those limits.
- A durable prompt whose signal aborts before it is stored ends `cancelled` at once, without waiting for its image writes, and neither it nor a cancel naming it is stored.
- A durable session whose store lost an image the session still keeps, or holds other bytes under its name, ends that turn with an error naming the image, and later prompts still run. An open reads only the images the session keeps, so a lost older one doesn't stop it.
- A durable retry of a prompt the session already holds is answered from the log without writing its images again.
- Each image block is read once, so a getter or a replaced array method can't make libfx check one value and store another.
- A 3.75 MiB image encodes in under 5 ms instead of about 90 ms, with the runtime's own base64 encoder where one exists.
- A durable steer with images still sends its image data as base64 in its queue message and log entry, as on main. Its images are saved by name once the steer runs as a turn; saving the steer itself by name comes with images from host tools in a follow-up.
- Sessions saved by earlier libfx versions open and continue. An earlier version refuses a session that names images as written by a newer libfx.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#165

title: Keep shell commands running on gVisor when a child process exits
body:
## Summary

- Shell commands on gVisor sandboxes, such as Modal, no longer fail with `Unexpected` and an indeterminate status when a process they started exits while fx checks the process tree.
- The first shell command's startup snapshot on gVisor is no longer cut off partway, so later commands reuse it instead of running the startup files every time.

title: Keep the Ctrl-O reading position when the transcript page rebuilds
body:
## Summary

- Scrolled back in the Ctrl-O transcript viewer, the view no longer jumps by a few rows when the page is rebuilt, such as when a running command finishes and its wrapped header changes height. The viewer keeps showing the entry it showed before the rebuild.

The viewer kept its position as a row offset into the page it was measured on. A rebuilt page reused that offset, so when rows above it changed height the view landed on different content. The rebuilt page now resolves the position from the entry that offset showed, through the existing bookmark that already handles resizes.

This was the intermittent macOS failure of `streaming scroll stays inline while Ctrl-O preserves native selection` in `tui-resume.test.ts`, which pages up while a command is still printing. On an arm64 Mac with the CI build flags it failed 7 of 10 runs before this change and 0 of 10 after.

title: Durable sessions: record a queue namespace on libfx's runs so a Workflow World's restart recovery doesn't fail them
body:
## What happens

On world-local and world-postgres, a World's `start()` re-enqueues every run that's still pending or running (`reenqueueActiveRuns` in `@workflow/world`). Since vercel/workflow#4835 (released in `@workflow/world` 5.0.4, `@workflow/world-local` 5.1.1, `@workflow/world-postgres` 5.0.4) it sends each run back to the queue namespace the run recorded when it was created (`run_created` → `executionContext.queueNamespace`). A run that recorded none goes to the starting process's default prefix, `__wkf_workflow_`.

libfx's `run_created` records no namespace (`createRun` in `sdk/durable.js` at 735670679a: `eventData: { deploymentId, workflowName: "libfx/session", input }`). So in an app that also uses the Workflow SDK and shares the World's data directory or database, the Workflow SDK's World recovers every open libfx session on its own route at startup. The Workflow handler doesn't know `libfx/session` and fails the run (`WorkflowNotRegisteredError`). Seen under `next dev` with world-local: an open libfx session ended `failed` after a restart.

## Proposal

1. Record the namespace libfx already uses (its prefix is `__libfx_wkf_workflow_`) when it creates a run:

   ```js
   eventData: { deploymentId, workflowName: "libfx/session", input, executionContext: { queueNamespace: "libfx" } }
   ```

   Recovery then sends the run to `__libfx_wkf_workflow_libfx/session` with `{ runId }`. That's a valid queue name under libfx's prefix, so it reaches libfx's handler instead of the Workflow SDK's.
2. Handle that message. Today `deliverTo` returns without doing anything when a delivery has no `input`, which is safe: the session is left alone, not failed. Better still, treat `{ runId }` as "continue this session if it has an unfinished turn", so a restart resumes libfx sessions the same way it resumes workflow runs.

Sessions created before the change record no namespace and stay exposed until they finish. Item 1 alone stops new sessions from being failed.

title: Run each durable session's turns on the agent that created it
body:
## Summary

- `createFxAgent()` takes a `name`, which defaults to `"default"`, and `agent.name` returns it. A name that isn't 1 to 64 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-` throws.
- A session's turns run only on agents with the name of the agent that created it, so one app can run several durable agents with different models, instructions and tools.
- A prompt sent through another agent, such as `coding.session(supportSessionId).prompt()`, runs on the session's own agent, and the sending agent's `onEvent` gets a `session.forwarded` event.
- A process with no agent of a turn's name refuses the delivery with an `FX_NO_AGENT` error that names it, and the queue delivers it again.
- `wakeHandler` from `libfx` returns one queue route for every agent in the process. `agent.wakeHandler()` also routes by name.
- Agents created without a durability share one for each sessions location, or one on Vercel, so they can reach each other's sessions.
- Sessions stored before this change belong to the `default` agent.

Closes #1246.

title: Say where fx upgrade saved the release channel
body:
## Summary

- `fx upgrade --channel dev` prints `Release channel set to dev in ~/.fx/settings.json.` before it upgrades, so it's clear the channel applies to later upgrades too. When the saved channel already matches, it prints `Release channel is already dev.` JSON output is unchanged.
- `fx upgrade --channel nightly` prints `fx upgrade: invalid value for --channel: nightly` before the usage line. Before, it printed only the usage line. The wording matches `fx ask: invalid value for --timeout: ...`.
- `fx upgrade --json` with bad arguments now prints `{"kind":"upgrade","error":"invalid arguments","code":"InvalidUpgradeArgs"}` and exits 2, like the other commands. Before, it printed `fx: InvalidUpgradeArgs` and exited 1, which also happens on `main`.
- The `fx-cli-shape` skill shows the saved line as the example for setter commands.

## Tests

title: Report unknown settings keys in fx doctor

- `fx doctor` warns about each key that isn't in the list, with the closest known key:
  - `unknown setting fast_mdoe in ~/.fx/settings.json (did you mean fast_mode?)`
  - `unknown setting statusLine.contxt in ~/.fx/settings.json (did you mean statusLine.context?)`
  - `unknown setting efort in ~/.fx/settings.json for workspace /path (did you mean effort?)`
  - `unknown setting max_agent_step in .fx.json (did you mean max_agent_steps?)`
- Startup still ignores unknown keys without a warning, so `fx status` and every other command stay quiet. Retired keys such as `maxxing_mode` are ignored without a report.
- The "ignored in project" warning now reads the same list instead of its own hand-kept copy. A project `.fx.json` that sets `workspaces` or an MCP approval key (`enabledMcpjsonServers`, `disabledMcpjsonServers`, `enableAllProjectMcpServers`) is now reported as ignored too; before, those were ignored silently.
- The CLI shape check reads the list. Every key the profile parser reads must be listed as profile-only, every key `parseProjectSafeFields` reads must be listed as project-safe, and a project-safe entry that parser doesn't read fails.

## Tests

- Unit tests cover the list (sorted, unique), finding unknown keys at the top level, in fixed objects, and in workspace overrides, project files checked at the top level only, and the doctor message forms.
- A CLI E2E test writes four misspelled keys plus a retired one, checks that `fx doctor --json` reports exactly the four with suggestions, and that `fx status` writes nothing to stderr.
- The shape check's tests cover a missing profile key, a missing project-safe key, a stale project-safe entry, and an empty list.

## Docs

title: Add fx config list and fx config get
body:
## Summary

- `fx config list` prints the values set in `.fx.json`, `~/.fx/settings.json`, and this workspace's override in it, one `key=value` per line in git's format. Nested keys are dotted (`statusLine.context`, `models.codex`) and lists print as compact JSON. Lines run from lowest to highest precedence, so the last line for a key is the one fx uses.
- `--show-origin` starts each line with `file:.fx.json`, `file:~/.fx/settings.json`, or `workspace:<path>`, then a tab, as `git config --list --show-origin` does. `--global` and `--workspace` narrow the list to the profile's own settings or this workspace's override, and `--json` prints the same entries for scripts.
- `fx config get <key>` prints the value fx uses. For an object such as `statusLine` it prints the keys under it. A key that isn't set prints nothing and exits 1, like `git config get`.
- A key that names no setting exits 2 with the closest known key: `fx config: unknown setting fast_mdoe (did you mean fast_mode?)`. `fx config list` reports unknown keys in the files on stderr, in the same words `fx doctor` uses, or in the JSON.
- `.fx.json` contributes only its project-safe keys, since the rest are ignored. Retired keys are left out.
- Bare `fx config` lists. `set` and `unset` come in a follow-up.

```
$ fx config list --show-origin
file:.fx.json	max_agent_steps=7
file:~/.fx/settings.json	fast_mode=true
file:~/.fx/settings.json	statusLine.context=true
workspace:/Users/example/project	fast_mode=false
$ fx config get fast_mode
false
```

The values come from the files only. A flag or an `FX_*` variable can still override one for a run, and `fx status` shows what a run uses; the help text says so.

## Tests

- Unit tests cover flattening and precedence across the three sources, both scopes, `get` choosing the entry fx uses and keeping `provider` apart from `provider_order`, allocation failure in `collect`, argument parsing, loading both files with unknown keys per scope, and naming a file that isn't valid JSON.
- A CLI E2E test checks the exact `list --show-origin` output, the stderr warning, `get` with and without `--global`, exit 1 for an unset key, exit 2 for a mistyped one, the `--workspace --json` output, and that the settings file is unchanged.

## Docs

title: Classify ACP provider and speed controls as model configuration
body:
## Summary

The ACP server now gives the `provider`, `fast`, and `ultrafast` session config options the `model_config` category. The `model` option is the only one left in the `model` category. Option IDs, names, and values don't change.

## Why

fx returned up to four config options in the `model` category, and `provider` came first in the list. The [ACP spec](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/session-config-options) tells clients to break ties between options in the same category by list order, so a client that finds the model selector by its category got the provider list instead. In T3 Code, the model picker showed fx's providers instead of its models.

The spec defines `model_config` for model-related parameters such as speed or quality trade-offs, and asks clients to render those options near the model selector. The category became stable in June 2026, as the [ACP announcement](https://agentclientprotocol.com/announcements/model-config-category-stabilized) describes. Clients that set options by ID keep working, and the spec requires clients that don't recognize a category to handle it gracefully.

The changed writers build the option list for `session/new`, `session/load`, and `session/set_config_option`, so all three responses use the new categories.

## Verification

- `zig fmt --check src/` and `zig build` pass.
- A new unit test in `src/acp/sessions.zig` checks that only the `model` option uses the `model` category.
- `tests/e2e/acp.test.ts` now checks that the provider option uses `model_config` and that the first `model` option is `model`, after both `session/new` and `session/load`. These assertions fail on `main`. `acp.test.ts` and `ultrafast-fake-gateway.test.ts` pass with 185 passed and 0 failed.
- I ran `./zig-out/bin/fx acp` against a local OpenAI-compatible provider with four models and drove it the way T3 Code does. The client selected the first `model` option, switched it to another model with `session/set_config_option`, and sent a prompt. The reply came from the selected model, fx exited with code 0, and stderr was empty.
- With this build, T3 Code listed all 73 models from my configured provider, and a prompt to a selected Gemini model completed.
- `scripts/detect-macos-need.sh main HEAD` reports no macOS-specific change.

## Docs

The [ACP server](https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/acp) page says clients can select a provider, model, and mode, which stays true. No manual change is needed.

title: Bug: a plain engine that resumes a yielded turn after a checkpoint leaves a journal that won't open
Add fx config set and fx config unset
body:
## Summary

- `fx config set <key> <value>` saves a plain preference at the top level of `~/.fx/settings.json` and prints one line on stdout, like `fx upgrade --channel` and `fx provider`: `fast_mode set to true in ~/.fx/settings.json.`, or `fast_mode is already true.` when nothing changes. `fx config unset <key>` removes it, and a parent object left empty goes too.
- Covered keys: `effort`, `fast_mode`, `ultrafast_mode`, `update_channel`, `theme`, `auto_upgrade`, `max_agent_steps`, `max_tool_result_bytes`, `auto_compact_percent`, `provider_strict`, `context`, `collapse_tool_calls`, `session_titles`, `slash_menu_categories`, `startup_scrollback`, `prompt_history.enabled`, `statusLine.*`, and `notifications.*`. Switches take `true`, `false`, `on`, or `off`. Each value is checked before saving, for example `invalid value for auto_compact_percent: 95 (use a whole number from 10 to 80)`.
- Permission, model, provider, account, and fx-managed keys are refused with exit 2 and a pointer to the command that owns them. An agent can run `fx config` through its shell tool, so it must not be able to raise its own permissions or swap the model behind permission reviews:
  - `can't change permission_mode with fx config; use /permissions in a session, or --permission-mode for one run`
  - `can't change models.codex with fx config; use /model in a session`
  - `can't change yolo_acknowledged with fx config; fx manages it`
- `--workspace` exits 2 on `set` and `unset`. fx treats preferences inside a workspace override as legacy: `/settings` saves globally, and saving a global preference removes the matching workspace value. `list` and `get` keep `--workspace` for reading.
- Writes go through the existing settings save path (`setUserPreferences`), so they use the same locking, atomic replace, file mode, and legacy workspace cleanup as `/settings`. The save path gains the seven keys it didn't write yet (`theme`, `auto_upgrade`, `max_agent_steps`, `max_tool_result_bytes`, `auto_compact_percent`, `provider_strict`, `context`) with matching validation, plus a removal for `unset`. Clearing `fast_mode` also drops the fx-managed `fast_mode_model_bound`.
- `unset` removes only the profile's top-level value. A legacy workspace copy of the same key, from an older fx, still applies until fx next saves that key; `fx config get` shows it.
- The theme name check moves into `validThemeName` in `src/core/shared/theme.zig`, so a saved name follows the same rule as a theme file.

## Tests

- Settings store: the new keys write and report no change when equal; removal clears a key, an emptied parent, and `fast_mode_model_bound`; validation rejects a bad theme, too few result bytes, an out-of-range percent, and removing a map or an unknown key.
- `fx config`: argument shapes for `set` and `unset`, `--workspace` and `--show-origin` refusals, each value turning into the patch the save path writes, the exact wording of value errors and refusals, and a check that every key `set` writes is a plain setting in the settings list.
- CLI E2E: set, set again, set with `--json`, unset, the saved file, `get` after `set`, three refusals with exact stderr and an unchanged file, and `--workspace`.
- Ran the binary: `fx status --json` reports `agent_step_limit` 0, then 12 after `fx config set max_agent_steps 12`, then 0 after `unset`.

## Docs

vercel-labs/fx-web#171, stacked on vercel-labs/fx-web#169, adds `set` and `unset` to `configure-fx/configuration` and `using-fx/cli`.

title: Request private channel and DM history scopes for MCP-v2 Slack sign-in

## Summary

MCP-v2 (`FX_MCP_ENGINE=v2`) Slack sign-in now requests `groups:history`, `im:history`, and `mpim:history` in addition to the existing nine user scopes. Without them, `slack_read_channel` and `slack_read_thread` fail with `missing_scope` in private channels, DMs, and group DMs.

The v1 engine is unchanged. It continues to request whatever fx.sh publishes for `?flow=auth`.

1. Slack Org Admins have approved the three new user scopes for the fx app.
2. fx.sh `/api/slack/auth` accepts this 12-scope set. Today it accepts only the exact nine-scope set and returns 400 for the URL this change produces. A companion fx-web change accepts both sets while still publishing nine to v1 clients.

Existing tokens keep their old scopes; users run `/mcp login slack` (or `fx mcp login slack`) again to pick up the new ones.
