title: Add fx ask --config key=value
body:
## Summary

- `fx ask --config key=value` overrides a setting for that one request, with the keys and value checks of `fx config set`:

  ```
  fx ask --config effort=high --config fast_mode=on "summarize the diff"
  ```

- It repeats, the last value for a key wins, and nothing is saved.
- Like `git -c`, it's the top settings layer. It beats every settings file, while dedicated flags such as `--fast` or `--no-fast` and `FX_*` variables still beat it, the same way they beat the files. In git, `GIT_EDITOR` beats `-c core.editor` for the same reason.
- A bad override exits 2 with the same wording as `fx config set`:
  - `fx ask: unknown setting fast_mdoe (did you mean fast_mode?)`
  - `fx ask: invalid value for fast_mode: maybe (use true or false)`
  - `fx ask: can't change permission_mode with --config; use /permissions in a session, or --permission-mode for one run`
  - `fx ask: --config needs key=value, such as --config fast_mode=on`
- Only `fx ask` takes it. An interactive session re-reads settings in about 20 places (after `/fast`, `/settings`, sign-in, a session switch), so an override there would either make `/fast` silently do nothing or vanish at the first re-read. `fx ask` reads settings once.

## How

- `config_runtime.applySettingOverrides` builds a settings object from the overrides (dotted keys become nested objects) and merges it on top of the loaded settings with the same parser and `mergeSettings` the files use.
- `app_lifecycle.loadStartupStateForRunWithOverrides` applies it right after the settings files load. `loadStartupStateForRun` passes no overrides, so other callers, such as the ACP server, are unchanged.
- `fx ask` parses `--config` through `cli_config.parseOverride`, which reuses `fx config set`'s value checks and refusals.

## Tests

- Unit: overrides beat file values, nest dotted keys, keep the last value, and leave the rest of the settings alone; `--config` parsing and every error message.
- E2E against a fake gateway: with `effort: low` and `fast_mode: false` in settings, `--config effort=low --config effort=high --config fast_mode=on` sends `reasoning: high` with fast speed; `--config fast_mode=on --no-fast` sends no fast speed; the settings file is unchanged. Removing the merge call makes this test fail.
- `fx ask --help` and the usage line list `--config <key=value>`.

Locally, `fx status --json returns valid status JSON` fails when run against a real profile whose `update_channel` is `dev`, because that test doesn't isolate `HOME`; it passes with a clean `HOME`, as in CI.

## Docs

fx.sh: `using-fx/fx-ask` gets `--config` in vercel-labs/fx-web#173.

Stacked on #1265.

title: Save full access as full-access
body:
## Summary

fx saved full access as `"yolo"` and printed `yolo` in JSON, while every flag, env var, slash command, and doc page says `full-access`. Now it uses one word everywhere it saves or prints:

| Where | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fx/settings.json` | `"permission_mode": "yolo"` | `"permission_mode": "full-access"` |
| `fx status --json`, `fx doctor --json` | `"permission_mode": "yolo"` | `"permission_mode": "full-access"` |
| `fx permissions --json` | `"mode": "yolo"` | `"mode": "full-access"` |

- Reading is unchanged: settings files and `FX_PERMISSION_MODE` that say `yolo` keep working, and the next save rewrites the word.
- ACP keeps `_meta.fx.permissionMode: "yolo"` in its mode list, because ACP clients may read that field. The mode's `value` and ID were already `full-access`, and the existing ACP test still pins `_meta`.
- The fx-managed `yolo_acknowledged` key and internal session state keep their names. Users never type them, and renaming them would need a migration.

## How

`types.PermissionMode.label()` is the saved and printed name. The settings write and `permissions.permissionModeLabel` use it; ACP's `_meta` uses the enum's own names.

## Tests

- Unit: the label round-trips through `PermissionMode.parse`; the settings save and the status snapshot write `full-access`.
- E2E: `yolo-permission-mode` (11 pass) now expects `full-access` from `fx status --json` and in the file `/permissions` and Shift+Tab save; the ACP mode tests, including a new case that starts a session from a saved `full-access`, pass when run. They sit in the `acp.test.ts` block that is skipped without an API key, so CI does not run them on this PR; #1275 moves them to the model-independent block, where CI runs them.
- Real binary with a saved `yolo`: `fx status --json`, `fx permissions --json`, and `fx doctor --json` report `full-access`; text output still says `full access`.

## Docs

fx.sh: the configuration page's Compatibility section says fx still writes `yolo`; that sentence goes. The companion PR is vercel-labs/fx-web#175.

Stacked on #1268.

title: Rename statusLine to status_line and notifications to sound
body:
## Summary

Two settings groups get the names users already see:

| Before | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `statusLine.context`, `.session`, `.workspace` | `status_line.*` | Every other settings key is snake_case |
| `notifications.turn_end`, `.attention_required`, `.max` | `sound.*` | `/sound` and `FX_SOUND` already call it sound |

Nothing breaks:

- Files with `statusLine` or `notifications` keep working.
- When fx saves one of those groups, it moves the older block to the new key, unknown children included, the way saving a model already moves the old `model` key under `models`. A group nothing saves keeps its older name.
- When a file has both spellings, the new key wins for any value both set, and `fx doctor` warns: `statusLine and status_line are both set in ~/.fx/settings.json; fx uses status_line where they differ, so remove statusLine`.
- `fx config` and `fx ask --config` accept the older spellings, such as `fx config get statusLine.context`, and always show and write the new ones. `fx config unset status_line.session` also clears an old `statusLine.session`, which would otherwise keep applying.
- Legacy copies inside workspace overrides keep their names; fx already removes those preferences when it saves.
- `sound` and `status_line` were unknown keys before, which startup ignores, so a file may already hold something like `"sound": false`. A value under either new name that isn't an object is still ignored, with a trace line, and saving that group replaces it. CI caught this through a `tui-resume` fixture that sets `sound: false`.

## How

The settings list records an older name with `renamed_to`. The parser reads the older key first so the current one wins, the save path moves the group with one helper, and `fx config list` shows an older group's values under the current name, leaving out any value the current key also sets.

## Tests

- Unit: either spelling parses and the current one wins; saving moves a group and keeps the current key's values; remove clears either spelling; `fx config` maps old spellings; the doctor message; the settings-list rename table.
- E2E: `cli` (doctor warning, `config list` and `unset` with an old file), `config-persistence` (32), `tui-slash-menu` (40, `/statusline` writes `status_line`), and `session-title` (7) pass locally.
- `notifications.test.ts` now expects `/sound` to save `sound` and remove `notifications`. It's a sound test, so it runs in CI only.
- Real binary: an old file lists as `status_line.*` and `sound.*`; `fx config set status_line.session on` turns `{"statusLine":{"context":true}}` into `{"status_line":{"context":true,"session":true}}`; `fx config get statusLine.contxt` suggests `status_line.context`.

## Docs

fx.sh: the configuration page's `statusLine.*` and `notifications.*` rows become `status_line.*` and `sound.*`, with a compatibility note. The companion PR is vercel-labs/fx-web#175.

Stacked on #1269.

title: Show FX_* setting overrides in fx config
body:
## Summary

An `FX_*` variable that overrides a setting used to win silently: `fx config` showed only the file. Now it shows where the value fx uses comes from, like git's `command line:` origin for `-c`:

```
$ FX_MAX_AGENT_STEPS=20 FX_SOUND=off fx config list --show-origin
file:.fx.json	max_agent_steps=7
file:~/.fx/settings.json	fast_mode=true
env:FX_MAX_AGENT_STEPS	max_agent_steps=20
env:FX_SOUND	sound.turn_end=false
env:FX_SOUND	sound.attention_required=false
env:FX_SOUND	sound.max=false
$ FX_MAX_AGENT_STEPS=20 fx config get max_agent_steps
20
```

- The documented setting overrides come last, as fx applies them: `FX_PROVIDER`, `FX_MODEL`, `FX_ULTRAFAST`, `FX_REVIEW_MODEL`, `FX_PROVIDER_ORDER`, `FX_PROVIDER_STRICT`, `FX_PERMISSION_MODE`, `FX_MAX_AGENT_STEPS`, `FX_AUTO_COMPACT_PERCENT`, `FX_THEME`, `FX_SOUND`, and `FX_AUTO_UPGRADE`.
- A value fx ignores, such as `FX_MAX_AGENT_STEPS=many`, isn't shown, so `get` falls back to the file the way fx does.
- `FX_SOUND` shows the three `sound.*` values its preset sets. `FX_MODEL` shows under the model of the provider in use, `models.codex` when the file chooses `codex`.
- `--json` gives env entries `"origin": "env"` and `"variable": "FX_NAME"` in place of `"file"`.
- `--global` and `--workspace` still show only their file.

## How

`src/core/config/env_settings.zig` reads each variable with the parser fx already uses for it (`agent_steps.parseMaxAgentSteps`, the compactor's `parsePercent`, `PermissionMode.parse`, the provider-order and env-boolean parsers). `FX_SOUND` and `FX_AUTO_UPGRADE` had their rules written inline at their one read site; those rules now live in `env_settings` and both fx and `fx config` call them. `fx config` appends the results as the last entries.

## Tests

- Unit: each override is read as fx reads it and ignored values are left out; the `FX_SOUND` presets and `FX_AUTO_UPGRADE` words; `load` adds env entries only without a scope, and `FX_MODEL` follows the saved provider; text and JSON rendering.
- E2E: `fx config list --show-origin` ends with the env lines, `get` returns the env value, an ignored value falls back to `.fx.json`, and `--global` shows no env lines. The `fx config` tests now clear the documented overrides, since `runFx` passes the runner's environment through.
- Real binary: `fx config get max_agent_steps` matches `fx status --json` `agent_step_limit` for `FX_MAX_AGENT_STEPS=20`, `many`, and `0`.

## Docs

fx.sh: the configuration page documents `FX_AUTO_COMPACT_PERCENT` and says `fx config list --show-origin` shows env overrides. The companion PR is vercel-labs/fx-web#175.

Stacked on #1270.

title: Keep a journal loadable when a yielded turn resumes past its checkpoint
body:
## Summary

- A `createFxEngine()` with a `persistence` store that saved a checkpoint at a yield and then continued the turn with `resume()` no longer writes records a new engine refuses to load. Before, every record the resumed turn appended made the next `createFxEngine()` throw `FX_JOURNAL_INVALID` until a later checkpoint covered it, so a crash in between lost the session.
- The checkpoint at a yield holds the open turn, and a load from it starts that turn without the progress record it folded. The first progress after such a checkpoint now carries the whole turn, as the first progress after a commit does, instead of extending that record.
- Durable sessions weren't affected: their worker closes the engine after a yield.

Fixes #1264.

title: Leave out images no request can carry before building it
body:
## Summary

- Each model request was built first with every image the conversation keeps, base64 encoded, and only then fit to the request limit (30 MiB and 100 images by default) by leaving out the oldest images. In a long image conversation, that first build held all of the history's images at once: about 500 MiB of request body at 375 MiB of images.
- The oldest images that pass the limit by their own size now leave before the first build, so a request is built close to the size it is sent at. A body is never smaller than its images, so no image the exact fit would keep leaves early, and the exact fit afterwards is unchanged.
- On the WebAssembly libfx backend, whose memory never shrinks, a session with one 3.75 MiB image per turn ran out of memory at turn 102 (`WriteFailed`, 2.9 GiB). It now runs 140 turns, 525 MiB of images, in 1.4 GiB. On native, the same 140 turns take 13 seconds instead of 78 and peak at 1.9 GB of memory instead of 3.5 GB.

title: Document running local tests with sound off
body:
## Summary

- `AGENTS.md` tells contributors to set `FX_SOUND=0` when they run the Bun test suites locally, because sound playback during a macOS test run can overload the machine and crash it.
- It names the two tests the variable doesn't silence, `notifications.test.ts` and the `/sound on` scenario in `tui-command-permissions.test.ts`, and says to leave them to CI.
- It warns that the full `bun test` run includes both and `bun test tui-*.test.ts` includes the `/sound on` test, so on macOS contributors pass test files by name.

title: Accept the agent-run flags on fx pr, fx issue, and fx acp
body:
`fx pr`, `fx issue`, and `fx acp` now take the same agent-run flags as `fx ask`, and a flag on the wrong side of a command says where it goes.

Stacked on #1271.

## Changes

- `fx pr` and `fx issue` accept `--permission-mode` and its shortcuts, `--provider`, `--model`, `--effort`, `--fast`/`--no-fast`, `--ultrafast`/`--no-ultrafast`, `--provider-order`, and `--provider-strict`/`--no-provider-strict`. They previously took only `--auto`.
- `fx acp` accepts the same set except `--provider-order` and `--provider-strict`. ACP sessions don't apply AI Gateway provider routing, so those flags would do nothing. `fx acp --permission-mode` sets the mode new sessions start in, like `FX_PERMISSION_MODE`, without saving it.
- One parser, `src/core/cli/agent_run_flags.zig`, reads the set for `fx ask`, `fx pr`, `fx issue`, and `fx acp`. `commands.zig` generates the option docs from one list, so a new agent-run flag is added once.
- Placement errors name the fix:

  ```
  $ fx --model x ask hi
  fx: put agent-run flags after the command, as in fx ask --model <id>
  $ fx --auto status
  fx: agent-run flags such as --permission-mode apply to a session and to fx ask, fx pr, fx issue, and fx acp
  $ fx ask --add-dir /tmp hi
  fx ask: unknown flag --add-dir; it goes before the command: fx --add-dir <path> ask
  ```

- Four deterministic ACP permission-mode tests lived in the block that is skipped without an API key, so CI never ran them. They use only the fake gateway and now run in the model-independent block, along with the new `fx acp --permission-mode` test.

## Testing

- New E2E: `fx issue --auto --model <id> --effort high --fast` against the fake gateway sends that model, `reasoning: high`, and fast speed.
- New E2E: `fx acp --permission-mode ask` and `fx acp --full-access` start new sessions in those modes over a saved `auto`, and the settings file is unchanged.
- `cli.test.ts` covers the new `fx acp` usage, bad values, `--provider-order` rejection, and the placement messages.
- Unit tests for the shared parser, `fx acp` and workflow parsing, and the help output.

## Docs

Companion fx.sh update: vercel-labs/fx-web#177

title: Replace fx setup with fx login vercel --api-key
body:
`fx login vercel --api-key` replaces `fx setup`, so signing in to AI Gateway has one command with two ways to connect. `fx setup` and `/setup` keep working with a warning.

Stacked on #1275.

## Changes

- `fx login vercel --api-key` pastes and saves an AI Gateway API key, exactly as `fx setup` does: it saves the key without selecting it. Plain `fx login vercel` still signs in through the browser. `fx login --api-key` defaults to vercel; `fx login codex --api-key` fails with `fx login: --api-key works only with vercel`.
- `fx login` reads its arguments through the shared flag parser, so a mistyped flag is named: `fx login: unknown flag --api-ky (did you mean --api-key?)`.
- `fx setup` prints `fx setup is deprecated; use fx login vercel --api-key`, then behaves as before, including under host-managed authentication. The warning comes from a new `replaced_by` field on the command spec, so a catalog that maps another token to the setup command prints nothing. `fx setup` leaves top-level help.
- `/setup`, an alias of `/provider`, now warns that `/login` signs in or adds an API key and `/provider` chooses a provider, then opens the provider picker as before. It leaves slash help and completion. Typing `/setup ` with a query still goes to the inline picker without the warning, since provider arguments never reach the command router.
- The missing-credentials message, the onboarding hint (`You can change this anytime with /provider.`), and the README now name the new spellings.

## Testing

- E2E: `fx login --api-key` and `fx login vercel --api-key` report a disabled key store and a missing terminal with `fx login:` messages; the vercel-only rule, an unknown flag, and two providers exit 2. `fx setup` prints the warning first. Host-managed `fx setup` warns while `fx login --api-key` stays silent. The `/setup` TUI test checks the warning in scrollback.
- Unit: `fx login --api-key` stores a pasted key in every argument order without the warning; the argument parser; `/setup` routes to its own handler while `/provider` does not; the deprecation warning for `setup` and none for `login`.
- On the built binary in a real terminal, `fx login vercel --api-key` opens the same hidden key prompt as `fx setup`.

## Docs

Companion fx.sh update: vercel-labs/fx-web#178

title: Let the shell snapshot helper exit on its own
body:
## Summary

- After the shell snapshot capture reads the login shell's output, it closes the helper's lifeline and waits for the helper to exit, instead of killing the helper's process group with SIGKILL.
- The helper stops the login shell and everything the shell started before it exits, so on gVisor the first shell command no longer ends the whole sandbox with exit 137.
- If the helper is still running about two seconds after its lifeline closes, fx kills its process group and logs that it did.

title: Turn sessions v2 on with experimental.sessions_v2
body:
`experimental.sessions_v2` turns the v2 session store on, so the experiment is a setting like any other. `--sessions-v2` and `FX_SESSIONS_V2` keep working with a warning.

Stacked on #1276.

## Changes

- `experimental.sessions_v2` is a profile setting. `fx config set experimental.sessions_v2 true` saves it, `fx ask --config experimental.sessions_v2=true` sets it for one run, and a project's `.fx.json` can't turn it on. A non-object value under `experimental`, which startup used to ignore as an unknown key, is still ignored rather than an error, and saving replaces it with a trace line.
- The setting reaches every place that chooses a session store: the interactive app at bootstrap, `fx ask` from its startup state (so `--config` applies), `fx session` and `fx sessions`, `fx doctor`, and ACP when the server starts. Commands that don't open a store never read the setting, so `fx help` and the other startup-benchmark paths don't load settings for it.
- `--sessions-v2` and `FX_SESSIONS_V2` keep working, but each prints one warning per run, such as `fx: --sessions-v2 is deprecated; use fx config set experimental.sessions_v2 true`. `fx --sessions-v2 ask --sessions-v2` warns once. The flag leaves `fx --help` and `fx ask --help` through a new `OptionDoc.hidden`, and a hidden option is never suggested for a mistyped flag. The shape registry marks `FX_SESSIONS_V2` deprecated.
- With the setting on, the exit hint says plain `fx --resume <id>`, because the setting reopens the v2 session. With only the flag or the env var, the hint still names `--sessions-v2`.

## Testing

- `sessions-v2.test.ts` (99 pass) now turns v2 on through the setting, including every tmux test. One test keeps `--sessions-v2` before and after `ask` and `FX_SESSIONS_V2=1`, and checks each prints its warning and still saves to v2. A new tmux test checks the plain exit hint with the setting on.
- The ACP session-backend tests and `ultrafast-fake-gateway.test.ts` (27 pass) choose the backend through the setting, so their empty-stderr checks hold.
- Unit: the setting is profile-only, overridable with `--config`, and tolerant of a stray value; the store writes the group and replaces a stray value; `fx config set` turns the key into the patch.
- On the built binary: `fx config set`, `get`, `list`, and `unset` for the key; the two warnings; and `fx --help` and `fx ask --help` without the flag.

## Docs

None. fx.sh has never documented the v2 session store, its flag, or its env var.

title: Name setting scopes global and workspace in /allowlist and fx mcp
body:
`/allowlist` and `fx mcp` now name where a setting lives with the same words as `fx config`: `global` for the profile and `workspace` for this folder's entry, plus `--project` only for the committed `.mcp.json`. The older words still work.

Stacked on #1278.

## Changes

- `/allowlist global add …` writes the profile's top level and `/allowlist workspace add …` writes this folder's entry, as `user` and `local` did. `/allowlist view global|workspace` works too. `user` and `local` still work as aliases.
- Everything `/allowlist` prints uses the new words: `(scope=global)`, `* allowlist: workspace persistent allow rules:`, and `global rules are shadowed by workspace settings`. The usage line, `/help`, and completion offer only `global` and `workspace`; typed old words still run but aren't completed.
- The MCP-v2 `fx mcp remove` takes `--global` for `~/.fx/mcp.json` and `--project` for `.mcp.json`; `--profile` still works. `fx mcp add` accepts `--global` as an explicit form of its default and now rejects `--global` with `--project`, matching `remove`. The usage lines and the "is in both" message name `--global`.
- JSON output is unchanged: MCP list entries keep `"source": "profile"`, because JSON fields are only added.

## Testing

- E2E: `config-persistence.test.ts` (32 pass) drives `/allowlist` in a real session with the new words and checks the saved file, and still uses `user` once to prove the alias. `mcp-verbs.test.ts` (13 pass) checks the new usage and message, `remove --global`, and `remove --profile`. `tui-slash-menu.test.ts` (40 pass).
- Unit: a new test adds and views rules with `global` and `workspace` and checks the usage for an unknown scope; the existing scope tests still type `user` and `local` and now expect the new labels; MCP parsing maps `--global` and `--profile` to the profile file and rejects `--global` with `--project` on add; completion offers the new words.

## Docs

Companion fx.sh update: vercel-labs/fx-web#179

title: Expect tui-usage in the PGSO corpus test
body:
## Summary

- Let PGSO runs pass their driver tests again by expecting the renamed `tui-usage.test.ts` instead of the removed `tui-cost.test.ts`.

title: Refresh the PGSO corpus test after the usage rename
body:
## Summary

- Unblock the macOS arm64 PGSO corpus preflight by expecting `tui-usage.test.ts` instead of its old name.

Verified with the 32 corpus tests, the behavior shard planner, `zig fmt --check src/`, `zig build`, and the freshly built binary's `--version` and `help` commands. Both binary commands exited successfully with empty stderr.

title: Honor NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb in the interactive session and fx ask
body:
fx now follows the two standard color variables everywhere it draws text. Until now only top-level help read them: the interactive session ignored `NO_COLOR` and started under `TERM=dumb`, and `fx ask` turned color off only with `--no-color`.

## What changes

- `NO_COLOR` set to any non-empty value removes color from the interactive session. Bold, dim, italic, underline, reverse, and strikethrough stay, so the selected option in a picker or question prompt is still marked (it is bold).
- `TERM=dumb` refuses the interactive session, which needs cursor movement, and exits 1 with `fx: TERM=dumb can't show the interactive session; use fx ask, or run fx in a terminal that supports cursor movement`. A missing terminal still reports the existing TTY error first.
- `fx ask` treats `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb` like `--no-color`: the layout stays, colors and hyperlinks go.
- Help now ignores an empty `NO_COLOR`, as the standard says, instead of treating its presence as set.

## How it works

`src/core/shared/terminal_env.zig` owns both checks, and help, `fx ask`, and the session all use it.

The session's colors are removed where the terminal engine parses SGR codes into cells, through one process-wide switch, `engine.colors_enabled`, set before `App.init`. Dropping color only when frames are written does not work: the frame diff compares the target grid with a grid fed from its own output, so colored target cells never match and every frame repaints. With the switch at the parser, every grid holds colorless cells and the diff stays stable. The switch is set only on the interactive path, so `fx replay` and the SDK keep their colors.

## PGSO

The PGSO corpus, pipeline, and startup measurement set `NO_COLOR=1`, which used to change nothing in the session. With this change it would train fx without color: the tests that check colors fail in training, and LLVM would learn that the color paths users run are cold. The PGSO environment and the approval review benchmark no longer set it.

## Tests

- Engine unit test: with colors off, a bold red line keeps its bold and its serialized row has no color codes.
- `tui-startup.test.ts`: `/help` shows colors without `NO_COLOR` and none with it; `TERM=dumb` exits 1 with the message.
- `ask-presentation.test.ts`: `NO_COLOR=1` and `TERM=dumb` render like `--no-color`.
- Many TUI tests already set `NO_COLOR=1`, which used to do nothing. The question-selection check in `tui-decision-prompts.test.ts` now looks for bold, the cue that survives `NO_COLOR`. Three sessions that check colors directly, one in `tui-resize.test.ts` and two in `tui-resume.test.ts`, now clear `NO_COLOR`.

## Docs

vercel-labs/fx-web#180 adds `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb` to the configuration page and notes them on the `fx ask` page.

title: Name every test hook FX_TEST_
body:
Every environment variable fx reads only for tests now starts with `FX_TEST_`. Before this change, test hooks used five prefixes: `FX_E2E_`, `FX_TERMINAL_TEST_`, `FX_COMMAND_TEST_`, `FX_TEST_`, and none at all (`FX_SKIP_ONBOARDING`, `FX_SNAPSHOT_MARKER`). That made it hard to tell a hook from a real setting.

## What changes

- 40 hooks are renamed, with no fallback to the old names. That includes the three that `fx usage` added on `main` (`FX_TEST_CHATGPT_ORIGIN`, `FX_TEST_GROK_ORIGIN`, `FX_TEST_USAGE_CLOCK_FILE`):
  - `FX_E2E_<NAME>` → `FX_TEST_<NAME>`, for example `FX_E2E_GATEWAY_CHAT_URL` → `FX_TEST_GATEWAY_CHAT_URL`
  - `FX_TERMINAL_TEST_<NAME>` → `FX_TEST_TERMINAL_<NAME>`
  - `FX_COMMAND_TEST_<NAME>` → `FX_TEST_COMMAND_<NAME>`
  - `FX_SKIP_ONBOARDING` → `FX_TEST_SKIP_ONBOARDING`, `FX_SNAPSHOT_MARKER` → `FX_TEST_SNAPSHOT_MARKER`
- Every place that sets them moves too: the E2E and eval suites, the PGSO pipeline and corpus, the benchmarks, and the SDK term test.
- `scripts/check_cli_shape.py` now rejects a registered variable whose job is `test` and whose name lacks `FX_TEST_`, and the reverse, so new hooks stay on the prefix.

Variables that only the E2E harness reads, such as `FX_E2E_REAL_API`, are not fx's and are unchanged.

None of these variables is documented on fx.sh or meant for users, so there is no docs change.

## Tests

- `python3 -m scripts.check_cli_shape` passes, and `scripts/tests/test_check_cli_shape.py` covers the new prefix rule.
- Locally, an E2E set that sets every renamed hook used by an E2E file passes: `tui-composer-edit-contracts`, `tui-auth-source-selection`, `session-title`, `acp`, `auth-refresh`, `slack-install`, `gateway-stream-lifecycle`, and `mcp-auth`.

title: Report fx mcp list usage errors as JSON with --json
body:
`fx mcp list --json` printed its usage errors as text, unlike every other command that takes `--json`. A script that ran `fx mcp list --bogus --json` got `fx mcp: unknown flag --bogus` on stderr and nothing to parse.

## What changes

When `--json` is anywhere in the arguments, a bad flag or an extra argument to `fx mcp list` now prints the shared failure shape on stdout, with exit 2 and nothing on stderr:

```json
{"kind":"mcp_list","error":"invalid arguments","code":"InvalidLocalSurfaceArgs"}
```

`kind` matches the success output. Without `--json`, the text error and usage are unchanged. The branch now uses `writeUsageOrJsonError`, which `fx status`, `fx sessions`, and the other `--json` commands already share.

The `FX_MCP_ENGINE=v2` engine keeps text errors. It has no JSON error format yet, and its success output has a different shape.

The fx.sh MCP page doesn't describe usage errors, so there is no docs change.

## Tests

- Unit: `mcp list usage errors print the JSON failure shape when --json is present` in `cli_surface.zig`.
- E2E: `fx mcp list reports bad arguments as JSON when --json is given` in `cli.test.ts`, with `--json` before and after the bad flag, an extra argument, and the unchanged text form.

title: Add FX_HOME to move fx's folder
body:
`FX_HOME` points fx at another folder for everything it keeps in `~/.fx`. It works like `CARGO_HOME` or `GNUPGHOME`, so tests, CI, and a second profile can be isolated without changing `HOME`, which every other tool also reads.

## What changes

- `FX_HOME=/tmp/fx-test fx` uses `/tmp/fx-test/settings.json`, `/tmp/fx-test/sessions`, and every other file fx keeps in `~/.fx`: sign-ins, MCP config and credentials, prompt history, usage, skills, themes, the file-index cache, recordings, traces, diagnostics, and Slack credentials. The OS keychain stays shared.
- The value must be an absolute path other than `/`. Otherwise fx exits 1 before it touches any file: `fx: FX_HOME must be an absolute path`. An empty value counts as unset, and trailing slashes are ignored.
- Messages that name a file there say `$FX_HOME/settings.json` instead of `~/.fx/settings.json` when it is set, for example `theme set to light in $FX_HOME/settings.json.` The `"file"` field in `fx config --json` output follows the same rule. Help text still documents the default, `~/.fx`.
- `fx status` and `/status` show the folder in use as `fx_home=<path>`, and `fx status --json` adds an `fx_home` field.

## How it works

`main` reads `FX_HOME` once, before any mode runs (including the terminal helper processes), and hands it to `profile_paths.useFxHome`. Every path into the folder now goes through `src/core/shared/profile_paths.zig`:

- `rootPath(alloc, home, parts)` builds a path, and the existing named helpers use it.
- Code that opens the folder without following symlinks used to open `HOME` and then `.fx`. It now opens `rootParent(home)` and then `rootName()`, which are `HOME` and `.fx` by default, or the parent and last part of `$FX_HOME`. The checks on each open are unchanged.
- `displayText` and `displayRoot` give messages the right name. `displayText` builds both versions of a string at compile time.
- `src/usage/` imports only `std`, so its host now hands it the folder's parent and name (`fx_dir_name`), and the `/usage` cache follows `FX_HOME` like the rest.

No code outside `profile_paths.zig` joins `HOME` with `.fx` anymore. The registry lists `FX_HOME` as a stable location variable.

## Tests

- Unit: `FX_HOME moves every profile path and how messages name it` in `profile_paths.zig` covers validation, both path helpers, and the message helpers.
- E2E: `FX_HOME holds settings and sessions in place of ~/.fx` in `cli.test.ts` sets a value, checks the message and `fx status --json`, saves an `fx ask` session that `fx sessions` lists, confirms that `HOME/.fx` was never created, and checks the relative-path error. `fx usage keeps its cache in FX_HOME` checks the usage cache the same way, and fails without the host change.
- By hand: an interactive session under `FX_HOME` wrote its session, prompt history, recording, shutdown report, and continue marker into the folder and created no `HOME/.fx`.

## Docs

vercel-labs/fx-web#181 documents `FX_HOME` on the configuration and data-and-privacy pages.

title: Brighten inline code in assistant replies
body: Inline code in assistant replies used the same gray as tool-call targets and the status line, so commands, paths, and flags inside a reply were easy to miss. This change gives inline code the theme's brightest neutral color. | Theme | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `fx-dark` | `38;5;245` (same as tool targets) | `38;5;255` | | `fx-light` | `38;5;247` (low contrast on white) | `38;5;235` | The new values match the existing `hint_style` and `user_card_marker_style` colors, so the builtin themes stay monochrome. The builtin retint table in `src/ui/transcript/store.zig` already maps `255` and `235` to each other, so switching between dark and light still recolors earlier replies. `AssistantPacer.rethemeInlineCode` now reads both colors from the builtin themes instead of hardcoding them, and a comptime assertion keeps the in-place rewrite safe. Blockquote content was already rendered at full brightness. Only the `│` rule is dim, so this change leaves blockquotes alone. ## Verification - `zig fmt --check src/` passes. - `zig build` passes. - `zig build test`: every rendering and theme test passes. Locally, 12 `command_runner` tests fail because a local `~/.profile` writes to stderr under the tests' temporary `HOME`. That is unrelated to this change, and CI is the gate. - `cd tests/e2e && FX_SOUND=0 bun test tui-resize.test.ts -t 'idle theme monitoring stays silent'` passes. - I ran `./zig-out/bin/fx` in tmux against a fake gateway. Inline code renders as `ESC[38;5;255m...ESC[39m`, including inside a blockquote, and stderr was empty. ## Docs No manual page names the inline code color, so the docs need no change. | After | Before | |:---|:---| | | |

title: Run direct MCP calls to unloaded tools in the shell and fx ask
body:
## Problem

In the interactive shell and `fx ask`, a selected MCP tool stays advertised only for the rest of the turn that selected it. A new turn starts with an empty selection, because neither host passes `initial_dynamic_tools`. When the model calls a tool it selected in an earlier turn, the call fails:

```
Dynamic MCP tool not selected for this model step: mcp_kit_execute. Use capability_search or mcp_select_tool to load its definition; the selected tool can be called on the next model step after its schema is advertised.
```

The model then spends a step on `mcp_select_tool` and another on the retry. Servers that expose a small set of tools the model uses every turn hit this repeatedly. With Kit (`search_tools`, `execute`, `request_status`), it happened five times in one session.

## Change

ACP already handles this case. `AgentRuntimeDeps.resolve_unselected_mcp_tool` lets `advertiseUnselectedMcpCalls` look up a live MCP tool the model called by its exact name and advertise its current definition before admission, so the call runs under the normal validation and MCP permission path. Only `src/acp/prompt.zig` set the hook. This change sets it for the other two root hosts:

- `src/core/app/app_callbacks.zig` and `src/main.zig`: `App.resolveUnselectedMcpTool` projects the tool through `self.mcp.toolSchema` with the session's permission rules and context limits, matching `App.snapshotMcpDefinition`.
- `src/core/cli/cli_ask.zig`: reuses `tool_runtime.resolveUnselectedMcpTool`, as ACP does.

A name that doesn't resolve, including an unknown, denied, or oversized tool, keeps the existing unsupported or not-selected result. Subagents are unchanged.

## Tests

- New: `a resumed fx ask turn runs a direct call to a tool selected in an earlier turn` in `tests/e2e/mcp-stdio.test.ts`. It fails on `main` with the not-selected error and passes with this change.
- Updated: `the first dynamic call after MCP reload ...` asserted the old TUI behavior that a direct call in a new turn returns selection guidance without calling the tool. The call now loads the reloaded definition and runs, so the test asserts two `tools/call` requests.

Local results on macOS arm64 with Zig 0.17.0:

- `bun test mcp-stdio.test.ts`: 132 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test acp.test.ts -t 'direct call to a supplied MCP tool'`: 1 pass
- `zig build test`: the same `command_runner` and `command_effect` shell-execution tests fail locally with and without this change (16 on `main`, 15 here), so they come from the local shell environment. CI is the authority.
- Built binary with a real Kit server: `fx ask` turn 1 selected Kit's tools and called `mcp_kit_execute`. A resumed turn 2 called `mcp_kit_execute` directly, and the call succeeded. The trace logged `loaded unselected MCP tool for direct call tool=mcp_kit_execute`.

## Docs

No manual change needed. The MCP pages describe `capability_search` and `mcp_select_tool` as the way to load tools and don't state that direct calls fail.

title: Add fx completion for bash, zsh, and fish
body:
`fx completion bash|zsh|fish` prints a shell completion script. Tab then completes commands, subcommands, flags, setting keys after `fx config get`, `set`, and `unset`, and fixed flag values such as `--permission-mode ask|auto|full-access`.

```sh
source <(fx completion bash)      # ~/.bashrc
source <(fx completion zsh)       # ~/.zshrc, after compinit
fx completion fish | source       # ~/.config/fish/config.fish
```

This adds a new top-level command, `completion`, which the maintainer approved.

## How it works

The scripts come from the same command specs that help and the flag parser read, plus the settings list, so a new flag or setting shows up in completion without other edits. Two small additions to the specs make that possible:

- `TopLevelSpec.subcommands` lists the words that may follow a command, such as `config set` or `login codex`, and can nest (`mcp trust approve`). Help prints them under a new "Commands:" section. `config`, `workspace`, and `session` used to list them under "Options:", and `mcp` as free text. A `<key>` right after a word, as in `get <key>`, tells completion to offer setting keys.
- `OptionDoc.values` lists a flag's fixed values, for flags whose placeholder doesn't already name them. `--period <today|7d|month>` needs no list. `--permission-mode <mode>` and `--provider <name>` get one.

`src/core/cli/completion.zig` builds one model from those lists, then writes it as bash, zsh, or fish. All three scripts walk the command line the same way and never run fx, so Tab is instant and doesn't depend on the network or the session store. The bash script works with bash 3.2, the default on macOS. zsh shows descriptions through `_describe`, and fish through `complete`. Arguments that fx can't complete from fixed data, such as paths, fall back to the shell's file completion.

## Help changes

- `fx config`, `fx workspace`, and `fx session` list their subcommands under "Commands:" instead of "Options:".
- `fx mcp --help` lists its subcommands with a description each, and `fx login --help` and `fx logout --help` list the providers.

The cases cover words, nested words, flags after a skipped flag value, setting keys, and fixed values. The usage errors and `fx completion --help` are covered too.

title: Name status_line.context in fx config help
body:
`fx config --help` still used the old `statusLine.context` name in two examples, from before settings moved to snake_case. Both now say `status_line.context`.

A unit test reads that help and fails when a setting key it names is an old name or does not exist, so the next rename cannot leave the help behind. It fails on the old text and passes on the new.

title: Name the unknown connection in fx provider errors
body:
`fx provider` with a name that is neither built in nor a configured connection printed the raw error name:

```
$ fx provider nonesuch
fx: UnknownConfiguredProvider
```

It now names the provider and where connections are defined, in the same form as the other `fx provider` errors:

```
$ fx provider nonesuch
fx provider: unknown provider nonesuch; expected gateway, codex, grok, or a name under "providers" in ~/.fx/settings.json
```

The exit code stays 1 and settings are not touched. A new test in `configured-providers.test.ts` checks the message, the exit code, the unchanged settings file, and that no request is sent.

title: Add fx config schema for settings.json and .fx.json
body:
`fx config schema` prints a JSON Schema for `~/.fx/settings.json`, and `fx config schema --project` prints the one for a project `.fx.json`. Editors that read JSON Schema, such as VS Code, can then complete keys, show what each one does, and flag mistakes before fx reads the file.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://fx.sh/schemas/settings.json",
  "fast_mode": true
}
```

The companion fx-web change serves both schemas at `https://fx.sh/schemas/settings.json` and `https://fx.sh/schemas/fx.json`.

## What the schema checks

It is built from the settings list, `src/core/config/settings_keys.zig`, which now gives every key its kind, a one-line description, and its allowed values or bounds:

- Plain settings get exact types: switches are booleans, `auto_compact_percent` is an integer from 10 to 80, `permission_mode` is one of `ask`, `auto`, `full-access`, or `yolo`, and `provider_order` holds at most 8 strings.
- Object settings with fixed children, such as `status_line` and `sound`, list their switches and reject unknown children.
- `providers`, `permission`, and `context_limits` are described only as objects. Their own parsers check their contents, so the schema never flags a file fx accepts.
- Unknown keys are flagged, the same ones `fx doctor` reports. Renamed and older keys, such as `statusLine` and `model`, stay valid and are marked deprecated. `skill_match_fuzzy`, which fx refuses to load, is always flagged.
- `workspaces` entries use their own definition: they accept `additional_directories` and the project MCP approvals, and reject `providers`. The top level does the opposite.
- `.fx.json` accepts only the project-safe keys.

fx's parser ignores case and some aliases, so a value such as `"Auto"` loads but is flagged. The schema lists the spellings fx writes and documents.

## `$schema` is now a known key

A file that names its schema used to make `fx doctor` warn `unknown setting $schema`. `$schema` is now in the settings list under a new placement, `.editor`: fx knows it in both files and never reads it. `fx config list` doesn't show it, and completion doesn't offer it.

Completion also stops offering the older `model`, `codex_model`, and `grok_model` keys, which fx folds into `models` and doesn't write back.

## Keeping the list honest

Unit tests tie the list to the code that reads the files:

- For every key, the settings parser rejects a value of the wrong kind, accepts one of the listed kind, accepts every listed value, accepts each bound, and rejects one past it. A profile key in `.fx.json` is ignored rather than rejected. Changing a key's kind, a bound, or its placement in the list fails this test.
- Every value the permission mode, update channel, tool choice, and credential source parsers accept is listed.
- `fx config set` writes each key with the type the list gives it.
- The schema writer includes each key exactly where fx reads it, and the list itself has a description for every key and child.

## Tests

- Unit: the tests above, plus `fx config schema` argument parsing. `zig build test` fails only the 12 `command_runner` tests that fail on this machine on `main`.
- E2E in `cli.test.ts`: both schemas, a misplaced `--project`, and `$schema` in both files without a `fx doctor` warning. The completion cases now include `fx config schema --project`.
- The generated schemas compile under Ajv 8 in strict draft 2020-12 mode. A realistic `settings.json` and `.fx.json` validate, and typos, wrong types, bad enum values, out-of-range numbers, misplaced keys, and too many `provider_order` entries are rejected.

## Docs

vercel-labs/fx-web#186 serves both schemas at their `$id` URLs and documents `$schema` on the configuration and CLI pages.

title: Check that ACP and libfx run options keep their CLI and settings names
body:
The same run options appear on five surfaces under different names: the agent-run flag, the setting, its `FX_*` variable, the ACP config option, and the libfx model option. For example, Fast mode is `--fast`, `fast_mode`, `FX_FAST`, ACP `fast`, and libfx `model.fast`, and the permission mode is ACP's `mode`. Nothing tied them together, so a new ACP option or libfx field could appear with no CLI flag or setting behind it.

`scripts/cli_shape_registry.json` gains a `run_options` table with one row per option, naming it on every surface. The CLI shape check, which already runs in `Build & Test`, now fails when:

- `src/acp/sessions.zig` offers a config option that no row names, or a row names one it doesn't offer.
- `FxModelOptions` in `sdk/types/libfx.d.cts` declares a field that no row names, or a row names one it doesn't declare.
- A row names a flag that `src/builtins/commands.zig` doesn't list, a setting missing from the settings list, a variable that isn't a setting override, or a top-level libfx option the declarations don't have.

Names may still differ by surface, as ACP's `mode` does. The table only makes each name written down. The fx-cli-shape skill now says to add the row in the same change as the option.

ACP's permission modes are not tied to `permission_mode` values, because the mode registry allows custom mode IDs.

## Tests

- `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_check_cli_shape` covers four new cases: an ACP option with no row, a libfx model field with no row, a row naming a missing flag, and a row whose variable isn't a setting override. Two existing tests now avoid double reports when another check already flags the same entry.
- On the real tree the check passes. Removing the `ultrafast` row reports both `src/acp/sessions.zig:2493` and the libfx field.

title: Expose semantic execution hooks to libfx hosts
body:
## Summary

Add optional execution hooks to libfx and `fx acp`. The JavaScript host controls tracing and export.

- Report model calls, tools, approvals, child tasks, and saved results.
- Keep session and turn IDs stable when work resumes.
- Keep content capture and remote MCP correlation off by default. When enabled, MCP correlation sends an opaque UUID in `libfx/correlationId` metadata.
- Do not change permissions, results, or errors.

## Validation

- Native and Wasm builds and focused tests passed.
- The built `fx acp` sent hooks, then disabled them after reload. Exit code: 0. No stderr output.
- Hooks-enabled steering passed: 10 walks and 92 steps.
- Browser checks passed for approvals, MCP, child tasks, parent IDs, and credential exclusion in `sdk/index.html`.
- All 17 model-driver runs passed, including hooks on and off.
- CI is pending for `8410860d`. Keep this PR in draft.

## Docs

Update the API, tools, MCP, and ACP manual pages.

<details>
<summary>Required manual page changes</summary>

Exact per-page manual changes to apply with this release:

### `/docs/lib/api`

Source: `apps/marketing/app/(site)/(docs)/docs/lib/api/page.mdx`.

Add `hooks?: FxHooks` to `AgentOptions`; engine options inherit it. Add this row
to the agent options table:

| Option | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hooks` | Receives versioned semantic execution events, independently of diagnostics and turn output. The host owns tracing conventions, redaction, buffering, and export. | None |

Insert this section before `DiagnosticEvent`:

#### Semantic execution hooks

Pass `hooks` to `createFxAgent()` or `createFxEngine()`:

```ts
interface FxHooks {
  captureContent?: boolean
  onEvent(event: FxHookEvent): void | Promise<void>
  onError?(error: unknown): void | Promise<void>
  parent?: { rootSessionId: string; sessionId: string; turnId: string; callId: string }
}
```

Events report turns, steps, model calls, tools, permission evaluation, actual
approval/question/MCP input waits, MCP operations, delegation, and journal
acceptance. They carry session and logical turn IDs plus an execution ID for
each prompt or resume. Model and request ordinals are execution-local. Child
events identify their root/parent sessions and durable work where available.
These are execution identities, not trace or span IDs.

`tool.end` means execution returned; `tool.result` means conversation acceptance.
`journal.commit` follows a successful append and validated cursor; its sequence
bounds are `number | null` when unavailable. A yielded, paused, or handed-off
execution doesn't mean the logical turn failed. Auxiliary title-model calls may
report events after `turn.end` with the same turn/execution IDs.

Content capture defaults to off. With `captureContent: true`, each event shares
a 64 KiB text budget. Model requests retain the last 128 messages and allocate
content to the newest messages first, then instructions, tool descriptions, and
schemas. `contentTruncated` marks omissions. Tool `inputSchemaJson` is complete
JSON or null, up to 8 KiB; other JSON text fields can be prefixes after truncation.
Headers, credentials, raw image bytes, and opaque provider state aren't protocol
fields. Application text can still be sensitive; redact before export.

Callbacks run in delivery order, but their promises aren't awaited. Callback
throws/rejections go to `onError` without failing or retrying agent effects.
The host must flush its own exporter. Delivery is best effort, not an exactly-once
outbox. The package declarations define the complete `FxHookEvent` union.

Add `observation?: FxToolObservation` to `ToolContext`. Its `wait(request, effect)`
reports host-owned input work while preserving the effect's response/error.
`childHooks()` supplies the parent relationship for a host-created child engine.
Always execute the host effect when observation is absent too; instrumentation
doesn't decide permissions.

### `/docs/lib/tools`

Source: `apps/marketing/app/(site)/(docs)/docs/lib/tools/page.mdx`.

Append this section:

#### Observe host-owned waits and child engines

When hooks are installed, a tool receives `context.observation`. Use
`observation.wait(request, effect)` to report an approval or question your host
implements. The request kind is `approval`, `question`, `mcp_form`, or `mcp_url`.
The effect returns `{ outcome, answers?, value? }`; outcomes are `accepted`,
`denied`, `cancelled`, `failed`, or `timed_out`. The observer doesn't replace the
effect's value/error or make an authorization decision.

Always call the effect without the wrapper when `context.observation` is absent.
Disabling instrumentation must not bypass an approval or skip a question.
JavaScript host-tool callbacks apply only to the engine's root session; native
descendant metadata doesn't authorize a cross-session host-tool request.

For a child engine created inside a tool, pass
`hooks: context.observation.childHooks()` when observation is present. The child
retains the caller's session/turn/tool relationship. Native descendants retain
their own immediate parents rather than inheriting the outer tool as their
parent. Close a child engine when its work is finished.

### `/docs/lib/mcp`

Source: `apps/marketing/app/(site)/(docs)/docs/lib/mcp/page.mdx`.

Append this section, and add the same options to `McpOptions` and its table in
the API reference:

#### MCP instrumentation

With engine hooks installed, adapter calls report the configured server, original
remote tool name, owning fx call, and terminal outcome. Set `serverName` on
`createMcpAdapter()` for a stable local identity; otherwise it uses the client's
reported server name when available.

Hooks don't change the remote request by default. To propagate correlation,
explicitly pass `{ propagateCorrelation: true }`. The adapter sends an opaque
UUID as `_meta["libfx/correlationId"]` and reports it in `mcp.request` with
`requestIdKind: "correlation"`. The token contains no internal execution or tool
IDs. It isn't a `progressToken` and doesn't request progress notifications.
Without this option, calls still emit `mcp.start` and `mcp.end`, but no synthetic
remote request identity. Native JSON-RPC IDs and MCP-v2 handles are distinguished
by `requestIdKind: "jsonrpc"` and `"engine"`.

| Option | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `serverName` | Local server identity for hook events. | Client's reported name, or null |
| `propagateCorrelation` | Send an opaque UUID in `libfx/correlationId` metadata. | `false` |

### `/docs/using-fx/acp`

Source: `apps/marketing/app/(site)/(docs)/docs/using-fx/acp/page.mdx`.

Insert this section after `Session updates`:

#### Semantic execution observation

An ACP host can request semantic events on `session/new`, `session/load`, or
`session/resume` through `_meta.fx.hooks`:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "method": "session/new",
  "params": {
    "mcpServers": [],
    "_meta": { "fx": { "hooks": { "captureContent": false } } }
  }
}
```

A successful response confirms `result._meta.fx.hooksVersion: 1`. Subsequent
`libfx/hook` notifications carry versioned execution facts independently of
ordinary `session/update` output. The host owns span conventions and export.

Hook configuration is connection/session runtime state, not saved tracing state.
Every new/load/resume request replaces it; omitting hooks disables them,
including when reloading the already active session. Content capture is opt-in
and bounded. Observation doesn't change ACP permissions or effect decisions.

Clients should wait for a prompt response before new/load/resume. Parent hook settings are captured at prompt start; native children use the active setting when they start, so reconfiguration during ongoing work is not atomic across the whole tree.

</details>

title: Rank @ file suggestions by their best match
body:
## Summary

- `@` suggestions rank a file whose name starts with the query, or contains it as a whole word, above files where the letters are scattered across word breaks. `@stat` now lists `STATUS.md` before `spikes/noisy/clusters-a.toml`.
- A query that spells a file name up to its extension is an exact match, so `@file_index` lists `src/core/workspace/file_index.zig` before `benchmarks/file_index_bench.zig`.
- A query can start in the folder that holds a file and finish in its name, so `@vercle` finds `vercel-json/clean-urls.mdx`. A match inside the name wins a close call, and a match that ends in a folder or starts above the file's own folder ranks below every name match.
- Highlighted letters show the match that set the rank, including letters in the folder.
- Completing a name after a `/` ranks and highlights the entries in that folder with the same scoring.
- One- and two-letter searches over 100,000 files take about 1 ms longer; longer queries are as fast as before or faster.

## Why

The scorer took the first occurrence of each query letter and compared matches one field at a time, with word-break hits ahead of prefix and contiguity. Letters scattered across `-` and `.` collected more word-break hits than a whole-word prefix, so `@stat` put `clusters-a.toml` and three `conn-storm-*-activity.csv` files above `STATUS.md`. Each path is now scored by its best placement under fzf's path scoring scheme, and search skips placements that can no longer reach the 64 kept results without changing which results are kept.

## Verification

- `zig fmt --check src/` and the `file_index.zig` and `path_completion.zig` tests, which compare the alignment search with a brute-force search on more than 600,000 small cases and check that skipped searches leave the results unchanged.
- `tests/e2e/tui-file-picker.test.ts`: 22 pass.
- `./zig-out/bin/fx` in a 43,000-file repository: `@stat` and `@vercle` list the expected files and highlights, and the process exits cleanly.
- On generated queries over the same 43,000 paths, the mean reciprocal rank of the intended file rose from 0.054 to 0.224.

title: Save tool and steer images once by name
body:
## Summary

- In a durable session, a host tool's images are saved once in the session's image store, like prompt images, and the session's records, progress and checkpoints name them instead of holding their bytes.
- Tool images count in the session's image window together with prompt images. An older one leaves the conversation, and the model sees a note in its place.
- A tool image the store refuses stays in the result, held inline. The tool has already run, so the image is never lost. It still counts in the window like any image, and when it leaves it keeps the name of its bytes, so a session never holds more images than its window.
- A call's result is recorded as soon as the call finishes, so a turn reopened after a crash answers the call with its result instead of saying it may have partly run. That record now holds the result's images too, by name when the store holds them, and an open stages them with the rest of the open turn. Before, a turn reopened there got the result's text alone.
- A durable steer saves its images before it is sent, and its log entry names them. A steer whose image can't be saved throws the store's error.
- An open whose open turn holds many tool images may stage every image it reports missing.
- `zig build test` now runs the Zig tests in `journal.zig` and `libfx_journal.zig`. `main.zig` never listed those files, so their tests didn't run.

## Tests

- `test-journal.mjs`, both ways between native and wasm: a turn that crashed right after its screenshot's result reopens with the screenshot without running the tool again, and a screenshot the store refused leaves the window first, before and after a reopen. Each fails without its fix.
- Zig tests: a recorded tool result keeps its images and names the stored one; the window counts an inline tool image and names it when it drops it; an open stages a recorded result's images. Each fails without its fix.
- `ImageStore.tla` counts a refused tool image in the window and checks `WindowBound`, at most `Window` images between turns. `ImageStore-InlineUncounted.cfg` shows a window that skips it breaks that, and `drive-images.mjs` walks the new graph on both backends.
