title: Linux paste clipboard image
Slack MCP: a rejected token refresh shows as InvalidOAuthResponse instead of needs_auth
body:
## What happens

After the Slack login stops refreshing, every Slack call fails and `fx mcp list --connect` shows:

```
slack source=profile scope=profile policy=optional transport=http state=failed auth=authenticated status=failed
```

With `FX_TRACE=1 FX_TRACE_SCOPES=mcp FX_TRACE_STDERR=1`, the only trace line is:

```
[mcp] connection failed for server slack: InvalidOAuthResponse
```

fx doesn't mark the server `needs_auth`, so it never asks me to sign in again. Each time, I run `fx mcp auth slack` and then `/mcp reload` in every open session. This has happened on three days in a row with the Slack preset (`fx mcp add slack`).

## Cause

Slack's token endpoint (`https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.user.access`) reports errors with HTTP 200 and `"ok": false`, not with an RFC 6749 400 response:

```
$ curl -sS -D - -X POST https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.user.access \
    -d 'grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=xoxe-1-bogus&client_id=12364000946.12017137861236'
HTTP/2 200
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"ok":false,"error":"invalid_refresh_token"}
```

`refreshCredentialsCore` looks for `invalid_grant` only when the status is 400 ([mcp_auth.zig#L942-L948](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/5a3a5f39bf53abdd6744e7f2e8c4390e469c653a/src/core/mcp/mcp_auth.zig#L942-L948)). A 200 goes straight to `dupeRequiredSecret(alloc, object, "access_token")`, which returns `error.InvalidOAuthResponse` because the body has no `access_token` ([L956](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/5a3a5f39bf53abdd6744e7f2e8c4390e469c653a/src/core/mcp/mcp_auth.zig#L956)).

The rejection never becomes `McpRefreshRejected`. The `Refused` path that `tests/tla/mcp_host/SharedLogins.tla` models (drop the tokens, need a login, pick up a newer saved login) doesn't run.

## Suggested fix

When the token endpoint returns 200 with `"ok": false`, map `"error": "invalid_refresh_token"` to `McpRefreshRejected` and other errors to `McpRefreshUnavailable`. The same check probably belongs in the authorization-code exchange.

## Open question

I don't know why the refresh token goes bad each day. I usually have several fx sessions open with Slack connected. If two processes refresh with the same rotating refresh token, Slack would reject the second one. I haven't confirmed this.

fx 0.0.13 on macOS with the Keychain store. Code links are at 5a3a5f39bf53.

title: MCP re-auth fails with InvalidOAuthScope when the saved scope is comma-separated (Slack)
body:
## What happens

When a Slack entry uses its own Slack app (`oauth.client_id` set to an app other than fx's), signing in again while a saved login exists fails before the browser opens:

```
fx mcp auth failed: InvalidOAuthScope.
```

Running `fx mcp logout slack` before `fx mcp auth slack` works, because no saved scope is left. Reproduced on fx 0.0.13 with a saved Slack login.

## Cause

Slack's `oauth.v2.user.access` returns `scope` as a comma-separated list, for example `"scope": "channels:history,chat:write,im:history"`. fx saves it as is.

On the next sign-in, `requestedScope` always merges the saved scope first ([mcp_auth.zig#L692](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/5a3a5f39bf53abdd6744e7f2e8c4390e469c653a/src/core/mcp/mcp_auth.zig#L692)). `appendScopeTokens` splits only on whitespace ([L2515](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/5a3a5f39bf53abdd6744e7f2e8c4390e469c653a/src/core/mcp/mcp_auth.zig#L2515)), so the whole list becomes one token. With a long scope list, that token is over `max_scope_token_bytes` (256), and `appendUnique` returns `error.InvalidOAuthScope` ([L2525](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/5a3a5f39bf53abdd6744e7f2e8c4390e469c653a/src/core/mcp/mcp_auth.zig#L2525)). With a short list, fx would send Slack a scope like `a,b` that Slack doesn't recognize.

The Slack preset doesn't hit this because the fx.sh bridge sends a fixed scope.

## Suggested fix

Split saved scopes on commas as well as whitespace, or convert the token response's `scope` to space-separated before saving it.

title: Speed up short @ file searches and show more file rows
body:
## Summary

- One- and two-letter `@` file searches return 3 to 5 times faster, and so do searches with many exact matches, such as `@readme`. Results are unchanged.
- The `@` file picker shows up to 10 rows, up from 6, while at least five conversation rows stay visible. Short terminals keep the old height, and other pickers still show 6 rows.
- Moving through the file list scrolls the rows on screen, including when a status line takes the picker's first row. On a short terminal, moving back up leaves the list in place until the selection passes its top row, as before.

## Why

After #1301, one-letter searches were the only ones still slower than before it. Most of their time went to scoring paths that could never enter the 64 kept results. Once the worst kept result has the best score a non-exact match can reach, only an exact match or a shorter path can still beat it, so ranking now skips longer non-exact paths without scoring them. Once all 64 kept results are exact, it skips every non-exact path. The exact-match rule is now one `exactFit` helper shared by the ASCII and non-ASCII scorers, instead of two copies.

The file a user wants is often just below the sixth row. In 1,664 generated searches it ranked 7th to 10th in 9% of them, and the old list hid it.

The picker's height now depends on the terminal, so keyboard navigation can no longer assume a fixed row count. Each committed frame's receipt records how many file rows it painted, and navigation scrolls within that count.

## Numbers

Search time, median of 100 runs over 100,000 paths:

| Query | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `s` | 3.37 ms | 0.73 ms |
| `e` | 3.42 ms | 1.04 ms |
| `st` | 6.08 ms | 1.83 ms |
| `sta` | 5.77 ms | 2.90 ms |
| `stat` | 6.76 ms | 3.86 ms |
| `test` | 7.31 ms | 4.60 ms |
| `index` | 3.02 ms | 1.47 ms |
| `readme` | 5.36 ms | 1.07 ms |
| `button` | 5.41 ms | 5.45 ms |
| `usestate` | 7.88 ms | 7.91 ms |
| `component` | 6.49 ms | 6.49 ms |

Ranking is identical on all 1,664 generated searches over this repo's paths and a 43,000-file monorepo.

File picker:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Rows shown, 40-row terminal | 6 | 10 |
| Rows shown, 16-row terminal | 6 | 6 |
| Intended file on screen, 1,664 generated searches | 53% | 62% |
| Intended file on screen, 340 searches typed into the running app | 33% (112) | 39% (134) |

Peak memory is unchanged, at 76 MB in the 43,000-file repo.

## Verification

- `zig fmt --check src/`
- Inline tests for `file_index`, `path_completion`, `list_window` and `file_completion_state`: 446 pass, 1 skipped. New tests cover crowded short queries, a top 64 that is all exact, picker height by terminal size, and navigation within the painted rows.
- Two planted defects in the new skip, `>=` in place of `>` and dropping the exact-match exception, each fail the new tests.
- A separate checker compared the skipping ranking with scoring every path on 1,500 seeded cases, 163 of them crowded, and found no differences.
- `tests/e2e/tui-file-picker.test.ts`: 23 pass, 1 skipped. The new test checks 10 rows at 40 terminal rows, then 6 rows and the scroll window at 16. It fails when navigation scrolls a fixed 10 rows.
- `./zig-out/bin/fx` in tmux: `@s` shows 6 rows at 16 terminal rows and 10 rows at 40. At 16 rows, seven Downs and one Up leave the same rows on screen as `main`. `@stat` lists the same files as `main`. Exit code 0, empty stderr.

title: Keep a durable session cancel from stopping the prompt it starts
body:
## Summary

- On a queue that outlives the process, such as Vercel's, a session cancel that arrives while a prompt waits to start no longer cancels that prompt when its delivery starts it. The prompt runs, as it does when the sender stores the cancel first.
- On the same queues, a steer that arrives while several prompts wait no longer cuts short the first prompt its delivery starts. As when the sender stores the steer first, a text steer joins the latest waiting prompt, and a steer with images ends that prompt and runs as its own turn.

title: Send restored steering in the envelope the model saw
body:
## Summary

- A steer that joined a running turn reaches the model as a live update, wrapped in `<user_steering>`. A saved turn keeps only the steer's text, so after a resume, and in every later turn, the model saw the same steer as a plain user message.
- Requests now put each restored steer back in its envelope. A parent agent's steering keeps its sender label in the saved text, which selects the parent envelope, so the model gets back the exact text it saw when the turn took the steer.
- The notice a libfx session adds when it resumes an interrupted turn rides in the same steering list. fx wrote it, so it stays plain text rather than reaching the model as the user's live update.
- Saved sessions and compaction are unchanged: the envelope is added only to the request.

## Tests

- A unit test in `execution_memory.zig` saves a user steer and a parent steer, restores them, and checks that the request gets the exact original text back, and that the resume notice stays plain.
- The gateway flow test of steering during a response now checks that the next turn's request carries the steer inside `<user_steering>`. It fails without the fix.
- The `sessions-v2.test.ts` E2E test resumes a steered session with `-c` and now checks the same on the built binary. It fails without the fix.

title: Stop reporting no-match exits as failed commands
body:
## Summary

- Report a `grep`, `rg`, `egrep`, `fgrep`, or `ag` that finds no matches as an ordinary result instead of a failed command, both to the model and in the transcript.
- Report `diff` and `cmp` finding differences, and `test` or `[` evaluating false, the same way.
- Keep `exit_code` 1 in the shell result and add `exit_meaning`, such as `"no matches found"`.
- Treat `cd <dir> && grep ...` the same as `grep ...`, while a `cd` that fails still counts as a failure.
- Keep reporting the exit as a failure for TTY sessions, commands that write to stderr, and other command chains.

title: Keep tenants apart when libfx agents share a process
body:
## Summary

- A queue delivery runs only an input its session already stored. A delivery the session's log doesn't hold, such as one posted straight to the queue route, runs nothing, writes nothing, and emits `session.refused`.
- Every durability, including `vercel()`, stores a prompt, steer, cancel or resume with its caller's context and settings before queueing it. The queued message carries only the input's id, session, agent name and store.
- A steer that reuses a prompt's id is rejected with `FX_MESSAGE_ID_IN_USE` on every durability. On `vercel()` the worker used to drop it with a `session.error`.
- Creating an agent under a name another agent already has on the same store, with different options, throws `FX_AGENT_NAME_IN_USE`. Agents created with the same options still share that name's sessions.
- `wakeHandler()` delivers each message to the agent of its name on the store the message names, and answers `FX_NO_AGENT` when the process has none. It no longer hands the message to an agent of that name on another store.
- `world()` takes a `store` option naming the store its sessions live in, defaulting to its name. `local()` treats each folder as its own store.
- A prompt or steer whose input, context and settings come to more than 8 MiB of JSON is rejected with `FX_INPUT_TOO_LARGE` before anything is stored.
- The Node native addon reads the environment from libc on every lookup, so an app that adds environment variables after the first engine starts no longer crashes the process on macOS.
- Prompts queued by an earlier libfx and still undelivered when this version deploys are refused instead of run.

## Docs

The fx.sh pages change in vercel-labs/fx-web#194.

title: Run the agent's git inspection commands through safe git in auto mode
body:
## Summary

- In `auto` mode, a git command the agent runs now goes through safe git: fx runs the trusted git with the programs a repository's own config can name turned off, in the default `user` shell profile as well as `clean`. Before this, `git status` with any flags and `git fetch` were routine auto commands that ran plain git without a review, and the `user` profile never reached safe git at all.
- Every agent shell command and terminal session, in every permission mode, runs git with the programs a repository's own config names for reading turned off, however the command is written. That covers `cd sub && git status`, `git -C sub status`, a chain such as `git status && git diff`, an absolute git path, `git blame`, and terminal sessions.
- fsmonitor, the pager, and signature display are off for every repository. The repository's filter drivers are blanked, its textconv drivers show the file's own content, and git reports that it cannot run its external diff programs or signature verifiers. A log format the repository sets gives way to the default, and a promisor remote whose config names a transport program cannot lazy fetch. Hooks stay on.
- An inspection shape safe git cannot run directly, such as `git diff HEAD`, `git log -p`, or `git status --porcelain=v3`, goes to review and then runs with those programs turned off. On git older than 2.31, which ignores that environment, it is returned to the agent without running.
- `git fetch` is always refused in `auto` mode. A repository's config can name `remote.<name>.uploadpack`, `core.sshCommand`, `core.gitProxy` and `credential.helper`, `-c` cannot turn those off without also turning off the user's own ssh and credential configuration, and git keeps a repository's `uploadpack` over any override.
- A promisor remote, which is how a partial clone fetches a missing object on demand, can no longer start that remote's transport program: fx passes `--no-lazy-fetch` and sets `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, and refuses a repository whose config marks a remote as a promisor when git is older than 2.45 and cannot be told to stop.
- `git log` and `git show` run through safe git name the default format, so a repository's `format.pretty` cannot make them run a signature verifier.
- `git show` joins the read-only commands fx runs through safe git, and `git status` accepts `--ignored`, `-uno` and `--porcelain=v2`.
- No git command is a routine auto command any more. Routine non-git commands such as `npm test` and `zig build` are unchanged.
- A user-profile alias or function that redefines `git` keeps the review path, as every other redefined routine name does.
- `ask` mode still asks a person to approve the exact command, and an approved git command runs with the same programs turned off.
- Mutating git (`commit`, `push`, `checkout`, `pull`) still runs with the repository's hooks after review or approval.

Linear: [FXC-283](https://linear.app/vercel/issue/FXC-283)

## Docs

- `docs/configure-fx/permissions`, Auto mode, "Runs directly": replace the bullet "Run recognized project commands, including `git status`, local dependency installs, tests, builds, and development servers" with "Run recognized project commands, including local dependency installs, tests, builds, and development servers", and add "Run read-only git commands such as `git status`, `git diff`, `git log` and `git show` with every program a repository's own git config can name turned off, and with lazy fetching from a promisor remote disabled. Other git inspection commands go to review, then run with the same programs turned off. `git fetch` is returned to the agent without running."
- `docs/configure-fx/permissions`, all modes: add "Every git command the agent runs, in any permission mode, runs with the fsmonitor, pager, filter drivers, textconv, external diff programs and signature verifiers a repository's own git config names turned off. The repository's hooks still run."

title: Retry a resumed turn's size rejection with fewer images
body:
## Summary

- When fx resumes a turn whose saved reply has to restart, such as after the write that commits the turn failed, it moves that reply aside and sends the request again. The size retry counted the moved-aside reply as output when deciding whether sending again was safe. So when a provider refused the restarted request for its size, the turn ended instead of leaving the oldest images out.
- A provider refuses a request for its size before any output, so the retry now checks only whether the current attempt has shown text or started a tool call. Other retries keep their existing checks.

## Tests

- A gateway flow test saves a checkpoint that holds an image and part of a reply, then resumes it against a 413 followed by a success. It checks that the resumed turn sends the request again without the image and finishes. It fails without the change, which sends one request.
- `vision-route-fake-gateway.test.ts` passes.
- A libfx session whose turn-commit write fails, resumed by a new engine against a provider that refuses large requests, now leaves out images and finishes. Before the change it stopped after one refused request.

title: Keep CLI-only code out of the libfx builds
body:
## Summary

- `libfx.node` and `fx-core.wasm` no longer contain the ACP E2E test controls, which wrote marker files and waited on a release file when their `FX_E2E_ACP_PROMPT_*` variables were set. The fx binary keeps them for its E2E tests.
- The libfx builds no longer compile `src/main.zig`. The terminal UI reads the version from the build options, which `build.zig` takes from the same `pub const version` in `src/main.zig`, so a change to the CLI's composition root can no longer break a libfx build.

title: Report herdr working after a prompt closes mid-turn
Copy libfx session context when a session opens
body:
## Summary

- A libfx session keeps a copy of its `context` and session settings, taken when `agent.session()` is called. Changing the object afterward no longer changes what later prompts and steers store or what their tool calls receive.
- The 8 MiB input limit now covers the context a prompt or steer actually stores, so an app can no longer get a larger input stored by growing the context object after opening the session.
- Remote durable tests stop before running when the Vercel access token or project settings are missing, instead of reporting every test as failed.
- The steering tests check how much of the reply the model sent rather than wall-clock time, so they also pass against Vercel's World.

title: Fix MCP-v2 crashes, hangs, and lost sign-ins
body:
## Summary

- fx no longer aborts after about 30 calls to an HTTP server that leaves its response streams open.
- An HTTP server that never answers `initialize` no longer hangs `fx mcp show` and every turn. The start fails, and fx tries the server again later.
- Waking the MCP engine no longer starts a thread that never goes away.
- A stdio server that stops reading its input no longer freezes every MCP call.
- A sign-in no longer reads memory that was already freed.
- An access token with a line break or another control byte is refused instead of crashing fx at every launch.
- A line break in an environment variable used for a header holds that server back with a note naming the variable, instead of crashing fx.
- Only Slack's own MCP server signs in as fx's Slack app; a server that shares its client id signs in on its own.
- A form answer goes only to the question that was shown. An answer to a question that is gone is refused.
- The sign-in listener drops a browser connection that stays silent and serves the next one. Only a return carrying this sign-in's state ends the wait; anything else gets a 404.
- A sign-in answer that isn't for this sign-in says "the answer that came back wasn't for this sign-in".
- A remote server's metadata can no longer point fx's token, registration and revocation requests at internal addresses.
- `oauth.scopes` in the config is asked for when nothing else names scopes.
- A config change during a sign-in ends it with "Couldn't sign in to NAME: the MCP config changed before the browser came back; run /mcp login NAME again." instead of leaving "Signing in to NAME" up forever.
- `/mcp login NAME --no-browser` signs in to NAME instead of taking the flag as the server.
- A login saved for a `.mcp.json` server is kept for that repository only, and never attaches to your own servers or another repository's.
- A sign-in made in another fx window is picked up before fx says a server needs a login.
- A window whose refresh is refused no longer deletes the login another window just saved.
- fx windows refresh a login one at a time and use a newer login another window saved, so a server that rotates refresh tokens, such as Plain, no longer signs every window out.
- A refreshed login that can't be saved is reported, and fx saves it again.
- MCP-v2 no longer copies the old engine's logins, so the two engines never refresh one login apart.
- Slack signs in at Slack's own page with `http://localhost:3118/callback` instead of going through fx.sh, so Slack renews its logins without the Slack app's secret and they no longer end after 12 hours.
- A token refresh the server refuses with an error, including Slack's HTTP 200 with `ok:false`, ends the login and asks for a new sign-in instead of retrying the same refresh on every call.
- A refresh that fails for now while a server starts, such as a 503, shows the server as retrying and keeps its login, instead of leaving `fx mcp show` waiting forever.
- A tool call whose login couldn't be renewed tells the model the tool didn't run and to try again shortly, instead of that it may have run.
- When a server needs a login, the model tells the user to run `/mcp login NAME` in the shell, and `fx mcp login NAME` in a terminal from `fx ask` or an editor.
- `fx mcp login` and `/mcp login` name the port when a fixed callback port is already in use.
- `fx mcp` commands write a trace when `FX_TRACE` or `FX_TRACE_LOG` asks for one.
- fx never writes over a saved-sign-ins file it can't read, and sign-in and sign-out say what is wrong with it.
- A sign-out no longer comes back after another window saves.
- A config change no longer freezes the shell while the old servers stop.
- A config change while a server is in use no longer runs two copies of it.
- ACP `session.notices: false` turns context notices off.
- A 2025 stdio server's ping during `initialize` is answered.
- A server that never answers fx's `initialized` notification fails after 60 s with that reason, instead of looking ready with no tools.
- A call past the 32 open HTTP streams waits for one to free up, instead of being reported as lost.
- Progress messages no longer pile up idle timers.
- A large tool list is gathered in linear time.
- A server that sends faster than fx reads waits, so one server can no longer grow fx's memory to about 1 GB.
- A server that floods fx no longer holds back timeouts and other servers.
- A stdio server that ignores SIGTERM and closed stdin is stopped when fx exits.
- A server start that fails partway no longer closes its pipes twice.
- A discover result with an invalid `resultType` counts as a legacy answer, so fx falls back to `initialize`.
- Freeing always-loaded tools after a failed allocation frees what was allocated.
- `fx ask` prints a note for each server skipped because of its config.
- A capability search that names no server and finds no MCP tool says which servers it couldn't look in and why: one needs a login, another is unavailable.
- A server whose name has a control character, or another character a terminal can't show, is skipped with a note that shows the name escaped, so a repository's `.mcp.json` can't send escape sequences to the terminal.
- One `~/.fx/mcp.json` entry fx can't read is skipped with a note naming it, and the other servers still load.
- A text item over 1 MiB no longer fails a tool result. In a saved session the whole result, up to 8 MiB, is stored, and `read_tool_result` can read any part of it.
- A stdio server gets only `HOME`, `LOGNAME`, `PATH`, `SHELL`, `TERM` and `USER` from fx's environment, plus its config's `env`.
- `fx mcp add` and `fx mcp remove` refuse a linked `.mcp.json` or `~/.fx/mcp.json` and name what it points to.
- `fx mcp approve --all` approves the servers it lists, and a server added later still waits for approval.
- The status line mentions MCP only when a server needs attention.
- A server that fails starts again by itself once its backoff is over, up to its retry limit, and the count starts over once it has stayed up for 60 s.

title: Prepare v0.0.14 release
body:
## Summary

- Extend the approved 0.0.14 changelog with the newly merged CLI and libfx changes.
- Document the new tenant-isolation protections and libfx input and configuration requirements.
- Keep the version at 0.0.14; no publication or release-workflow changes.

title: Continue a dead local process's libfx turns when its agent next starts
body:
On `local()`, the queue lives in the process. When a process dies, it takes the turn it was running with it, and any prompt it stored but hadn't delivered yet. The session's log keeps that work, but nothing continues it until the session gets its next prompt or a `session.resume()`. Restarting a dev server in the middle of a turn leaves that turn open until someone sends another message.

With this change, an agent continues that work itself. The first time an agent is used in a process, such as by a request that reopens a session's stream, it looks through the newest sessions in its folder in the background. It continues each session of its name that a process on this machine, started in the same working directory, left with an open turn or a stored prompt when it died. `onEvent` gets a `session.recovered` event for each session, and `local({ recover: false })` turns recovery off.

## How it works

- **When:** recovery starts the first time an agent is used in a process, not when the agent is created, since an agent does no I/O until a session is used. It runs once per process for each agent name and durability, and `close()` stops it.
- **What it looks at:** the 1,000 most recently created sessions in the agent's own World, 200 per page, reading 8 logs at a time.
- **Which sessions it continues:** a session of the agent's name that has an open turn or a stored prompt, has no lease that still stands, and whose last writer has died. The last writer is the holder of the newest lease, or the sender of a newer input. On `local()`, that writer must also have run on this host in the same working directory.
- **How:** the agent queues the stored input whose message the dead process's queue lost: the newest input no turn took, or else the open turn's own input. That message carries only what every queued message carries (the input's type and id, the session, the agent name, and the store), on the agent's own queue. Its delivery goes through the agent's own worker like any other, so deadlines, cut-offs, fencing and leases apply, and a process that still runs keeps delivering its own work. Nothing a live process holds runs twice.
- **What changes in the log:** each input a sender stores now carries the sender's holder info as `from`, and `local()`'s holder info adds the working directory as `cwd`. Leases and checkpoints keep every field the holder info returned.
- **`world()`:** a new `recover(writer)` option makes recovery available to an app's own World. It needs `livenessKnown` and a World with `runs.list()`. An agent on a World without `runs.list()` emits `recovery.error` and runs its prompts as before. `vercel()` is unchanged, since its queue keeps messages across crashes.

`sdk/README.md`, the types, and the type fixtures describe the new option and events.

`session.resume()` also changes. A resume that starts while another live worker already runs the session's open turn now reads the stream from that worker's own `turn_start` or `turn_resume` line, even when that line came before the resume. Before, the resume waited for a line that had already passed and ended `idle` once the other worker finished. Without this fix, a client that reopens a session right after a restart could race the recovery and see `idle`.

## How this fits the tenant rules on `main`

This branch was rebased onto the change that keeps tenants apart when agents share a process. The recovery follows those rules rather than adding an exception to them:

- **A recovery is an ordinary queued message.** There is no `recover` message type. A recovery names an input the session's log already holds, so its delivery passes the same "runs only an input its session already stored" check as any other (`TenantIsolation.tla` `OnlySentRuns`). A delivery with an unknown type, such as the `recover` messages of an earlier draft of this change, is refused as malformed, and one naming an input the log doesn't hold is refused with `session.refused`. The turn runs with the context and settings its caller stored, never with anything from the delivery.
- **A recovery stays on its own store.** An agent lists only its own World's sessions and sends on its own queue with its own `store`, so delivery by name and store reaches the agent of that name on that folder. A test runs two agents named `default` with different options on two folders in one process and checks that each continues only its own folder's session.
- **The per-folder store does not replace the working-directory check.** On `main`, `local()` treats each folder as its own store, and one name on one store must be one configuration. That rule is enforced within a process. Every app on a machine that creates its agents without a durability keeps its sessions in the same folder under the temporary directory, which is one store key for all of them. Without the working-directory check, another project's agent named `default` would continue a killed turn with that project's tools and API key. The check stays, and `local()` documents why.

## Questions for reviewers

- **Working-directory scope.** A process counts as the same app when it ran on this host with the same `process.cwd()`. An app started from a different directory, or one that calls `process.chdir()` before it writes, won't recover the other's sessions. A process whose working directory was deleted writes `cwd: null` and is never recovered. Is the working directory the right boundary, or would you rather scope recovery to something the app names?
- **The 1,000-session cap.** Each agent reads at most 1,000 sessions, newest first, once per process. Older sessions with stranded work wait for their next prompt or `session.resume()`, as before. Is 1,000 the right bound for a dev machine, and should it be an option?
- **Sessions from before this change.** Their inputs have no `from` and their leases no `cwd`, so recovery never continues them. They behave as they did before this change. That seems safer than guessing, but it means the first upgrade doesn't finish a turn that was already stranded.
- **Process id reuse.** Liveness is `process.kill(pid, 0)` on the writer's pid, as for leases. A pid that another live process now uses counts as alive, so that session isn't recovered. A container that restarts with the same pid, and the same hostname, never recovers its sessions. That fails safe, but a per-process instance id in `holderInfo()` would fix it, at the cost of one more field in every lease and input.
- **Once per durability object, not per store.** Two `local({ dir })` calls on one folder each look through it once. Their duplicate recoveries are harmless, because the lease lets one worker run the session and the other finds it held, but keying on the store would avoid them. I kept the durability object so that two Worlds that misname one store still each get looked at.
- **Modeling the tenant interaction.** `AgentRouting.tla` models recovery, but `TenantIsolation.tla` does not. Since a recovery is a message naming a stored input on the agent's own store, the existing `OnlySentRuns`, `RunsOnSenderAgent`, `RunsInSenderStore` and `RunsWithSenderContext` properties cover it by construction, and the tests above check it in code. Should `TenantIsolation.tla` get an explicit `Recover` action anyway?
- **Durable queues.** `world()` accepts `recover` with `queueDurable: true`. Recovery isn't needed there, since the queue keeps the message, and is only extra deliveries. Should `world()` refuse that combination?

## Model

`AgentRouting.tla` gains `MaxCrashes` and `Recovery`. A crash drops a queued message while its input stays stored. An agent that starts queues a recovery, naming itself, for each of its sessions with stored work and no message on its way, and a later crash can lose that recovery too. `Recovered`, that every stored input eventually runs, holds under fairness along with `Drains`, `RunsOnOwner` still holds with crashes and recoveries, and `Witness-NoRecovery` shows that `Recovered` fails without recovery. With `MaxCrashes = 0`, the send graph is the same as on `main`, with 2,325 states. `drive-agents.mjs recover` walks the real code along the new graph, with each process in a worker thread, and CI runs it after the send walk.

## Tests and model checks

New tests in `sdk/tests/test-durable-core.mjs` on `local`: a dead process's open turn and its stored prompt continue on first use; only the agent's own sessions whose last writer died on this host and in this directory are continued; paging; a World without `runs.list()`; `recover: false`; a resume racing a recovery; the recovery's queued message; forged and unknown deliveries; and two stores in one process. On every backend, a resume while another worker runs the open turn. `sdk/tests/test-durable.mjs` on `local` and `world` kills a child process during an idempotent and a non-idempotent tool call, then checks that a new agent finishes the turn when it's first used, with the non-idempotent call reported to the model rather than run twice.

The native addon and Wasm surfaces came from `main`'s CI build, since this change touches no Zig. The Bun rows ran on Bun 1.4.2, the version CI uses, except the `drive.mjs` walks and the native `drive-steer.mjs` walks, which ran on Bun 1.3.4. Bun 1.3.4 has no JSPI, so its Wasm runs can't start an engine.

title: Give fx's commands, flags, and settings one consistent shape
body:
fx's commands, flags, and settings grew one feature at a time, so one idea often had several spellings, each command parsed flags its own way, and settings could only be changed by editing JSON. This brings the whole control surface to one shape, modeled on git and the Unix conventions. This PR replaces the stack #1229 to #1294 and #1292. It is four commits on current `main`: the first is the stack with the fixes from a review of it, the second and fourth have the fixes from a review of this PR, and the third brings two of `main`'s newest changes in line. The fixes are listed below. It lands as one PR so the control surface can be reviewed and merged as one design. Help, completion, and the CI shape check read the same option lists the parser does, and the renames touch the same command files, so separate PRs would each land against a surface that is only partly converted. ## How it fits together Before, each command checked its arguments with its own code, its help text was written separately, and settings changed only by editing `settings.json`: ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph cmd["Each command"] parse["Hand-written flag checks"] help["Help text, written separately"] end user["You"] -->|edit JSON by hand| file["~/.fx/settings.json"] file --> doctor["fx doctor"] ``` After, one set of option lists in `src/builtins/commands.zig` drives the parser, help, completion, and the shape check, and one settings list drives `fx config`, `fx doctor`, completion, and the schema. `fx config set` and `unset` write through the same settings store the session uses: ```mermaid flowchart LR options["Option lists
src/builtins/commands.zig"] --> parser["cli_flags.Parser"] parser --> commands["Every command"] options --> help["Help and usage"] options --> completion["fx completion"] options --> check["CI shape check"] keys["Settings list
settings_keys.zig"] --> config["fx config"] keys --> doctor["fx doctor"] keys --> completion keys --> schema["fx config schema"] keys --> check config -->|set, unset| store["settings_store"] --> file["$FX_HOME/settings.json"] ``` ## What changes for people and scripts **Flags and errors** - Every command reads its flags through one parser, from the same option lists its help prints. `--flag=value` works everywhere, and the last occurrence of a flag wins. - A wrong command line exits 2 and names the problem, with the closest match for a typo: `fx stauts` suggests `status`, `fx --modle` suggests `--model`. Work that fails after parsing still exits 1. - A launch flag given after a command says where it goes: `fx ask --add-dir x` reports `it goes before the command: fx --add-dir ask`. - `fx ""` starts a session with a first prompt. `-r` is short for `--resume`. `-p` and `--print` point to `fx ask`. - Resume is down to seven spellings. Each removed spelling exits 2 and names its replacement. - `fx pr`, `fx issue`, and `fx acp` take the same run flags as `fx ask`, including `--permission-mode` and `--provider`. - `/fast` takes `on` or `off`, and still toggles with no argument. **Settings** - `fx config list`, `get`, `set`, `unset`, and `schema`, in git's format. `--show-origin` says which file or `FX_*` variable each value comes from. - `fx ask --config key=value` overrides a setting for one request. - `fx doctor` reports unknown settings keys, with the closest real name. - `statusLine` becomes `status_line`, `notifications` becomes `sound`, and full access is saved as `full-access`. The old names keep working. - `/allowlist` and `fx mcp` call their scopes `global` and `workspace`. - `fx login vercel --api-key` replaces `fx setup`, which still runs, with a warning. **Conventions** - `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb` are honored. - `FX_HOME` moves `~/.fx`. - Test-only variables share the `FX_TEST_` prefix. - `fx mcp list --json` and `fx mcp show --json` report usage errors as JSON. - `fx completion bash|zsh|fish` prints a completion script. - `fx provider` and `fx ask --provider` name an unknown connection instead of printing the error name. **Checks and repository** - CI fails when code reads an unregistered `FX_*` variable, accepts a flag that help leaves out, parses a flag by hand, or names a flag, setting, test hook, ACP option, or libfx option against the conventions. - The `fx-cli-shape` skill describes the rules for adding commands, flags, and settings, and `AGENTS.md` points to it. - `AGENTS.md` lists command-line flags as the highest layer of config precedence, above environment variables. - PGSO training and qualification no longer set `NO_COLOR=1`. fx honors it now, so setting it would profile only the plain-text output path. ## Review fixes A review of the stack found these, and they are part of the first commit. - `fx config get` reports the value a run uses, defaults included, by reading settings through `resolveSettings`, the same function the session uses. `--show-origin` names the layer that sets that value, or `default`, and `get` prints the warnings `fx status` does. `fx config list` still shows what each file sets, as `git config --list` does. - `fx config set` and `unset` remove the workspace copy of the key they change, so the reported change takes effect. A large `FX_MAX_AGENT_STEPS` no longer crashes `fx config list`. - Launch flags work after `-c`, `--continue`, `-r`, `--resume`, and `fx session resume`, as in `fx -c --model x`, with the last flag winning. - `fx pr` and `fx issue` reject a flag they don't take instead of sending it as context. Context that starts with a dash follows `--`. - `fx mcp add` and `remove` take `--global`. A dash word where a server name goes is an unknown flag, with a suggestion. - The CLI shape check scans all of `src/`, in either argument order and through named constants. The remaining hand-written comparisons are listed by flag or by file, with the reason. - `fx sessions convert` reads its flag through the shared parser. - `fx ask --json` usage errors report `"exit_code": 2`, matching the process. - Bash completion loads with `eval "$(fx completion bash)"`, which works in macOS's bash 3.2. - An unknown provider exits 2 in `fx provider` and `fx ask --provider`, and names `$FX_HOME/settings.json` when `FX_HOME` is set. - The last flags compared by hand go through the shared parser: `fx mcp` and `/mcp`, which read the same option lists as their help and completion, and `fx slack`. The shape check's exemptions now list only code that reads other programs' flags. - Usage errors name the problem where they printed only usage: `fx mcp lsit` suggests `list`, and `fx credits --jsno`, `fx sessions --limit abc` (from the flag's `<1-100>` placeholder), `fx config set fast_mode` and `set fast_mode=true`, and `--json` errors name what's wrong. `fx config set max_agent_steps -5` reaches the value check. `fx config get --json` on a key with no value reports `ConfigKeyNotSet`. - Completion offers only what fx accepts: `--resume` offers `last`, not `id`; `config set` and `unset` offer only the keys they change; a subcommand offers its own flags, not its parent's. - `FX_PROVIDER_ORDER`, `FX_PROVIDER_STRICT`, and `FX_REVIEW_MODEL` beat `fx ask --config`, as the docs say. - `FX_HOME` works without `HOME`, fx creates its missing parent folders, and `FX_HOME` set to the home folder is refused. - The global flags live in one list: the launch-wide ones are `launch_wide_options`, the usage line is built from `launch_options`, and the help test checks both directions. - The libfx check reads `provider` from the provider config types rather than anywhere in the file, and the ACP check covers the IDs `session/set_config_option` accepts. - Old spellings warn that they stop working in fx 0.0.17, from one constant: `fx setup`, `/setup`, `fx mcp --profile`, and `/allowlist user` and `local`. `fx doctor` reports `statusLine`, `notifications`, and a saved `yolo`. The shape check fails once fx's version reaches 0.0.17. - Smaller fixes: - `fx resume --help` gives the removal hint. - `sandbox` is a retired key. - `fx doctor` no longer advises a removal that would lose settings. - Setter messages say "global". - CI messages point at the skill's rules. A review of this PR found these, and they are the second and fourth commits. - A message that quotes a word from the command line, the environment, or a settings file shows its control characters as visible escapes such as `\x1b`, so a pasted escape sequence can't move the cursor or rewrite the screen. This covers unknown flags and commands, flag values, `fx config` keys and values, `fx ask --config`, `fx mcp` verbs, `fx upgrade --channel`, the `-p` hint, and workspace paths read from `settings.json`. - `fx config` names the cause when it can't read or save `settings.json`, in place of an error name: a symlink or hard link, a file over 64 KiB, another fx saving at the same time, permissions, or a full or read-only disk. - `FX_HOME` that names a file, or a path through one, is refused at startup, as a relative path already is. - "Did you mean" suggestions for flags, commands, settings keys, and `fx mcp` verbs come from one rule, `cli_flags.Nearest`. Command names keep their stricter limit of one edit for words of four letters or fewer, so a prompt such as `fx add` isn't read as a typo. - Saving a renamed settings group logs each older value it drops because the new name also sets it. - `cli_flags.Parser` has a fuzz target, `cli_flags`, that parses fuzzed argument lists against `fx ask`'s options. It checks that parsing stops on its own, returns only documented options with values borrowed from the arguments, agrees with `firstFailure`, gives the same answer twice, and describes every failure and out-of-range value in terminal-safe text. - The Linux E2E job installs fish, so the fish completion test runs. Like the bash and zsh tests, it stubs file completion and compares only the words fx offers. - One function builds the run options `fx pr` and `fx issue` pass in both output modes, `agentRunOptions` takes an enum instead of a bool, and a leftover doc comment and a `--resume-id` in a test usage string are gone. ## Rebased on current `main` `main` removed the v1 session store with `--sessions-v2` and `FX_SESSIONS_V2`, the old MCP client with `FX_MCP_ENGINE`, `fx ask --continue-recovery`, and `fx session migrate`. This branch's changes to those are dropped, including the `experimental.sessions_v2` setting, which never shipped and has nothing left to turn on. `main`'s new code follows the conventions here: - Its test hooks use the `FX_TEST_` names, and `FX_SHELL_PARITY_ALL_SHELLS` is now `FX_TEST_SHELL_PARITY_ALL_SHELLS`. - Its tests that run the current binary resume with `--resume`, including the new TUI tests that used `--resume-last`. The session-conversion drivers keep `--resume-id` for the older releases they run. - ChatGPT and Grok sign-in, the v1 conversion check, `fx mcp`, and `fx usage` find the profile through `FX_HOME`. - `fx mcp list --json` and `show --json` usage errors are JSON in the MCP-v2 code, and `fx mcp` suggests the closest verb. - `fx update`, `main`'s new name for `fx upgrade`, reads its flags through the shared parser, and completion offers it. - The note fx prints after it tightens a shared `~/.fx` names `$FX_HOME` when `FX_HOME` is set. ## Release notes For the changelog of the release that ships this: - Usage errors exit 2 instead of 1, with a message that names the problem. - `statusLine` is now `status_line` and `notifications` is now `sound`. fx reads the old names until 0.0.17 and writes the new ones, so an older fx that opens a profile saved by this one doesn't see those settings. - `FLASH_SYNC_UPDATES` is gone; use `FX_SYNC_UPDATES`. - `fx resume`, `--resume-last`, `--resume-id`, and the other removed resume spellings fail with a hint to the new form. A bare `fx --resume` opens the session picker. - `fx ask --verbose`, which did nothing, is rejected. - `fx setup`, `/setup`, `fx mcp --profile`, and `/allowlist user` and `local` warn and stop working in fx 0.0.17. - The test hooks are renamed to `FX_TEST_*`, with no fallback; this affects only fx's own tests and tools. ## Testing - `zig build`, `zig fmt --check src/`, `python3 scripts/check_cli_shape.py` (also on the tree merged with current `main`), `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_check_cli_shape`, the public-surface, compactor, indexer, and recovery boundary scripts, the PGSO corpus check, and `ci-shards.test.ts` pass. - Unit tests: the full `zig build test` passes on the final tree. - E2E on the final binary, run one file at a time: `config-persistence` (33), `mcp-verbs` (21), `vision-route-fake-gateway` (53), `acp` (169), `sessions` (99), `gateway-stream-lifecycle` (227), `tmux-helpers` (11), `tui-auth-source-selection` (159), `tui-interrupt-recovery` (11), `tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle` (76), and `tui-resume` (77) pass. `cli.test.ts` passes 144 of 145. The failure is `fx status --json returns valid status JSON`, which reads the real profile's update channel outside CI. - Earlier in this round, on `main` at `8c580bb0d` with the review fixes, `mcp-stdio` (91), `auto-mode-reliability` (41), `web-search-fake-gateway` (18), `tui-slash-menu` (36), `tui-composer-edit-contracts` (34), and `tui-resize` (57) pass. `tui-interrupt-recovery`'s `immediate prompt after cancellation` test failed once while other tests loaded the machine, and passed three times alone. - By hand on the built binary: - Escape sequences in `fx config get` and `set`, `fx ask --config`, `fx sessions --limit`, an unknown flag, `fx mcp`, and `fx upgrade --channel` print as `\x1b`. - `fx --modle`, `fx stauts`, `fx mcp lsit`, `fx config get fast_mdoe`, and `fx update --chanel` still suggest the closest name, and `fx add` stays a prompt. - `FX_HOME` that names a file, or a path through one, exits 1 with `FX_HOME must name a folder`, and a new folder works. - `fx config set` through a symlinked `settings.json`, or with a 1 MiB file, names the cause as text and as JSON. - `zig build fuzz -Dfuzz-target=cli_flags --fuzz=300K`, then `--fuzz=600K`, found no failure in 901,541 runs, about 40,000 a second here, which sets the nightly target at 1,200,000 iterations. After that commit, `zig build test`, `cli.test.ts` (144, the same one failure), `poisoned-repository` (7), `acp` (169), and `gateway-stream-lifecycle` (227) pass, and `fx acp` still rejects `--provider-order` while `fx pr` takes it. fish isn't installed here, so CI runs the fish completion test for the first time. - The renamed hooks in the `fuzzy_match`, `prompt_context`, and `session` TLA drivers and in `tests/evals/tool-schema-ab.ts` weren't run here. CI doesn't run those drivers either. ## Docs vercel-labs/fx-web#199 replaces the 15 docs PRs and matches this behavior.

title: Show times in the local time zone
body:
## Summary

- Show entry times in the ctrl+o full transcript in the local time zone instead of UTC.
- Show `fx sessions` updated times in the local time zone.
- Show `fx usage` updated times and Codex and Grok reset times in the local time zone.
- Show the `fx slack` access expiry in the local time zone.
- Read the zone from `TZ` or the system setting, with daylight saving time applied for each timestamp's own date.
- Show the UTC offset, such as `+0530`, when the zone has no plain abbreviation.
- Keep usage periods in UTC days, since AI Gateway reports by UTC day.

title: Bring the MCP TLA+ models and drivers up to date and run them in CI
body:
## Summary

- The MCP models in `tests/tla/mcp/` and `tests/tla/mcp_host/` match the code in #1322: a refused refresh token is never sent again, a disconnect answers a waiting tool list, and the byte budget and the exit reaper have models of their own.

title: Remove the v1 session store
body:
## Summary

fx now keeps every session in the store that `--sessions-v2` used to switch on. This removes the previous store: its writer, its listing and catalog, migration, the switch, and every host branch that chose between the two. The converter and the part of the old reader it needs stay, with no release set for their removal (D65), so a session saved by any earlier release still opens.

- Opening an earlier session converts it together with its subagent sessions, through every open path: `fx -c`, `fx -r`, `fx resume`, `/resume`, `fx ask --resume`, and ACP `session/load`. `fx sessions convert` converts them all. A session's old folder is deleted only after its converted copy is published and matches it (D60).
- `fx session recover` on a damaged earlier session copies what the old store's recover kept into a new session and leaves the original as it was (D64).
- `--sessions-v2`, `FX_SESSIONS_V2`, `fx session migrate` with `--allow-large`, and `fx ask --continue-recovery` with the `durable` key of its JSON are gone, as are the "quit unexpectedly" notice and `fx doctor`'s checks of the old store. Each removed form exits 1: `fx --sessions-v2` as an unknown subcommand, and the others with their command's usage.
- libfx terminal snapshots keep their format and load unchanged (D63).

The decisions are numbered in `tests/tla/session_manager/system-design.md`, which defines D1 to D88.

## Behavior changes

Compared with the previous store:

- A session whose last turn never ended keeps that turn, marked interrupted (D77). When fx is killed while a response is being retried, the reopened session shows the turn's finished pieces but not the text the retried attempt had streamed (D80).
- An API-key 401 on a new session's first turn keeps the rejected prompt as a saved session, which `fx sessions` lists and `--resume last` opens. The previous store discarded it.
- Prompt images are also kept as blobs of the session (D79). Each request names that blob for every prompt image it sends, as `[Image #N (image/png) is saved at "<path>".]`, and the notice for an image too large to send, or left out to keep the request within its size limit, names the same file, in the running session and after a resume, so the note main added for the old `images/` folder still names a file the model can open. Without a saved session, as with `--no-save`, the notice names the copy fx captured for the run. A recalled image names the same blob, since it holds the same bytes. An image the oldest format saved only as a path is captured once when the session converts (D82), and images saved with id 0 get the numbers the old resume gave them (D69).
- Recalling a prompt from the input history uses the image bytes saved with it, so a deleted temporary copy no longer refuses the recall (D84).
- Salvage leaves out a side file that is missing or changed, says its content is unavailable, and exits 1 with `recovered_with_unverified_artifacts`, where the old store refused the whole recovery (D74). A session whose `permissions.json` is damaged is recovered without its saved rules (D72).
- `fx doctor` counts the earlier sessions not converted yet and names each one that can't be converted, with its reason and what `fx session recover` would copy (D73).
- `fx` refuses a `~/.fx`, `~/.fx/sessions`, or `v2` path that is not a real folder before the turn: `fx ask` warns and runs without saving, and a resume fails with `SessionPathUnsafe` (D67).
- `--resume last` and `fx session last` fail with `NoReadableSessions` when the only session they found is damaged (D76), and `fx session --id` on a damaged earlier session names the file and the reason (D78).
- A schema-3 prompt that is not UTF-8 stays in the old format, read only, and is reported with its file, turn, and reason (D66). A pending `legacy_to_v3` upgrade is refused and kept for `fx session recover` (D70).
- An update relaunch whose session had no turn opens a fresh session instead of failing to find it (D81).
- `fx -c` with an unreadable bookmark from the old store says the remembered session ID could not be read and names `fx -r` and `fx --resume <id>` again (D86).
- A subagent's own subagent, which builds before 0.0.8 could create, stays in the old format, and its family converts without it. No fx opens one, since a subagent has had no subagent tool since 0.0.8. `fx sessions convert` lists each under `kept` with the reason, and `fx doctor` names it (D88).
- A file a conversion can't carry across is left out and named with its cause, in the notice and in `fx sessions convert`, and that session's earlier folder is kept, so the file stays where it was: a side file over 512 MiB (D62), or hosted terminal state that is not a folder or a regular file, can't be read, or is nested deeper than 8 folders (D56). `--json` lists each under `left_out` with its `cause` and `reason`, and `fx doctor` counts the earlier folders, subagents' among them, that keep such a file. A retry after a crash names those files again.

## Bugs fixed along the way

- Every interactive session pointed at its store through `App.init`'s stack frame: `App.init` opened the store inside a local `App` and returned that `App` by value. A later turn could crash once the frame was reused, which is what CI's interactive performance gate hit. The bug was already on `main`'s v2 path. The store is now allocated once and owned by the persistence runtime, and `rebindAfterMove` points the store's notice at the moved `App`.
- The `/resume` picker listed every converted session above every unconverted one, even a newer one. It now orders them newest first, as `fx sessions` does.
- A FIFO in place of an earlier session's `events.jsonl`, `session.json`, or `permissions.json` hung the converter on open. Every converter and salvage read now opens only regular files, so such a session is refused and keeps its folder.
- After a resume, a tool result the model had seen whole came back as its preview. It now comes back whole from its blob, or says that its body is unavailable.
- The WebAssembly builds of ACP's model and effort commits still read the removed `writable` field.
- After a compaction inside a turn, a resumed session showed the model the steps of that turn the summary already covered: up to 170 extra messages in real sessions, enough to fill the window. The bug was already on `main`'s v2 path. The compacted record now saves how much of the turn the summary covers, and a resume leaves that out, as the previous store did (D87).
- A v1 session whose hosted terminal folders were not 0700, as a backup restore or a copy between machines can leave them, could not be converted, though the previous store opened it, and `fx doctor` reported nothing. The converter now reads them at any mode, never through a symlink, and copies them private. An entry it can't copy, such as a link, is left out and kept in the earlier folder instead of failing the conversion.
- A compaction inside an open v1 turn that kept an earlier turn lost that turn's trim when the recovery checkpoint replaced the open turn. A converted child whose v1 folder a cleanup kept was reported with the wrong reason. A folder another process removed between its open and its lock counted as unreadable.
- The converter's and the v1 listing cache's own unit tests never ran, because the test list in `src/main.zig` did not name their files.
- A side file over the per-file limit was left out of the converted copy and then deleted with the session's earlier folder. The copy now names the first 32 files it left out and counts them all, in place of its fingerprint, so neither a later open nor a retry after a crash removes that folder, even once the file changes, and neither does an older fx, which removes a folder only when its fingerprint matches.
- Salvage copied hosted terminal state under the earlier session's ID, where the salvaged session never reads it. It no longer copies it, as the previous store's recover never did.
- A kept subagent whose parent session can't be read was reported as having lost its parent. It now says the parent can't be read.
- An image recalled from the input history, or yanked back after a cut, was saved with only the path of its copy in fx's temporary folder, so a resumed session no longer had it once fx exited. A recalled image now keeps the bytes saved with its prompt and is saved as a blob like any other prompt image.

## Tests

- The converter's tests read sessions that the v0.0.14 release wrote, committed under `tests/fixtures/v1-sessions/` with the `generate.ts` that rebuilt them (D68, D83). Tests that could only set up their state through the removed writer are deleted, and the cases that still matter on the kept path are fixture tests.
- Unit tests of the removed writer, migration, catalog, recovery checkpoint, and cache files are deleted with the code they tested. The v1 code left without callers, including bodies that called deleted functions, is deleted too, and a temporary check that analyzes every public declaration of the kept session modules passes.
- In `tui-resume.test.ts`, "missing diff artifact degrades to the inline preview on resume" and "resume compacts a legacy log with inline diff snapshots" are deleted with the old store's diff side files, and the spilled-diff test is now "large diff snapshots reload on resume".
- In `tui-composer-edit-contracts.test.ts`, the history recall test expects the recalled image to name the same saved file as the original, the blob that holds its bytes once, where the old store wrote a new copy for each recall.
- `sessions-v2.test.ts` is now `sessions.test.ts`. Every E2E file that read the old store's files reads the session log, through the helpers in `tests/e2e/saved-sessions.ts`.
- `Wiring.tla` models one store (D85). `V1Conversion.tla` models salvage, and the conversion drivers in `tests/tla/drivers/session_manager/conversion/` run against sessions written by built releases, now including a v0.0.7 family with a subagent's own subagent and a compaction inside a turn.
- `V1Conversion.tla` gains `keeps`, the members whose earlier folder keeps something their copy left out. `NoLossOnDelete` checks that no conversion or cleanup removes that folder; two new mutants drop each guard and are caught. Two conversion drivers run it against the built binary, with an oversized side file and with a terminal link, and a binary without the keep rule is rejected by TLC at its convert step.

## Verification

- `check.sh V1Conversion` full config: no error, 102,951,784 distinct states. Its 25 mutants are caught, and the trace checker's self-test passes 27/27. `check.sh Wiring`: no error, 6 of 6 mutants caught, and the trace self-test passes 14/14.
- Session-manager drivers 76/76: conversion, runtime, and fork.
- CI on the exact head, including the macOS arm64 checks and the PGSO training jobs.
- The built binary, by hand: `fx -c` with an unreadable bookmark, the interactive performance flow, a FIFO in a session folder, a session holding a 600 MiB side file and a terminal link, which converts, names both, and keeps them in its earlier folder, a left-out file made readable afterwards, whose folder the next run keeps, salvage of a damaged session with a terminal link, which reports `recovered`, and a converted session with a 512 MiB side file whose earlier folder the v0.0.14 release's `fx sessions convert` keeps with `FX_SESSIONS_V2=1` (a build that still writes the fingerprint loses that folder).
- On a copy of a real profile with 14,380 root sessions in 16,374 folders:
  - `fx sessions convert` converted 14,368 roots in 7.5 minutes (13 ms per family at the median, 360 ms at p99) and lost or changed nothing. It refused 12 damaged sessions with the file and reason, leaving them and 3 of their children as they were, and kept and named 3 subagents of subagents.
  - TLC accepted 2,116 sampled converted logs, 23 family logs, and a fork.
  - Continuing every root on `main`'s v1 and on this branch against a fake gateway showed the model the same messages for 14,366 roots. 13 open in neither, with the same refusal. The last one loops on both, because its text quotes the fake gateway's review instruction; its converted history matches v1's after v1's own migration, with all 137 side files matched.
  - 21 sampled sessions passed under TLC and the oracle, and 4 continued with a real model matched on both stores.

## Docs

vercel-labs/fx-web#203 updates the Sessions, CLI, Slash commands, and Troubleshooting pages.

title: Fix libfx crash recovery, steering, input limits and packaging
body:
## Summary

### Crash recovery

- A turn whose process crashed right after saving its end now shows as finished: the next process writes the missing `turn_end` before any queued turn runs, and a retry of that prompt resolves at once instead of after 30 s.
- A turn's end record says how the turn ended, so a `turn_end` that recovery writes, and a retry answered from the journal, report the turn's real stop reason. Only a turn an earlier libfx ended reports `unknown`.
- When recovery ends a turn whose reply the stream showed only in part, it first shows the rest of the reply, once, so a viewer and a replay read the whole reply. A reply fx restarted after a crash also shows once.
- A turn that ended without a record, such as a refused prompt or a cancel before any record, also gets its missing `turn_end` after a crash.
- A cancel that arrives while a turn's end is being stored doesn't change it: the turn ends as its record says. On WebAssembly, a cancelled turn's record says `cancelled`, not `refused` or `error`.
- A steer that a crashed turn had accepted now appears once in the stream when the turn resumes, also after a second crash.
- A turn that stops at its deadline between steps emits `session.deadline`, and a deadline that arrives while the turn's end is being stored ends the turn as its record says.
- A `resume()` that continued a turn writes no idle line after that turn ends.

### Steering

- On native, a steer that arrives as a step ends in a tool call joins the turn and the call runs, as on WebAssembly. The stream no longer says `end_turn` for a turn the journal records as cancelled.
- A steer stored while a tool runs reaches the model in the request right after that tool's result, from any server.
- A steer that another server stores just before a reply ends continues that turn instead of running as a turn of its own. One stored after the turn's last read runs once, as the next turn.
- A turn a steer with images ended is `cancelled`, as its journal says, and has the steer's `messageId` as `endedBySteer` in its result and `turn_end` line, also after recovery, so an app can tell it from a turn `cancel()` ended.

### Durable sessions and stores

- A reader in another process gets a running turn's lines in the same order and under the same cursors as a replay from cursor 0.
- A fenced turn rejects with the store's `FxFencedError`, and a model request after a tool call waits for the store's answer to the record holding the call's result, so a fenced engine sends nothing more.
- A worker another one replaced, that wakes after a stall, writes no more UI lines. libfx's bundled world-local names a stream line only as it lands, so a line whose write was in flight can't sort ahead of lines readers already have, and a killed worker's fence lock is taken over at once instead of after 30 s.
- A delivery no longer starts a turn early and sends a second model request when it read the log as the previous worker's run ended.
- `agent.session()` does no I/O. The durability starts on first use, and a new session's `id` is `null` until then. `session(id)` on a World durability throws `FX_SESSION_ID_INVALID` at once for an id that isn't a run id.
- `steer()` and `cancel()` reject after `close()`, and `memory()` no longer redelivers a message every 10 ms when no agent listens, so the process exits.
- Upgrading from a dev build that wrote `local()` sessions with world-local 5.0 keeps those sessions: libfx moves them into the new layout before the store opens, and rejects with `FX_LOCAL_STORE_LAYOUT` if it cannot.
- Under `NODE_ENV=development` in Node, creating an agent again with the name of one that already runs replaces it and emits `agent.replaced`, so `next dev` works; the newest definition always wins. Elsewhere this still throws `FX_AGENT_NAME_IN_USE`, whose message now says that agents created without a name all share the name `default`.
- `checkpoint()` past its limits rejects with `FX_CHECKPOINT_TOO_LARGE`, naming the limit, and a save the engine skips emits `checkpoint.error`. A session that hasn't saved a checkpoint yet still reports `checkpoint.mismatch` when it continues on another model.

### Images and input limits

- Images within their documented limits are accepted beside the 8 MiB prompt frame, and the limits apply to `resizeImage`'s output, so large photos are resized instead of refused.
- A prompt or steer that could never run is refused by `prompt()` and `steer()` before it is stored.
- A durable session keeps the images one model request can carry, 100 images whose base64 fits in 30 MiB, instead of 4,096 images and 512 MiB, so opening a session with many photos takes a fraction of the time and memory. An open reads up to 8 saved images at once.
- An engine's own store keeps conversations with images up to 32 MiB, from 4 MiB. On native, a model request that would pass 30 MiB leaves out its oldest images, as on WebAssembly; a request whose text alone is over 32 MiB still fails before it is sent.
- A tool result with more than 8 images fails with a message naming the limit.

### Multiple tenants

- Agents share the 64 native runtimes: while they run short, an agent may take one only while it holds fewer than its share, and the last free one is kept for an agent that holds none. An agent's turns past its share run on WebAssembly and emit `runtime.fallback`; without JSPI they fail with `LIBFX_NATIVE_LIMIT`, naming the limit.
- The native fetch bridge frees request and response buffers over 64 KiB after each request.
- A delivery forwarded to the agent its session belongs to is queued once, even when the queue already holds that message for the agent.

### Errors, notices and events

- A provider's HTTP error body, the length-limit notice and an unconfirmed Ultrafast notice no longer stream as reply text. A refused turn has the provider's error in `result.error`, including a custom provider's own message for a rejected key, and other notices reach `onEvent` as `turn.notice`. A content-filtered turn's error says the filter stopped it.
- Every `tool_start` of a cancelled turn gets a `tool_end`, on native and WebAssembly.
- The missing-credentials error says no AI Gateway credentials were found and where libfx looks for them.
- A non-function `fetch` or `onEvent` is refused, naming the option; a provider tool other than `web_search` is refused, naming the tool; an agent turn's unsupported-effort error names the model and the capability.
- `credentials()`, `onCredentials` and `refreshLock` name the session for the model-list request too. A refresh refused because the token belongs to another account isn't run again, and the turn fails with `LIBFX_GROK_ACCOUNT_CHANGED`.
- A custom model declared `supportsToolUse: false` is offered no tools, and `backend: "auto"` requests the catalog once when the model refuses Ultrafast.
- A `file:` URL string for the WebAssembly module is read from disk; a `wasm` URL that answers with an error status rejects with `LIBFX_WASM_LOAD_FAILED`, naming the URL and status. With `backend: "wasm"`, the JSPI error no longer says no native addon was found, and `vercel()`'s authorization error says it needs a Vercel deployment or `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`.
- `libfx/wasm` exports only what its types declare, and `FxStopReason` lists `"yielded"`.
- The model catalog is fetched at most once per agent, a prompt with a known model id does not wait for it, and cancelling a turn stops its wait for the catalog.
- A `web_search` `tool_start` event carries the search query. After a cut-off `idempotent: false` call, the model is no longer told the call has a confirmed result. Cancelling a turn on WebAssembly ends it `cancelled` even when the request body fails after the abort.

### Packages

- `npm i libfx` installs only the native addon for the machine. Each addon is published as a version of libfx itself, such as `libfx@0.0.15-0.linux-x64`, which libfx lists as the optional dependency `libfx-linux-x64`, and likewise for `linux-arm64`, `darwin-x64` and `darwin-arm64`. No other package is published, and Next.js still needs no config. What `npm i libfx` unpacks drops from about 46 MiB to about 18 MiB.
- `fx-term.wasm` stays inside libfx. A terminal published as its own version of libfx would resolve to the release on an app's next fresh install, so it ships with libfx until it can be a package of its own.
- The release workflow publishes the four addon versions before libfx, with provenance, under the dist-tag `addon` (`addon-dev` for dev builds), so `latest` and `dev` only ever name a release.
- The bundled Vercel World no longer carries the path of the machine that built it.
- The package no longer bundles undici; the bundled Worlds use `node:http`. `next build --webpack` no longer warns about libfx's loader. The package includes the libfx docs. The README states that WebAssembly on Bun needs 1.3.10 or newer, except 1.3.14.

### fx CLI

- The crash continuation this PR first had for the fx CLI, where `fx -c` continued a crashed turn once, is not in it: it was built on the session store #1328 removed. On the new store a crashed turn is kept, marked interrupted, and waits for the user. Continuing it on its own will come in a follow-up.

### Browser terminal

- The browser terminal draws approval prompts and keeps the page responsive while it waits for an answer.
- When its session store refuses a save, the app gets `session.persist_error`, and on a revision conflict fx says on screen that it stopped saving the conversation.
- It reports `transport.start`, `transport.response` and `transport.error`; prompt history uses the workspace adapter's root; a refused workspace says why on screen and emits `workspace.invalid`; `terminal.size` fires only when the size changes.
- In auto mode, a browser workspace with `permission: "prompt"` asks the user for an action that would go to review, because the browser has no reviewer to clear it. `AGENTS.md`'s permission section records this one exception; everywhere else a missing reviewer still holds the action.

## Decisions

- After a crash leaves an `idempotent: false` call's outcome unknown, the model is told it may have partly run and the turn goes on.
- A crash's cut-off partial text stays in the stream before `turn_resume`, and the re-run starts after it.

## Before release

- No npm setup is needed: every addon version publishes as `libfx` through its existing trusted publisher.
- The fx.sh homepage keeps loading `fx-term.wasm` from libfx; fx-web's `libfx@0.0.14` pins move when it upgrades.
- An app that passes its own `@workflow/world-local` to `world()` gets the fence-lock and stream-placement fixes once world-local ships them (vercel/workflow#4908 and vercel/workflow#4909); `local()` has them now.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#200
