title: Bug: Backspace appends a control byte instead of deleting in MCP form fields
body:
### Issue details

Backspace does not delete in the fields of the `/mcp` add server form. It appends the raw byte to the field, so the field shows a stray escape and the value that gets saved can contain a control character.

Steps to reproduce on fx 0.0.14 (macOS, `TERM=xterm-256color`):

1. Run `fx`.
2. Run `/mcp`.
3. Press `a` to open the add server form.
4. Type `ab` in the **Name** field.
5. Press Backspace.

Expected: the field shows `a`.

Actual: the field shows `ab` followed by a control byte, and nothing is deleted. Holding or repeating Backspace keeps appending bytes until the field overflows and renders with an ellipsis.

The same happens in the **Command** field, with Ctrl-H (0x08) as well as Backspace (0x7f), and in the **Arguments** field, which shares the code path. Backspace works in the main prompt, in the `/mcp` filter field (`/`), and in the `/model` picker search, so the problem is limited to the MCP add and argument forms.

Impact: the control byte becomes part of the field value. The add form writes those values to the server entry, so a field edited with Backspace can store a control character in `~/.fx/mcp.json`. It also breaks the ordinary editing flow of the form, because there is no way to correct a typo.

Cause, from reading `main`:

- `handleMcpAddInput` and `handleMcpArgumentInput` in `src/core/app/app_input_runtime.zig` special-case `\t` and `\r` and send every other byte to `handleTextByte`, which appends it to the composer draft.
- The terminal decoder has already resolved the byte into a `composer_shortcut` (`.delete_backward` for 127 and 8 in `src/ui/input/shortcuts.zig`), but these two handlers receive only the byte and never the shortcut.
- The MCP filter field in the same file handles `0x7f` explicitly, which is why the filter deletes correctly.

I reproduced this with `FX_RECORD` and have a fix with a regression test ready to open as a pull request.

### Trace

No response

### Sensitive information

- [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

title: Apply composer editing keys to MCP form fields
body:
Fixes #1332.

## What changes

The composer editing keys now work in the `/mcp` add server form and in the MCP argument form. Backspace, Ctrl-H, Ctrl-W, and Ctrl-U edit the field as they do in the main prompt, and a control byte is no longer written into the field value.

## Why

`handleMcpAddInput` and `handleMcpArgumentInput` in `src/core/app/app_input_runtime.zig` handled only Tab and Enter, then sent every other byte to `handleTextByte`, which appends it to the composer draft. The terminal decoder had already resolved bytes 127 and 8 into the `delete_backward` shortcut in `src/ui/input/shortcuts.zig`, but these two handlers received only the raw byte and never the shortcut. Pressing Backspace therefore appended the byte: the field showed a stray control character, the field could not be corrected, and the value could be written to the server entry in `~/.fx/mcp.json`.

The change passes the decoded `RawTerminalInput` into both handlers. Field bytes now go through one helper that applies a `composer_shortcut` when the decoder produced one, drops a control byte that is not text, and otherwise inserts text exactly as before. The MCP filter field already handled `0x7f` directly, so it is unchanged.

Two details worth a reviewer's eye:

- The drop covers `0x7f` as well as bytes below `0x20`. Every path that builds a raw input event today attaches the decoder's shortcut for 127, so this is not load-bearing now, but it keeps the reported symptom closed if a future ingress omits the shortcut. A test asserts it.
- `RoutingFakeApp` in the test block gains an `mcp` field, which makes the MCP routing branches compile for the existing routing tests. `mcp.menu.active` defaults to false and the fake declares no `mcpHostMenuKey`, so no existing test changes behavior. The full suite confirms this: no test outside the two added here moved between pass and fail.

## How I verified

- `zig fmt --check src/` passes. `zig build` succeeds.
- `zig build test` on the final commit: 10171 pass, 3 skip, 13 fail (10187 total). Neither added test appears in the failure list. The same command on the base commit without this change gives 10169 pass, 3 skip, 13 fail (10185 total), and the set of failing test names is identical between the two runs, so the change adds two passing tests and no failures. Those 13 are 12 in `core.execution.command_runner.*` and one in `core.agent.runtime.assistant_stream`.
- The added tests fail without the fix. While developing them, the add-field test reported `expected "a", found "ab"` followed by the appended byte.
- `scripts/detect-macos-need.sh origin/main 61e389a` reports `No macOS-specific change; macOS arm64 checks skipped`, so that required check passes without a runner.
- Drove `./zig-out/bin/fx` on a pseudo-terminal. From `/mcp`, pressed `a`, typed `ab` in **Name**, then Backspace: the field showed `a`. Repeated it in **Command** (`npxx` became `np`), and confirmed Ctrl-H deletes, Ctrl-W deletes a word, and Ctrl-U clears the line. Backspace on an empty field is a no-op. Escape still cancels the form, and Tab still switches transport.
- Saved a server against a throwaway profile with `HOME=$(mktemp -d) FX_DISABLE_KEYCHAIN=1`, typing `demoo` and `echoo` and correcting each field with Backspace. The resulting `mcp.json` held `{"mcp":{"demo":{"type":"local","command":["echo"],...}}}` with no control bytes.

## Docs

No manual page describes the editing keys of the MCP forms, so no manual change is needed. If a maintainer wants it recorded, the natural place is https://fx.sh/docs/capabilities/mcp under "Add a remote server".

## Notes for review

- The commit is signed with an SSH signing key and GitHub reports it as verified.
- I am an outside contributor, so I left the `type:` label off.
- The required checks (`Build & Test`, `E2E (deterministic)`, `Shellcheck`, `Startup Latency`, `macOS arm64`) have not started on this draft. If a maintainer needs to approve the workflow run for a first-time contributor, that is the missing step.

title: Bug: IncompleteStream when an openai-chat-completions server ends the stream after finish_reason without `data: [DONE]`
body:
### Summary

A custom `openai-chat-completions` connection reports `fx: IncompleteStream` on every reply. The full answer prints to stdout first. The failure happens at the end of the stream.

The server sends a final chunk that carries `finish_reason`, then closes the connection. It never sends `data: [DONE]`.

### Environment

- fx version: v0.0.14, installed with setup.sh
- Platform: macOS (darwin)
- Connection: custom `openai-chat-completions` provider in `~/.fx/settings.json`
- Endpoint: `https://api.minimaxi.com/v1`, model `MiniMax-M3` (MiniMax)
- Command: `fx ask 'What model are you?'`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Define a custom connection:

```json
{
  "provider": "minimax",
  "providers": {
    "minimax": {
      "protocol": "openai-chat-completions",
      "base_url": "https://api.minimaxi.com/v1",
      "auth": { "type": "bearer", "env": "MINIMAX_API_KEY" },
      "model_metadata": {
        "MiniMax-M3": {
          "context_window": 131072,
          "max_output_tokens": 8192,
          "supports_tool_use": true
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "models": { "minimax": "MiniMax-M3" }
}
```

2. Run:

```bash
fx ask 'What model are you?'
```

3. The answer prints to stdout. The process then exits non-zero:

```
fx: IncompleteStream
```

The prompt content does not matter. Every prompt fails the same way.

### Raw wire capture

A direct `curl -N` to the same endpoint with `"stream": true` returns `HTTP/2 200` and `content-type: text/event-stream`.

Event 19 of 19, the final event on the wire:

```
data: {"id":"<redacted>","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant"}}],"created":1792243918,"model":"MiniMax-M3","object":"chat.completion.chunk","usage":null,"service_tier":"standard"}
```

Then the connection closes.

- `data:` events captured: 19
- `finish_reason` present: yes, value `stop`
- `data: [DONE]` present: no, the string never appears in the body

The first 18 events carry assistant content. Content is redacted from this report.

### Root cause

In `src/gateway/chat_completions_protocol.zig`, `consume_stream`:

```zig
const chunk = data orelse return error.IncompleteStream;
```

`framing.next()` returns null at EOF. The reducer already reached `phase == .finished` when it accepted the `finish_reason` chunk (`self.phase = .finished;` in `Reducer.accept`). fx still returns `error.IncompleteStream`, because it waits for a framed `[DONE]` that this server never sends.

The doc comment on `consume_stream` states:

> Stops exactly at framed [DONE], without waiting for EOF or consuming another event.

This makes `[DONE]` mandatory. Several OpenAI-compatible servers end a stream by closing the connection instead.

### Attribution

The endpoint omits the `data: [DONE]` sentinel that OpenAI-style streams end with, so the server side is non-conformant. DeepSeek and Qwen document the sentinel in their Chat Completions specs, and major clients treat a missing sentinel as a server defect.

At the same time, most clients treat EOF as end-of-stream instead of requiring the sentinel, so fx is stricter than the ecosystem norm. Since the reducer already tracks `finish_reason`, accepting EOF at `phase == .finished` keeps truncation detection intact. A stream cut off before `finish_reason` still fails.

### Expected behavior

A stream that delivered `finish_reason` and then reached EOF should complete as a normal turn.

A stream cut off before `finish_reason` must still fail with `error.IncompleteStream`.

### Suggested fix

In `consume_stream`, treat EOF after a finished choice as a normal end:

```zig
const chunk = data orelse {
    if (reducer.phase == .finished) {
        reducer.phase = .done;
        return reducer.finish(cancel_flag.load(.seq_cst));
    }
    return error.IncompleteStream;
};
```

This keeps every guard inside `finish()`:

- `finish_reason` must be `stop` or `tool_calls`
- `length` still maps to `error.OutputTruncated`
- `content_filter` still maps to `error.ContentFiltered`
- refusal, tool name and argument validation still run
- a stream without any `finish_reason` still returns `error.IncompleteStream`

title: Use ACP stop reasons at the protocol boundary
body:
`fx acp` returns internal stop-reason names that ACP v1 clients may reject. Translate output limits, turn limits, and refusals to `max_tokens`, `max_turn_requests`, and `refusal` across prompt response serializers. Keep libfx's existing result strings, cancellation, and yield/resume behavior unchanged.

Fixes #1157.

Exercised the built `./zig-out/bin/fx` through native ACP against a local fake provider: four baseline failures become passes, with six focused regression/control cases and 41 focused Zig tests passing. Native and Wasm libfx compatibility, yield/resume, and cancellation checks also pass. The steering regression checks both responses, usage ownership, request count, and clean shutdown. `max_model_turns` has serializer coverage because it has no current production producer.

Required hosted CI remains pending. Prepared with Codex assistance and a separate local review.

title: Name the source in read_tool_result rows
body:
## Summary

- `read_tool_result` rows name the command, file, URL, or MCP tool whose saved output they read, such as `Read more output from zig build test`.
- Searches of saved output show the search text, for example `Searched zig build test output for "error:"`.
- Reads of compacted history name the record they open, such as `Opened earlier tool call T5`, and history searches show `Searched earlier conversation`.
- Reloading saved images shows `Reloaded saved images`.
- When the source call is no longer in the conversation, for example after compaction, the row shows `Read more command output` or `Read more output`.
- Resumed sessions show the same labels the live session showed.
- `fx ask` progress lines use the same labels.
- ACP tool call titles for reads use the full label, live and after `session/load`. Other tools keep their verb-only titles.

title: Keep a finished reply when a crash cuts off its turn's end
body:
## Summary

- An engine's `turn.result`, and the turn's updates, now end only once every record of the turn is stored. The record that holds a turn's end or yield is sent as a barrier, so a store may not acknowledge it before it is durable. A failure to store it rejects the result instead of surfacing later from `close()`.
- Just before a turn ends with its reply, the core saves a recovery checkpoint with the action `delivering_response`. If the process stops before the turn's end is stored, `resume()` ends the turn with that reply and makes no model request. Before, the resume asked the model again, sent `[Response interrupted. Restarting.]`, and replaced a reply the store already held.
- An engine's `resume()` now tells the core that its host holds none of the turn, so the resumed turn sends the reply it saved, or the start of a reply it restarts, as `text_delta`. Until now every resume was treated as coming from a client that kept the turn's earlier output, so an engine in a new process got no text. A durable session's worker resumes saying its stream already holds that output, and ACP clients and the CLI are unchanged.
- The checkpoint saved after each model response is unchanged, so a reply that a later check rejects, such as a required vision call that never came, still recovers with a new request. A steer waiting at resume, or a stop hook still to run, continues the turn with a request as before.
- `Resumption.tla` models a turn's end as save the reply, send the end, and the end lands, and checks `SavedAnswerNotRequested` and `ResultOnlyAfterDurableEnd`. `mutants.py` adds three planted bugs and a witness for them.

## Reproduction on main

A store that holds the append carrying `turn_committed`: engine A's `turn.result` resolved with `end_turn` while the append was still held. The store then held a `turn_progress` with A's whole reply but no turn end. A new engine's `resume()` made one model request and sent `[Response interrupted. Restarting.]` followed by a different reply.

## Tests

- `sdk/tests/test-journal.mjs`: a crash after the final reply delivers the saved reply with no model request, and the next turn's history holds it once; a turn's result and updates wait for a held turn end, whose record is a barrier; a turn whose end fails to store rejects its result. Two tests that cut off only the commit to exercise a restarted request now crash during the request. A resumed engine turn sends the saved reply as its text, a resume that says its host holds the output sends none, and a restarted reply sends the start the last process had made before the restart notice.
- `src/core/agent/runtime/tests/gateway_flow.zig`: delivery from a restored checkpoint with no request; a reply that calls a tool is not saved for delivery; a steer waiting at a saved reply asks the model again. Five tests that check the sequence of recovery checkpoints now expect the one that saves the final reply, with the attempts the last settled checkpoint counted.
- Planted bugs, each failing `test-journal.mjs`: the result not waiting, the end not a barrier, the core never saving the final reply, a resume ignoring it, and an engine resume not saying its host holds none of the turn.
- `acp.test.ts` "ACP recovery retains image snapshots through provider failure and reload" covers a reply rejected after it finished.

## Docs

title: Keep retrying model requests through network and gateway failures
body:
## Summary

- Network drops, gateway errors, and rate limits retry until the request gets a response or you press Esc. fx no longer gives up after a fixed number of attempts.
- Retries wait 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 s, then every 30 s. While offline, fx retries after 1 and 2 s, then every 5 s, in the TUI, `fx ask`, and ACP alike.
- A gateway's Retry-After is honored on 429 and 5xx, capped at 30 s.
- A 429 whose body names a used-up quota, such as `insufficient_quota`, ends the turn instead of retrying, for every provider.
- A gateway error event with a client-error code, such as an invalid request, auth, quota, or unknown model, ends the turn after one request, even when the stream has no finish event. An unrecognized code is judged by the event's HTTP status.
- The gateway's `gateway_stream_terminated` error, which arrives without an HTTP status, is retried as a gateway error.
- A TLS setup failure, a stream that ends without a finish event, a finish event fx can't read, and a provider error with no code or status keep retrying like every other transient failure. Only Esc stops them.
- The status line shows the cause, a countdown, the attempt, and the elapsed time, such as `Gateway error · next try in 4s · attempt 3 · 12s`. It keeps counting while a resend is in flight and clears when the response starts or the request ends.
- When an answer breaks off before any tool call, fx resends the same request without telling the model the previous response was interrupted.
- Esc during a retry ends the request and the turn. The separate Esc-to-pause for network waits is gone.
- With Fast on, fx turns Fast off after three gateway errors in a row instead of after the first failure.
- Retry notices no longer include the provider's raw error text.
- `fx ask` prints a notice only when the status changes, and `fx ask --json` reports `recovery` as `state`, `attempt`, `need`, and `message`, with `failed` when a request that was retrying ends on an error.
- ACP `modelResponseRecovery` uses the same fields.

Stacked on #1331.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#202

title: Bug: Chat Completions providers end the turn when the model calls an unknown tool or sends malformed arguments
body:
### Issue details

## Problem

With a configured provider that uses `"protocol": "openai-chat-completions"` (we use OpenRouter through `FX_CONFIGURED_PROVIDERS`), one bad tool call from the model ends the whole turn. The client sees `The turn failed: InvalidToolName` when the model names a tool it wasn't given, or `The turn failed: InvalidToolArguments` when the arguments aren't a valid JSON object. The model never sees an error it could correct, so the user has to send another message to continue.

We hit this in `fx acp` with MCP servers loaded. For example, a model reading `mcp_notion_notion-update-page`'s schema decided to fetch a spec it mentions and called a tool name that wasn't advertised.

## Expected behavior

fx answers the call with an error and the turn continues, as it does for other providers. The tool loop already handles both cases:

- A name with no registered tool is answered with `Unsupported tool: NAME` and never runs (`src/core/agent/runtime/orchestrator.zig:10805`, the `.unsupported` preparation).
- Arguments that are not a valid JSON object are classified by `ToolArgumentIntegrity` and answered without running the tool (`src/core/agent/runtime/lifecycle.zig`; test `processQueuedPrompt settles rejected shell arguments without streamed activity` in `tests/tool_flow.zig:1030`, where the model then replies "Recovered.").

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a provider with `"protocol": "openai-chat-completions"` and select it.
2. Send: `Call a tool named totally_missing_tool with arguments {} (call it directly even though it is not in your tool list), then tell me the error you got back.`
3. The turn fails with `InvalidToolName` instead of the model reporting `Unsupported tool: totally_missing_tool`.

## Cause

Line numbers are from `main` at `8145499e`.

The Chat Completions stream parser rejects these calls before the tool loop sees them, in `src/gateway/chat_completions_protocol.zig`:

- Line 887 (`accept_tools`): while streaming, a name that is not a prefix of an advertised name fails the stream with `InvalidToolName`.
- Line 959 (`finish`): a name that isn't advertised fails with `InvalidToolName`.
- Line 960 (`finish`): `validate_arguments` fails with `InvalidToolArguments` when the arguments aren't a valid JSON object.
- Line 310 (`validate_history`): any history call whose `argument_integrity` isn't `.valid` fails the request. Removing only the checks above would move the failure to the next request, because the tool loop stores a rejected call with `{}` arguments and its integrity still marked malformed (`dupeBlockedToolCall`, `lifecycle.zig:438`).

There is also an ACP display bug on the same path. A call the tool loop answers as unsupported never gets a final `tool_call_update`, so ACP clients show it as pending forever. For calls fx runs itself, `sendToolCallPending` records `.not_applicable` (`src/acp/prompt.zig:353`), and `pushToolLifecycle` passes the `.terminal` event only to `sendProviderTerminal` (line 3254), which returns unless the call is `.pending` (line 365). Calls that execute are finalized by the executor transport, and rejected calls by `recordToolCallRejected`, but an unsupported call reaches neither. The test `modern mixed batch materializes unsupported terminal before admission` (`tests/tool_flow.zig:3057`) asserts that unsupported calls do not go through the rejected hook, so the fix belongs in ACP rather than the orchestrator.

## Suggested fix

In `src/gateway/chat_completions_protocol.zig`:

1. Drop the advertised-prefix check in `accept_tools`. Keep the name length bound.
2. In `finish`, replace the `known_name` and `validate_arguments` checks with `validate_name(tool.name.items)`. An empty name or one with characters outside the allowed set still fails, because history could not carry it back.
3. In `validate_history`, remove the `argument_integrity != .valid` rejection. The `validate_arguments` call that follows still checks the `{}` text being replayed.
4. Update the tests that expect the old failures, and add tests that an unknown name and malformed arguments reach the tool loop as written and that a rejected call replays.

In `src/acp/prompt.zig`, record when a local call's final status is sent. When a lifecycle `.terminal` event with a `failed`, `denied`, or `cancelled` outcome arrives for a local call that has none yet, send a failed `tool_call_update` with the result the model received. Leave `completed` outcomes alone, because a file edit's completion can be deferred.

#1141 proposed the unknown-name part of this and was closed without merging. It did not cover malformed arguments, the history check, or the pending ACP status.

## Verification of the fix

We applied the changes above in a fork:

- The Chat Completions tests pass (85), including two new tests.
- The full `zig build test` has the same 16 failures as unmodified `main` in our environment: command runner output checks, the native `printf` matrix, and one ANSI rendering test. None are related to this change.
- Running a real model through `fx acp`, a call to `totally_missing_tool` is answered with `Unsupported tool: totally_missing_tool`, the model finishes its reply, and the client receives `status: failed` for the call.

### Trace

_No response_

### Sensitive information

- [X] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

title: Refresh the model catalog during a session
body:
## Summary

- Refetch the AI Gateway model catalog during a session once it is five minutes old, when you send a prompt, type `/model` completions, or change credentials. An idle session makes no catalog requests.
- Revalidate the catalog in the background when the model picker opens, unless a fetch is running or one started in the last five seconds.
- Keep listing the cached models in the picker and completions while a refresh runs, and keep the open picker's provider tab and selected model when the refreshed catalog lands.
- Keep the cached catalog when a refresh fails.
- Let prompts proceed while a catalog retry is in flight. Only the first catalog load for a credential delays capability checks.
- Back off catalog retries after consecutive failures, for every trigger: 5 seconds, then 10, 20, and so on up to five minutes. A success or credential change resets the backoff.
- Fail an AI Gateway catalog request after 30 seconds as a retryable timeout, so a stalled endpoint cannot hold refreshes.
- Reject an AI Gateway catalog response larger than 16 MB and keep the cached catalog, so an oversized response cannot grow memory on every refresh.
- Time catalog staleness and retries with a clock that keeps counting through sleep but ignores system time changes, so adjusting the clock no longer forces or delays a refresh.
- Tell you in the failed model picker that fx retries automatically, instead of asking you to retry `/model`.
- Refresh the Codex and Grok catalogs, which go stale after 60 seconds, when you send a prompt, as `/model` completions already do.
- Refetch a stale gateway catalog for ACP clients when they request session config options. The refresh still runs inline, so a stalled endpoint can delay that response by up to 30 seconds, at most once every five minutes.

title: libfx 0.0.14: with local() durability, a steer stored just before a tool returns misses the running turn
body:
**libfx:** 0.0.14 and 0.0.14-dev.1561.g1a070af32cdf, native backend, Node 25 (macOS arm64). Works on 0.0.13-dev.1432.g1df91f0b4ebf.

## What happens

With `local()` durability, `session.steer()` sent while a tool is running doesn't reach the running turn. The model request after the tool goes out without it, the turn ends with `end_turn`, and about a second later the steer runs as a turn of its own.

With `memory()` durability, the same code works: the turn emits `user_message` and the request after the tool carries the steer. 0.0.13-dev.1432 also works with `local()`.

The `steer()` docs say it "waits for a running tool", so we expected the steer to join the turn.

On 0.0.14 the `local()` run below misses the turn every time (6 of 6 runs). On dev.1432 it joined the turn in 3 of 3.

## Repro without a key

`node steer.mjs local` (or `node steer.mjs` for `memory()`)

```js
import { createFxAgent, memory } from "libfx"
import { local } from "libfx/durable-local"
import { mkdtempSync } from "node:fs"
import { tmpdir } from "node:os"
import { join } from "node:path"

const sse = (parts) => new Response(new ReadableStream({ start(c) {
  for (const p of parts) c.enqueue(new TextEncoder().encode(`data: ${JSON.stringify(p)}\n\n`)); c.close() } }),
  { headers: { "content-type": "text/event-stream" } })
const usage = { inputTokens: { total: 1, noCache: 1, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 }, outputTokens: { total: 1, text: 1, reasoning: 0 } }
const text = (t) => sse([{ type: "stream-start", warnings: [] }, { type: "text-start", id: "t" }, { type: "text-delta", id: "t", delta: t },
  { type: "text-end", id: "t" }, { type: "finish", finishReason: { unified: "stop", raw: "end_turn" }, usage }])
let calls = 0
const requests = []
const fetch = async (url, init) => {
  if (!String(url).endsWith("/ai/language-model")) return new Response(JSON.stringify({ data: [] }))
  const body = JSON.parse(init.body)
  const steered = JSON.stringify(body.prompt ?? body).includes("Keep it short.")
  requests.push(steered ? "request with steer" : "request without steer")
  if (requests.length === 1)
    return sse([{ type: "stream-start", warnings: [] },
      { type: "tool-call", toolCallId: `call_${++calls}`, toolName: "wait", input: "{}" },
      { type: "finish", finishReason: { unified: "tool-calls", raw: "tool_use" }, usage }])
  return text(steered ? "saw the steer" : "no steer")
}

let release, started
const running = new Promise((r) => (started = r))
const agent = createFxAgent({
  apiKey: "k", model: "anthropic/m", fetch,
  durability: process.argv[2] === "local" ? local({ dir: mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "steer-")) }) : memory(),
  tools: [{ name: "wait", description: "w", idempotent: true, inputSchema: { type: "object", properties: {} },
    execute: async () => { started(); await new Promise((r) => (release = r)); return "waited" } }]
})
const session = agent.session()
const turn = session.prompt("work")
const events = []; let answer = ""
const reading = (async () => { for await (const e of turn) { events.push(e.type); if (e.type === "text_delta") answer += e.delta } })()
await running
await session.steer("Keep it short.") // the tool is still running
release()
await reading
const result = await turn.result
console.log({ durability: process.argv[2] ?? "memory", events: events.join(" "), answer, stopReason: result.stopReason, requests })
await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1500))
console.log("1.5s later:", requests)
await agent.close()
```

0.0.14, `local`:

```
{
  durability: 'local',
  events: 'tool_start tool_end text_delta',
  answer: 'no steer',
  stopReason: 'end_turn',
  requests: [ 'request without steer', 'request without steer' ]
}
1.5s later: [ 'request without steer', 'request without steer', 'request with steer' ]
```

0.0.14, `memory`, and 0.0.13-dev.1432, `local`:

```
{
  events: 'tool_start tool_end user_message text_delta',
  answer: 'saw the steer',
  stopReason: 'end_turn',
  requests: [ 'request without steer', 'request with steer' ]
}
```

## Expected

A steer sent while a tool runs is in the next model request of that turn, whatever the durability.

title: Accept empty streamed model names on custom connections
body:
Some OpenAI-compatible gateways send `model: ""` in otherwise valid Chat Completions chunks. fx rejects the first such chunk with `InvalidChunk` and aborts the response.

Treat an empty model string as absent metadata. Preserve any previously observed nonempty identity and continue rejecting wrong types, oversized names, and conflicting identities. Generation IDs remain strict; the requested model is never substituted as the served model.

Addresses the empty-model failure reported by @espetro in #1173. This does not establish full Bifrost compatibility or address the report's separate reasoning-format concerns.

Validation on macOS arm64 with Zig 0.17.0 and Bun 1.3.14:

- 60 parser tests and 48 configured-provider E2E cases passed.
- Built `./zig-out/bin/fx ask --json --no-save` against a loopback fixture: normal, empty, and mixed model chunks all returned the expected text and usage. The baseline passed the normal control and failed the other two with `InvalidChunk`.
- ReleaseSafe build, formatting, and public-surface checks passed; independent source and evidence review found no blocking issue.

These results are from the preserved local candidate. Required hosted CI remains pending.

title: HTTP client ignores HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / NO_PROXY
body:
fx's HTTP client doesn't appear to read the standard proxy environment variables (`HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, or the lowercase forms), so requests to providers go direct even when a proxy is set. That makes fx unusable on networks or in sandboxes where all egress has to go through a proxy.

### Repro

fx 0.0.14 (`fx-linux-x86_64`), Debian bookworm and Ubuntu 24.04.

```bash
# Nothing listens on port 9, so any proxy-aware client fails to connect.
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...   # a working key

mkdir -p ~/.fx && cat > ~/.fx/settings.json <<'JSON'
{"providers":{"openai":{"protocol":"openai-chat-completions",
  "base_url":"https://api.openai.com/v1",
  "auth":{"type":"bearer","env":"OPENAI_API_KEY"}}}}
JSON

FX_PROVIDER=openai fx ask --json --no-save --model gpt-4.1-mini "say hi"
```

### Expected

The request goes to the proxy at `127.0.0.1:9` and fails to connect, as it would with `curl`, Node (`NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`), Python or Go.

### Actual

The request succeeds: fx connects to `api.openai.com` directly. AI Gateway (`ai-gateway.vercel.sh`) behaves the same way. The binary contains none of the strings `HTTPS_PROXY`, `https_proxy`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY` or `NO_PROXY`.

### Suggested fix

Honour `HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` (and lowercase) plus `NO_PROXY` for every outbound request (providers, gateway, MCP over HTTP/SSE, web fetch, update checks), using `CONNECT` for `https://` targets. Zig's `std.http.Client` has proxy support (`initDefaultProxies` reads the environment), so this may mostly be wiring. Trusting `SSL_CERT_FILE` / `SSL_CERT_DIR` would also let a TLS-inspecting proxy's CA be added.

Possibly related: #1034.

title: ACP: completed shell tool_call_update has a clipped JSON summary instead of the command output
body:
Over `fx acp`, a `shell` tool call streams its stdout in `in_progress` updates, but the final `status: "completed"` update's `content` is a JSON status summary cut off mid-string rather than the command's output. ACP clients that read the completed update (the usual pattern) lose the output, and the clipped text isn't valid JSON.

### Repro

fx 0.0.14 (`fx-linux-x86_64`). Start `fx acp`, send `initialize`, `session/new`, then a `session/prompt` such as: run `echo hello-$((6*7))` with your shell tool. Trimmed updates:

```json
{"sessionUpdate":"tool_call","toolCallId":"call_v…","name":"shell","kind":"execute",
 "status":"pending","rawInput":{"action":"run","command":"echo hello-$((6*7))"}}

{"sessionUpdate":"tool_call_update","toolCallId":"call_v…","status":"in_progress",
 "content":[{"type":"content","content":{"type":"text","text":"hello-42\n"}}]}

{"sessionUpdate":"tool_call_update","toolCallId":"call_v…","status":"completed",
 "content":[{"type":"content","content":{"type":"text","text":
   "{\"session_id\":null,\"state\":\"completed\",\"backend\":\"captured\",\"persistence\":\"process\",\"output_truncated\":false,\"output_incomplete\":false,\"output_terminal_safe\":true,\"full_output_handle\":\"fx-command-repl"}}],
 "command_result":{"kind":"command","command":"echo hello-$((6*7))","exit_code":0,
   "stdout_bytes":9,"truncated":false,"output_file":"fx-command-replay-….bin"}}
```

### Expected

The completed update's `content` holds the command's output (`hello-42\n`), with a truncation marker if it's long, and any structured result goes in `rawOutput`.

### Actual

`content` is a JSON object clipped at roughly 200 characters (cut inside `full_output_handle`), without the output. `command_result`, a non-standard top-level field, has the exit code but not the output either. The output only exists in the earlier `in_progress` updates.

### Suggested fix

- Put the (possibly truncated) output in the completed update's `content`.
- Move the structured summary to `rawOutput`, and don't clip JSON mid-string.
- Optionally move `command_result` under `_meta.fx` so it can't collide with future ACP fields.

title: Preserve defined shell helpers in snapshots
body:
Shell snapshots omit every underscore-prefixed function, so a captured wrapper can fail with `command not found` when it calls its helper.

Preserve defined helpers in Bash and Zsh snapshots. Zsh uses the shell's unloaded-function attributes to continue excluding underscore-prefixed autoload stubs; a loaded function containing autoload text remains included. Fx's internal helpers and Zsh's existing prompt exclusions remain excluded. Snapshot reuse and fallback behavior are unchanged.

Fixes #1329, reported by @tomdale.

Validation on macOS arm64 with Zig 0.17.0:

- Four focused Bash/Zsh capture and command-runner regressions failed on the baseline and passed on the candidate.
- Built `./zig-out/bin/fx` exercised a wrapper through `_` and `__` helpers using a local fake Gateway. The baseline shell tool exited 127; the candidate tool exited 0 with the expected output and no child stderr. Both used one startup load and snapshot replay.
- ReleaseSafe build, formatting, public-surface, and diff checks passed. Independent source and evidence review found no blocking issue.

These are preserved local results. Linux and required hosted CI remain pending; live zoxide/conda integrations were not tested.

title: Run libfx host tools when the model pretty-prints their input
body:
## Summary

- On the native libfx backend, a host tool runs when the model sends its input as pretty-printed JSON, instead of the SDK throwing a `SyntaxError` and closing the agent.
- A resumed turn that reruns such a call runs it instead of failing the same way.
- Every JSON-RPC message fx writes over ACP stays on one line, even when a caller passes JSON with line breaks.

Fixes #1215.

title: Test image sessions in a real browser
body:
## Summary

- The browser lane (`test:browser-wasm`) sent images in single prompts but never through a saved session. It now runs three image sessions in headless Chrome against the core WebAssembly build:
  - a durable session on `memory()` whose three turns carry 12 MiB of images, three times what a 4 MiB checkpoint holds;
  - an engine that records to a `createMemoryPersistence()` store with a Blob image, reopened in a new engine that sends the image again;
  - a request the provider refuses with a 413, sent again without the oldest image.

## Tests

- `node sdk/tests/test-core-browser.mjs` after building the core and terminal surfaces: all 9 cases pass, including the new one.
- With `fx-core.wasm` built from c7f5a38af, before sessions saved each image once, the durable case fails: `durable image turn 1 ended error: libfx journal is too large`.

title: Add a seeded simulation of long libfx sessions
body:
## Summary

- Adds `sdk/tests/sim/`, a seeded simulation of long libfx sessions that runs on request, not in CI. `sdk/AGENTS.md` gets a row with the commands.
  - `engine.mjs` runs engines that record to a store through plans of image prompts (bytes, Blobs and base64), tool turns that pause and resume, prompts libfx must refuse, cancels, and crashes between and during turns, with store faults and a provider size limit. After each step it checks what each model request carries and what the store holds. At the end it reopens the store as it stood after every write and checks that the session opens, resumes, and lost no finished turn. `--backend both` runs each plan on native and wasm and compares them.
  - `durable.mjs` runs `createFxAgent` sessions on two workers sharing one `local()` World, with steers, crashes at a model request or a World write, and failed writes the host retries under the same `messageId`.
  - `budget.mjs` checks that memory and time per turn stay flat as a session's images grow.
  - A failing plan is saved to a file; `--plan FILE --shrink` replays it with steps removed while it still fails.

## Tests

On this branch, after the core builds:

- `engine.mjs`: 60 runs native, 20 wasm, 10 on both backends compared; none failed.
- `durable.mjs`: 20 runs native, 10 wasm; none failed.
- `budget.mjs`, 60 turns of 3.75 MiB images: 4.14 bytes of memory per image byte on native and 3.38 on wasm, under the budgets of 5 and 4; late turns no slower than early ones.

title: Keep unit tests from leaking environment and shell capture state
body:
## Summary

- Test fixtures that install their own environment now reset it on teardown, so the commands later tests run inherit the test runner's environment instead of an empty one.
- `zig build test` no longer fails 12 command runner tests on machines whose shell profile reads `$HOME`.
- The zsh timeout test now waits for the shell capture it starts, so the capture can no longer write into memory a finished test already freed and crash a later test.
- A new test fails when an earlier test leaves an empty environment behind.

title: Answer unknown tools and malformed arguments on Chat Completions connections
body:
## Summary

- On a Chat Completions connection, a call to a tool fx didn't offer is answered with `Unsupported tool: NAME` and the turn continues, instead of failing with `InvalidToolName`.
- A call whose arguments aren't a JSON object is answered with an error the model can correct and doesn't run, instead of ending the turn with `InvalidToolArguments`.
- A valid call in the same step still runs when another call in that step is rejected.
- In `fx acp`, a direct call to an MCP tool the session hasn't loaded runs, as it does on AI Gateway.
- The automatic permission reviewer retries once when its decision names the wrong tool or has malformed arguments, instead of holding the action without a retry.

Part of #1340. This doesn't change the ACP update for unsupported tool calls that the issue also reports.

title: Deflake file approval decisions in tui-permissions tests
body:
`tui-permissions.test.ts` sends `1` as soon as a file approval's text appears. fx ignores an affirmative choice until the review frame settles and logs `file_approval_confirmation_blocked` when it does, so an early key was dropped and the test timed out after 30s.

`decide` now waits for fx's answer after each key and resends only after a block. A resend can't answer a later approval. `launch` traces the `permission` scope and registers each session's trace path in a `WeakMap`, which is how `decide` finds it.

```ts
await session.sendKeys(String(choice));
// read only trace lines written after the key
if (added.includes("event=permission_decision")) return; // accepted
if (added.includes("file_approval_confirmation_blocked")) break; // resend
```

`file approval keeps fragmented mouse scrolling inside the review` also waits for the first turn to finish before it sends its second prompt, matching the resized-approval test. In CI that prompt was sometimes lost while the first turn was still streaming. I couldn't reproduce the loss locally, so a product bug in mid-turn input isn't ruled out.

**Merge danger:** two-way door, limited to `tests/e2e/tui-permissions.test.ts`.

title: Remove the MCP v1 client
body:
## Summary

- Every MCP server runs on the new engine, and the `FX_MCP_ENGINE` switch is gone.
- `fx mcp` and `/mcp` take only `list`, `show`, `add`, `remove`, `login`, `logout`, `approve`, and `reject`. An old command shows their usage, `fx mcp path` points to `fx mcp list`, and `/mcp`'s help lists the new commands.
- The model no longer sees the `mcp_features` tool.
- In libfx's WebAssembly terminal, `/mcp` says MCP servers are unavailable there, since the embedding app provides MCP tools.
- A subagent can use its parent's MCP servers before they finish starting.
- ACP tool calls to MCP servers keep their server and tool identity, live and after `session/load`.
- A shell subagent keeps an MCP tool it selected on its next request.
- Starting a server, renewing its login, and restarting it each have a time limit, and a malformed reply fails its request instead of hanging.
- HTTP answers that aren't JSON or an event stream, and sign-in metadata that isn't JSON, are refused.
- `fx mcp login` asks the server where to sign in and which scopes it needs before it opens the browser.
- A scope step-up is saved with the login.
- A question that no screen can show is answered cancel, so the server goes on.
- A stdio server that fails to start says why, with its exit code and its last stderr lines.
- A stdio server inherits only `HOME`, `LOGNAME`, `PATH`, `SHELL`, `TERM`, and `USER` from fx, plus its own `environment` entries.
- A server's `startup_timeout_ms` and `operation_timeout_ms` take effect. `required` and a `restart_limit` other than the default do nothing, and `fx mcp list` notes each one.
- Progress notes from a running MCP tool show in `fx ask` and on the shell's working line.
- Event streams that end lines with CR or CRLF no longer hang.
- 2025 servers that annotate their tools with headers keep those tools.
- A failed tool-list refresh keeps the last list, and each page of a list expires on its own.
- After a server changes its tools, fx lists them again before the next call and refuses a tool that's gone.
- When a 2025 server answers a call with "open this URL first", fx asks to open each URL, waits up to 10 minutes for the server to confirm them, and calls again. Retry and Cancel stay available while it waits.
- `fx slack`'s help names `fx mcp login`.
- Sign-ins made with the old client aren't carried over, so each remote server needs one new `fx mcp login`. The old store, `~/.fx/mcp-credentials/credentials.json` or the Keychain item `FX_MCP_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS_V1`, is left as it is and can be deleted by hand.

Stacked on #1327. Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#195.

title: Load public CA roots when macOS denies Keychain access
body:
Gateway catalog and model requests fail in a macOS sandbox that denies reads of `/Library/Keychains/System.keychain`. Zig's certificate scan reads both the public system-root store and this protected Keychain, then aborts on `PermissionDenied` even though `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` is readable.

Load the public CA bundle when the normal macOS scan returns a permission denial. Use the same initialization for Gateway requests and connection warming, preserving the pool's certificate-clock synchronization. Certificate verification stays enabled; an unreadable or empty fallback fails closed. Custom CA certificates installed only in Keychain are unavailable in the fallback, as documented in the README. Other scan failures retain the existing failure behavior.

Validation:
- ReleaseSafe macOS arm64 build with Zig 0.17.0.
- 84 focused HTTP-pool and imported shared-module tests pass, including simulated Keychain denial and denial of both trust sources. The fallback regression fails with `CertificateBundleLoadFailure` when the fallback is removed.
- Freshly built current-main runtime (head `9b9a6bf9`) initializes an ACP session, fetches 260 authenticated Gateway models, and returns the exact requested `fx-main-tls-ok` response under a deny-default sandbox that still denies System Keychain reads. Stock releases 0.0.13 and 0.0.14 fail this scenario.
- A backport to the 0.0.13 runtime also passes real model requests through a packaged embedding host: file writes wait for approval, an approved write completes, a denied write stays absent, pending-approval and active-turn cancellation complete, and a client-hosted browser MCP call returns the page title after approval. These host checks are separate from the current-main build evidence.
- Native TLS probe using the backport: valid Gateway HTTPS succeeds; a local self-signed server is rejected; denying both trust sources refuses initialization.
- Formatting, public-surface audit, and `git diff --check` pass. The focused suite also compiles for x86_64 Linux (not executed on this macOS host).

Hosted CI is blocked by the first-contributor approval gate: CI run 39205784286 and macOS run 39205784174 both report `action_required`. An upstream maintainer must approve these workflow runs; this draft is not yet ready for review. Suggested classification: `type: bug` (maintainer label access required).

title: Record unsupported tool calls as rejected
body:
## Summary

- ACP clients get a final `failed` update for a call to a tool fx doesn't have, instead of the call staying pending after the turn ends.
- `fx ask --json` lists those calls in `tool_calls` with status `error`.
- The `/trace` report counts those calls as rejected.

Fixes #1340. The issue suggests finishing these calls inside ACP. This records them through the rejection hook that every other refused call already uses, so `fx ask --json` and `/trace` get them too. Two existing tests asserted the old omission and now expect the call.

title: Tell the model where attached images are saved
body:
## Summary

- The model now sees where each pasted, dropped, or attached image is saved, so its tools can open the image without searching the disk for it.
- The note names the session's saved copy of the image, not the file it was attached from.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#204.

title: Stop requests from waiting on an unreachable address
body:
## Summary

- Requests reach a server through an address that answers when another of its addresses never does, as on networks that advertise IPv6 but drop it (#1172). Before, fx waited on the unreachable address and repeated "Network interrupted · ConnectionSetupTimedOut" until the turn stopped.
- `fx`, `fx ask`, and `fx acp` connect the same way regardless of the CPU count or how many MCP servers, requests, and other tasks fx is running.
- When no address answers, fx still reports `ConnectionSetupTimedOut` and retries on the same schedule as before.

title: Model-check closing and resuming model requests
body:
## Summary

- Extend the recovery model to the durable save before every send, torn records, every way a request ends, fx's stop for unclear failures and its Fast lookahead, late outcomes, and compaction, plus a timed model for the wait cap and the countdown.
- Add a model of closing and resuming a request across process exits, whose `today-*` configs reproduce today's resume bugs: "quit unexpectedly" after closing the window, the sticky question, asking after one death, resending a paused turn, and EOF cancelling.
- Require every planted defect to break only its own rule.
- Add a driver that checks `recovery.zig` against every transition of its model and must reject a planted defect; CI runs it in Build & Test.

Stacked on #1339.

title: Resume a model request after fx is closed
body:
## Summary

- Closing the terminal window, or sending fx SIGHUP or SIGTERM, during a model request no longer reports that fx quit unexpectedly. The next launch sends the request again without a question.
- A single crash or kill also resends the request on its own. When the same request has crashed fx twice, fx asks instead: "This request crashed fx twice, so it was not resent."
- fx asks before resending a request interrupted more than a day ago, or a turn with no request in flight, such as one an error stopped or a crash during a tool.
- Sending "continue" after a relaunch now includes the interrupted prompt. It used to start a turn without it.
- "Resuming the interrupted request" and "compacting, then retrying" show the elapsed time.

ACP and `fx ask` keep their current handling, and a follow-up covers them.

## Docs

vercel-labs/fx-web#205 updates the Sessions and Troubleshooting pages.

Stacked on #1358.

title: Keep diff counts visible on long grouped edit rows
body:
## Summary

- Grouped edit and write rows that are too long for the terminal now shorten the path and keep the `+N / -M` diff counts at the end of the row.
- On terminals too narrow to fit the counts, rows are clipped from the end as before.

title: Save the request on a close in ACP, and cancel it in fx ask
body:
## Summary

- `fx acp` now saves the request in flight on SIGHUP, SIGTERM, or the end of stdin, instead of dying mid-request or cancelling it.
- When a client loads that session, fx reports the request as `interrupted`, adding `need: "crash_loop"` when the request crashed fx twice so the client can ask first. `continueRecovery` resumes it.
- `fx ask` cancels on SIGHUP, as it does on SIGINT and SIGTERM, so a closed terminal no longer leaves a checkpoint behind.
- A new ACP prompt after a restart now includes the interrupted turn. It used to start without it.
- Plain `fx` shows "Interrupted turn · fx -c to continue" when the session `fx -c` opens still has an unfinished turn.

Hosts that embed the server, such as libfx, keep their current shutdown.

Stacked on #1359.

title: Remove unused subagent helpers
body:
## Summary

- Remove the session store's unused subagent bootstrap-metadata and control-session-ID loaders, along with the types and preference readers only they used.
- Remove the unused child permission admission check and its test.
- Fix the subagent entry in the context inventory, which named a function that no longer exists. It now names the path the code takes.
- No behavior changes.

title: Walk the fx TUI along the resume model in tmux
body:
## Summary

- Add `tests/tla/drivers/resume/driver.ts`, which runs the built fx through tmux along `Resume.tla`, one process at a time: launches, messages, finished responses, closes, kills, quits, "continue", and a day passing.
- After every step, the files fx keeps, the request on the wire, and the question it asks at launch must match a state the model reaches. `--self-check` reruns one walk with a planted wrong expectation that the driver must reject.
- It runs on request, not in CI: a full walk is 181 walks and takes about half an hour. `--walks` and `--grep` run a subset.
- `Resume.tla` now lets a new message or a quit answer a question, as fx does. Every config keeps its expected verdict.

Stacked on #1361.

title: Save v2 prompt images as blobs the model can open
body:
## Summary

- Each pasted, dropped, or attached image is saved once in the session's blobs folder when its turn starts, before the first request, and the model's note gives that file's path.
- The saved prompt names the image's blob instead of also storing the image as base64.
- Images in a v1 session become blobs the same way when the session converts.
- Resumed and forked sessions read an image from its blob when a request, the vision tool, or a recall needs it, instead of loading every image when the session opens.
- A saved prompt that names a missing image blob marks the session as damaged, as a missing piece blob does.
- A damaged image blob no longer stops the session from opening. fx checks each image against its digest when it reads it.
- An image the session can't save stays in the prompt as before, and the model gets no path for it. Without a saved session, as with `--no-save`, notes and notices name no file.
- Prompts saved before this change read as they did.

title: Recover Codex, Grok, and custom provider replies that stop mid-stream
body:
## Summary

- A Codex, Grok, or custom connection reply that sends nothing for 10 minutes after it starts is now ended and retried, as AI Gateway replies already are. Before, the turn waited until it was cancelled, and `fx ask` and subagents waited forever.
- A Codex or Grok error response whose body stops arriving is also ended after 10 minutes.
- Custom connection requests finish about 10 ms sooner, since the connection watch no longer restarts when the response starts.
- Requests with their own deadline, such as permission reviews, keep their current timeouts.

title: Stop MCP-v2 from sending calls on closed HTTP connections
body:
## Summary

MCP-v2 sent calls on pooled HTTP connections that the server had already closed. The call failed before it reached the server, and fx reported `the server went away. The tool may have run.` This change sets `keep_alive = false` on both v2 request paths, as the v1 engine already does.

## Cause

`Client.run` and `Client.fetchRun` in `src/mcp/io/http.zig` call `std.http.Client.request` with the default `keep_alive = true`. The client's pool hands back an idle connection without checking it. Servers and load balancers close idle connections. Vercel's edge closes them after about 340 seconds, so the first call after a quiet stretch goes out on a closed socket. The v1 engine sets `.keep_alive = false` on every request in `src/core/mcp/streamable_http.zig`, so it does not hit this.

## Reproduction

1. Add a remote MCP server hosted on Vercel to `~/.fx/mcp.json` with `"type": "http"`.
2. Start fx with `FX_MCP_ENGINE=v2` and call one of the server's tools.
3. Wait six minutes, then call it again. The call fails with `the server went away. The tool may have run.`, and the server never receives it.

## Tests

- The fixed-length one-shot connection tests in `tests/e2e/mcp-http.test.ts` also run with `FX_MCP_ENGINE=v2`. Their fixture answers one request per connection and never closes it, so a reused connection gets no answer. Without this change both v2 cases hang until the 20 second timeout. With it they pass, and every request carries `Connection: close`.
- The fixture declines `subscriptions/listen` with JSON-RPC error `-32601`. v2 sends that request and v1 does not.
- `bun test mcp-http.test.ts`: 43 pass. `bun test mcp-auth.test.ts -t "MCP-v2 login"`: 10 pass. These cover `fetchRun`.
- `zig fmt --check src/` passes.
- `zig build test` on macOS arm64: 10,354 pass. Two tests fail locally in code this change does not touch: the `assistant_stream` OSC 8 rendering test and the `command_runner` startup-file snapshot test.
- With the built binary, `FX_MCP_ENGINE=v2 ./zig-out/bin/fx mcp show <server>` against a live Vercel-hosted server reports `ready` with empty stderr. A v0.0.14 build with this change completed a tool call after a six-minute idle against the same server. The same call failed without it.

## Trade-off

Each v2 request now opens a new connection, as v1 requests already do. That adds a TCP and TLS handshake per call. Retrying once on a stale pooled connection would avoid the handshake, but a retried `tools/call` can run a tool twice when the first request did reach the server.



Fixes #1367.

title: Bug: MCP-v2 HTTP calls fail after an idle period with "the server went away"
body:
### Issue details

With `FX_MCP_ENGINE=v2`, the first call to a remote HTTP MCP server after a few idle minutes can fail with:

```
MCP server '<name>' ended the call: the server went away. The tool may have run.
```

The server never receives the call.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Add a remote MCP server hosted on Vercel to `~/.fx/mcp.json` with `"type": "http"`.
2. Start fx with `FX_MCP_ENGINE=v2` and call one of its tools. The call succeeds.
3. Wait six minutes and call the tool again.

Expected: the call reaches the server, as it does with the default engine.

Actual: the call fails with the error above.

`Client.run` and `Client.fetchRun` in `src/mcp/io/http.zig` use the `std.http.Client` keep-alive pool, which hands back an idle connection without checking it. Vercel's edge closes idle connections after about 340 seconds, so the next request goes out on a closed socket. The v1 engine sets `keep_alive = false` on every request. #1366 applies the same setting to v2 and adds a deterministic test that fails on `main`.

Reproduced with fx 0.0.14 on macOS arm64.

### Trace

_No response_

### Sensitive information

- [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

title: Read only new entries from durable session logs
body:
## Summary

- A durable session on a World reads only the log entries written since its server last read the log, back to the newest checkpoint among them, instead of the whole log and its checkpoint on every read.
- A prompt run in the request that took it starts its worker from the log its sender just read, so the worker no longer reads the log again before taking its lease.
- A read whose listing skipped a slot keeps no view past it, so a write the World lists late is read once it shows. The worker reads the log itself when its sender's read skipped a slot or another write landed before the sender's input.
- Every read still returns its own copy of the entries, so code or a tool that changes what it read does not change later reads or saved checkpoints.
- In a 40-turn chat, a turn starts after 7 serial World calls instead of 11, and the wait to start no longer grows with the conversation.

title: Stop capping native libfx model requests at 8 MiB
body:
## Summary

- Native libfx sends model requests larger than 8 MiB instead of failing the turn with `HostStreamBackpressure`, as the WebAssembly backend and the CLI already do.
- A native session that grows past 8 MiB keeps working instead of failing on every later turn.
- When a provider refuses a native request as too large, the agent leaves out the oldest images, or compacts the conversation at most once for that request, then retries.
- Native requests with images are fitted to the same 30 MiB default as the WebAssembly backend and the CLI, or to the lower limit learned from a provider's refusal, instead of leaving out their oldest images to fit 8 MiB.
- The native addon frees each request body once Node has taken it, instead of keeping up to 8 MiB between requests.

title: Run oversized durable steers as their own turn
body:
## Summary

- A durable steer with more than 64 KiB of text ends the running turn at its next safe point and runs as the next turn, the way a steer with images does. It used to wait for the running turn to finish.
- Two such steers sent close together each run as a turn of their own, and the session keeps taking prompts. Before, every delivery failed, the queue retried without end, the next prompt failed, and `close()` did not return.
- A durable harness can refuse a steer by throwing from `steer()` or rejecting its promise, and the steer runs as the next turn. A thrown refusal used to fail the delivery and run the step it cut off a second time.

title: Refuse durable deliveries that reach the wrong agent
body:
## Summary

- A queue delivery that reaches an agent other than the one its input was sent through is refused: it runs nothing, queues nothing, and the agent's `onEvent` gets `session.refused` with the reason `"misrouted message"`. Before, a forged delivery naming another agent made that agent queue a second copy of the message for the session's owner.
- A prompt sent through another agent's session object is still sent on to the session's owner by the agent it was sent through.

title: Correct how soon Vercel continues a crashed durable turn
body:
## Summary

- The libfx README now says that if the invocation Vercel runs again after a crash also exits, the next delivery waits for Vercel Queues' hold on the message to run out, up to five minutes. It used to say only that the delivery runs again about a second later, which holds for the first exit.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#206
Upstream: vercel/workflow#4927

title: Show shell output in ACP's finished tool update
body:
## Summary

- ACP clients see what a `shell` command printed in its completed or failed update, instead of a clipped JSON status object.
- Output longer than the 200-byte preview, or output the shell already cut, ends with `... output truncated ...`.
- Shell calls replayed by `session/load` show the same output.
- libfx `tool_end` events for shell calls carry the output instead of the JSON.

Fixes #1345. `command_result` stays where it is, and no `rawOutput` is added.

title: Require a model for Codex and Grok libfx agents
body:
## Summary

- `createFxEngine()` with `provider: "codex"` or `provider: "grok"` and no `model` now throws `provider "grok" needs a model; fx's default model is an AI Gateway id`, instead of sending the AI Gateway id `spacexai/grok-4.7` to the plan's API and failing with a 404.
- A durable Codex or Grok session with no model, from the agent or from `agent.session(id, { model })`, now ends with that error before any request is sent.
- The TypeScript types require `model` on Codex, Grok, and custom-provider engines.
- The SDK README says Codex and Grok agents need a model the plan serves, such as `grok-4.7`.

title: Send images to models the catalog lists with vision
body:
## Summary

- Images from tools and attachments now reach models the model catalog lists with `vision` but without `file-input`, including the default `spacexai/grok-4.7`, instead of being withheld with a note to use the vision tool.
- libfx host tools that return images to those models now get the images to the model; before, the images were dropped.
- Those models are no longer offered the vision tool, since they read images directly.
- When image support is unknown at the start of a turn and the catalog answers during it, the request's image route, vision tool, and tool image notice all follow the new answer. Before, one request could mix the old and new answers.
- A request with attached images and unknown image support now gets the turn's catalog check before it fails, so a catalog that has recovered is used.

title: Stop rerunning a step that keeps crashing its worker
body:
## Summary

A durable session stops running a step once the deadline has cut it off three times in a row. A step that crashes its process instead, such as a call that runs it out of memory, was run again after every crash. Each delivery took the session over and ran the step again, and on Vercel, where one process serves several invocations, the sessions beside it died each time too. That went on until Vercel Queues gave up on the message, which can take a day.

A worker that takes over a lease its holder never released now counts that takeover as one cut-off of the open turn's step, toward the same bound of three. After three cut-offs in a row, by crashes, deadlines or both, the step isn't run again: a call is answered as possibly run, even for an `idempotent: true` tool, and a model request ends the turn, cancelled. A session that shares the process loses its worker in each of those crashes too, and they count toward its own three.

## Changes

- `sdk/durable.js`: the fold counts a `lease` entry that takes over an unreleased lease from a different holder as a cut-off. A holder renewing its own lease takes nothing over. The rest of the guard already existed for deadline cut-offs.
- `tests/tla/sdk/DurableSession.tla`:
  - `Claim` counts the takeover when `CrashCuts` holds.
  - The new `RunsBounded` invariant bounds how often a write starts.
  - `HandoffsBounded` now says that no worker heading the chain runs a step past the bound. A worker that knows the step is spent can still crash before it acts, so the count itself can pass three.
  - A call answered as possibly run now moves the model's chain, as the record it writes does in the code. Without that, the model let a claim made on an older read run the answered call again.
- New `DurableSession-crash.cfg` and `Witness-NoCrashBound.cfg`, wired into `check.sh`; every other config sets `CrashCuts = TRUE`.
- `tests/tla/drivers/drive.mjs`: a `crash` graph, run in CI with seed 6.
- `sdk/README.md`, `sdk/types/libfx.d.cts` (`session.deadline`'s `cutoffs`), and `sdk/AGENTS.md`.

## Tests

- `test-durable-core.mjs`: a fold test for takeovers, renewals, releases and step changes. It fails on `main`.
- `test-durable.mjs`: three child processes in turn are killed while an idempotent lookup runs, and the fourth worker doesn't run it again; the model hears it may have partly run. It fails on `main` (the call runs a fourth time) and passes on native and wasm.
- `bun tests/tla/drivers/drive.mjs crash --walks 20 --seed 6` fails on `main` at walk 13, where a takeover and two deadlines cut off a model request and the old code asks the model again. With this change it passes on native, wasm and `--durability world`. Five of the seed's 20 walks reach the bound.
- TLC: every `DurableSession` config passes, and every witness is reached. The deeper configs, `MaxEpoch` 4 and 5 with three freezes (2.2M and 13.6M states), were also checked once locally. They pass, but are too large for the driver.
- The SDK durable-session batch from `sdk/AGENTS.md` passed.

The crash graph adds about two minutes to the SDK job's model-check step.

## Docs

Companion: vercel-labs/fx-web#207, which adds the same paragraph to the durability page and updates the `session.deadline` row.

title: Finish ACP tool calls a cancel stopped before they ran
body:
## Summary

- After a cancel, a tool call that never ran gets a final `failed` update reading `Cancelled`, instead of staying pending in the ACP client.

The ACP spec asks clients to mark unfinished calls cancelled. fx already sent a final update for the call that was running, so it now does the same for the calls it skipped.

title: Show a running command's recent output in ACP progress
body:
## Summary

- While a shell command runs, ACP clients see its most recent output, up to 200 bytes starting at a whole line, instead of only the newest line.

Updates still go out once per output chunk, so a very chatty command still sends many of them.

title: Keep pastes when input arrives right after them
body:
## Summary

- Keep a bracketed paste in the draft when another key reaches fx in the same read as the paste's end marker. Before, fx discarded the whole paste and showed "Paste was not applied because extra input followed its end marker."
- Ignore the input that arrived right after the paste and show "Input that arrived right after the paste was ignored." An Enter pressed while a large paste is still arriving no longer drops the paste, and pressing Enter again sends it.
- Keep refusing to run input that follows an end marker embedded in pasted text, so a crafted clipboard still cannot run a command or submit the draft.
- Apply the same behavior when pasting into approval amendments, question answers, and sign-in code entry.

title: Finish ACP tool calls a turn leaves open
body:
## Summary

- When a turn ends with a tool call still open, ACP clients get a final `failed` update for it instead of a call that stays pending. Before, only a cancelled turn did this.
- The case this fixes in practice: a provider web search starts streaming, the connection breaks, and recovery gives up. The prompt returned `refused` and the search stayed pending.
- The text follows the terminal transcript's wording for the turn's outcome: "Cancelled", "Tool failed", "Tool state preserved for recovery", or "Tool completion was not reported".

## How

The core calls `finalize_turn` once per turn and sends no tool events after it. The terminal transcript closes its open rows there. ACP's `finalizeTurn` now does the same, and the cancel-only sweep at the end of `handlePrompt` is removed, so there is still one sweep. A yielded turn is not finalized and keeps its cards open, as before.

## Testing

- New unit test for the outcome-to-text mapping, and the existing cancelled-turn card test still passes.
- New ACP E2E test "ACP finishes a provider search the turn ended before it finished": fails on main (the search gets only `pending`), passes here.
- `bun test acp.test.ts` (176/176), `bun test web-search-fake-gateway.test.ts` (18/18), `zig build test`.
- Ran `./zig-out/bin/fx acp` against a fake Gateway: the broken search now ends `failed`; length-limited steps, cancelled subagents, and cancelled turns behave as before.

title: Clear the previous session's usage when a new session starts
body:
## Summary

- Clear the footer's context usage on `/new` and `/clear` when fx can't save sessions, for example when `~/.fx/sessions` is a symlink.
- Start the new session's token and web search totals at zero in that case, as they already do when sessions are saved.

title: Return parse-error guidance for user-profile shell commands
body:
## Summary

- A user-profile shell command with a quoting or syntax error returns the parse-error `retry_guidance` in zsh and bash.
- A zsh `tty` command with a quoting or syntax error returns the same guidance when the error is its only output.
- A bash 5.2 command with an unclosed quote returns the guidance. bash 5.2 no longer follows `unexpected EOF while looking for matching` with a `syntax error` line.
- For bash, sh, and dash, the guidance now says other lines may already have run, because those shells run a command line by line. zsh keeps the guidance that nothing executed, because it parses the whole command first.
- zsh guidance is given only when the parse error is the command's only output, including output an earlier `running` result already returned. Any other output means something ran, such as an `eval` in a startup file or in the command, so the guidance is left out instead.
- A zsh `[` or `test` failure such as `parse error: condition expected` no longer gets parse-error guidance, because the command keeps running after it.

title: Keep words that start with = literal in zsh commands
body:
## Summary

- zsh commands run to completion when they contain an unquoted word that starts with `=`, such as an `echo ======` separator or the `==` in `[ "$a" == b ]`. This covers user-profile, clean-profile, and `tty` commands.
- A `setopt equals` in the user's startup files no longer applies to these commands. A command that runs `setopt equals` itself still gets zsh's `=command` expansion.
- The shell tool description no longer tells the model to quote words that begin with `=`.

title: Compact the conversation when a restarted reply is refused as too long
body:
## Summary

- A reply that was cut off and restarted now compacts the conversation and retries when the provider refuses the restart as too long, instead of failing the turn with HTTP 400.
- A turn resumed from its saved checkpoint after a crash or pause gets the same recovery.

title: Keep a steer typed during a Stop hook in the same turn
body:
## Summary

- A steer submitted while a Stop hook runs on a reply that used a provider-executed tool now continues the same turn, instead of ending it as interrupted.
- A steer that waits while a Stop hook allows the reply now continues the same turn, instead of running later as a separate turn.
- After a steer continues the turn, the Stop hook runs again on the new reply.

title: Run every unit test in zig build test
body:
## Summary

- `zig build test` runs the tests in `js_host_clipboard.zig`, `js_host_url_opener.zig`, and `browser_capabilities.zig`. Only the browser build uses these files, so no test build compiled them before.
- `zig build test` runs the approval review benchmark's tests. Before, only `zig build test-approval-review-benchmark` ran them, and nothing called that step.
- `zig build test` and `zig build test-session-manager` also run the session manager's tests with its fault and trace hooks compiled in. That runs 29 tests that fx's build left out and 5 that always skipped without hooks. Shipped artifacts still leave the hooks out.

title: Isolate the status JSON test from the real profile
body:
## Summary

- "fx status --json returns valid status JSON" in `tests/e2e/cli.test.ts` now runs fx with its own profile from `createIsolatedTestHome()`, so it no longer fails on a machine whose `~/.fx/settings.json` uses the dev update channel.
- The test also clears `FX_HOME`, so a profile that `FX_HOME` points to can't leak in either.

title: Review auto mode commands that shells read differently
body:
## Summary

- A quoted or escaped `&&` in an auto mode command, such as `'&&'` or `\&\&`, is now an argument to the command, as it is to the shell, instead of a separator between two separately checked commands. `git fetch '&&' git status --prune` now goes to review instead of running.
- Auto mode sends a command to review when one of its words starts with an unquoted `#`, which every shell reads as the start of a comment.

title: Bound how much git config one load reads
body:
## Summary

- fx reads a repository's git config itself to list files for `@` completion, `glob_files`, and `grep_files`. A config that includes itself a few times made fx read it about a million times, so memory grew by gigabytes and the file tools never answered. Opening fx in such a repository was enough.
- One config load now reads at most 64 files and parses at most 1 MiB. Past either limit, the file listing is marked incomplete and safe git refuses the repository, as it already does for config fx cannot read.

title: Review git fetch options that run programs in auto mode
body:
## Summary

- In auto mode, `git fetch` runs without review only when every option is a known flag, such as `--tags`, `--all`, or `--depth=<n>`. Any other option goes to review.
- `git fetch --upload-pack=<command>`, which makes git run that command, now goes to review instead of running, including abbreviations such as `--upl=<command>`.
- `git fetch --filter=<spec>`, which turns a full clone into a partial clone, now goes to review instead of running.
- Abbreviated prune options such as `--prun` now go to review too, as `--prune` already did.

title: Remove the 64-tool limit on libfx agents
body:
## Summary

- Agents take more than 64 tools through the `tools` option of `createFxAgent()` and `createFxEngine()`.
- `createMcpAdapter()` keeps every tool a server lists, across up to 64 pages, instead of failing with "MCP listTools() returned an invalid tool catalog" once a server lists more than 64 tools.
- The "invalid tool catalog" error now means only that `listTools()` returned something other than a list of tools.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#209

title: Review auto mode commands with zsh extended glob characters
body:
## Summary

- In auto mode, a routine command with a `^` or `#` in a word now goes to review instead of running.
- When a user's zsh startup files turn on `extendedglob`, fx replays that option, and zsh reads these characters as glob patterns: `^x` matches every file not named `x`, and `x#` matches any run of `x`. A file in the workspace could then supply the words a routine command received. For example, `git fetch ^x .` could expand to a file named `--upload-pack=<command>`, and git would run that command.
- Commands such as `npm install react@^18` also go to review now, even when the `^` is quoted.

title: Add a fuzz build step, nightly fuzzing, and shell parity tests
body:
## Summary

- `zig build fuzz` builds only the fuzz tests listed in `tests/fuzz/targets.json`. `-Dfuzz-target=<name>` picks one target, and `--fuzz=N` searches for new failing inputs.
- `zig build test` replays each target's saved inputs from `tests/fuzz/corpus/<target>/` on every pull request.
- A nightly Fuzz workflow fuzzes every target for about 20 minutes. A failure uploads the failing input and opens or updates the issue `Nightly fuzz failure: <target>`. A pull request that changes the fuzzing setup, like this one, fuzzes each target for two minutes.
- The shell parity tests run every command form fx runs without review through sh, dash, bash, and zsh, with and without `extendedglob`, and check that each one runs exactly as fx parsed it. The new `shell_parity` target checks generated commands the same way. The Linux unit test job requires every shell, so a missing one fails the tests instead of skipping them.
- Stream targets for the Chat Completions, AI Gateway, and Responses readers. Each one cuts generated reasoning, text, and a tool call into events at generated points, reads them back in pieces of generated size, and checks that the result matches exactly.
- A `terminal_grid` target feeds generated terminal output to the terminal engine and checks that output split into reads of any size reaches the same state, that checkpoints restore exactly, and that the screen shows each frame after its repaint diff.
- A `transcript_paint` target streams generated assistant text and transcript writes into the real transcript runtime while it resizes the terminal, settled or debounced. After every frame it checks that the runtime's model of the terminal shows the same rows and cursor as a terminal fed the bytes fx wrote.
- New targets for the command lexer and classifier. The lexer target checks token positions, agreement with `pipe_segments`, and that values survive being lexed again in single quotes. The classifier target checks that the base command it reports matches the lexer for a simple command.
- Web fetch targets. `url_policy` checks that an admitted URL reads back the same, has a request target and host that can't break the request line or authority, has only a public literal address, and that `std.Uri` sees the same host and port. Followed redirects keep the host and port. `http_response` checks that a response reads the same however its bytes are split, and that Content-Length, chunked, and close-delimited bodies decode exactly or fail only for size.
- An `acp_jsonrpc` target checks that every ACP frame is one line of JSON that carries its id, method, message, and payload, and that the line reader gives the same lines and overflows for any read size.
