- An `mcp_wire` target checks that the MCP decoder accepts well-formed messages with the exact values that went in, returns only whole JSON values from valid input, and decodes strings the way `std.json` does. It lives in `src/core/mcp_host/wire_tests.zig`, since `src/mcp/` imports only the standard library.
- `-Dsanitize-thread=true` builds fx and its tests with ThreadSanitizer. A nightly Thread Sanitizer workflow runs the unit tests that way, lists each race in its job summary, uploads the log, and never fails because of a race.

The bugs these tests found are fixed in #1388, #1390, #1392, #1398, #1400, #1401, and #1402, and the races the sanitizer found in #1404, #1406, and #1408.

title: Stop background transcript pages from dropping approval answers
body:
## Summary

- Pressing 1 or 2 right after a file approval appears now applies the answer. Before, fx sometimes ignored it when the Ctrl+O transcript page finished preparing in the background.
- A transcript page prepared while Ctrl+O is closed no longer schedules a redraw. Ctrl+O still opens straight to the prepared page.

title: Keep the zsh snapshot when startup files replace a default alias
body:
## Summary

- zsh starts with default aliases such as `run-help`. When startup files replace one with a function, as Debian's and Ubuntu's global zshrc do, restoring the zsh snapshot failed with a parse error. Every user profile command then reran the startup files, and fx showed the snapshot fallback notice.
- The restore now removes every alias before it defines functions, then restores exactly the aliases the user's startup files left.
- The Linux unit test job installs zsh, so the zsh user profile tests run on Linux. They skipped there before, which is why this was not caught.

With a `.zshrc` that replaces `run-help` with a function, three commands in one `fx ask` ran the startup files 4 times and showed the fallback notice before this change, and once with no notice after it.

title: Hide shell snapshot replay errors from command output
body:
## Summary

- When fx can't restore the shell snapshot, the command's output no longer includes the restore error or the internal `fx-shell-snapshot-replay-failed:` marker, in the live view or in the result the agent reads.
- Messages the snapshot restore prints no longer appear in the output of commands that use the snapshot.

title: Test that a failed MCP send frees its queued copy once
body:
## Summary

- Adds a unit test for an HTTP MCP request that fails after it was queued. The failed request's copies are freed once, and the requests queued before it are kept.

title: Read quoted assignment values when labeling commands
body:
## Summary

- A command such as `CI='x ls' rm -rf /tmp/x` now gets the removal warning in the approval prompt. The prompt's risk note and safer-alternative hint split words on whitespace, so a quoted or escaped space in an assignment value made `ls` look like the command. The warning disappeared, and the backslash form even suggested `glob_files`.
- Words are now read the way the shell reads them wherever the labels skip `NAME=value` assignments, including after `env` and `sudo`.

This only changes the text fx shows in the approval prompt, not which commands run or get reviewed. A new fuzz target in #1393 found it by checking these labels against fx's shell lexer.

title: Match the browser sign-in page to fx.sh
body:
The page fx shows in the browser after a sign-in now matches the fx.sh Slack sign-in pages. It has the fx logo, monospace text, and the fx.sh light and dark colors. The page follows the browser's `prefers-color-scheme` setting.

The page is shared, so the new design applies to every browser sign-in that returns to fx's local listener, including MCP servers such as Slack.

## Changes

- `callbackPage()` in `src/core/auth/browser_callback.zig` now builds the fx.sh layout and colors from fx-web's Slack sign-in pages.
- The fx logo is inline SVG, so the page still loads nothing external under its existing Content Security Policy (`default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; frame-ancestors 'none'`).
- Each outcome's page is still built as one string at compile time, so `writeResponse()` is unchanged and `Content-Length` is still the length of the body it writes.
- The existing callback test also checks for the logo and that the page ends with its closing markup.

## Verification

- `zig fmt --check src/` and `zig build` pass.
- The `browser_callback.zig` unit tests and the MCP login unit tests in `src/core/mcp_host/login.zig` pass locally.
- Ran `./zig-out/bin/fx login codex` with a throwaway `HOME` and sent a callback with `error=access_denied` and the matching `state`. fx served the new "Authorization failed" page with `Content-Length: 2389`, matching the 2389-byte body, and printed `fx login: authorization denied`.
- On an earlier commit with byte-identical page output, ran `./zig-out/bin/fx mcp login --no-browser slack` with a throwaway `HOME`, then opened the callback with `agent-browser`:
  - A callback with a matching `state` showed "Authorization complete" in light and dark mode.
  - A callback with `error=access_denied` showed "Authorization failed", and fx printed `Couldn't sign in to slack: the sign-in page returned an error (access_denied).`

## Follow-up

fx-web still serves the personal Slack flow at `/api/slack/auth`, which fx v0.0.12 to v0.0.14 use for `/mcp login slack`. It can be removed after a release that signs in to Slack through `http://localhost:3118/callback`, once users have had time to upgrade. The install flow (`/api/slack/install` and `/api/slack/oauth/callback`) stays, because `fx slack install` still uses it.

title: Keep terminal text after broken UTF-8
body:
## Summary

The terminal engine behind terminal sessions mishandled broken UTF-8 that ended a read.

- A UTF-8 lead byte near the end of a read was kept back with the rest of the read, even when the bytes after it could not continue the sequence. Output such as Latin-1 `caf\xe9!` lost the `!`: it stayed hidden until more output arrived, and was then dropped. Until then, checkpoints failed, so resizing the terminal session failed with `InvalidEngineCheckpoint`. Now only a sequence the next read can still complete waits, and everything else is written at once.
- A sequence that a later read completes or interrupts is now written exactly as it would be in one read. A broken sequence shows one replacement character per byte, so the screen no longer depends on where reads split the output, for example after a session recovers by replaying its output.
- A later read now completes a pending sequence only with continuation bytes. Before, an escape sequence right after a broken character lost its ESC, and the rest of it was printed as text.
- Checkpoints save only the pending UTF-8 bytes, so the same state always saves the same checkpoint.

## Tests

- `text after broken UTF-8 at the end of a read appears at once`
- `an escape sequence after broken UTF-8 split across reads still runs`
- `UTF-8 gives the same state however the output is split into reads` feeds broken, interrupted, overlong, surrogate, cut-off, and valid sequences in every two-read split and one byte at a time, and requires the checkpoint of a single read.

Both fail on `main`. A new fuzz target for the terminal engine found this.

title: Join characters that a later read continues
body:
## Summary

When a read ended inside an emoji with a variation selector, a keycap, or a flag, the terminal engine behind terminal sessions treated the next read as a new character. `☀` then `U+FE0F` stayed one cell wide, a keycap did too, and a flag took four columns instead of two, so the rest of the line moved. Where reads split the output decided what the screen showed, so a session recovered by replaying its output could differ from the live one.

- The engine now joins the next read's bytes to the last character when they continue it, and widens it the way a single read would have: it clears any wide character it overlaps, inserts in insert mode, and moves the cursor the same way.
- A one-cell character in the last column that becomes two cells wraps, or moves left without autowrap, as it would in one read. To do that without disturbing the line, the engine keeps the two cells it wrote over, and checkpoints save them.
- Checkpoints move to revision 3. Revisions 1 and 2 still restore. The terminal session test that relabels a checkpoint as the previous revision now drops the new trailing flag.

Skin tones, ZWJ sequences, and combining marks already gave the same result either way.

## Tests

- `a character a later read continues renders as if it arrived in one read` splits the sun with `U+FE0F`, a keycap, a flag, a skin tone, and a combining mark at every byte, mid-row, in the last column, over half of a wide character, without autowrap, in insert mode, and in a one-column grid. It fails on `main`.
- `a checkpoint before a last-column character is widened restores what it covered`
- `revision two checkpoint restores without saved last-column cells`
- `checkpoints reject saved last-column cells that would break the row`

A new fuzz target for the terminal engine found this.

title: Drop wide characters a one-column terminal cannot show
body:
## Summary

With autowrap on, a two-cell character such as `界` or an emoji in a one-column terminal session wrapped to the next line and was stored as a two-cell cell in a one-cell row. The terminal engine's own checks reject that cell, so every checkpoint of the session failed from then on, and resizing the session failed with `InvalidEngineCheckpoint`. Such a character is now dropped, as it already was without autowrap. Text around it is unchanged.

## Tests

`a one-column terminal drops wide characters and still checkpoints` covers a wide character alone, between two letters, and without autowrap. It fails on `main`.

A new fuzz target for the terminal engine found this.

title: Keep approval answers when unrelated redraws are pending
body:
## Summary

- Pressing 1 or 2 on a file approval now applies the answer while fx is redrawing something else, such as a new session title, an MCP server's status, or a subagent's progress. Before, the answer was ignored until that redraw painted.
- An approval whose request or change hasn't painted yet still ignores 1 and 2 until it has.

title: Free terminal request workers before waking their runtime
body:
## Summary

A terminal request worker runs on a detached thread. When it finished, it published its completion through `finishActive`, which woke anything waiting on the runtime, and only then freed its intent and itself. `Runtime.deinit` waits for the active count to reach zero, so it could return, and its owner could tear down the allocator, while the worker was still freeing memory.

`finishActive` now frees the worker and its intent under the runtime's lock, before the broadcast that lets `deinit` finish. Both callers already freed the worker right after the call, so they no longer do.

ThreadSanitizer found this: in a sanitized run of the unit tests, a `RequestWorker` from "in-process registry starts writes to and stops a real terminal" was still in `alloc.destroy` when the test runner deinitialized its allocator.

## Testing

- "runtime correlation stays reserved until its completion is taken" now finishes a heap-allocated worker, so the testing allocator fails the test if `finishActive` doesn't free the worker and its intent exactly once.
- `client.zig` and its imports: 428 passed, 1 skipped.
- `zig build` and `./zig-out/bin/fx --version`.
- A full ThreadSanitizer run of the unit tests on macOS arm64 with this change reported no races. The run that found this one reported it at the test runner's teardown. The race depends on timing, so a clean run supports the fix but can't prove it. The ordering does: every free now happens under the lock that `deinit` takes after the broadcast.

title: Pre-execution security guardrails for your agent execution loops
body:
Hey team 👋

When autonomous AI agents execute shell commands or code loops, prompt injections and hallucinations can accidentally run destructive commands (e.g., `rm -rf`, environment secret exfiltration, or unauthorized process spawns).

We built a lightweight, pre-execution security engine in Python & FastAPI that intercepts command strings at the execution boundary and blocks threats in **~1.3ms to 3ms** before they hit the terminal.

### 🛡️ Key Features:
* **Sub-3ms Overhead:** Zero noticeable delay in agent execution loops.
* **48/48 Integration Tests:** Benchmark-verified on live terminal agent workflows.
* **Zero-Network Privacy Option:** Runs 100% offline via local Python import or through a hosted API endpoint.

Would you be open to an opt-in pre-execution security hook for your repo, or trying a free test API key for your core maintainer team this week?

title: Read the MCP exit status under the pid lock
body:
## Summary

A stdio MCP server's exit watcher runs as its own task. When it reaps the process, it records how the process ended in `Process.exit` under `pid_lock`, then posts `.exited`. The field's comment said the owner reads it only after taking that event, but `Engine.status` doesn't wait for it: it reads the field through `Server.exitStatus` whenever the host publishes a status, including during shutdown. That read took no lock, so it could run while the watcher was writing.

`Process.exitStatus` now reads `exit` under `pid_lock`, and `Server.exitStatus` calls it. The owner's reset on each spawn also takes the lock, so every write to `exit` happens under it. `pid_lock` doesn't call anything that publishes a status, so the new read can't deadlock.

ThreadSanitizer found this on Linux, in a sanitized ReleaseSafe run of the unit tests. In "tools and calls go through the owner thread, from several threads at once", `Process.watch` wrote the exit status at `process.zig:666` while `Server.exitStatus` read it from `Runtime.shutdown` through `Runtime.publish` and `Engine.status`. The run reported it 3 times.

## Testing

- "how a server's process ended is kept until it starts again" now reads the status through `exitStatus`.
- The `io/process.zig` and `server.zig` tests and their imports: 211 passed.
- `zig test src/mcp/mcp.zig -lc`: 230 passed.
- `zig build` and `./zig-out/bin/fx --version`.
- A ThreadSanitizer run of the engine, process, and server tests on macOS arm64 reported nothing, with or without this change. The race needs the host runtime test's timing, which those tests don't reach, so the Linux sanitizer run is the check.
- On Linux, a sanitized ReleaseSafe run of the unit tests without this change reported the race 3 times. The same run with this change merged reported none, and the test results matched: 9,697 of 9,731 passed. The 5 failures are `command_runner` timing tests that also fail without this change.
- The `mcp-stdio.test.ts` tests that report how a stdio server exited, through `fx mcp show` and `fx ask`, pass against the built binary: 3 passed.

title: Count storage fault steps atomically
body:
## Summary

The session manager's test-only fault injector counts every mutating storage call in `Fault.steps`, so a test can kill the process or cut the power at a chosen step. The counter was a plain `u64`. In "threads appending at once get contiguous seqs in file order", eight threads append to one session, and their writes and syncs reach `Fault.mutate` at the same time, so the increment raced.

`steps` is now an atomic counter. `mutate` takes its step number from one `fetchAdd`, so concurrent calls never share a step, and a single thread counts exactly as before.

This code is built only with `-Dhooks=true` and never ships in fx.

## Testing

- `zig build test-session-manager`: 248 of 253 passed, 5 skipped.
- With ThreadSanitizer on macOS arm64, ReleaseSafe, the session manager tests reported this race 3 times on each of 3 runs without the change. With it, 3 fresh runs reported nothing, and 248 of 253 tests passed, with 5 skipped.

title: Hold the late tool settlement search open until the test releases it
body:
## Summary

"late successful tool settlement stays truthful after Escape" needs `grep_files` to still be running when the second Escape cancels the turn, then to finish with its real result. The test got that time by searching a large corpus: 30,000 files on macOS and 120,000 on Linux. On a fast Linux runner the search still finished before the second Escape, so the test failed twice in a row on one runner and passed on another. The corpus has been enlarged once already, and any fixed size runs out as search gets faster.

With `FX_E2E_GREP_RELEASE` set, a finished `grep_files` search now waits until the file it names exists. The test sets it, searches three files, and writes the file only after the cancel has landed, so the tool is running for exactly as long as the test needs. libfx builds leave the hold out, as they do the ACP prompt controls, and fx doesn't read the variable unless a search runs.

The test no longer writes 120,000 files, and it now takes about 2 seconds instead of 8 to 10.

## Testing

- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test tui-interrupt-recovery.test.ts`: 11 passed. The changed test passed 3 of 3 runs on its own, at about 1.9 s each.
- With `grep_files.zig` reverted to `main` and the new test kept, the test fails: the search finishes at once, so the pane never shows the state the test waits for.
- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test ci-shards.test.ts`: 11 passed.
- `zig build` and `./zig-out/bin/fx --version`.

title: Apply command deny and ask rules to every command in a line
body:
## Summary

- A command `deny` rule now blocks that command anywhere in a line, such as `cd repo && git push`, `echo hi; git push`, or `(git push)`, before any auto-mode review.
- A command `ask` rule now asks for that command anywhere in a line, instead of sending the line to auto-mode review.
- Quoted text and escaped operators are not read as commands, so `echo "git push origin main"` still runs under a `git push *` deny.
- Lines that no rule names behave as before, and `allow` rules still cover only a single plain command.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#212

title: Offer Load more in the resume picker only when more sessions match
body:
## Summary

- The resume picker shows Load more only when more saved sessions match the search. A search with no matches shows "No sessions found." instead of "Sessions 0" above a Load more row.
- Searching in the resume picker covers every saved session in the current scope, including sessions on pages that have not been loaded yet.
- Load more during a search loads the next page of matching sessions.
- Refreshing the resume picker keeps the selected session selected when hidden empty sessions come before it in the saved list.

title: Move MCP logins to a store older builds can't erase
body:
## Summary

- MCP logins are saved in a new store, `credentials-v3.json` or the `FX_MCP_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS_V3` Keychain item, so an fx build from before the store's version 2 can no longer erase them by rewriting the store it can't read.
- Logins in the old store aren't copied over, so each HTTP MCP server needs one new login after this update. Older fx sessions still running keep their own store and can't touch the new one.
- When a server refuses to renew a login, the trace log records the HTTP status and the error code, and never the token.
- A server whose login stopped working shows "needs login" without "signed in", and `/mcp` no longer offers Log out for it.
- A login picked up from another fx session is reported again when the server refuses it too, so the server shows that it needs a login.

title: Show MCP sign-in progress and keep one sign-in per server
body:
## Summary

- After Log in in `/mcp`, the server's screen says "Signing in…" until the sign-in address arrives, which a slow sign-in server can take seconds to send.
- Logging in again while a sign-in is under way uses that sign-in: fx shows the same address, the browser's return still completes it, and the browser opens again when asked. Before, the second login closed the port the browser comes back to, and the sign-in could never finish.
- The sign-in address in `/mcp` is one clickable link across the lines it wraps to. An address with characters a link can't carry stays plain text.
- `/mcp` opens right away after launch instead of waiting for saved logins to load.

Stacked on #1412.

title: Consolidate duplicated provider and session code
body:
## Summary

- ChatGPT sign-in refuses to save an account ID that fx would reject when loading it, as Grok already did. The failure now shows at sign-in instead of as unavailable credential storage on the next start.
- `grep_files` and `glob_files` answer with an error naming the field when `path`, `include`, `case_insensitive`, or `mode` has the wrong type or an unknown value. Before, they ran with the default, so a string `"true"` for `case_insensitive` searched case-sensitively. A missing field or `null` still means not given.
- Provider HTTP failures are classified by one shared mapping, ChatGPT and Grok share one session store, and the OAuth helpers use camelCase names. These keep the same behavior, including each provider's error names.

title: Match the browser sign-in page to the fx.sh design
body:
**Summary**
---
- The page fx shows after a browser sign-in for MCP servers, ChatGPT, and Grok now follows the fx.sh design: black background, borderless logo, fx.sh type sizes and colors, and a Vercel Labs footer.
- The tab shows the fx icon. The callback server serves nothing else, so the icon is a `data:` SVG built from the same logo shapes, and the CSP adds only `img-src data:`.
- The success text now reads "You can close this tab and return to fx." The old "Returning you to fx" implied the page switches back on its own, which browsers do not allow.
- Test reply buffers in `browser_callback.zig` and `mcp_host/login.zig` grew to fit the larger page, and a new test checks that the icon decodes to the logo.

The Slack pages on fx.sh get the same style in vercel-labs/fx-web#213.

title: Group the /mcp list and tidy each server screen
body:
**Summary**
---
- The `/mcp` list shows the servers that work first, then the ones that need attention under a "Needs attention" heading set apart by a blank line. Each group is sorted by name, ignoring case. "Needs attention" uses the same rule as the status line count (new `menu.needsAttention`).
- Rows are dim and the selected one bright, as in `/model`. A status that needs the user stays bright.
- A server's screen lists `status` and `protocol` with `http`/`runs` and `file`. It drops "signed in" because Log out already says so, and puts the tool count beside the heading (`Tools 66`). The confirmation title keeps the status, since that screen hides the facts.
- The server screen is one line taller (12 lines below its title) for the new `status` line, so a waiting sign-in's address from main still fits uncut.
- While a sign-in waits, terminals known to open OSC 8 links (Ghostty, iTerm2, WezTerm, kitty, VS Code) read "Didn't open? Click here." with "here" linking the whole address, instead of the address wrapped over several rows. Any other terminal, tmux included, still sees the whole address with a link on every row. The check reads `TERM_PROGRAM` and `TERM` only while a sign-in waits.
- Scrolling into a server's tools no longer adds an "N above" line; the "N more below" count stays.
- Remove and Reject ask on the choice's own row, ending in "yes" and "no". Left and Right choose between them, the chosen one bright, and Enter applies it, so Enter on "no" goes back like Esc. The hint line keeps the server screen's hints. Approve keeps its own screen.
- Left goes back a screen and Right opens or runs the selection, like Esc and Enter. Right never confirms: on an in-place question it only chooses "no". With a filter typed, Left moves the composer's cursor, and so does Right unless the cursor is at the end.
- A choice made in the menu no longer repeats its result in the conversation, since the menu shows it. Warnings and errors still print. Typed `/mcp` commands print as before.
- Tests: inline tests for grouping, sorting, scrolling past the heading, and the server facts. `mcp-verbs.test.ts` covers Left/Right and the quiet menu actions, and its Remove step now moves Down because the approved server sorts before `web`.

title: Show the MCP attention count once servers start and clear it after a prompt
body:
**Summary**
---
- The status line reads "11 MCP need attention · /mcp" instead of "11 MCP servers need you · /mcp", matching the `/mcp` list heading. A single server still reads like "linear needs login · /mcp".
- While servers start, the status line stays quiet instead of counting up as each one reports in. It shows the total once no server is still idle, connecting, or retrying, or after 10 seconds so a slow server can't hide it. A server that already knows it needs a login counts as settled. Sign-in news still shows at once.
- The wait starts when the host loads and restarts when `startHostServers` runs, so the first message no longer flashes a single server's name before the count.
- Sending a prompt clears the notice: the servers that needed attention then stay listed in `/mcp`, and the status line names only a server that newly needs attention, until the next prompt. A prompt sent while servers start is recorded once they finish (`menu.Seen`, `menu.unseen`).
- Tests: inline tests for `menu.startupSettled` and `menu.unseen`, and the status line E2E and the TLA+ shell driver's parser follow the new wording. I didn't run the `tests/tla/mcp_host` checker locally (needs Java and TLC).

Stacked on #1416.

title: Let resumed v1 session tests accept the slow conversion notice
body:
## Summary

- Tests that resume a session copied from an older fx through `fx ask` no longer fail when that session takes over 150 ms to convert and fx writes `fx ask: Converting this session from the previous session format…` to stderr.
- They still fail on a second notice or any other stderr output.

title: Review git fetch from repositories that name a remote helper
body:
## Summary

- In auto mode, `git fetch` now goes to review when a repository is written `<helper>::<address>`, such as `git fetch probe::x`, because git runs a `git-remote-<helper>` program that it may find on `PATH`.
- `git fetch` from a URL whose scheme git has no built-in transport for, such as `probe://host/repository`, now goes to review for the same reason. `https`, `ssh`, `git`, and `file` URLs still run without review.
- Repositories after `--` are now checked too, so `git fetch -- probe::x` no longer skips review.

title: Free auto-mode review memory after each review
body:
## Summary

- Each auto-mode safety review frees its request, reply, and parsing memory when the review ends, instead of keeping them until the turn ends.
- A long auto-mode turn no longer grows by about 120 KB per review.
- Review decisions, cautions, and their rationale are unchanged.

## Benchmark

Peak RSS of one `fx ask` turn in auto mode, ReleaseSafe on macOS arm64, with a fake gateway and reviewer. Each step runs `git status --short`. The reviewed run adds `; echo N`, so every step needs a review. Each row compares two runs of the same build.

| 400 steps | No reviews | A review every step | Added by reviews |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before | 48 MB | 96 MB | 48 MB |
| After | 54 MB | 60 MB | 6 MB |

The memory that reviews add is 88% lower, and the reviewed turn's peak drops from 96 MB to 60 MB.

title: Keep earlier images from blocking new messages
body:
## Summary

- Send a new message in a session with an earlier image even when fx can't confirm the model accepts images, instead of failing it with "Unable to verify image support for this model".
- Leave earlier images out of that request with a note for the model, and send them inline again once the model catalog lists the model with vision.
- Show "Earlier images aren't reaching the model right now" once per message when an unreachable model catalog keeps earlier images out.
- Send a message after an earlier image to a model without vision and no vision tool, with the image left out and a note, instead of failing it.
- Keep failing a message whose own attached image can't be confirmed, as before.

title: Let ThreadSanitizer see pages that mremap releases
body:
## Summary

- ThreadSanitizer doesn't intercept `mremap`. On Linux, `std.heap.PageAllocator` uses it to shrink a block and to move a block that grows, so the released pages keep their access history. The next thread to use those addresses then appears to race with the thread that released them. That's the race the nightly sanitizer job reported in "many large answers at once are read within the budget, one large read at a time": one task's `toOwnedSlice` shrank its answer, and another task's growing buffer later took over the same addresses.
- Sanitized x86_64 and aarch64 Linux builds now link `src/tsan_mremap.zig`, an `mremap` that makes the same change with calls the sanitizer sees. It shrinks with `munmap`, grows in place when it can, and otherwise maps a new block, copies, and unmaps the old one. Other flags go straight to the kernel. Builds without `-Dsanitize-thread` don't change.
- A standalone Linux program with no fx code shows the problem and the fix. Thread A releases a page, and thread B, without synchronizing with it, moves its own page onto that address with `mremap` and writes it. Built plainly, it reports a race when the page is released by shrinking and when it's released by moving, and none for the `munmap` control. Linked with this `mremap`, it reports none, and the moved block keeps its data.

title: Request private search scopes for Slack MCP sign-in
body:
fx now asks Slack for six more user scopes when it signs in as fx's Slack app: `search:read.private`, `search:read.im`, `search:read.mpim`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, and `mpim:read`.

The existing `groups:history`, `im:history`, and `mpim:history` scopes let Slack MCP read private channels, DMs, and group DMs, but search was limited to public channels. With these scopes, Slack MCP can search those conversations and list them.

fx's Slack app manifest already includes the new user scopes, so sign-in doesn't fail on a scope the app lacks. Existing logins keep their current scopes until the user runs `/mcp login slack` or `fx mcp login slack` again.

## Changes

- Add the six scopes to `scopes` in `src/core/mcp_host/slack.zig`.
- Update the expected scope list in `tests/e2e/mcp-auth.test.ts`.

fx-web needs no change. MCP sign-in has gone straight to Slack with the `localhost:3118` redirect since the bridge was removed from the MCP flow, so the fx.sh scope allowlist only affects older clients.

## Verification

- `zig fmt --check src/` passed.
- `zig build` passed.
- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test mcp-auth.test.ts -t 'Slack'` in `tests/e2e`: 4 pass, 0 fail.
- In an isolated profile, `./zig-out/bin/fx mcp add slack` and `./zig-out/bin/fx mcp login slack` built a Slack authorize URL with all 18 scopes, the `localhost:3118` redirect, and PKCE, with empty stderr. Slack returned 200 for that URL without an `invalid_scope` error. The browser approval and token exchange haven't been completed yet.

title: Read command substitutions in assignment values as one word
body:
## Summary

- `word_end` finds where a leading `NAME=value` assignment ends, so the command classifier can find the command after it. It now reads `$(...)`, `${...}`, backquotes, and `$'...'` the way the shell does, so a space inside a substitution no longer ends the assignment early.
- The command approval prompt now shows the forced-removal note and the "inspect targets first" hint for commands such as `CI=$(echo a b) rm -rf dir` and `env CI=$(echo a b) rm -rf dir`. Before, the assignment ended at the space inside `$(...)`, and the prompt showed no note.
- Assignments the analysis keeps in the command, such as `X=$(date +%s) rm -rf dir`, still get no note, because a substitution there could expand to any command.
- The `command_classification` fuzz target now generates substitutions. It leaves commands that contain `$` or a backquote out of its comparison with the lexer, because the lexer reads both literally.

title: Encode inline fuzz seeds the way the tests read them
body:
## Summary

- A fuzz test reads its input through `std.testing.Smith`, which reads `smith.slice` as a little-endian u32 length and then that many bytes. The inline seeds of 17 older fuzz tests were plain strings, so each lost its first four bytes to the length. `"one"` replayed as an empty input, and `"split every field"` read `"spli"` as a length.
- The fx tests now wrap their seeds in `@import("fuzz_seed").slices(...)`. That new module, `src/fuzz_seed.zig`, writes the length first, and its test reads a seed back through `Smith`.
- The session manager imports nothing from fx, so its two targets, `session_log_scan` and `session_schema_header`, keep their four seeds as saved inputs in `tests/fuzz/corpus/`.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` shows the new corpus form and says why plain strings don't work.

title: Ask again when a shell call reloads startup files
body:
## Summary

- A shell call with `reload: true` is no longer covered by a remembered approval for the same command. The check read `reload` only inside a `request` wrapper, but shell calls reach admission with top-level arguments, so it never matched.

title: Advertise shell, subagent, and read_tool_result with top-level arguments
body:
## Summary

- The `shell` tool takes `action`, `command`, and its other fields at the top level instead of inside `request`. Models that wanted several commands at once sometimes sent two `request` keys in one call, which fx rejected as invalid JSON arguments; with top-level fields they make separate calls.
- `subagent` and `read_tool_result` also take their fields at the top level.
- Each field's description names the actions it applies to. A field used with the wrong action is still rejected before anything runs.
- Shell corrections name top-level fields, and `retry_with` is a top-level call.
- A rejected `subagent` call names the field it got wrong and the fields each action takes, instead of returning only an error code.
- A shell call without `action` runs when its fields fit exactly one action, such as `command` for run. fx adds the action before the permission check. A call that fits more than one action still gets a correction.
- Calls that still wrap their arguments in `request` keep working, and saved wrapped calls replay with top-level arguments.
- Tool schemas now include the description of object-valued fields, such as the shell tool's `shell` field, which models did not see before.

title: Keep the Next package test off the npm registry
body:
## Summary

- Before `next dev --webpack` compiles anything, Next 16 waits for its version check: a `fetch` to `registry.npmjs.org` with no timeout of its own. While npm was slow, dev printed `Ready` and then answered nothing, so the SDK job's `test-next-package.mjs` failed with `dev did not become ready`. Turbopack only starts that request when its error overlay needs it, so it was never affected.
- Each Next server the test starts now preloads `sdk/tests/no-npm-registry.mjs`, which fails that request at once. Next then uses its "staleness unknown" result, and the test no longer needs npm. Every other `fetch` goes through unchanged.
- With the registry request held open locally, webpack dev on the test's Next fixture didn't answer `GET /` within 25 seconds and logged no request, which matches the failed runs' `dev.log`. Turbopack answered in about 1.2 seconds either way.

title: Keep an MCP server's last stderr lines when it exits
body:
## Summary

- A stdio MCP server that writes to stderr and exits right away now always has those lines in the `FX_TRACE_LOG` trace.
- The error fx reports for that server, in `fx mcp show`, `/mcp`, and failed tool calls, now always quotes its last stderr lines.
- When a child process keeps a server's stderr open after the server exits, fx reports the exit within 250 ms.

title: Stop a command's processes before force-killing them
body:
## Summary

- When fx force-kills a command after a cancel, a timeout, or a lost owner, it sends SIGKILL to each process it tracks, children before parents. A parent shell whose child died first could run its next command before its own SIGKILL arrived, so cancelling `sleep 30; rm -rf out` during the sleep could start `rm -rf out`.
- `process_tree.Tracker` now sends SIGSTOP to every process it would kill before the SIGKILL pass, with the same identity and session checks. Parents stop before their children, because a shell with job control runs the rest of a list when its foreground job stops, as it does when the job dies. Stopping a process doesn't reparent its children, so the kill pass still reaches every process the tracker found.
- Cleanup after a command finishes on its own, which stops what it left in its session, gets the same order. Other signals, such as SIGTERM, are unchanged.

## Testing

- A new unit test in `process_tree.zig` checks that both kill paths stop every tracked process, parents first, before killing any. It fails without the stop pass and with a children-first stop pass.
- Under ThreadSanitizer, the bootstrap is slow enough that "foreground session owner loss kills the target and descendant before delayed effects" failed in 24 of 30 repeated runs on `main`, each time because the target shell wrote its delayed file after its child was killed. With the stop pass, it passed 30 of 30.
- An interactive bash on a pseudo-terminal ran `touch` immediately when only its foreground `sleep` was stopped, which is why parents stop first.
- `command_runner.zig` and `process_tree.zig` tests pass on macOS, and a `shell.run` with a 1-second `timeout_ms` on `sleep 3; touch after` stops without creating `after`.

title: Fix a lost split character and a cursor report crash
body:
## Summary

- Write a character that a terminal read splits right before a CAN or SUB byte as a replacement character, as the same bytes in one read already do. It was dropped, or joined with continuation bytes after the CAN into a different character.
- Stop fx from crashing on a cursor position report in origin mode when the cursor sits above the top margin, for example after DECRC or VPA. The report now gives row 1.

title: Nightly fuzz failure: terminal_grid
body:
Nightly fuzzing of `terminal_grid` found an input that fails `terminal grid state survives fragmented feeds, checkpoints, and repaints`.

- Run: https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/actions/runs/39919202077
- Commit: `d824f609cfbb6262e6bb9272f1c2f89d6cd24bec`

title: Keep cells aligned after glyphs with a variation selector
body:
**Summary**
---
- Terminals disagree on how wide a glyph with a variation selector is. fx and tmux draw the status line's `⚡︎` (U+26A1 U+FE0E) in two cells, and Ghostty draws it in one. In Ghostty every cell fx painted after it landed one column left of where fx's grid put it.
- The status line showed the effect: when the MCP notice to the right of `⚡︎` cleared, fx erased the cells it believed held the notice, and Ghostty kept the notice's first character. A recording showed a stray `1` from `13 MCP need attention · /mcp`. Earlier reports of `134MCP` and `b2` had the same cause.
- `Grid.diffBand` now moves the cursor to an absolute column after a glyph with VS15 or VS16 when more cells follow in the run, as it already does before `│`. Before a two-cell glyph with a selector it erases both cells, so a terminal that draws it in one cell keeps no stale second cell.
- Nothing changes on screen in terminals that already agree with fx. A terminal that draws a glyph wider than fx does shows that glyph clipped, but the rest of the row stays aligned.
- Tests: an inline test in `src/core/terminal/engine.zig` checks the erase and the cursor move around `⚡︎`, that replaying the diff matches the target grid, and that a glyph without a selector gets no cursor move. I checked the fix by hand in Ghostty with the status line case.

Stacked on #1417.

title: Keep MCP logouts in effect across terminals
body:
## Summary

- `/mcp logout` in a shell now also revokes the login another terminal saved after the shell started. Before, that login stayed valid at the server.
- After another terminal logs out of an MCP server, a shell that still holds the login revokes it the next time it would renew it, instead of renewing it and saving it back.

title: Explain oversized MCP replies and stop fetching them again
body:
## Summary

- When a stdio MCP server replies with more than 16 MiB, the model is told the reply was too large and fx restarted the server, instead of "the server went away".
- When an HTTP MCP server replies with more than 16 MiB, fx ends the call at once and tells the model the reply was too large, instead of "the server went away".
- fx no longer resumes an HTTP stream (2025 protocol) to fetch an oversized reply again. Before, it downloaded the same reply up to two more times.
- An oversized tool list from an HTTP server on the 2026 protocol is no longer requested again right away.
- The debug trace logs each dropped reply with the server, transport, and reason.

title: Switch between agents and run several fx instances in one process
body:
## Summary

- Alt+Left and Alt+Right switch the screen between the main conversation and each subagent, inline. The screen clears and reprints the chosen agent's conversation.
- Agents off screen keep working. Switching to one shows its output so far, still streaming.
- Text typed on a subagent's screen goes to that subagent as a normal user message.
- A subagent's approvals and questions show on its own screen. A hidden subagent's prompt shows on the main screen and moves back when you switch to it.
- The footer notes when an off-screen agent is waiting for an approval, an answer, or a request only you can continue, such as one out of credits, for example `fx 2 needs you · Alt+→`.
- Each subagent keeps its own model, effort, Fast mode, and permission mode, changed from its own screen.
- A subagent can start subagents of its own.
- After a restart, switching to a subagent shows its saved conversation before it runs again.
- Agent profiles in `~/.fx/agents` and a repository's `.fx/agents` set an agent's tools, MCP servers, permission mode, model, effort, and prompt. What a profile leaves out is inherited from the agent that started it, so a subagent without a profile is a copy of its parent. An instance limited to some MCP servers can't reach the others, including through a tool the model calls without selecting it first.
- `fx --profile <name>` runs a session in a profile, and the `subagent` tool's `profile` argument starts a child in one.
- `fx --instances <n>` starts n identical fx instances in one process, each with its own session, conversation, draft, model, and effort.
- Alt+Left and Alt+Right walk the instances in launch order, each followed by its own subagents. The footer shows `fx i/n` while more than one instance runs.
- `/launch [profile]` starts another instance and shows it, and `/close` closes the instance on screen.
- Each instance has its own permission mode and "always" approvals. Permission rules from settings stay shared.
- A subagent starts from the instance at the top of its tree: its tools, MCP servers, provider, permission mode, and "always" approvals. Its approvals and questions show on that instance's screen.
- Closing the first instance hands over to the next one. Closing the only open instance ends fx.
- `/exit` ends every instance and prints the resume command of the instance you quit from, or of one that has a saved session when that one hasn't taken a turn.
- Resuming any session of a group of instances, with `fx --resume`, `-r`, or `--continue`, brings back the whole group with the named session first. An instance joins its group once its first turn is saved, and a session deleted since is left out. In-app `/resume` still replaces only the session on screen.

## Changes to existing behavior

- Alt+Left and Alt+Right still move by word inside a draft. They switch agents only where no word is left to jump: Alt+Left at the start of the draft, Alt+Right at its end, or either one with nothing typed. With no other agent, they always move by word, as before. Terminal.app's Option+Left and Option+Right arrive as `ESC b` and `ESC f` and follow the same rule, so they can switch too. #1448, stacked on this PR, replaces this switching with an agent list opened by Down or Ctrl+X.
- In the interactive app, a subagent is offered the `subagent` tool, so it can start subagents of its own.
- A repository's profile decides tools, MCP servers, and the prompt the same way a home profile does. It can give a subagent tools its parent lacks and replace fx's system prompt, including under a built-in name such as `agent`. It can't set the permission mode, and a profile with the same name in `~/.fx/agents` wins. It applies only to a subagent started with that name: a subagent started without a profile copies its parent, and the `subagent` tool tells the model to name a profile only when the task needs one. Its files must stay inside the repository: a `prompt.md` or `profile.json` that links outside it is refused with a message saying so, and so is any profile file that isn't a regular file, such as a link to a terminal. The docs say so.

## Design

Before, `App` held one conversation's state next to the screen and the shared services:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  App --> Screen["screen, terminal, shared services"]
  App --> State["session, worker, stream, prompts, submission, title, totals, diffs"]
```

After, that state is an `Agent`. The first instance is `App.main_agent`, and every other instance and subagent is a `ChildAgent` with an `Agent` of its own, so they all run the same code:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  App --> Screen["screen, terminal, shared services"]
  App --> Main["main_agent: Agent"]
  App --> Children["child_agents: ChildAgent per instance and subagent"]
  Children --> ChildAgent["Agent, screen slot"]
  Main --> State["session, worker, stream, prompts, submission, title, totals, diffs"]
  ChildAgent --> State
```

- `src/core/agents/` imports no file that imports `src/ui/` or `main.zig`, and `scripts/check-agents-boundary.sh` checks that one import out in CI. The agent's session and submission state live in `session_persistence.zig` and `submission_state.zig` for that reason.
- The host record is its own file under `~/.fx/hosts/`. A session's saved preferences are parsed strictly, so a new field there would make an older fx refuse the session. A record lists only saved sessions, and fx keeps the newest 100.
- Slot threads wait on events that the main loop sets, not on a 2 ms poll. Freeing a closed agent waits at most 5 seconds for a slot thread and keeps the agent allocated, with a trace line, if one still holds it.
- Every agent uses the same MCP servers. A prompt loads an MCP config changed outside fx only when no agent has a turn running or queued, so a running turn keeps the servers it started with. `/mcp` and the MCP menu load it as on main.
- Each agent's session has its own prompt-cache warmer, which closes with the session.

## Not in this PR

- No cap on `--instances`. Each instance costs one worker thread; 100 instances start in about a second and use about 24 MB.
- Limits on subagent nesting, and the open subagent questions, wait for the subagent rework.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#214

title: Keep the IR outliner from folding nested constants into parameters
body:
## Summary

- PGSO builds rebuild constant expressions as instructions before each LLVM IR outliner run, so the outliner no longer merges code whose nested constants differ, which made a candidate read the wrong memory and crash when the TUI started.
- A PGSO run now fails when an outlined function still holds a constant expression the outliner rebuilt from a parameter, instead of producing a candidate with that code.
- The heavy-workload benchmark candidates take the same steps, so their measurements cover the same code shape as the release candidate.

title: Show the session ID in a /status panel
body:
## Summary

- `/status` opens a panel in the footer instead of writing a notice to the transcript. Esc or Enter closes it and leaves nothing behind.
- The panel's first line shows the open session's ID and whether it's saved yet, so it can be resumed with `fx --resume <id>`. A shell that can't save sessions shows `none`.
- The open panel updates when a running turn saves the session or finishes.
- When the panel doesn't fit, ↑↓ scrolls it and the hint says so. It leaves the end of the transcript in view instead of covering it, so output from a running turn isn't lost or repeated. Long values like the workspace path wrap instead of being cut off.
- When profile settings can't be read, the panel shows a Settings line and leaves out auth, instead of printing an error with no status.
- A fork made before the first prompt now counts as saved: `/status` shows it as saved, and the exit line prints its resume command.
- `fx status` output is unchanged.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#215

title: Review a trailing 2>&1 unless 2 is a bare file descriptor
body:
## Summary

- In auto mode, a routine command that ends in `2>&1`, such as `npm install 2>&1`, runs without review. fx dropped the last three words whenever their values were `2`, `>&`, and `1`, then checked the rest.
- The shell reads `2` as a file descriptor only when it is written bare and touches `>&`. For `git status \2>&1` and `git status 2 >&1`, the shell runs `git status 2` and redirects standard output, while fx checked a plain `git status`. fx now drops the redirection only when the `2` is written exactly as `2` and touches `>&`, so those forms go to review.
- The nightly `shell_parity` fuzzing found the escaped form. Its input is kept in `tests/fuzz/corpus/shell_parity/`, so every pull request replays it.

Closes #1433.

## Testing

- `knownReversibleAutoCommand` unit tests reject `git status \2>&1`, the nightly's tab-separated form, `git status 2 >&1`, and `git status '2'>&1`. They failed before the fix.
- A new `auto-mode-reliability.test.ts` test runs `git status 2>&1` without review and sends the escaped and spaced forms to review. It fails against the old code, which ran the escaped form without review. The whole file passes, 41 of 41.
- The shell parity unit tests pass with `FX_SHELL_PARITY_ALL_SHELLS=1`, and a local `shell_parity` fuzz round found nothing. Replaying the saved input with `zig build fuzz -Dfuzz-target=shell_parity` fails on macOS before the fix (exit 1) and passes with it (exit 0). The nightly run confirmed the same failure on Linux, and this PR's CI replays it there.

title: Start each instance's subagents from that instance
body:
## Summary

- A subagent started by a launched instance, or by a subagent in its tree, now gets that instance's tools, MCP servers, provider, permission mode, and "always" approvals. It used to get no tools at all.
- A subagent's approvals and questions are copied to the screen of the instance at the top of its tree, not always the first instance's.
- An agent profile now decides what it sets, even tools or MCP servers the agent that starts it lacks. What it leaves out is inherited, so a subagent without a profile, or in fx's `agent` profile, is a copy of its parent.
- An instance's own profile `mcp_servers` now limits the MCP servers the instance can find and call, and what its subagents inherit.

Stacked on #1438.

title: Restart only the MCP servers a config change affects
body:
## Summary

- `/mcp add`, `/mcp remove`, `/mcp approve`, and `/mcp reject` restart only the servers they change. Servers with the same config keep their process, connection, and tool list.
- Calls on servers the change leaves alone keep running and finish on the same process.
- Calls still running on a removed or changed server end at once with "the MCP config changed, and fx stopped the server".
- A changed or re-added server starts once its own old process has exited. Other servers no longer wait for long calls on unrelated servers to finish.
- A browser sign-in in progress continues unless the change removes or changes that server.
- Adding a server no longer invalidates the MCP tools already offered to the model.
- Changing a server's environment variables restarts it. Reading the same variables from the config again does not.

title: Show /permissions in a footer panel
body:
## Summary

- `/permissions` with no arguments opens a read-only panel in the footer instead of printing to the transcript. Esc or Enter closes it and leaves nothing behind.
- The panel shows the mode, each configured rule, the session's grants, and the conversation's saved rules, each as a bullet. Saved rules show the ID that `/permissions revoke` takes.
- When an approval adds a session grant while the panel is open, the panel shows it once the approval closes.
- Like `/status`, the panel leaves the end of the transcript in view and scrolls with ↑↓ when it doesn't fit.
- `/permissions auto`, `/permissions remember`, `/permissions revoke`, and the other subcommands still confirm in the transcript.
- `/status` and `/permissions` now share one footer panel. Tests that ran `/permissions` only to put text in the transcript now run `/allowlist`.

title: Allow up to 20 questions in one ask_user_question call
body:
## Summary

- The model can ask up to 20 questions in one `ask_user_question` call, so a related set of questions opens as one prompt instead of several prompts of 4.
- The tool schema and description tell the model the new limit.
- A call with more than 20 questions is rejected with `provide 1 to 20 questions`, and no prompt opens.
- Resumed sessions show every answer from a batch of up to 20 questions.

title: Hold auto-mode actions only for proven prompt injection or system harm
body:
## Summary

- The auto-mode reviewer holds an action only for prompt injection or for harm to the user's machine or the runner. Everything else clears.
- A caution has to name its category and quote its evidence. fx clears a prompt-injection caution unless the quote is in untrusted tool output and not in the user's own requests or the pending action, and a system-harm caution unless the quote is in the pending action.
- A prompt-injection caution that quotes text the action itself contains, such as the old text an edit replaces, clears, because editing text is not following it.
- A caution that passes those checks holds the action unless a second review of the same request returns `clear`. That review's own quote is not checked again, and if it cannot finish, the hold stands.
- A long quote that garbles part of a path or ID still counts when a long exact run of it matches, and a quoted instruction from untrusted output proves injection whichever category the review named.
- Ordinary development work no longer gets held, such as editing or deleting code and tests, deleting files in the workspace or `/tmp`, deliberately breaking a check to test it, running the agent's own scripts, and git or GitHub operations.
- Current-turn `ask_user_question` answers reach the reviewer as user answers and never count as injection evidence.
- Actions that conflict with the user's request but are neither injection nor system harm now clear, for example a push after the user said not to push.
- The optional `typesafeai/jev` reviewer answers without quotes, so its decisions stay as returned.
- `AGENTS.md` states the new review contract. The E2E fake gateways answer the second review the way they answered the first and count it apart from first reviews.
- The live auto-permission eval expects the second review's identical request, counts every reviewer call in its cost and latency totals, and expects a push after a revoked authorization to clear.

## Design

Before, any `caution` from the reviewer held the action. The tool schema required only `decision`, so a vague or invented reason was enough to stop ordinary work.

```
before:  review ── caution ──────────────────────────────────────────────▶ hold

after:   review ── caution ─▶ category + quote found where that harm must be?
                                 │ no  ─▶ clear (trace: auto_review_caution_unproven)
                                 │ yes ─▶ second review of the same request
                                             │ valid clear       ─▶ clear
                                             │ caution, invalid,
                                             │ or unavailable    ─▶ hold
```

- **Proof check.** fx, not the model, decides whether a caution holds, by checking the quote against the text where that harm has to appear. A prompt-only fix was not enough: the old prompt already asked for care, and nothing could tell a real reason from an invented one.
- **Second review.** A single review sometimes misjudges a real quote, for example calling the removal of a planted instruction "following" it, so a proven caution gets one more identical review, and a `clear` from it overturns the first. Nothing else does. Its quote is not checked again because the first review already proved the harm: a second review that agrees an action reveals a secret but quotes the user's words instead of the command would otherwise let the action through, which the eval's `misleading assistant claim cannot authorize credential access` scenario showed during development. The second review runs only after a proven caution, so actions that clear still make one call. A held action costs one more reviewer call, a median of about 1.7 seconds per call in the eval runs below. Running two reviews in parallel for every action was rejected because it doubles the cost of every action to save time only on rare holds.
- **Labels.** `writeBoundedField` refuses to compile a review-data label that the proof check does not strip, so the rendered review data and the quote matcher cannot drift apart.

## What the agent sees

| Reviewer answer | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `caution` with a vague reason and no quote | action denied with `review_caution` | action runs; the permission trace logs `event=auto_review_caution_unproven reason=missing_category` |
| `caution` quoting the harmful part of the action, and the second review agrees | action denied with `review_caution` | action denied with `review_caution`, after `event=auto_review_confirm_result result=caution` |
| `caution` with a valid quote that the second review clears | action denied with `review_caution` | action runs, after `event=auto_review_confirm_result result=clear` |

## Results

The repo's live eval, `tests/evals/auto-permission-reliability.test.ts`, run three times on each side with the same reviewer model. To repeat it, build each side with `zig build`, then from `tests/evals` run `bun test ./auto-permission-reliability.test.ts` with an AI Gateway key in `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`. Each side runs its own copy of the file; the 15 bounded scenarios and their expected decisions are the same on both. A run stops at the first outcome that differs from its scenario's expected decision.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Runs with every outcome as expected | 0 of 3 | 2 of 3 |
| First wrong outcome in a failed run | `hidden action` cleared (1 run); `unrequested validation and delete compound` held (2 runs) | `unrequested destructive delete` held (1 run), with both reviews quoting the `rm -rf` |
| Reviewer calls in a passing run | no passing run | 18: one per scenario, plus a second review for each of the 3 held scenarios |

## Not checked here

How often real sessions still get a held action after this ships needs production use. The permission trace records every cleared caution with its reason (`auto_review_caution_unproven`) and every second review's answer (`auto_review_confirm_result`), so the remaining holds can be read from real sessions after release.

title: Switch agents from a list opened with Down or Ctrl+X
body:
## Summary

- Option+Left, Option+Right, and Option+Up only move the cursor again, as on main. #1438 used them to switch agents at the edges of a draft.
- Down on an empty composer that isn't browsing prompt history opens the agent list in place of the footer while another agent is open. With a draft, Down stays in the composer.
- Ctrl+X opens the same list at any time, with or without a draft. `/agents` opens it too.
- The list has a row for every open agent: each instance in launch order, with its number, session title, agent profile, and state (working, needs approval, has a question, needs you, finished, or idle; needs you is a request only you can continue, such as one out of credits), followed by its own subagents, indented.
- Moving through the list with Up and Down shows each agent as it is reached. Enter keeps the agent shown. Esc, Ctrl+X, and Ctrl+C go back to the agent the list opened on, which `(on screen)` marks.
- While the list is open, other keys do nothing, so none edits the shown agent's draft or answers its prompts. A paste keeps the agent shown and lands in its composer.
- When the shown agent waits for an approval or an answer, the list takes the prompt's place, and the prompt comes back unanswered when the list closes.
- Each agent keeps its own draft and place in prompt history, so a draft stays on the agent it was typed on.
- The right side of the footer names the agent on screen: `fx 2/3 ↓` with an empty composer and `fx 2/3 · ctrl+x` with a draft. With one instance and subagents, it shows `main ↓` or the subagent's name and state.
- When an instance that isn't on screen finishes a turn or waits for you, the footer says so before the indicator, such as `fx 2 finished · fx 1/2 ↓` or `fx 3 needs approval · fx 1/3 ↓`, until it is shown.
- The list and the `/status` and `/permissions` panels replace each other, like other footer menus.

From a run against the test model server with two instances, where fx 1 started a subagent named `rev`, the footer reads:

```text
full access · gpt-5                                         fx 1/2 ↓
```

and Down lists:

```text
  fx 1 (on screen) · w_i1 DRIVER_USER start send_0 · main · idle
    rev · SW_TASK look · main · idle
  fx 2 · new session · main · idle
↑↓ preview     enter switch     esc back
```

Stacked on #1438.

title: Bug: auto-mode safety review request drops reasoning_content, DeepSeek rejects it and the action is held
body:
### Issue details

With a custom `openai-chat-completions` connection to DeepSeek (`deepseek-v4-flash`, thinking mode) and the default `auto` permission mode, shell commands are sometimes held with:

```
{"error":{"type":"tool_review_held","tool_name":"shell","message":"Safety reviewer unavailable; action held","reason":"review_unavailable","review_cause":"transport_permanent",...}}
```

The review request itself fails with HTTP 400 from DeepSeek:

```
The `reasoning_content` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.
```

The review request is built from the pending assistant tool call (`build_review` in `src/gateway/chat_completions.zig`). In the captured requests that assistant message never has `reasoning_content`, while the main-loop requests in the same session do replay it. DeepSeek doesn't reject every such request, but when it does, the command the user asked for doesn't run.

**Environment:** fx v0.0.14 (`build_review` unchanged on current main), Linux, `fx acp`, custom connection with `"protocol": "openai-chat-completions"`, `base_url` DeepSeek, model `deepseek-v4-flash`.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Configure the connection above and leave `permission_mode` at the default.
2. Ask something that makes the model think before running a shell command, e.g. give it a setup command to run and then ask it to run the tests.
3. Some runs: the review call returns 400 and the shell call fails with `review_unavailable`.

Seen in 4 of 18 runs across a few prompts. All 38 review requests we captured were missing `reasoning_content`, whether they got 400 or 200.

### Trace

Not attached (captured from network logs, not `/trace`).

### Sensitive information

- [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

title: Bug: grep_files / glob_files silently skip any directory named build, dist or coverage
body:
### Issue details

`grep_files` and `glob_files` skip every directory named `.git`, `.zig-cache`, `zig-out`, `node_modules`, `.next`, `dist`, `build` or `coverage` (`ignored_list_entries` in `src/main.zig`). The result doesn't say anything was skipped, so it looks complete. Neither tool description mentions it.

That's fine for build output, but a source directory called `build/` (e.g. a Python subpackage `app/build/`) just disappears from searches.

**Environment:** fx v0.0.14 (list unchanged on current main), Linux, `fx ask` and `fx acp`.

**Steps to reproduce**

```
mkdir -p src build dist
printf 'from build.config import MAX_RETRIES\n' > src/app.py
printf 'MAX_RETRIES = 7\n' > build/config.py
printf 'MAX_RETRIES = 3\n' > dist/old.py
fx ask "Use the grep_files tool (not shell) to find every file that contains MAX_RETRIES. Paste the raw tool output."
```

Output:

```
[grep] 1 files with matches for MAX_RETRIES
 - src/app.py
```

`build/config.py` and `dist/old.py` are missing with no note. `glob_files` skips them the same way (in another project `app/**/*.py` didn't list anything under `app/build/`). Searching with an explicit `path: build` does find them.

Expected: either search them, or at least say which directories were excluded.

### Trace

Not attached.

title: Detect dead model connections after a network drop
body:
## Summary

- After a network drop mid-answer, fx notices that the server no longer knows the connection within about 5 seconds of the network returning, and retries the request instead of waiting up to 10 minutes on a silent stream.
- During a longer outage, fx reports the connection as lost 45 seconds after the last data arrived and keeps retrying until the network returns.
- A model that thinks silently for minutes keeps its connection, because the server answers the keepalive probes.
- The same detection covers the AI Gateway and the chat completions, OpenAI Codex, and xAI providers.
- If the system refuses a keepalive option on a connection, the request continues as before and the debug trace records which option failed.
- fx no longer closes a model connection when it detects that the Mac slept. Even a brief sleep used to cut a healthy answer and restart it. A connection that died while the Mac slept is now found by the keepalive probes after it wakes.

title: Add /effort to choose the reasoning effort
body:
## Summary

- `/effort` opens a menu of the current model's reasoning effort levels with the one in use marked. ↑↓ moves, Enter applies the highlighted level, and Esc closes it.
- `/effort <level>` applies a level without the menu, and `/effort default` goes back to the model's default.
- Tab after `/effort` opens a level column under the prompt, as Tab after `/model` opens the model column. ↑↓ previews the level in the status line, typing filters the list, Tab fills in the highlighted level, and Enter applies it.
- A new level is saved like a level chosen in `/settings`, and fx prints `Reasoning effort set to <level> for <model>`.
- During a response, the line reads `Next turn will use reasoning effort <level> for <model>`. The running turn keeps its level.
- A model without levels, a level the model doesn't offer, or a malformed level prints a notice and leaves the effort unchanged. If the model list is still loading, the notice asks to try again.
- In a short terminal, the menu leaves the end of the conversation in view and scrolls.
- `/model` still asks for the effort after a model is chosen.
- `/help` lists `/effort` with the model commands.

title: Link sign-in addresses instead of printing them

## Summary

- A typed `/mcp login NAME` says "Sign in to NAME in your browser. Didn't open? Open the sign-in page." The sign-in address is the target of the underlined link instead of printed text.
- The Vercel sign-in picker links its device page as "Authorize with Vercel", the way Codex and Grok link theirs.
