title: Bug: HTTPS requests fail when a sandbox blocks access to the macOS system keychain
body:
### Issue details

 ## Environment

 - fx 0.0.15, build `7f2383af7098`
 - macOS, Apple Silicon
 - Provider: Codex subscription
 - fx runs inside an Agent Safehouse sandbox

 ## Steps to reproduce

 1. Run fx inside a sandbox that does not permit reading
`/Library/Keychains/System.keychain`.
 2. Send a prompt to a remote model.

 ## Expected behavior

 fx can make HTTPS requests using trusted CA certificates without requiring the
sandboxed agent and its subprocesses to read the system keychain file.

 Is there a supported way to provide trusted certificates separately, or could fx
support one?

 ## Actual behavior

 The request fails:

 ```text
 system: request failed: CertificateBundleLoadFailure
 ```

 The macOS sandbox log reports that fx was denied access to the system keychain:

 ```text
 Sandbox: fx(16809) deny(1) file-read-data /Library/Keychains/System.keychain
 ```

 I have not tested whether granting read access to the system keychain resolves the
error. I would prefer to keep that file inaccessible to the agent and its
subprocesses while retaining TLS certificate verification.

### Trace

_No response_

### Sensitive information

- [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

- The line shows even when `fx -c` would ask before sending the request again, such as after two crashes or for a request interrupted more than a day ago.

- The check runs after the first frame is on screen, so it does not delay startup.

Stacked on #1476.

title: Skip a new session's admission reads when its first prompt creates the run
body:
## Summary

A new chat's first prompt with a `messageId` read the session's log and UI stream three times before acceptance (two times without one), and every read returned 404 because the run did not exist yet. The in-request worker then read the log once more before taking its lease.

This change skips those reads when libfx can prove they would return nothing:

- The agent remembers the session ids it minted (bounded set). On the first prompt to one of them, `log.fresh()` creates the run first. Only when this call's own `run_created` took the first slot are the viewer-start read, the retry-outcome read and the sender's read skipped: the World creates a run only when none exists, and every libfx write goes through `ensureRun`, so the log and the stream were empty. Otherwise the prompt reads as before, after the same writes.
- A full read that found no run now leaves `covered` at 0, and the run's own creation events advance it only when they land at the very next slot. `newestSeen` is taken after the sender's writes, so the worker can start from the sender's read through the existing `handoffEntries` contiguity check instead of reading the log again.

Persistence before the queue send, the backstop, leases, fencing and acceptance order are unchanged. Follow-up messages take the same path as before.

Replaces #1473, which overlapped these reads. Measured on follow-ups it showed no net gain.

## Historical preview measurements

These are one-off historical measurements from an internal A/B campaign, not a benchmark reproducible from this PR. The deployment, packaging, and analysis scripts are not included here. They are not a performance guarantee for the revised head. The committed tests reproduce the reduction in World reads, not the end-to-end millisecond figures.

12 balanced warm pairs of new chats on Vercel previews, 24/24 prompts complete with no issues. Both sides use SDK packages built from the same source with the same native and WebAssembly engines and World bundles; only `durable.js` and its generated CommonJS bundle differ. The measured `durable.js` is the first commit of this branch; the second commit is a behavior-preserving cleanup from review (one helper for the slot a write returned, and `fresh()` reusing `ensureRun`), with no change to which calls are made or in what order. The third only rewords a comment; its minified `durable.js` is byte-identical to the second's.

| Metric | Baseline p50 | Candidate p50 | Median paired delta | Candidate faster |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 404 reads during admission | 3 | 0 | -3 | 12/12 |
| World calls during admission | 6 | 3 | -3 | 12/12 |
| SDK admission (`prompt.accepted`) | 580 ms | 386 ms | -232 ms | 8/12 |
| Accepted to model request | 177 ms | 120 ms | -34 ms | 8/12 |
| HTTP POST to acceptance | 900 ms | 728 ms | -255 ms | 8/12 |
| Time to first text | 2,289 ms | 2,029 ms | -259 ms | 8/12 |

The delta column is the median of candidate minus baseline within each pair. Restricting to the 9 pairs where neither side hit a new instance gives -235 ms admission, -242 ms POST to acceptance and -233 ms first text. The minted-id hint applied on every candidate prompt. The samples are small, so treat the numbers as descriptive rather than a significance claim.

## Original validation

- `node sdk/tests/test-durable-core.mjs`: memory 55, local 56, world 58, queue 75.
- `node sdk/tests/test-durable.mjs` with native and WebAssembly engines: memory 61, local 58, world 55 each.
- `tests/tla/sdk/check.sh`, plus `drive.mjs` send, lookup, write, cutoff, leased and queue, `drive-intake.mjs` on memory and world, `drive-tenants.mjs` and `drive-agents.mjs`.

New tests (on local, world and queue; the handoff ones on queue) cover the read-free first prompt, retries of the same message, a minted id that another server prompted first, a failed first write followed by a retry, the worker handoff for new sessions with and without the in-band fence, a creation event that does not land at the next slot, and a World that answers `run_created` on an existing run with success at a later slot. Each guard the change relies on (the `made` check, the contiguity check in `passOver`, the zero after an empty read, `newestSeen` after the writes, and the in-band snapshot in `fresh()`) has a test that fails when the guard is removed.

## Review corrections

- The creation-slot test uses an ordinary prompt instead of the order-dependent `omega` fixture. It passes in isolation.
- A deterministic test holds `run_created`, aborts the prompt, verifies that no input is stored or queued, then retries the same message ID and verifies one execution.
- The minted-ID bound is named `maxMintedIds`; its value remains 1024.
- Current local core results: memory 55, local 57, world 59, queue 76. Native and WebAssembly durable suites: 61/58/55 each. Formatting, build, full Zig tests, native fresh-session smoke, isolated regressions and 10 formal graph drivers passed on the corrected head. The shared TLC checker passed, with identical model/config hashes checked before reusing its graphs. CI for this head remains pending.

## Notes

- If a prompt is cancelled while its run is being created, the prompt is not stored and the run stays empty. Before, the run was created later inside `send`, so the cancelled prompt was stored first.
- Image prompts gain nothing: the image write creates the run first, so `fresh()` returns false.
- The conflict path is covered by tests on world-local. On world-vercel it relies on the client's conditional create and its retry, which turns a create that already landed into a 409. The live A/B did not exercise a competing creator.



## Publication status

Published as a draft to run CI on the corrected head. Local gate code checks passed after setting the repo-local identity and resolving the test-run issue, but the gates could not approve exact-head CI before publication. The author explicitly authorized draft publication for CI; this is not merge approval. The final readiness gate must run after required CI succeeds.

title: Keep more std helpers out of line in PGSO builds

title: Stop full-detail loads before fx closes its session store on exit
body:
## Summary

- Quitting fx while the full-detail transcript is still loading in the background no longer crashes with a segmentation fault (exit status 139).

## Quit time

ReleaseSafe builds of this branch and its base, run alternately on the same machine:

| Case | Base | This branch |
|---|---|---|

title: Skip the preload fault case on static Linux builds
body:
The `fault=true` case in `tui-interrupt-recovery.test.ts` makes `fsync` fail by preloading a library into fx, with `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` on macOS and `LD_PRELOAD` on Linux. A static Linux binary has no ELF interpreter, so the library never loads, the fault never fires, and the case fails. Linux release builds and PGSO candidates are static.

The case now skips when `FX_BIN` is a Linux ELF without a `PT_INTERP` program header. macOS and the dynamically linked Linux CI build still run it, so CI coverage doesn't change.

The session manager compiles its storage fault injector only with `-Dhooks=true`, so a release binary has no in-process way to fail this sync. Adding one would put test-only code into release builds of the session store.

## Testing

- macOS arm64, `zig build`: `FX_SOUND=0 bun test ./tui-interrupt-recovery.test.ts -t 'persistence failure'` passes both cases.
- Linux arm64 with a static `aarch64-linux-musl` build as `zig-out/bin/fx`: `fault=false` passes and `fault=true` is skipped.
- The header check returns true for `/bin/ls`, which is dynamically linked, and false for the static fx build.

title: Walk the recovery module along its model, and add a timed model
body:
## Summary

- `tests/tla/drivers/recovery/driver.ts` walks `src/core/recovery/recovery.zig` along every edge of `Recovery.tla`'s state graph, then along seeded random paths, through a small Zig lab, `lab.zig`. After every step the module's phase, attempt, crash count, status, plan and saved record must match the model. CI runs it after `check.sh`.
- `--self-check` plants two module bugs, an immediate resend after a failure and a crash count cleared by a sign-in, plus a wrong expectation. Each must be rejected.
- The walk found one drift. `Recovery.tla` cleared the crash count on any Enter or sign-in, while `recovery.zig` and `Resume.tla` clear it only when the user answers the crash-loop question. The model now matches the code, and its header no longer says fx doesn't save the record.
- `RecoveryTimed.tla` puts the model on a one-second clock. No wait passes the 30-second cap, a status with nothing flowing changes every second, and on a healthy world a request ends within one capped wait and one send. Two planted bugs, an uncapped Retry-After and a frozen countdown, must each be caught.

This rebuilds the two parts of #1358 that still apply against today's module, without its old stop after repeated failures.

## Verification

- `tests/tla/recovery/check.sh`: 24 of 24 verdicts as required.
- `bun tests/tla/drivers/recovery/driver.ts --self-check`: 5,192 walks and 41,075 steps, all matching; both planted bugs and the wrong expectation rejected.
- Before the model fix, the same driver reported 61 mismatching walks, all the crash count after a sign-in.
- `RecoveryTimed.tla` with `HealTicks = 5` fails `HealsWithin`, so `Ceiling + SendTicks` is the tight bound.

title: Add a Linux arm64 PGSO platform
body:
`scripts/pgso/linux.py` builds `aarch64-linux` PGSO candidates on an arm64 Linux host, next to the macOS module from #1492.

Zig links the static musl control with its own `ld.lld`, and a `zig cc` link of the same object picks different inputs and flags. So the control build records Zig's link command (`--verbose-link`), and the instrumented and candidate links rerun it with only the Zig object replaced. The candidate link adds the profile's symbol order and checks the applied order against the link map. The candidate must match the control's ELF layout and contain no profile sections.

Shared code changes:

- New platform hooks for control build flags, recording the control build, the instrumented link, candidate object flags, host OS versions, and the external benchmark control's strip step. macOS keeps its existing commands.
- Benchmark artifacts build for the toolchain's target instead of the default target.
- The corpus links the macOS Keychain into a scenario home only on macOS hosts.

No workflow runs the Linux platform yet. Linux candidates don't pass the startup gate yet, because profile use compiles startup functions for size; a follow-up handles that.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/pgso/tests -t .` passes all 224 tests, including 14 new Linux tests built from real `llvm-readelf` and `ld.lld` output.
- On an arm64 Linux machine, `python3 -m scripts.pgso train --target aarch64-linux` passed every stage, from validation through the full training corpus and profile use. It produced a 6,511,800-byte candidate; the control is 10,821,040 bytes. The candidate runs `--version`, `help`, and `status --json` with empty stderr and writes no profile output. That run used this change on #1492's head, before #1497 added helpers to the outlined list. A rerun on this exact commit is in progress.

title: Send custom connection headers and preserve session resume
body:
Custom OpenAI-compatible connections cannot send the request headers required by endpoints such as OpenCode Go, Azure OpenAI, and Cloudflare AI Gateway. This adds literal `headers` and environment-backed `header_env` while preserving the existing credential and saved-session checks.

This builds on #1198 by **Jay Gupta (@jaygupta17)**. His two original commits are cherry-picked with authorship and `-x` provenance retained, adapted to current `main` and Zig 0.17. The follow-up commits address two reproduced review findings:

- Normalize HTTP header names and sort both header collections before computing provider identity. Reordering equivalent JSON entries or changing header-name casing preserves session resume; changing a literal value or environment slot still rejects implicit resume.
- Restore every environment representation after the request-header unit test, including an initially absent environment, so teardown cannot leave a pointer to the fixture's destroyed map.

Regression coverage exercises reordered and recased headers through the built CLI, rejects changed bindings before sending another request, and restores absent, map, block, raw, and libc environment state.

Closes #1109.

## Validation

- `mise exec zig@0.17.0 -- zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe`
- 15 focused Zig tests passed: configured-provider parsing/binding, environment restoration, and request headers.
- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test configured-providers.test.ts`: 56 passed, 0 failed, 263 assertions.
- A separate `./zig-out/bin/fx ask` loopback smoke received both header types, returned the expected completion, exited 0, and produced clean stderr.
- Zig formatting, public-surface checks, compactor/indexer boundaries, PGSO classification, and `git diff --check` passed.

Full CI and the repository's ship gate remain pending; this PR stays in draft until those checks complete.

## Docs

The manual lives in the private fx.sh repository. The [Custom model connections](https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/custom-model-connections) page needs these changes:

- Add `headers` as an optional object of literal header name/value pairs, and `header_env` as an optional object mapping header names to environment-variable names. Recommend `header_env` for credentials.
- Show a connection using `auth: { "type": "none" }`, `headers: { "x-project": "example-project" }`, and `header_env: { "api-key": "CUSTOM_PROVIDER_API_KEY" }`. Explain that the named environment variable must be set before launching fx.
- Replace the statement that custom request/authentication headers are unsupported. Header configuration cannot replace `accept`, `accept-encoding`, `authorization`, `connection`, `content-length`, `content-type`, `host`, `transfer-encoding`, or `user-agent`.
- Explain that duplicate names and invalid header bytes are rejected, and an unset or invalid environment-backed value fails before sending.
- Document that equivalent header ordering/casing preserves saved-session identity. Changing literal values or environment-variable names changes the connection binding and rejects implicit resume; rotating the value in the same credential environment slot retains that slot's identity.

title: Share one fuzzy matcher across menus and pickers
body:
## Summary

- The `/` menu matches commands and their aliases in any letter case, by every word, and by letters in order, so `/mdl` finds `/model`. On `main`, `/mdl` opens no menu.
- A one-letter `/` query lists prefix matches first, then the other commands that match. On `main` it lists only the commands that start with that letter.
- The `/skills` menu, the `$` menu, and skills in the `/` menu also match by every word and by letters in order, so `fxcommit` finds `fx-commit`. On `main`, `fxcommit` shows "No skills found."
- The Models menu and `/model` suggestions list a model whose own name, after the provider, equals the query before models whose names only start with it.
- The Models, `/`, and skills menus list exact names first, then prefixes, then text anywhere, then every word, then letters in order. Equal matches keep the menu's order.
- `/resume`, the `/mcp` server, tool, and verb lists, `/help`, `/settings`, the `/provider` columns, the effort and speed pickers, and the login team picker keep their order and still show what matches the typed text. When nothing does, they show word and letters-in-order matches instead, so `ctx7` finds `context7`, `perms` finds `/permissions`, and `stline` finds the status line settings. On `main` those three show `No server matches "ctx7"`, "No commands found.", and "No settings found."
- A query of more than 64 characters, such as a pasted paragraph, still matches only where it appears as typed, as every menu does today, so a long paste stays fast.

## Before and after

Before, each menu matched with its own code, so the same query behaved differently from one menu to the next.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Models menu and /model"] --> a["matchModelQuery, fuzzyModelScore"]
  B["/ menu"] --> b["completionCommandMatchRank"]
  C["Skills menus"] --> c["skillMatchRank"]
  D["/resume"] --> d["session_catalog matchesQuery"]
  E["/mcp lists"] --> e["matches, toolMatches, runtimeArgMatches"]
  F["/help and /settings"] --> f["helpCatalogSpecMatches, settings tokenMatches"]
  G["Provider, effort, speed, and team pickers"] --> g["label and team substring filters"]
```

After, each menu describes its items as fields and asks one engine. Ranked menus sort by how well each item matches, and filtered menus keep their own order.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Models menu and /model"] --> R["fuzzy_match.Ranking"]
  B["/ menu"] --> R
  C["Skills menus"] --> R
  D["/resume"] --> F["fuzzy_match.Filter"]
  E["/mcp lists"] --> F
  H["/help and /settings"] --> F
  G["Provider, effort, speed, and team pickers"] --> F
  R --> M["fuzzy_match.match"]
  F --> M
```

None of the existing matchers could be extended to the other menus. The Models menu's matcher splits words at every non-ASCII byte and knows only model ids, and `fuzzyModelScore` matches when any one word appears, which suits picking one model but floods a filtered list. `fuzzyModelScore` stays for subagent model overrides, which rely on its score bands.

title: Show a file's control bytes as text in diffs and saved edits
body:
## Summary

- Opening Ctrl+O on an edit no longer makes fx exit with `AnsiBandOverflow` when a nearby line holds a terminal escape sequence such as a screen clear. The sequence shows as text, for example `\x1b[2J\x1b[H`.
- C1 control characters such as U+009B now show as `\u{009b}` in diffs instead of reaching the terminal, which some terminals read as the start of an escape sequence.
- Editing a file that contains invalid UTF-8 no longer fails the session save and stops the turn. The invalid bytes show as `\xNN` in the edit preview and in Ctrl+O, live and after resume.
- Sessions saved by earlier versions that hold such lines now open safely in Ctrl+O too.
- Tabs and CRLF line endings in diffs look the same as before.

title: Bug: Shell snapshot misses edits to $ZDOTDIR/.zshrc when ZDOTDIR isn’t exported
body:
### Issue details

If `~/.zshenv` sets `ZDOTDIR` without `export`, fx never notices edits to `$ZDOTDIR/.zshrc`. It keeps replaying the snapshot it captured at startup, so changes made through fx's own shell tool don't show up in later commands. `${ZDOTDIR}` is also unset inside the commands fx runs, even though a real login zsh has it set

This is separate from the known limitation in #1329 (it covers edits to a file your startup files source. Here `$ZDOTDIR/.zshrc` is a top-level startup file that zsh reads directly and it still isn't watched


## Repro

Needs zsh, since `print -r` is a zsh builtin.

```zsh
d=$(mktemp -d); mkdir $d/zd
print -r -- "unset ZDOTDIR; ZDOTDIR=$d/zd" > $d/.zshenv
print -r -- 'export MARK=v1' > $d/zd/.zshrc
cd $d

# zsh itself handles the unexported form fine:
ZDOTDIR=$d zsh -lic 'echo "param=$ZDOTDIR mark=$MARK"'
# => param=/tmp/.../zd mark=v1

ZDOTDIR=$d fx ask --auto --no-save --json "Run these as three separate shell tool calls. Wait for each result before making the next call. Call 1: echo \$MARK  Call 2: echo 'export MARK=v2' > $d/zd/.zshrc  Call 3: echo \$MARK"
```

Call 3 should print `v2`. On fx 0.0.15 (Ubuntu 24.04, zsh 5.9, gpt-6-luna):

```
Running echo $MARK
v1
Running echo 'export MARK=v2' > ./zd/.zshrc
Running echo $MARK
v1
```

The model rewrote call 2 to a relative path, but cwd is `$d` so it writes to the same file.

The same run in a fresh temp dir with `export ZDOTDIR=$d/zd` prints `v2` on call 3. The `export` is the only difference between the two runs.

## Cause

The capture script collects variables with `env`, which only prints exported ones (`src/core/terminal/shell_resolver.zig:331`):

```
\\/usr/bin/env -0
```

`ZDOTDIR` is picked up from that list (`src/core/terminal/shell_snapshot.zig:708`):

```zig
if (std.mem.eql(u8, key, "ZDOTDIR") and value.len != 0) {
    generation.zdotdir = try alloc.dupe(u8, value);
}
```

and that value decides which directories get watched (`src/core/terminal/shell_snapshot.zig:658`):

```zig
const dirs = [_]?[]const u8{ io_mod.getenv("ZDOTDIR"), io_mod.homeDir(), snapshot_zdotdir };
```

An unexported `ZDOTDIR` shows up in neither `env -0` nor `getenv`, so the directory holding the startup files never makes it into that list. Both lines came in with #1137.

## Does anyone actually skip the export?

`ZDOTDIR` is a shell parameter, so zsh reads `$ZDOTDIR/.zshrc` either way. Kitty's zsh integration carries a comment saying it normally shouldn't be exported, and has code for the case where it is. Ghostty's version started as a copy of Kitty's. Most dotfiles I looked at do export it, so this setup is a minority, but it works fine under zsh.

## Possible fix

Emit `ZDOTDIR` explicitly from the capture script instead of relying on `env`. Happy to put up a PR but would love to know if you'd prefer that narrow fix or something more general for shell parameters.

Tested on commit `d72b46594ca6` (fx 0.0.15), no local changes


### Sensitive information

- [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

title: Shrink the libfx native addons
body:
## Summary

- Each `@libfx` platform package's native addon is 0.5 to 0.8 MB smaller. Like the fx executable, it's now built without unwind tables, stack canaries or stack probes. It stays `ReleaseSafe`, with its safety checks.
- Unlike the fx executable, the addon keeps its frame pointers. Apple's arm64 ABI requires them, and crash reports and profilers of an app using libfx walk them through the addon. On x86-64 they also make the addon about 0.2 MB smaller.
- The package size check fails when an addon carries unwind tables or has lost its frame pointers.

## Sizes

Local builds of the addon, before and after:

| Platform | Before | After | Saved |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linux x64 | 9,070,104 B | 8,315,744 B | 754,360 B |
| Linux arm64 | 7,723,296 B | 7,118,336 B | 604,960 B |
| macOS arm64 | 7,618,528 B | 6,994,608 B | 623,920 B |
| macOS x64 | 8,825,927 B | 8,346,563 B | 479,364 B |

Keeping the frame pointers costs nothing on macOS arm64 and 30,880 B on Linux arm64. Without them, macOS's `sample` walked only 1 of the 7 addon frames on an agent thread waiting for the Gateway, and with them it walks all 7, as on `main`.

#1518, which leaves fx's built-in tools out of the addon, is stacked on this PR.

title: Keep a tool result's time when fx rebuilds the turn
body:
## Summary

- Long agent turns use less CPU. An unchanged turn now rebuilds to the same bytes, so fx no longer parses every earlier tool result again on each step. In a paired 1,000-step turn against a local fake gateway, fx used 50 to 59 percent less CPU than `main`, on ReleaseSafe and Debug builds.
- Each tool result keeps the time fx took it. Before, every rebuild stamped it again, so a saved result had the time its line was written, a few milliseconds later. A libfx turn resumed from its checkpoint, and a turn written afresh after a real change, now keep each result's original time.
- With `FX_TRACE_LOG` set, the session trace gets one `sessions_v2_stream` line for each stream and commit decision. It counts the earlier results that had to be parsed again, which should stay 0.
- The session log format does not change, and older and newer fx read each other's sessions.

## Testing

- `zig build test` runs a new agent runtime test. It checks that an ordinary tool result and a committed file write are each stamped where they enter the turn, and that later requests and the saved turn keep that time. It fails when either stamp is removed.
- `tests/tla/session/TurnStream.tla` models how a turn streams, compacts, recovers, and is rewritten. `tests/tla/drivers/session/stream.test.ts` runs `fx ask` turns that TLC checks against the model, including that no rebuild parses a result again.
- To repeat the CPU comparison, build `main` and run the driver's long turn against both binaries. The test reports `cpuRatio`, this branch's CPU time divided by `main`'s.

```bash
FX_TLA_STRESS_STEPS=1000 FX_TLA_BASE_BIN=/path/to/main/zig-out/bin/fx \
  bun test ./tests/tla/drivers/session/stream.test.ts -t 'step turn is a behavior'
```

title: Fix MCP call timeouts and false truncation notices
body:
## Summary

- MCP calls wait up to 5 minutes for an answer or a progress update before fx stops waiting, up from 60 seconds, so browser tools such as Aside's `repl` can finish long scripts.
- When fx stops waiting, the model is told that the server did not answer within its operation timeout and to raise `operation_timeout_ms` for that server if it needs longer, instead of `Cancelled`.
- Servers an editor supplies over ACP get the same timeout message without the setting, which they cannot change.
- `capability_search` marks each tool whose schema it loaded with `schema_loaded: true` and no longer calls its shortened description truncated, because the loaded schema carries the whole description.
- A tool whose schema was rejected or did not fit the schema budget still gets the truncation marker and notice.
- Search results list each tool description once. The duplicate `purpose` field is gone.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#228

title: Add fx mcp call to run MCP tools from shell commands
body:
## Summary

- Add `fx mcp call TOOL [JSON | -]`, which runs one of the session's MCP tools from a command the shell tool runs and prints only the tool's data, so the command can save a large result to a file or filter it before anything reaches the model.
- Check each call against the same permission rules, prompt, and automatic review as a direct call of that tool by the agent that ran the command, including a subagent.
- Accept a call only while the shell call that started the command is running. Anywhere else, `fx mcp call` exits 3 and says why.
- Return results whole instead of cutting them at the model's 64 KiB limit: up to 16 MiB, or 8 MiB when the tool returns text.
- Print structured content that is only a `result` string, as FastMCP servers such as DeepWiki wrap a tool's text, as that text, so a saved file holds the document rather than a JSON wrapper.
- When standard output is a file or a pipe, write one line to standard error with the result's size and shape, including the values of short text fields that repeat, such as a status. The model can then filter the file without first inspecting it. Unique values such as titles and IDs never appear.
- Add `fx mcp call list SERVER`, `fx mcp call search QUERY`, and `fx mcp call help TOOL`. They print the tools the agent may use, one per line, or one tool's arguments and description, with no permission check, as `capability_search` has none. A tool the permission rules deny does not appear.
- Show each MCP call a command makes as its own tool row in the TUI, in the command's group, with the row a direct call of that tool gets: `Running MCP`, then `Ran MCP`, `Failed`, or `Cancelled`.
- Keep a shell call from yielding while one of its `fx mcp call` requests is in flight.
- Keep a permission prompt open when its command exits, and run nothing after it is answered.
- Exit with a distinct code for each outcome: 0 success, 1 failure, 2 usage, 3 no running shell call, 4 too many calls, 5 permission not granted, 6 tool error.
- Tell the model, in the MCP server list on Linux and macOS, to use `fx mcp call` for large or filtered results.
- Make `/mcp call` in the TUI explain that the verb runs only from a command.
- List `fx mcp call` and its `list`, `search`, and `help` words in `fx mcp`'s spec, so shell completion offers them.
- Check the `tests/tla/mcp_call` model in its own workflow, `.github/workflows/tla-mcp-call.yml`, on every push to `main` and on pull requests labeled `ci:tla-mcp-call`.

## Design

Before, an MCP result reached a session only as a tool result, inside the model's context:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  model[Model] -->|MCP tool call| agent[fx agent]
  agent -->|permission check| perms[Permission rules, prompt, review]
  agent --> runtime[MCP runtime]
  runtime --> server[MCP server]
  runtime -->|result, cut at 64 KiB| model
  model -->|shell tool| command[Command]
```

After, a command the shell tool runs makes the same call, and the result goes where the command sends it:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  model[Model] -->|shell tool| shell[Shell call]
  shell -->|registers, gets a token| bridge[Bridge on a private Unix socket]
  shell -->|socket path and token in its environment| command[Command]
  command --> client[fx mcp call]
  client -->|one request line| bridge
  bridge -->|admission, cancel, cleanup| core[Pure core, mcp_call.zig]
  bridge -->|permission check, as a direct call| perms[Permission rules, prompt, review]
  bridge -->|call or lookup| runtime[MCP runtime]
  runtime --> server[MCP server]
  bridge -->|tool row| tui[TUI]
  bridge -->|result| client
  client -->|standard output| file[File or pipe]
```

- The bridge runs inside the session instead of as a client that connects to MCP servers itself. A separate client would need its own logins and settings, and would skip the permission rules, prompt, and review a direct call gets.
- The socket lives in a new 0700 directory with a random name, and each shell call gets its own random token. Only a command a running shell call started can reach the bridge, and only while that call runs. A TCP port on localhost would be reachable by other users on the machine.
- A pure core decides admission, cancellation, and cleanup, so its rules can be checked against the TLA+ model in `tests/tla/mcp_call`. The bridge's sockets only carry out the core's effects.
- The accept loop, each connection, and each call's disconnect watch run as `std.Io` tasks the bridge owns. The end of the last shell call awaits the accept loop and cancels and awaits the connections, so nothing outlives the bridge.
- `list`, `search`, and `help` format the same search pages and tool schemas `capability_search` uses (`src/core/mcp/tool_lookup.zig`), so a command finds tools through the agent's own search.

## Example

Before:

```text
$ fx mcp call mcp_linear_list_issues '{}'
'call' isn't a fx mcp command.
```

After, in a command the shell tool runs:

```text
$ fx mcp call mcp_linear_list_issues '{"assignee":"me"}' > /tmp/issues.json
fx mcp call: wrote 61862 bytes of JSON: {issues: [203 × {title, status: "Fixed"|"Canceled"|"In Progress"|"Done"|"Duplicate", statusType: "completed"|"canceled"|"started"|"duplicate", url, priority, createdAt, updatedAt, id}], hasNextPage: boolean}
```

Outside a shell call:

```text
$ fx mcp call mcp_linear_list_issues '{}'
fx mcp call: no running fx shell call to reach. It works only in a command that fx's shell tool runs, while that call runs.
```

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#229

title: Keep Linux PGSO startup code fast
body:
Stacked on #1502.

Profile use compiles the functions it judges cold for size. On Linux that makes short commands slower than the control: `fx help` failed the startup gate in every Linux run without this change.

This change keeps the startup path fast:

- Training keeps a profile for each of the five direct startup scenarios (`direct-help`, `direct-version`, `direct-status`, `direct-doctor`, `direct-sessions`).
- Before profile use, a first pass applies the production profile, and `ir_size.py minsize-functions` reads which startup functions came out `minsize`. Their records are removed from the production profile. Startup functions that stay hot, those the build inlines away, and those any heavy benchmark runs keep their records. The benchmarks build from the production profile, so dropping the allocator or `Io.Mutex` records slowed `ui-activity` by about 6 points.
- Every startup function is marked `nooutline` (`ir_size.py no-outline`) before outlining, so neither the IR outliner nor llc's machine outliner moves its code into helpers far from the rest of the startup code. Those helpers cost `fx --version` extra page faults.
- The candidate link places the startup functions first, in the order they first run.

macOS has no startup scenarios, so its build is unchanged. Distributed builds don't carry the startup profiles, so they reject Linux.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/pgso/tests -t .` passes all 238 tests. New coverage: `minsize-functions` and `no-outline` against real LLVM, record removal, the two-pass exemption with faked tools, startup profiles kept during training, startup-first link order, and the distributed rejection.
- On an arm64 Linux machine, `python3 -m scripts.pgso all --target aarch64-linux`:
  - With the startup exemption and `nooutline`, training, profile use, the behavior corpus, and the startup gate passed. `help` was 34% faster than the control and `--version` 6% slower, within the 10% limit. `ui-activity` failed at +11.9%.
  - With this commit's narrower exemption, training and profile use passed. The behavior corpus then hit timeouts in `tui-resume.test.ts` while the host was heavily loaded. The same tests pass three of three times against both the control and this candidate on recheck.
- The narrower exemption's gates on a rebuild from the same inputs, run alternately on local disk:
  - The startup gate passed all five commands in 6 of 6 rounds. Median p50: `help` −7.0%, `--version` +1.1%, `status` −7.9%, `doctor` −8.9%, `sessions` −6.8%.
  - `ui-activity` ran +5.3% to +6.7% at p50, against +13.6% to +17.8% with the broader exemption.
- A clean end-to-end run of every gate still needs a quiet Linux arm64 machine. The Linux CI workflow will provide it.

title: Leave fx's built-in tools out of the libfx addon
body:
## Summary

- libfx's native addon no longer contains fx's built-in tools: shell, file, web, skills and the rest. libfx agents never offered them, because the addon runs only the host's tools (`allow_native_tools = false`), so nothing an app sees changes. The addon is about 10% smaller on every platform.
- The addon keeps each built-in tool's name, so an MCP tool's alias still never takes one.
- The fx CLI and the WebAssembly builds keep every tool.

## Sizes

Local builds of the addon on top of #1513, before and after:

| Platform | Before | After | Saved |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linux x64 | 8,315,744 B | 7,458,464 B | 857,280 B |
| Linux arm64 | 7,118,336 B | 6,379,856 B | 738,480 B |
| macOS arm64 | 6,994,608 B | 6,271,856 B | 722,752 B |
| macOS x64 | 8,346,563 B | 7,505,879 B | 840,684 B |

The package size check now fails if an addon contains fx's built-in tools, which the size budgets alone wouldn't catch.

Together with #1513, the addons are 15% to 18% smaller than on `main`.

Stacked on #1513.

title: Start fx balance with the same I/O as fx credits
body:
## Summary

- `fx balance` starts with the same threaded I/O as `fx credits`, including when it reads a stored credential from the system key store.

title: Add a Linux arm64 PGSO workflow
body:
Stacked on #1517.

`.github/workflows/pgso-linux-arm64.yml` builds and qualifies a Linux arm64 candidate with `python3 -m scripts.pgso all --target aarch64-linux` in one job on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`. It uploads the manifest, logs, measurements, and candidate even when a gate fails. It runs on the same pull request paths as the macOS workflow and on dispatch. Distributed builds don't carry the startup profiles that Linux candidates need, so it doesn't shard and has a 345-minute timeout.

`setup-pgso` now installs the Linux tools from pinned, checksummed release archives:

- Zig 0.17.0 through `.github/actions/setup-zig`
- LLVM 22.1.8 (`LLVM-22.1.8-Linux-ARM64.tar.xz`). The release ships no `libLLVM.so`, which `ir_size.py` loads, so the action links one from the release's static archives and checks that it loads.
- Bun 1.3.14, plus tmux and the other packages the E2E corpus uses
- Hyperfine 1.20.0

The macOS steps are unchanged apart from a `runner.os` condition. The `ir_size` tests now load `libLLVM.so` on Linux, so they run there instead of skipping.

The workflow isn't a required check, and releases don't use it yet.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/pgso/tests -t .` passes all 238 tests on macOS arm64 and in an arm64 Linux container with LLVM 22.1.8, with no skips on Linux.
- The CI checks from the PGSO and CI script suites pass: `scripts.tests.test_macos_signing`, `test_signed_macos`, `test_detect_macos_need`, `test_detect_ci_need`, `test_fuzz_nightly`, the corpus listing, `ci-shards.test.ts`, and `shellcheck`.
- `actionlint` reports only the existing `ci.yml` notes.
- The `libLLVM.so` link step and the pinned archives match a Linux arm64 build that trained and qualified candidates in a local VM.
- The full run is this PR's own `Linux arm64 PGSO candidate` check.

title: Tighten a shared ~/.fx at startup instead of skipping its settings
body:
## Summary

- When other users can write to `~/.fx` or `~/.fx/settings.json`, fx removes their write access at startup and loads the settings. It used to skip them.
- The start that makes this change shows a one-line note in the transcript asking you to check `settings.json`. `fx ask` and other commands print the same note on stderr. It no longer counts as a configuration issue.
- Saved prompt history stays available in that case.
- If fx can't change the permissions, for example on a folder you don't own, it still skips the settings as before.

title: Keep a cancelled turn's id so a retried prompt does not run again
body:
## Summary

- Cancelling a turn in a libfx session keeps its turn id, so a host that retries the prompt with the same id gets the ended turn back instead of running the prompt again.
- A cancelled turn is still not resumed when the session reopens, including when saving the cancelled turn fails.

Stacked on #1506.

title: Remove the unreachable stall stop from HTTP status retries
body:
## Summary

- 5xx and 429 responses keep retrying exactly as before. The stall-stop branch on that path, which recovery could never select for a status failure, is removed.

Stacked on #1506.

title: Send a subagent's permission requests to the ACP client
body:
Fixes #1465.

## Summary

Under `fx acp`, a subagent that needs approval now sends its request to the client, and the client's answer goes back to that subagent. Before this change, the child moved to `awaiting_approval` and waited until the turn was cancelled: its request went to the subagent approval registry, which only the terminal app reads.

- While a child's turn runs, the ACP host sends each of its pending approvals as `session/request_permission` on the parent's session. Child sessions are internal and the client never sees them, so the parent's `sessionId` is the one the client can answer on.
- The request names the child in `_meta.fx.subagent`, with the child's `sessionId`, its `workId`, and the child's own `toolCallId`. A request without `_meta.fx.subagent` comes from the parent. `toolCall.toolCallId` is `<child sessionId>/<child toolCallId>`, so it can't match one of the parent's calls.
- The request uses the same fields and options as the parent's own requests: the title, kind, and `rawInput` describe the child's tool call. The registry now keeps that call with its pending approval.
- Several children can wait on the client at once, each with its own request. Each answer goes only to the child that asked.
- Cancelling the turn denies an open request, as it does for the parent's own requests. When a child's turn ends while its request is open, for example because the child was stopped, fx withdraws the request with `$/cancel_request`, and a late answer has no effect.

## Behavior that doesn't change

- Permission policy. Every action still goes through `permissions.zig` and the child's admission first. Only requests that already reached the approval registry are sent, and they are the same ones the terminal app shows.
- `auto` mode. A security review's hold still returns guidance to the agent without a prompt, because a hold never reaches the registry.
- Resume and reload. Reopening a session already marks a child that was `running` or `awaiting_approval` as interrupted, so nothing is left to send. When the child runs again, it asks again and the client gets a new request.
- Questions. Children run with `interactive = false` in every host, so `ask_user_question` never reaches any client from a child. This change covers permission requests only.
- The WebAssembly host, which starts no threads, doesn't forward child approvals.

## Relation to #1132

#1132 adds the experimental `--subagents-v2` tool, which runs each child as a separate fx process, and notes that "in `fx ask` and ACP, a child's prompts don't reach the user yet." This change targets the default subagent tool on `main`, whose children run inside the parent's process. It doesn't touch the v2 code path and doesn't conflict with it. #1088 deliberately leaves ACP and subagent approvals out of scope.

## Verification

- `zig fmt --check src/` and `zig build` pass, and `zig build fx-core-wasm -Dwasm-surface=core` builds.
- `zig build test` on macOS arm64, with a clean `HOME`: 9857 pass, 4 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is the MCP HTTP test "a kept connection the server reset or closed while idle...", which is intermittent locally. It passed on a later run and doesn't touch this code.
- New unit tests cover the request params in `src/acp/permission_requests.zig` and the per-child lookup in the approval registry.
- Three new tests in `tests/e2e/acp.test.ts`:
  - A child's request arrives on the parent's session with `_meta.fx.subagent`, and `allow_once` lets the child write its file.
  - Two children wait on the client at once. Rejecting one and allowing the other writes only the allowed file.
  - `session/cancel` with a child's request open sends `$/cancel_request` for it, the prompt ends `cancelled`, a late `allow_once` changes nothing, and the server answers the next prompt.
- On a build of `main` without this change, all three tests hang until the 30-second timeout.
- All 5 subagent tests in `acp.test.ts` pass. The full file run locally had 14 MCP and session-load failures. Running those tests against a build of `main` without this change failed 6 of them, and running them again on this branch failed 5, with a different subset failing each time. CI's Linux run is the gate for those.
- Ran `./zig-out/bin/fx acp` with a temporary `HOME`, `FX_DISABLE_KEYCHAIN=1`, `permission_mode: "ask"`, and a fake gateway, using a client like the one in #1465. The parent started two subagents: one ran `touch made-by-child.txt` and one read `package.json`. The shell child's request arrived as `session/request_permission` on the parent session with `_meta.fx.subagent`. The client answered `allow_once`, the file was created, the prompt ended with `end_turn`, fx exited 0, and stderr was empty.
