title: Read the log again when a turn ran after a prompt's handoff read
body:
## Summary

A prompt that the request runs itself (`runInRequest`) hands its sender's read of the log to its worker. If the previous turn's loop in the same process picked the prompt up and ran it while the sender was waiting on the backstop send, the worker then started early from that stale read (no lease, prompt pending) and sent a second model request for the same turn. Its claim was refused, so no record or UI line was duplicated, but the extra model request was billed. The committed race tests reproduce duplicate turn starts on the base and pass with this fix.

The fix:

- Each session worker counts the claims it starts. `mark()` returns the count, or `null` while a claim is running.
- The sender takes a mark just before its read and passes it with the handoff; `consume()` takes one before each of its own reads.
- Before deciding, the worker reads the log again while no claim is running and the count moved since the mark, then decides from that read as main does.
- The sender holds the session's worker from before its read until the worker takes the delivery, so the count survives a worker that would otherwise be dropped and recreated in between.

Leases, fencing, the backstop, recovery, acceptance and tenant checks are unchanged. A prompt to an idle session reads nothing more: counting World `events.list` calls over the same scripted runs, this branch and main make the same number for a new session's first prompt, an idle follow-up and a steer while running.

## Validation

- New queue tests, each failing on main's `durable.js` and passing here:
  - the previous turn's loop runs the prompt while its backstop is sent;
  - the sender reads while a claim's lease is still landing (covers `mark()` returning `null`);
  - another sender's worker runs the prompt while its backstop is sent (covers the hold).
- New tests that a failed backstop or input write leaves no worker held.
- `node sdk/tests/test-durable-core.mjs`: memory 55, local 52, world 54, queue 71.
- `node sdk/tests/test-durable.mjs` native: memory 61, local 58, world 55; wasm: memory 61, local 58.
- `tests/tla/sdk/check.sh`; `drive.mjs` send, lookup, write, cutoff, leased and queue; `drive-intake.mjs` on memory and world. `DurableSession.tla` does not model a read used after awaits or count model requests, so the spec is unchanged.
- Historical, uncommitted native-engine probes reported 8/8 duplicates on the base and 0/8 with the fix, plus zero duplicates in five natural runs. These are one-off observations, not reproducible commands supplied by this PR. Use the committed race tests as the repeatable correctness evidence.
- Mutations: with the re-read guard disabled or the claim count never raised, the first race test fails; with `mark()` ignoring a running claim, only the lease-landing test fails; with no hold, only the other-sender test fails.

## Review correction

The other-sender test now awaits the competing turn and its captured `waitUntil` work, so receive cleanup has completed before the held sender continues. It no longer uses `sleep(30)` for ordering. Repeated local checks pass; the no-hold mutation produces a duplicate, and all three race tests fail on the base. Core counts remain 55/52/54/71. Native durable suites passed 61/58/55; WebAssembly memory/local passed 61/58. Eight formal graph drivers passed against the corrected head using matching model/config hashes and shared TLC graphs. The runtime implementation is unchanged. An initial full Zig test run failed in an unchanged macOS Keychain test while other worktrees ran their suites. A serial `zig build test --summary all` rerun passed with exit 0. CI for this head remains pending.

## Not covered

The count is per agent object in one process. A turn run by another process, or by a second same-name agent in the same process, can still leave a stale handoff, and the extra request is still billed and refused. Closing that would cost a read on every in-request prompt or giving up the early start's latency.


## Publication status

Published as a draft to run CI on the corrected head. Local gate code checks passed after setting the repo-local identity and resolving the test-run issue, but the gates could not approve exact-head CI before publication. The author explicitly authorized draft publication for CI; this is not merge approval. The final readiness gate must run after required CI succeeds.

title: Start an in-request turn while its backstop is being queued
body:
## Summary

A prompt that the request runs itself waited for its backstop `queue.send` before the in-request worker started, so the first model request went out one queue round trip later than it could (about 50 ms warm; a new instance's first send took about 400 ms in our earlier traces).

The worker now starts as soon as the input is stored, while the backstop is being sent:

- `send()` starts the queue send without awaiting it, hands the worker a promise of the backstop, and awaits the send before returning. `accepted` and `seeded` still come only after the send succeeds.
- `consume()` folds the log without the pending delivery. That can only make a lease look alive, never dead, so only an early claim goes ahead before the send settles; every other path (forwarding to another agent, a running session, a standing lease) waits for the backstop first, and the ones that decide from the lease fold the log again with it.
- `claim()` appends the lease, and any early writes, only after the backstop resolves, and the lease names the real message. Every log write, UI line and tool already waits for the lease, so nothing durable happens before the backstop exists.
- A send that fails fails the claim: nothing is written, the turn is cancelled through the existing path, the caller hears the failure, and the delivery reports it once as a `session.error` event (today a failed send emits none). The only cost is a model request that started and is dropped.

Persistence before the queue send, acceptance after it, leases, fencing and the queue payload are unchanged. The worker's `delivery` argument now carries either the delivery or a promise of the backstop, rather than adding a parameter, because `consume()` and `claim()` are private to the module and each already threads the delivery through to the lease.

One existing test changes: "a prompt the request runs itself starts its worker from the sender's read, without reading the log again" now allows the turn's own poll for steers, which can run while the lease waits for the backstop, as at most one read between the input and the lease. It tells that poll from a worker reading the log again by whether the turn's model request has gone out, so disabling the handoff still fails it. Nothing may be written in between.

This touches `send()` near the code #1496 changes, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.

## Measurements

12 balanced warm pairs per workload on Vercel previews, 48/48 prompts complete with no issues. Both sides use packages built from the same source with the same native and WebAssembly engines and World bundles; only `durable.js` differs. The measured `durable.js` is the first commit's; the second commit changes a test and one comment, and its minified `durable.js` is byte-identical to the measured one.

| Metric | New chats | Faster | Follow-ups | Faster |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Accepted to model request | -75 ms (p50 199 -> 140 ms) | 11/12 | -55 ms (p50 87 -> 30 ms) | 12/12 |
| SDK admission (`prompt.accepted`) | -45 ms | 6/12 | -9 ms | 7/12 |
| HTTP POST to acceptance | -72 ms | 7/12 | -89 ms | 8/12 |
| Time to first text | -14 ms | 6/12 | -248 ms | 8/12 |

Deltas are medians of candidate minus baseline within each pair; the p50s in parentheses are each side's own median, so they need not differ by the delta. The model request start is the effect this change targets and it moves consistently. Admission and POST to acceptance are not expected to change, and their deltas are within run-to-run noise. Time to first text varies by about a second with the model, so its follow-up delta is directional, not a significance claim. On new chats the worker still reads the log before it starts on this base, which hides part of the gain; #1496 removes that read.

## Validation

- `node sdk/tests/test-durable-core.mjs`: memory 55, local 52, world 54, queue 72.
- `node sdk/tests/test-durable.mjs` on memory, local and world, with native and WebAssembly engines: 61, 58 and 55 each.
- `tests/tla/sdk/check.sh`, `drive.mjs` send, lookup, write, cutoff, leased and queue, `drive-intake.mjs` on memory and world, `drive-tenants.mjs` and `drive-agents.mjs`.

New queue tests cover a turn that starts while the send is held (only the input is written, nothing is shown, no step runs, the prompt is not accepted), a send that fails after the model request started (no lease, record or UI line, nothing queued again, and the retry runs each step once with a lease that names its backstop, on the default World and one with known liveness), an abort while the send is held, an image prompt, a busy session, and a steer while the backstop is in flight. Mutations that write the lease before the send resolves, let a failed send succeed the claim, skip the rethrow, accept early, let the non-early path skip waiting, or disable the handoff each fail a test.

Not run: `test-durable.mjs vercel native` and `drive.mjs --durability vercel` (no Vercel token for the World tests).

`DurableSession.tla` and `PromptIntake.tla` don't model the order of the backstop and the lease. The modelled rule, that nothing is written or shown and no tool runs before the claim lands, still holds, and a failed send looks like an early worker that crashed, so no spec change is required.

title: Overlay mostly undefined constants in PGSO builds
body:
## Summary

- Shrink the macOS arm64 PGSO release binary by 114,912 bytes by packing the mostly undefined constants Zig emits for `return error.X` and `return null` into one shared constant. Measured against a PGSO run of main at `5e9cf15ca`: 6,264,144 to 6,149,232.
- Run the new `ir_size.py overlay-constants` pass after `sparse-constants` for the release and benchmark candidates.
- Keep speed-optimized code unchanged: constants that hot code reads, or that are under 64 bytes, keep zeros in their undefined bytes.
- Leave constants alone that hold relocated pointers, compare or convert their address, live in a named section, are thread-local, or are listed in `llvm.used`.

title: Keep the IR outliner from reversing greater-than comparisons
body:
## Summary

- PGSO builds rewrite each greater-than comparison as the less-than comparison with its operands swapped before every IR outliner run, so outlined code keeps each comparison's direction.
- The PGSO candidate no longer panics with `index out of bounds` when it loads a skill file larger than 64 KiB.
- Benchmark candidates get the same rewrite before their outliner runs.

title: Shrink built-in tool schemas and fix common tool-call failures
body:
## Summary

- Send built-in tool definitions at about half their previous size. In a new TUI session with default settings, the first request's tool definitions drop from 20,897 to 9,844 bytes, and `tests/evals/tool-schema-ab.ts tokens` counts 2,154 to 3,489 fewer input tokens for that request across six models.
- `shell` shortens a `yield_time_ms` above the action's limit (30 seconds for `run`, 5 minutes for `interact`) to that limit and runs the call instead of rejecting it.
- The `shell` description for headless `fx ask --no-save` no longer mentions tty fields its schema does not have.
- The `shell` description points the model to `glob_files`, `grep_files`, and `read_file` for listing, finding, and reading files.
- The web search guidance excludes questions `gh` can answer and questions about the repository being worked in.
- `vision` ignores an empty or null image source sent next to the one in use, such as `image_ids: []` with `paths`, and its input errors say how to fix the call.
- `ask_user_question` accepts `questions` sent as a JSON string. The new `ask_questions_text` fuzz target sends arbitrary text through that decode.
- `read_tool_result` rejects a call that sets both `handle` and `search` and points to `query`, instead of silently dropping the handle.
- The GitHub routing eval counts any local command, such as `ls`, as a local first step, asks about a repository that exists, and runs in checkouts with real history.
- Add `tests/evals/tool-schema-ab.ts`, an on-request eval that compares tool schema variants across models through a recording proxy, with deterministic tests for its helpers.

title: Open the engine while a prompt's backstop is sent
body:
## Summary

A prompt that the request runs itself (`runInRequest`) stored its input, sent its delayed backstop, waited for the queue to answer, and only then started its worker. The worker now starts as soon as the input is stored and opens its engine while the backstop is sent:

- The speculative claim makes no lease, log or UI write and sends no model request until its backstop succeeds. A later delivery with a successful backstop can displace a still-write-free opener and recover stored inputs in canonical log order. As on the stack base, that recovery can include an earlier input whose own sender failed; this is not a per-input queue-commit protocol.
- Only an early start goes ahead before the backstop's id is known. A forward to another agent, a session already running here, a standing lease or an open turn wait for the backstop and fold the log again with the real delivery, as before. A delivery can only end a lease that stood without it (`redelivers`), so the early-start decision stays valid once the id is known.
- Before any early start, and again after waiting for the backstop, the worker reads the log again if a claim started here after its sender's read. This keeps #1525's fix in place: without the second read, a turn that runs while the backstop is in flight leaves the start decision on a stale read.
- Acceptance is unchanged: it resolves only after the input is stored and the backstop queued, and never when the send fails.
- A failed backstop rejects the prompt without waiting out a slow engine open. A late engine closes in the background, and the agent's `close()` waits for it.

## Stack

This is stacked on #1496 and #1525. Its base, `esteban/libfx-stack-1496-1525`, is #1496 with #1525 applied and their `send()` conflict resolved (`hold()` and `mark()` stay ahead of the fresh-session skip, `letGo` stays in `finally`). The diff here is only this change. Review #1496 and #1525 first; this rebases onto `main` once they land. It supersedes #1526.

## Historical preview measurements

The following are one-off measurements of `8851b818d`, before the contention repair. The internal A/B and native probe scripts are not included in this PR, so these numbers are not reproducible from the repository. They have not been remeasured on the repaired implementation.

Vercel previews with SDK packages built from the same source and engines; only `durable.js` and its generated CommonJS bundle differ (baseline: the stack base). 12 balanced warm pairs per workload, 24/24 prompts complete each, no `session.error`.

| Metric | Median paired delta | Candidate faster |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Follow-ups: accepted to model request | -65 ms | 11/12 |
| Follow-ups: time to first text | -164 ms | 8/12 |
| New chats: accepted to model request | -37 ms | 8/12 |
| New chats: time to first text | -95 ms (noisy) | 7/12 |

The delta column is the median of candidate minus baseline within each pair. Admission itself is unchanged within noise (follow-ups -3 ms, 7/12).

Duplicate model requests: in an earlier gate run on #1496 alone, this change made the stale-handoff race that #1525 fixes occur in natural back-to-back follow-ups (7/240). On this stack, a natural back-to-back driver gave 0/40 duplicates in each of 6 runs, and a forced-interleaving driver gave 0/8 in each of 2 runs, both with the native engine.

## Original validation

- `node sdk/tests/test-durable-core.mjs`: memory 55, local 56, world 58, queue 86.
- `node sdk/tests/test-durable.mjs` with the native engine: memory 61, local 58, world 55.
- `tests/tla/sdk/check.sh`; `drive.mjs` send, lookup, write, cutoff, queue and leased; `drive-intake.mjs` on memory and world; `drive-agents.mjs`. `DurableSession.tla` models the claim but not admission or the backstop, so the spec is unchanged; the drivers run without `runInRequest`.

New queue tests cover: the engine opening during a held backstop send on a first prompt and a follow-up, with no write, stream line, model request or acceptance before it, and a lease that names the backstop; a failed backstop, which stores only the input, sends no model request and lets a retry store once and run once; a failed backstop while the engine is still opening, which rejects at once and closes the engine later; an abort during the send; recovery on another server through the backstop after the process dies; and a prompt to another agent's session whose backstop fails, which is not forwarded. Each fails on the base's code or under a mutation that removes the guard it covers. Removing the re-read after the backstop wait fails "a sender that reads while a claim's lease is still landing does not start a turn twice".

Two of #1525's race tests held b's backstop send until a's worker had run b. With this change b's worker claims before its backstop resolves, so that script deadlocked. They now hold b after its input write instead, which still lands before b's sender hands off. With the re-read guard removed, all three race tests fail with duplicate turns.

## Contention repair and current local verification

- Added deterministic success/failure, opening/opened-engine, late-cleanup, concurrent-delivery, steering, remote-retry and cancellation coverage. The second prompt completes while the first send is held, and late completion of the displaced opener cannot duplicate a model request or release the successor's lease.
- The corrected stack base already includes #1496's creation-abort test and isolated-slot correction, and #1525's deterministic hold correction. This PR retains the input-write barrier needed for engine overlap.
- Current core counts: memory 55, local 57, world 59, queue 98. Native durable suites: 61/58/55. Independent runtime and native probes found no blocker.
- Current verification passed: formatting, build, full Zig tests, native and WebAssembly rebuilds, durable suites (native and WASM: 61/58/55), native race probes, 19 graph drivers, binary smoke and 13 CLI E2E tests. The TLC checker completed with exit 0. The models do not cover speculative backstop/open interleavings; the deterministic concurrency tests and native probes cover those cases. Live Vercel remeasurement, a browser-demo interaction and CI for this head remain pending.

## Notes

- Opening the engine reads the Gateway credential (environment, `durability.gatewayKey()` or the OIDC token), including for a failed sender. Its speculative claim sends no model request. Another successfully backed delivery can recover the already-stored input, as on the base.
- The original implementation delayed a second prompt behind the first pending backstop, and could defer it to a 2-second queue retry after failure. The repair lets a backed contender revoke only a write-free opener, await its teardown, reread the log and recover pending inputs in order. A claim with authorized writes or an active model still uses the existing busy-worker retry.


## Publication status

Published as a draft to run CI on the corrected head. Local gate code checks passed after setting the repo-local identity and resolving the test-run issue, but the gates could not approve exact-head CI before publication. The author explicitly authorized draft publication for CI; this is not merge approval. The final readiness gate must run after required CI succeeds.

title: Distinguish fast models from Fast mode in the model picker
body:
## Summary

- The model picker labels `-fast` models "Fast", since they always run fast.
- Models that offer Fast mode as an option now read "Fast mode" instead of "Fast".
- A `-fast` model that also offers Fast mode shows both labels, "Fast · Fast mode".
- Models that offer Ultra mode now read "Ultra mode" instead of "Ultra".

title: Keep getIo and two string helpers out of line
body:
## Summary

- Shrink the macOS arm64 PGSO release binary by 49,248 bytes by keeping `getIo` out of line instead of copying it into its call sites. Against main's PGSO candidate at `49edeb445`, the candidate drops from 6,165,648 to 6,116,400 bytes (`__text` -38,304).
- Shrink ordinary ReleaseSafe builds by 114,912 bytes on macOS arm64 and 64,288 on Linux x86_64.
- Keep `mem.startsWith` and `ascii.eqlIgnoreCase` out of line in PGSO builds.

title: Measure startup on fresh copies of both binaries
body:
## Summary

- The startup gate copies the control and candidate binaries into its measurement directory just before measuring and times the copies, so both start from the same page-cache state.
- The gate checks that each copy's SHA-256 matches its artifact and stops before measuring if one does not.
- On Linux, a candidate whose pages were read back from disk no longer fails `help` and `--version` against a control that was still freshly written.

title: Let subagents work alongside their parent and report back
body:
## Summary

- A `message` to a subagent returns at once, and the parent keeps working or ends its turn while the subagent works.
- When a subagent's work ends, its report joins the parent's running turn, or starts the parent's next turn when it is idle. It shows as one card, with the full text under `ctrl+o`.
- A subagent reports when its work ends by default. `report: every_turn` reports after each of its turns, including turns the user types on its screen, and `report: never` reports only failures.
- A message to a busy subagent joins its running turn at the next step, or waits, and every message still waiting goes into its next turn together.
- At most 64 messages from other agents wait for one subagent. Past that, `message` returns `queue_full`.
- An agent takes messages in the order they arrive, and a message from another agent is marked as that agent's output, never the user's instructions.
- The parent's `stop` ends a subagent's turn, drops the messages waiting for it, and owes no report.
- Esc on a subagent's screen stops its turn and drops the parent's messages it hasn't read. Its report, or a short notice, tells the parent how many.
- A report says when the user started the turn, and why its work was cancelled: the user stopped it, or fx quit.
- A report still owed when fx quits or crashes arrives when the session resumes, and a report that joined a running turn comes back as the same card.
- `/close` stops an instance's subagents without reports. Reports they already owed stay in the session.
- An image or `$skill` sent to a busy subagent ends its turn so the user's prompt runs next, and the parent's work counts as done.
- A subagent with no mode of its own follows its parent's permission mode as it changes, and the parent's screen shows the oldest subagent prompt first.
- `fx ask` waits for every subagent it starts and runs each report as another turn before it exits. ACP shows each report on the tool call that sent the work.
- The subagent tool no longer has the one-off `run` action. A subagent an older fx started for a single task can't take messages.

Stacked on #1448.

title: Match the permission review eval to the requests fx sends
body:
## Summary

- The live auto-permission eval expects the review instruction as the prompt's first and only system message, and the closing tool result of the pending call as its last message, which is the order fx sends.
- It expects a review on GPT-5.6 or later to ask OpenAI for explicit caching, instead of failing on those provider options.
- The delegated-action scenario counts the saved session's title request among the requests it expects.
- The MCP fixture server answers `initialize` with the protocol version fx asks for. It answered 2024-11-05, which fx no longer speaks, so both dynamic MCP publish scenarios failed before any review started. It also answers other requests, such as `server/discover`, with "method not found" instead of letting them time out.
- With these fixed, every remaining failure comes from the live reviewer itself. Most are its judgment: it sometimes returns caution for task-conflicting actions the policy says to clear ("unknown destructive wrapper", "unrequested validation and delete compound", "unmentioned selected dynamic MCP publish"), and sometimes clears "hidden action", which expects caution. Rarely, fx sends a review a second time, which the eval's send count rejects. Those are left for a separate change.

title: Use the shared stable sort in usage, the compactor, and v1 conversion
body:
## Summary

- Shrink the macOS arm64 PGSO release binary by 82,080 bytes by moving eight `std.mem.sort` calls in usage, the compactor, and v1 session conversion to the shared stable sort, `sort_utils.sort`. Each removed call site had its own block sort copy. Against main's PGSO candidate at `ae9b41c4a`, the candidate drops from 6,165,648 to 6,083,568 bytes (`__text` -73,716).
- Sorting results are unchanged, because a stable sort's output is fully determined by its comparator. `sort_utils` already tests this element for element against `std.mem.sort`.
- Allow `sort_utils` in the compactor's import boundary. It depends only on `std`.

title: Share one JSON parser across typed parse sites
body:
## Summary

- Shrink the macOS arm64 PGSO release binary by adding `json_decode`, a drop-in for `std.json.parseFromSlice` and `parseFromSliceLeaky` that shares one parser across types. `std.json` generates a full parser for every type it parses into, which added up to about 100 KB in the release binary. Against main's PGSO candidate at `ae9b41c4a`, the candidate drops from 6,165,648 to 6,067,152 bytes, 98,496 smaller (`__text` -102,724).
- Keep parsing identical. Each type gets a compile-time table of field names, offsets, defaults, and child types, and one function walks it over `std.json.Scanner`. Numbers, enum tags, optionals, slices, and unions still go through `std.json`'s own functions, so every document parses to the same value, or fails with the same error, under the same options. Types with a `jsonParse` method still use it, and tuples, packed structs, and sentinel arrays fall back to `std.json`.
- Move the 50 typed production call sites to it, outside the MCP engine, the indexer, the session manager, ACP, and the JS hosts. Allow it in the compactor's import boundary, and note it in `AGENTS.md`.

## Testing

- The new tests compare `json_decode` with `std.json` on a corpus of valid and invalid documents under six option sets, on 4,000 mutated documents, and on a full usage cache file with 2,000 mutated copies.
- `zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe` passes.
- On a local release replay, `fx sessions --all --json` prints byte-identical output to main's build over 100 saved sessions.

title: Bug: openai-chat-completions fails with InvalidChunk when the finish chunk carries an empty legacy `function_call` ({"name":"","arguments":""})
body:
### Summary A custom `openai-chat-completions` connection reports `fx: InvalidChunk` on every reply. The full answer prints first; the failure happens on the final chunk. The server's finish chunk includes the deprecated `delta.function_call` field populated with empty strings: ```json "delta": {"content": "", "role": "assistant", "function_call": {"name": "", "arguments": ""}}, "finish_reason": "stop" ``` fx appears to treat any non-null `function_call` as a legacy function call and rejects it because `name` is empty, which aborts the stream. The same stream succeeds when `function_call` is `null` or omitted. This is the same symptom as #1173 but a different trigger: there the offending field is `model: ""`; here `model` is populated and the offending field is the empty `function_call`. ### Environment - fx version: v0.0.16 (latest release), build revision `481104fdbc24`, stable channel - Platform: macOS 27.0.1, arm64 - Connection: custom `openai-chat-completions` provider, `auth: none` - Real-world source: a local OpenAI-compatible gateway (Magpie) forwarding to an upstream (WorkBuddy) serving `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `glm-5.3`. Both models emit this finish chunk on every streamed response. Other upstreams behind the same gateway (Anthropic, Codex, Gemini) omit `function_call` and work fine. ### Minimal reproduction (no external service needed) `server.py` is a ~40-line stdlib-only Python server that streams three chunks plus `[DONE]`. Its mode argument controls only the final delta's `function_call`.
server.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Minimal OpenAI-compatible SSE server reproducing fx InvalidChunk on an empty function_call. Usage: python3 server.py [bad|null|omit] (default: bad) """ import json, sys from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer MODE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "bad" MODEL = "repro-model" def chunk(delta, finish=None, usage=None): return {"id": "chatcmpl-repro", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "created": 1793341426, "model": MODEL, "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": delta, "finish_reason": finish, "logprobs": None}], "usage": usage} class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def do_POST(self): self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("content-length", 0))) final_delta = {"content": "", "role": "assistant"} if MODE == "bad": final_delta["function_call"] = {"name": "", "arguments": ""} elif MODE == "null": final_delta["function_call"] = None events = [ chunk({"role": "assistant", "content": ""}), chunk({"content": "Hi!"}), chunk(final_delta, finish="stop", usage={"prompt_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens": 2, "total_tokens": 12}), ] body = "".join(f"data: {json.dumps(e, separators=(',', ':'))}\n\n" for e in events) + "data: [DONE]\n\n" data = body.encode() self.send_response(200) self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/event-stream") self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data))) self.end_headers() self.wfile.write(data) def log_message(self, *a): pass HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 3499), H).serve_forever() ```
`settings.json`: ```json { "provider": "repro", "providers": { "repro": { "protocol": "openai-chat-completions", "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:3499/v1", "auth": { "type": "none" }, "model_metadata": { "repro-model": { "context_window": 128000, "max_output_tokens": 8192, "supports_tool_use": true } } } }, "models": { "repro": "repro-model" } } ``` Run: ```bash mkdir -p /tmp/fxrepro/home/.fx /tmp/fxrepro/ws cp settings.json /tmp/fxrepro/home/.fx/settings.json python3 server.py bad & # or: null | omit cd /tmp/fxrepro/ws && HOME=/tmp/fxrepro/home fx ask "say hi" ``` Results: | `server.py` mode | final `delta.function_call` | fx result | |---|---|---| | `bad` | `{"name":"","arguments":""}` | `Hi!` then `fx: InvalidChunk`, exit 1 | | `null` | `null` | `Hi!`, exit 0 | | `omit` | field absent | `Hi!`, exit 0 | ### Exact stream sent in `bad` mode ``` data: {"id":"chatcmpl-repro","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1793341426,"model":"repro-model","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":""},"finish_reason":null,"logprobs":null}],"usage":null} data: {"id":"chatcmpl-repro","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1793341426,"model":"repro-model","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"Hi!"},"finish_reason":null,"logprobs":null}],"usage":null} data: {"id":"chatcmpl-repro","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1793341426,"model":"repro-model","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"","role":"assistant","function_call":{"name":"","arguments":""}},"finish_reason":"stop","logprobs":null}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":10,"completion_tokens":2,"total_tokens":12}} data: [DONE] ``` ### What I ruled out Against the real gateway, I captured the wire traffic and replayed it to fx from a local server while changing one variable at a time: - HTTP framing is not the cause. The chunked transfer encoding validated end to end, and serving the same body with `Content-Length` and no chunking still fails with `InvalidChunk`. The error name points at the transport layer, but the rejection is SSE/JSON-level. - Removing the leading `: heartbeat` SSE comment, merging chunks, dropping `data: [DONE]`, and trimming the extra non-standard `usage` fields (`prompt_cache_hit_tokens`, `credit`, etc.) each still failed. - Changing only `function_call` to `null` or removing it made the identical stream succeed. ### Expected behavior Treat a `function_call` (and, by the same logic, a `tool_calls` entry) whose `name` and `arguments` are both empty as absent, rather than failing the stream. This shape typically comes from servers that serialize zero-valued structs instead of omitting them. fx never requested legacy function calling: its request contains `tools` (14 entries) and `tool_choice`, and no `functions` key. ### Suggested fixes, in order of preference 1. In the chunk decoder, normalize an all-empty `delta.function_call` to null before validation. 2. More generally, ignore the deprecated `function_call` delta when the request did not use legacy `functions`, or log and skip a malformed delta instead of terminating the stream after content has already arrived. 3. Include the offending field or chunk (redacted) in the `InvalidChunk` error or `stream_error` event. As with #1173, isolating this required a man-in-the-middle proxy and replay bisection. ### Related - #1173: same `InvalidChunk` failure, triggered by `model: ""` (Bifrost) - #1334: a separate strict-parsing failure (`IncompleteStream` without `data: [DONE]`)

title: Move mostly empty writable globals to zero-fill in PGSO builds
body:
## Summary

- Shrink the macOS arm64 PGSO release binary by one page by moving std's `Progress` state to zero-fill. Its 18 KB initializer is undefined except for one 255, and that byte alone made the linker write the whole global into `__DATA`. Against main's PGSO candidate at `b959ef781`, the candidate drops from 6,165,648 to 6,149,216 bytes, 16,432 smaller (`__data` 23,624 to 5,480).
- Add `ir_size.py zero-fill-globals` after `overlay-constants`. It gives internal writable globals of at least 4 KB whose nonzero bytes fit in 64 bytes an all-zero initializer, and stores those bytes at the start of `main`, following the alias Zig uses for it. Nothing reads them earlier, and no later stage folds the stores back.

## Testing

- New tests run a module before and after the pass under `lli` and compare results, follow an aliased `main`, and leave constant, external, thread-local, sectioned, small, and dense globals untouched.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/pgso/tests -t .` passes (220 tests).
- On the local replay binary, `fx sessions --all --json` prints the same output as main's over 100 saved sessions.

title: Right-align ordered list numbers
body:
## Summary

- Right-align ordered list numbers in three columns, so the markers of items 1 through 999 end in the same column and the item text starts in one column. Longer numbers are not padded.
- Keep content nested under an ordered item, such as sub-lists, continuation paragraphs, and quotes, lined up under the item's text.
- Draw ordered lists inside quotes as before, with their numbers as written.

title: Parse the remaining typed JSON sites with json_decode
body:
## Summary

- Shrink the macOS arm64 PGSO release binary by moving the remaining typed JSON parse sites outside the session manager and the MCP engine to `json_decode`. Four `jsonParse` methods still called `std.json.innerParse`, which generates a full std parser for the type it reads: the `Wire` form of a conversation interruption in `session_event`, and the image parts and wrapped content in `prompt_context`. ACP's shell result view and the JS host's workspace info also parsed through `std.json`. The PGSO candidate drops from 5,952,240 bytes on main `ae3737b0b` to 5,935,824, a saving of 16,416 bytes (`__text` -8,468), as the local replay predicted.
- Make `json_decode.innerParse` public, with the same contract as `std.json.innerParse` over a `std.json.Scanner`. Every caller of those `jsonParse` methods passes a `Scanner`, so the build checks that the methods still accept every source they receive.
- Leave the session manager on `std.json`: it is built as its own module and cannot import a file the root module owns.

## Testing

- `zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe` passes, including the `json_decode` tests that compare it with `std.json`.
- `zig build fx-core-wasm` and `zig build fx-term-wasm` build.
- On a local release replay: `acp.test.ts` 168/168, `session-recovery.test.ts` 33/33, and `vision-route-fake-gateway.test.ts` 53/53 in a quiet run. `sessions.test.ts` passed 98 of 99 under heavy machine load; the one timeout passes on its own on this build and on main's.

title: Read error names through one function in PGSO builds
body:
## Summary

- Shrink the macOS arm64 PGSO release binary by reading error names through one function. Zig's `__zig_error_name_table` holds a 16-byte pointer and length for each of fx's 1,628 errors, and every `@errorName` reads its entry in place, so the pointers keep the table's 26 KB in relocated data. The PGSO candidate drops from 5,952,240 bytes on main `ae3737b0b` to 5,919,392, a saving of 32,848 bytes: `__DATA_CONST` shrinks from 10 pages to 8. The stage reads all 1,629 names, rewrites 795 reads, and sends 3 through a stack slot. An exact local replay of the candidate predicted the same size.
- Add a `compact-error-names` stage after `zero-fill-globals`. Each of the 790 reads becomes a call to `pgso.error_name(index)`, which returns the same pointer and length from 16-bit offsets into one blob of the same names, each still NUL-terminated for the sentinel `@errorName` returns. Two reads in the indexer's bounded read go through a PHI that also merges a local slice, and with the production profile the IR outliner moves a third into a pair copy that 54 callers share. In both cases the pair goes to a stack slot laid out like the entry, and the PHI or call carries the slot. A call qualifies only when the callee is defined in the module and only loads the name and length from that parameter; the callee is left unchanged.
- Change nothing unless the table and every use of it have the shapes the stage recognizes.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/pgso/tests -t .` passes. The new tests run a small module in LLVM's interpreter before and after the stage, including a read of each name's NUL, including an entry passed to a shared copy that another caller also uses, and check that five unrecognized uses (including a defined function that keeps the pointer) and a module without the table are left unchanged. Dropping the NUL, skipping a stack-slot store, an off-by-one length, passing the old pointer to the copy, skipping the callee check, or accepting a declared callee each fails a test.
- On a local release replay, `fx replay` with a missing file and with a directory prints the same `FileNotFound` and `ReadFailed` messages as main's build, and `fx sessions --all --json`, `fx usage --json`, `fx help`, and `fx --version` print byte-identical output.
- On the same build: `gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` 214/214, `sessions.test.ts` 99/99, `tui-resume.test.ts` 69/69, `vision-route-fake-gateway.test.ts` 53/53, `session-recovery.test.ts` 33/33, `tui-resize.test.ts` 57/57, and `cli.test.ts` 129/130; the one failure reads the local profile's update channel.
- On the exact replay of CI's candidate with the call handling: `poisoned-repository.test.ts` 7/7, `file-tool-paths.test.ts` 25/25, and `tui-file-picker.test.ts` 23/23, which drive the indexer and safe git reads that use the bounded read. `fx --version`, `help`, `sessions --all --json`, `mcp list --json`, `status --json`, `doctor --json`, and `fx replay` with a missing file and a non-tape file print byte-identical output to the unchanged replay, including the `FileNotFound` and `BadTapeMagic` messages.

title: Fix command test failures and a grep race under ThreadSanitizer
body:
## Summary

- The ThreadSanitizer run sets `atexit_sleep_ms=0`, so the five `command_runner` natural-completion tests that fail in every nightly run pass. Those tests run each command through the sanitized fx, and by default a sanitized process with other threads still running waits a second before it exits.
- Parallel `grep_files` scans give each worker its own arena, which removes the data race ThreadSanitizer reported in [run 41017956098](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/actions/runs/41017956098). Results, ordering, and the collection cap are unchanged.

title: Ship the Linux arm64 PGSO candidate in stable releases
body:
## Summary

- The stable release now ships the qualified Linux arm64 PGSO candidate instead of a plain ReleaseSafe cross-compile, the same way it ships macOS arm64. On this PR's Linux arm64 PGSO run (41102227518), the candidate is 6,187,504 bytes (5.90 MiB) against 10,434,760 bytes (9.95 MiB) for the plain build.
- `release.yml` calls `pgso-linux-arm64.yml` with 90-day evidence retention. A new `package-linux-aarch64` job on a native arm64 runner confirms eligibility with `scripts.pgso report`, checks the binary's SHA-256 against the qualified candidate in the manifest, smoke-tests it, and packages `fx-linux-aarch64.tar.gz` with the same contents as before. `release` waits for it.
- `pgso-linux-arm64.yml` gains a `workflow_call` trigger with the macOS workflow's `evidence-retention-days` input and `artifact-id` output.
- `setup-pgso` installs Zig on Linux through the same pinned `mlugg/setup-zig` as macOS. The shared `setup-zig` action uses mutable tags, and it would otherwise become part of the release chain. The release pin test now follows every local action and reusable workflow that `release.yml` reaches, and fails if that step goes back to `setup-zig`.
- `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `scripts/pgso/README.md` now say the stable release ships the Linux arm64 candidate. `AGENTS.md` also names the Linux arm64 qualification, alongside macOS arm64, as authoritative for the 7.000 MiB ceiling.
- Linux x86_64 keeps the plain build.

title: Run a held prompt in the request on Worlds whose queue holds messages
body:
## Summary

A durable agent's prompt runs in the request that took it, so the first model request goes out without a queue hop. Today the queue keeps a delayed backstop for that prompt, delivered only after the request's deadline. Workflow's World adds an experimental send-and-hold queue API, and this PR uses it on a World that declares `capabilities.experimental_queueHold`:

- The request sends the prompt undelayed, with `experimental_hold: { consumerGroup }` and the same idempotency key as before. The consumer group is the wake route's (see below).
- When the queue holds the message (the result's `experimental_hold.status` is `"held"`), the request runs the turn through `experimental_hold.consume()` under `waitUntil`. That is the message's first delivery: the queue renews its lease while the turn runs and acknowledges it after. If the request dies, the queue delivers the same message to the route, and since the lease names that message, the redelivery takes the session over. No delayed backstop is sent, and no takeover waits for the request's deadline.
- When the queue doesn't hold it (`status: "not_held"` with a reason, or no `experimental_hold` in the result), the request runs nothing and the queue delivers the message as usual.
- Worlds without the capability, and durabilities given no consumer group, keep today's path exactly, delayed backstop included.

### The hold's consumer group

A held message that lapses is delivered to the consumer group it was claimed for, so that group must be the wake route's. Vercel subscribes a vercel.json `queue/v2beta` trigger under a group it names after the `functions` key (and the service's name, for a Vercel service), never `default`, and vercel.json doesn't accept a `consumer` field. So the durability names the group:

- `holdFunction`: the wake route's vercel.json `functions` key, such as `"app/api/libfx/route.js"`, with `holdService` for a route in a Vercel service. libfx derives the group as Vercel does: `_` becomes `__`, `/` becomes `_S`, `.` becomes `_D`, letters, digits and `-` stay, and any other character becomes `_` and its hex code. The function is a local copy of `vercelTriggerConsumerGroup` from `@workflow/world-vercel`, pinned by a test.
- `holdConsumerGroup`: the group itself, such as `"default"` for a trigger in generated Build Output configuration.

`world()` and `vercel()` take both forms. They're mutually exclusive, and each needs `runInRequest`. Without either, the request keeps the delayed backstop rather than claim a group that might not match the route.

## Changes

- `sdk/durable.js`
  - The World backend's `queue.send()` takes `hold`. It passes `experimental_hold` only to an undelayed send on a World with the capability, and returns `held` when the queue took the hold. `queue.holds()` is true when the World declares the capability and the durability names a consumer group. The memory backend is unchanged.
  - The inline prompt path takes the hold branch when the World can hold messages. The handler given to `consume()` is the World queue consumer's handler for this agent: it calls `receive()` with the delivery from `meta`, and its result means the same as in the consumer (`queueAnswer()`, factored out of `deliverTo`). It also passes along the sender's read of the log, so the worker doesn't read the log again before its first model request. The consume work is tracked by the agent, so `close()` waits for it.
- `sdk/durable/world.mjs`, `sdk/durable/vercel.mjs`, `sdk/types/durable-world.d.ts`, `sdk/types/durable-vercel.d.ts`: `holdConsumerGroup`, `holdFunction` and `holdService`, plus the consumer-group naming. `runInRequest` documents both paths. `World` types `capabilities`, and `QueueHoldResult` / `QueueResult` describe the hold's answer.
- `sdk/durable/package.json`: `@workflow/world-vercel` 5.2.1 → 5.6.0.
- `sdk/README.md`: the vercel.json trigger is unchanged, and the README shows `vercel({ holdFunction })`, with `holdService` and `holdConsumerGroup` for the other cases.
- `sdk/tests/queue-world.mjs`: with `hold: "held" | "not_held"`, the test World declares the capability and answers hold sends with `experimental_hold` the way world-vercel does.
- `sdk/tests/test-durable-core.mjs` (queue): a held prompt runs through `consume`, undelayed and keyed, with no delayed send, and its lease names `{ messageId, attempt: 1 }`. A request that dies mid-turn is taken over by the queue's redelivery and fenced at its next write. A prompt the queue doesn't hold runs nothing in the request and is delivered by the queue. A World that has the capability but no consumer group keeps the backstop. The held send carries the group, from `holdFunction` or `holdConsumerGroup`. `holdFunction` derives the names Vercel gives (`api/libfx.ts` to `api_Slibfx_Dts`, `app/api/libfx/route.ts` to `app_Sapi_Slibfx_Sroute_Dts`, `api/my_fn.ts` to `api_Smy__fn_Dts`, service `web` with `api/flow.ts` to `web_7Eapi_Sflow_Dts`), and the option checks reject invalid combinations. The existing backstop test now checks that a World without the capability is never asked for a hold.

The TLA+ models don't model where a delivery runs, and a held message is an ordinary first delivery, so the specs are unchanged.

## Testing

- `node sdk/tests/test-durable-core.mjs queue`: 106/106. The held and not-held tests fail without the `durable.js` change.
- `node sdk/tests/test-durable-core.mjs memory | local | world`: 55/55, 61/61, 59/59.
- `node sdk/tests/test-types.mjs`: all type checks passed.
- `node sdk/tests/test-vercel-storage.mjs` and `scripts/check-public-surface.sh` pass.
- Not run locally, because the environment has no Zig, Bun, or TLC: `test-durable.mjs` (needs a native or wasm build) and the TLA+ drivers. CI covers them.

## Rollout chain

The World hold API is released: `@workflow/world-vercel` 5.6.0 is on npm, pinning `@vercel/queue` 0.11.0, and declares `capabilities.experimental_queueHold`. This PR moves the World that `vercel()` bundles (`sdk/durable/package.json`) from 5.2.1 to 5.6.0. With it, `vercel({ holdFunction })` holds prompts for the wake route: send-and-hold is on in the Vercel Queues service, so a held prompt runs in the request, and if the queue answers `not_held` it delivers the message as usual. Worlds without the capability, and durabilities with no consumer group, keep the delayed backstop.

## Risks and open questions

- An app that sets neither `holdFunction` nor `holdConsumerGroup` gets no hold. That's deliberate, since a wrong group would leave the route a second copy of the message.
- `world()` keeps a local copy of the consumer-group naming, because `libfx/durable-world` doesn't bundle world-vercel. A test pins the copy to the published `vercelTriggerConsumerGroup`. The libfx `.d.ts` files keep structural `QueueHoldResult`/`QueueResult` types, because the published package has no dependency on `@workflow/world`.
- `vercel({ leaseMs })` still sends every prompt through the queue, as before. A held message could also run in the request with renewed leases, but that's left for later.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Add a Linux x86_64 PGSO platform and workflow
body:
## Summary - The Linux PGSO platform now builds `x86_64-linux` as well as `aarch64-linux`. Only three steps depend on the architecture: the host check, the path of LLVM's profile runtime, and the `zig cc` target. `linux.Platform` carries those values, and `linux.ARM64` and `linux.X86_64` are the two platforms. Every other step is shared. - `.github/workflows/pgso-linux-x86_64.yml` runs the same single build-and-qualify job as the arm64 workflow, on a GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` runner. A test requires the two workflow files to differ only in their architecture values. On this head, run 41273833568 qualified an 8,181,520-byte (7.80 MiB) candidate against 12,581,488 bytes (12.00 MiB) for the plain build, 35.0% smaller and 0.45 MiB under the 8.250 MiB ceiling. All five startup commands and all six heavy workloads stayed within the 10% limit. Startup p50 changed by 0.0% to +7.8%. ui-activity was the closest heavy workload at +9.1% p50, and the four approval workloads were 9.1% to 19.6% faster. Before main was merged, run 41187538412 on `35f1b265a` qualified a 7.70 MiB candidate in which every startup command was faster. - `setup-pgso` picks the pinned LLVM 22.1.8 and Hyperfine 1.20.0 archives for the runner's architecture, and keeps the existing `pgso-linux-arm64` Zig cache key. A contract test runs both Linux steps with stub tools and checks that ARM64 and X64 request their pinned archive and digest, and that any other runner architecture fails before downloading. - A new test requires every platform name the pipeline reads to exist on macOS and on both Linux platforms. - Each platform now declares its size ceiling, and `size_gate` requires one instead of defaulting to 7.000 MiB. macOS arm64 and Linux arm64 keep 7.000 MiB, and Linux x86_64 gets 8.250 MiB, because x86_64 code is larger. The first x86_64 candidate (run 41105122303) was 7.698 MiB and failed the 7.000 MiB ceiling. After main grew by about 215 KB, the candidate in run 41263879130 was 8,182,704 bytes (7.804 MiB), under an 8.000 MiB ceiling but with only 0.196 MiB of the required 0.250 MiB headroom. The 0.250 MiB preferred headroom still applies everywhere. - `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` describe the x86_64 workflow. `scripts/pgso/README.md` describes the x86_64 platform, its workflow, and its 8.250 MiB ceiling. - Releases still ship the plain x86_64 Linux build. #1566 switches them over. ## Design The registry maps each target to the platform that builds it. Before this change, Linux was one module whose constants fixed it to aarch64: ```mermaid flowchart LR registry["platforms.for_target"] --> macos["macos module
aarch64-macos"] registry --> linux["linux module
aarch64-linux constants
shared ld.lld and ELF steps"] ``` Now the Linux steps stay in `linux.py`, and two `Platform` values supply the per-architecture data: ```mermaid flowchart LR registry["platforms.for_target"] --> macos["macos module
aarch64-macos, 7.000 MiB"] registry --> arm["linux.ARM64
aarch64-linux, 7.000 MiB"] registry --> x86["linux.X86_64
x86_64-linux, 8.250 MiB"] arm --> steps["linux.py shared steps
ld.lld relinks, ELF checks"] x86 --> steps ``` Two simpler options were weaker: - A copied `linux_x86_64` module would duplicate every Linux step, about 600 lines, to change five values: the target, display name, host architecture, profile runtime triple, and size ceiling. - Passing the target into every platform function would change the macOS interface for a Linux-only need. `Platform` changes neither the shared code nor the macOS module. The pipeline still reads each platform through the same names, and a test checks that every platform has all of them.

title: Keep skill discovery warnings out of the main transcript
body:
## Summary

- Stop showing the `skills: N discovery issues; some skills may be missing (ctrl+o to view)` line in the main transcript at startup.
- Stop printing the skill discovery warning in the main transcript each time `/skills` runs.

title: Outline the whole fx program in one IR outliner pass
body:
## Summary

- Shrink the macOS arm64 PGSO release binary by running the IR outliner once over the whole profiled fx module instead of over two `llvm-split` halves. Code repeated across the halves can now share one outlined copy. The PGSO candidate drops from 5,902,976 bytes on main `8c580bb0d` to 5,886,560, a saving of 16,416 bytes (`__text` -13,344).
- The split also made every private and internal symbol external until the cleanup internalized them again; the outliner now sees the module as profile use left it. The benchmark candidates already outline their whole module this way.
- Remove the split and relink steps and the `llvm-split` and `llvm-link` tool requirements.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/pgso/tests -t .` passes (254 tests); the profile-use sequence tests now expect one outline of the profile-use bitcode.
- On CI's `macos-15` runner the whole-module outliner took 302 seconds, against 61 and 164 seconds for the two halves on main, within its 900-second limit; locally it peaks at 5.9 GB. The PGSO run passed every gate on the first attempt.

title: Remove recovery code the retry stack no longer uses
body:
## Summary

- Remove the `system_resumed` recovery cause. fx stopped reporting it once waking the Mac kept model connections open (#1451).
- Load a recovery checkpoint that an older fx saved with `system_resumed` as a lost connection, which is how fx always recovered from it.
- Find fx's process in the resume E2E tests and the resume driver with `processPid()`, which now walks past tmux's shell on Linux (#1489), instead of keeping their own copies of that walk.
- Remove `persistFailedTurnWorkOnce`, which only the stall stop called. The retry stack removes that stop.

title: Lower the PGSO size ceilings to 6.0 and 6.25 MiB
body:
## Summary

- Lower the PGSO size ceiling from a shared 7.0 MiB to 6.0 MiB for macOS arm64 and 6.25 MiB for Linux arm64. The macOS candidate on main `34d770ab1` is 5.65 MiB (5,919,392 bytes) and the Linux candidate for #1548 5.86 MiB (6,141,952 bytes), so with the 0.25 MiB of headroom release eligibility requires, the old ceiling allowed about 1.1 MiB of growth on macOS before a release needed trimming.
- Each new ceiling leaves about 110 to 150 KB of growth above the current candidates (109,920 bytes on macOS, 149,504 on Linux), close to the 190 KB that 7.0 MiB left when #1295 set it.
- Each platform module sets `SIZE_CEILING_MIB`, and `size_gate` takes the ceiling as an argument instead of a shared default.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/pgso -t .` passes (255 tests), including the byte boundary at exactly 6.0 MiB, the preferred-headroom check, and a test that pins each platform's ceiling.
- This PR's macOS and Linux PGSO runs check the current candidates against the new ceilings.

title: Delete empty composer lines with Ctrl-U
body:
## Summary

- Ctrl-U and Cmd-Backspace delete the current empty line in a multiline draft instead of doing nothing. Nonempty line starts and empty drafts stay unchanged.
- Undo and Ctrl-Y restore the deleted newline. Selection deletion still takes precedence.
- Regression tests cover leading, middle, trailing, and consecutive empty lines through raw Ctrl-U, Kitty Ctrl-U, and Cmd-Backspace. Each TUI session uses an isolated profile.

## Testing

- Zig 0.17: `zig build` and `zig fmt --check src/core/input/composer_kill_ring.zig` pass. All six focused `composer_kill_ring` unit tests pass through a temporary import harness.
- From `tests/e2e`: `FX_SOUND=0 bun test tui-input-line-delete.test.ts ci-shards.test.ts` passes all 13 tests.

title: Resend a reply that runs out of output tokens before any text
body:
## Summary

- A reply that runs out of output tokens before any text, including one that ends in a cut-off tool call, is dropped and sent again once. Before, a cut-off tool call ended the turn.
- The resend asks for `low` effort when the model offers it below the current effort. The next step uses the selected effort again.
- The resend raises the output limit when the first request named none. The empty-reply retry already did this; it now also covers replies that end in a cut-off tool call.
- No resend is sent when it would repeat the same request, and a resend that is cut off again ends the turn.
- Codex resends an empty cut-off reply at `low` effort when the model offers it, where it used to stop.
- Configured OpenAI-compatible providers pass a cut-off reply to the agent loop and get the same resend and message as other providers, instead of failing the turn with `OutputTruncated`. A cut-off permission review on these providers still counts as unavailable.
- When cut-off tool calls end the turn, the message says they were not run and how to retry, and no longer claims a partial response is preserved.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#235

title: Read built-in tool arguments through one decoder
body:
## Summary

- Read the JSON arguments of `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `glob_files`, `grep_files`, and `read_tool_result` through one decoder, `tool_args.ArgsDecoder`. Each tool parsed its arguments by hand with the same checks and the same failure text for invalid JSON, a non-object, a missing string field, and a field of the wrong type, and `grep_files` kept its own optional-string helper.
- The decoder records the first problem as the text the model receives, built from the same templates, so every message is unchanged. Each tool still checks its enums, integers, booleans, and nested objects itself, including where JSON null is an error rather than a missing field (`read_tool_result`'s `query` and `start_byte`, `read_file`'s line fields).
- Behavior and size: no change in behavior. A shaped local replay of the macOS PGSO candidate shows `__text` −252 bytes and `__cstring` −1,343 bytes, with no change in file size.

## Testing

- `zig build test` passes. The tools' existing decode tests pin each failure message, and new `tool_args` tests cover the decoder's messages, missing and null optional strings, and every allocation failure.
- `zig fmt --check src/` and `scripts/check-public-surface.sh` pass.
- On the built binary: `file-tool-paths.test.ts` 25/25, `file-tool-permissions.test.ts` 2/2, and `ask-presentation.test.ts` 19/19.

title: Keep parser state across the terminal fuzz repaint split

## Summary

title: Share prologue and epilogue code across size-optimized functions
body:
## Summary

- Pass `-homogeneous-prolog-epilog` to llc for the fx candidate. Each function that profile use compiles for size saves `x29` and `x30` inline, then calls one of a few dozen shared helpers that store the remaining callee-saved registers, and returns through a matching helper that restores them. Today every size-optimized function repeats those loads and stores inline, and the machine outliner leaves them there: the current candidate has 8,018 inline `stp x29, x30` prologues.
- Functions compiled for speed keep inline prologues. In a replay of `main`, none of the 57 speed-compiled functions calls a helper.
- fx builds without frame pointers or unwind tables (`omit_frame_pointer = true`, `unwind_tables = .none`), so the helpers change no stack walking. Benchmark candidates keep the default code generation.
- Rename `FX_MACHINE_OUTLINER_FLAGS` to `FX_CODEGEN_FLAGS`, and update the README paragraph on the fx candidate, which still described the two-partition outliner.

## Size

This PR's macOS arm64 PGSO candidate is 5,837,312 bytes. Replaying the run's own seed bitcode and merged profile without the flag gives the same code generated the current way; the replay with the flag reproduces CI's candidate section for section:

| | `__TEXT` | `__text` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Without `-homogeneous-prolog-epilog` | 5,718,016 | 5,114,744 |
| This PR's candidate | 5,636,096 | 5,030,820 |

That saves 81,920 bytes (five pages). The startup, behavior, and heavy benchmark gates pass. Against the control built in the same run, the startup gates are 2.8% to 4.3% faster at the median, as on `main`. `Heavy ui-activity` first failed on its 95th percentile (+13.6%, median +0.75%); that benchmark keeps default code generation, so this PR does not change it, and it passed on rerun.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/pgso/tests -t .` passes (254 tests).
- On the replayed candidate: `--version`, `help`, `help ask`, `sessions`, `status`, `doctor` (twice), `mcp list`, `session last`, `ask` without a prompt, an unknown command, and `provider` print byte-identical output and exit codes to the current candidate's, after normalizing the workspace path.
- E2E against the replayed candidate in a `34d770ab1` checkout: `cli.test.ts` 129 pass and 1 fail; the current candidate fails the same `update_channel` assertion in the same checkout.

title: Preserve UTF-8 in ACP command progress
body:
In rare cases, the ACP client connected to fx randomly disconnects. It happened when my agent was responding in Russian.

The issue is that when the message contains UTF-8 code point longer than 1 byte per character, the fx streaming can cut it mid character. fx responds in fixed 4,096 byte chunks. That leads to my ACP client in https://github.com/molefrog/tgfx to disconnect. 

This PR fixes that.

ACP clients could disconnect when a shell output chunk ended partway through a UTF-8 code point. Retain the unfinished bytes per call and output stream, escape malformed bytes with the existing helper, and flush remaining bytes before the final tool update.

title: Treat a relative HOME as unset in fx mcp
body:
## Summary

- `fx mcp` no longer aborts when HOME is a relative path. It read HOME through the CLI's own environment hook, which skipped the absolute-path check that `io_mod.homeDir` applies everywhere else, so `HOME=relative/home fx mcp add NAME URL` built a relative profile path and exited with "panic: reached unreachable code". It now fails with "fx mcp: HOME isn't set", as it does when HOME is unset, and writes nothing.
- `fx mcp` and `fx usage` now read HOME through `io_mod.homeDir`, which every other reader uses. `fx usage` drops its own copy of the check, the CLI's unused `getenv` hook goes, and `snapshotPath` in `file_index.zig` drops a check that `homeDir` already makes.
- `fx status` and the shell's `/status` named `rel/home/.fx` as fx's folder when HOME was relative, though fx keeps nothing there. They now read HOME the same way, so `fx status --json` leaves `fx_home` out.
- A relative HOME counts as unset everywhere `io_mod.homeDir` is used, `FX_HOME` included. With `HOME=rel/home` and `FX_HOME` set, `fx mcp` and `fx status` use `FX_HOME`, as they do when HOME is unset, and `fx usage` gets past its HOME check instead of refusing.

| `HOME=rel/home` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `fx mcp add probe http://127.0.0.1:9/mcp` | exit 134, `panic: reached unreachable code` | exit 1, `fx mcp: HOME isn't set` |
| `fx mcp add probe2 -- /bin/echo hi` | exit 134, `panic: reached unreachable code` | exit 1, `fx mcp: HOME isn't set` |
| `fx usage` | exit 1, `fx usage: HOME is not set` | unchanged |
| `fx status --json` | `"fx_home":"rel/home/.fx"` | no `fx_home` |

With an absolute HOME, `fx mcp add` and `fx mcp list` work as before.

## Testing

- `zig build test` passes. The new test "top-level MCP and usage treat a relative HOME as unset" fails when `runMcpVerbs` reads HOME directly again.
- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test cli.test.ts -t "add fails precisely without HOME"` passes. Its new relative HOME case fails on main, where fx aborts.
- Ran `./zig-out/bin/fx` with `HOME=rel/home` from an empty folder for the commands above: none aborted and none created a file.

title: Say when HOME is not an absolute path
body:
Stacked on #1561.

## Summary

- fx treats an unset and a relative HOME the same way, but its messages said "HOME is not set" or "HOME isn't set". With `HOME=rel/home`, HOME is set, so a user who checks it sees a value and can't tell what's wrong. `fx mcp`, `fx usage`, `fx sessions`, and the workspace and session errors now say "HOME is not set to an absolute path", and ACP's MCP setup says "MCP servers: HOME is not set to an absolute path." The text is defined once, next to `io_mod.homeDir`, so the copies can't drift apart again.
- `/mcp` in the shell got an empty home when HOME was unusable and built `.fx/mcp.json` against the current folder, so `/mcp add` failed with a message about the config file. Every verb that reads or writes `~/.fx` now refuses a home that is not absolute before it builds a profile or credential path, as `fx mcp` already does. `help` and `call` don't use `~/.fx`, so they still run.

| `HOME=rel/home` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/mcp add probe http://127.0.0.1:9/mcp` in the shell | `Couldn't add probe to ~/.fx/mcp.json: ~/.fx/mcp.json has a server entry fx can't read.` | `/mcp: HOME is not set to an absolute path` |
| `fx sessions` | `fx sessions: HOME is not set` | `fx sessions: HOME is not set to an absolute path` |
| `fx mcp add probe -- /bin/echo hi` | `fx mcp: HOME isn't set` | `fx mcp: HOME is not set to an absolute path` |

With an absolute HOME, `/mcp add` still saves to `~/.fx/mcp.json`.

## Testing

- `zig build test` passes, including the new test "every verb that uses ~/.fx needs an absolute home".
- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test cli.test.ts -t "add fails precisely without HOME"` passes.
- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test mcp-verbs.test.ts` passes, including the new test "/mcp names HOME and writes nothing when HOME is not absolute". It types `/mcp add` in the shell with a relative HOME and fails on #1561's head, where fx printed a message about the config file.
- Drove `./zig-out/bin/fx` in a pseudo-terminal with `HOME=rel/home` and typed `/mcp add probe http://127.0.0.1:9/mcp`: it printed the new message, created no file, and left a workspace `.fx/mcp.json` unchanged. With an absolute HOME the same command saved the server.

title: Clear herdr attention after answering questions
body:
## Summary

Clear herdr's Needs attention indicator when a question answer resumes an fx turn. fx already reported `blocked` when it asked a question, but it did not report `working` when the answer arrived. Herdr correctly retained the last reported state.

- Report `working` only after the worker accepts the complete answer batch.
- Run the report before waking the worker so a fast turn cannot report `idle` first and then be incorrectly marked working.
- Keep failed submissions, stale answers, cancellation, and partially answered batches from reporting a resume.

No herdr code or protocol changes are needed.

## Testing

- Zig 0.17 build passed.
- Question-focused Zig unit tests passed: 161 tests, including the mutex ordering, allocation-failure, stale-response, cancellation, and batch-submission checks.
- `cd tests/e2e && FX_SOUND=0 bun test ./tui-decision-prompts.test.ts` passed: 54 tests, 834 assertions.
- New TTY tests exercise the built `./zig-out/bin/fx` with option answers, freeform answers, and immediate completion. They assert `idle → working → blocked → working → idle`, a live process, and empty stderr.
- The option and freeform regression tests fail on the pre-fix build with the expected missing `working` report.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

All required CI gates passed for `d6ea4dc0a3656c3cae30383cfea6432ff3d28402`, including Build & Test, deterministic E2E, Shellcheck, Startup Latency, and the macOS arm64 gate. The macOS detector intentionally skipped native platform jobs for this change.

Two E2E files passed only on the harness's retry on the same commit: [file-picker byte budget](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/pull/1563#issuecomment-6546351672) and [gateway-stream replay](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/pull/1563#issuecomment-6546372384). Both flaky results are documented; no root cause or fix for either flake is claimed.

The existing decision-prompt E2E owner remains verification-only in the PGSO corpus.

title: Read a backslash before a newline as a line continuation
body:
## Summary

- fx's shell word reader now treats a backslash before a newline as a line continuation, outside single quotes, as the shell does. It used to drop the backslash and keep the newline, so `printf "a\<newline>b"` read as `a<newline>b` while sh, dash, bash, and zsh all pass `ab`. #1491 listed newline among the characters a double-quoted backslash escapes but still kept the newline.
- A continuation between words starts no empty word: `a \<newline> b` reads as `a` and `b`.
- Auto mode already sends any command with a raw newline to review, so no review decision changes. The words fx reads for `/mcp` arguments and for the git push branch evidence now match the shell's.

## Testing

- `zig build test` passes, including the new test "tokenize_argv reads a backslash before a newline as a line continuation", whose command sh, dash, bash, and zsh all read as `ab`, `ab`, `c`.
- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test mcp-verbs.test.ts -t "joins a backslash-newline"` passes. The new test pastes `/mcp add probe -- /bin/echo "a\<newline>b"` into the shell and expects the saved argument `ab`; on main fx saved `a<newline>b`.
- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test auto-mode-reliability.test.ts` passes, 44 of 44.

title: Reject blank custom answers to multiple-choice questions
body:
## Summary

- Keep a multiple-choice question open when Enter is pressed on an empty or whitespace-only custom answer. Previously, fx submitted the blank answer and continued the turn.
- Leave the answer editable without advancing the batch or replacing a previously confirmed answer. Preserve blank values in value-only prompts and compact input submissions, where an empty string can be valid.
- Add unit and TUI regressions for blank submissions, continued editing, batch state, and valid answers after rejection.

## Testing

- `zig build` and `zig fmt --check src/core/agent/question_prompt.zig` passed with Zig 0.17.0.
- 45 focused ReleaseSafe Zig tests passed through a temporary wrapper importing `core/agent/question_prompt.zig`. The wrapper was removed afterward.
- `cd tests/e2e && FX_SOUND=0 bun test tui-decision-prompts.test.ts -t 'question'`: 26 passed, 0 failed.
- Manually ran the freshly built `./zig-out/bin/fx` in a live terminal with an isolated profile and local fake gateway. Empty and whitespace-only Enter left the question open without sending a follow-up request; entering a custom answer then submitted it. `/quit` exited with code 0 and empty stderr.
- `git diff --check` passed. The new unit and TUI regressions failed against the original behavior before the fix.

title: Ship the Linux x86_64 PGSO candidate in stable releases
body:
## Summary

- The stable release now ships the qualified Linux x86_64 PGSO candidate instead of a plain ReleaseSafe cross-compile. On this PR's Linux x86_64 PGSO run (41284880646), the candidate is 8,189,584 bytes (7.81 MiB) against 12,590,544 bytes (12.01 MiB) for the plain build, 35.0% smaller and 0.44 MiB under the 8.250 MiB ceiling.

The steps are unchanged: eligibility, the SHA-256 check against the manifest, the smoke test, and an archive with `fx`, `LICENSE`, and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. `release` waits for it.
- The release tests now cover both Linux targets, and the pin and secrets tests include the x86_64 workflow.
- `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `scripts/pgso/README.md` now say the stable release ships the Linux x86_64 candidate. `AGENTS.md` lists the 8.250 MiB Linux x86_64 ceiling and says the release builds, rather than cross-compiles, its binaries.
- macOS x86_64 keeps the plain build.
