title: Hold one compaction cycle in memory and read older cycles in Ctrl+O from the log
body:
## Summary

- The main screen holds the current compaction cycle, plus the previous one until the first turn after the compaction ends. Older turns leave memory once the session log has them and they have scrolled off screen.
- A resize reprints only the held cycles instead of the whole session.
- Resuming a session shows the turns since the newest compaction. A turn that a compaction split, such as one that overflowed the context window, shows in full.
- Resuming right after a compaction, before any new turn, shows the turns before it, as the screen showed them before fx quit.
- Ctrl+O reaches every compaction cycle. Its newest pages show the current and previous cycles, and scrolling up reads older cycles from the session log one cycle at a time.
- When Ctrl+O can't read an older cycle from the log, its footer says so, and PageUp tries again.
- Each agent and fx instance keeps its own window, and Ctrl+O reads the session of the agent on screen.
- The transcript no longer trims old rows by size. Command output stays capped at 1 MiB per command.
- Long sessions stay responsive. A frame sends the terminal parser only the bytes it has not seen, and worker events apply in 32 ms slices so input and painting keep running during bursts of tool output. In a 40-turn session with 2,400 tool calls, no main-thread stall exceeds 100 ms (main has more than 80, the longest over 2 s), and the last turn takes 3 s instead of 11 s.

## Why these pieces

- The transcript window decides what to drop by what the session log already holds and what is off screen. A byte cap can't do that: it trims by size, so it either lets memory grow or loses turns Ctrl+O should show.
- The frozen prefix renders finished entries once and resumes the render after them. Without it, every frame re-rendered every held entry, the cost that grew with the cycle.
- Ctrl+O reads one older cycle at a time from the log instead of keeping every cycle in memory, which is what the byte cap was there to prevent.

## Why one PR

The speedups were measured on top of the window, against the same 40-turn session. Feeding the parser only new bytes took the last turn from about 11 s to 3 s but left 88 stalls over 100 ms. The cursor walk's fast path for ASCII removed about a third of those, and the 32 ms event slices removed the rest. Landed apart, each would need its own baseline, and none of them alone gets the session under 100 ms.

## Before

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  worker[Worker events, all at once] --> runtime[Transcript runtime: every entry, trimmed at 1 MiB]
  runtime --> painter[Painter: parses the whole flow each frame]
  runtime --> ctrlo[Ctrl+O pages: the entries in memory only]
  log[(Session log)] -->|resume: every turn| runtime
```

## After

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  worker[Worker events, in 32 ms slices] --> runtime[Transcript runtime]
  runtime <--> window[Transcript window core: which cycles to hold, drop, and reprint]
  runtime --> prefix[Frozen prefix: render resumes after finished entries]
  prefix --> painter[Painter: parses only new bytes]
  runtime --> ctrlo[Ctrl+O pages]
  log[(Session log)] -->|resume: newest cycle| runtime
  log -->|older cycles, one at a time| ctrlo
```

## Verification

- `zig build test` passes. The prefix oracle now runs in every test build and compares each resumed render with a full one.
- `tests/tla/transcript_window/check.sh` passes: TLC on the model, both driver directions against the real core, every planted bug caught, and the built fx through compaction, Ctrl+O, and resume. CI runs it with `--ci` when the window's code or model changes.
- `tests/e2e/tui-transcript-window.test.ts` builds a session whose replies pass 1 MiB across six compactions. On this branch Ctrl+O reaches every cycle, live and after `--resume`. On main it stops before the oldest cycle.
- With `./zig-out/bin/fx` against a fake gateway: the 40-turn session above, and a 21-cycle session where Ctrl+O walks every cycle down and back up, live and after a resume.
- With two fx instances in one process, each with its own compaction cycles, Ctrl+O on each reaches only its own cycles, before and after switching between them.

## Known limits

- A damaged line in the session log can hide its compaction cycle from Ctrl+O, along with every older cycle except the first, because Ctrl+O can no longer find where those cycles start. fx keeps running and the newer cycles stay reachable, but nothing says turns are missing. #1590 adds a footer notice for this.
- Ctrl+O reads an older cycle on the main loop with no loading indicator. In the tests a cycle takes tens of milliseconds.
- Memory within one cycle is bounded by the model's context, plus command output capped at 1 MiB per command.

title: Keep network requests off the input loop
body:
## Summary

- A message sent during a running turn is queued at once instead of waiting for a login refresh. The turn refreshes a due token before its first request.
- A resumed request whose login is due for refresh now runs instead of being dropped.
- `/credits` checks the balance in the background and says "Checking credits…", so typing keeps working while the Gateway answers.
- Running `/credits` again while a check is in progress says the credits are still loading.
- `/credits` and `fx credits` stop after 30 seconds when the Gateway stalls.
- `/credits` renews a login that has come due in the background before it asks for the balance. When the login needs a new sign-in, it says to run `/login`.
- Retrying a prompt after a non-retryable login error refreshes in the background instead of freezing the terminal.
- When fx cannot start the task that renews a login, it shows the retryable refresh notice instead of renewing on the input loop.
- `/logout` signs out at once and revokes the session at the issuer in the background, with a warning if revocation fails. Quitting fx right after waits at most 2 seconds for the revocation.
- Grok logout deletes the local session before revoking its refresh token, so a failed deletion no longer leaves a revoked token saved.
- Starting a Vercel sign-in shows "Preparing sign-in…" at once and requests the device code in the background. Esc cancels the request.
- The team picker and the Vercel choice in `/provider` list teams in the background and say "loading teams..." until the list arrives. The teams request now has a deadline and a 4 MiB size limit, so a long team list still loads.
- Terminal tests fail when fx makes a network request on the input loop.

## Before and after

| Action, with a slow server | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Send a message during a turn while the login renews (token server takes 5 s) | Typing stops until the token server answers | Typed text shows within 1 s |
| `/credits` (Gateway takes 3 s) | Typing stops until the Gateway answers | Typed text shows within 1 s |
| `/logout` (issuer takes 3 s per revocation) | Typing stops for both revocations | "Signed out of fx." within 1 s |
| Quit right after `/logout` (issuer stalls) | `/logout` itself froze first | Exit waits at most 2 s |

The tests in `tui-auth-source-selection.test.ts` and `tui-slash-extra.test.ts` time each row; on `main` they fail at the 1 s check.

## Design

Every request that ran on the input loop now runs in a background task that the event loop polls each frame (it already polls every 8 ms). The input loop only reads finished results.

- **Queued prompts** reuse the turn's own refresh. The worker already renews a due token before each request, so the input loop only checks that a login exists. A second refresh path would have duplicated it.
- **`/credits`** runs in its own `std.Io` task that renews a due login, then asks for the balance. Credits have no worker of their own to borrow, and the lookup must be cancellable on exit.
- **Sign-in** requests its device code on the sign-in worker that already polls for the token. The worker now prepares first when it starts without a code, so no new thread is added.
- **Team lists** load in one `std.Io` task tagged with the screen that asked for it, so a list that arrives after that screen closes is dropped instead of opening a picker.
- **Revocation** after `/logout` runs in a `std.Io` task, because the local sign-out must not wait on the issuer. Shutdown waits 2 seconds, then cancels.
- **Cancellation** uses one `oauth_transport.Cancellable` wrapper that adds the task's cancel flag to every OAuth request.
- **The guard** marks the input loop thread and checks it where bounded HTTP requests and Gateway streams start. Terminal tests set `FX_TEST_INPUT_LOOP_NETWORK_GUARD=1`, which turns a request on the input loop into a panic. A review-only rule would not stop the next regression.

Before, on `main`:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph loop[Input loop]
    submit[Submit during a turn] --> refresh[OAuth refresh]
    credits[/credits/] --> creditsGet[Credits GET]
    logout[/logout/] --> revoke[Revoke at issuer]
    login[/login/] --> device[Discovery and device code]
    picker[Team pickers] --> teams[Team list]
  end
  refresh --> net((Network))
  creditsGet --> net
  revoke --> net
  device --> net
  teams --> net
```

After, on this PR:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph loop[Input loop]
    submit[Submit during a turn]
    credits[/credits/]
    logout[/logout/]
    login[/login/]
    picker[Team pickers]
    collect[Per-frame collectors]
  end
  subgraph tasks[Background tasks]
    turn[Turn worker refresh]
    creditsTask[Credits task]
    revokeTask[Revocation task]
    signIn[Sign-in worker]
    teamTask[Team list task]
  end
  submit --> turn
  credits --> creditsTask
  logout --> revokeTask
  login --> signIn
  picker --> teamTask
  turn --> net((Network))
  creditsTask --> net
  revokeTask --> net
  signIn --> net
  teamTask --> net
  creditsTask -. result .-> collect
  revokeTask -. result .-> collect
  signIn -. result .-> collect
  teamTask -. result .-> collect
```

title: Load MCP config changes made outside the session
body:
## Summary

- A running session loads MCP servers added, removed, or changed outside it, by `fx mcp` in a shell such as the agent's, another fx, or an edit to `~/.fx/mcp.json` or `.mcp.json`, when the next prompt is sent.
- Project servers approved or rejected in another fx are loaded the same way.
- `/mcp` commands and the `/mcp` menu load those changes first, so `/mcp login NAME` finds a server that `fx mcp add` added in a shell.
- Only the servers whose config changed restart. The others keep their processes and sign-ins.
- A prompt sent while a turn is running or queued keeps the current servers, and the next prompt after it loads the change.
- A server that a prompt just loaded, such as one that needs a login, stays on the status line instead of being cleared as already seen.
- A config change fx can't load keeps the current servers and warns once per change, saying what's wrong, such as `~/.fx/mcp.json isn't valid JSON`.
- `/mcp reload` and `fx mcp reload` now say that fx loads MCP config changes at the next prompt or `/mcp` command.

title: Measure a PGSO speed comparison again before failing it
body:
## Summary

- When a PGSO startup command or heavy workload fails only its speed comparison, `qualify.py` measures it once more and uses the second measurement. A real regression fails both measurements, and command failures and timeouts are still final.
- The retry writes into a `retry` subdirectory of that measurement's logs, so the first attempt's logs stay intact. The result keeps the failed comparison as `first_attempt`, and the job log prints `measuring again after a speed failure: <name> (p50 …, p95 …)`.
- The change is in `measure_with_one_retry`, which `measure_startup` and `measure_heavy_workloads` call for each command and workload. Both the single-job Linux workflows and the distributed macOS shards go through it.
- `scripts/compare_signed_macos.py` also calls `measure_startup`, but it only reports the latency of two notarized copies and a control-versus-control calibration, and it strips the PGSO pass/fail from its records. It passes `retry_speed_failures=False`, so it still reports one measurement per command.
- `scripts/pgso/README.md` describes the rule.

## Why

These measurements run on shared GitHub runners. On October 31, 2026, five PGSO run attempts on #1544 and #1546 failed a speed comparison when the candidate's median was about the same or faster. A few slow samples pushed the p95 over the 10% limit:

| Run | Platform | Comparison | p50 | p95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 41102227377 | macOS arm64 | `status --json` | −1.2% | +10.1% |
| 41187538622, attempt 1 | macOS arm64 | `--version` | −1.8% | +18.7% |
| 41187538622, attempt 2 | macOS arm64 | `--version` | −0.7% | +10.1% |
| 41242034180 | macOS arm64 | approval-payload | −14.1% | +12.1% |
| 41242034153 | Linux x86_64 | `help` | +3.8% | +18.5% |

Each failure needed someone to notice it and rerun it:

- On macOS, each comparison is its own job, and rerunning the failed job took under two minutes.
- On Linux, qualification is a single job, so a rerun repeats the whole build and qualification. The first attempt of 41242034153 took 1 hour 50 minutes.

The `status --json` and approval-payload failures passed on their reruns. `--version` failed on its rerun too, then passed in the next run of the same macOS code (41242034180). The x86_64 `help` failure is being rerun on #1546.

Other options were weaker:

- More samples make every run longer, and they don't stop a burst of slow moments from landing on one binary.
- A looser limit would also hide real regressions.
- Rerunning by hand is what happens now. It needs someone watching, and on Linux it repeats a two-hour job.

The retry measures only the failed comparison again, and only when it fails. Timings from a qualified Linux x86_64 run (41187538412) put one extra measurement at 1.0 to 2.3 seconds for a startup command. A heavy workload takes from 6.5 seconds (ui-activity) to about 13 minutes (file-index-100k, 785 seconds).

The tradeoff is that a candidate right at the 10% limit gets two chances, so it is somewhat more likely to pass. Allowing only one retry keeps that bounded, and a regression clearly over the limit still fails both measurements.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/pgso/tests -t .` with LLVM 22: 260 OK. Of those, 36 are the `test_qualify` tests, six of them new:
  - A startup speed failure is measured again into `logs/retry`, and the second measurement decides. The evidence carries `first_attempt`, and the job log shows the retry line.
  - A startup regression that repeats fails after exactly one retry.
  - A heavy workload speed failure is measured again into its own `retry` logs.
  - A heavy workload whose candidate crashes is not measured again.
  - A Hyperfine microbenchmark regression that repeats fails after exactly one retry.
  - With `retry_speed_failures=False`, a startup speed failure is measured once and records no first attempt.
- An existing startup test now also checks that a passing command is measured once and records no first attempt.
- `test_signed_macos` checks that every signed-comparison measurement passes `retry_speed_failures=False`. It runs with the other `ci.yml` scripts modules, all OK.
- Six mutants each fail at least one of these tests: no retry; retrying after execution failures; retrying twice; writing the retry over the first attempt's logs; ignoring `retry_speed_failures`; and the signed comparison leaving the retry on.
- `scripts/check-public-surface.sh`: OK.

title: Sign in to an MCP server when it is added
body:
## Summary

- `fx mcp add NAME URL` connects to a new HTTP server and, when it asks for a login, opens the browser and signs in the way `fx mcp login` does, waiting up to the login's five minutes.
- Where fx can't open a browser (SSH, `FX_NO_OPEN_BROWSER`, or Linux without a display), `fx mcp add` prints the `fx mcp login NAME` command instead of waiting.
- `/mcp add NAME URL` in the shell starts the same sign-in once the shell has loaded the server and it asks for a login. The address and the outcome show in the transcript, as for a typed `/mcp login`.
- `--no-login` on `fx mcp add` and `/mcp add` adds the server without signing in, and `fx mcp add --no-login` doesn't contact the server.
- Without `--no-login`, `fx mcp add` contacts a new HTTP server once to see whether it needs a login.
- A sign-in that fails or runs out of time leaves the server added, and add says how to sign in later.
- A server added with `--project` isn't signed in to, since it waits for approval first.
- `fx mcp add -h` and `/mcp add -h` list `--no-login`.

title: Trim shell results, group independent tool calls, and withhold images in blocks
body:
## Summary

- Shell results leave out fields that are null or false, so a command that printed nothing returns about 70 characters to the model instead of about 340.
- Shell results include `backend` and `persistence` with the session ID of a command the model can still use, and otherwise only when they differ from the default.
- `output_terminal_safe` appears only when unsafe bytes in the output were escaped.
- The system prompt asks the model to make tool calls that do not depend on each other together in one step.
- When a session holds more images than one request can carry, fx withholds the oldest ones a block at a time, so the cached conversation stays the same until the next block is withheld instead of changing with every new image.

title: Keep Claude's prompt cache warm while a session waits
body:
## Summary

- While an interactive or `fx acp` session on a Claude model through AI Gateway waits, fx resends its last request with a one-token reply limit 4.5 minutes after that request started and every 4.5 minutes after, so the next message reads the conversation from the prompt cache instead of writing it again.
- Pings stop 30 minutes after the last request started, and at the next request, `/new`, `/clear`, a resume, compaction, or exit.
- A ping that fails, writes the cache instead of reading it, or would go out more than 15 seconds late, such as after the machine sleeps, ends warming until the next request.
- Claude models that think by token budget are not pinged when a reasoning effort is set, since a one-token reply limit does not stop their thinking.
- Sessions with prompt caching turned off are not pinged.
- The tokens pings use are added to the session's usage when the next request starts.
- `"cache_warming": false` in settings turns pings off.
- `fx ask`, subagents, and apps that embed fx through the SDK never send pings.

## Why

Claude's prompt cache entry lives 5 minutes, and each read refreshes it at no extra cost ([Anthropic: prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching)). When a user pauses longer than that, to read a diff or run the code, the next message writes the whole conversation to the cache again at 1.25x the input price instead of reading it at 0.1x. A ping is the same request with a one-token reply, so it costs a cache read and one output token, and only while the session waits.

Two simpler options were not enough:

- **The 1-hour cache lifetime.** Anthropic charges 2x the input price for every 1-hour write, including the many follow-ups that arrive within 5 minutes anyway. Pings cost nothing on those turns.
- **A plain repeating timer.** It would keep pinging an abandoned session, ping an old conversation after `/new` or compaction, send a ping in the middle of the next real request, and pay a full write when it wakes after the machine slept. Each of those needs a rule, so the rules live in a small planner with no I/O, checked by a TLA+ model. Each mutation config in `tests/tla/cache_warming` plants one defect, and TLC reports the rule it breaks.

Pi's coding agent takes the same approach: a refresh at 90% of the lifetime, a one-token reply with no retries, a stop after sleep, and a 30-minute cap on idle warming ([cache-warmer.ts](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c2760d32cc8d3d4a9237c680883fad5fc6e34183/packages/coding-agent/src/core/cache-warmer.ts)).

## Design

Before, nothing runs between requests, and the cache entry expires 5 minutes after the last one:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[User] -->|prompt| O[Orchestrator]
  O -->|request| G[AI Gateway]
  G -->|reply, cache entry lives 5 min| O
  O -.->|next prompt after a long pause rewrites the cache| G
```

After, each conversation's `SessionRuntime` owns a warmer. The orchestrator arms it with the exact body of each completed request and disarms it before the next one. The warmer's `std.Io` task asks the planner when to ping and when to stop:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[User] -->|prompt| O[Orchestrator]
  O -->|request| G[AI Gateway]
  S[SessionRuntime] -->|owns, closes| W[Warmer task]
  O -->|arm after a completed request| W
  O -->|disarm before the next request| W
  W <-->|events and plans| P[Planner: cache_warming.step]
  W -->|same body, maxOutputTokens 1, every 4.5 min for up to 30 min| G
```

- `cache_warming.zig` is the planner. It is pure, with no clock, I/O, or allocation, and it decides which requests are warmed and when each ping is due or warming stops.
- `cache_warmer.zig` holds one copy of the last request, runs the timer as a `std.Io` task, and sends pings through `gateway_step` with the request's own credential and no retries.
- The TUI and `fx acp` pass the session's warmer to the agent. `/new`, `/clear`, resume, and compaction disarm it, and exit or closing an ACP session closes it.
- `cache_warming` is a profile setting, on by default, listed with the other settings for `fx config get` and the schema.
- `FX_TEST_CACHE_WARMING_TTL_MS` is an internal test hook that shortens the lifetime so the end-to-end tests finish in seconds. It is registered in `scripts/cli_shape_registry.json`.

## Testing

- `tests/tla/cache_warming/check.sh`: the model passes, and each of the 7 mutation configs fails on the rule it names.
- `bun tests/tla/drivers/cache_warming/driver.ts`: seeded event sequences run through the real planner against the model with no mismatches.
- `zig build test`: planner, warmer, and orchestrator flow tests, including exact ping bodies, the cap, a late wake, stale answers, cancel on close, and malformed bodies.
- End-to-end tests against a fake gateway, in `tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` and `acp.test.ts`:
  - pings resend the exact request, stop at the cap, and their usage is saved with the next prompt;
  - `/new` stops the pings;
  - `cache_warming: false` sends none;
  - an idle ACP session pings until the next session replaces it.

Docs for the setting are in vercel-labs/fx-web#238.

title: Durable UI stream: text deltas can arrive out of order with the bundled file World
A planned queue hand-off adds "Resuming from unexpected session interruption." to every queued turn, and the notices stack
body:
## Summary

With `vercel({ leaseMs })`, a queue delivery runs the turn by resuming it from the journal. Each such resume adds the user message "Resuming from unexpected session interruption." to the turn's steering, unless the turn yielded. A planned hand-off to the queue isn't a yield, so every queued turn tells the model it was interrupted when nothing failed.

The notices are never collapsed. Each resume appends one more, and they stay in the history, so later turns carry every earlier notice.

We observed this with the local queue. We haven't confirmed it on hosted Vercel Queues yet.

## Cause

From reading the source: `resumeCheckpoint` in `src/acp/libfx_journal.zig` copies the turn's saved steering and appends one notice when `yielded` is false (`const notices: usize = if (yielded) 0 else 1;`). Nothing checks for a notice already in the list. The function is the same in v0.0.14, v0.0.15 and v0.0.16, and `main` at 98286126 hasn't changed that file since v0.0.16.

## Effect on one run

One run with 17 model requests, every request body logged, once without the queue and once through it:

| | Without the queue | Through the queue |
|---|---|---|
| Requests carrying a notice | 0 of 17 | 12 of 17 |
| Notices per request | 0 | 1, or 2 in a later turn of the same session |
| Notices in the run | 0 | 15 (690 characters) |

- **Tokens.** One notice is 46 characters, roughly 10 to 15 input tokens (an estimate), so about 150 to 225 extra input tokens per run.
- **Prompt cache.** A notice stays at a stable position once added, so it doesn't break a cached prefix.
- **The message itself** is the cost that matters: on every queued turn, the model reads that its session was interrupted.
- **A real crash** adds one more notice on top.

## Possible fixes

Either is enough, and both are better:
- Treat a planned hand-off like a yield: no notice when the previous holder released the lease, or when the backstop delivery found no crash.
- Keep at most one resume notice per turn: drop earlier notices when a resume appends a new one.

title: Reduce repetitive shell output sent to the model
body:
Shell results become input to the model's next step. Successful test runs can add hundreds of repetitive pass lines, consuming context without changing the outcome. Add an optional `rtk` setting to trim that repetition inside fx.

fx runs the command normally, then filters a copy of its result before preparing the model request. Native Zig rules recognize passing Bun, Cargo, and Zig test lines and English Git status advice. Diagnostics and summaries remain visible; failed, incomplete, truncated, terminal-backed, and unsupported results pass through. Terminal output and saved history retain the original, which the model can retrieve with `read_tool_result`.

Enable with `fx config set rtk true`, or `fx ask --config rtk=true` for one run. It defaults to off, is profile-only, and applies to terminal, headless, and ACP sessions and their subagents. Disabled requests bypass the reducer. No RTK binary, copied RTK code, or runtime dependency is added.

## Benchmarks

18 workloads: nine project-test runs (373 test executions, with overlapping suites), five Git cases, and four generated scale/failure cases. Each command executes once; the saved original model view and reduced request share the same metadata and surrounding prompt. Counts use tiktoken 0.12.0, `o200k_base`, with omission notices included.

| Workload | Visible output tokens | Output reduction | Prompt + tools JSON tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Bun configured-provider tests (52 tests) | 1147 → 171 | 85.1% | 5412 → 4390 (18.9% less) |
| Bun combined project suites (63 tests) | 1411 → 184 | 87.0% | 5698 → 4414 (22.5% less) |
| Zig MCP core subset (105 tests) | 2444 → 124 | 94.9% | 6756 → 4336 (35.8% less) |
| Zig MCP protocol subset (53 tests) | 1086 → 47 | 95.7% | 5347 → 4257 (20.4% less) |
| Git status, 50 modified + 100 untracked | 1035 → 1004 | 3.0% | 5663 → 5618 (0.8% less) |
| Bun generated scale: 200 passing tests | 1877 → 1813 | 3.4% | 6282 → 6213 (1.1% less) |
| Git status, 500 modified + 500 untracked, clipped | 5124 → 5124 | 0.0% | 11417 → 11417 (0.0% less) |
| Bun failure control: 200 pass, 1 fail | 1915 → 1915 | 0.0% | 6332 → 6332 (0.0% less) |

The existing 16 KiB inline-result cap matters: clipped logs are left unchanged and save 0%, as do failed, clean, and unsupported controls. Very fast Bun tests without timing markers mostly remain unchanged. Request counts are a serialized-input context proxy, not provider-reported usage or cost savings. Later full-output reads can offset savings.

[Full 18-workload results, both encodings, reproducible commands, and exclusions](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/blob/284d49d457c44586ee00315e31620a6bb42608b4/benchmarks/rtk.md).

## Validation

Linux container: ReleaseSafe build, 8 RTK behavior unit tests, 10 CLI/ACP/TUI scenarios, and 5 benchmark captures pass. The Linux binary grows by 13.4 KiB (0.11%). The expanded benchmark has 18 passing captures and 126 assertions. Full CI and macOS verification await maintainer approval.

## Docs

- [Configuration](https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/configuration): add profile-only `rtk`, boolean, default `false`, plus enable/unset and per-run override examples.
- [Tools](https://fx.sh/docs/capabilities/tools): describe supported reductions, conservative fallbacks, preserved terminal/history output, and retrieval through `full_output_handle` and `read_tool_result`.

These manual pages are maintained separately. Contributor instructions, development setup, and workflows are unchanged by this patch.

title: Fix Ctrl-Backspace word deletion
body:
## Summary

Fix Ctrl-Backspace deleting one character instead of the previous word when a terminal reports the Control modifier. Decode Ctrl-Backspace as the existing backward-word deletion action for Kitty CSI u and modifyOtherKeys reports.

- Preserve Cmd-Backspace line deletion and the existing Backspace, Ctrl-H, and Option-Backspace behavior.
- Cover Shift and lock modifiers, press/repeat/release events, and Cmd modifier precedence in parser tests.
- Exercise Unicode word deletion in the middle of a multiline draft through the built binary. Give the existing line-deletion test an isolated profile as well.

Raw Ctrl-H (`0x08`) remains a character delete. Terminals that send the same byte for Ctrl-Backspace cannot distinguish those keys without a terminal key binding.

## Validation

- Reproduced the bug before the fix: the new parser regression failed with `expected .delete_word_left, found .remapped_byte`.
- Zig 0.17.0 build: passed.
- Focused Zig input escape-parser tests: 67 passed. Used a temporary test entry point importing `src/ui/input/runtime.zig` with `--test-filter 'input escape parser' -lc`.
- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test tui-input-line-delete.test.ts` from `tests/e2e`: 7 passed, 0 failed on macOS arm64. The built `zig-out/bin/fx` stayed alive and stderr stayed empty for each interaction.
- Zig formatting and `git diff --check`: passed.

The existing E2E file remains verification-only in the PGSO corpus. No new E2E file or classification change is needed.

CI passed for commit `0719b139fdb8271962eb4d6838b8b02b5df1509e`: [Build & Test, all deterministic E2E shards, and SDK checks](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/actions/runs/41500638629), [macOS arm64 unit tests and both platform E2E shards](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/actions/runs/41500641419), startup latency, Shellcheck, and all four release-target binary builds and smoke tests. Earlier macOS runs were superseded by the label-triggered run, not retried for a code failure.

The ten-minute automated-review window ended at 18:36:42 UTC on November 2, 2026 with no review received. No Vade check was reported. The PR remains draft because the repository's final ship gate was not available in this environment.

## Docs

Update [Keyboard shortcuts](https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/keyboard-shortcuts), under **Delete text**, to list `ctrl+backspace` alongside `option+backspace` for deleting the previous word. State that Ctrl-Backspace needs a terminal that reports its modifier separately; a terminal that sends Ctrl-H for this key keeps character deletion and needs a terminal key binding to distinguish it. The manual source is maintained outside this public repository and is not changed in this PR.

title: Ask the model to continue when it stops without a reply
body:
## Summary

- When a reply stops for `other` with no text and no tool call, such as Gemini's `UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL`, fx asks the model once to call its next tool or give its answer instead of ending the turn with "Done.".
- fx shows "The model stopped without a reply (provider reason: UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL). Asking it to continue." when it sends that request.
- If the next reply is empty too, or no step is left, the turn ends as failed with "The model stopped without a reply (provider reason: UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL). Continue with a follow-up prompt if needed." and `fx ask` exits 1.
- Each separate stall in a long turn gets its own request to continue.
- When steering or a subagent's report continues the turn after an empty reply, fx sends no request to continue and saves no "Done." for the empty reply.
- Replies with text, and empty replies that finish with `stop` or `length`, behave as before.
- The trace log records the provider's own finish reason as `provider_finish_reason=`, and `/trace` network lines show it as `provider_stop_reason=`.

## Why

The AI SDK reports every Gemini finish reason it does not list as `other` ([map-google-finish-reason.ts](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/google/src/map-google-finish-reason.ts)), so a Gemini reply that stops with `UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL` arrives with no text, no tool call, and finish reason `other`. fx counted that as a finished turn and printed its own "Done.", so the task stopped halfway with nothing saying why. In one reported session, such a step ran for 136 seconds and used 8,621 output tokens before returning nothing.

Two simpler options were not enough:

- **End the turn with the notice right away.** The model stopped mid-task, and it can usually go on when asked. In a live check through AI Gateway, with a local proxy replacing one reply with this stop, 11 models from 10 providers each picked the task back up after the request to continue.
- **Treat the stop as an error and let request recovery resend it.** A resend repeats the same input, and fx would show the stop as a gateway error. Gemini CLI retries these stops and, after an empty response, adds a message at the end of the conversation that asks for a final answer or a tool call ([geminiChat.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts)), which is what the request to continue does.

The request goes out once per stall. A second empty reply in a row ends the turn as failed, so a model that keeps stalling cannot loop. Empty replies that finish with `stop` can be a deliberate end, so they are left alone.

## Design

Before, the step loop counts an empty `other` reply as a finished turn:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  G[AI Gateway] -->|finish other, no text, no tool call| L[Step loop]
  L -->|counted as completed| D["Turn ends with Done."]
```

After, steering or a subagent's report continues the turn first, the first stall gets one request to continue, and a second stall in a row fails the turn with the reason:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  G[AI Gateway] -->|finish other and raw reason, no text, no tool call| L[Step loop]
  L -->|steering or a subagent's report| C[Continue with it]
  L -->|first stall| N[Notice and one request to continue]
  N -->|next step| G
  L -->|second stall in a row, or no step left| F[Turn fails with the notice]
  G -->|raw reason| T[Trace log and /trace]
```

- The step loop in `orchestrator.zig` handles the stop beside the other ways a step ends without a tool call. The request to continue goes into the turn the same way as the silent-tool continuation, and the failure goes through `finishFailedTurnWithNotice` like the other failed turns.
- Steering or a subagent's report that continues the turn after an empty reply adds no assistant message when there is no text and nothing to replay, as after a cancel, so the next request never carries a "Done." the model did not write.
- `ProviderFinishRaw` keeps the provider's reason inline on each completion, cut to 48 printable bytes, so a completion owns no new memory. Only the AI Gateway stream fills it; for other providers the notice names the finish reason instead.
- `tests/tla/agent_runtime/EmptyReply.tla` models these rules, with six planted mutations that each break a named rule, and a driver runs real `fx ask` turns of the built binary against the model. CI runs both on every pull request, beside the recovery model.
- The `provider_finish_raw` fuzz target covers the bounded copy of the raw reason.

title: Fail a subagent's call to a tool it can't reach, not its turn
body:
Stacked on #1534.

## Problem

A subagent that calls an MCP tool it hasn't selected yet ends its whole turn with `agent_turn_failed: UnsupportedTool`. A root session that makes the same call loads the tool through `advertiseUnselectedMcpCalls` and runs it. When that lookup finds nothing, the root falls back to a failed tool result it can recover from. This reproduces on the subagents v2 stack (#1438, #1448, #1534).

This PR fixes only the fatal error, so a child's call now fails recoverably. A child still doesn't load the tool the way the root does, even when the server is within its access: its `resolve_unselected_mcp_tool` lookup returns nothing. That's a separate follow-up.

### Repro

Build this branch's base (`fazxes/mailbox`) and run:

```sh
./zig-out/bin/fx ask --auto --json -- 'Call the subagent tool with action "message", agent "probe", and the message: "Your very first tool call must be mcp_linear_list_teams with arguments {}. Do not call mcp_select_tool first." Then wait for its report and reply with it verbatim.'
```

Before this change, `probe` reports:

```
Subagent failed: agent_turn_failed: UnsupportedTool. Earlier tool calls may have completed; their effects are not rolled back.
```

## Cause

v2 sets `live_tool_authority` for every subagent, so each child call first resolves its permission target in `resolveLiveToolAuthority`. For a tool that is neither registered nor an available dynamic tool, `permissionTargetForLiveAuthority` raises `error.UnsupportedTool`. `permissionTargetResolutionFailureMessage` maps only path errors, so the error went up and ended the turn. A root session never reaches that check: the call falls through to the dispatcher, which returns a semantic failure.

## Fix

- `permissionTargetForCall` in `tooling/tool_admission.zig` now splits a call that has no target the same way the dispatcher does (`tool_mcp_registry.resolve`):
  - With an MCP runtime and the name not advertised this step, it raises `error.DynamicToolNotSelected`.
  - Otherwise, it raises `error.UnsupportedTool`. That includes a selected tool outside the child's admitted servers, and any call when no MCP runtime is running.
- `resolveLiveToolAuthority` in `orchestrator.zig` maps those errors to the dispatcher's text: the "Dynamic MCP tool not selected" message, which says to call `mcp_select_tool`, or `Unsupported tool: <name>`. Both arrive as a tool failure, not a turn failure.

The call still never executes, and the live authority provider isn't asked about it, so child access doesn't widen. Nothing is selected automatically. Nothing else depends on `error.UnsupportedTool` by name. The two `try deps.permission_target_for_call(...)` grant paths in `orchestrator.zig` only run without live authority, and a root call to an unknown tool resolves to an ordinary `.once` decision, so they never see either error.

## Tests

- `a call with no target splits into unselected and unsupported like the dispatcher` (`tool_admission.zig`)
- `child call to an unselected dynamic tool fails the call and the turn continues`
- `child call to a selected tool outside its admission is refused and the turn continues`
- New cases in `child target failures settle the batch before and after permission without effects`: before permission for `DynamicToolNotSelected`, and after permission, through the revalidation loop, for `UnsupportedTool`.

The two child tests fail on the base and pass with the fix. The `child `, `live authority`, `dynamic MCP`, `permission target`, `Unsupported tool`, and `not selected` test groups pass, and `zig fmt --check src/` is clean.

End to end with `./zig-out/bin/fx`: the child's first `mcp_linear_list_teams` call failed with `DynamicToolNotSelected` and got the not-selected message, the child called `mcp_select_tool`, retried, and reported the team list to the parent. The child finished with outcome `ok`, and stderr contained only progress lines.

title: Set the PGSO size ceilings from current candidate sizes
body:
## Summary

- Set each PGSO size ceiling from the current candidate size, leaving about 0.3 MiB of growth room beyond the 0.250 MiB preferred headroom: 6.500 MiB for macOS arm64 (was 7.000), 6.750 MiB for Linux arm64 (was 7.000), and 8.750 MiB for Linux x86_64 (was 8.250).
- Linux x86_64 now fails qualification on `main`: its candidate measures 8.156 MiB, which meets the 8.250 MiB ceiling but not the preferred headroom. The stable release needs that qualification to package Linux (`release` needs `package-linux`, which needs `build-linux-x86_64`), so a release from `main` fails until the ceiling rises or the binary shrinks.
- Rename the ceiling test, since Linux x86_64 is no longer the only platform with a ceiling above macOS's, and update the ceilings in `scripts/pgso/README.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

This replaces #1550, which added per-platform ceilings that #1544 has since added on `main`.

## Ceilings

| Platform | Candidate | Ceiling | Growth room beyond the 0.250 MiB headroom |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| macOS arm64 | 5.927 MiB (6,214,976 bytes) | 6.500 MiB | 0.323 MiB |
| Linux arm64 | 5.942 MiB (6,231,136 bytes) on the earlier `main` | 6.750 MiB | about 0.3 MiB after the same growth |
| Linux x86_64 | 8.156 MiB (8,552,320 bytes) | 8.750 MiB | 0.344 MiB |

macOS and Linux x86_64 sizes are from this PR's runs on `main` `0d1b727f8`. Between the first two pushes, `main` gained #1534, #1447, #1448, #1438, and #1581, and the candidates grew by 213,408 bytes on macOS and 293,400 bytes on Linux x86_64. The first two commits used tighter ceilings (6.000 and 6.250, then 6.250 and 6.500 MiB), which that growth outran.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/pgso/tests -t .` passes (265 tests).
- `scripts/check-public-surface.sh` passes.
- This commit's PGSO runs qualify each candidate against its new ceiling.

title: Say in Ctrl+O when a damaged log line hides older history
body:
## Summary

- When Ctrl+O reads older history and stops at a damaged session log line, its footer reads "part of older history couldn't be read · fx doctor · esc close". `fx doctor` names the session and the `fx session recover` command that copies its good turns into a new session.
- Once shown, the notice stays until the transcript is cleared, as `/new` does, including after Ctrl+O closes and reopens. The damaged line is still in the log, so the same cycles stay missing.
- When the damage hides the cycle Ctrl+O asked for, Ctrl+O stays on the pages it has and does not offer a retry.
- A cycle that was read whole shows no notice, even when a damaged line comes right after it in the log.

Stacked on #1569.

title: Clear and redraw the terminal after a ctrl+g update reload
body:
## Summary

- Pressing ctrl+g to load an installed update clears the terminal and its scrollback, then draws the resumed conversation from the top, the way a resize redraws it. The new build no longer prints a second copy below the old screen.
- Shell output from before fx started is cleared too, as it is on resize.
- When the session had no saved turn, the fresh session the update opens is drawn on a cleared terminal, so the welcome banner appears once.
- The debug trace records when an update reload, `/resume`, or `/fork` clears the terminal and its scrollback.

title: Keep ANSI in ACP command output when the client asks
body:
## Problem

- `fx acp` strips ANSI from live command output chunks, so a client that renders a terminal shows plain text while a command runs.
- The completed update keeps escapes in its 200-byte preview, so color appears only after the command ends, and only for that preview.

## Changes

- `initialize` accepts `_meta.fx.ansiOutput: true`. Command output chunks then keep their escapes.
- Without it, chunks are stripped as before.
- `agentCapabilities._meta.fx.ansiOutput` advertises the option.
- Tests cover initialize parsing, the capability, and one chunk sent with and without the option.

## Visual proof

Same command, mid-run, rendered by an ACP client with wterm.

Before (main):

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cce54209-1fe9-4f54-a50b-01c4fa819aaa)

After:

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/de9ab654-95f2-44b3-a268-e12257b0b9de)

## Docs

- https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/acp, "Session updates": add "Command output chunks in `tool_call_update` are plain text. A client that renders terminal escapes can set `_meta.fx.ansiOutput: true` on `initialize` to receive output as printed. fx advertises support in `agentCapabilities._meta.fx.ansiOutput`."

title: Point the interrupted-turn hint at /resume
body:
## Summary

- Plain `fx` shows `Interrupted turn · /resume to continue` when the latest session in the workspace has an unfinished turn, instead of telling you to quit and relaunch with `fx -c`.

## Before and after

After fx is killed mid-request, plain `fx` in the same workspace shows:

```
before: * session: Interrupted turn · fx -c to continue
after:  * session: Interrupted turn · /resume to continue
```

The new e2e test follows that advice from the fresh session: `/resume`, then Enter, sends the interrupted request again without quitting.

## Docs

vercel-labs/fx-web#244 updates the sessions page to name `/resume`.

title: Print the unit test count in CI
body:
## Summary

- The `Build & Test` unit test step prints Zig's build summary, so its log ends with how many unit tests passed.

## Before and after

The end of the unit test step in the `Build & Test (ReleaseSafe)` log:

```
before (main, 0d1b727f8): Unit tests elapsed: 826s
after  (this PR):         Build Summary: 21/21 steps succeeded; 10578/10604 tests passed (26 skipped)
                          Unit tests elapsed: 584s
```

title: Sort host records and profiles with the shared stable sort
body:
## Summary

- Sort in `host_record.staleGroups` and `profiles.list` with `sort_utils.sort` instead of `std.mem.sort`. Each `std.mem.sort` call generates a separate block sort, with its merge and rotate helpers, for its element type; between two PGSO runs on 2026-11-02 the release binary's `sort.block` code grew from 14,592 to 29,864 bytes. `sort_utils.sort` takes the same arguments, is also stable, and shares one implementation across element types.
- Add an `AGENTS.md` line next to the shared JSON parser naming `sort_utils.sort`, and the code that keeps `std.mem.sort` because it cannot import it (`src/core/indexer/`, `src/core/session_manager/`, and files that import only `std`, such as `src/core/mcp_host/mcp_call.zig`).

## Size

A shaped local replay of the macOS arm64 PGSO candidate on `main` `0d1b727f8`:

| | File | `__text` |
|---|---:|---:|
| `main` | 6,114,848 | 5,237,860 |
| This PR | 6,082,016 | 5,215,212 |

That saves 32,832 bytes (two pages).

## Testing

- `zig build test` passes, including the three `staleGroups` tests that check the order it returns.
- On the built binary: `tui-host-instances.test.ts` 32/32, `ask-presentation.test.ts` 20/20, `mcp-stdio.test.ts` 108/108, and `acp.test.ts` 156 pass (13 key-gated tests skipped); one `acp.test.ts` test failed once and passed on four reruns, and passes twice on `main`. `cli.test.ts` fails only its `update_channel` assertion, which fails the same way on `main` locally.

title: Limit subagents to two levels and mark messages from turns the user typed
body:
## Summary

- A message a subagent sends its parent during a turn the user typed on its screen now carries `"started_by":"user"`, as reports already do. The words stay the subagent's.
- Subagents nest two levels deep. A subagent's own subagents are not offered the `subagent` tool, and a call to it is refused.
- In auto mode, the reviewer holds a command that prints a stored token or key after the user said not to read credentials in 14 of 15 runs, up from 10 of 15 on main, measured interleaved on the same scenarios. Workspace deletes are unchanged at 39 of 45.
- With several instances open, herdr shows the busiest one: blocked over working, and working over idle. Before, any instance that finished a turn reported idle. fx now works out the state from every agent at the end of each main-loop pass and sends it only when it changes, because the pane's state also changes when no turn ends or asks for attention: an approval answered, a prompt queued, an instance closed. The per-turn herdr hooks are removed.
- Three tests that failed on slow runners now wait on what they check: the command runner's cancel test, the file picker's memory check, and the ACP session contention test.
- Three E2E races that passed only on retry are fixed: the trace test's subagent report could cut main's steps short, the ultrafast launch-flag test could match its own typed prompt, and the subagent profile test could count the builder's requests before the builder sent one.
- The TLA+ session manager runtime driver starts its subagent with `message` instead of the removed `run`.

Merge after #1601. Until then, an Enter with nothing typed on a subagent's screen leaves a turn open that stops the parent's next work for that subagent from starting, and the `started_by` marker reads the same record.

title: Keep a turn going when a command fails again after an edit
body:
## Summary

- When the model writes or edits a file and reruns a command that failed, a new failure goes back to the model instead of ending the turn.
- The same command failing in three steps in a row with no file change still ends the turn with "Repeated identical shell failures stopped the tool loop." Two failures in a row used to be enough.
- A write or edit that fails does not count as a file change, so a failing edit plus the same failing command still ends the turn on the third step.

title: Fix a race in the Esc drop test
body:
## Summary

- The Esc drop test in `tui-host-switch.test.ts` now sends main's second message only once the subagent's request is out. Sent sooner, the subagent's turn took the message into that request, so the stop had nothing to drop and the test failed.
- Run 24 times on a loaded machine, the test failed once on main and never with this change.

title: Port provider-aware model backend and model hub
body:
## Summary

- Port provider-keyed model catalogs, discovery, metadata, roles and fallback selection from Proto for the providers already supported by proto-fx.
- Replace the staged model picker with the native model hub. `/model` opens it; selection, role assignment and provider changes use typed runtime operations.
- Carry provider-specific request options through the real transports, including Codex session state, Cursor images and discovery, Anthropic controls, Gemini through OpenCode Zen, and device/key authentication.
- Preserve this checkout's existing policy that Vercel Gateway is not an available product connection.

## Remaining before review

Local integration checks pass on `7639c16c156f5fbcc33c713bb65113ad6fa9a0d0`. Exact-commit CI is running; the final ship gate remains pending.

This checkout already diverged from upstream before this port (182 commits ahead and 154 behind at draft creation). To preserve that work, deterministic CI runs in a verification-only fork PR against the original checkout commit. The upstream draft has merge conflicts unrelated to selecting a verification baseline; resolving the existing branch divergence is separate from this port. The baseline-preserving CI run is tracked in [the verification PR](https://github.com/myanvoos/fx/pull/1).

## Verification

Final local snapshot: native build; 205 focused Zig tests; 62 configured-provider/corpus-shard tests; both changed `/model` TUI tests (19 assertions); WASM core build and SDK smoke; formatting and architecture/public-surface checks all pass.

Runtime interactions exercised:

- Native model-hub TUI: `/model` (and rejection of `/models`), custom role creation, workspace-scoped role assignment, cross-provider selection, actual request model/credential, clean exit and empty stderr.
- Actual model-hub mouse motion, drag, wheel and rendered-row clicks; observed TTFT/token rate appears after a request and persists across restart. Both runs exit cleanly.
- Configured Chat reasoning replay and saved-session continuation; seven permission-review response recovery cases, including refusal and incomplete streams.
- Provider-keyed discovery for all six supported configured discovery modes, including live refresh after seeded metadata and durable cache writes.
- Cursor live catalog CLI request with its provider-owned credential; seeded catalogs refresh from the source.
- Cursor text and image requests through the built binary and local protobuf/Connect service, including transmitted PNG data and usage.
- Oversized CLI context promotes to the configured larger provider/model with its credential and reports the serving model.
- Native configured Responses V1 and V2 compaction through the real TUI, including endpoint/model/trigger policy and replay in the next request. Both paths exit cleanly.
- Two-turn ACP Codex fixture: WebSocket reuse, low-to-high effort configuration update, deliberate disconnect, and full-context SSE recovery without stale response chaining.
- Model-selection refresh preserves credential ownership; cross-provider TUI selection and a subsequent request exit cleanly with no supervisor panic.
- ACP configured-provider switching, explicit saved models and staged credential ownership.
- Grok device-code login and OpenRouter pasted-key validation against local auth fixtures.
- Gemini image + thought + tool-call replay and per-model endpoint override; OpenCode Go preset request through an explicit local endpoint; Anthropic Messages and Claude Code executable request paths.
- Cross-provider fallback: first endpoint fails, second endpoint receives its own credential and succeeds; CLI reports the serving model.
- CLI web search routes a configured conversation through its Codex worker credential and back, reporting the actual search provider.
- WebAssembly core build and core SDK smoke: prompt, stream, usage, checkpoint and close.
- Compactor/indexer/recovery boundaries, public-surface check and deterministic E2E corpus/shard classification checks.

Existing changed E2E owners retain their verification-only corpus classification; no new root E2E file is introduced.

## Docs

The authenticated contributor cannot access the private manual repository. Update the following manual pages with these changes:

- https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/models, “Browse and select”: replace the staged picker description with: “Run `/model`, or press Ctrl+P, to open the model hub. The sidebar contains Roles, All models, and provider catalogs. Use the arrow keys to move between the sidebar and model list, type to search, and press Enter to select. Escape closes the hub. F5 refreshes the selected provider, or all providers from All models. Each provider keeps its own credentials, catalog and refresh status.” Remove examples passing model IDs, effort or speed as `/model` arguments; use the hub, `/effort`, `/fast`, `/ultrafast`, or process-level model flags instead.
- https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/models, “Reasoning effort”: replace the automatic post-selection step with “Highlight a model and press Ctrl+T to choose its reasoning effort. `/effort` still changes the current model's effort.” Add a “Model roles” section: “Use the Roles sidebar to edit assignments and ordered fallbacks, including custom roles. From a model row, Ctrl+R selects workspace or global scope and then the role. Workspace assignments are personal profile overrides, not committed project settings. Provider-qualified selections keep the selected provider's own credentials and request policy.” Add: “In Roles, Enter chooses an assignment, `f` adds a fallback, `t` changes thinking, `x` clears, `c` toggles cycle membership, and `[`/`]` reorder. `n` creates a custom role, `r` renames it, `d` deletes it, `T` edits its tag, and `b` edits its bank.”
- https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/custom-model-connections: document `~/.proto-fx/models.json` provider defaults and partial `model_metadata` overrides. List display name/description, per-million-token costs, context/output limits, reasoning, tokenizer, endpoint/headers, compatibility, context promotion and remote compaction metadata. Clarify that model headers override provider headers case-insensitively and explicit per-model endpoints take precedence. Add configured discovery modes `ollama`, `llama.cpp`, `lm-studio`, `openai-models-list`, `proxy`, and `litellm`, with `timeout_ms` and `inject_v1` for the OpenAI model-list mode. Native Codex/Grok overrides change metadata and request policy without changing their authentication or transport identity.
- https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/configuration: document `model_roles`, `model_tags`, role banks, ordered role cycles, fallback chains, and `context_promotion_enabled` as profile-owned settings with workspace overrides where supported. Explain that `.fx.json` remains restricted to repository-safe defaults. Use `model_roles` (role name to comma-separated selector chain), `model_role_bank` (role name to a selector or selector array), `model_tags` (role name to `tag`, `name`, `color`, and `hidden`), `cycle_order` (role-name array), and `fallback_chains` (selector to fallback chain). Provider-qualified selectors have the form `provider/model`; a role reference has the form `@role`.
- https://fx.sh/docs/getting-started/authentication, Grok: replace the manual callback/browser-code instructions with “Sign-in displays a verification URL and user code. Complete authorization in the browser while proto-fx polls the device-code request. Expiry or rejection leaves the existing credential unchanged; run `/login` again to retry.” OpenRouter: add “Pasted keys are checked using OpenRouter's key-information endpoint before they are saved. A rejected key does not replace the saved credential.”
- https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/context-compaction: document explicit larger-context promotion targets and provider-native compaction eligibility, including configured Responses compact endpoints and Codex streaming compaction. Explain that a configured compaction model can belong to another provider and uses that provider's credential. Provider replay state is retained with the compacted conversation.
- https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/slash-commands and https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/keyboard-shortcuts: document bare `/model` as the sole model-picker slash command; remove argument syntax and the staged inline model/effort/speed picker. Add the hub's role, thinking and refresh shortcuts.
- https://fx.sh/docs/capabilities/vision: include Cursor image support and Gemini through OpenCode Zen. Do not imply a new native Google, Bedrock or Azure provider.

The SDK's public JavaScript configuration shape is unchanged; native profile configuration is not a new JavaScript SDK option.

title: Copy mostly zero constants as a zero fill and their nonzero stores
body:
## Summary

- `sparse-constants` rewrites a copy from an internal constant into stores of the constant's defined leaves, which suits Zig's mostly undefined `return error.X` results. It skipped any constant with more than 16 leaves or 128 defined bytes, and it counts zeros as defined, so the default value of a large struct, whose fields are almost all zero, stayed a constant. The few pointers in such a value keep all of its bytes in relocated data (`__DATA_CONST`).
- When the leaf stores alone exceed those limits, the pass now copies the constant as a zero fill of the copied bytes followed by stores of its nonzero leaves, at most 64 leaves and 512 bytes. Every other byte the constant defines is zero, and an undefined byte may hold zero, so the destination ends up the same.
- Constants within the old limits keep the leaf stores they had. The nonzero-leaf walk is the one `zero-fill-globals` already uses, now with its limits as parameters.

## Size

An exact local replay of this PR's base (`main` `f4fea5eb0`, CI's seed bitcode and merged profile; it reproduces CI's `__TEXT` segment and sections byte for byte), rerunning the stages from `sparse-constants` on:

| | File | `__DATA_CONST` | `__DATA_CONST,__const` | `__TEXT,__const` | `__text` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `main` | 6,180,576 | 196,608 | 181,056 | 356,600 | 5,313,724 |
| This PR | 6,147,744 | 163,840 | 152,368 | 352,152 | 5,320,808 |

That saves 32,832 bytes (two pages). The pass now rewrites 949 constants instead of 894 (55 through the zero fill) and 1,734 copies instead of 1,636. The largest are two 7,568-byte default values of an agent's state, copied in `App.init` and the agents runtime, and a 5,536-byte default screen.

On today's base (`main` `2cb0b4486`), the PR's macOS arm64 PGSO candidate is 6,214,976 bytes with `__DATA_CONST` at 163,840, two pages below the 196,608 of the `main` candidates measured this week. All three PGSO candidates (macOS arm64, Linux arm64, Linux x86_64) pass every release gate.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/pgso/tests -t .` passes (269 tests). New tests check that a mostly zero default value becomes one zero fill and its three nonzero stores, that the rewritten copy reads back every byte under LLVM's interpreter over a destination filled with 0xAB, that a constant with 65 nonzero leaves keeps its copy, and that small constants keep their leaf stores without a zero fill. Planting each of four bugs (no zero fill, zero leaves stored, a zero fill for every constant, no leaf limit) fails at least one test.
- On the replayed candidate: `--version`, `help`, `help ask`, `sessions`, `status`, `doctor` (twice), `mcp list`, `session last`, `ask` without a prompt, an unknown command, and `provider` print byte-identical output and exit codes to `main`'s candidate.

title: Keep the tab title on the agent on screen and open subagent turns only when text is sent
body:
## Summary

- The terminal tab shows the title of the agent on screen. Before, whichever agent last got a title took over the tab, so a subagent's title could replace main's while main was on screen, and switching agents never changed it.
- Pressing Enter with nothing typed on a subagent's screen no longer opens a turn there. fx opened the turn's work in the parent's log before checking for text, and nothing closed it until the next real turn. After a restart, crash repair reported that turn as interrupted and woke the parent for a full turn about work that never ran. While it stayed open, the parent's next work for that subagent never started. The work now opens only once the text is queued.
- A subagent turn the user started keeps that through a restart. The spawn line records `by`, and the report crash repair sends carries `"started_by":"user"`. Before, repair's finish had no data, so the parent couldn't tell it from its own work.
- Unit tests in `main.zig` that switch agents write their terminal output to `/dev/null`. A switch now sets the tab title, and writing it to the test runner's stdout broke the build protocol.

## Testing

- `zig build test` passes.
- New E2E tests in `tui-host-switch`: the tab title follows a switch to a subagent and back, an empty Enter on a subagent's screen opens no work, and a turn typed on a subagent's screen that fx dies during reaches main after a resume as the user's. All three fail on main. The file passes 23/23.
- `tui-host-instances` 32/32, `tui-slash-menu` 36/36, `tui-permissions` 25/25.
- New unit tests cover the spawn line's `by` round trip, the report for a crash-repaired work, and submits on a subagent's screen: text, or an image alone, opens one work once queued, and a submit that isn't queued opens none.

title: Share one JSON writer across types
body:
## Summary

- `std.json.Stringify` generates a writer for every type it writes, and each call inlines the writer's punctuation and safety checks, so every struct, slice, optional, and call site carried its own copy of the writing logic.
- `src/core/shared/json_encode.zig` describes each type once at compile time, as a table of fields, offsets, and child types, and one shared function walks that table at run time. Scalars keep a small helper that writes them through `std.json`, so number formatting, enum names, and `jsonStringify` methods are `std.json`'s own. Packed structs and vectors still write through `std.json`. It mirrors `json_decode.zig` on the parsing side.
- Every call site that can import it now uses `json_encode.value` and `valueAlloc` (547 sites in 95 files), and the seven `jsonStringify` methods write their fields through `json_encode.write`. `src/mcp/`, `src/core/session_manager/`, and files that import only `std` keep `std.json.Stringify`. `AGENTS.md` now points at `json_encode`.

## Size

A local macOS arm64 build of `main` (`4352278f8`) and of this branch, each run through the PGSO release pipeline with the same merged profile:

| | `main` | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| File | 6,098,432 | 6,082,016 | −16,416 |
| `__TEXT` segment | 5,865,472 | 5,832,704 | −32,768 |
| `__DATA_CONST` segment | 196,608 | 212,992 | +16,384 |
| `__text` | 5,219,448 | 5,189,092 | −30,356 |
| `__TEXT,__const` | 360,296 | 358,680 | −1,616 |
| `__DATA_CONST,__const` | 185,760 | 205,840 | +20,080 |
| `__cstring` | 269,566 | 267,860 | −1,706 |

The descriptions are read-only data that holds pointers, so they land in `__DATA_CONST`. A layout with 24-byte descriptions and field names stored next to their fields measured 1,376 bytes larger in total, because the release pipeline's `overlay-constants` pass already packs small constants into the unused bytes of the 32-byte ones.

## Speed

A ReleaseSafe micro-benchmark that writes a 12,657-byte document of nested structs, slices, optionals, enums, and unions takes 18.7 µs with `json_encode` and 16.2 µs with `std.json`, about 14% longer. A turn's gateway request of about 20 KB costs a few microseconds more. The PGSO candidate's startup and heavy benchmarks decide whether that shows up anywhere.

## Testing

- `zig test src/core/shared/json_encode.zig`, in Debug and ReleaseSafe, passes. Every test writes the same value through `std.json` and through `json_encode` under seven sets of options (whitespace, `emit_null_optional_fields`, `emit_strings_as_arrays`, `escape_unicode`, `emit_nonportable_numbers_as_strings`) and expects the same bytes. The cases cover nested structs, optionals of optionals, null optional fields, slices, arrays, sentinel slices and pointers, invalid UTF-8, tagged unions with `void` payloads, non-exhaustive enums, errors, vectors, packed and extern structs, tuples, `std.json.Value`, a `jsonStringify` method that calls back into `json_encode.write`, recursive types, anonymous struct literals with `comptime` fields, a document written piece by piece, allocation failure, and a full writer. Planting each of five bugs (null optional fields always written, a `void` payload written as `null`, bytes always written as arrays, an optional payload skipped, a `comptime` field read from the struct) fails the tests.
- `zig build test` passes.
- On the release-built candidates, 16 commands (`status --json`, `doctor --json`, `config --json`, `help --json`, `sessions --json`, `mcp list --json`, `session last --json`, and error paths) print the same bytes as `main`'s. An `fx ask --json` turn with a tool call against a fake gateway sends gateway requests and writes session files identical to `main`'s, apart from session IDs, times, and the temporary workspace path.
- E2E against the release-built candidate, with no model credentials in the environment: `acp.test.ts` 157/157, `gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` 251/251, `mcp-stdio.test.ts` 108/108, `tui-decision-prompts.test.ts` 55/55, `auto-mode-reliability.test.ts` 44/44, `session-recovery.test.ts` 33/33, `tui-host-instances.test.ts` 32/32, `file-tool-paths.test.ts` 25/25, `ask-presentation.test.ts` 20/20, `tui-interrupt-recovery.test.ts` 11/11, `auth-refresh.test.ts` 7/7. `sessions.test.ts` passed 96 and failed its two disk-fault grid tests during a run that overlapped a full unit-test build; rerun alone, those tests passed 27/27 twice each on this candidate and on `main`'s. `cli.test.ts` fails only its `update_channel` assertion, which fails the same way on `main` locally.

Show subagent reports and messages as tool rows

title: Show control bytes in prompts as text
body:
## Summary

- A prompt's control bytes show as text, such as `\x1b]2;pwned\x07`, instead of reaching the terminal. A subagent's first prompt is its parent's task, so a parent model could send the terminal escape sequences that retitle the tab, recolor or clear the screen, or write the clipboard where the terminal allows it.
- The agent list shows control bytes in an agent's title, name, or profile the same way.
- Line breaks and tabs in a prompt draw as before, and a prompt with nothing to escape draws unchanged.

title: Keep fx running when herdr doesn't answer
body:
## Summary

- fx keeps running when herdr accepts a report but doesn't answer within 250 ms. Before, it panicked with `programmer bug caused syscall error: AGAIN` and exited with code 134.
- A herdr that never answers costs each report a 250 ms wait, as the receive timeout did.

title: Stop model replies from sending control codes to the terminal
body:
## Summary

- A reply containing an erase-screen code (`ESC[2J` or `ESC[J`) no longer makes fx exit with `fx: AnsiBandOverflow`.
- Control codes in a reply show as text, such as `\x1b[2J`, instead of being run by the terminal, so a reply can't clear the screen or scrollback, switch to the alternate screen, or change the window title.
- Resuming a session that contains such a reply shows the same text instead of replaying the codes.
- A carriage return inside a reply line shows as `\x0d` instead of moving the cursor back over the start of the line.
- A link or image URL containing a control code now renders as a link with the code shown as text. Before, it stayed plain text and the raw byte reached the terminal.
- A joined emoji or a direction mark in a prompt draws as written again instead of as `\u{200d}` or `\u{200f}`.
- Tabs, emoji joiners, and direction marks in replies display as before.
- The saved session and the conversation sent to the model keep the reply exactly as the model wrote it.

title: Keep a stopped turn flagged as stopped when its history is copied

A stopped turn that went through any of them rendered as "failed" again, in the transcript and in ACP's history replay, both of which read the flag through `interruptedTurnNotice`.

## Testing
