title: Say what's wrong when ~/.fx/mcp.json can't be read
body:
## Summary

- `fx ask` and interactive fx say what's wrong with `~/.fx/mcp.json` when they can't load it, such as `~/.fx/mcp.json isn't valid JSON`, in place of an error name such as `fx: McpConfigInvalidJson`.
- `fx mcp list` says when `~/.fx/mcp.json` is a link that loops or passes through too many links, is over 1 MB (the most fx reads), or isn't a plain file, in place of "something went wrong" or a message that names no file.
- `fx mcp add` says when the file it would edit is a link that loops or passes through too many links, or is over 1 MB.
- When a changed MCP config fails to load in a running fx, the notice names these problems too.
- `fx ask --json` reports these three failures as `McpConfigLinkLoop`, `McpConfigTooLarge`, and `McpConfigNotPlainFile`, in place of `SymLinkLoop`, `StreamTooLong`, and `DurablePathUnsafe`. `fx status` and `fx doctor` don't change.

title: Add toolbox and keep each conversation's tool list fixed
body:
## Summary

- Send the same tools with every request in a conversation: the built-in tools and a new `toolbox` tool. Nothing the model calls adds a tool to the list.
- Remove the `skill`, `capability_search`, and `mcp_select_tool` tools. `toolbox` is the only way to read a skill, find a tool, or use an MCP tool.
- Replace the skill list and the MCP server block in the prompt with a short toolbox menu that names each skill, MCP server, and built-in tool kept in toolbox.
- Open a skill, an MCP server, or a tool with `toolbox` to get its instructions, its tools, or its definition. A server with up to 10 tools comes with each tool's arguments when they fit in 8 KiB, and otherwise with its tools' names. `kind` says which one to open when the menu lists a name under two headings.
- Run a tool by name with `toolbox`. The run goes through the same permission checks, auto mode review holds, and subagent profile limits as a direct call, and the transcript, `fx ask --json`, and ACP clients show it as that tool. A call that also opens or searches runs nothing and gets toolbox's reason.
- Search skills, MCP tools, and the built-in tools kept in toolbox with `toolbox`. Each tool found comes with its arguments, so the model can run it next. `server` searches one MCP server, an empty search with `server` lists its tools, `limit` returns up to 20 matches, and `cursor` gets the next page of a server's.
- Decide an open or a search by the rules for the tool it replaced: opening a skill by `skill` rules for that skill's name, opening an MCP server or tool by `mcp_select_tool`, and searching by `capability_search`. Session grants for those names still apply. An open of a name a skill has is decided as that skill, as open reads it, even when a tool or server has the same name.
- Decide the same way for agent profiles: a profile that lists `toolbox` or `*` can open and search everything, one that lists only some of the replaced names gets just those, and `!skill` keeps skills out. A profile that lists a tool the run keeps in toolbox gets `toolbox` to run it, and `!toolbox` leaves toolbox out.
- Point a direct call of an MCP tool fx didn't send at `toolbox` run, without changing the tools, and tell a run whose MCP tool changed before it ran to open it again.
- Keep the menu as first sent for the conversation while fx runs, and add a note to the turn naming what toolbox holds when a skill or MCP server is added or removed. A resumed conversation gets the menu built again, which matches unless skills, servers, or placement changed.
- Fit the menu within `skill_catalog_bytes`, at most 32 KiB, and `skill_description_bytes` by shortening descriptions, then listing fewer entries, with a Ctrl+O notice. The change note stays within 4 KiB however much its names need escaping.
- List a skill once in the menu and in a `toolbox` search when several skills folders hold a copy with the same name and description, as the skill catalog does on `main`. The listed copy opens by its location.
- End a skill's description in the menu after the last whole word within 200 characters, followed by `...`, while `skill_description_bytes` is not configured, as the skill catalog does on `main`. Opening a skill still reads it whole, and a search keeps its 1 KiB limit.
- Keep `install_skill` in toolbox by default.
- Add the `tool_placement` setting, in `~/.fx/settings.json` and workspace entries, to move built-in tools into toolbox or out of it. `fx config schema` lists its two values, `direct` and `toolbox`.
- Add `fx config set`, `unset`, and `get` for `tool_placement.<tool>`.
- Add the `--tool-placement <tool=toolbox|direct>` launch flag to change placement for one run.
- Count skills and MCP tools used through toolbox in compaction's record of what a conversation used.
- Label a streaming toolbox call by what it opens, runs, or searches, and write control characters in a name the model gave as visible text, in `fx ask` progress rows and in toolbox's messages.

## Why

Providers cache the start of a prompt, and the tools come before the conversation. On `main` the tool list changes mid-conversation: `mcp_select_tool` adds the selected tool's schema to every later request, and a skill or server added during a session changes the prompt's skill list or MCP block. Each change makes the provider miss the cache from that point on, so the rest of the conversation is billed as new input.

With toolbox the tools and the menu are fixed when the conversation starts. What changes later reaches the model as a note at the end of the turn, after everything the cache already holds.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    title main
    participant fx
    participant Model
    fx->>Model: tools: built-ins, skill, capability_search, mcp_select_tool
    Model->>fx: capability_search "create issue"
    fx->>Model: tools: built-ins, ..., the matching tools' schemas
    Note over fx,Model: the tools changed, so the cache misses from here
    Model->>fx: mcp_linear_create_issue
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    title This PR
    participant fx
    participant Model
    fx->>Model: tools: built-ins, toolbox (menu in the prompt)
    Model->>fx: toolbox search "create issue" in linear
    fx->>Model: the matching tools, each with its arguments
    Model->>fx: toolbox run mcp_linear_create_issue
    fx->>Model: the same tools on every request
    Note over fx,Model: a server added later is a note at the end of the turn
```

On `main` the model uses an MCP tool like this:

```
capability_search {"query": "create issue"}
mcp_linear_create_issue {"title": "..."}
```

With toolbox:

```
toolbox {"search": "create issue", "server": "linear"}
toolbox {"run": "mcp_linear_create_issue", "arguments": {"title": "..."}}
```

A search returns only the tools that match, with their arguments, in its result, so a server with 100 tools never loads more than the model needs, and the tools fx sends don't change.

## Results

Measured with `tests/evals/toolbox-ab.ts`: one live run per model and task, on this branch (4f3cbec8c) and on `main` (24a8fcb69), with 9 model families (Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6.1, Gemini 4, Kimi K3, GLM 5.3, Grok 4.7, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Max, MiniMax M3) and 5 tasks: read a skill, use an MCP tool, find a file, use an MCP server added in the middle of a TUI session, and use one tool of an MCP server with 100 tools. Each conversation runs in its own profile behind a recording proxy, and only the main agent's requests are counted. All 45 tasks passed on both. Numbers from single runs vary from run to run.

To repeat it, build both and run this from `tests/evals` (the TUI task needs tmux):

```bash
FX_TOOLBOX_AB_BASELINE_BIN=/path/to/main/zig-out/bin/fx \
FX_TOOLBOX_AB_CANDIDATE_BIN=/path/to/this/zig-out/bin/fx \
FX_TOOLBOX_AB_MODELS=anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5,openai/gpt-6.1-sol,google/gemini-4-argon,moonshotai/kimi-k3,zai/glm-5.3,xai/grok-4.7,deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash,alibaba/qwen3.8-max,minimax/minimax-m3 \
bun test toolbox-ab.test.ts
```

| | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Conversations whose tools changed | 27 of 45 | 0 of 45 |
| Input of later requests read from the cache | 61.3% | 82.0% |
| Input of later requests not read from the cache | 211,848 tokens | 95,920 tokens |
| Requests, all tasks | 136 | 132 |
| Requests, the server with 100 tools | 30 | 30 |
| Tool definition bytes, `fx ask` | 7,545 to 8,135 | 7,346 to 7,936 |

On the server with 100 tools, `main` added 1 to 6 tool schemas to the tools of each conversation. Here the model searched the server and ran the tool it found, and the tools stayed the same. The ReleaseSafe binary is 147,744 to 161,152 bytes larger, depending on the target, and startup time is unchanged.

## Design notes

- A run is admitted as a direct call of the tool it carries, so permission rules, auto mode, and subagent limits see that tool. `tests/tla/toolbox/Toolbox.tla` checks that the tools and the menu never change in a conversation (ToolsFixed, MenuFixed, PrefixStable) and that a run is always admitted (RunNeedsAdmission).
- A call is run as the tool it carries only when it is a run and nothing else, the same rule the tool's own argument check applies. The `toolbox_run_shape` fuzz target checks that the two agree, and `tool_placement_parse` fuzzes the flag and settings parsers.
- A search's arguments come back in its result, never as tools: the page keeps every match it has room for and gives up the last rows' arguments first, and a row without them says to open the tool.
- There is no switch back to the old tools. Denying `toolbox` denies everything kept in it, skills and MCP tools included. `tool_placement` moves built-in tools only.
- Sessions saved on `main` resume here, and sessions saved here resume on `main`.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#255

title: Share the Keychain session lock across FX_HOME profiles
body:
On macOS every fx profile reads the same Keychain session, whatever `FX_HOME` says, but each profile took `auth.lock` in its own folder. Two profiles could refresh that one session at the same time, both with the same refresh token. Each refresh rotates that token, so when the issuer rejects the second use with `invalid_grant`, `refreshFxSession` retires the session and signs the user out of every profile.

A profile that `FX_HOME` moves now takes `auth.lock` in the default `~/.fx`, the same file a profile that wasn't moved takes. A second profile waits for the first refresh to finish and then loads the rotated session instead of refreshing it again. Everything else the profile keeps, including an `auth.json` that hasn't migrated to the Keychain yet, stays in `$FX_HOME`.

Nothing changes without `FX_HOME`, with `FX_DISABLE_KEYCHAIN=1`, or off macOS, because each profile then has its own session file. With `HOME` unset there's no default folder to share, so the lock stays in the profile. The new `profile_paths.sharedRootParent` names the home folder only while `FX_HOME` is set, so code outside `profile_paths.zig` still never joins `HOME` with `.fx`.

This came up running fx as a separate profile beside the user's own fx: a wrapper sets `FX_HOME` to keep its settings and sessions apart and relies on the shared Keychain sign-in, as the configuration page describes.

## Testing

- `zig build test` passes.
- New unit tests: two Keychain mutations with different profile folders and one shared lock folder, where the second gets `LockBusy` and the lock file is in the shared folder, not the profile. `sharedRootParent` returns null without `FX_HOME`, with `HOME` unset, and with a relative `HOME`.
- With the built binary on macOS arm64, signed in with `fx login`, and `FX_HOME` set to an empty private folder, `./zig-out/bin/fx status` reports the Keychain session and leaves no `auth.lock` in that folder.
- While another process holds an exclusive `flock` on `~/.fx/auth.lock`, the same command waits for the 2-second lock deadline and reports `auth_help=Credential refresh is temporarily unavailable. Retry shortly.` A build of `main` (412d841) answers in about half a second with the session loaded, because it locks a new `$FX_HOME/auth.lock` instead.

## Docs

On the configuration page, under "Files and precedence", after "The OS keychain is shared between profiles.", add: "On macOS, a profile that `FX_HOME` moves locks that shared sign-in in `~/.fx/auth.lock`, so fx creates `~/.fx` for that file if it doesn't exist."

title: Test partial zero-fill copies and move the leaf choice into a helper
body:
## Summary

- The `sparse-constants` tests now cover a zero-filled copy shorter than its constant. The bytes past the copied length must keep their old value and no leaf past it may be stored, so zero-filling the whole constant or storing past the copy fails a test.
- `sparse_constants` picks between leaf stores and a zero fill through a new `_copy_leaves` helper. The pass's output is unchanged: on fx's release-pipeline IR it writes the same bitcode, byte for byte.

title: Keep the MCP stdin-close unit test passing on a busy machine
body:
## Summary

- The MCP unit test for a stop that closes stdin gives the server up to five seconds to exit before SIGTERM, instead of 100 ms, so a slow machine no longer makes it fail.

title: Stop fx ask from waiting on an unreachable model catalog
body:
## Summary

- On a dead network, `fx ask` sends its first request about 2 seconds after it starts, so it shows `Offline` and starts recovering instead of first waiting 20 to 30 seconds for the model catalog.
- `fx ask` stops waiting for the model catalog only when the catalog request still has no connection after 2 seconds, that is, its DNS lookup, connect, or TLS handshake has not finished. It then uses the model's built-in capabilities, as it already did after a failed catalog load.
- Once the catalog request has connected, `fx ask` waits for the catalog as before, within the catalog's own deadline, so a slow link still gets the catalog and its limits.
- Catalogs from the Codex, Grok, and configured providers, whose requests don't report a connection, are waited for as before.

title: Cancel the session title request when a turn is cancelled
body:
## Summary

- Ctrl-C during `fx ask` now exits within a moment while the Gateway has not sent response headers. Before, fx sat out the background session title request's 15 s timeout first.
- `session/cancel` on an ACP session's first prompt now gets its reply at once instead of after the title request's timeout.
- A cancelled first turn keeps the title fx derives from the prompt, since its generated title request is dropped.
- A turn that is not cancelled still waits for its generated title, as before.

title: Print errors that end an fx command in plain words
body:
## Summary

- `fx ask` prints an error that ends it in plain words instead of its name: `fx: unreadable reply` for a stream event too deep to read, where it printed `fx: InvalidGatewaySseEvent`, and `fx: session not found` for an unknown `--resume` session.
- Other `fx` commands that end on an error with no message of their own print it in plain words too. The error name still goes to the trace log, and `fx ask --json` still reports it in `error`.
- An unreadable or oversized stream event from the Codex or Grok provider reads as "unreadable reply" or "reply too large to read", as one from the Gateway does.

title: End the turn at once on Esc during a stuck lookup on every connection path
body:
## Summary

- Esc or the connection setup deadline during a DNS lookup or connect that hangs now ends the turn at once with direct OpenAI Codex, xAI Grok, configured chat-completions providers, `fx acp`, and libfx's native addon. Before, only the AI Gateway in the TUI and `fx ask` did, and the rest sat out the whole lookup.
- Ctrl-C on `fx ask` with one of those providers now exits at once while the lookup hangs, instead of after it returns.
- After Esc in the TUI, the next prompt starts its request right away instead of waiting for the stuck lookup to end.
- A model request with an overall deadline now ends at that deadline while its lookup hangs.
- When fx walks away in the middle of a connect or TLS setup, it now closes that connection at once on every path, the pooled Gateway path included, instead of leaving it open until the server answers or gives up.
- A lookup fx walked away from still runs to its end in the background. When it returns, fx does not connect, or closes what it connected, and frees the memory the request used.

title: Keep the persistent child SIGKILL test off the runner's process group
body:
## Summary

- The persistent child SIGKILL test in `gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` writes its pid file before the marker it waits for, so it no longer reads a missing or empty pid file.
- The test's cleanup signals only a recorded pid above 1 that is not the runner, so an empty pid file can no longer send SIGKILL to pid 0 and kill the runner's own process group.
- Cleanup skips the recorded pids once they have exited, so it never signals a pid the system has given to another process.

title: Print errors that stop the interactive session in plain words
body:
## Summary

- When an error stops the interactive session and fx has no message of its own for it, fx now prints plain words instead of the raw error name. For example, `fx --resume <id>` with a file where the session store's folder belongs prints `fx: session path unsafe` instead of `fx: SessionPathUnsafe`.
- A relaunch that fails after an update now names its cause the same way, such as `relaunch failed: permission denied`.
- The raw error name still goes to the trace log.

title: Resume a running turn when its window closes before SIGHUP
body:
## Summary

- Closing the terminal window while fx is working on a request no longer saves the turn as cancelled, so `fx --resume last` and `fx -c` send the request again on their own.
- When fx sees the window close before SIGHUP arrives, it saves the request as a clean close, the same as when SIGHUP arrives first.
- Closing the window while fx is idle still shuts fx down normally.
- Esc, Ctrl+C twice, and /quit still cancel the running request, and reopening does not send it again.

title: Shrink the skill catalog and recover from more tool-call mistakes
body:
## Summary

- The skill catalog lists a skill once when several skills folders hold a copy with the same name and description.
- Skill descriptions in the catalog default to their first 200 characters instead of 1,024. A configured `skill_description_bytes` still sets a byte limit, and `capability_search` results keep the 1 KiB default.
- The runtime notes for permission modes, noninteractive runs, verifying changed files, folder AGENTS.md rules, and MCP servers are shorter.
- `shell` accepts a call that sends an empty string or `false` for fields its action does not use.
- `shell` accepts a `shell` field that names the login shell on a run without a terminal.
- `subagent` accepts a call that sends an empty string or `false` for fields its action does not use.
- `subagent` `wait` accepts an `agent` field and ignores it.
- When `edit_file` cannot find `old_string`, the error shows the file lines it most likely meant, if reading the file needs no approval.
- When `old_string` matches more than once, the error shows each match with the two lines before it, under the same condition.
- A failed edit of a file that a read rule denies, or asks about first, keeps the plain error and shows none of the file.
- The TUI status line shows the first line of a multi-line file-tool failure.
- With tracing on, fx logs each skill copy the catalog leaves out, an `agent` that `subagent` `wait` ignores, and a `shell` field dropped because it names the login shell.

## Why one PR

Both halves change what a model gets on each request, and they were measured together: the same tasks on nine models, each change on its own and then as one build. Splitting them would ship a build that no run measured.

## Before and after

A wrong `old_string` on a file fx may read:

Before:

```
edit_file failed: old_string not found in file. Re-read the file to see its current contents; if the change is already applied, do not retry this edit.
```

After:

```
edit_file failed: old_string not found in file; the closest match is lines 3-6.
They currently read:
def load(path):
    with open(path) as f:
        data = f.read()
    return data.strip()
If the change is already applied, do not retry this edit.
```

The skill catalog for one profile with 174 skills installed across seven skills folders:

| | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catalog entries | 336 | 220 |
| Catalog bytes | 80,000 | 56,820 |
| Prompt messages, JSON bytes | 91,392 | 67,310 |

The permission-mode note in ask mode:

- Before: "Runtime context: permission mode is ask. Sensitive tool calls may require user approval unless configured rules or session grants already decide them. Tool admission remains authoritative."
- After: "Runtime context: permission mode is ask. Sensitive tool calls may need user approval unless configured rules or session grants decide them."

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#256

title: Give fx acp the catalog wait fx ask uses
body:
## Summary

- On a dead network, `fx acp` answers `initialize` about 2 seconds after it starts loading the model catalog, instead of first waiting 20 to 30 seconds for the catalog's DNS lookup or connect to fail.
- The same wait applies to the other places where `fx acp` loads the catalog for the first time: a host's effort, fast, or ultrafast override, and a prompt's first capability lookup.
- As in `fx ask`, `fx acp` stops waiting only while the catalog request has no connection. A catalog request that has connected is waited for as before, so a slow link still gets the catalog and its capabilities.

Stacked on #1662, which adds the wait for `fx ask`.

title: Name the cause when fx can't connect to the model catalog
body:
## Summary

- When fx can't connect to the model catalog, including a catalog request that times out, it prints one line that says so and asks the user to check their network connection or firewall.
- That line also says what fx holds back until the catalog loads: earlier images, images from tools, fast mode, or a combination of them.
- For connection failures, the line replaces the separate "Earlier images aren't reaching the model right now..." and "Fast mode is unavailable for this model right now..." lines, and it still appears once per turn.
- When an image attached to the turn can't be sent because fx couldn't connect to the catalog, fx first prints a line that names the failed connection, then the existing "Unable to verify image support..." error.
- `fx models` says it couldn't connect to AI Gateway and asks the user to check their network connection or firewall, in place of "could not list models: Unavailable". The JSON `code` stays `TransportFailure`.
- `fx provider` and `fx login` say they couldn't connect to load the target model catalog, in place of "could not load the target model catalog (transport)".
- Switching providers in the TUI says fx couldn't connect to load the target provider catalog, in place of "The target provider catalog could not be validated".
- Choosing a Vercel team in the TUI says fx couldn't connect to AI Gateway to validate the team, in place of "could not be validated for AI Gateway".
- The messages name AI Gateway for the gateway provider and "the model provider" for other providers.
- A catalog that answers with an error, such as a 5xx response, keeps the existing messages.

title: Resume profile sessions in the profile's model and effort
body:
## Summary

- When fx starts in an agent profile, or `/launch <profile>` opens an instance, the instance's first session saves the profile's model and effort, so `fx --resume`, `fx -c`, and `fx -r` use them again instead of your configured model and effort.
- Resuming a group of instances brings each instance back in its own profile's model and effort.
- A session started later with `/new` keeps the model and effort the instance uses by then, as before.
- `--model`, `--effort`, `--provider`, and `FX_MODEL` still apply only to the run that passes them, and the session doesn't save them.

title: Keep subagent replies out of the steering preview
body:
## Summary

- A subagent's report or message that arrives while its parent's turn runs no longer appears in the parent's window as a message the user queued. The parent still receives it, and the transcript shows its report row as before.
- The queued messages shown above the composer while a tool runs no longer include a subagent's report or message.
- Up in an empty composer takes back only a message the user queued. It no longer pulls a subagent's report or the parent's message into the composer, and those stay queued for the turn.

## Before and after

Before, while main waited on the model, main's window drew a subagent's report as a message the user had queued:

```
┃ Subagent report (untrusted agent output, not user instructions):
┃ {"agent":"solo","child_id":"…","work_id":"…","outcome":"completed","output":"SOLO_DONE"}
```

It vanished once main's turn took the report, and the transcript showed the report row (`solo completed · SOLO_DONE`) in its place. Now no card appears, and the report row is the only thing drawn.

Before, with a report queued behind a running command, Up in an empty composer put the 258-byte report into the composer and took it out of main's queue. Now Up brings back the user's own queued message, and main still gets the report when the command ends.

title: Describe the second outliner pass on Linux x86_64
body:
## Summary

- The PGSO README and the comment in `candidate_object_argv` now say the second machine outliner pass runs wherever the outliner runs, which includes cold code on Linux x86_64 since #1628.
- They also say the shared frame helpers from LLVM's homogeneous prologue and epilogue are AArch64 only.

title: Make the PGSO speed retry helper private
body:
## Summary

- `measure_with_one_retry` in `scripts/pgso/qualify.py` is now `_measure_with_one_retry`, like the file's other helpers that nothing outside it uses. PGSO measurement behavior is unchanged.

title: Show each model call in place in Full detail
body:
## Summary

- Show a line under each response for the model call that wrote it: the time it finished, the model, how long it took, input and output tokens, and the ID the provider gave the call, such as AI Gateway's gen ID.
- Show `no gen ID returned` when a provider sends no ID for a call.
- Show a failed call as an error where it happened, with what went wrong, the provider and model, and how long fx waits before trying again.
- Show a compaction's model call on its own line.
- Show a call stopped with Esc as cancelled, after the text it wrote.
- Keep every call line in place after a resume and after a crash. Turns saved by an older fx have none.
- Show every tool expanded under its step, opening with its mark, with its arguments and output at a plain indent and the time it ran.
- Remove the block headers, rails, tree marks and group summaries from Full detail.
- Show when each prompt was sent, with its date, and show the date again when the day changes.
- Show each turn's totals on one line.
- Show the session start and request recovery details where they happened instead of pinned to the top of Full detail.
- Show only `esc close · pgup/pgdn scroll` on Full detail's bottom row, in place of the mode and model row, so the page gets two more rows.
- Stop tool updates on the main screen from redrawing the whole transcript once a finished turn holds a line only Full detail shows.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#257

title: Make fx doctor check that fx works, not only what is configured
body:
## Summary

- `fx doctor` exits 1 when any check fails. Warnings alone still exit 0, and a bad flag still exits 2 with an error that names that flag.
- The credential is checked against the provider's model list for AI Gateway, ChatGPT, and Grok, and no model call is made. A refused credential fails. A credential the provider never answers for, or answers only with its public list, such as an fx login with no team, is a warning.
- A provider configured under `providers` in settings is not asked, since its model list comes from those settings.
- A model the provider does not list fails.
- Each approved MCP server is connected in its own `fx mcp show` process and gets its own line, however many tools it has. An unapproved server is never started. Checks run in config order, at most one per CPU at once (at least 4, at most 16), and the next starts as one ends, all under the one limit. So servers that hang hold their slots until the limit, and the servers queued behind them get a line that says they were not checked. A queued check starts only while at least min(1 s, a quarter of the limit) is left, so a check the limit cuts had at least that long, and its line gives its own time, such as `did not answer in 1.2 s, when doctor's 5 s limit ended`.
- A server whose name starts with `-` is not checked, and no fix line names it in an `fx mcp` command, because every `fx mcp` command reads such a name as an option and takes no `--` before a name. Whatever its state, also when it needs an environment variable, its line's fix says to rename it in the file it comes from.
- Every `fix:` line passes text it did not write itself, such as a server name, an environment variable name, or a file path, to the shell as one word: text with any character other than letters, digits, and `._/-` is single-quoted. A project `.mcp.json` can no longer make a fix line run a command of its own, and the quoted line still runs: `fx mcp approve 'x; touch y #'` approves the server named `x; touch y #`.
- Each server's row (`mcp_server=` in text, `mcp.servers` in `--json`) gives the `connection` (`ready`, `failed`, `timed_out`, or `not_checked`) and `authentication` (`ok`, `needs_login`, or `not_checked`) that doctor found, and `mcp_connection_check` reads `checked`. `fx status` output is unchanged.
- A project `.mcp.json` that keeps a server from loading, such as a file that is not JSON or an entry fx can't read, fails with a `fix:` line, as a broken `~/.fx/mcp.json` already did.
- All network checks share one 5 second limit. A provider or MCP server check that hangs, or that doctor could not start in time, fails with its own line. A gh that hangs is a warning, since gh is optional.
- On a terminal, text output first writes one line to stderr naming the network checks doctor waits for and the limit, such as `checking AI Gateway, 3 MCP servers, and gh (up to 5 s)...`. `--json`, and a stderr that is not a terminal, get nothing new.
- No check process outlives doctor, unless doctor itself is killed with SIGKILL: then no handler runs, and its checks run until their own timeouts end. A check doctor stops, at the deadline or on Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, or SIGHUP, is killed with its process group and every process still running under it, also those in process groups of their own such as the stdio MCP servers `fx mcp show` starts, so none of them is running when doctor exits. A signal that arrives while doctor is still starting its checks stops them the same way, the checks still waiting never start, and doctor then ends by that signal.
- A check that ends on its own stops its stdio servers through fx's MCP shutdown, so a server that ignores SIGTERM can run for up to about 2 seconds after doctor exits, until that shutdown sends it SIGKILL.
- Every problem has a `fix:` line, except a session an older fx saved that has nothing left to recover. Text output adds a `[doctor] version=` line, and `--json` adds `fix` to each check and the fx `version`.
- A malformed settings file fails with its path. An invalid `FX_` value is a warning that names the value fx uses instead.
- The repository is found from a subfolder, and git that is missing, too old, or refused by fx's git rules is a warning with a fix.
- Inside a repository, doctor runs `gh repo view --json url` in the workspace, under the same limit and outside the MCP cap. gh then picks the remote, host, and active account, and reads `GH_HOST` and `GH_REPO`, as it does for `fx pr` and `fx issue`. It gets the environment those get, plus `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1` and `GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1`, so it never prompts and never writes its update state. Exit 0 is ok (`gh can use this repository`). Exit 4, gh's code for a command that needs a sign-in, is a warning, `gh is not signed in for this repository`, with `fix: gh auth login`. Any other exit is a warning, `gh could not use this repository`, with `fix: run gh repo view to see why`, and a gh that does not answer in time is a warning that says so. gh's output is never read, printed, or traced, since it can hold remote URLs and tokens; doctor traces only the exit status. A gh missing from `PATH` is a warning, as before. Outside a repository, gh is not run.
- The install line shows the fx version, binary path, and release channel, and warns about another fx on `PATH`.
- Skill files that fail to load are listed with their path.
- Old session side folders are listed with a count. `fx doctor --fix` removes them, and plain `fx doctor` no longer deletes anything.
- No config file and no saved sessions are no longer warnings.
- `fx doctor --json` leaves the startup latency benchmark and the PGSO startup timing, since it now waits on network checks. PGSO still trains on it: the direct-doctor training scenario expects exit 1 through a new `expected_exit` field in the corpus format, read by a new `allowed_returncodes` parameter of `run_checked`, and `doctor.test.ts` is a verification scenario.

## Before and after

The same folder with no credential, on `main` and on this branch:

```text
$ fx doctor          # main
[doctor] ok=3 warn=4 fail=1
...
[warn] config: no config files found; using defaults and env overrides
[fail] auth: fx needs access to Vercel AI Gateway. Run fx login to sign in, fx login vercel --api-key to use an API key, or set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY.
[warn] sessions: no saved sessions yet
[warn] git: not a git repository; pr/issue workflows will be limited
[warn] gh: GitHub CLI not found in PATH; publish workflows unavailable
$ echo $?
0
```

```text
$ fx doctor          # this branch
[doctor] ok=6 warn=1 fail=1
[doctor] version=0.0.16
...
[ok] install: fx 0.0.16 at /Users/example/.local/bin/fx (stable channel)
[ok] config: no config files; fx uses its defaults and env overrides
[fail] auth: fx needs access to Vercel AI Gateway. Run fx login to sign in, fx login vercel --api-key to use an API key, or set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY.
  fix: fx login
[ok] sessions: no saved sessions yet
[warn] git: this folder is not in a git repository; fx pr and fx issue need one
  fix: run git init here, or run fx in a repository
$ echo $?
1
```

Before, doctor read local state, removed old session folders on its own, and exited 0 whatever it found:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[fx doctor] --> B[Local checks: settings, credential present, sessions, git, gh on PATH]
  B --> C[Remove old session side folders]
  C --> D[Print what it found]
  D --> E[Exit 0, even with a fail line]
```

After, the local checks run first, then the network checks under one deadline, and every check is stopped and joined before the report:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[fx doctor] --> B[Local checks: install, settings, env, MCP config, auth, sessions, git, skills]
  B --> C[Start the network checks under one 5 s deadline]
  C --> P[Provider model list: Io task with a cancel flag]
  C --> M[fx mcp show NAME --json for each approved server, 4 to 16 at a time, the next as one ends: child in its own process group, read by an Io task]
  C --> G[gh repo view --json url in the workspace: child in its own process group, reaped by an Io task]
  P --> W{All done, the deadline, or a signal}
  M --> W
  G --> W
  W --> K[Note which checks finished in time, cancel and await the provider task, kill each unfinished child with everything it started]
  K --> J[1 s reap grace, cancel any waiter still blocked, join every task]
  J --> R[Report one line per check with fix lines, exit 1 on a fail]
  J --> S[After a signal: remove the handler and end by the signal]
```

## Why it is built this way

- A child per MCP server: doctor checks a server with `fx mcp show NAME --json`, the command a person runs to check it, rather than loading every server into doctor's own MCP host. Each check gets its own process and process group, so a server with thousands of tools cannot crash the other checks, and a kill at the deadline stops exactly that check. Checks run in config order with at most one per CPU (4 to 16) at once, so servers that hang hold their slots until the limit, and the servers queued behind them get "was not checked".
- Io tasks that are cancelled and joined: the provider request and one waiter per child are `std.Io` tasks. At the deadline doctor notes which checks finished, sets the provider request's cancel flag and cancels its task, kills the unfinished child groups, and joins every task before it reports. Nothing doctor started is running when it prints, and a result that came late is dropped instead of being read halfway. A waiter blocked by a process that left the child's group is cancelled after a 1 second grace, so the limit still holds.
- Process groups and a tree kill: each child runs in a process group of its own, so the terminal's Ctrl-C reaches only doctor, and killing the group stops what the child started in it and closes the child's pipe. A group kill alone misses what the child moved to groups of their own: `fx mcp show` starts each stdio server in its own group and tells fx's MCP helper about it a moment later, so a check killed in between left a server nothing would stop. To stop the checks still running, doctor first sends SIGSTOP to each one's group, then waits until each stop has landed or the check has exited, 100 ms at most for all of them together, because kill(2) only queues the signal and a check still running could start a server after doctor looked. Then, for each check, it lists the processes the check started with the identity-checked tracker the shell tool and the terminal host already use (`process_tree.Tracker`), and kills the group and all of them. Whether a stop has landed comes from one new `process_tree.processIsStopped`, next to the snapshot readers it uses.
- A signal flag: the handler for SIGINT, SIGTERM, and SIGHUP only records the signal. Doctor's own thread looks at it after each check it starts and while it waits, stops every check as it does at the deadline, removes the handler, and ends by the signal. The handler it replaces killed the groups it knew of and ended doctor at once, which missed a child spawned but not yet listed, and the signal could reach any thread.
- Quoted fix lines: a project `.mcp.json` comes with the repository, so its server names are text someone else chose, and doctor prints them in commands a person pastes. The quoting is one new helper next to fx's shell lexer, `command_lex.quoteWord`. The existing quoting code stays as it is, because none of it fits: `command_runner` always quotes, the command line `mcp_host/config.zig` builds is display-only and leaves `;` bare, and shell completion escapes only inside quotes it writes itself.
- gh decides for itself: which repository, host, and account `fx pr` uses depends on the remotes, the remote gh marked as resolved, `GH_HOST`, `GH_REPO`, and gh's accounts on each host. Rather than copy those rules, doctor runs a gh command that applies them all, and reads only its exit code.
- A cap on the MCP checks: each check is an fx process with its server, and starting every one at once let 40 healthy servers miss the limit on a loaded machine. One per CPU, from 4 to 16, keeps them inside it. Doctor's own thread starts the next queued check as one ends, in its wait loop. Before each start it looks first at the time left, and stops starting once less than min(1 s, a quarter of the limit) is left, so a healthy server is not cut moments after its check started; then at the signal and the limit. A check still queued then never starts, and the trace names each one and why.
- A fixed-memory reader: `fx mcp show --json` lists every tool with its schema, which can run to megabytes. Doctor streams that JSON and keeps only the status, the error, cut at a whole character, and the tool count, so its memory stays the same however large the answer is.
- `--fix`: a diagnostic that deletes files on every run is surprising, so plain doctor now only counts old side folders and `--fix` removes them.
- One deadline: every network check shares the 5 second limit, so doctor ends in about 5 seconds plus its local checks however many checks hang. `FX_TEST_DOCTOR_DEADLINE_MS`, from 1 to 60000, shortens it for tests only.
- `tests/tla/doctor/Doctor.tla` models the provider task, the children started one at a time and only while fewer than `Cap` are busy, what they start in their own group and in groups of their own, an ending signal at any point, also between a spawn and the step that lists the child, the cancel, the kill, and the join. The earlier start cutoff needs no step of its own, since the model's timer can fire at any step; a comment in the spec says so. `check.sh` passes the design, also with one slot (`doctor-cap.cfg`), and requires each of ten planted bugs to fail a named property, among them a handler that ends doctor at once (`NoChildAfterExit`), a kill that misses a server in its own group (`NoChildAfterExit`), a fan-out that ignores the signal (`NoStartAfterSignalSeen`), and a start with no free slot (`CapHolds`). `tests/tla/drivers/doctor/` runs the built binary along the model, a signal during the fan-out included. The child-status reader has its own file and a fuzz target.

## Docs

The fx.sh pages are updated in https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx-web/pull/268: what doctor checks, the exit codes, `--fix`, the network checks and their 5 second limit, how many MCP servers are checked at once, how gh is checked, the rename fix for a server whose name starts with `-`, the quoted `fix:` lines, and what Ctrl-C stops, with the SIGKILL exception.

title: Read a login file again when another fx changed it
body:
## Summary

- When another fx signs out or refreshes the login while this one is reading it, fx now reads the login as it is after that change: none after a logout, or the new login after a refresh. Before, it could fail with "credential storage unavailable". This covers the fx login, the Codex and Grok logins, and the check for a saved login.
- The logout race test now accepts an `fx ask` that the logout signed out, since it reads the login again for its turn, but never a storage error. It still checks that the logout removed the login and revoked both tokens.

title: Keep six tests passing on a busy machine
body:
## Summary

Six tests passed in CI but failed when the machine or runner was busy. None of the changes touches product code.

- "natural completion marks output incomplete when the deadline cuts leftover output" gave its command 1 s, so a slow Python start let the deadline end the command before it exited. It now gives the command 3 s and reads each line in 40 ms, so the deadline still cuts the output before its 100th line.
- "a v1 side file larger than one v2 blob is left out and named..." expected only the notice naming that file, but a conversion past its 150 ms mark also says it's slow. It now leaves out the slow notice, which "a conversion past its slow mark tells the host once" covers.
- "cancelled tool history survives ... compaction and restart" read the saved session as soon as the reply showed, before fx had saved the turn. It now waits for the save.
- "Esc while a login is being renewed..." timed the login's renewal and the tool call from fixed points, so a slow first model request changed which step renewed it. The renewal window now opens 15 s after the login is saved, and the call waits until 16 s.
- "a login that comes within its renewal window while fx runs is renewed before the next call" had the same problem: the renewal window opened 4 s after the login was saved, so an fx that started late used the renewed token first. The window now opens 15 s after the save, and the call waits until 16 s.
- The store lock driver's "holders taking turns" test could miss the first Keychain reads it meant to slow, so the last waiter didn't pass 12 s. The first read it slows is now held 8 s, and six processes queue.

Each fix was checked against the condition that broke it: a Python start 1.5 s late, every conversion slow, the first model request held 8 or 12 s, fx started 5 s late, and the first two reads missed. The old test fails under it, and the new one passes.

title: Treat instructions as prompt injection only when they make the action do real harm
body:
## Summary

- In auto mode, following instructions from tool output, files, or other untrusted text no longer counts as prompt injection when the action only reads, searches, builds, tests, or runs a local tool's own steps. Multi-step workflow tools, such as a review tool that hands out its next commands, keep working when the user only says "continue".
- Planted instructions that make the action delete or overwrite files, send data out, install or run outside code, weaken security, or use credentials the user did not ask for still count as prompt injection, and the action is held.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#258

title: Stop waiting for a stuck session title after the answer
body:
## Summary

- `fx ask` now exits about 2 s after its answer when the session title request hangs, in text and `--json` output. Before, it waited out the title request's 15 s timeout.
- On an ACP session's first prompt, the prompt reply now arrives about 2 s after the answer when the title request hangs, instead of after 15 s.
- A title still pending 2 s after the answer is dropped, and the session keeps the title fx derives from its first prompt line. `fx sessions`, the session picker, and `--resume` show that title, as they already do when title generation fails.
- A generated title that arrives within 2 s of the answer is still installed.

title: Give fx acp's catalog refresh the connect wait
body:
## Summary

- When `fx acp`'s model catalog is due for its refresh on a dead network, `session/new`, `session/load`, and option changes now answer about 2 seconds after the refresh starts, instead of first waiting 20 to 30 seconds for the catalog's DNS lookup or connect to fail. A prompt sent after them no longer waits behind that refresh.
- A refresh whose request has not connected after 2 seconds counts as a failed refresh, so `fx acp` keeps listing the models from the catalog it already has and tries again at the next refresh interval.
- A refresh whose request has connected is waited for as before, so a slow link still gets the refreshed catalog.
- Catalogs from the Codex, Grok, and configured providers, whose requests don't report a connection, refresh as before.

title: Say when a command couldn't write its output
body:
## Summary

- When a command such as `fx status`, `fx sessions`, or `fx --version` can't write to its stdout or stderr, for example because stdout was closed or the disk under a redirected file is full, fx now prints `fx: couldn't write the output` instead of `fx: connection dropped`.
- A failed write that fx can't tie to its own output, such as a request to the network, still reads as a dropped connection.
- The raw error name still goes to the trace log.

title: Report a login that logout deletes mid-read as signed out
body:
## Summary

- `fx ask` reports that it is signed out, not that saved credential storage is unavailable, when `fx logout` deletes the login while `fx ask` is reading it.
- The logout race e2e test accepts both orders of `fx ask` and `fx logout`: the ask answers with the refreshed login, or it stops signed out without sending a request. In both orders the login stays deleted and both tokens are revoked.

title: Wait for the model picker test's real reply
body:
## Summary

- The model picker Ultrafast E2E test sent `Return the marker selection response.` and then waited for `marker selection response`. The typed prompt already contains that text, so the wait could end before fx sent its request, and the next line saw no Gateway request.
- That happened on #1678's Linux run (light mode first, then both modes on the retry), while the same tests pass locally and on main.
- The prompt is now `Return the model picker marker.`, so the wait ends only when the reply arrives.

## Testing

- `cd tests/e2e && FX_SOUND=0 bun test ultrafast-fake-gateway.test.ts -t "actual model picker selects Ultrafast"`: 2 pass, 0 fail, three runs in a row.

title: Isolate CLI test profiles and skip the process snapshot on plain failures
body:
## Summary

- Eight tests in `cli.test.ts` and the upgrade-links test in `tui-resume.test.ts` run fx in a home of their own, so they no longer read the developer's `~/.fx` or create `~/.fx/auth.lock` in it.
- The live `fx models`, `fx credits`, and `fx ask` tests in `cli.test.ts` use the key in the environment instead of the developer's `fx login`.
- `runFx`, `runEval`, and `TmuxSession` no longer pass the developer's `FX_HOME` to fx. A test that needs it sets it in its own environment.
- The `fx upgrade`, `fx update`, and `fx replay` spawns in `tui-resume.test.ts` and the direct fx spawns in `cli.test.ts` and `gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` drop the developer's `FX_HOME` the same way, so the upgrade tests no longer write into that profile. The other test files that start fx with the inherited environment are tracked separately.
- `runFx` no longer runs a system-wide `ps` after a plain nonzero exit, so `add fails precisely without HOME and on a flag it doesn't have` stays under Bun's 5 second limit on a busy machine.
- `runFx` still records the process snapshot when fx times out or a signal ends it.
- A caller can pass `processSnapshot: true` to `runFx` to keep the snapshot on any nonzero exit. `shell timeout reaps env-cleared Bash double-fork descendants` does, so its failure message still lists the processes left after fx closes.

title: Start many HTTP MCP servers at once without crashing
body:
## Summary

- Starting fx with many HTTP MCP servers no longer crashes Debug builds with `programmer bug caused syscall error: ISCONN`.
- Release builds no longer report a TCP connect that the kernel finished as failed, so MCP, gateway, and upgrade requests keep their first connection instead of failing with `Unexpected` or `ConnectionPending`.
- Canceling a request while it is still connecting still stops it, within about 20 ms.

title: Say when fx ask couldn't write its answer
body:
## Summary

- When `fx ask` can't write its answer to stdout, for example because stdout was closed, it now exits 1 and prints `fx: couldn't write the output` instead of exiting 0 with nothing shown. The turn is still saved, so `fx session` or a resume shows the answer.
- `fx ask --json` with a stdout it can't write prints the same message instead of the raw cause, such as `fx: not open for writing`.
- `fx pr` and `fx issue` report an answer they couldn't write the same way.
- When fx starts with stdin, stdout, or stderr closed, a file fx opens no longer takes that stream's place, so an answer meant for a closed stdout no longer lands in fx's own files, such as the session store's lock.
- A reader that stops early, as with `| head`, is handled as before.

title: Give each Keychain test run its own item
body:
## Summary

- Keep the two macOS Keychain round-trip tests from failing, skipping, or reporting a leak when two test runs overlap on one machine. Each test now stores its item under a name that includes the process ID, so overlapping runs never share an item.

## Testing

Built the two round-trip tests as their own binary at each commit and ran 8 copies at once, 5 rounds:

```
main:     40 of 40 runs failed or skipped (MCP test: 12 failed, 23 skipped; gateway key test: 35 skipped)
this PR:   0 of 40 runs failed or skipped
```

No `FX_TEST_` item is left in the login Keychain afterwards. `python3 -m scripts.check_cli_shape` passes.

title: Let test servers stop when no client connects
body:
## Summary

- Stopping a unit-test server returns on macOS even when its client never connected, so `zig build test` reports the failing test instead of hanging in `connection watch closes a body that stops sending as stalled`.
- Test servers no longer open a wake-up connection to themselves when they stop.
- `FakeJevServer` in `src/builtins/gateway/typesafe_permission_reviewer.zig` and `InterruptedReadServer` in `src/core/upgrade/upgrade_helpers.zig` stop when no client connects. `src/main.zig` now registers `typesafe_permission_reviewer.zig`, so its tests run in `zig build test` through a direct import. Before, only an indirect reference reached them.
- Stopping these two servers is bounded. When the thread is still running after the limit, the stop shuts down the connection the thread is serving and connects once to the listener. This ends a wait in `accept` or a read or write on that connection. Then the stop joins the thread and the test fails with `TestThreadStillWaiting` instead of hanging the suite. A thread blocked on anything other than `accept` or that connection still holds up the join.

Linear: [FXC-287](https://linear.app/vercel/issue/FXC-287)

title: End quietly when the output reader goes away
body:
## Summary

- When the reader of fx's output stops early, as `| head` does, every command now ends quietly with status 141, as `fx --version` and `fx help` already did. Before, `fx status` printed `fx: connection dropped`, `fx ask --json` printed `fx: broken pipe`, and `fx ask` exited 0.
- `fx ask` still finishes the turn and saves it, so `fx session` or a resume shows the whole answer, and a running tool is still stopped when fx exits.
- A write that fails for another reason still prints `fx: couldn't write the output`.

title: Wait for fx's own output after typing in three E2E tests
body:
## Summary

- Make the slash menu test wait for the help catalog that `/help` opens, instead of the typed `/help`, which the command suggestions already show.
- Make the MCP and agent switching tests wait until fx has taken the typed line from the composer, instead of waiting for the typed text.

The model picker test this PR first fixed was fixed on main in bd00b5b21.

title: Closing fx while several agents have requests in flight saves only one of them as a clean close
body:
## What happens

When fx gets SIGHUP or SIGTERM (a closed window, a logout, a reboot), it saves the model request in flight as a clean close, so the next launch resumes it without counting a crash (`RequestRecovery.closeActive`, `tests/tla/recovery/Resume.tla` `NoFalseCrashQuestion`). Only one request per process can be saved this way. `register` in `src/core/agent/runtime/request_recovery.zig` keeps a single process-wide `active` request, and each request that keeps a record replaces the one before it.

One fx process now runs main, its subagents and other instances, so several requests can be in flight at once. On SIGHUP only the request that started last is saved as a clean close, and the others are saved as abrupt deaths. If that last request has already finished, `unregister` has emptied the slot and no request is saved clean.

The first time, main's request still resumes, but it counts as an abrupt death. If the window is closed the same way again during the resumed request, the next launch stops and asks "This request crashed fx twice · Enter to retry, Esc to cancel", although fx never crashed.

## Steps to reproduce

With the fake gateway used in `tests/e2e/tui-host-switch.test.ts`:

1. Have main message a subagent, then hold main's next model request open.
2. Have the subagent run a short command, such as `sleep 2`, and hold its next model request open, so it starts after main's.
3. Send SIGHUP to fx.
4. Resume main. Its request resumes and is held again. Switch to the subagent and send it a message, so its request again starts after main's, then send SIGHUP again.
5. Resume main.

## Expected

Main's request resumes without a question, as it does when main is the only agent with a request in flight.

## Actual

- After step 3, main's last recovery record has no clean-exit flag, and the subagent's has it. The trace's `[recovery] event=closed` line names the subagent's request (`subagent_id=1`).
- If the subagent's later request has finished before step 3, the trace shows `[app] event=closing signal=1 record_saved=false`, and no request is saved clean.
- At step 5, fx shows "This request crashed fx twice · Enter to retry, Esc to cancel" in place of resuming. With main alone, the same two closes resume both times.

This happens on `main` (checked at `88e00c39b`).

## Notes

The comment on `active` says one host process runs one request that keeps a record at a time, which stopped being true when one process started running several agents. `closeActive` could close every registered request, each with its own bounded lock wait, in place of a single slot. A subagent's interrupted turn is not resumed on the next launch, so the clean record a subagent gets today goes unused. Main's and each instance's requests are the ones that need it.

title: Show a steer that a resumed turn places
body:
## Summary

On the native backend, a steer that a turn has accepted and not yet placed, such as one waiting for a running tool, reaches the model when the turn resumes but never produces a `user_message` event. A host that builds its view from the stream misses a message the model acted on.

Two things trigger it, and neither needs anything unusual:

- **A deadline handoff.** A long tool call near a worker's time limit is enough, with no crash. The stream reads `turn_start tool_start turn_yield turn_resume tool_start tool_end turn_end`.
- **A crash.** A `SIGKILL` while the steer waits gives `turn_start tool_start turn_resume tool_start tool_end turn_end`.

After this change, the steer's `user_message` appears once, after the tool's result, which is where the model reads it.

WebAssembly doesn't have this bug. Its core takes a steer only at a boundary, so a steer waiting for a tool is never accepted, and the worker sends it again through the normal path.

## Cause

`publishSteeringReplay` was called only at the two turn-boundary paths. The resume path in `src/acp/prompt.zig` passes the journal's pending inputs to `libfx_journal.resumeCheckpoint` and published nothing.

## Fix

**Showing the steer.** `publishResumedInputs` runs from `setJournalProgress`, after the progress that places the inputs is written. That progress comes right before the turn's first model request, so the event lands after any rerun tool's result, and a resume that ends before its first request shows nothing. Publishing straight from the resume path puts the event before the tool's result: I tried it, and the new order assertion rejects it.

**Not showing it twice.** Publishing on resume adds a new case: a steer shown at a boundary shows again if a crash loses the progress that placed it. A durable session now drops that repeat. After `turn_resume` lands, `shownSteers` in `sdk/durable.js` reads the stream for the steers the log says are held, using the existing ranker, and `drive` skips a `user_message` a reader already sees. A resume with no held steers reads nothing. A line from the replaced worker that lands after `turn_resume` stays hidden, so the resume's own line shows in its place. If the read fails, the turn resumes and may show a repeat.

## Known limitation

A host on a plain `createFxEngine()` can still see that repeat, with the same `id`. The engine can't tell what host code received, so the host has to key stored events by `id`. `sdk/README.md` and the `user_message` type now say so.

## Overlap with open pull requests

#1694 changes `publishSteeringReplay` and adds `author` to `PendingInput`. Whichever lands second needs a rebase, and `publishResumedInputs` should then pass `input.author`. #1330 changes `src/acp/prompt.zig` and `sdk/durable.js`, and #1370 changes `sdk/durable.js`.

## How I verified it

On Linux x86_64 with Zig 0.17.0, Node 24, and Bun 1.4.2, at base commit `88e00c39`:

- **New tests:** a `SIGKILL` while a steer waits, the same crash with the line already on the stream, and a deadline handoff. Without the fix, the crash and deadline tests fail on native with the streams above. Without the dedupe, the seeded test fails with two `user_message` lines. On WebAssembly the seeded test returns early, because that core can't reach this state.
- **Unit tests:** `zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe` passes 10476 of 10509 fx tests, with 31 skipped and 2 failed. The same 2 tests fail on unmodified `main` on this machine: `an edit to the file a symlinked AGENTS.md names is delivered on a later turn (D93)` and `git worktree reports dirty for obvious metadata and tracked-file changes`.
- **SDK:** `test-agent-steering.mjs` on native and wasm, `test-durable.mjs` on memory and local with both backends, `test-durable-core.mjs` on memory and local, `test-durable-harness.mjs`, `test-journal.mjs` in both directions, and `test-types.mjs`. I didn't run the `world` and `queue` durable modes locally, so CI is their first run on this change.
- **E2E:** `acp.test.ts` and `cli.test.ts`.
- **Models:** `tests/tla/sdk/check.sh`, `drive-steer.mjs` on `ideal` and `faults`, which includes deadline handoffs, with `--hooks` and `--backend wasm`, then `drive.mjs send` and `lookup`, and `drive-tenants.mjs`. CI runs the other drivers. `tests/tla/sdk/DurableSteer.tla` is unchanged, because it models where a steer lands and this change affects only what a host is told.
- **`./zig-out/bin/fx`:** it starts, draws its first frame, and exits with empty stderr. The terminal app doesn't reach this path, so the fix ran through the built `libfx.node` against a local mock gateway.

## Docs

- https://fx.sh/docs/lib/steering, "Steer an engine": add after the last paragraph: "When an engine resumes a turn after a crash, a steer's `user_message` event can repeat with the same `id`, because the engine can't tell what your code already received. If you store these events, key them by `id`. A session shows each one once."

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Keep an instance's model and effort across /new
body:
## Summary

- `/new` in an instance opened with `/launch <profile>` keeps the instance's model and effort instead of falling back to your configured ones.
- `/new` in the first instance saves the model and effort it keeps running, so resuming that session uses them instead of your configured ones.
- `/new` in a launched instance keeps a `--model` or `FX_MODEL` choice for the run, and the new session doesn't save it.
- A `/model` or `/effort` choice made before `/new` carries into the new session, and `/clear` works the same way.
- In the libfx terminal, `/new` starts with the model and effort the closing session saved instead of the workspace's.

title: Keep underscore helper functions in the shell snapshot
body:
## Summary

- Commands that go through a startup-file wrapper whose helper function starts with `_`, such as Socket Firewall's `pnpm` and `npm` wrappers, now run in fx as they do in the user's terminal, instead of failing with `command not found: _socket_fw_wrap`.
- zsh completion functions that compinit or `autoload` loads from their own files still stay out of the shell snapshot.
- bash functions from bash-completion and other completion scripts still stay out of the shell snapshot.
- A bash startup-file function that uses an extglob pattern such as `@(a|b)` no longer stops the shell snapshot and sends every later command through full startup.

title: Save every agent's request in flight when the window closes
body:
## Summary

- Closing the window, logging out or rebooting while several agents wait on the model (main, its subagents, other instances) now saves each of their requests as a clean close, not only the one that started last.
- A request that ends no longer takes another agent's request out of the ones saved on close.
- After the window is closed twice this way, the next launch resumes main's request instead of asking "This request crashed fx twice".

Fixes #1695.

title: Keep the screen in place when ctrl+g reloads an update
body:
## Summary

- When ctrl+g reloads fx into an installed update, the conversation stays where it is until the new build draws it again. Before, it moved up by the rows a launch keeps free for the welcome message, or off the screen when startup scrollback was on.
- The same holds when the reloaded session had no saved turn and fx opens a fresh one.

title: Prioritize active agents and close subagents with Delete
body:
## Summary

- Put working agents first without changing their relative order, then sort inactive agents by their latest completed reply. Keep the same agent selected when rows move and restore reply order when resuming a session.
- Close a selected subagent with two presses of Delete/Backspace instead of `x`. Show `press delete again to close this subagent` after the first press.

## Verification

- `zig fmt --check src/`
- `zig build`
- `zig build test`
- `cd tests/e2e && FX_SOUND=0 bun test --max-concurrency 1 tui-host-switch.test.ts`: 29 passed.
- `cd tests/e2e && FX_SOUND=0 bun test --max-concurrency 1 tui-host-instances.test.ts`: 34 passed.

Terminal tests used a fresh private `TMUX_TMPDIR` per file, matching CI's isolation.

## Docs

Manual updates needed in the companion documentation repository:

- https://fx.sh/docs/capabilities/subagents: add an agent-list section describing working-first order, inactive agents ordered by their latest completed reply, and two presses of Delete/Backspace to close the selected subagent. Closing stops its work and removes it from the list; it does not delete its saved history.
- https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/keyboard-shortcuts: document Delete/Backspace twice in the agent list as the subagent close shortcut, replacing `x`/`X` wherever listed.
- https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/instances: explain that instance numbers stay unchanged when activity or recent replies move rows, and that selection follows the agent rather than its former row.

title: List live sessions and read the last turns of any session or subagent
body:
## Summary

- `fx sessions --live` lists only the sessions an fx process has open right now, in this workspace or, with `--all`, in every workspace, newest first.
- A session drops off the list as soon as its process ends, including a crash or SIGKILL, because liveness comes from the session's own writer lock.
- Each live session shows its title, the model saved with it, and `working` while a turn is open or `idle` otherwise. A session whose log can't be read shows `unknown`.
- Each session's subagents are listed below it, and a subagent's own subagents below that, each with its state and the `<id>/<name>` address that reads it. A subagent closed for good is left out.
- `fx sessions --live --json` prints the list as `kind: live_sessions`, with an `agents` array on each session and subagent.
- `fx sessions --live` with `--limit` or `--cursor` exits 2 and names the flag.
- `fx session <id> --tail <1-1000>` prints only the last turns, under their own turn numbers. JSON keeps `history_len` as the full count and adds `first_turn`. It works with `last` and `--id`, and `fx session recover` refuses it.
- `fx session <id>/<agent>` reads a subagent by the name its parent gave it, and `<id>/<agent>/<agent>` reads that subagent's own. An unknown name exits 1 and lists the names the session has.
- An address with a part no subagent can have exits 1 with `InvalidAgentAddress` and names that part and the naming rule, or says the address has an empty name or goes more than 4 agents deep.
- `fx session` shows saved turn text with every control byte other than line breaks and tabs written as a visible escape, so text a model or a tool saved can't act on the terminal. JSON output is unchanged.
- The model shown is the one saved with the session, labeled `saved model` in text and `saved_model` in JSON, so a model chosen for one run, such as through `FX_MODEL`, doesn't show.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#259

title: Hold Ctrl+G's upgrade while another agent is busy
body:
## Summary

- Ctrl+G no longer upgrades while a subagent or another instance is working, which used to cancel that agent's turn. It shows "upgrade is unavailable while solo is working" instead.
- The same holds while another agent needs approval, has a question, or needs the user ("upgrade is unavailable while solo needs approval", "... has a question", "... needs you").
- On a subagent's screen, a busy main agent holds the upgrade the same way.
- Once every other agent is idle, Ctrl+G upgrades as before.

CI note: two files failed once and passed on retry. `tui-host-switch.test.ts` failed in "the agent list keeps working order, sorts idle responses newest first", added in #1701, which checks the list's sort order; it passed 10 of 10 runs locally on this branch. `tui-auth-source-selection.test.ts` covers sign-in. This change touches neither the list's order nor sign-in.

title: Keep the transcript in place when a question is cancelled
body:
## Summary

- Pressing Esc on a question that pushed the transcript into scrollback keeps the transcript on the same rows and puts the freed rows below the footer, also after an earlier terminal resize.
- Resizing the terminal while a question is open no longer pins the footer to the bottom after Esc, so no blank band opens above the transcript.
- A repaint after a cancellation keeps the transcript and footer where they are instead of moving them down.

title: Add the CLI shape values to the skill and CONTRIBUTING.md
body:
## Summary

- The `fx-cli-shape` skill in `.fx/skills/fx-cli-shape/` now starts with the values its rules come from: guessable names that follow open standards and git, one name per concept, one job per mechanism, scripts as first-class users, limited trust in project files, one source of truth, a small surface, and no silent breakage.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` has a section on adding or changing a command, flag, or setting, with the core rules, a pointer to the skill, and the CI check that enforces them. Before, it pointed contributors only to the `technical-writer` skill.
- The skill gains gotchas from recent changes: a deprecation warning first ships in the first release tagged after it merges; tests write the `/help` command count as a literal; a placeholder slash command is removed, not hidden, and gets a line in the router's removed-commands test; and an `FX_*` override that `fx config list` reports must be registered `stable`.
- The rules no longer say `/alias` exists.

title: Tell the parent agent when fx stops a subagent for invalid shell calls
body:
## Summary

- When fx stops a subagent because its model sends the same invalid shell call twice in a row, the parent agent now gets a report that says the subagent failed and why: "Repeated shell validation failures stopped the tool loop...". It used to get `completed` with an empty output, so it could neither recover nor tell the user.
- The parent's row for that subagent reads `lane4 failed` instead of `lane4 completed`. The subagent's own screen still shows the stop notice.
- `fx ask` now exits 1 when this stop ends its run, as it already does for the repeated shell failure stop.
- A subagent report whose reply is empty now says "The subagent ended its turn without a reply." instead of giving an empty output.

## Before and after

What main's model received for a subagent stopped this way:

```text
before: {"agent":"lane4",...,"outcome":"completed","output":""}
after:  {"agent":"lane4",...,"outcome":"failed","output":"Subagent failed: agent_turn_failed. ... Repeated shell validation failures stopped the tool loop. The invalid shell calls were not executed and produced no shell effect."}
```

title: Follow ACP v1 for session errors, close, and system prompts
body:
## Summary

- A request frame over 8 MiB gets `-32600` instead of `-32000`, which ACP v1 assigns to "Authentication required".
- The SDK answers a failed journal flush with `-32603` instead of `-32000`.
- A request that names a session that doesn't exist or isn't active gets `-32002` with `data.sessionId` set to that ID. This covers `session/prompt`, `session/cancel`, `session/set_mode`, `session/set_config_option`, the `libfx/*` methods, and `session/load` or `session/resume` of a missing session. A request without a `sessionId` still gets `-32602`.
- `session/close` of a session that isn't active returns `{}` and leaves the active session open.
- `session/new` takes `systemPrompt` as ACP v1's `{"mode": "append", "content": [...]}` object and refuses the older bare array. fx no longer reads the root `systemPromptMode` or `_meta.fx.systemPrompt`.
- `session/load` and `session/resume` take `systemPrompt` too. One fx can't apply fails the request before the session loads, and a different one replaces the stored prompt from the next turn.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#260

title: Free a rotated refresh token once and read out-of-range expiries as expired
body:
## Summary

- A Grok or Codex token refresh whose reply rotates the refresh token but gives a lifetime fx can't use (missing for Grok, or large enough to overflow) now ends that sign-in the way a rejected refresh does, and fx asks you to sign in again. Before, fx freed the new refresh token twice and could crash.
- A saved Grok or Codex login whose `expires_at_ms` is so far in the past that subtracting fx's one-minute margin overflows now reads as expired. `fx status` and every other command that reads the login keep working instead of aborting with `panic: integer overflow`.
- A saved MCP login whose `skew_ms` is at the top of i64 no longer aborts fx with `integer overflow` before its first request: the sum of the clock and the skew now saturates, so that login reads as due for a refresh and fx renews it. A negative skew keeps its old reading, and the server's 401 still starts a refresh.

This supersedes #446 and #756. The double free has no issue of its own; it came up while reviewing #437. Builds on #756 by @adi-IL; the parse-to-expired test follows #446 by @beardthelion.

Fixes #445

title: Read v2 sessions in the shell command TLA driver
body:
## Summary

- The shell command TLA driver (`bun test ./tests/tla/drivers/shell_command/`) reads tool results from v2 sessions, `sessions/v2/<id>/log.jsonl` and its blobs. It read the v1 `events.jsonl` layout, which fx no longer writes.
- On main it failed with `current INCONCLUSIVE: unreadable results: guard same rejected call repeated/c2`: when the loop guard ends a turn, the last call's result is only in the saved session. It now passes: 4 pass, 1 skip (the proposed design, which runs only with `FX_TLA_PROPOSED=1`).
- No CI job runs this driver, which is why the break went unnoticed.

title: Pick agents by name in the agent switching tests
body:
## Summary

- The agent switching tests pick an agent by its name in the agent list, so they pass whatever order the list shows.
- A test that switches agents no longer fails when a reply or a restart reorders the list while it runs, as these tests did on macOS in the PGSO behavior check that runs before a release.

title: Read tool calls whose request arrives as JSON text
body:
## Summary

- A shell call whose only argument is `request` holding the JSON text of the call, as MiMo sends it, now runs as the flat call, and permission review and the saved history see the flat call.
- A `read_tool_result` call with `request` as JSON text now reads the result, and the next request replays it with top-level arguments.
- A subagent call with `request` as JSON text now runs and replays flat for every action the tool takes: `message`, `wait`, `status`, `stop`, and `close`. `run` is not an action and is refused in every form.
- Request text nested more than 64 levels is left as sent and refused like any request fx cannot read. The limit is the one fx puts on provider JSON. Because of that limit, deep text never reaches `std.json.Stringify`, which aborts fx past 256 levels.
- Text longer than 64 KiB, text that is not a JSON object, and a shell or subagent wrapper with fields beside it keep their current errors, including the shell correction advice.
- A text-wrapped `read_tool_result` call shows the same row as its object form, such as `Searching earlier conversation`. The row decodes the text in a 4 KiB buffer, and a request whose decoded form does not fit keeps the generic row: about 2.2 KiB of plain query text, or a search of about 25 short phrases.
- `src/main.zig` lists `read_tool_result_presentation.zig` with the other tooling files.
