title: Upgrade to Zig 0.17.1
body:
## Summary

- Build fx with Zig 0.17.1 in every workflow that installs Zig, including releases, PGSO, fuzzing, and benchmarks.
- Set `minimum_zig_version` to 0.17.1 and require 0.17.1 in the PGSO toolchain check. LLVM stays at 22.1.8, which 0.17.1 still bundles.
- Ask contributors for Zig 0.17.1 in the README and the contributing guide.
- Close an MCP HTTP connection when its answer is left unread, as Zig 0.17.0 did. Zig 0.17.1 reads such an answer to the end instead, so a 202, 401, or 403 without a length, or a server that holds the connection open, kept the request from ending.
- Keep PGSO on the bitcode Zig generates before LLVM's passes. Zig 0.17.1's `-femit-llvm-bc` is optimized, so PGSO now reruns the `pgso-ir` compile with `--verbose-llvm-bc`, which adds about 25 seconds for fx.
- Keep the unoptimized bitcode under the hash of the module `pgso-ir` installed, and reuse it when a `zig build` cache hit installs that module again. Two compiles of one commit are not byte-identical, because the debug info records the generated `builtin.zig` path, so without this the benchmark pairs fail their bitcode identity check.
- Say in `CONTRIBUTING.md` that Zig 0.17.0 still builds fx without a warning, while CI tests only 0.17.1 and the PGSO pipeline stops on any other version.
- Read the macOS SDK version from `Version`, the key Zig 0.17.1's SDK stub uses, so macOS PGSO accepts the stub instead of stopping with "invalid Zig Darwin SDK version".
- Fix the PGSO provenance test case for a mismatched Zig version, which set the fixture's own version and failed.

title: Run the ACP models and drivers in CI
body:
## Summary

The ACP models in `tests/tla/acp/`, and the drivers that run `fx acp` along them, never ran in CI. A change to `src/acp/` could break a modeled rule without anything failing.

- A new `TLA+ ACP models and drivers` job runs `tests/tla/acp/check.sh --ci` against the binary from `Build fx (ReleaseSafe)`.
- `--ci` checks every ACP config, then runs every `tests/tla/drivers/acp/*/driver.ts`, so a new driver runs in CI without a workflow change. It runs them all and fails at the end if any failed.
- The planted bugs (`check-spec.ts`) stay local, as for the MCP models: they measure the checks, not the code.
- `scripts/detect-ci-need.sh` gains an `acp` output. A pull request runs the job when it changes `src/acp/`, the ACP models or drivers, the code they share (`tests/tla/drivers/lib/`, `tests/tla/lib/`), the fake Gateway in `tests/e2e/tmux-helpers.ts`, or the build and CI files.
- `Build & Test` now requires the job.
- Shellcheck checks `tests/tla/acp/check.sh` with `-x`, so it follows the script's source of `tests/tla/lib/tlc.sh`. The other scripts in the list source nothing, and their result is the same.

title: Accept benign Chat Completions stream variants
body:
## Summary

- A configured `openai-chat-completions` connection accepts chunks whose `model` is an empty string. The empty name sets no identity, and a non-string, oversized, or conflicting model still fails the turn.
- A legacy `function_call` whose `name` and `arguments` are absent, null, or empty counts as absent. One that names a call, and any `audio`, still fails with `InvalidChunk`.
- A stream that closes after the finished choice without `data: [DONE]` completes the turn. A stream that closes before any `finish_reason`, including one whose finish event never got its blank line, still fails with `IncompleteStream`, so a partly delivered tool call never runs.
- A stream cut inside a trailing usage event completes with the usage that arrived whole.
- A usage trailer that repeats the finished choice may omit `finish_reason` or send null. A reason that is present must still match, and the trailer still needs usage and may not add content, tool calls, or a refusal.

title: Watch and restore an unexported ZDOTDIR in the shell snapshot

- When the startup files set ZDOTDIR without exporting it, as `ZDOTDIR=~/.config/zsh` in `~/.zshenv` does, an edit to `$ZDOTDIR/.zshrc` now refreshes the snapshot before the next command.

- A startup file edited in the folder that `~/.zshenv` moves ZDOTDIR to, while fx captures the snapshot, refreshes the snapshot before the next command.
- After a failed replay with a moved ZDOTDIR, commands run with the full startup, and fx captures again only after a watched startup file changes.
- In bash, a startup file that turns extglob on only while it defines a function, and off again afterwards, no longer makes the replay fail and every later command run the startup files again.

title: Send ACP v1 stop reasons, config categories, and valid UTF-8 progress from fx acp
body:
## Summary

- fx acp answers a length-limited turn with stop reason `max_tokens` and a turn-limit stop with `max_turn_requests`, on the prompt response and on absorbed steering responses.
- A failed turn that fx keeps in its history ends with `end_turn`; one it leaves out ends with `refusal`; a step-limit stop ends with `max_turn_requests`. ACP drops a refused turn from the next prompt, so `refusal` now always means the next request leaves the turn out.
- fx keeps a failed turn after an empty reply twice, malformed tool arguments, a repeated terminal validation or shell failure, and a failed request after a tool step. Those turns end with `end_turn`, and the next request still holds the prompt and its tool calls.
- fx leaves out a failed first request and a stream cut inside a tool call. Those turns still end with `refusal`, and the next request leaves them out.
- A turn that stops at the agent step limit answers `max_turn_requests` and stays in the next request, where `refusal` would tell the client to drop it.
- libfx keeps its own stop reason names, such as `max_output_tokens` and `yielded`. For failed turns it reports `end_turn` when fx keeps the turn, `refused` when fx leaves it out, and `max_model_turns` at the step limit. No libfx test pins `refused` for these endings.
- The `provider`, `fast`, and `ultrafast` config options use category `model_config`, so the `model` option is the only one in category `model` and ACP clients find the model picker.
- Shell progress updates stay valid UTF-8 when a chunk of command output ends inside a character: the unfinished bytes wait for the next chunk of the same call and stream.
- Command output bytes that are not valid UTF-8, and a character left unfinished when the command ends, are sent as `\xNN` escapes.

Fixes #1157

title: Let web_fetch accept DNS64 answers for public hosts
body:
## Summary

- web_fetch fetches public hosts on IPv6-only networks with DNS64/NAT64, where a URL whose host has no public IPv6 address of its own used to fail with `NonPublicDnsAnswer`, because DNS64 answers with a NAT64 address.
- An address in the NAT64 well-known prefix `64:ff9b::/96`, from DNS or a URL literal, is judged by the IPv4 address in its last 32 bits.
- A NAT64 address that wraps a loopback, private, link-local, or other special IPv4 address is still refused before any connection.
- The local-use prefix `64:ff9b:1::/48` and IPv4-compatible and IPv4-mapped addresses are still refused.

Fixes #1184

Builds on the patch suggested in #1184 by @lemonadev03.

title: Stop rejecting replies to non-English requests that quote English
body:
## Summary

- A request written in another Latin-script language, such as Vietnamese or Indonesian, that quotes English now gets the reply it asks for in any script. fx used to reject that reply, retry once, and fail with "The model response used a different language than your request".
- Plain English prompts keep the guard: fx still replaces a reply in another script once and then fails the turn.
- fx expects a Latin reply only when the whole prompt reads as English: no Latin letter outside ASCII, and an English function word in every clause of three or more words.
- English prompts that fail that test, such as one with an accented name like José or a terse clause like "Run zig build.", no longer get the guard.
- An accent stored as a base letter and a combining mark, such as Vietnamese in decomposed form, counts like the same precomposed letter, so that request is no longer read as English.
- A broken byte in front of an accented letter no longer hides the letter from the guard.
- A request in Dutch, Polish, Turkish, Czech, German, Danish, Vietnamese typed without accents, and other Latin-script languages is no longer read as English because it uses a word that English shares, such as "to", "we", "of", "by", "my", "her", "for", or "can". English contractions such as "don't" and "it's" still count.
- The English word list is 55 words and leaves out the words that other Latin-script languages use as ordinary words, such as `to`, `we`, `of`, `by`, `my`, `her`, `for` and `will`. 17 more, such as `can`, `don` and `it`, count only as contraction stems.
- A word such as `can`, `don` or `it` counts as English only as a contraction before `'t`, `'s`, `'re`, `'ll`, `'ve`, `'d` or `'m` (with either apostrophe), so a Turkish name with a suffix such as `Can'a`, or French `l'eau`, is not read as English.
- No-break, narrow no-break, ideographic and the other Unicode space separators split words like an ASCII space, so words joined by them are counted one by one.
- A clause ends at any line break outside code spans: LF, CR, VT, FF, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029, so a request and an English line separated by a lone CR are read as two clauses.
- The guard decodes text with the shared `display_width.decodeNextRune`, finds spaces with `unicode_classes.isWhitespace`, and searches the prompt for the language-switch phrases with `ascii_case.containsIgnoreCase`.
- Known limit: a request that runs straight into its English with no punctuation, shares only "the" or "that" with it (Vietnamese without accents), or starts a clause with a capital "I" (Italian, Polish) can still get the English expectation.
- Two more known limits: a request whose clauses all have fewer than three words, and a stray unmatched backtick that turns the rest of the prompt into code, can still get the English expectation.

Fixes #809

title: Show Vercel team names safely and fail sign-in when teams can't load

The in-app `/login` no longer exits with `fx: ansi band overflow`, and `fx login` no longer writes the raw sequences to the terminal.

title: Make the startup benchmark remove only its own fixture folder
body:
## Summary

- `benchmarks/startup.sh` makes its fixture folder with `mktemp -d` and sets its EXIT trap only after that succeeds, so it removes only a folder it created. A folder already at the old `fx-session-list-benchmark-$$` path, or any other folder in TMPDIR, now survives a normal run, an early exit (no fx binary, no hyperfine), and SIGTERM.

title: Send subagent permission requests to the ACP client
body:
## Summary

- `fx acp` sends a subagent's permission request to the client as `session/request_permission` on the parent session while the prompt is open. `_meta.fx.subagent` has `childId` and `workId`, and `name` when the subagent has one. Before, the subagent waited forever and the prompt never returned.
- Only a subagent call that asks the client gets a card on the parent session. The card is announced `pending` with the request, moves to `in_progress` when the call starts, and ends once: `completed` when the call succeeded, `failed` when it was rejected, failed, or cut short by a stop or a cancel.
- The card's `toolCallId`, and the one in the request, is `<childId>:<n>:<modelCallId>`: the child id, the 1-based order of the child's calls that got a card, and the id the model chose. When one run's model reuses an id, each call gets its own card with its own updates. Every id is unique in the session and stays the same across the card's updates.
- Only an allow runs the subagent's action. A reject, an error answer, an unknown option, or a cancelled outcome denies it, and the prompt returns.
- Two subagents that ask at once get separate requests, and each answer applies only to its own request.
- `session/cancel` withdraws open subagent requests with `$/cancel_request`. A late answer runs nothing.
- When a prompt ends or is cancelled, every subagent card still open ends as `failed` before the prompt response. No card update follows the response. A subagent call that asks after that gets no card.
- A request cancelled after it was inserted and before it was written is withdrawn again after the write, so the client is not left showing it. This holds for the parent's own permission requests and for host tool, journal, and elicitation requests.
- A late or repeated answer, each request a cancel settles, and an error, malformed, or unknown answer leave one trace line each, and a subagent call's report that arrives after the prompt's close leaves one trace line naming its card.
- A subagent that asks while no prompt is open, after it was stopped, or when no slot is left gets no request and no card. Its model reads that the tool did not run because it needs approval and fx could not ask, with the cause: the prompt ended or was cancelled, the agent that asked was stopped, too many approval requests are open, or the client cannot show approval prompts. The result's `reason` stays `permission_required`, so it does not read as a refusal by the person.
- When the parent stops a subagent that is waiting on the client, fx withdraws its request, ends its card as `failed`, and the prompt returns. Its model reads the stopped cause. A prompt that closes or is cancelled while a subagent waits gives its model the prompt cause.
- A worker that is stopped while it waits for an approval reports that it was stopped, not a plain denial. This also applies to the terminal app's approvals.
- For SDK hooks, one subagent approval is one `wait.start` and one `wait.end`, not two nested pairs, and a wait that the prompt's close or a stop ended is `cancelled`, as the parent's own is, not `failed`.
- A permission wait whose request is no longer in the registry, for the parent's own request or a subagent's, ends as a refusal that says the prompt closed, not as a denial, and leaves one trace line. A cancelled answer to the parent's own request still denies.
- If the parent's own turn fails, its subagent's request stays open, and an allow still runs the action.
- At most 32 requests are open at the client at once. Subagent requests use at most 31 of them, so the parent's own request always has a slot. A subagent request past that limit is refused with the too-many-requests cause.
- A prompt that fails to start closes the subagent gate again, so a later subagent request is refused. It also closes the steering the start opened, so a steering message is not queued for a turn that never runs.
- `fx ask` does not run a subagent's gated action, because it has no way to ask for a subagent. The subagent's model reads that the tool did not run and that noninteractive mode cannot show an approval prompt, instead of waiting forever. That text is unchanged.
- A subagent's approved file write is no longer asked again when the live authority changes twice before the write. The terminal app's subagents use the same revalidation, so this also applies there.
- Unchanged here, and outside ACP: the terminal app's approval screen still submits a plain denial when it fails, and `fx ask` still denies when reading its approval answer from stdin fails.

Fixes #1465

title: Send Chat Completions permission reviews without the pending tool call

title: Honor HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, and NO_PROXY
body:
## Summary

- Model requests, sign-in and token refresh, model catalogs and version checks, MCP HTTP servers, upgrades, and web_fetch now go through the proxy that `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, or `ALL_PROXY` names. fx opens an HTTP CONNECT tunnel to the host and runs TLS to that host inside it.
- Lowercase variables win over uppercase ones, and empty values are ignored. A value without a scheme, such as `proxy:3128`, is read as `http://proxy:3128`. Connections to port 80 use `HTTP_PROXY`, every other port uses `HTTPS_PROXY` (web_fetch always uses `HTTPS_PROXY`, because it fetches every URL over https), and `ALL_PROXY` stands in for either one when it is unset.
- `NO_PROXY` keeps hosts and their subdomains, IP addresses, CIDR blocks, and `host:port` entries off the proxy, and `*` turns the proxy off. `localhost` and loopback addresses always connect directly.
- Credentials in the proxy URL are percent-decoded and sent as `Proxy-Authorization: Basic`. They never appear in error messages or trace logs.
- When the proxy refuses CONNECT, the request ends at once with a message that names the proxy, the target, and the reason, for example `proxy 127.0.0.1:3128 refused CONNECT to api.example.com:443: 407 Proxy Authentication Required`. `fx ask`, the interactive app, and web_fetch's error show it, and only the request whose own connection failed shows it.
- A model request through a proxy that answers 502, 503, or 504, or that fx cannot reach, is retried the same way as a dropped network. The `fx models` error, the Grok version lookup error, and the `fx upgrade` error name the proxy and say why in a whole sentence, such as `could not connect to proxy 127.0.0.1:3128 (connection refused)`. A proxy that answers with something other than HTTP, or sends bytes before fx speaks, ends the request. A proxy that sends an interim 1xx head, other than 101, before its final answer is waited out; a 101 ends the request. fx never falls back to a direct connection or to plain HTTP.
- A retry notice that names the proxy keeps "next try in" or "retrying", for a 502 answer and for a proxy host name of 253 bytes: it gives the proxy's host:port and the cause in at most 48 bytes, such as `Offline · next try in 1s · proxy 127.0.0.1:3128 answered 502` or `Offline · retrying · attempt 2 · proxy 127.0.0.1:3128 unreachable`, and cuts a host name too long for that with an ellipsis. The final error and `fx models` keep the whole sentence.
- A Grok client version lookup that ends `fx ask` and each request of `fx upgrade` name a proxy that failed them, for example `fx: could not connect to proxy 127.0.0.1:3128 (connection refused)` and `error: failed to fetch latest version from CDN: could not connect to proxy 127.0.0.1:3128 (connection refused)` (the same in `fx upgrade --json`); with no proxy, or when the proxy is not at fault, both say what they said before. A failing Jev permission-review request adds the proxy's sentence to its existing trace line and nothing to the screen; the AI Gateway reviewer opens its connection on a task of its own, so its trace line stays plain.
- A proxy fx cannot connect to is named the same way on macOS and Linux, including in web_fetch's error, for a closed port and for a proxy host name that does not resolve. Only the reason in the parentheses can differ: macOS reports a refused connect as `unexpected close`.
- Known limit: an MCP HTTP server reached through a failing proxy shows the MCP connect error, not the proxy's answer, because `src/mcp/io` would have to import `net_proxy_io`.
- Known limit: the AI Gateway permission reviewer's trace line does not name a proxy failure, because its connection runs on a task of its own that takes the held failure first. The Jev reviewer's trace line does.
- `https://` and SOCKS proxy URLs are refused with a message that names the variable. So are a value that is not a URL fx can read, a URL with no host, and a port outside 1 to 65535, each with its own reason.
- A proxy host with an underscore, such as `squid_proxy`, works.
- fx copies the proxy host and the `NO_PROXY` list when it first reads them, so a program that embeds fx and changes its environment later cannot change them.
- When `REQUEST_METHOD` is set, as under CGI, an uppercase `HTTP_PROXY` is ignored, because a server turns a request header named `Proxy` into that variable (httpoxy). Lowercase `http_proxy`, `ALL_PROXY`, and the HTTPS forms still apply.
- `NO_PROXY` entries that fx cannot read, and entries after the 1000th, are dropped and logged once in the debug trace.
- web_fetch still checks every DNS answer against its public-address rules before it dials, and its CONNECT names the checked address, so a proxy can't be used to reach a private address.
- Startup reads no proxy settings. fx reads them at its first connection.

Fixes #1344

title: Map fx's _meta.fx keys to sh.fx keys and capabilities
body:
## Summary

- List every `_meta.fx` key that fx's ACP server reads or writes, and the two fields of `clientCapabilities.libfx`, with where each appears and its new sh.fx key or capability.
- Split the steering key, which names three things today, into the `sh.fx/steering` capability, `sh.fx/steeringDelivery`, and `sh.fx/steerInput`.
- Turn `hooksVersion` into the `sh.fx/hooks` capability, and the client's tools into the `sh.fx/hostTools` capability.
- Drop the `_meta.fx.systemPrompt` copy, the root `systemPromptMode` field, and the client's libfx instructions in favor of ACP's standard `systemPrompt`.
- Check that every row has a known kind, a key that follows the naming rules, and no repeat.

Stacked on #1732.

title: Specify steering and queued prompts for sh.fx
body:
## Summary

- A `session/prompt` sent while a turn runs sets `sh.fx/delivery` in `_meta` to `"steer"` or `"queue"`, following ACP's prompt delivery draft for v2, and fx lists the `sh.fx/promptDelivery` capability.
- A steer holds text only, stops a reply the model is streaming, and joins the turn at its next request. A reply that ends while steers wait goes on with them.
- Steers that arrive while the turn finishes or after it stops taking input, and steers still waiting when the client stops the turn, run together as the next turn, before queued prompts, and report `next_turn`.
- fx holds queued prompts in one order across clients and runs each as its own turn.
- `session/cancel` stops only the running turn. `$/cancel_request` withdraws a waiting prompt with `-32800`, and `session/close` answers every waiting prompt with `-32800`.
- The SDK's journal methods stay under `sh.fx/hostSteering`.
- `tests/tla/acp/AcpPromptDelivery.tla` models these rules, and its `Today` configs fail where fx's ACP path breaks them now.
- `tests/tla/drivers/acp/prompt_delivery/driver.ts` runs `fx acp` through 8 plans of prompts, steers, tool calls, and stops, and checks each run against the model.

Stacked on #1733.

title: Exit cleanly when the terminal is revoked
body:
## Summary

- The interactive shell exits when its terminal is revoked, instead of polling the revoked terminal in a loop at full CPU.
- On macOS 15, where a read on a revoked controlling terminal fails with EIO, fx now ends cleanly too. It takes that error as the end of input only when a second check shows the terminal is gone: a poll that reports it closed, or stdin that is no longer a terminal.
- A revoke that cuts off a paste ends fx with exit status 0, where it used to exit 1 with `fx: terminal sync recovery failed`.
- Restoring the terminal on exit, and after the team picker or a masked key prompt, no longer aborts fx when stdin is no longer open.
- A revoked terminal now ends the team picker with exit status 1, instead of spinning at full CPU.
- A revoked terminal no longer makes `fx login vercel` spin at full CPU while it waits for browser authorization: the wait for a key sleeps out each 100 ms slice once stdin is gone, and the sign-in keeps polling the issuer.
- A revoked terminal no longer makes `fx mcp login` spin at full CPU while it waits for a pasted address (`--no-browser`, over SSH, or with no display): a failed read on a terminal that is gone ends the login with status 1 and a short message, unless the sign-in already finished, which then counts as done, and any other failed read sleeps out the 100 ms slice. A read of 0, which is how macOS 27 answers a revoked terminal, still waits for the browser, as before. The line is `Couldn't sign in to NAME: the terminal is gone.`
- Ctrl+Z, `bg`, and `fg` keep fx alive.

Known limit:

- When a parent starts fx with SIGTTIN and SIGTTOU ignored, fx keeps running in the background after `bg`, and a read there still fails with EIO on a terminal that is still there. fx then prints `fx: a disk read or write failed` and exits 1, as before this change. `tests/tla/shell_runtime/TerminalRevoke.tla` records it (`ReadErrorOnlyWhenLive`), and the driver's `job-control-signals-ignored` run shows it.

Follow-ups, not changed here:

- A revoke during startup, before the input loop runs, still ends fx with exit status 1: with `fx: a disk read or write failed` once fx has started, or with `fx requires an interactive terminal (TTY).` when the revoke lands before fx checks for a terminal.

title: Specify following a session and catching up for sh.fx
body:
## Summary

- A session can be open on several connections at once. A client joins a running session with ACP's own `session/load`, which replays the whole session and the running turn so far, or `session/resume`, which sends live updates. Joining needs no capability.
- While the session is open elsewhere, fx keeps its `cwd`, `additionalDirectories`, and `mcpServers`, and returns the session's folder as `sh.fx/cwd`. A `systemPrompt` applies from the next turn.
- `session/close` closes the session on the calling connection only, and a running turn goes on.
- With `sh.fx/logPosition`, fx gives the position of the last saved turn on load, resume, and each saved turn. A client sends it back in `sh.fx/replayFrom` on `session/load` to get only later turns, and `sh.fx/replay` says whether fx replayed after the position or the whole session.
- `tests/tla/acp/AcpFollow.tla` models these rules with replayed messages that keep their ids, and its `Today` configs fail where fx breaks them now.

Stacked on #1734.

title: Read TLC's final distinct-state count in the driver helper
body:
## Summary

- The TLA+ driver helper reports TLC's final distinct-state count. It used to read the first progress line instead, so a long run's "166,275 distinct states found" came out as 275.
- Short runs, which print no progress lines, report the same count as before.

title: Give fx-term.wasm its own turn and step ids
body:
## Summary

- In fx-term.wasm, a tool call from a later model step shows in its own tool block below the text before it, instead of joining the first block above that text.
- In fx-term.wasm, the tool calls of the second and later turns show under their own prompt. Before, they did not show at all.
- Tool calls from steps with no text between them still share one block, as in native fx.
- The WebAssembly builds give each turn, step, and subagent its own id, counting from 1 as native fx does. Before, every one got id 1.

Not changed here: when a streamed tool call follows text that does not end in a newline, fx first writes a line break, and that break counts as text after the tool call (`src/core/agent/runtime/assistant_stream.zig`). After this change, the next tool step opens a new block with nothing shown between the two blocks. Before it, fx-term.wasm showed both calls in one block. Native fx runs the same code for this case.

Builds on #590 by @srps.

title: Send operational ACP text as Session Notices to editors that show them
body:
## Summary

- An editor that advertises ACP v1 Session Notices (`clientCapabilities.session.notices: {}`) now gets fx's own text about a turn as `notice` updates instead of `agent_message_chunk`: the empty-reply nudge, the length resend, Ultrafast and catalog notes, and a restarted answer at `info` severity.
- System notices, such as the provider length-limit warning, reach that editor as `warning` notices.
- Each such message is one notice. The line breaks fx sends after a line are dropped, so they no longer become updates of their own.
- The text that says why a turn failed, such as a second empty reply, the step limit, or an image the catalog could not clear, stays an agent message.
- The text that ends a turn on a provider error event, such as an `invalid_request_error`, or on a response-language failure also stays an agent message.
- HTTP and auth failures, such as `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY authentication failed · HTTP 401`, stay agent messages.
- The text fx saves as the reply stays an agent message, so a live turn matches what `session/load` replays: `Done.` for a reply with no text, `The reply ran out of output tokens before any text.` for an empty reply that a length limit cut off and fx does not resend, and the note that a length limit cut off a reply's tool calls.
- Diff previews stay agent messages.
- Editors that don't advertise notices get exactly the agent messages they got before.
- The agent runtime marks two kinds of text, the reason a turn failed and the reply fx saves. ACP keeps them as agent messages. The terminal UI, `fx ask` and subagents show them as before.
- The core calls a turn-failure hook at the provider error and language failure exits. On other hosts these two texts are system notices (the TUI styles them; `fx ask` prefixes `[notice]` in raw and JSON output), and only ACP needs them as agent messages, so only ACP sets the hook and every other host falls back to the system notice.

ACP v1 says an agent must not rely on a notice for fatal-error reporting, authorization, or a required user action, and a client may ignore notices. A turn that fails with an HTTP error, such as a 401, returns only its stop reason (`refused`), so the 401 text is that turn's only error report, and it stays an agent message even for an editor that shows notices. A turn that ends on a provider error event or a response-language failure answers the prompt with a JSON-RPC error, so its failure text is its only reason, and it stays an agent message too.

Before and after, one `fx acp` turn for an editor that shows notices. The model stops without a reply, fx asks it to continue, and the model answers.

```
main
  agent_message_chunk  "The model stopped without a reply (provider reason: UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL). Asking it to continue."
  agent_message_chunk  "\n"
  agent_message_chunk  "REPLY_2"

this branch
  notice (info)        "The model stopped without a reply (provider reason: UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL). Asking it to continue."
  agent_message_chunk  "REPLY_2"
```

Fixes #1016

title: Accept loopback MCP URLs with no port, and skip one bad profile entry in ACP, fx status, and fx doctor
body:
## Summary

- An MCP server at a plain http loopback URL with no port, such as `http://localhost/mcp` or `http://127.0.0.1/mcp`, now loads and connects on port 80. `http://[::1]/mcp` now loads too, but fx does not reach a server at an IPv6 address literal with or without a port, as on main. It used to be skipped with `its "url" isn't valid`. This holds for `~/.fx/mcp.json` and `.mcp.json`.
- An `oauth.resource` at such a URL, and an HTTP server an ACP client sends in `mcpServers` at such a URL, are taken the same way.
- Plain http to any other host is still refused, with or without a port. A URL with an empty port, such as `http://localhost:/mcp`, is still refused. The libfx gateway URL still needs an explicit port, as `sdk/NAPI.md` says.
- An ACP session that sets `_meta.fx.profileMcpServers` now skips one `~/.fx/mcp.json` entry fx can't read and loads the others, as `fx mcp list` and the TUI do. Before, that one entry left the session with no profile server at all.
- Each profile entry ACP skips gets an `ACP profile MCP config skipped cause=... server=... problem=...` line in the `mcp` trace.
- `fx status` and `fx doctor` now do the same for `~/.fx/mcp.json`. They count the servers that load and name each entry they skip as a configuration issue, so `mcp_servers` is no longer 0 when one entry can't be read. `fx doctor` warns about the skipped entry where it used to fail, and `fx status` reports it as an `mcp_config_warning` with the cause `skipped_entry`, unless the file already has a warning of its own, which then stays the one shown. Each skipped entry is always listed as a configuration issue. The warning names the first skipped entry and counts the others. A file fx can't read at all, such as invalid JSON, still fails both.
- The `mcpServers` alias names fx ignores also show as configuration issues in `fx status` and `fx doctor`, as they do in `fx mcp list`.
- Every profile reader now takes the skipped list. The strict read that only tests used is removed, and those tests now check the skip note's `problem` instead of an error.
- ACP's refusal of a request server's URL now reads "MCP server url must be a valid HTTPS or loopback HTTP endpoint", without "explicit".

Fixes #1218

title: Tell the permission reviewer which shell runs a command
body:
## Summary

- In auto mode, the review of a shell command now states its environment on its own line. For `user` and `clean` it also states the shell path and the startup-file rule on their own lines. The browser workspace shell states `workspace_clean` and names no shell. Before, the shell path appeared only inside the encoded `@fx-terminal-env` identity on the `target[target]` line.
- The review of a `user` command now says the user's startup files are read first, so their aliases and functions apply and can change what the command runs.
- The review of a `clean` command now says the startup files are skipped.
- A command routed to a shell whose path is empty, or longer than the system path limit, is held as incomplete review evidence, without a reviewer call.
- Which commands go to review does not change.

Builds on #238 by @beardthelion.

Fixes #237

title: Keep the composer on the bottom row after a footer surface closes
body:
## Summary

- Closing the slash picker, a question, or an approval in a long session puts the composer and status line back on the bottom rows, with the transcript rows it covered painted back above them.
- Output that arrives while a surface is open still moves into scrollback in order, and every transcript row reaches scrollback exactly once, also across repeated open and close cycles.
- A resize or Ctrl+O while a surface is open keeps the covered rows out of scrollback. Ctrl+Z moves them into scrollback first, and after `fg` the close still lands on the bottom row with no row repeated.
- Quitting (with `/quit`, SIGTERM or SIGHUP), suspending, or starting a fresh session with a surface open first moves the covered rows into scrollback, also right after a resize.
- If a SIGTERM or SIGHUP close cannot draw its exit frame within 500 ms, or the terminal is already gone, fx logs the rows it left out of scrollback.
- If fx crashes or is killed with SIGKILL while a surface is open, the covered rows are only in the session log and Ctrl+O.
- A multi-line draft covers and returns rows the same way.

Fixes #815

title: Treat Thai nonspacing marks as zero-width
body:
## Summary

- Thai vowel and tone marks (U+0E31, U+0E34-U+0E3A, U+0E47-U+0E4E) take no cell after a base character. fx measures all text with one width table, so the transcript and pickers change with the composer. The cursor, text typed after a mark, repaints, and wrapping stay on the columns the terminal draws: after typing กั้งabc the cursor is 2 columns left of where it was.
- U+0E33 SARA AM still takes its own cell, so น้ำ is two cells wide.
- Left, Right, and Backspace move over a Thai character and its marks as one character, as they already did for Latin combining marks.
- The marks on a character in the last column of a composer row are now shown. This also fixes Latin combining marks in the last column, which were dropped before.
- In a window two columns wide or narrower the composer row has no cells for characters, so it draws no marks either and stays the bar alone, as on main, however many Thai marks are typed.

Only Thai is covered. Nonspacing marks in Lao and other scripts still take one cell each.

A cell holds at most 64 bytes of text, its base character and its suffix together. #1763 drops marks past that limit instead of ending fx, and this change is stacked on it.

A nonspacing mark at content column 0 of its row, with nothing but zero-width characters such as U+200B before it, has no base character. It is drawn on a dotted circle (U+25CC) in a cell of its own, and the marks after it stack there, so it never joins a prefix cell. One helper, `display_width.bareMarkUnitAt`, decides this for each surface that draws text after a prefix cell: the composer, the question prompt's free-text answer, its header, its option labels and descriptions, and the answer rows a resolved question leaves in the transcript, the approval feedback draft, the command of an approval panel (inline and in the review screen), the steering banner of a queued message (the fork menu draws its rows with the same layout and painter, so it follows), the card of a sent message, the status row above the composer, and the session titles in the resume menu. Each counts the circle's cell in its wrapping and its cursor, and none of them changes the text that is sent. A question's header, its option labels and descriptions, and an approval command draw a zero-width space as the visible text `\u{200b}` (and so does the row a chosen label leaves in the transcript), so a mark after one sits on that text and gets no circle there. In typed text (the composer, the free-text answer, the steering banner, the approval draft and the sent message) the zero-width space stays invisible and the mark after it gets the circle. A variation selector has no glyph of its own, so it is not drawn on a circle. The approval feedback draft scrolls by character, so its window never starts on a mark whose base was cut off.

In a reply's list item or quote that starts with a nonspacing mark with no base, fx does not show that mark; plain reply lines and tool rows are unchanged or better than before. Other places that draw text after a fixed glyph, such as reply paragraphs, tool rows, transcript notices, code panels, the footer menus and pickers, and the session header, still draw such a mark on the cell before it.

Builds on #267 by @PunGrumpy.

title: libfx steering check: a steer sent after a cancel stays in the cancelled turn
body:
## What happens

The durable-session steering model check in the `SDK (Bun + N-API/WASM)` job sometimes finds a walk where a steering prompt sent after a cancel stays in the cancelled turn. The model expects that prompt to start a new turn.

From [main CI run 42320592869](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/actions/runs/42320592869/job/128245944645), attempt 1, on f1902e708:

```text
FAIL walk 1 after Send(p) Start ToolArgs ToolCall Send(s2) ToolEnd Cancel Retry(s2) Send(s1) Retry(s1) Start
  the code shows   {"turns":[{"owner":"p","state":"cancelled","ctx":["p","s1","s2"]}],"phase":"gen","twice":[]}
  the model allows {"turns":[{"owner":"p","state":"cancelled","ctx":["p","s2"]},{"owner":"s1","state":"running","ctx":["s1"]}],"phase":"gen","twice":[]}
```

## Steps to reproduce

It fails intermittently. Rerun the `SDK (Bun + N-API/WASM)` job on main until the steering walks fail. Attempt 1 of run 42320592869 failed with the walk above, and attempt 2 on the same commit passed.

## Expected

`s1`, sent after `Cancel`, starts its own running turn. The cancelled turn's context holds only `p` and `s2`.

## Actual

`s1` joins the cancelled turn's context, and no new turn starts for it.

## Notes

- The same job also failed on 15dab7bb4 ([run 42287070194](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/actions/runs/42287070194/job/128133618476)), in a different walk: `Start(A) Claim(A) Deadline(A) Freeze(A) Wake(A) Start(B) Deadline(A) Freeze(A) Claim(B) Wake(A) Model1(A) Claim(B)`. That run's next commit passed.
- The steering walk above may be a real race between a cancel and a steer that arrives just after it, not test noise.
- Related: #1342, where a steer stored just before a tool returns misses the running turn.

title: Say which entries glob_files and grep_files skip outside a git repository
body:
## Summary

- Outside a git repository, `glob_files` and `grep_files` now end their output with a line naming the entries they skipped by name, such as `... skipped 3 entries named build, coverage, dist outside a git repository; pass path to search one`. Before, folders like `build`, `dist` and `node_modules` dropped out of the results with no sign.
- The note counts only entries below the searched path, so passing `path` to a subfolder, or to a skipped folder itself, reports only what that search left out.
- Hidden entries such as `.next` appear in the note only when hidden files are searched.
- Inside a git repository the output is unchanged, because `.gitignore` decides what is searched there.
- The tool descriptions are unchanged.
- The `@` file index snapshot moves to format v4, which stores the skipped paths, so a search answered from the snapshot prints the same note as a fresh scan. The snapshot is a cache: fx refuses a v3 file, scans again, and the next save writes v4.

Fixes #1450

title: Specify session state, status, and list changes for sh.fx
body:
## Summary

- fx sends a session's state, `running`, `requires_action`, or `idle` with the turn's `stopReason`, as the `_sh.fx/session/state_update` notification to a client that lists `sh.fx/sessionState`. It sends it on every change, and after the client opens the session. The `update` holds ACP's `StateUpdate`, so it becomes v2's `state_update`.
- fx supports ACP's unstable `session/status`: `open` while this process holds the session, `saved` when it's only on disk, `-32002` for a session fx doesn't know, and the state as `sh.fx/state`.
- `session/list` answers at once, also while a turn runs, and a row of a session fx holds gives its state as `sh.fx/state`.
- A client that lists `sh.fx/listChanges` gets the rowless `_sh.fx/session/list_changed` hint with the folder, after a session in a folder it listed is saved first, saves a turn, gets a new title, or is deleted.
- `tests/tla/acp/AcpSessionState.tla` models these rules, and its `Today` configs fail where fx breaks them now.
- `tests/tla/drivers/acp/session_state/driver.ts` runs `fx acp` through 3 plans of sessions, turns, lists, and status requests, and checks each run against the model.

Stacked on #1736.

title: Share the fx login and MCP credential locks across FX_HOME profiles
body:
## Summary

- On macOS with the Keychain, fx processes in different `FX_HOME` profiles refresh the shared fx login one at a time, and the shared MCP credentials one at a time too. A second refresh no longer sends a used refresh token and deletes the login for every profile.
- With `FX_HOME` set, fx takes the fx login's lock in `~/.fx/auth.lock`, the same lock the default profile takes, and the MCP credential store's lock and each login's refresh lock in `~/.fx/mcp-credentials`, the same folder the default profile uses. Older fx builds in the default profile that use these items take the same locks. fx creates `~/.fx`, and `~/.fx/mcp-credentials` for the MCP credentials, when missing, and sets existing ones to private (0700), as the default profile does.
- Without `FX_HOME`, with `FX_DISABLE_KEYCHAIN=1`, or off macOS, the lock stays in the profile as before. The MCP file store is one per profile and locks in its profile.
- When `HOME` is not an absolute path, when `~/.fx` can't be opened or made private, or when its lock can't be taken, fx keeps the lock in the profile and writes one debug trace line that names the step and the error, and the lock's path when the lock can't be taken. A lock can't be taken when a symlink, a file other users can read, a folder, or a fifo is in its place, as a stale file a `sudo` run left would be. Sign-in and refresh then work as before this change. A lock that another fx holds is never worked around.
- An older fx build in a profile that `FX_HOME` moved still locks its own profile, so mixed versions are not protected. A lock kept in the profile does not stop the old race either.

Builds on #1659 by @ValentinTorassa.

title: Check startup aliases before a routine auto-mode command skips review
body:
## Summary

- In auto mode, a routine command such as `git status` now reads the shell snapshot at admission and captures it first when none exists yet or the startup files changed. The first command of a process and the first command after a startup-file edit are now checked against the user's aliases and functions, like every later command.
- A routine command goes to the reviewer when a startup-file alias or function redefines one of its words, or when the snapshot capture fails.
- A routine command with `reload: true` goes to the reviewer, because the reload replaces the snapshot it was checked against.
- A routine approval is bound to the snapshot epoch it checked. If the startup files change before the command runs, the command is refused with exit 126 instead of running under the new startup files.
- After a failed snapshot replay, a bound approval reruns with full startup only when the startup files are unchanged.
- When the startup files set `ZDOTDIR` to a folder that fx's own environment does not name, a failed snapshot replay refuses neither the command whose replay failed nor another approval bound to the same snapshot when the startup files did not change, because the failed state keeps the moved `ZDOTDIR` (from #1716, which this PR builds on). A retry goes to review and runs.
- Routine commands whose words the startup files do not redefine still run without review.
- A single-threaded build, such as the WebAssembly core and terminal builds, reports the snapshot capture as failed, so a routine command's startup names stay unknown and the command goes to the reviewer.

Before and after, with `alias git='touch MARKER'` in the startup files and a routine `git status` in auto mode: on `main` the reviewer gets 0 requests and `MARKER` is created; with this change the reviewer gets 1 request and no `MARKER` is created.

Builds on #1716.

Fixes #258

Related: #259

title: Wipe OAuth and API key secrets before their memory is freed
body:
## Summary

- Signing in and refreshing with Vercel, Codex, and Grok, and signing out of Vercel and Grok, no longer leave access tokens, refresh tokens, device codes, or authorization codes in freed memory. Parsed token replies, request bodies, and growing buffers are wiped before each block goes back to the allocator, including the blocks a buffer outgrows.
- Reading and saving the auth session files wipes the file buffer and the saved JSON before they are freed. The saved files are unchanged byte for byte.
- libfx wipes its copy of the API key when a runtime is destroyed and when creating one fails after the key was copied. `sdk/NAPI.md` now says so.
- Known limit: the MCP credential store in `src/core/mcp_host/credentials.zig` has the same pattern. Its writer wipes only the final buffer, not the blocks it outgrows, and its parse of saved credentials releases its arena without wiping.

Fixes #365

title: Specify what the clients of an sh.fx session see of each other
body:
## Summary

- A prompt that starts a turn, or runs after the queue, goes to every other client that has the session open as `user_message_chunk` updates. Its sender gets no copy. A steer's chunk still goes to every client, because it marks where the steer joined the turn.
- A permission request goes to every client that has the session open, and to a client that opens it while the request waits. The first answer decides, fx cancels the request on the other clients with `$/cancel_request`, and it ignores later answers.
- Any client that has the session open can stop the running turn with `session/cancel`.
- A client that lists `sh.fx/sessionClients` gets its own id at `initialize`, and `_sh.fx/session/clients_update` with every client's id and `clientInfo` when a client opens or closes the session.
- `tests/tla/acp/AcpSharedSession.tla` models these rules, and its `Today` configs fail where fx breaks them now.
