title: Add a Zig skill for Zig 0.17 code
body:
## Summary

- Add the `zig` agent skill in `.fx/skills/zig/`, next to `fx-cli-shape` and `technical-writer`.
- Cover what Zig 0.17.x removed, deprecated, or changed without a compile error, including what 0.17.1 fixed, what it still breaks, and its two silent changes to `std.http` request teardown and `-femit-llvm-bc`.
- Cover Zig ownership, error, I/O, concurrency, testing, and build-mode practice in the same skill.
- Bundle a scanner for removed and deprecated APIs, a rename script for 0.16 code, compile-checked examples, and eval cases.
- Make the scanner and the rename script safe on any tree: they skip symbolic links and files that are not regular files inside a directory, never write through a link, name each file they cannot read and go on with the rest, escape control bytes in printed paths, and stay linear on long lines. The scanner exits 2 when a path cannot be read and no longer reports double-pointer types as the removed `**` operator.
- Run the skill's tests, including the compile check of its examples, in the `Build & Test` job.
- Point to the skill from the Zig section of `AGENTS.md`.

title: Accept per-chunk usage counts on Chat Completions streams
body:
## Summary

- A configured `openai-chat-completions` connection to a server that puts each chunk's own token counts in `usage`, such as Cloudflare Workers AI, now returns its reply instead of failing the turn with `ConflictingIdentity`.
- Usage on a chunk that carries a choice, the finish chunk included, is provisional: a usage that would lower a count fx already has is dropped, and a usage trailer's counts replace the ones fx kept.
- A reply without a usage trailer records the counts fx kept, which is the last usage on a chunk that lowered no count. For a stream of per-chunk counts, that is the first chunk's counts.
- A finish chunk's usage no longer fixes the reply's counts, so a usage trailer with higher counts after it replaces them instead of failing the turn.
- A usage trailer below a count fx kept, or a second trailer with other counts, still fails the turn with `ConflictingIdentity`.

Builds on #1203 by @lingoboris.

Stacked on #1715.

title: Load public CA roots when a macOS sandbox denies the keychain
body:
## Summary

- In a macOS sandbox that denies reads of `/Library/Keychains/System.keychain`, such as Agent Safehouse, HTTPS requests no longer fail with "couldn't load trusted certificates". fx loads the public CA bundle at `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` instead and still verifies every server certificate.
- The fallback applies only on macOS, and only when the keychain scan stops on a permission error. Any other scan error, an unreadable `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`, or one that holds no certificates still fails the request before it connects.
- While the fallback is in use, certificate authorities that are trusted only in the keychain are not trusted.
- Every HTTPS client in fx loads its roots the same way, so the fallback covers AI Gateway requests, configured providers, Codex and Grok, sign-in, the permission reviewer, `fx upgrade`, HTTP MCP servers, and `web_fetch`.

Builds on #1354 by @henrikogaard.

Fixes #1493

title: Specify subagents for sh.fx, following ACP's Subagent Sessions
body:
## Summary

- fx follows ACP's unstable Subagent Sessions with ACP's own names, for a client that lists `subagents` in `clientCapabilities`. A client that doesn't sees a subagent only through the parent's tool call and its report.
- fx announces a child with `subagent_update` before any update of its work, and every update and permission request of the child uses the child's own session id.
- `session/cancel` with a child's id stops only that child, and the parent's turn goes on with the child's result. Stopping the parent stops its children.
- A child's permission request goes to every client of the parent, and ends with the child.
- A reload of the parent replays each child's announcement and history before the response, without sending a recorded request again.
- For a client that lists `sh.fx/subagentPrompts`, each child grants `sh.fx/prompt`, and a message to a child works as on any fx session: it steers the child while it works, runs as its next turn if its work ends first, and starts its work while it's idle. The child's report goes to the parent, as today.
- `tests/tla/acp/AcpSubagents.tla` models these rules, and its `Today` configs fail where fx breaks them now.

Stacked on #1750.

title: Stop JS host terminals from reporting a failed settings save
body:
## Summary

- In fx-term.wasm and other JS host terminals, `/model` no longer prints "model: active for this process but not saved to global settings (HomeNotSet)" after the host config store saves the model.
- `/permissions ask`, `auto`, and `full-access` no longer print a `permission-mode` settings failure on JS host terminals.
- The full-access acknowledgment no longer prints a failed save on JS host terminals, and it holds for the session, so the warning does not come back on the next switch to full access.
- `/settings startup-scrollback on|off` prints the new value instead of a settings failure on JS host terminals.
- A host that passes `HOME` in the terminal env gets the same quiet result, where before fx tried the settings file and printed `FileNotFound`.
- Native fx still saves these preferences to `~/.fx/settings.json` and still reports a save that fails.

Builds on #586 by @srps.

Follow-up: on fx-term.wasm, `/allowlist add url https://example.com` still prints "allowlist: failed to add rule to settings (scope=workspace, error=HomeNotSet)". Allowlist rules are a permission write rather than a preference, so this PR leaves them as they are.

title: Specify fork and rewind for sh.fx
body:
## Summary

- fx supports ACP's unstable `session/fork`, which copies a session's saved turns into a new one and leaves the source as it was.
- A client that lists `sh.fx/fork` can name a prompt by its message id in `sh.fx/forkBefore`, and the fork holds only the turns before it, as fx's `/fork` does.
- A client that lists `sh.fx/rewind` sends `_sh.fx/session/rewind` with the same prompt, and fx removes that prompt's turn and every turn after it, keeping the session's id. Neither a fork nor a rewind changes any file.
- After a rewind, fx sends `_sh.fx/session/history_replaced` to the other clients that have the session open, a position from before the rewind replays the whole session, and the session list gets a change hint.
- While a turn runs, `session/fork` and the rewind get `-32600`.
- `tests/tla/acp/AcpForkRewind.tla` models these rules, and its `Today` configs fail where fx breaks them now.

Stacked on #1754.

title: Specify the combined file changes of one turn for sh.fx
body:
## Summary

- A client that lists `sh.fx/turnDiff` asks for one turn's combined file changes with `_sh.fx/session/turn_diff`, naming the turn by its prompt. fx answers with the changes its own tools made in that turn, each file before the turn's first change and after its last, for saved turns and for the running turn so far.
- The answer carries what fx's terminal shows: per file the added and removed line counts and a preview of up to 6 changed lines, each up to 4 KiB and 24 KiB in all, as the inline diff does.
- With `full` set, each file also gets its review with 5 lines of context, as fx's full transcript shows.
- `untracked` says when the turn ran a shell command, whose changes to files fx doesn't track.

Stacked on #1756.

title: Test that a plain ACP client gets only ACP v1 names
body:
## Summary

- A new `acp.test.ts` test runs an ACP client that lists no `sh.fx/` capability through a session, a turn with a shell call, `session/list`, and a replay, and checks that every method, `session/update` kind, and response field fx sends it is ACP v1's, from the pinned ACP copy.
- Until fx moves to the sh.fx names, the test allows only the `_meta.fx` keys that `sh-fx.md` lists in "Keys in use today", so a new non-standard key fails at once.
- `FX_ACP_STANDARD_ONLY=1` allows no `_meta.fx` key, for the change that moves the names. Today it reports `_meta.fx.steering`, `_meta.fx.permissionMode`, and `_meta.fx.toolCall`.

Stacked on #1757.

title: Read clipboard images off the input thread
body:
## Summary

- `/paste` and Ctrl+V return at once and show "reading clipboard". Typing and other keys keep working while osascript exports the image.
- A second `/paste` or Ctrl+V during a read shows "already reading clipboard" and starts no second export.
- A read that runs past 10 seconds stops with "clipboard read timed out".
- Quitting during a read ends fx at once. fx sends osascript SIGKILL before it reaps it: the standard library's kill sends SIGTERM and then blocks until the child exits, so an osascript that ignored SIGTERM would hold up shutdown.
- The image goes to the agent that asked for it, even when another agent is on screen. That agent shows it the next time it is on screen.
- If the agent that asked has closed, the image is dropped with "clipboard image not attached: the agent that asked has closed".
- If the model picker holds the composer when the read finishes, the image is inserted when the picker closes.

Fixes #414

Builds on #415 by @reyanshgupta, which had the shape used here: a background runtime that owns the read, a guard against a second start, and a bounded child that can be cancelled. That diff patched helpers that have since been removed, so this is written fresh against the current tree.

title: Sign in Grok Team accounts and keep the Team on refresh
body:
## Summary

- `fx login grok` with a Grok Team subscription now finishes and saves the Team as the account, instead of failing with `GrokUserInfoRequestFailed` after the browser step. fx reads the Team from the access token's `principal_type` and `principal_id` claims and does not ask `/oauth2/userinfo` for it.
- Refreshing a Team login sends `principal_type=Team` and `principal_id`, so the refreshed token stays on the Team and fx keeps the login instead of signing it out as a changed account.
- A Team token whose `principal_id` is missing or not a safe account id fails sign-in, and a saved Team login with such a token is signed out before any refresh request.
- Personal accounts, and tokens without principal claims, keep the userinfo path and send no principal fields on refresh.

That userinfo refuses Team tokens comes from the reporter and one other user, and can't be checked here without a Team account. The tests' fake issuer follows their description.

Builds on #456 by @redreceipt.

Fixes #461

title: Record libfx's queue namespace on its Workflow runs
body:
## Summary

- An open libfx session in a World the app shares with the Workflow SDK, such as a world-local data folder or a world-postgres database, no longer ends `failed` when the app restarts. Each session's run records libfx's queue namespace, so the World's startup recovery sends it to libfx's queue instead of the Workflow SDK's.
- libfx's queue route acks a recovery message, which carries no prompt, at its first delivery, even when no agent in the process is named `default`. Before, such a process refused it, and world-local delivered it again every 5 seconds, up to 256 times.
- Sessions an earlier libfx created recorded no namespace, so recovery still sends them to the default queue.

Fixes #1253

title: Hand steers stored in this process straight to the running turn
body:
## Summary

- A steer sent from the app's own process while a tool runs is now in the request that carries the tool's result, on `memory()`, `local()` and any World, even when the tool returns the moment `steer()` resolves.
- A steer another process stores still arrives on the running worker's next poll, 250 ms on `local()` and 1 s on `vercel()`, as before.
- Steers reach the model in the order the session's log stored them: a steer sent from this process behind one another process stored waits until the worker has read that one.
- A steer, cancel or prompt sent from this process while the worker is still writing one of its own records waits for that record to land, at most one poll interval, so the steer is still handed to the running turn.
- A steer sent from this process while the model streams a reply cuts the reply short at once, instead of after the worker's next read.
- A cancel sent from this process reaches the running turn as soon as it is stored.

The wait for a record still landing adds this much, measured on `local()` with 200 log events, each call made the moment a tool starts (while the worker writes its records), 30 calls per run, median of three runs taken in turns with the same change without the wait:

| Call | Without the wait, p50 / p90 | With it, p50 / p90 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `steer()` | 6.5 / 11.9 ms | 11.1 / 17.5 ms |
| `cancel()` | 10.3 / 16.0 ms | 13.0 / 19.4 ms |
| `prompt()`, until accepted | 61.0 / 79.3 ms | 72.1 / 85.9 ms |

Not in this change, as a follow-up: on `local()`, a turn takes over 60 s to reach its first tool call at 20,000 log events, because the worker reads the whole log after each append and every 250 ms.

Fixes #1342

title: Drop zero-width marks that would take a cell past 64 bytes
body:
## Summary

- fx no longer exits with `fx: out of memory` when typed, pasted, or model-written text puts more combining marks, zero-width joiners, variation selectors, or tag characters on one character than a cell can hold.
- A cell that fx builds holds at most 64 bytes of text, its base character plus its marks, which is the limit the hosted terminal `screen` snapshot already enforces. A cell restored from a checkpoint that an older fx saved can hold more, and keeps the marks it has. A base `e` keeps 31 U+0301 marks, or 21 U+200B characters.
- Marks past the limit are dropped whole and the earlier marks stay, so the cell is the same however the bytes are split across reads. The cell's width and the cursor position do not change.
- A feed that drops marks writes one trace line to the debug log with the number of dropped units and bytes.
- `fx replay` plays a tape that holds a long run of marks on one cell, or enough different marks on enough characters to fill the whole combining pool (65,535 suffixes or 4 MiB), without failing with `combining pool capacity exceeded`. A mark that needs a suffix the full pool has no entry for is dropped and counted like a mark past the cell limit, so the cell keeps its base and earlier marks and the cursor does not move; a selector it drops still leaves its character the width the whole sequence gives. A suffix the pool already holds is still kept, and the trace line for the feed names the pool as the reason. Only a terminal reset (ESC c) frees the pool, not a clear or a scroll.
- A hosted terminal whose output fills the pool no longer reports its screen as corrupt.

title: Show libfx UI lines in order on local()
body:
## Summary

- A viewer following a libfx session on `local()` sees each turn's lines in the order they happened, even when one write to the data folder is slow. A line that landed late used to show after the lines behind it, so a streamed reply could read out of order.
- If the writer is killed in the middle of a turn, the lines saved on `local()` are the start of the turn, with none missing from the middle.
- `local()` writes each batch of lines one chunk at a time, which costs more on the bundled world-local 5.1.1: a batch of 40 chunks takes about 10 ms instead of 3.7 ms.
- Other Worlds, the Vercel World included, still take a batch in one `writeMulti` call.
- An app that passes its own world-local older than 5.2.0 to `world()` keeps the race and should upgrade. world-local 5.2.0 and later land a call's chunks in order.

Fixes #1583

title: Show the steers a resumed libfx turn places
body:
## Summary

- A libfx turn that resumes after a deadline hand-off or a crash now shows each steer it places as a `user_message` event, once, after the progress that places it is written. Before, the model got the steer and no event reached the stream.
- A durable session reads its UI stream once after `turn_resume`, only when the turn holds unplaced steers, and drops a line the stream already shows. A steer that a boundary showed before a crash lost the progress that placed it is not shown twice.
- A plain engine cannot tell what its host received, so its host can see the same `user_message` twice with the same `id`. `sdk/README.md` and the types say so.
- A resume that ends before its first request shows nothing for the steers it never placed.

A crash between the progress that places a resumed steer and its line loses the line, and nothing shows it later.

The stream read costs time on a long stream. A resume that holds one steer, on `local()`, median of 5 runs:

| Stream events | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | 85 ms | 62 ms |
| 20,000 | 6.5 s | 7.9 s |

A resume with no steer held reads nothing: 5.2 s before and 5.1 s after at 20,000 events.

Twenty rounds of the resume with a concurrent stream writer on `local()` (10 SIGKILL, 10 deadline hand-offs, noise lines plus one late line from the replaced worker at a random moment): 0 steers missed, 0 shown twice.

Builds on #1696 by @shadowcodex.

title: Bug: model picker stays on unable to load models during catalog retry
body:
### Issue details

The model picker stays on `unable to load models` for a whole catalog retry, including while the refetch is in flight. A new process can list the same Grok catalog successfully.

#### Environment

- fx 0.0.16 (`481104fdbc24`), Linux, stable channel
- Provider: Grok subscription
- Saved model: `grok-4.7`

#### What happens

In the interactive session, `/model` and the model query show `unable to load models` repeatedly. Checked from the same machine and account on 2026-11-07:

- `fx doctor`: 8 ok, 0 failed
- `fx models`: `grok-4.7`, `grok-4.7-build-fast`, `grok-4.6`, `grok-4.5`
- `fx status`: Grok subscription, `auth_refreshable=true`

`cli-chat-proxy.grok.com`, `x.ai`, and `api.x.ai` resolve to IPv6 only. An unauthenticated request to `https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/models` returns 401. `https://x.ai/cli/stable` returns `1.0.77`. A transport failure on that path is one way to enter the failed state. After that, the picker keeps the failure text through the backoff.

#### Expected

While a refetch is in flight, show `loading models...`. When the catalog is down, name the failure and that fx will retry. A Grok failure should name the model provider, not AI Gateway. After a retry succeeds, the picker should list the same models `fx models` returns in a new process.

#### Why the picker stays failed

On v0.0.16:

- `src/ui/footer/picker_presentation.zig` shows `unable to load models` when the model stage is failed and not loading.
- `src/core/app/app_render_runtime.zig` sets `model_completions_loading` from `isModelCacheLoading()` and `model_completions_failed` from `isModelCacheFailed()`.
- `isModelCacheLoading()` is true only when `state == .loading`, or while a startup credential is still pending. `isModelCacheFailed()` is true when `state == .failed`.
- `beginLoad` in `src/core/app/model_cache_runtime.zig` moves `state` to `.loading` only when the previous state is `.idle`. A retry from `.failed` sets `fetch_in_flight` and leaves `state` as `.failed`, so the query keeps the failure label for the whole request.
- A failed fetch backs off from 5 seconds, doubling up to 5 minutes. Until that backoff ends, `beginLoad` does not start another fetch.
- The full model menu does consult `fetch_in_flight` and can show `Loading models…` during a retry. A non-retryable failure still falls through to `Unable to load models.` Retryable transport and gateway failures say `Could not reach AI Gateway; fx retries automatically.` even for Grok. `model_catalog.serviceName` already returns `the model provider` for a non-Gateway provider, and this text does not use it.

`unable to load models` is still the model-stage failure label in `picker_presentation.zig` on main (`eab1401ca1`).

This is not #1148. That report was the Grok modality parse failure fixed in v0.0.13. This session is on v0.0.16, and `fx models` returns a catalog. #1671 names a connection failure for withheld images and fast mode. It does not change this picker label.

### Trace

No `/trace` output. The interactive picker did not record a catalog category, and a fresh `fx models` succeeded.

### Sensitive information

- [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

title: Free each tool call's scratch when the call ends
body:
## Summary

- A tool call's working memory is freed when the call ends. A long agent turn keeps only the result each call sends back to the model, so reading, searching, MCP, and subagent calls no longer add their scratch to the turn for every step.
- Memory in a long turn no longer grows with the size of the files it reads.
- Shell and vision calls keep the memory behavior they had: the turn adopts their completion and its output capture.
- `fx ask` still prints the `McpInputRequired` error code after a turn that ends on an MCP input request.
- On hosts without threads, where calls run one at a time, each call also gets its own memory, and a failed call's error text is no longer freed before it is copied.

Peak RSS on the long-turn memory fixture (`benchmarks/long_turn_memory.py`, sampled with `ps` on macOS arm64, ReleaseSafe):

| Turn | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 300 steps, 1 KiB reads | 35.2 MiB | 31.1 MiB |
| 300 steps, 128 KiB reads | 84.3 MiB | 35.7 MiB |
| 1000 steps, 1 KiB reads | 96.8 MiB | 77.1 MiB |
| 1000 steps, 128 KiB reads | 242.6 MiB | 85.2 MiB |
| 1000 steps, 1 MiB reads | 1117.5 MiB | 85.2 MiB |

On Linux x86_64, the long-turn memory job in `bench.yml` (500 steps of 1 KiB reads) completed on this branch at a 35.6 MiB peak.

Memory still grows by about 70 KiB per step at small reads. That growth does not depend on what the tools read, and this change leaves it as it was.

Builds on #484 by @iamken1204.

Fixes #483

title: Let main keep steering its subagents after 64 messages
body:
## Summary

- Main can keep sending messages into its subagents' running turns for the whole session. A subagent refuses a message only while it already holds 64 that it hasn't read.
- A subagent with 64 unread messages no longer blocks messages to the other subagents.
- A refused message now tells main which subagent is full and when to send again, instead of returning only `feedback_capacity`.
- fx no longer keeps a closed subagent's message records for the rest of the session, and a subagent's new work no longer carries the last work's records.

title: Keep rows in scrollback when a prompt is submitted during a resume
body:
## Summary

- Keep every resumed row in scrollback, in order and once, when a prompt is submitted while a resume is still publishing. Before, the first frame after the handoff painted the new turn over rows that never reached scrollback, so a few rows just above the turn were missing.
- Print a turn that is taller than the transcript area in full, in order, with its separator row, below the last resumed row.
- Leave resize and Ctrl+O at the handoff as they were: neither produced a missing row, and the new handoff state is dropped on a resize, a reset, or the full transcript.

Found while checking #353.

title: Move fx acp and the SDK to the sh.fx names
body:
## Summary

- `initialize` lists fx's extensions in `agentCapabilities._meta` and reads the client's list from `clientCapabilities._meta`. fx sends an extension's notifications and `_meta` keys only when both sides list it, so a plain ACP client gets only ACP v1 messages.
- The `libfx/*` methods become `_sh.fx/*`, the `_meta.fx` keys become `sh.fx/` keys, and `clientCapabilities.libfx` becomes the `sh.fx/hostTools` capability. The SDK moves in the same change and sends its instructions as ACP's `systemPrompt` in append mode on `_sh.fx/session/new`.
- `session/remove` becomes ACP's `session/delete` in the wasm build and returns `{}`.
- A steer through `session/prompt` uses `sh.fx/delivery`. Until queued prompts land, fx lists only `steer`, refuses `queue` with `-32602`, and fails a steer still waiting when the client stops the turn with `-32800`.
- Error text and the model capability codes no longer name libfx (`MODEL_UNSUPPORTED_*`). The SDK keeps its public `LIBFX_MODEL_UNSUPPORTED_*` codes.
- The spec gains sections for the journal, hooks, host tools and the three detail keys, and its tables of old names no longer promise a transition. The prompt delivery model's Today configs follow the new answer to a stop (`StopKeepsSteers`), and the plain ACP client test is strict.
- Requests fx refuses during a turn, checked against the CLI: checkpoint, restore, snapshot and the journal methods need an idle session, as the spec says; `session/list` gets its own fix; `set_config_option` stays refused because its handler frees the model name the running turn reads; `session/delete` and `mcp/message` are unchanged.
- fx never changes a mode or option on its own outside a client's request: a model switch that turns off an unsupported speed answers with the full option list.
- The TLA+ ACP job builds the native addon for the session target driver's kernel plans.

Stacked on #1758. It also carries #1708, merged into this branch, until #1708 lands on main. The docs change is vercel-labs/fx-web#262.

title: Stop fx from crashing when a subagent finishes during a compaction
body:
## Summary

- fx no longer crashes with "start index N is larger than end index 0" when it compacts main's conversation in the middle of a turn while a subagent finishes.
- Compaction records that the compactor keeps during that race are no longer dropped from main's saved session.

title: Show model catalog retries in the inline picker
body:
When a failed catalog retries, the inline `/model` picker now shows `loading models...`. It shows the failure during backoff and lists models when the retry succeeds. A refresh can still keep the previously loaded catalog visible.

I built `./zig-out/bin/fx` with Zig 0.17.0 and ran a tmux regression against a local fake gateway. The first catalog request returns 503, and the test holds the second request open. The baseline keeps displaying the failure while that request is in flight. The fix shows loading, then displays the recovered model. The neighboring model picker cases passed.

The Linux Zig unit runs had the same 11 failures and four crashes by test name on the base and patched source. The local slash-menu file run passed 30 cases, with 11 failures outside the model picker cases. The draft is waiting on CI.

Refs #1766

title: Test that a login file that keeps changing is given up
body:
## Summary

`session_presence.openCurrent` opens a login file again when another fx replaced or deleted it after it was opened, and gives up after its last open with `LoginFileKeptChanging`. The tests covered a file replaced once and a file deleted, but not that bound.

- The new test saves a new login over the file after every open and checks that the helper returns `LoginFileKeptChanging` after `max_opens` opens.
- Only test code changes.

## Testing

- The login-file tests in `src/core/auth/session_presence.zig`, run on their own: all pass.
- The new test fails when the helper returns none instead of the error (`expected error.LoginFileKeptChanging`), and when it stops one open early (`expected 3, found 2`).

title: Tell a toolbox run its MCP tool is no longer available
body:
## Summary

- A toolbox run of an MCP tool that the server removed after the run was admitted now gets `<name> is no longer available. Use toolbox search to find current tools.` in place of `Unsupported tool: <name>`. The model's name is written as visible text.
- A direct call of the same tool keeps `Unsupported tool: <name>`.
- `refreshChangedMcpTool` takes the `ToolCall` and reads its `name` and `carried_by`, not a bare flag. Behavior is unchanged.
- The tool placement fuzz test names its separator list and indexes it by `.len`. Behavior is unchanged.

The removed-tool answer comes from `tool_mcp_registry.zig`, where the host's empty reply becomes the result, so the dispatch context now carries `carried_by` to it. The `.unsupported` arm in `resolveToolDispatchPrelude` uses the same helper.

Stacked on #1658. This branch has #1658's current head merged in.

Checked on the merged head with the full `zig build test`, the `tool_placement_parse` fuzz replay, `mcp-http.test.ts` (the frozen old tool test now asserts the new text) and `toolbox.test.ts`.

title: Score rejected calls and cache tokens in the tool schema A/B harness
body:
## Summary

- The harness counts tool calls fx rejected apart from shell commands that started and then failed (a nonzero exit, a timeout, a stop, or a lost process), per run and in the summary table.
- Each run records the prompt-cache tokens the provider read and wrote, and the summary shows the mean of each.
- Five new tasks: an edit whose `old_string` is one stale line, one whose block is stale, one whose `old_string` is not unique, a long multi-file refactor, and a long repository audit.
- A variant can name a `transform` module that rewrites the request and the streamed events, to try a tool shape before fx implements it. A transform that throws fails its run with the error.
- `run --resume` reuses the result files a stopped run already wrote.

title: Escape tool names in fx mcp call error messages
body:
## Summary

- `fx mcp call` and `fx mcp call help` show a tool name that holds control bytes or escape sequences as visible escapes, such as `\x1b]0;x\x07`, in their error messages. Before, the raw bytes went into the command's output, which the shell tool returns to the model. For a name that holds ESC ] 0 ; t BEL, the message now reads `fx mcp call: mcp_x\x1b]0;t\x07 did not run. No MCP tool named mcp_x\x1b]0;t\x07 is available to this agent.` where it used to carry those bytes as they were.
- A name that is plain text prints the same as before.

Covered by unit tests in the client, the bridge, and the tool runtime, and by an E2E test in `mcp-stdio.test.ts` that runs the built binary with a name that holds an ESC and a BEL.

title: Stop background requests from waiting out a stuck DNS lookup
body:
## Summary

- When DNS hangs, quitting the TUI after `/usage` or `/credits` now exits at once. Before, quit waited until the stuck lookup gave up.
- Ctrl-C now ends `fx ask` at once while a model catalog request or a Codex or Grok version lookup hangs, and `fx acp` now exits at once when its client closes. Before, each waited out the lookup.
- A Grok version lookup now stops at its 3 s limit while DNS hangs, and catalog, usage, credits, and sign-in requests stop at their own limits. Before, they ran until the lookup gave up.
- These requests now open their connection the way turn requests do: on a connection job that the request leaves on Ctrl-C, quit, or its time limit. The job closes any connection it opens after the request left.

title: Return errors instead of panicking when terminal attributes fail
body:
## Summary

- Restoring the terminal after its window closes no longer panics with "reached unreachable code" when the terminal descriptor is closed or revoked. fx finishes exiting.
- Resuming fx after Ctrl+Z on a terminal that is gone ends fx with an error instead of a panic.
- The team picker falls back to line selection, and the API key prompt reports an error, when the terminal descriptor is closed, instead of panicking.

Ctrl+Z resume on a terminal that is gone, before: `thread ... panic: reached unreachable code`, exit 134.
Ctrl+Z resume on a terminal that is gone, now: `fx: not a terminal`, exit 1.

Linear: [FXC-292](https://linear.app/vercel/issue/FXC-292)

title: Link the control's C objects into macOS PGSO builds
body:
## Summary

- The macOS PGSO links now add the objects and archives that the ReleaseSafe control linked beside Zig's own object, such as C the build compiles. That covers the instrumented link, the `zig cc` candidate link, and the temporal candidate link, and the two `zig cc -###` probes that find the compiler runtime before the instrumented and temporal links, since Zig resolves symbols even in a dry run. Before, they linked only Zig's object, the compiler runtime, and libSystem.
- The macOS control build passes `--verbose-link`. `record_control_build` reads Zig's final `zig ld` line, copies each extra input under `control/link-inputs/`, and records its hash in `logs/control-link.json`. Each link checks the hashes before it runs.
- The seed upload carries `control/link-inputs/`. The candidate job links on another runner, so it copies the record and the objects from the seed.
- A control link that names a library other than libSystem fails, because these links would drop it.
- Linux is unchanged. It already relinks from Zig's own recorded link, which names the C objects.

Stacked on #1637. #1638 is stacked on this PR.

## Why

#1638 is the first PR that links the JavaScript engine into fx. Without this change, the macOS PGSO seed build of #1638 and the PRs above it fails at the instrumented link with `undefined symbol: _JS_NewRuntime2` and every other `JS_*` symbol, as in [run 42269121645](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/actions/runs/42269121645). The stable release runs this pipeline.

At this PR's own head, fx links no C, so the record has no inputs and every link command is the same as before.

## Testing

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/pgso/tests` passes at this PR's head, 317 tests. Each PGSO workflow runs it.
- New tests check that the macOS record reads the link Zig prints under its build step, copies and hashes its inputs, refuses an input that changed and a link that names another library, and that the three link commands and both `zig cc -###` probes add the inputs right after the object they rebuild. Another test links the seed's copies in a candidate run after the seed's build cache is gone.
- `test_candidate_object_and_signing_contract` now records a control link without C before it links the candidate, as a real run does.
- `zig build` passes at this PR's head.
- The macOS PGSO workflow at #1639's head `5d77d143a`, the top of the stack, passes its seed stage: the control, bitcode, and instrumented builds ([run 44791561181](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/actions/runs/44791561181)). The seed's control record lists the four QuickJS objects, and its instrumented binary has the engine's 106 `JS_` functions, counted with `nm -U instrumented/fx | grep -c ' T _JS_'` on that run's seed artifact. Without this PR, the seed stage fails at the instrumented link, as in run 42269121645 above.
- On this PR's own head, the macOS PGSO candidate is 6.585 MiB and fails only the workflow's 0.250 MiB adoption-headroom check below the 6.750 MiB ceiling ([run 44783981150](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/actions/runs/44783981150)). fx links no C at this head, so the size is main's: the same check passed at 6.412 MiB before this stack was rebased onto main ([run 44008280433](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/actions/runs/44008280433)).
- The PGSO workflows run on this PR, since it changes `scripts/pgso`, and on #1639 with the whole stack.

title: Send cache points to Amazon Nova models
body:
## Summary

- Amazon Nova Micro, Lite, Pro, and Nova 2 Lite now read their stable instructions from the prompt cache. Before, every request through fx reported 0 cached tokens, because Nova caches only behind an explicit Bedrock cache point and the Gateway's automatic caching adds none.
- fx marks the stable system instructions with a Bedrock cache point for those four models only. Every other model sends the same markers as before.
- A Nova cache write bills at the plain input price and a cache read at a quarter of it, so a one-shot request costs no more than before.
- In repeated live fx runs, later requests to Nova Pro read roughly 8,600 of about 10,650 input tokens from the cache. The same build without the change read none.

title: Keep the continuation prompt in the saved turn
body:
## Summary

- When a turn stops without a final answer and fx asks the model to continue, the saved turn keeps that prompt where fx sent it. The next turn's request now starts with every message the last one carried, so the provider's prompt cache still covers it. Before, the request changed at that message and the rest of the conversation was read as new input.
- This covers the three prompts fx sends to get a turn going again: "Summarize what you just did." after silent tool steps, the request to continue after an empty reply, and "Continue from the preceding tool result." after a model refuses a request that ends on a tool result. A resumed session, `fx ask --resume`, and a second ACP prompt send the same messages the live turn did.
- A turn the user cancels keeps the prompt too, as it keeps the steering the user typed.
- fx's own prompt is not shown as something the user typed. The transcript, Ctrl+O and ACP `session/load` skip it, and compaction treats it as ordinary text.
- A Stop hook's continuation message and a tool's notice to the model stay out of the saved turn, as before.

The prompt is saved as a steering entry inside a marker (`src/core/shared/recovery_prompt.zig`) instead of a new saved field. Steering already carries a step boundary through the session log, resume, compaction cuts and replay, so the session format does not change and sessions saved before this change read as they did. A new field would have needed a schema version, a session event and its own compaction cut rule for one rare case.

title: Keep a message sent right after a subagent stop
body:
## Summary

- A message main sends to a subagent right after stopping it waits and starts the subagent's next turn, instead of failing with `child_cancelled`.
- A stop and a message to the same subagent in one step run in the order main wrote them, so the message is no longer lost. Calls to different subagents still run together.
- A stop or close that ends a turn with messages the turn hadn't read counts them in its answer, once, so main hears about every dropped message.
- A message sent while the user's own stop ends a subagent's turn waits for its next turn instead of joining the turn that ends.
- A message to a subagent that is being closed is refused with `child_closing`.

title: Send an image folder's rules as a note, not in the instructions
body:
## Summary

- An image attached from a folder with its own `AGENTS.md` no longer changes the instructions, so the provider's cached prompt still matches up to the turn that attaches it.
- That folder's rules arrive once, in a note after the text of the turn that attached the image, the way rules reach a tool call.
- A later image from the same folder gets the short reminder line instead of a second copy of the rules.
- A resumed session counts those rules as delivered, so it does not send them again unless the file changed.
- This applies to images added in the TUI and with `fx ask --image`. ACP and libfx hosts are unchanged.

title: Test a script larger than any pipe buffer in the command runner
body:
## Summary

- Adds a unit test that runs a script larger than 256 KiB through the captured-command path.
- Makes a regression of the large-script fix fail on any Mac. `main` already fixed that hang in a13c6e573, but the existing long-script test is 24 KiB, which an idle macOS pipe (64 KiB) holds whole, so it can miss a regression.
- Only macOS starts the shell suspended, so on Linux the test checks that a large script runs and cannot catch that regression.
- With the script write forced back inline, the new test times out on macOS. On `main` it passes.
- Moves the filler line of the existing 24 KiB test into a constant that both tests use. The script that test runs is unchanged.
- Changes no product code.

title: Run the subagent and session-write models in CI
body:
## Summary

- CI runs the subagent steering and stop-then-message TLA+ models and the session-write model, and drives the built fx along them, on `main` and on pull requests that change the subagent or session-write code, these models, their drivers, or the helpers the drivers load.
- `Build & Test` fails when that job fails.
- The planted bugs and the configs of fx's old defects still run only by hand, with both `check.sh` scripts and no arguments.

title: Queue prompts and run untaken steers as the next turn in fx acp
body:
## Summary

- `fx acp` lists `queue` in `sh.fx/promptDelivery`. A `session/prompt` sent with `"sh.fx/delivery": "queue"` during a turn runs as a turn of its own after it, in the order fx received it, and gets its own response.
- A steer the turn never takes, because the client stopped the turn or the turn had stopped taking input, runs in the next turn instead of failing. Steers waiting together run as one turn, before any queued prompt, and each answer carries `"sh.fx/steeringDelivery": "next_turn"`.
- Steers that start a turn this way show as `user_message_chunk` updates with `sh.fx/steerInput`.
- A steer that arrives while the model streams a reply cuts the reply short and the turn continues with it, as in the CLI. During a tool call it still waits.
- `session/cancel` stops only the running turn. Waiting steers and queued prompts still run after it.
- `$/cancel_request` with the id of a steer or queued prompt that hasn't run answers it with `-32800`.
- `session/close`, and `session/new`, `session/load` or `session/resume` during a turn, answer every steer and queued prompt that hasn't run with `-32800`.
- A prompt past 64 queued prompts fails with `-32600` "Prompt queue is full".

Stacked on #1770.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#326

title: Rerun stored harness runs whose arm changed
body:
## Summary

- `run --resume` reuses a stored run only when the arm's binary, variant, and transform source are the same as when it ran; any other stored run runs again. The key covers the transform module's own file, not the modules it imports.
- When `run --resume` drops a stored run, because its arm key differs or its file cannot be read, it prints one line that names the file and why.
- `tokens` and `probe` refuse a variant that names a transform, instead of measuring it as if it had none.
- `rescore` keeps a run whose transform failed marked as failed, and tests cover it and the proxy's 501 answers to a failed transform.

title: Skip the failed-edit hint on files past 100,000 lines
body:
## Summary

- A failed `edit_file` on a file of more than 100,000 lines returns the plain recovery advice without the closest lines, so it no longer compares every file line with `old_string` and holds a list of every line start.

Before and after, ReleaseSafe builds of main `165f70959` and this branch, one failed edit through the e2e fake gateway:

| File | main | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1.7M identical lines, 256-line `old_string` | 2.00 s, 44 MiB, hint | 0.45 s, 22 MiB, plain |
| 16M empty lines, 2-line `old_string` | 0.41 s, 346 MiB, plain | 0.09 s, 24 MiB, plain |
| 100,000 lines | hint | hint |
| 100,001 lines | hint | plain |

title: End shortened skill descriptions at a whole word
body:
## Summary

- The skill catalog ends a description longer than 200 characters after the last whole word that fits, followed by `...`, instead of cutting it mid-word; the entry still holds at most 200 characters.

Before: `... improve a frontend interface. Covers we`
After: `... improve a frontend interface. Covers...`

Skill choice, one model step on a captured catalog of 229 skills, 22 prompts x 3 trials per arm, on nine models from seven providers: 537 of 594 right against 526 of 594 on main. Per model the count fell by at most 1 and rose by up to 4. One model picked a wrong skill 4 times against once on main; 5 more trials per arm gave 2 against 4, so over 8 trials both arms have 6 wrong or over-triggering picks.

The captured catalog is 58,490 bytes against 59,218 on main, with 164 of 229 descriptions marked. A description whose last whole word ends a sentence ends in `....`, as 5 of them do. A catalog over its budget and a configured `skill_description_bytes` still cut descriptions without `...`, as on main.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#265

title: Bug: an expired fx login and stalled DNS hold fx ask and fx acp startup for 15 s
body:
## What happens

When the fx login in `~/.fx/auth.json` has expired and DNS lookups stall, fx refreshes the login before its first request and waits for the refresh until the OAuth request limit of 15 s (`default_request_timeout_ms` in `src/core/auth/oauth_transport.zig`) runs out.

- `fx ask` doesn't stop on Ctrl-C during that wait. With Ctrl-C sent 2 s after start, it exited 13.6 s later with status 130. With an `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` and the same stalled lookups, Ctrl-C ends it in 0.6 s.
- `fx acp` answers `initialize` after 15.3 s, and the client can't cancel it.

#1777 made the other background requests (usage, credits, the model catalogs, and a sign-in refresh that gets stopped) leave a stuck lookup at once. At startup nothing stops this refresh, so it still waits out the full limit.

## Steps to reproduce

On macOS, with a local build at `zig-out/bin/fx`:

1. Make DNS lookups stall. Build a small library that interposes `getaddrinfo`, sleeps 20 s for every name except loopback names and IP literals (resuming the sleep on `EINTR`, as a lookup on a dropped network does), and then fails. Load it into fx with `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` through a small launcher binary, because SIP strips that variable when fx starts through `/bin/sh`.
2. Use a fresh `HOME` whose `~/.fx/auth.json` holds an fx login with a `refresh_token` and an `expires_at_ms` in the past. Leave `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` unset.
3. Run `fx ask "Say hello."` and press Ctrl-C after 2 s. fx exits about 13.6 s later.
4. Run `fx acp` and send `initialize`. The response arrives about 15.3 s later.

Measured on main at 547d40d3d.

## Expected

- `fx ask` stops within about a second of Ctrl-C, as it does with an API key.
- `fx acp` doesn't hold `initialize` for the full refresh limit.

## Notes

Two ways to fix it:

- Pass Ctrl-C into the startup refresh in `fx ask`. This changes how `fx ask` starts up, but not what a working sign-in does.
- Give the startup refresh a shorter limit in `fx ask` and `fx acp`. That also covers ACP, but a slow sign-in that would have worked could fail.

Related work on request recovery and stuck connections, all merged:

- #1617, #1632: retries for server errors and unreadable replies, Retry-After handling, resume after a crash or closed window
- #1662, #1670: `fx ask` and `fx acp` show Offline within about 2 s on a dead network
- #1664, #1667, #1683: errors in plain words, including failed output writes
- #1665: Esc ends a turn at once on every connection path
- #1663: Ctrl-C no longer waits for the session title request
- #1668: closing the window during a request resumes it on reopen
- #1666, #1387: test fixes for the SIGKILL cleanup test and the status JSON test
- #1681, #1682: no wait for a stuck session title, and `fx acp` catalog refreshes wait only while connected
- #1688, #1692: `fx ask` reports a closed stdout, and ends quietly when its output pipe closes
- #1777: background requests stop waiting out a stuck DNS lookup

title: Say why fx mcp call did not run a held call
body:
## Summary

- When auto mode holds a call that a command makes through `fx mcp call`, the command now prints why, with the same message a direct tool call gets. A call too large for the safety review to see in full now says so and tells the agent to make it smaller, instead of only saying permission was not granted.
- When the safety review holds the call, the message includes the reviewer's advice.

title: Read the whole shell snapshot replay in bash 3.2
body:
## Summary

- With macOS's `/bin/bash` 3.2 as the login shell, a shell snapshot larger than about 64 KB, such as one with thousands of functions, now restores in full instead of sending every command through full startup.
- A command with a quoting error under bash 3.2 still gets the hint that the shell could not parse it.

title: Read saved MCP logins again when the first read fails
body:
## Summary

When the Keychain didn't answer fx's first read of the saved MCP logins within its 10 s budget, fx started every HTTP server without its login. The server answered 401, and `fx mcp show` said `needs login`, with `fx mcp login NAME` as the next step, though the login was saved.

- A server that asks for a login now reads the store again first, and connects with the saved login when that read works. `fx mcp show` then reports the server as ready.
- While the store still can't be read, the server shows as `failed` with the reason, and the model gets the same reason. For example: `the Keychain item FX_MCP_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS_V3 couldn't be read: the Keychain refused it or didn't answer`. Asking for a sign-in doesn't help then, because it couldn't be saved there either.
- A store that a newer fx saved gets the same treatment: `~/.fx/mcp-credentials/credentials-v3.json couldn't be read: a newer fx saved it, or it's damaged`.
- A server that a reload adds, for example with `/mcp add`, reads its saved login the same way, so a store that can't be read then shows it as failed too, not as `needs login`.

## Testing

- Three new e2e tests in `tests/e2e/mcp-auth.test.ts`. One pauses the first Keychain read past its budget and checks that `fx mcp show` ends ready. One uses a store a newer fx saved and checks the `failed` status and its error, in text and JSON. Both fail on `main` with `status needs login` and `next fx mcp login fixture`, and pass here. The third makes the store unreadable while the shell runs, adds a server with `/mcp add --no-login`, and checks the status line says `web failed · /mcp`; before the reload fix it said `web needs login · /mcp`.
- All of `mcp-auth.test.ts` passes: 67 of 67. The MCP host TLA+ drivers pass: 47 of 47.
- Against Plain's MCP server, with the first Keychain read paused for 13 s, `fx mcp show plain` ends `ready, 393 tools` after 12 s. Before, it said `needs login`.

title: Say when an MCP logout didn't revoke the login
body:
## Summary

`fx mcp logout` and `/mcp logout` said `Signed out of NAME.` whether or not the server revoked the login. When its authorization server lists no revocation endpoint, no revocation goes out, and the tokens keep working there until they expire. When a revocation goes out but the server refuses it, or doesn't answer within the 2 s fx waits, they may keep working too.

- A logout that sends no revocation now says `Signed out of NAME here, but the login wasn't revoked at its server, so its tokens stay valid until they expire.`
- A logout whose revocation isn't answered with a 2xx, as RFC 7009 gives for a revoked token, now says `Signed out of NAME here, but its server didn't confirm the revocation, so its tokens may stay valid until they expire.` The MCP engine's auth client keeps the status its revocation was answered with, so the host can tell.
- A logout whose revocation the server confirms still says `Signed out of NAME.`

## Testing

- Three new e2e tests in `tests/e2e/mcp-auth.test.ts`: a login without a revocation endpoint, a revocation answered 503, and one answered after 4 s. Each checks its message, the revocations the server got, and that the server is signed out. All three fail on `main`, which prints `Signed out of fixture.`, and pass here. The existing logout test, whose server answers 200, still sees `Signed out of fixture.`
- The credentials and mixed-builds TLA+ drivers save logins without a revocation endpoint, so they now expect the new message. Both pass, 5 of 5, with each trace accepted.
- The unit tests of `src/mcp/engine.zig`, `src/mcp/server.zig`, and `src/mcp/auth/client.zig` pass: 243 of 243.
- Against Plain's MCP server, which lists no revocation endpoint, `fx mcp logout plain` prints the first new message and exits 0.

title: Lay out the agent list in columns
body:
## Summary

- The agent list opens with a count of the open agents, such as `Agents 3`.
- Each row shows the agent's name, title, state, profile, and model in aligned columns in place of one line joined by middle dots.
- Each fx comes first in the order it started, with its subagents under it on a `├` and `└` branch. Its working subagents come first, then the rest by newest reply. An fx no longer moves below agents that are working.
- The only fx open is named `main`. While several are open, each is named by its number, such as `fx 2`.
- A title too long for its column ends in `…`. A narrow terminal leaves out the profile, then the model, so the name, title, and state always fit.
- A state that waits for you, such as `needs approval`, is bright on a row that is not selected.
- The list no longer marks the agent it opened from with `(on screen)`.
- The list shows up to 10 agents under the count. A terminal too short for the count and three agents shows only the agents.

## Before and after

The list's rows at 80 columns, from its unit tests on `main` and on this branch.

```
    tester · Run the auth tests · tester · needs approval · gpt-5.4-mini

```

title: Send a message right after a subagent starts into its first turn
body:
## Summary

- A message main sends to a subagent right after starting it joins the subagent's first turn, instead of waiting for the turn after the first task.
- While that turn is still starting, main's message call waits for it to begin, for up to 10 seconds. A start that takes longer leaves the message for the subagent's next turn, as before.
- Stopping main or quitting fx while the message waits ends the wait at once.
- Closing the subagent while the message waits refuses it with `child_closing`.

title: Send earlier turns unchanged on later requests
body:
## Summary

- Continuing a session after a turn that used file tools no longer fails with HTTP 400 "Invalid signature in thinking block" on Claude Fable 5.1 and later, and the AI Gateway no longer drops that turn's final-reply reasoning.
- Earlier turns go back to the model as fx first sent them: fx no longer inserts a "Session file evidence" message before an earlier turn's final reply.

title: Rank /resume ahead of /reset in a new session
body:
Some terminals and multiplexers capture `cmd + r` before it reaches fx, so the sessions picker shortcut doesn't work for everyone, and typing `/re` in a new session offered `/reset` first even though there is no context to reset yet.

- Rank `/resume` ahead of `/reset` in the `/` menu, Tab completion, and inline completion while the session on screen has no turns, no turn running, and no prompt on its way
- Keep the current order once the session has a turn, and on a subagent's screen, which refuses `/resume`

Downside is that the order is no longer consistent which could introduce confusion. Let me know what you think is best @fazxes

title: Pick a profile from /launch and close instances with Delete
body:
## Summary

- Typing `/launch ` opens a profile selector with aligned model, effort, tool-set, and project-source columns. The list is gray and the selected row is white. Enter launches the selected profile, with the default profile first.
- Rows follow the same settings precedence as the new instance. Tool sets are labeled `all tools` or `custom`; the selector makes no read-only guarantee. Model and effort values are escaped before display.
- The selector loads once per opening, reads no prompts, and releases its snapshot when the composer leaves `/launch`. Loading is capped at 128 directory entries and 1 MiB of settings. Cell widths are bounded before padding. A limited scan shows a warning and keeps the default selectable even when it was not scanned.
- In the agent list, Delete twice closes the selected instance and its subagents. The list stays open on the replacement instance. The last open instance cannot be closed with Delete.

The security update preserves the existing rebased branch history, including dd70f1137.

## Verification

- `zig fmt --check src/`, `zig build`, and `zig build test`: passed on `a3f88c9`.
- Focused `/launch` and Delete flows: 3 pass, 0 fail.
- Isolated runtime checks for escaped terminal sequences, conservative labels, metadata reload on reopening, and the scan-limit warning: passed.
- Full run of `tui-host-instances.test.ts` and `tui-host-switch.test.ts`: 70 pass, 7 fail. Those seven cases passed when rerun alone. A second full run without the unit suite in parallel finished with 74 pass, 3 fail, exit 1.

The last full run failed in:
- `an instance with no turn stays out of the host record, and quitting from it names a saved one`
- `main can still steer a working subagent after it has read 64 earlier messages`
- `a subagent with 64 unread messages refuses one more and says why, while another working subagent still takes messages`

Failures include a process exiting before the composer appears and a subagent-message timeout. The root cause is not confirmed; there is no claim that these are unrelated to the branch. Keep this PR in draft until the failures are explained and CI passes.

## Docs

- Instances: document the `/launch ` selector, its columns, default selection, and loading limits. Changes on disk appear when the selector is reopened; explicit `/launch <name>` still validates and loads the requested profile.
- Agent list: document Delete twice for closing instances as well as subagents. The last open instance stays open; `/close` can end fx.

title: Keep subagents across session switches and let /fork copy them
body:
## Summary

- `/fork`, `/new`, `/clear`, `/reset` and `/resume` no longer freeze when a subagent of the open session is still working, also in a launched instance.
- A switch stops only the tasks the session's subagents are running, saved as cancelled. The subagents stay in that session with their history and take new work when it is opened again.
- The session a switch opens shows how many subagent tasks it stopped.
- When the session had subagents at the chosen prompt, `/fork` asks once whether to bring them into the fork: Enter or `y` copies them all, `n` or Esc forks without them.
- Each copy holds its subagent's history up to the fork point, and a task still running there ends in the copy as cancelled. A copy never starts a report turn in the fork.
- Subagents started after the chosen prompt, closed for good, or whose newest work there was lost are not offered, and the originals are never changed.
- A fork of a fork offers the first fork's copies too, also at a prompt inside the history the first fork copied, such as its first own prompt.

## Before and after

Before, with a subagent still working, `/fork` froze on the fork menu after Enter, and `/new`, `/clear`, `/reset` and `/resume` froze the same way. fx had to be killed.

After, the switch finishes, and the session it opens says:

```
* session: stopped 1 running subagent task; the subagent stays in the previous session
```

When the session had subagents at the chosen prompt, `/fork` first shows the prompt and asks:

```
  Bring 1 subagent into the fork?
enter yes     n or esc no
```

## Design

The freeze is a wait cycle. A switch closed the old session on the main loop, and closing its subagent host joins each hosted subagent's slot thread. A slot thread that is still running waits for the main loop to end its run, so the two wait for each other. `/close` and quit never froze, because they stop the subagents first.

A switch now does the same: it stops the session's subagents (`stopSubagentsForSwitch`, the same `stopSet` and `dropSet` steps `/close` uses), then closes the session. A timeout on the join would still leave a run writing into a closed session, and detaching the threads would leak them, so the order of the steps is the fix. `Wiring.tla` models the switch, and `SwitchEnds` checks that every switch finishes.

Before:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Loop as Main loop
    participant Host as Subagent host
    participant Slot as Slot thread
    Loop->>Host: close the old session
    Host->>Slot: join
    Slot->>Loop: wait for the loop to end the run
    Note over Loop,Slot: each waits for the other
```

After:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Loop as Main loop
    participant Host as Subagent host
    participant Slot as Slot thread
    Loop->>Slot: stop the running task
    Slot-->>Host: run ends as cancelled
    Loop->>Host: close the old session
    Host->>Slot: join, which returns
    Loop->>Loop: open the next session and show the stop notice
```

A fork copies the subagents' logs rather than sharing them. A child session has one parent and one writer, so a child shared by the source and the fork would get two parents writing to one log. A copy leaves the original unchanged, and the two can go separate ways. The manager makes each copy (`openForkWithChildren`), cut at the fork point's time, and registers it in the fork's first batch, before the fork is published. A fork therefore has all its copies or none, which `ForkChildren.tla` checks. D97 in `tests/tla/session_manager/system-design.md` records the decision.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["/fork, Enter on a prompt"] --> B{"subagents at that prompt?"}
    B -- no --> F["fork"]
    B -- yes --> Q["Bring N subagents into the fork?"]
    Q -- "n or Esc" --> F
    Q -- "Enter or y" --> C["copy each log up to the fork point"]
    C --> F
    F --> S["switch: stop the source's running tasks, close it, open the fork"]
```

## Tests

- E2E (`tests/e2e/sessions.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/tui-host-instances.test.ts`): each switch with a working subagent, also in a launched instance and with a subagent waiting on a shell command; the subagent kept in the source with its history; the question answered with Enter, `n` and Esc; no question when no subagent existed at the fork point; a copy whose turn runs across the fork point; a fork of a fork at its first prompt, which asks again and copies the copy.
- Session manager: copies up to the fork point, copies offered inside a fork's copied history and copied again from there, a copy cut inside an open turn, a failed copy, a power loss at every step of a fork with a copy (hook build only), seeded property runs, and the `session_child_copy` fuzz target.
- TLA+: `Wiring.tla` gains the stop-first switch (`SwitchEnds`), and the new `ForkChildren.tla` checks that a fork has all its copies or none. The trace checkers read the copies, and `mutants.py` plants a bug in each new rule.
- The fork driver gains scenarios for a fork with a copy and for `/new` while a subagent works. Its old steering scenario failed on main, because it sends the subagent action `run`, which no longer exists. It now checks the D97 behavior instead.

## Docs

The manual changes are in vercel-labs/fx-web#274: the fork question on the sessions page, and a new "Start another conversation" section on the subagents page.

title: Add effort levels, request fields, headers, and two protocols to custom connections
body:
## Summary

- A custom model can declare its effort levels under `reasoning_efforts`, each with the request fields that select it. `/effort`, `--effort`, the footer, and the model picker offer exactly those levels.
- An effort the model does not declare is left out of the request, and fx says so once per session with the level, the model, and the setting to add it to.
- A model can add fields to every request with `request`. A field from `request` or from a level that names a field fx writes itself, such as `messages`, makes settings fail to load.
- A Chat Completions model can send its output limit as `max_completion_tokens` with `output_limit_field`.
- A connection can send extra `headers` whose values come from environment variables. fx masks those values in error text as it masks the key, and it does not let them replace the headers it sets.
- A refused setting on a custom connection names `~/.fx/settings.json`, the setting's path, and what to do, in `fx ask`, the TUI, `fx doctor`, ACP, and `fx provider`. A header whose variable is unset, empty, or unsendable names the header, its connection, and the variable before anything is sent.
- A saved session stays on the connection it started on. Resuming it after that connection's `protocol`, `base_url`, or `auth` changed, or after the connection was removed, sends nothing and says what to do, where fx said before that a credential was temporarily unavailable. The next TUI turn after such an edit in an open session does the same, where it offered a retry. Other edits, such as timeouts, headers, or effort levels, apply to the resumed session.
- With `fetch_models`, `fx models` and the model picker list the server's models from `GET {base_url}/models` next to the declared ones. When that request fails, fx shows the declared models, and `fx models` prints one line with the reason.
- `model_defaults` gives every model on the connection, including models only the server lists, the metadata fields it does not set itself.
- `timeouts` sets the connect, first-response, and stall limits of each request on the connection, in place of the built-in ones.
- `title_model` names new sessions on the connection, also on connections that need no key.
- `vision_model` turns on the image fallback for models that cannot read images. Custom connections now send structured-output requests, which the fallback needs.
- Usage records cached prompt tokens and reasoning tokens when the server reports them. `fx ask --json` shows the cached count as `cache_read_tokens`.
- A connection can speak `openai-responses` or `anthropic-messages` as well as `openai-chat-completions`, with tools, reasoning, images, and resumed sessions on each.
- On `openai-responses`, fx asks for a model's reasoning back encrypted only when the model's settings declare effort levels, so a model that does not reason works against OpenAI's API.
- libfx custom providers accept `outputLimitField`, `request`, `reasoningEfforts`, `modelDefaults`, `titleModel`, and `visionModel`. They refuse the options that need fx's own HTTP client: other protocols, headers, `fetch_models`, and timeouts.
- TLA+ models of the configured catalog, request shapes, deadlines, and resuming a session on an edited connection, with bun drivers that check fx against them, run in CI only for a manual dispatch or the `ci:tla-configured-provider` label.

## Design

Before this change a custom connection had one protocol, and its requests went through the Chat Completions codec to the shared HTTP client:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S["settings.json providers"] --> P["configured_provider.zig: one protocol"]
  P --> C["chat_completions_protocol.zig"]
  C --> H["client.zig: openBoundedPost and its watch"]
  H --> E[("POST base_url/chat/completions")]
```

After it, the connection's protocol picks one of three codecs, and a transport of its own adds what only a custom connection has:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S["settings.json providers"] --> P["configured_provider.zig: protocol, request fields, levels, headers, timeouts"]
  P --> F["request_fragment.zig"]
  P --> K{"protocol"}
  K -->|openai-chat-completions| C["chat_completions_protocol.zig"]
  K -->|openai-responses| R["configured_responses.zig over responses_protocol.zig"]
  K -->|anthropic-messages| M["anthropic_messages_protocol.zig"]
  C --> X["configured_transport.zig: headers, the protocol's path, the model list"]
  R --> X
  M --> X
  X --> H["client.zig watch with request_deadlines.zig"]
  H --> E[("POST base_url/{path}, GET base_url/models")]
```

Why each new piece exists:

- `src/gateway/configured_transport.zig`: a custom connection needs headers from the environment, its own timeouts, a path per protocol, and the server's model list. The Gateway client is built around Gateway URLs and credentials, and widening it for one kind of caller would bend a contract every provider shares, so the connection's transport sends through the same HTTP client and watch with its own settings.
- `src/gateway/configured_responses.zig`: Responses on a custom connection reuses the Gateway's Responses codec, `responses_protocol.zig`, and adds only the request fields, the effort levels, and `include` for reasoning models.
- `src/gateway/anthropic_messages_protocol.zig`: fx had no Messages codec. Messages needs alternating roles, `max_tokens` on every request, the system prompt in its own field, and thinking blocks replayed with their signatures, which none of the other codecs write.
- `src/gateway/function_tools.zig`: the Chat codec's tool helpers, moved so the Messages codec shares them instead of copying them.
- `src/gateway/request_deadlines.zig`: the connect, first-response, and stall bounds as one function of the elapsed times, which the shared watch calls and the TLA+ lab drives with its own clock. The watch's timing for every other provider is unchanged.
- `src/core/config/request_fragment.zig`: `request` and each effort level are the same thing, extra top-level request fields with fx's own fields refused, so one parser and one writer serve both.
- `GET {base_url}/models` is sent only when `fetch_models` is on, through the connection's transport and credential.
- `.github/workflows/tla-configured-provider.yml`: the TLC checks and drivers take minutes, so they run on request.

The macOS arm64 ReleaseSafe binary is about 98 KB larger, for the Messages codec and the transport.

## Before and after

A settings file that main refuses, and the same kind of mistake on this branch:

```text
# main, a model with reasoning_efforts
$ fx ask --no-save hi
fx: unknown field

# this branch, a request field fx writes
$ fx ask --no-save hi
fx: ~/.fx/settings.json: providers.local.model_metadata.local-model.request.messages: fx writes this field itself; remove it

# this branch, a header whose variable is unset
$ fx ask --no-save hi
fx: the header X-Org of connection local reads FX_PROBE_ORG, which is not set; set it, or remove the header from ~/.fx/settings.json
```

Resuming a session after its connection's protocol changed:

```text
# before
fx ask: Credential refresh is temporarily unavailable. Retry shortly.

# after
fx ask: This session's custom connection changed in ~/.fx/settings.json after the session was saved: its protocol, base_url, or auth. Change it back, or start a new session.
```

The TUI printed `fx: configured provider changed` for `fx --resume` and `Unable to resume selected session.` for `/resume`; both now show the same sentence, and a removed connection says `This session's custom connection is no longer in ~/.fx/settings.json. Add it back, or start a new session.`

An effort the model does not declare, and a model list the server could not give:

```text
[notice] Effort high is not available for local-model, so it is not sent. To offer it, add it to the model's reasoning_efforts in settings.json.
fx models: could not get the model list of local: the reply was not a model list; showing the models in settings
```

## Docs

The fx.sh page update is in https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx-web/pull/269. It covers `docs/configure-fx/custom-model-connections` (new connection and model fields, effort levels, request fields, headers, timeouts, model list, the two new protocols, and the updated compatibility notes) and adds a short entry to `docs/using-fx/troubleshooting`.

title: Show what an idle agent waits on while its subagents work
body:
**Summary**
---
- When the agent on screen ends its turn while its own subagents keep working, the row above the composer now reads `• waiting on 1 subagent (12s) · ↓ to view`. Before, the last line was the finished turn's `5s (↑822 ↓502)`, which made the session look stopped.
- The clock counts from when the agent's last turn ended and the bullet blinks in step with it, like the thinking row. The key reads `ctrl+x` when the composer has text, and narrow rows drop the hint instead of wrapping. The footer keeps its `N subagents working` note.
- While the row shows, the tick requests animation frames the same way the thinking row does. It skips them for hidden agents, open approvals or questions, and when a worker status takes the row, and it counts subagents only when a frame is due (every 50 ms), not on every loop pass.
- A unit test in `render_input.zig` covers the row, its short form, and the blink. The agent-switching E2E tests check the row, that its clock advances, that the bullet blinks, and that an agent waits only on its own subagents.

**Behavior worth a look**
---
- Only the screen agent's direct subagents with a turn running count. A subagent whose own turn ended while its subagent works does not, and one started with `report: "never"` does.
- After a stopped or failed turn, the row shows no clock, because that turn saves no end time.

title: Hold the turn clock during compaction and show how much of the summary is written
body:
## Summary

- The compaction row counts its own time from 0s for `/compact`, automatic compaction, and compaction after a provider overflow. Before, automatic and overflow compaction showed the turn's clock.
- The compaction row shows how much of the summary the model has written so far, before its time, such as `• Compacting 66% (15s)`. It reads 0% while the model reads the conversation, stays below 100% until the summary is saved, shows 100% while fx saves it, and never goes down.
- The turn clock stops while a compaction runs and continues from the time it showed when compaction started, so the compaction time is no longer added to the turn.
- The time under a finished turn, such as `12s (↑34 ↓433)`, also leaves out compaction time, as the turn clock does. That time is the saved `turn_summary.turn_duration_ms`, which the libfx session journal also exposes. `started_at_ms` and `completed_at_ms` do not change, so `completed_at_ms - started_at_ms` still gives the wall time.
- A successful compaction leaves `✓ Context compacted (2m10s)` in the transcript, with the time its row showed last. Before, a successful compaction left nothing in the transcript. The line is not saved, so a resumed session does not show it. Cancelled, failed, and empty compactions keep their feedback in the status row, as before.

## Design

- The clock rules move into `src/core/output/turn_clock.zig`, which imports only `std` and `compaction_activity.zig`. The TLA+ driver builds that file on its own and walks the real rules along the model. `activity_status.zig` now calls it.
- A running compaction holds the turn clock through the same `waiting_since_ms` freeze that approvals and questions already use. Every wait follows one rule, and a prompt that overlaps a compaction is taken off the turn once. A second clock for compaction would need its own overlap rules.
- The finished-turn time subtracts the compaction time measured around the one in-turn `compactContext` call, in the worker's `TurnSummaryAccumulator`. Moving the turn's start time instead would change the saved `started_at_ms`.
- The percentage comes from the summary as it streams in, not from time. The request already asks for one line per tool call, starting with its ID, and then the Rules, Facts, Decisions, Status and Open sections, in that order. `src/core/compactor/progress.zig` reads only the start of each line, so a chunk can end anywhere, and counts each call and section once. It reads each line with the notes reader's own rules, `ledger.lineStart`, so it counts exactly the notes and headings the reader keeps. The share is the calls and sections written over the calls in every part plus the sections.
- The count travels through the compactor's existing `Progress` interface as an optional `written_fn`, which, unlike `report_fn`, cannot stop a compaction. The worker's `compaction_activity.State.written` keeps only a higher count for the running operation, so a fallback model's reply or a follow-up request for missed turns never lowers it, and a late count for an older compaction changes nothing.
- The transcript line comes from the terminal app's settle callback in `src/core/app/app_callbacks.zig`, which every successful compaction passes once. `fx ask` and ACP do not use that callback, so their output does not change. The compaction operation now records when it settled, so the line shows the row's own clock.

## Tests

- `tests/tla/turn_clock/`: a TLA+ model of both clocks and of the row's count. `check.sh` runs TLC on it. The `*-today.cfg` configs show the old behavior breaking the new rules, and seven planted mutations must each be caught by their named rule: four of them are for the count (it falls, it reaches 100% before saving, a late count applies, a new compaction keeps the old count).
- `tests/tla/drivers/turn_clock/`: a Bun driver that walks the real `turn_clock.zig` and the real count in `compaction_activity.zig`, through a small Zig lab, along every edge of the model's graph that the code can tell apart. `--self-check` rejects six planted bugs.
- Fuzz target `turn_clock`: checks the clock laws on random event sequences. Fuzz target `compaction_progress`: feeds random replies in random chunks to the count and checks that it never panics, never falls, never reaches 100%, and gives the same count however the text is split.
- `src/core/compactor/progress.zig` tests the edge cases: a chunk that ends inside an ID or a dash, a range clipped to the part's calls, a call noted twice, no tool calls, a reply that ignores the format, two parts, a property test on random splits from a logged seed, and ten thousand calls fed one byte at a time. A race test in `worker_runtime.zig` has a reader take snapshots while a writer updates the count.
- A VT test draws the footer into the emulator grid during a compaction, at 120 and 28 columns.
- `tests/e2e/tui-compaction-activity.test.ts`: the overflow test checks both clocks, the finished-turn time, and the transcript line on screen. A new test streams part of a held summary and checks that the row's percentage rises from 0% without reaching 100%, and another closes the summary stream midway and checks that the count holds while another model finishes. A live test, run with `FX_E2E_REAL_API=1`, starts an automatic compaction in the middle of a real turn and checks that its count rises.
- The E2E tests and `sdk/node/test-term-compaction.mjs`, which checked that a successful compaction left nothing in the transcript, now check for this one line and nothing else.
- The tests in `telemetry.zig` never ran, because no test root imported the file. `agent_runtime.zig` now imports it.
- Six E2E and TLA driver waits drop `Preparing compaction` from their patterns, because that row no longer exists.

title: Say when an MCP server refuses a login
body:
Say when an MCP server refuses a login
## Summary

When an MCP server answered 401 to the token fx sent, fx still said "Signed in" after the token exchange, and later showed only "needs login" with no error. The person signed in again and again and could not tell that the server was refusing the token (the ClickState report). Now fx asks the server first, and says what the server said.

| Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `fx mcp login NAME`, `/mcp login NAME`, and the sign-in `fx mcp add` starts: the server refuses the new login | `Signed in to NAME.`, exit 0 | `Couldn't sign in to NAME: NAME refused the new login (invalid_token: "No authorization provided").` on stderr, exit 1, nothing saved |
| the same, and the server accepts it | `Signed in to NAME.` | unchanged |
| the same, and the check request gets no answer about the token (network error, 5xx, no answer in time, a 403 that isn't a step-up) | `Signed in to NAME.` | `Signed in to NAME, but fx couldn't check the login with it.`, exit 0, the login is kept |
