title: Don't crash when an HTTP answer's body fails partway
body:
## Summary

fx crashed with `panic: attempt to use null value` whenever the body of an HTTP answer failed partway: the server was still sending it when the request's time limit ended, or the connection dropped in the middle. `fetchOnOpenJob` copied `std.http.Client.fetch`'s `return response.bodyErr().?`, and `bodyErr()` is only set for broken chunk framing, so every other failed read unwrapped a null.

- A failed body read now returns the body's own error, the connection's read error, or `ReadFailed`, and the caller reports the request as failed.
- API key validation, the Jev permission reviewer, and the non-streaming `postGatewayCompletion` called std's `fetch` directly, with the same unwrap. They now use a new `fetchWithClient`, which shares `fetchOnOpenJob`'s send-and-read steps. No fx code calls std's `fetch` anymore.

## Before and after

`fx logout grok` against a revoke endpoint whose 200 answer is still arriving at the 15 s limit:

```
before: thread 91836612 panic: attempt to use null value   (exit 134)
after:  Signed out of Grok.
        fx logout: local Grok session removed, but remote revocation could not be confirmed   (exit 0)
```

In the TUI, `/logout` of fx login against such an issuer ended the whole session about 15 s later; now fx shows `Warning: signed out locally, but the remote session could not be revoked.` and keeps running. A connection dropped after 3 of 100 body bytes crashed at once; now it's reported the same way. `fx models` with a Grok model list that never finishes now ends with its usual "could not list models" error after 30 s.

## Tests

- New e2e tests, each failing on main: the CLI Grok logout and the TUI fx login logout against an answer that drips, and a Jev review answer cut off mid-body, which now holds the action.

title: Check the prompt cache layout against the toolbox menu
body:
## Summary

- The prompt_context check reads a request as base, toolbox menu, project rules, turn context and runtime notes, so it passes against a current fx build again.
- The prompt cache model has one menu block in place of the skills and MCP blocks, and its stable end and second cache marker sit on the project rules.
- The planted design that marks every system block now marks every block ahead of the conversation, so it still passes the limit of four markers on both provider families.
- A request that still sends the old skill or MCP catalog is reported as a catalog, not as a marker inside the base group.
- A menu led by the skipped-skill warning, and project rules that mention the menu's tag, still read as the menu and the project block.

## Why the check failed

The unchanged driver passes on `40ce2d03c`, the commit before #1658 merged, and fails from `9f7aca62f`, the first commit of #1658. That change replaced the skill and MCP catalogs with one toolbox menu. Requests now run base, menu, project rules, with the cache markers after base and after the project rules. The driver and the model expected base, skills, project rules, MCP, with the second marker after the MCP catalog. #1669 did not break it: the driver passes on `574e56e6c`, which contains it. fx's markers kept their meaning (after the shared prompt, and after the stable instructions), so the model changes only where its block list and positions had to.

On this branch the driver passes (21 tests, 0 failures) and all 44 configs in `check.sh` keep their verdicts. Four planted bugs in the real fx code each make the driver fail, for the reason the bug should show: a menu that carries a per-process value (SameWorktreeReuse), a menu that changes on the second request of a turn (SessionReuse), the first marker on the menu, and the stable marker dropped (both rejected as not matching the layout).

## CI

CI does not run this check or its drivers, so the break went unnoticed. No workflow or script mentions `tests/tla/prompt_context`. This PR does not add it. The models CI runs today are recovery, agent_runtime and gateway_open on every pull request, the SDK, MCP, MCP host, transcript window, subagent and session-write checks when their code changes, and mcp_call with the `ci:tla-mcp-call` label. Not run by CI: acp, agents_menu, cache_warming, cli, durable, full_detail, fuzzy_match, image_route, indexer, prompt_context, session_manager, shell_command, shell_eval_error, terminal, toolbox, usage, and the provider_auth, resume and remaining session drivers.

## Gap in what the driver covers

Each driver session is one `fx ask` process with one turn, and the instructions are built once per turn. The kept toolbox menu (`Toolbox.tla` MenuFixed) only matters from a second turn in the same process, so the driver cannot see a bug there: a menu that re-renders in that path still passes it.

## Every other driver and `check.sh`, once, on main

Run on a build of main `9238f978e` on a Mac (a Linux sandbox run hit a full disk and is discarded). 68 items: 62 passed, including two setup steps, 4 failed and 2 timed out. No failure besides prompt_context traces to the toolbox or catalog change, so this PR repairs nothing else. The two timeouts are not verdicts.

Passed: the model checks of acp, agent_runtime, agents_menu, cache_warming, cli, durable, full_detail, fuzzy_match, gateway_open, image_route, indexer, mcp, mcp_call, mcp_host, prompt_context (the model alone), recovery, sdk, session, shell_command, shell_eval_error, subagent, terminal, toolbox, transcript_window and usage; the drivers of acp (4), agent_runtime, agents_menu (3), cache_warming, cli, full_detail, gateway_open, mcp_host, mcp (bridge test), provider_auth, recovery, resume, shell_command, shell_eval_error, subagent (2), usage (model.ts and lean) and sdk (12 runs).

| Item | Result | First error and what I found |
|---|---|---|
| prompt_context driver (contract, midsession) | fails on main, passes here | `marker inside the base group`; this PR |
| mcp driver | one unit failed in the sweep, passes on rerun | `FAIL U03 u03-ignores-sigterm`, `final kill_sent is false, expected true`; the sweep ran under load above 20 |
| session driver | fails, on rerun too | `status.test.ts:188`, `closedAsBefore(report)` is false; it fails the same way at `b5cf9cd25`, before the toolbox change |
| session_manager driver | 16 failures, 14 on rerun | `Timed out waiting for pane predicate`, and `TLC REJECTED ... not a behavior of V1Conversion`; 14 fail at `b5cf9cd25` too, and the one test that differs fails at `40ce2d03c`, before #1658 |
| usage model test | timed out at 45 min | its first two tests passed; not rerun |
| session_manager check | timed out at 90 min | the specs before V1Conversion passed with no error; V1Conversion was at 94 million states; not rerun |

title: Keep the durable core outage tests from depending on the clock
body:
## Summary

- The durable core outage tests no longer fail when a CI runner stalls for half a second while libfx retries a stopped engine. libfx's behavior is unchanged.
- The simulated outage in those tests ends when the test ends it, not 1.5 s after an engine opens.
- The first engine the outage refuses opens 2 s late, so an outage ended by the clock would fail both tests every time.
- `LIBFX_TEST_ONLY` runs only the durable core tests whose names contain it, as `test-durable.mjs` does.

title: Show auto-mode reviews, git state, settings, and skills in traces
body:
## Summary

- `/trace` now records each auto-mode safety review. An `auto_reviews` record counts the reviews this session by result (`clear`, `caution`, `unavailable`, `held`, and `error`) and counts the holds reused within a turn.
- A `held_auto_review` record keeps each of the 32 newest reviews that didn't clear, so a session of cleared commands can't push them out, and an `auto_review` record keeps each of the 64 newest reviews. Each one has its risk or reason, the tool and call ID, whether a subagent asked, how long the review took, the command, file path, or tool arguments it judged, and the reviewer's rationale, with secrets masked.
- A `git` record has the workspace's branch, `git status --short --branch`, the last five commits, and the staged and unstaged diff stats, read through safe git in the workspace folder. Each line git printed is one string in a list, with its leading spaces.
- `/trace` waits for git for 3 seconds in all, safe git's own checks included, because it runs on the terminal's thread. Each git command runs in its own process group; at the limit the running one is ended and reaped and the rest do not start. The record then has `"error": "timeout"`, `"timeout_ms": 3000`, and `unfinished`, which names each field git did not finish, and it keeps what finished. A git that a signal ends gives `"error": "signal"` with the signal number instead of a crash.
- A `setting` record for each setting has its key, its value as `fx config list --show-origin` prints it with secrets masked, and the file or `FX_*` variable that set it. An `unknown_setting` record names each key fx doesn't know.
- A `skill` record for each skill fx found has its name and source, and a `skill_problem` record for each skill it couldn't load has its path and the cause.
- The schema at the top of `src/core/app/trace_report.zig` documents each new record. Git lines, setting keys and values, skill names, and paths longer than 400 bytes are cut and end with their full size.
- `fx pr --create` and `fx issue --create` report a `gh` that a signal ended as a failed publish (`gh command failed`) instead of crashing. fx read the exit code of `gh` without checking whether `gh` had exited at all.

A review from a real auto-mode run:

```json
{"type":"auto_review","at":"2026-11-12T19:10:44.416Z","at_ms":1794510644416,"outcome":"clear","risk":"low","tool":"shell","origin":"root","reused":false,"elapsed_ms":1270,"call_id":"call-44fa3f7e-d5ef-47e7-b677-8268de57c851-0","action_kind":"command","action":"curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://example.com","action_bytes":59,"rationale":"The exact command makes a standard HTTPS request to example.com and discards the response body while printing the HTTP status code; it does not show evidence of either defined harm.","rationale_bytes":181}
```

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#285

title: Keep a finished subagent's list row working until its turn is applied
body:
## Summary

- In the agent list, a subagent that has just finished no longer drops below an older idle agent for a moment and then moves back up by itself.
- Its row keeps showing working until its reply is saved, and then shows idle or finished in its right place in one step.
- While a subagent's finished turn is not applied yet, the list, the footer's "N subagents working" note, and the idle parent's "waiting on N subagents" row all count it as working. A subagent that waits for approval keeps its own states: the list shows it as needing approval, the note leaves it out, and the parent's row still waits on it.
- The test that answers two subagents' approvals waits for the second subagent's file before it reads it. It read the file as soon as main showed the next prompt, and the subagent writes it on another thread after the approval.
- The model in tests/tla/agents_menu gets the rule that a row's state and its place come from the same applied update, with a planted bug that its rules catch. A driver reads every frame of the built fx's list while subagents finish, and TLC checks the frames against that rule.

## Before and after

The driver holds three subagents and releases them one by one. These are the list's rows, top to bottom, in the frames after gamma's reply is released.

main:

```
gamma working, alpha idle, beta idle
alpha idle, beta idle, gamma idle      <- gamma idle at the bottom for one frame
gamma idle, alpha idle, beta idle
```

This branch:

```
gamma working, alpha idle, beta idle
gamma idle, alpha idle, beta idle
```

The agent list order E2E test, in a Linux arm64 VM, on ReleaseSafe builds, 2 workers with 100 runs each, pinned to 2 CPUs with 6 busy loops:

| Build | Failed runs |
| --- | --- |
| main | 11 of 200, 4 of 200 |
| this branch | 0 of 200, 0 of 200 |

Before main was merged in, the same loop gave 16 of 200 on main and 0 of 200 on this branch. A reviewer's runs of the same loop gave 12 of 200 and 11 of 200 on main, and 0 of 200 on this branch.

## Not fixed here

`main can still steer a working subagent after it has read 64 earlier messages` and `a subagent with 64 unread messages refuses one more and says why` also fail on the Linux arm64 PGSO candidate. I could not reproduce that, so this PR does not change it.

- Seen in PGSO arm64 runs 42571956263 (both attempts hung 121 s), 42599090371 (the 65th message got `queue_full` with a null result), 42691566051 (hung 121 s) and 42941974214 (hung 121 s, with an empty pane). It did not fail in the x86_64 PGSO runs or in ci.yml over the same days.
- A `queue_full` answer means 64 messages to the subagent were waiting for its next turn instead of joining its running turn (src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig:640). So the first message was turned away from the running turn and every later one queued behind it. The 121 s hang is the same state seen from the first test.
- Not reproduced: about 600 runs of the two tests, on a ReleaseSafe build and on the arm64 PGSO candidate from run 42941644940, in a Linux arm64 VM under 12 busy loops and under pinned CPUs. The one failure was tmux failing to start.
- The PGSO artifacts have no behavior-corpus logs, so the failing runs show only the test output.

title: Let full access open and run MCP tools that a rule denies
body:
## Summary

- In full access, a deny rule no longer hides or blocks an MCP tool on any path: `toolbox` search, open and run, the `fx mcp call` forms (`list`, `search`, `help`, and a call), a subagent's own tools, and ACP's always-loaded tools.
- In `ask` and `auto`, a deny rule still hides and refuses the tool on every path, with the same words as before.
- A subagent follows the mode it runs in. A subagent whose profile sets full access under a host in `auto` ignores the rules, and one whose profile sets `auto` under a host in full access still gets them.
- A subagent limited to other servers is still refused in every mode. Only the rules go, not the access.

## The rule

In full access, no MCP deny rule hides or blocks an MCP tool on any path. Outside full access nothing changes. This follows `AGENTS.md`: "`permission_mode` controls baseline (`ask`, `auto`, or `full-access`; `yolo` remains an alias). Full access bypasses fx permission policy". Built-in tools already worked this way, and MCP tools did not.

Before this change the paths disagreed. `toolbox` search and the open of a small server read no rules in full access, and every other path read the host's rules. So with a deny rule on a tool `T`, full access listed `T` and then said it was not in the toolbox when the agent opened or ran it.

## Before and after in full access, with a deny rule on `T`

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `toolbox` search | lists `T` | lists `T` |
| `toolbox` open, small server | lists `T` with its arguments | same |
| `toolbox` open, large server | omits `T` | lists `T` |
| `toolbox` open `T` | "Nothing named `T` is in the toolbox menu." | shows `T` and its arguments |
| `toolbox` run `T` | "No tool named `T` is in the toolbox." | runs `T` |
| `fx mcp call` list, search, help, call | `T` hidden; help says "No MCP tool named `T` is available to this agent." | `T` listed, found, and callable |
| subagent whose profile sets full access, host in `auto` | refused like the host | same as the host in full access |
| subagent in `auto`, host in full access | rule applies | rule applies (unchanged) |
| ACP always-loaded tools | `T` left out | `T` advertised |

## What changed in the code

- `permissions.mcpRules(mode, rules)` is the one place that picks the rule set for an MCP path: no rules in full access, the host's rules otherwise. Six readers in `tool_runtime.zig` go through `mcpRulesOf`, which reads the mode of the agent that uses the tool: the dispatch field (toolbox search reads it), the bridge's list and search, resolving a tool that is not selected, opening a tool, the refresh of a tool whose definition changed, and the per-step snapshot.
- The hosts (TUI, ACP, `fx ask`) build a subagent's tool list and access view without rules. The profile's server scope (`cloneIntegrations`, `narrowMcpView`) is unchanged. A separate step, `cloneWithoutDeniedMcp`, applies the rules with the subagent's own mode, so a profile that sets another mode than its host is judged by its own.
- ACP's always-loaded tool list read the session's rules directly and now goes through `mcpRules`. This reader was not in the original list of paths. The sibling search found it.
- `App.snapshotMcpDefinition` is the per-step refresh of a selected tool. The TUI wires it into every agent, and the orchestrator calls it on each step. It now takes the mode of the agent that refreshes the tool, through `agentSnapshotMcpDefinition`, and gets its rules from `mcpRules`. Before, it passed the host's rules in every mode, so a selected tool that a rule names would have dropped out at the next step of an agent in full access. `App.snapshotMcpDefinition` in `main.zig` picks the rule set itself, with `permissions.mcpRules`. That adds no state, field, branch or import to `App`, so it stays there as it is. The ship gate's optional advice was to call `mcpRules` in `agentSnapshotMcpDefinition` and pass the rule set, so that `main.zig` only forwards. I kept it, because the mode is already an argument there and the rule set comes from the same one-line call every other reader makes.

## Unchanged

- `ask` and `auto`: the guard tests below hold the old words and exit codes for the main agent and for a subagent, and they pass on `main` too. They are there to show that nothing changed outside full access, so they do not fail first.
- Access views: a subagent limited to another server is refused in every mode. That guard test passes on `main` and on this branch.
- A server that needs a login gives the same words in every mode.
- `/permissions remember deny` still cannot save a rule for an MCP tool, so a saved-session rule cannot name one.

## Verification

Commands, from the repository root unless noted.

- Model: `sh tests/tla/mcp_host/check.sh`. `tests/tla/mcp_host/McpRules.tla` states `FullAccessIgnoresRules`, `DenyHoldsOutside`, `PathsAgree`, `AccessHolds`, and `UndeniedShown` over ten paths plus the subagent's tool list, with a subagent that runs in another mode than its host and a session that changes mode. The smoke (144 states) and stress (2,304 states) configs pass, 9 planted bugs are caught, and 3 findings show the code before the fix violating the model: split rules in full access, paths that disagree, and a tool list built from the host's rules.
- Driver: `bun test ./tests/tla/drivers/mcp_host/`. `mcp-rules.test.ts` runs real `fx ask` sessions and has TLC check each trace. Four tests check five traces, and the model accepts all five on this branch. Two controls are rejected by the model, as they should be.
- Unit tests, which run in `zig build test`:
  - `permissions.zig`: `mcpRules` gives no rules in full access and the host's rules in every other mode.
  - `tool_runtime.zig`: "every MCP reader takes the host's rules outside full access and none in it" checks all six readers in ask, auto and full access. To see it catch a reader, replace one `mcpRulesOf(ctx)` in `tool_runtime.zig` with `ctx.permission_rules`. Each of the six replacements, one at a time, fails the test with `expected 0, found 1`.
  - `main.zig`: "the per-step refresh of an MCP tool takes the rules of the mode of the agent that runs it" calls the agent's own deps against a real host with a tool that a rule denies. An agent in full access keeps the tool, and an agent in ask loses it. It fails if `App.snapshotMcpDefinition` goes back to passing the host's rules in every mode.
  - `authority.zig`: the tool list cut by the subagent's own mode, and through `resolveWith`.
- E2E, from `tests/e2e` with the keys unset and `FX_SOUND=0`:
  - `bun test mcp-stdio.test.ts -t "MCP deny rules by permission mode"` and `-t "fx mcp call"`: every path, main agent and subagent, mixed modes, a whole-server rule, allow plus deny, a down server.
  - `bun test mcp-auth.test.ts -t "a tool of a server that needs a login"`: the login words are the same in every mode.
  - `bun test acp.test.ts -t "an always-loaded MCP tool a deny rule names"`.
  - `bun test tui-mcp-deny-rules.test.ts`: the TUI, including a mode change. It needs `tmux`. The file is wired into the shard weights and the PGSO corpus as a verification scenario.
- Merge with `main`: the one conflict was in the test blocks at the end of `src/core/subagent/authority.zig`. `main`'s `LiveHost` fixture and its tests are kept as they are, with this pull request's two `cloneWithoutDeniedMcp` tests after them, and the product code merged as it was. `resolveWith` still calls `cloneWithoutDeniedMcp(..., current.permission_mode, host.rules)`. With that call changed to apply the host's rules in every mode, "a child's integrations follow the mode it runs in, not its host's…" fails with `expected 2, found 1`.
- Run on Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 after the merge, keys unset and `FX_SOUND=0`: the `core.subagent.` group of unit tests with the named tests above (218 tests, 0 failed), `sh tests/tla/mcp_host/check.sh` (124 runs, 0 failed), `bun test ./tests/tla/drivers/mcp_host/` (59 pass, 12 skip themselves, 0 fail), and the four e2e commands above (12, 22, 1 and 1 pass, with 13 ACP tests skipped on Linux). `tui-mcp-deny-rules.test.ts` ran on a Mac against the macOS binary: 4 pass.
- The full-access tests fail on `main`'s binary and pass here. The guard tests (`ask`, `auto`, the access view, the login words) pass on both.
- One existing test changed: "list, search, and help hide a tool the permission rules deny" ran the bridge in full access and expected the tool hidden, which was the old behavior. It now runs in `auto`, and a new test beside it expects the tool shown in full access.

## Docs

One sentence goes on the permissions page, in the Persistent rules section: the rules apply in `ask` and `auto` mode but not in `full-access`. It is in vercel-labs/fx-web#334, a draft that should merge after this pull request. The page already says that `full-access` disables fx permission checks.

title: Bug: `fx ask --resume` compacts early because each process starts without the token calibration
body:
## What happens

A program that drives fx with one `fx ask --resume <id>` process per user message gets automatic compaction well below `auto_compact_percent`. With `gpt-6.1-sol` on a Codex subscription (500k window, so compaction is due at 400k), a session was compacted twice at the start of a turn while the provider reported 181k–291k input tokens. Within a turn, the same session grew to 291k without compacting.

## Cause

Before each request, fx estimates the request's size from its serialized bytes, and after the reply it calibrates that estimate against the provider's `input_tokens` (#745). #964 moved the calibration from a per-turn local to `Agent.request_token_calibration`, so the first request of a turn calibrates from the previous turn. It still lives only in memory. A new `fx ask` process that resumes the session starts without it, so its first request is measured with the raw estimate, and the compaction decision in `orchestrator.zig` uses that number.

The raw estimate runs well above the provider's count when the history holds non-English text, tool output, and Codex reasoning, so the first request of every resumed process can cross `compact_at_tokens` early. Requests after the first are calibrated and close to the provider's count.

## Measurements

A clean profile, `gpt-6.1-sol` through the Codex subscription, effort `high`. Process A asks for a 1,500-word story in Russian, saves it with a tool, and counts its words. Process B resumes the session with one more message. `FX_TRACE=1 FX_TRACE_SCOPES=context_compaction` logged the decisions, and `input_tokens` comes from the session's `model_call` items.

| Request | Calibration | fx estimate | Provider `input_tokens` | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A, first | none | 5,530 | 3,924 | 1.41 |
| A, last | from the previous reply | 10,635 | 10,461 | 1.02 |
| B, first (resumed) | none | 16,016 | 10,485 | 1.53 |
| B, second | from the previous reply | 11,928 | 11,483 | 1.04 |

In the long session above, the second compaction ran at the start of a resumed turn whose compaction request the provider counted at 185,835 tokens, so the uncalibrated estimate was at least 400k, more than 2.1 times the real size.

## Expected

A resumed session compacts at the same real size as a session that keeps running in one process.

## Possible fix

The session log already records the provider's `input_tokens` in each `model_call` item. If the item also recorded fx's own estimate of that request, a resumed process could seed `request_token_calibration` from the last `model_call` for the same provider and model before its first compaction check, and skip it after a compaction or a model change, as the in-memory calibration does now. A test would run two `fx ask` processes on one session and check that the second one's first estimate is calibrated.

I'm happy to open a PR along these lines if the approach fits.

title: Tell the model when a shell command it waits on goes quiet
body:
## Summary

- A running shell result shows how long the command has run (`running_ms`) and how long since its last output (`quiet_ms`).
- After 2 minutes without output, the result adds `quiet_notice`, which asks the model to check whether the command is still working or has hung. fx does not stop the command.
- An `interact` wait that saw the command print within the last 2 minutes returns when the command reaches 2 minutes without output, instead of waiting out its `yield_time_ms`.
- An `interact` wait that starts when the command is already past 2 minutes without output waits its full `yield_time_ms`, unless new output arrives.
- Finished, stopped, and terminal (`tty`) session results are unchanged.

title: Preview agents while moving through the agent list
body:
## Summary

- Show the highlighted agent's conversation as up and down move through the agent list, without pressing enter.
- Keep the agent shown when enter closes the list, so its composer takes what you type.
- Go back to the agent the list opened on with esc, ctrl+x, or ctrl+c, or stay on the agent shown when that one has closed.
- Close the list with up on its first row, staying on the agent shown. Down on the last row stays there.
- Show the first match when a search hides the highlighted row, and keep the search, with its cursor, in the composer while the list switches agents.
- Close the list into the shown agent's composer on a paste.
- Show the agent on the row above when the agent on screen closes, by delete in the list, /close, or its parent, and the next instance when it was the first row.
- Label the agent list's arrows `↑↓ preview` in its hint row.
- Close a subagent from the agent list, or quit fx, without crashing while the subagent's work is still ending: its agent is freed only after the subagent's thread lets go of it, and its session closes either way.

## Before and after

The hint row:

```text
Before: ↑↓ move     enter switch     esc back
After:  ↑↓ preview     enter switch     esc back
```

The agent list on fx 1 after one press of down: fx 2's row is highlighted, and its conversation shows above the list, which stays open until enter keeps fx 2 or esc goes back to fx 1.

```text
┃ HOST_B run the tests

  The tests pass on Linux and macOS.

  0s (↑6 ↓10)

┃
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Agents 3

  fx 1  HOST_A review the parser    idle            main  devstral-small
  fx 2  HOST_B run the tests        idle            main  devstral-small
  fx 3  HOST_C draft the changelog  idle            main  devstral-small
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
↑↓ preview     enter switch     delete close     esc back
```

Before, moving only moved the highlight:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    state "list closed" as Closed
    state "list open, agent on screen unchanged" as Open
    [*] --> Closed
    Closed --> Open: down, ctrl+x, or /agents
    Open --> Open: up or down moves the highlight
    Open --> Open: a search edit moves the highlight
    Open --> Closed: enter shows the highlighted agent
    Open --> Closed: esc, ctrl+x, ctrl+c, or a paste keep the agent on screen
    Open --> Open: delete twice closes the row, and a shown subagent gives the screen to its parent, a shown instance to the next instance
```

After, moving previews, and the list remembers the agent it opened on:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    state "list closed" as Closed
    state "list open, previewing the highlighted agent" as Open
    [*] --> Closed
    Closed --> Open: down, ctrl+x, or /agents, remembering the agent on screen
    Open --> Open: up or down shows the agent they land on
    Open --> Open: a search edit shows the first match when the highlighted row goes
    Open --> Closed: up on the first row keeps the agent shown
    Open --> Closed: enter keeps the agent shown
    Open --> Closed: esc, ctrl+x, or ctrl+c show the remembered agent, or keep the agent shown when it has closed
    Open --> Closed: a paste keeps the agent shown and lands in its composer
    Open --> Open: delete twice closes the row, and when it was shown, the row above takes its place
```

The agent list's model follows the same rules (`tests/tla/agents_menu/`). Its planted-bug configs `agents-menu-mutation-preview.cfg` and `agents-menu-mutation-pin.cfg` checked the old move-only rules, so they become `agents-menu-mutation-paste-back.cfg` and `agents-menu-mutation-up-stays.cfg` for the new ones.

title: Hold history rows a stable frame cannot replay
body:
## Summary

- A stable frame after a source rewrite could scroll the rows between history and the viewport with nothing to write them. Native scrollback got hundreds of blank rows and history claimed rows that were never written. It is the second path behind the Ctrl-O stress failure; the first is #1831, and this change does not depend on it.
- Cause: the stable plan granted those rows whenever a replay range existed (`runtime.zig`, the recovery rebase branch), while the append base replays history only for a flagged anchor, and the anchor a recovered frame leaves has no flag. The plan and the base now call one predicate, `stableHistoryReplayWanted`.
- A frame that cannot replay the owed rows grants none, logs `transcript_history_debt_held`, and keeps them owed. The next frame replays them from history. The catch-up branch of the plan gets the same check. A flagged replay no longer waits on a destructive invalidation, because the plan cannot see one. Rows already on screen still scroll out without an append, as the pinned status frame does.
- Before and after on Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64, tmux 3.4, bun 1.3.14, 3 CPUs plus 10 busy loops, the Ctrl-O history repro of `tui-full-transcript-brutal.test.ts`, both arms on top of #1831 so the first path does not hide this one): the old code left a blank gap of 458 to 1363 rows in 18 of 150 runs. This change left none in 300 runs (two batches of 150), with the longest blank run at 1 row. If the rate were still 12 percent, 150 clean runs would happen about once in 200 million times.
- Probe build of the fix, 100 runs: no frame scrolled rows without an append, and 17 runs held a frame (owed 483 or 947 rows, scroll 0). The next frame replayed them: `document_append_plan source_visual_offset=1542 target_visual_offset=2027`.
- Tests: six runtime tests in `runtime_tests.zig` plan and seal a real frame. They leave the debt the way a recovery does: a frame whose terminal write fails leaves a receipt that owes rows, and the next frame over a rewritten source commits stable with history four rows behind the viewport. The invalidation cases use an external clear. All six fail on main (`expected 0, found 5`, `expected 8, found 13`), and taking out the rebase check, the catch-up check, or the replay under an invalidation fails its own tests. The full `zig build test` and the transcript and resize suites pass. I found no deterministic VT sequence that gives a recovered frame followed by a rewrite, so the end-to-end proof is the Linux loop above; the stress test from #1831 covers it in CI once both land.

## Review

The full review ran on 3213d2ea4. The later commit e6577b31e changes only the tests, and was checked on its own.

title: Name why a terminal recording could not start
body:
## Summary

- When `FX_DEBUG_RECORD` is set and the recording cannot start, fx now says why instead of printing only `fx: unable to start terminal recording.`
- A full disk prints `fx: unable to start terminal recording: the disk is full. Free some space, or unset FX_DEBUG_RECORD.`
- A file-size limit prints `fx: unable to start terminal recording: a file-size limit was reached.`
- A permission error prints `fx: unable to start terminal recording: permission denied.` This covers both EACCES, such as a read-only folder, and EPERM, such as an immutable tape file or a folder macOS keeps from the terminal's privacy settings.
- A read-only disk prints `fx: unable to start terminal recording: the disk is read-only.`
- Any other failure keeps the old `fx: unable to start terminal recording.` line. The start still fails with exit code 1 under `FX_DEBUG_RECORD`, and a plain `FX_RECORD` path that cannot be created still runs without recording, as before.
- `TmuxSession` in the end-to-end tests now clears `FX_DEBUG_RECORD`, `FX_DEBUG_RECORD_SILENT_BANNER`, `FX_RECORD`, `FX_RECORD_INPUT`, `FX_MCP_CALL_SOCKET` and `FX_MCP_CALL_TOKEN` from each pane, unless the test sets one itself.
- A pane inherits the environment of its tmux server, not of the shell that runs the tests. A default server that a shell with `FX_DEBUG_RECORD=1` had started leaked it into every test pane, so recording started on the full disk image and nine fault grid tests failed on macOS with the generic line. Removing the variables from the test process did not help.
- The two MCP bridge variables leaked the same way. With a live socket, `fx mcp call` in a test pane reached another session's bridge and exited 1 ("the connection to fx was lost") instead of 3.
- The fault grid's full-disk rows for the app no longer accept the terminal recording line, so a recording that leaks into a test fails the row instead of passing it.

## Follow-ups

- The phrases for a full disk, a file-size limit, a permission error and a read-only disk are now written in three places: `types.plainErrorText`, `v2StorageFaultMessage` in `app_entry_runtime.zig`, and `recordingStartMessage`. One shared table would keep them from drifting.
- The recording message does not name the path that failed. That needs the path to travel with the error.

## Review

The full review ran on 8a4dc5014. The later commits e2d9b0a6b (the EPERM case) and d7ef781fc (a merge of main) were checked on their own.

title: Ask fx's questions through the ACP client's form
body:
## Summary

- When the ACP client sets `elicitation.form` in `clientCapabilities`, the model's questions reach it as an `elicitation/create` form, and the answers go back to the model.
- Each question is a choice of the model's options plus Other, with a text field for the user's own answer when they pick Other.
- Declining or cancelling the form cancels the question, and stopping the turn withdraws the form.
- A turn with such a client no longer tells the model there is no question UI, and gets the same notes as a TUI turn.
- Clients without form elicitation keep today's behavior: the question tool says it is unavailable, and the model asks in plain text.

title: Start the next request with the last request's messages
body:
## Summary

- On a model that reads images through Vision, each image is listed once, on the user message of the turn that attached it, in the live request and in the request a resumed session or a second ACP prompt builds. The next request starts with the last request, and the request grows by one line per image, not by every image on every turn. A turn with no image of its own lists none, and every earlier id stays named on the message that came with it. An authorized image that no earlier message carries, such as the image of a recovered request, is listed on the current message. The native image route is unchanged.
- Review mode's follow-up message is saved with the turn as fx's own message, so the next request keeps it. No host turns review mode on today, so the built binary cannot reach this; a flow test covers it.
- Notes that join a step boundary, a changed runtime context (git branch, date) and the notes a tool step's gate queued, now come before the steering the last step ended with: continuation prompts, the empty-reply nudge, the prefill recovery prompt, review mode's message, and steering taken after a reply. The saved turn restores them in that order, so the next request, `fx ask --resume`, and crash recovery no longer reorder them.
- When a reply adds a second steering message to a tail the previous request already carried and the context changed at that point, one request differs from the one before it. The next turn still starts with the last request.
- Two messages fx sends with no marker are still dropped by the save on this branch: Vision's outage notice, and the Stop hook's message (no production code registers a Stop hook today). This PR does not mark them. Open PR 1829 marks both and holds the notice until every result of its step is in; a notice that falls between two results of one step also cuts the later results from the saved step today, and 1829 removes that too. `tests/tla/saved_turn/saved-turn-main.cfg` models this branch as it is, and `check.sh` expects it to fail `NothingDropped`.
- A TLA+ model, `tests/tla/saved_turn/`, covers the order of a turn's messages at each step boundary, live and restored, with six planted defects. A driver runs the built fx (ask, resume, ACP) against it. The model holds 1829's held notices and the marked Stop hook message as options, and `saved-turn-kept.cfg` is what this PR keeps without them.
- This PR does not depend on 1829 and does not edit its branch. Both change the step loop's boundary code in `orchestrator.zig`. Whichever merges second should make 1829's `flushStepBoundary` use `insertBoundaryNotes`, so held notices join before the steering the step ended with. A trial merge of the two heads conflicts only in the header comment of `recovery_prompt.zig` and in `tests/e2e/vision-route-fake-gateway.test.ts`, where each branch adds a helper that does the same thing (`expectNextRequestExtends` here, `expectPromptExtends` there); keep one. 1829 also conflicts with current main in `orchestrator.zig`, which is not caused by this PR.

## Before and after

First differing message of the request after the one before it, with the binary built from main and from this branch:

| Case | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `fx ask --image` on a text-only model, then `fx ask --resume`; the same after an ACP image prompt and a second prompt | message 7, the user's message: live `Describe the attached image.\n\n<available_images>\n[Image #1]\n</available_images>`, resumed `Describe the attached image.` | none |
| The git branch changes while the empty-reply nudge step runs, then the session resumes | the user's message `Answer briefly.`: live without the runtime-context note, resumed with the `<fx-context-update>` block appended | none; the note joins before the nudge in both |
| 30 images on the first turn, then 100 turns | one list of 391 B in each request | one list of 391 B in each request |

Tests that fail on main and pass here:

- `tests/e2e/vision-route-fake-gateway.test.ts`: "a resumed session's next request starts with the request that carried the image references" and "each turn's next request starts with the last request of the turn before when later turns attach images too"
- `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`: "a runtime context change after an empty reply joins before the nudge, and a resumed session's next request starts with that request" (once per model family), "a request that carries the nudge and the runtime context note fails once and is sent again in the same order, and the next request extends the one that went through", and "a turn killed while the request with the nudge and the runtime context note waits resumes with that request's messages first"
- `tests/e2e/acp.test.ts`: "ACP's second prompt after an image prompt starts with the last request of the first"
- `src/core/agent/runtime/tests/gateway_flow.zig`: "the next turn extends the request that carried review mode's message", "review mode's message is saved as fx's own steering, not dropped and not the user's words", "the next turn extends a request that carried review mode's message and a changed runtime context", and the three "the next turn extends the request that carried a changed runtime context after ..." tests for the empty-reply nudge, a tool step and the nudge, and the continuation
- `src/core/agent/runtime/vision_contracts.zig`: "text-only projection lists each image once, on the message of the turn that attached it", "text-only projection grows by the lines of the images, not by the turns after them", and "text-only projection lists an authorized image no message carries on the current message"

title: Put the agents that need you first in the agent list
body:
## Summary

- Under each instance, the agent list puts the subagents waiting for the user first (needs approval, has a question, needs you), then the working ones, both in start order, then the idle ones by newest reply. A subagent whose own subagent waits moves up with it (`raiseParents`); instances keep their start order.
- The columns are now name, title, state, model, profile. The profile is named only when it isn't `main`; when no row has one, the column is gone. A narrow terminal still leaves out the profile first, then the model.
- When several hidden agents wait, the footer counts them, `3 agents require attention · main ↓`, in place of `reviewer and 2 more need you`. One waiting agent is still named, as in `reviewer needs approval`.

## Tests

- New E2E `the agent list puts subagents that wait for the user first, then working ones, then idle ones, and names only a profile other than main`: passes; fails on main. It also caught that a subagent started without a profile carries `main` as its profile name.
- `agents_menu_presentation` tests now read each row back through the VT emulator (`core/terminal/engine.zig`), and a new VT test checks the column order and that the model and profile are drawn dim.
- `app_agents_runtime` tests for the new order, a nested subagent raising its parent, and the 10,000-run random sort check.
- Updated E2E checks in `tui-host-switch` and `tui-host-instances` for the column order and the footer count.

- Review fix: the two `src/main.zig` waiting-note tests, and the hidden-instance note E2E, now expect `2 agents require attention`.
- `zig build test`: exit 0 (1177 s).
- `tui-host-switch.test.ts` 50/50. `tui-host-instances.test.ts` 44/47 under load: the waiting-note test passes with its fix, and the other two pass alone (2/2 each; the startup-picker one failed on a `tmux send-keys` timeout, and fx stayed under 8% CPU when rerun).
- `agents_menu` drivers: binary-to-spec 166 steps are behaviors of AgentsMenu; spec-to-binary 85 steps pass.

title: Accept multiline plain skill descriptions
body:
## Summary

- Decode multiline plain descriptions in skill metadata, including descriptions that start on the next line.
- Keep malformed continuations out of the catalog and cover parsing, discovery, and fuzz seeds.
- Restore discovery of the upstream [vercel-composition-patterns skill](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/blob/1a2c79d4e6c4a2283dc2c614b6538cbe1ed5ca62/skills/composition-patterns/SKILL.md#L1-L8) without changing its file.

## Verification

- `zig build` with Zig 0.17.0
- Focused Zig parser, discovery, and fuzz seed tests
- `zig fmt --check src/core/skills/skill_contract.zig src/core/skills/skill_runtime.zig`
- Ran the built binary in an isolated terminal profile with the original skill file. `/skills` listed the skill without a discovery warning; stderr was empty and the process exited 0.

## Docs

No manual change is needed. The skills page already describes the header as YAML. This change accepts another valid description form.

title: Keep bracketed paste on after a terminal reset
body:
## Summary

- Keep a multi-line paste in the input box within 30 seconds after a terminal reset, or another program, turns bracketed paste off under a running fx. Before, each line break in the paste pressed Enter and sent the first line as a message.

Stacked on #1880.

title: Keep network, catalog, and compaction failures in traces
body:
## Summary

On `main`, a failed call that later calls push out of the 32-call window leaves only a count in `session.errors`: the trace has no record of it, and Problems no longer names it. This change keeps failures apart from the windows.

- `/trace` keeps the 32 most recent failed network calls, failed model catalog events, and failed context compaction events in their own lists, so later entries that did not fail can't push them out of the trace.
- Each kept failure is a record after its section's window records: `failed_network_call` with the `network_call` fields, `failed_model_catalog_event` with the `model_catalog_event` fields, and `failed_compaction_event` with the `compaction_event` fields. A kept catalog or compaction event has the same `sequence` as its window record.
- The `network`, `model_catalog`, and `compaction` records gain `kept_failures`, which is 0 when the session has no failure. `model_catalog` and `compaction` also gain `session_failures`, every failure this session, including any no longer kept. For network calls, `session.errors` already counts them.
- The `network_call`, `model_catalog`, and `compaction` problem records come from the kept failures, newest three of each kind, so an old failure still shows there after later successes.
- Network call fields and model catalog and compaction details are cut on UTF-8 character boundaries when they are recorded, so a cut no longer leaves part of a character.
- The schema comment at the top of `src/core/app/trace_report.zig` documents the new records and fields.

## Sample

A `failed_network_call` record from a session whose gateway refused the connection:

```json
{"type":"failed_network_call","at":"2026-11-12T19:06:04.850Z","at_ms":1794510364850,"model":"openai/gpt-5","kind":"gateway","source":"parent","error":"ConnectionRefused","duration_ms":2,"response_bytes":0,"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0,"turn_id":1,"step_id":1}
```

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#290

title: Resend a waiting request with the team picked during its sign-in
body:
## Summary

- A request waiting for a sign-in now resends with the Vercel team chosen in that sign-in. Before, it resent with its old team, AI Gateway refused it again, and fx opened another sign-in.
- When AI Gateway refuses a login fx has just refreshed, fx names the Vercel team it sent the request for and how to choose another: press Esc twice, run `/login`, choose a team, and send the message again.
- fx names a team on screen, in that notice, in the status view, and in the `/usage` label, only by a slug or id that is a valid team name, so a saved login whose team slug holds control characters cannot put them on the screen.
- The team list a Vercel sign-in returns leaves out a team whose id or slug is not a valid team name, and a team whose name would not draw as it is shows under its slug. Before, such a team stopped the team picker with an empty screen.
- The retry after a refresh forced by a 401 sends the refreshed login's team with its key.
- In the TUI, subagents and tools running on the same fx login follow the picked team at their next refresh, like the request.
- `fx ask` and ACP still refuse a team change during a request, as before.

title: Keep HTTP connects from failing when a cancel signal arrives
body:
## Summary

- On macOS, a burst of HTTP connects could fail for no reason. A debug build of `fx` aborted with `programmer bug caused syscall error: ISCONN`. A release build returned `error.Unexpected` for that connect, and nothing was printed.
- The cause is in the std library: a late cancel signal makes `Io.Threaded` call `connect` twice on one socket. This change replaces only std's TCP `connect` on macOS with one that never calls it twice and that a cancel still ends within 25 ms.
- Linux and other targets keep std's connect. Linux: unverified by a run. Both Linux release binaries are byte-identical to the ones built from `origin/main` (see below).

## What happens today

`toolbox search` over many HTTP MCP servers starts all of their connects together. On macOS with a debug build:

| Servers | Runs that aborted today |
|---|---|
| 50 | 29 of 40 |
| 100 | 36 of 40 |

In a release build nothing is printed. In 150 instrumented release runs at 50 servers, 79 connects hit the failing retry, in 56 runs, and every run exited 0. In 1 run the search answer lacked servers 0 to 4 and listed 7, 8, 11 and 13 instead. In 1 run the search took 11 s instead of about 0.1 s. Neither case shows an error to the person.

## Cause

Zig 0.17.0, `lib/std`:

1. `Io/net/HostName.zig:310-312`: `HostName.connect` starts `connectMany` with `io.async` and cancels it in a `defer` on every exit, also after a successful connect.
2. `Io/Threaded.zig:1269-1290`: the cancel sends `SIG.IO` to the worker thread of that task. The signal can arrive after the thread has started another task. The handler has no `SA_RESTART` (`:1655-1665`, `:15140`).
3. `Io/Threaded.zig:12241-12272` (`posixConnect`): on `EINTR` it asks whether this connect was canceled, hears "no", and calls `connect` again. macOS answers `ISCONN`, which std treats as a bug (`:12270`, `errnoBug` at `:14442`).

How this was shown, with a copy of the std library that logs, selected by `ZIG_LIB_DIR` (the system Zig was not touched):

- All 6 spurious `EINTR` in a 10-run batch followed a signal that was sent for a different task than the one the thread was running. In 397 sampled signals, 391 came through the MCP HTTP client's connect (`src/mcp/io/http.zig:498`), 4 through the gateway client (`src/gateway/client.zig:1236`) and 2 through `src/core/shared/http_pool.zig:137`. All were sent by the cancel in `HostName.connect`.
- Removing fx's own two HTTP task cancels (`http.zig:173` and `:257`) changed nothing: 14 of 20 runs still aborted.
- Replacing only the cancel in `HostName.connect` with an `await` gave 20 of 20 runs with exit 0, no signal sent and no `EINTR`.
- A standalone program without fx (64 tasks, 20 connects each, to a loopback listener through `HostName.connect`) fails the same way on this Mac: 13 of 20 Debug runs abort with the same panic, and 13 of 20 ReleaseSafe runs return `error.Unexpected` (32 of 25,600 connects). With the cancel replaced by an `await` in the std copy, 0 of 20 runs failed in each mode.
- The Z1 and Z6 gateway tests are not linked to this: the 24 matching tests ran 1,360 times on std and as often on the std copy, with 0 failures in both.

## The fix

`src/core/shared/darwin_connect.zig` holds a wrapper that replaces only the `netConnectIp` entry of the process `Io`. `process_io_for` (`src/core/shared/io.zig`) installs it over the existing process-spawn wrapper. The happy-eyeballs and cancel logic of `HostName.connect` stays in std.

- The socket is opened as std does on macOS: the mode and protocol from std's `posixSocketModeProtocol`, then `FD_CLOEXEC` through `fcntl`. std sets no other option.
- The connect is non-blocking. The wrapper calls `connect` once, then waits with `poll` in 25 ms slices only on `EINPROGRESS` or `EINTR`. A signal that ends a wait early only repeats the wait.
- Between two slices it calls `Io.checkCancel`, which std documents for code that is neither in a syscall nor entering one. A cancel therefore takes effect within one slice. The socket is closed on every error path.
- After the connect it reads `SO_ERROR`, clears `O_NONBLOCK`, and takes the local address from `getsockname`, so later reads and writes behave as before.
- A connect with `options.timeout != .none` goes to std, which today stops with a TODO panic there. The wrapper does not change what such a caller gets.
- Other targets get the `Io` unchanged (`wrap` returns it).
- One `FX_TRACE` line per event under the scope `net`: `connect fd=<n> event=start|intr|done [result=...]`. It never holds an address.

## Tests and proof

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Zig tests: a storm of `SIG.IO` during 3,000 connects; a cancel ends within 100 ms and leaks no descriptor; a refused connect (the `SO_ERROR` path); a connect that fails at once leaks nothing; a held connect uses under 150 ms of CPU in 1.5 s; a returned socket is blocking and close-on-exec and carries its local address; the wrapper is what the test `Io` uses | pass in ReleaseSafe and Debug. The storm test failed 30 of 30 on today's code. |
| `toolbox.test.ts`: 50 HTTP servers, one search, 20 runs, no abort | pass on a Debug build. It aborted on today's. |
| `mcp-http`, `mcp-auth`, `mcp-stdio`, `cli`, `toolbox` E2E, keys unset | pass |
| full `zig build test` (includes the `src/gateway/` tests) | 10707 pass, 2 skipped |
| TLA+ `Connect.tla`, 5 properties, 6 planted bugs, 2 findings that std's loop violates | pass, planted bugs caught, findings exit 12 |
| `tests/tla/drivers/mcp_host/connect.test.ts` on the real `FX_TRACE` lines, Debug and ReleaseSafe | every trace accepted by TLC |
| all `mcp_host` models and drivers | pass |
| golden, 8 cases (healthy, `localhost` with two addresses, refused on v4 and v6, closed at accept, a server that accepts and never answers, a 500 after 1.5 s, a 500 for everything) | words and exit codes equal to `origin/main` |
| fault injection, the 7 failing cases of the golden set | equal to `origin/main` |
| ThreadSanitizer build (thread-leak reports off, because a shell worker thread still running at exit is reported as a leak; a data race still fails the run), the connect driver at 10, 25 and 50 servers | pass, no data race |
| mutation check: 11 planted bugs in `darwin_connect.zig` and `io.zig` (pass-through, a second `connect`, a signal that fails the wait, `O_NONBLOCK` kept, no `FD_CLOEXEC`, a leaked descriptor, no cancel check, `SO_ERROR` ignored, a 3 s slice, no `getsockname`, wrapper not installed) | 11 of 11 caught. The no-cancel-check bug is caught by the 600 s timeout, because that test never ends. |
| other targets build: `x86_64-linux`, the unit tests for `aarch64-linux`, `fx-core-wasm`, `fx-term-wasm` | pass |

The model is `tests/tla/mcp_host/Connect.tla`. It is not in a folder named after its module: `tests/AGENTS.md` names a model's folder after the module it describes, but only listed folders run in CI, and this place gives the model CI coverage through the MCP job (`scripts/detect-ci-need.sh`), next to its driver, which tests the MCP host's connects. The model describes `src/core/shared/darwin_connect.zig`, not an `mcp_host/` module.

`scripts/detect-ci-need.sh` and its test now run the TLA+ MCP job when `src/core/shared/darwin_connect.zig` changes, and `AGENTS.md` lists the file. `detect-macos-need.sh` already selects the macOS jobs for it ("has a macOS or Linux code path").

## Stress

Interleaved, one base run and then one new run, so both see the same machine load. Debug 50 servers 60 pairs, the others 40 pairs. "Finished" counts runs that ended with an answer.

| Build | Servers | base finished | base over 3 s | base p90 | new finished | new aborts, hangs, lost servers | new over 3 s | new p90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Debug | 50 | 20 of 60 (40 abort) | 0 | 659 ms | 60 of 60 | 0 | 0 | 682 ms |
| Debug | 100 | 12 of 40 (28 abort) | 0 | 756 ms | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 967 ms |
| ReleaseSafe | 100 | 40 of 40 | 0 | 587 ms | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 632 ms |
| ReleaseSafe | 200 | 40 of 40 | 2 | 475 ms | 40 of 40 | 0 | 2 | 443 ms |

The pass rule has a stated margin in the script. The new binaries must have 0 aborts, 0 hangs (a 90 s cap) and 0 lost servers, and their share of runs over 3 s and their p90 may not exceed base by more than 10 percentage points and 25% plus 300 ms.

`toolbox search` over 200 HTTP servers can take 3 to 12 s under load on both binaries. It is not changed by this PR. (On this shared machine, earlier stress runs that were not interleaved showed slow searches in both binaries, with `fx` idle and waiting for the MCP fixture.)

## CPU and startup

- 48 loopback connects with the accept delayed 2 s: 5, 5 and 8 ms of CPU through std, 8, 7 and 6 ms through the wrapper. macOS loopback never held a connect, not even at a backlog of 1, so this cannot show the wait loop.
- The wait loop with a stand-in that never connects, 2 s each: 1 waiting connect used 1 ms of CPU, 16 used 9 ms, 64 used 36 ms (about 1% of one core). Cancelling takes about 12 ms each.
- `fx` startup, before and after, ReleaseSafe, 72 runs per side, interleaved (ms; the control is `/usr/bin/true`, same on both sides):

| Command | base p50 / p90 / p95 | new p50 / p90 / p95 |
|---|---|---|
| `fx` (startup) | 14.40 / 21.43 / 25.12 | 13.86 / 20.77 / 22.83 |
| `fx help` | 21.88 / 34.05 / 47.16 | 19.74 / 33.71 / 51.39 |
| `fx status --json` | 45.15 / 71.90 / 89.97 | 41.29 / 67.11 / 87.96 |
| `fx doctor --json` | 42.93 / 63.77 / 73.43 | 44.52 / 67.10 / 75.40 |
| `fx sessions --json` | 36.68 / 61.34 / 77.45 | 38.12 / 65.86 / 70.10 |
| `/usr/bin/true` (control) | 17.73 / 31.68 / 43.10 | 17.58 / 27.71 / 31.36 |

The machine was shared (load 7 to 9), and the control differs by about as much as the commands do. An earlier run of the first command showed 13.0 ms against 12.6 ms (median), no clear difference.

## Linux

Linux: unverified by a run. There is no Linux run of the tests here. From reading `__inet_stream_connect`, a second blocking `connect` on a socket that is still connecting waits there and returns 0 when the handshake has completed, so the failure looks specific to macOS. Linux keeps std's connect.

As a check that nothing changes there, `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe` for each Linux target from `cf7a7754f` and from this branch gives byte-identical `fx` binaries:

| Target | sha256 (both) | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `x86_64-linux` | `cefcdffc3c6bf4c01c0e830dbed96104adc32d1c5ae7beca5361bcec053c4624` | 13,765,592 bytes |
| `aarch64-linux` | `e4f82d6e7883506ea987a993ebe95839204f0e7be26e0c4c06732da2b0053974` | 11,705,624 bytes |

## Not changed

- Unix-socket connects: `netConnectUnix` (`src/core/mcp_host/mcp_call_client.zig:72`, `src/core/terminal/native_session.zig:326`) has the same std retry on `EINTR`. It has not been seen to fail, and a Unix connect finishes in the kernel. Not changed.
- The test at `src/main.zig:4308` builds its own `Io` from `processIoOptions` and does not use the wrapper.
- A connect with a timeout still goes to std.

## Upstream

The std behavior is a separate bug in Zig 0.17.0. A draft of the issue, with a standalone program, is kept outside this repository. Nothing is filed.

## Docs

None.

title: Write traces as JSON Lines
body:
## Summary

- `/trace` writes `fx-trace-<time>-<random>.jsonl` in the temporary folder instead of a Markdown report. Each line is one JSON object with a `type` field. On macOS it is still copied to the clipboard, and the file is still created with mode 0600.
- The first line is an `fx_trace` header with `format_version` 1, the fx version and commit, and the time the trace was written. The last line is an `end` record that counts the records before it, so a reader can tell a whole trace from one that was cut off.
- Every section of the old report is now a typed record. Lists are a summary record followed by one record per item: problems, tool calls and web search calls, network turns and calls, model catalog events, compaction events, permission grants, MCP servers, renderer events, transcript entries, and debug log lines. Counts, durations, sizes, and flags are numbers and booleans, and each time has an ISO 8601 string and a Unix-milliseconds field.
- Values the Markdown report masked are still masked. Gateway error text, schema diagnostics, and request-shape text are now masked too.
- A tool call that did not succeed because an MCP server refused its parameters has a `cause` field naming the rejected arguments, in its `tool_call` record and in its problem's `call`.
- Text that is not valid UTF-8 is written with each bad byte as `\xNN`, so every string field stays a JSON string.
- The trace keeps every retained compaction event instead of the last 24, and debug log lines are no longer cut at 300 bytes.
- A last-shutdown report that is valid JSON but not an object is reported as `unreadable` instead of stopping fx.
- A time outside the years 1970 to 9999 is left out of every time field. A last-shutdown report with a very large `recorded_at_ms`, such as 9e18, stopped fx with an integer overflow when `/trace` formatted it. `main` has the same crash.
- The `/trace` completion text says the trace is JSONL.
- GitHub doesn't accept `.jsonl` attachments, so `README.md` now says to share the trace as a link from fx.sh/share. `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the bug report template say to share it as a link from fx.sh/share, which hides private data before upload, or to zip the trace file and attach the `.zip`. They don't suggest pasting the trace's text, because GitHub refuses an issue body over 65,536 characters and the trace of a one-turn session is already about 11 KB. On macOS, `/trace` copies the file itself, so they say to paste it on fx.sh/share rather than in the issue.
- The schema is documented in `src/core/app/trace_report.zig`, next to the writer, with the steps for adding a record type.

## Example records

One record of each main type, from a trace of a session that ran one shell command. The home and workspace paths are replaced.

```jsonl
{"type":"fx_trace","format_version":1,"fx_version":"0.0.16","git_commit":"a8182930a6b1","written_at":"2026-11-11T20:21:59.323Z","written_at_ms":1794428519323,"notice":"Private diagnostic report. It may include prompts, file paths, command output, and file snippets."}
{"type":"summary","os":"macos","arch":"aarch64","build":"Debug","model":"spacexai/grok-4.7","fast_mode":false,"permission_mode":"auto","workspace":"/Users/alice/projects/research"}
{"type":"problem","kind":"active_turn","processing":true,"stream_active":true,"queued":0}
{"type":"last_shutdown","status":"recorded","total_ms":1,"recorded_at":"2026-11-11T18:10:50.153Z","recorded_at_ms":1794420650153,"stages":[{"name":"terminal_released","step_ms":0},{"name":"transcript_loads_stopped","step_ms":1},{"name":"complete","step_ms":0}]}
{"type":"compaction","retained":0,"failed":0,"overwritten_before":0}
{"type":"network_call","at":"2026-11-11T20:21:52.236Z","at_ms":1794428512236,"model":"openai/gpt-5.6-luna","kind":"gateway","source":"parent","status":200,"duration_ms":1267,"response_bytes":31,"input_tokens":88,"output_tokens":44,"stop_reason":"stop"}
{"type":"tool_call","at":"2026-11-11T20:21:55.307Z","at_ms":1794428515307,"name":"shell","outcome":"succeeded","duration_ms":909,"source":"parent","args":"{\"action\":\"run\",\"command\":\"printf trace-probe-ok\"}","args_bytes":50,"result_preview":"{\"state\":\"completed\",\"exit_code\":0,\"duration_ms\":183,\"out","result_bytes":208}
{"type":"transcript_entry","at":"2026-11-11T20:21:47.633Z","at_ms":1794428507633,"kind":"raw","text":"𝒇x v0.0.16 · Run /help for commands"}
{"type":"end","records":43}
```

The `last_shutdown` stages and the `tool_call` result preview are shortened here. The `problem` record is from a trace taken during a turn.

### Before and after

The same scripted session, one `read_file` call against a local fake gateway, run once on `main` and once on this branch, so the times differ. On `main`, the last-shutdown and tool-call parts of the trace are these Markdown sections:

```markdown
## Last Shutdown
total_ms=42 recorded=2026-11-11T18:10:50Z
- terminal_released step_ms=1
- complete step_ms=0

## Tool Calls
### Local
last=1 succeeded=1 rejected=0 command_failed=0 tool_failed=0 runtime_failed=0 total=1ms
```
