title: Move running shell commands to the background when the user steers
body:
## Summary

- Steering typed while a shell command runs reaches the model within about a second instead of waiting for the command to finish.
- The command keeps running. Its shell result reports it as running under its session ID, with a note to read the steering first, so the agent can follow it with `interact` or end it with `stop`.
- Commands that finish within the first second still return their full result.
- Steering sent while the model is still writing a shell call lets the command start, then moves it to the background.
- A parent agent's steering into a subagent moves the subagent's running command to the background the same way. Subagent reports still wait for main's running command.
- Other tools, such as MCP calls and web fetch, still hold steering until they finish.

## Docs

`using-fx/working-with-fx`, Steering section: replace "While a tool or context compaction is running, fx applies the follow-up when it finishes." with "While a shell command is running, fx moves it to the background, where it keeps running, and continues with your follow-up. While another tool or context compaction is running, fx applies the follow-up when it finishes."

title: Stop a session's subagents when ACP switches to another session
body:
## Summary

- Switching the connection to another session with `session/new`, `session/load` or `session/resume` of another id, or `session/close`, stops the subagents the old session is running, as `/new`, `/resume` and `/fork` do in the terminal app. Their work ends as cancelled and owes no report.
- The next session no longer receives the old session's report as its own turn. Its client gets no update for the old session's tool call and no `delegation` hook event for the old subagent.
- A report that no prompt had taken before the switch is dropped from the queue, and fx's trace names it with `subagent_mail_dropped`. It stays owed in the old session's log, so reopening that session delivers it once.
- Reopening the old session posts no report for the stopped work, and its subagent list says the last work was cancelled. Before, the report was posted again on reopen.
- Loading the active session again under another `cwd` reopens it. Its subagents stop as a quit stops them. The report they owe now runs once, not twice: the host is joined, the reports it queued are dropped, and the reopened log posts them once. A message a child sent or a quiet note is in no log, so it stays queued, in order, and runs as a turn of the reopened session before the reports.
- A `libfx/new` that replaces a session stops that session's subagents and drops what they queued, as a switch does.
- Quitting and loading the active session under the same `cwd` behave as before.

What each kind of queued mail does:

| Mail | Switch or `session/close` | Load under another `cwd` | Load under the same `cwd` | Quit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Report with a work id | Dropped, traced. Stays owed in the old log, which posts it once when that session opens | Dropped, traced. The reopened log posts it once | Stays queued, runs once | Lost with the process. Stays owed in the log |
| Child message, quiet note | Dropped, traced. In no log | Stays queued, runs in order before the reports | Stays queued, runs in order | Lost with the process |

Not in this change: a message a child sends, as opposed to a report, that is dropped at a switch is in no log of the parent, so the old session cannot learn of it. Only the child's own log and the trace line have it.

Docs: [vercel-labs/fx-web#297](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx-web/pull/297)

title: Keep wait from blocking when a subagent's work ends with nothing to report
body:
## Summary

- `wait` returns when a subagent's work ends with nothing to report, however the start of the wait lines up with the end. That covers a work under the `never` rule, a work main stopped or closed, a user's turn on a subagent that owes no report, and a report that cannot be delivered and stays owed in the log. Before, a `wait` that began just as such a work ended stayed blocked until Esc unless something else arrived for main, and main's turn stayed open. Now main gets: "A subagent's turn ended without a report. Call status to see where things stand, or wait again."
- A subagent that main closes while the user is talking to it now closes when that turn ends. Before, it kept counting as working, so its close was never written, and a later `wait` with nothing else to deliver stayed blocked until Esc. Now that `wait` says: "No subagent is working and no message is waiting, so nothing more will arrive. Continue, or end your turn."
- What `wait` says is unchanged.
- The host gains a test-only hold between telling the owner that a work ended and clearing the child's busy flag. A test sets it with `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_SETTLE_HELD` and `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_SETTLE_RELEASE`, because that gap is too short to hit by timing: the test holds the host there, starts a `wait`, then lets the end go. libfx builds leave the hold out, and test builds use an inline hook in its place. Other builds read the two variables at each work end and use them only when both are absolute paths. The two older holds, for a start and for a stopped end, follow the same rule now: a relative release path crashed fx at the hold, and a relative held path wrote a marker file into the workspace and held the work for up to a minute.

## Testing

- Seven inline tests in `src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig` cover the end. Five hold the host in the gap and start a `wait` there: a work that owes no report, the parent's stop, the parent's close, a report the owner's sink refuses, and the user's turn. One starts a `wait` before the user's turn on a closing subagent ends. One checks that the close is written before main's `wait` is nudged: it holds the registry, waits for the close's entry on the host's closing list to carry its `settling` mark, checks that the nudge is not set yet, and checks that it is set once the close is written. A test in `end_test_controls.zig` checks that a relative path leaves a hold unarmed.
- Three E2E tests in `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/tui-host-switch.test.ts`: two start a `wait` in the gap, one with `fx ask` and one in the app, and one sets the start, stopped-end and settle holds to relative paths and checks that fx neither crashes nor writes a marker file.
- Checked on `a3a9aa588`, which is `d571b6a21` merged with `main` `e8aee092f` (Zig 0.17.1): `zig fmt --check src/` and `zig build` exit 0 and print nothing, and `check_deprecated.py` finds nothing in the three Zig files this change touches (0 removed, 0 deprecated, 0 to review). The 42 tests this change, #2059, #2075 and #2087 add (9, 18, 6 and 9) each have an OK line in the output of the built test binary (69 tests selected, with unnamed blocks), and 20 of 20 runs of that binary pass. The six E2E tests (this change's three, #2075's `a message to a subagent whose close is not written yet is refused`, and #2087's two) pass 3 of 3 runs each on Linux, and 3 of 3 on the macOS arm64 binary of this head built with `fx-cloud macos-build` and run on a Mac. The stop-message driver passes 3 of 3 runs (25 tests each), #2059's main-mail driver passes once (9 tests), and `sh tests/tla/subagent/check.sh` exits 0 with 51 `ok` lines, one for each config: the 48 of `main` (counted on `main` at `e8aee092f`) and the three WaitNudge configs. #2003's three, #2075's six and #2087's nine unit tests each have an OK line and pass 100 of 100 runs of the built binary. The unit runs use a local `build.zig` edit, not in this PR, that adds a test filter; each binary is built once and run in a loop. A full `zig build test --summary all` on this head passes 12179 of 12224 tests (32 skipped, 13 failed); on plain `main` at `e8aee092f` it passes 12170 of 12215 with the same 32 and 13, and every test binary compiles on both. The 13 failures are 9 test names (4 of them fail in two test binaries), and the names are the same on both.
- Merge with `main`'s #2075: it keeps a closing child on the host's closing list until its close is written, and marks the entry `settling` while one thread writes the close. The test of a user's turn on a closing subagent used to wait for the child to leave that list as the sign that the close write had begun, which no longer happens, so it ended in `CloseWriteNeverStarted` on the merged tree (20 of 20 runs). It now waits for the `settling` mark, and still checks that the nudge is not set before the close is written and is set after. This is its own commit after the merge commit. On `a3a9aa588` it passes 100 of 100 runs of the built binary. With this change's fix taken out (the two defers in `endUserWork` swapped, a sandbox-only edit, not in this PR) it fails 20 of 20 runs with `TestUnexpectedResult` at the check that the nudge is not set before the write, and none with `CloseWriteNeverStarted`.
- Merge with `main`'s #2087: it adds `Slot.ended`, which is set once a work's end is recorded and until the host chooses a next work (`Owner.markNext`), so a stop or close in that gap answers for what is true, and a test hold after the end hook (`FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_PUBLISH_HELD`). It does not change the order this change needs. Its one line on the host's end path is `markNext` in `nextOrIdleLocked`, in the branch where a next work was chosen and the child stays busy. It leaves alone what this change orders, the busy flag cleared and a closing subagent's close written before the nudge, and `Slot.ended` only changes what `Owner.stop` and `closeByUser` answer. The merge has two conflicts, both in text and none in the source. In `scripts/cli_shape_registry.json` the two rows of its publish hold and the two of this change's settle hold all stay. In the `subagent/` row of `tests/tla/README.md` the two sides edited different sentences and both edits stay: its gap sentence and its count, which the configs agree with (ten planted bugs and four configs of the code before the fixes, counted from the `stop-message*.cfg` files, without the two that plant an idle-note defect), and this change's WaitNudge sentence. #2087's nine unit tests and two E2E tests pass with this change (counts above).
- Three places settle a close: the end of a subagent's work (`workEnded`), the end of a user's turn on it (`endUserWork`), and `closeChild` itself when the subagent is idle at the close. Only the first two nudge main's `wait`. For a subagent that is already closing when its work or turn ends, that end is the only one that settles it, read from the code: `closeChild` returns at once for a subagent that is already closing, and no message or turn starts on a closing subagent. A settle that finds the entry already marked `settling` returns true and writes nothing; `main`'s test `a settle of a close that is being written leaves the write to the thread that has it` runs that second settle.
- `tests/tla/subagent/WaitNudge.tla` models `wait` against works that end with nothing to post. `wait-nudge.cfg` is the design, where `wait` always returns. `wait-nudge-today.cfg` is the old order, and `wait-nudge-mutation-check-first.cfg` is a planted bug. Both deadlock, as `check.sh` requires. The CI line for the subagent model job adds `wait-nudge`.

## Not in this change

- In the app, `wait` can still say nothing more will arrive while a report waits in the hand-off list until the next loop pass. That report is in transit where the quiet check cannot see it, so it needs its own change.
- A close can land just after the user's turn on a subagent clears its busy flag and before that turn settles the subagent. It can be main's close or the user's close from the agent list. Then `closeChild` finds the subagent idle and writes the close itself. The turn's settle finds that write under way and returns, and the turn nudges main's `wait` before the write is done. A `wait` that is waiting then returns "A subagent's turn ended without a report. Call status to see where things stand, or wait again." while the subagent is still in the registry, until the write returns. That text is true then, and a message to that name meanwhile is refused with `child_closing`. The window is a few instructions wide. A test with a hold that forces this order (the turn held after its busy clear and before its settle, and the close's write held) shows the early nudge in 20 of 20 runs. It needs its own change.
- A nudge that lands after `wait` registers and before it reads whether a subagent works stays set when `wait` or `awaitMailOrQuiet` returns because nothing works, and it ends the next `wait` at once, even while a subagent works. `main` has the same fault, and it needs its own change.
- The session-write, ACP prompt and close-write test controls (`src/core/session/write_test_controls.zig`, `src/acp/prompt_test_controls.zig`, `src/core/subagent/close_test_controls.zig`) have the same fault on `main`: a relative release path crashes fx at the control, and a relative marker path writes a marker file into the workspace. They need their own change.
- `src/core/subagent/publish_test_controls.zig`, the hold #2087 added to `main`, has the same fault: a relative `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_PUBLISH_RELEASE` makes fx panic in `assert` at the hold, and a relative `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_PUBLISH_HELD` writes a marker file into the workspace (the E2E test of relative paths above, with these two set as well, fails 3 of 3 runs on `a3a9aa588`; a sandbox-only edit). It needs the same check of two absolute paths, in its own change.

title: Sum fx ask and ACP prompt usage over every main turn
body:
## Summary

- `fx ask --json` `usage` sums every main turn of the run. When a subagent's report started a later turn, the JSON showed only that last turn, so the turn that sent the work was missing. For a run where main sends work (100 in) and answers (200), and the report starts a third request (400), main printed `{"input_tokens":400,"output_tokens":4,"cache_read_tokens":40}`; this PR prints `{"input_tokens":700,"output_tokens":7,"cache_read_tokens":70}`.
- The `usage` in an ACP `session/prompt` response sums every main turn of the prompt in the same way. For the same run main returned `{"inputTokens":400,"outputTokens":4,"cacheReadTokens":40}`; this PR returns `{"inputTokens":700,"outputTokens":7,"cacheReadTokens":70}`.
- A run or prompt that ends in an error, a refusal, or a cancel after several turns reports the turns before it as well.
- A run or prompt of one turn reports the same usage as before.
- Subagent usage stays out of both, as `--help` already says.

Not in this change: the ACP `usage_update` notification. It reports how much of the context window the last request used, not a total, so it stays as it is.

title: Recolor tables and hidden agents when the terminal theme changes
body:
## Summary

- Inline code and links in table cells change to the new theme's colors when the terminal switches between light and dark.
- An agent that was not on screen during the switch, such as another fx instance or main while a subagent is shown, shows the new colors when it comes back on screen.
- Assistant text that is still being paced out takes the custom theme's new colors, links included.
- With a custom theme that sets one color for several kinds of text, each kind changes to its own color in the other variant, for example red text and removed diff lines. In 256-color terminals this holds for at least two kinds that share one color.
- Links in the builtin themes change color on a light or dark switch.

title: Expect the catch-up flag on history debt a rewrite drops
body:
## Summary

- `main` fails six tests in `src/ui/transcript/runtime_tests.zig` on Linux and macOS: the history-debt tests from #1877 ("stable frame after a source rewrite …", "stable frame under an external clear …", "compatible stable frame without a replay range grants no owed rows", and "history debt a stable frame could not write is replayed by the next frame").
- Cause: #1877 and #1889 merged 13 seconds apart, and each passed CI without the other. #1889 flags the stable anchor a recovered receipt leaves when a source rewrite dropped rows the receipt owed. #1877's shared setup builds that same anchor and asserted it had no flag, so every one of its tests stopped at the setup.
- The setup now expects the flag. The six tests clear it before their frames, so they still cover an anchor whose owed rows no frame is asked to replay, the case #1877 guards. A new test shows that the flagged anchor replays the owed rows in its very next frame, with no held frame first. No runtime code changes.
- Each check still has a test that fails without it: removing #1877's rebase check fails its six tests, its catch-up check fails one, its replay under an invalidation fails one, and removing #1889's flag fails thirteen: the six from #1877, the new one, and six of #1889's own.

title: Treat empty optional fields of a subagent call as absent
body:
## What this changes

An empty string (zero bytes) in an optional field of a `subagent` call is now read as if the key were missing, for the fields in this table, which are fields the action takes. The decoder does this with one helper (`optionalFilledString` in `src/tools/agent/subagent.zig`), for a field written at the top level of a flat call or inside the `request` object:

| Action | Field | An empty string now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `instructions`, `report`, `model`, `effort`, `profile` | gives the call the result of the same call without that field |
| `status` | `agent` | lists every subagent, as `status` with no `agent` does, and its row reads as that of `status` with no `agent` (in `fx ask`, `checking subagents`; with the decoder change alone it read `checking`) |
| `wait` | `agent` | is ignored, and no longer writes the `wait ignored agent=...` trace line |

For a field in the table, the decoder drops the empty string before validation and planning run. Everything after it (validation, loading a named profile, resolving a named model, the closing check, the override check, the busy check) sees the same request as one with the key left out, so such a call gets exactly the result of the same call without that field. For example:

- A `message` with all five fields empty starts a new subagent, and a second one reaches it while it works.
- An empty `instructions` sent to an idle subagent leaves its saved instructions in place.
- A `message` to `parent` with all five fields empty is delivered.

On `main` the first of these was refused with `{"ok":false,"result":null,"error_code":"invalid_instructions"}`. One more case, before and after:

```
{"action":"status","agent":""}
main: {"ok":false,"result":null,"error_code":"invalid_agent"}
now:  the result of {"action":"status"}, for example
      {"ok":true,"result":"No subagents yet.","error_code":null} when there are none
```

Two other places that read the raw arguments of a `subagent` call and decide something from `agent` needed the same rule, so they read an empty `agent` of a `status` or a `wait` as none too:

- The row code, `subagentAction` and `subagentRoster` in `src/core/tooling/tool_presentation.zig`. It serves the transcript row, the `fx ask` line, the ACP tool title, and the line a saved result gives its row after a resume. With the decoder change alone, `status` with `agent: ""` showed `checking` with nothing after it, and the transcript row did not list the open subagents. It now reads as `status` with no `agent` does: `checking subagents` in `fx ask`, and the names of the open subagents in the transcript row. A session saved before this change that holds a refused `status` with `agent: ""` shows `couldn't check subagents` after a resume.
- The parallel grouping, `subagentTarget` in `src/core/agent/runtime/parallel_execution.zig`. It took a wrapped call with `agent: ""` to name a subagent called `""`, so two wrapped `status` or `wait` calls with an empty `agent` in one step ran one after the other, where two with no `agent` run together. A zero-length name is now no name.

With the end test hold (`FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_END_HELD` and `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_END_RELEASE`) keeping a closed subagent closing, a `message` to it with all five fields empty and the same `message` without them get the same answer, with `error_code` `child_closing`. On `main` the one with empty fields gets `invalid_instructions`.

## What does not change

A value that is present and not an empty string (a field of only spaces included) is read and handled exactly as on `main`, and `stop`, `close` and `message` still require a non-empty `agent`.

## Not in this change

- The tool description and parameter schema text (`src/builtins/tools.zig`) are not touched.
- There is no new field, flag, setting, error code or refusal text. Validation, planning and the subagent host do not change: `model_contract.zig` changes only in tests, and `tool_host.zig` is not touched. The row code now reads an empty `agent` of a `status` or a `wait` as no agent, as the decoder does, and the parallel grouping reads an empty `agent` inside a `request` object as no agent, for any action.
- An empty string or `false` in one of this tool's own fields that the action does not take (for example `message` on `wait`, or `report: false` on `stop`) was already skipped on `main` (`rejectOutsideAction`), and that is unchanged. A key that is not a field of the tool, and any field written beside a `request` wrapper, is still refused with `unknown_field`, even when empty. The test `decode ignores empty fields the action does not take` pins each case: `message` on `wait`, `report: false` on `stop`, `task: ""` on `wait`, and an empty `message` beside a `wait` wrapper.
- `subagentTarget` is unchanged for a flat call: it returns unknown for every flat call, so a flat call runs alone, as on `main`.
- In the fields of the table, a value that is not a string (`null`, `false`, a number) stays refused as `invalid_field_type`. The test `an empty agent on status or wait means no agent, and a required agent is still refused` pins it for `status` (`null`) and `wait` (`7`), and `decode rejects invalid creation overrides and report rules` pins it for `model` (`7`).
- `wait` still does not check its `agent`: the same test pins that `wait` accepts an `agent` of `""`, of spaces, and of `Not A Name`.
- Readers that show a call's raw arguments as the model sent them are unchanged, and decide nothing from these fields: the ACP `rawInput`, the libfx hooks' `argumentsJson`, the compaction projection, the history sent back to the model, and the trace's `in_flight_args`. The streaming label (`subagentStreamedAgent`) already read an empty `agent` as none.

## Testing

These tests fail on code without this change and pass with it. In `src/tools/agent/subagent.zig`:

- `an empty optional field on message means the field is absent, on every path`: each of the five fields, flat and wrapped, and all five together, decode to a plain message that plans as a new, idle, interrupted, running, or awaiting-approval subagent would plan one without the fields.
- `a message to the parent with empty optional fields is still only the message`.
- `a message still refuses what an empty optional field does not excuse`.
- `an empty agent on status or wait means no agent, and a required agent is still refused`.
- `decode ignores empty fields the action does not take`, which gained `status` with `agent: ""`.

In these decoder tests, the empty fields of `message` and the empty `agent` of `status` are tested both flat and inside a `request` object, and the empty `agent` of `wait` flat only. In `src/core/tooling/tool_presentation.zig`:

- `an empty field the decoder reads as absent leaves every subagent row as it is without the field`: for `message`, `status` and `wait`, flat and inside `request`, a call with its empty fields gives the same row in every row state, with and without a resolved roster, the same roster, and the same line from a saved result, as the call without them.

In `src/core/agent/runtime/parallel_execution.zig`:

- `a status or wait with an empty agent names no subagent, as one without the key`.
- `fuzzed subagent calls never run two calls to one subagent at once`: its generator now also writes a `wait` with an empty `agent`, and a seed of two such calls fails on the old code.

Three existing tests changed. `fuzzed subagent calls never run two calls to one subagent at once` gained the `wait` with an empty `agent` named above. `decode ignores empty fields the action does not take` gained `status` with `agent: ""`. `decode rejects invalid creation overrides and report rules` used `model: ""` for `invalid_model`; it now uses a model with a NUL byte, because an empty model is absent. The E2E helper `runStartGap`, which three other E2E tests use, gained an `emptyOptionalFields` option, reads its held marker only when the file exists, and takes the results of main's start and note calls from the first request that carries them, ahead of its report check. Behind that check, a report that reached main's turn first left both results empty, and before this fix the new test failed 37 of 50 runs on the macOS binary and 2 of 50 on Linux. The three other tests that use the helper passed 50 of 50 runs each on the macOS binary on `main`; in the two of them that capture the note's result, the report never came first in those runs. So this fix changes no result of theirs that was seen.

Two tests in `src/core/subagent/model_contract.zig` pass with and without this change. `an empty optional string is refused here, so only the decoder treats one as absent` pins that validation itself still refuses an empty optional string and an empty `agent`, so only the decoder treats an empty string as absent. `a message with no optional fields is planned on every path, and a present one is not` pins how planning treats a message without optional fields.

The E2E test `a message whose optional fields are all empty starts a subagent, and a second one joins its work` in `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` sends all five empty fields to a new subagent, then to that subagent while it works, and then `status` with an empty `agent`. It fails without this change.

title: Build the held history debt tests on an unflagged anchor
body:
## Summary

- `main`'s unit tests pass again. Six tests from #1877 build history debt with a recovering commit over a rewritten source, and their shared setup expected the anchor that commit leaves to have no catch-up flag. Since #1889, that commit flags the debt, so all six failed in the setup. The setup now checks that the flag is set, then clears it, so the tests still cover an anchor that owes rows without the flag, the state a recovery the flag does not cover leaves. No behavior changes.
- The tests still guard #1877's fix: taking out the rebase check in the stable plan fails all six, and taking out the catch-up check fails its own test.

title: Say that a subagent's session approval covers all agents
body:
## Summary

- A subagent's file prompt now offers "Apply + allow workspace file access for all agents" where it said "for this session". The Reveal variant reads the same.
- A subagent's file prompt for a folder outside the workspace now offers "Apply + allow file changes for all agents under <root>". "all agents" comes before the path, so a narrow row cuts the path and keeps the words.
- A subagent's command prompt now offers "Yes, and no agent asks again for this exact command", and its other tool prompts offer "Yes, and no agent asks again for this request".
- A subagent's MCP tool prompt now offers "Allow this MCP tool for all agents".
- The new wording shows wherever the subagent's prompt shows, on its own screen or lent to main's.
- The new file wording is 2 columns shorter than the old, so a subagent's file prompt still fits the 60-column minimum and its "allow" rows stay answerable. The command and request options are 4 columns longer and still fit, at 58 columns.
- Prompts for main's own requests keep their exact wording, including while main has open subagents.

A subagent's prompt no longer says "for this session" in these options. The approval still ends with the session, and the docs PR says so.

Not in this change: ACP's option "Allow for this session" is unchanged. A subagent's request does not reach an ACP client until #1722, and the wording needs the requester, which that PR adds.

Docs: https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx-web/pull/300

title: Refresh a quiet command's process tree less often
body:
## Summary

- A shell command that only waits uses far less CPU: once its process tree is quiet, the foreground supervisor refreshes the tree every 25 ms instead of every millisecond. On a busy Mac, a supervisor waiting on `sleep` went from about 3% of a core to under 1%.
- New and changing trees are still refreshed every millisecond, for the first 100 ms of a command and for 100 ms after a new process appears.
- A stop or a lost owner that arrives while the tree is quiet is noticed up to 25 ms later. From then on the supervisor refreshes every millisecond with the same grace period, and it never waits past a command's deadline, so timeouts start on time.
- Commands still finish as soon as they exit, because the target's exit wakes the supervisor at once.

title: Show what a subagent is for in the agent list while it has no title
body:
## Summary

- A subagent with no title yet shows what it is for in the agent list, where `new session` showed before: the first line of the instructions or task its parent started it with. This covers a subagent still on its first turn, one restored by `/resume` whose title was not saved, and a subagent's own subagent.
- A subagent with a title shows its title as before, and the rows of main and of other instances do not change.
- The agent list's search also matches what a subagent is for, whether or not its row shows a title. A row that matches only on that text keeps showing its title.
- Since #2024 on `main`, a working subagent's row keeps its title instead of showing its current call, so a match on the title shows while the subagent works, and so does a match on what it is for while the row has no title.

Not in this change: the terminal tab title and the statusline's session item show no purpose for an untitled subagent, because they draw a title without the list's escaping and would need their own; `fx sessions --live` lists subagents by name only, and a purpose there would be a new JSON field.

A title or a purpose with U+180E or U+061C, which the list does not escape, shifts its row's state column one cell to the left for each of them, and while the subagent works the call time is drawn in the wrong cells (`working 0s1` for `working 1s`). The list's shared escaping on `main` does the same for a title; this change sends the purpose through it and does not change it.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#301

title: Make a stop or close between two works of a subagent take effect
body:
## Summary

- A stop or close that lands as a subagent's next work is installed now ends that work before its turn begins. Before, the work ran in full although the answer said the stop had worked. In the interactive app a rare race can still begin the turn; see "Not in this change".
- The answer to such a stop or close counts the messages the dropped work carried, the same way it counts messages that were still waiting.
- The user's close of a subagent in that gap tells the main agent how many messages it dropped.
- The main agent's stop now also ends a turn the user started on the subagent's screen, or one its own subagent woke, when it lands as the work that turn waited for ends.
- The same gap held a second case: a turn that ends without reading a message that joined it keeps that message until the end hook queues it as the next work. A stop, close, or user close that landed in that gap counted nothing, and the hook then ran the message. Now the stop counts it and the hook drops it. A message sent after such a stop still starts the next work once.
- The user's own stop reaches the same slot. Esc on a turn the main agent did not start can land while the main agent's slot is between two works, and it counted nothing and left an installed work to run. It now counts and drops the slot's kept and installed messages, and ends an installed work before its turn begins.
- The user's close of a working subagent now counts the messages its turn had not read, as the main agent's stop does. One count function serves the stop, the user's stop, and both closes, so a message is counted once however many of them come.
- A stop after a work failed before its worker attached no longer counts the messages that work carried, which its failure report already named.
- A close that lands while a turn the main agent did not start is running is now written when that turn ends. Before, the turn's end left the closing child marked busy, so the close waited on a work that had already ended and was never written, and the child came back after a restart. `main` has the same defect.
- This PR contains #1920, which another PR of this work already carries through its own gate (see "Contains #1920"). `main` holds #1919, #1942 and #2014, which this branch carried before, so it has the fix of #2014.

## How the gap closes

The end hook arms the work it installs (`Owner.armNext`), under the host's admission lock. A stop or close either takes the lock before the install and drops the waiting messages, or after the arm and cancels the work. The slot no longer clears the stop flags after the hook returns. The user's stop takes the same lock first.

For a turn's unread messages, every stop counts the ones the slot holds that no earlier stop counted (`countDropped`). Before it queues the kept messages, the end hook asks `Owner.handOverLeftovers`, which applies the rule `slotMain` already used: a stop, user stop, close, or quit that came first drops them. Once the host queues them it counts them as waiting messages, so they are never counted twice.

## Tests

- Holds at each window: after a turn ends with messages unread and before the slot finishes the work, between the finished work and the end hook, and after the hook installed the next work. Each test lands a stop, the user's stop, or a close there and checks that the message does not run and the answer or the report counts it. A message sent after the stop runs once.
- A quit lands after a turn ended with a message unread and as the next work is installed, and with a message waiting or unread on a working subagent, and the message never starts.
- The main agent's close, the user's close and the user's stop land while the user's turn runs with a message waiting for it: the message is counted and never starts, and both closes are in the log once the turn ends. The user's stop of that turn with nothing waiting drops and tells nothing, and the next message starts.
- The main agent's close and the user's close land while a turn its own subagent's report woke waits for the work that ends: that turn is dropped and the close is written.
- A failure injected before the bind checks that a stop after a work that never attached counts nothing.
- `StopMessage.tla` has the ended state, the user's stop in the ended and starting states, and seven new planted bugs, each with its own mutation config. One of them, `close_leaves_kept`, breaks an invariant of this PR's own, `ClosingHoldsNoKept`: a closing subagent holds no message its slot kept from an ended turn or installed as its next work. It sits in `stop-message.cfg` and `stop-message-deep.cfg` beside `ClosingHoldsNothing`, which is exactly as `main`'s #2075 wrote it. There are 18 `stop-message-mutation*.cfg` configs in all (11 on `main` at `54a36f011`, 7 added here): 16 plant a bug in the stop and message rules, the "Sixteen planted bugs" of `tests/tla/README.md`, and 2 in the idle note. The count is the `stop-message-mutation-*.cfg` files, less the two whose bug is in the idle note (`note_after_take` and `names_busy`); on `main` the same count gives 9. `check.sh` names, for each, the rule that must catch it: `ClosingHoldsNoKept` for `close_leaves_kept`, `ClosingHoldsNothing` for #2075's `unmark_early`, `NoSilentLoss` for this PR's `leftover_uncounted` and `user_ended_uncounted`, and `StopHoldsForQueued` for its `late_rearm`, `leftover_gap`, `user_before_lock` and `user_next_runs`. The stop-message driver walks the real binary through the stop, the close, and the user's stop.
- The PR adds five test-only environment variables, registered in `scripts/cli_shape_registry.json` with job `test`: `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_RUN_HELD` and `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_RUN_RELEASE` hold the slot after a turn ended with parent messages unread, and `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_NEXT_HELD` and `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_NEXT_RELEASE` hold it after the end hook installed the next work, so the stop-message driver can land a stop, a close or the user's stop in those windows every time. `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_USER_STOP` names a request file that, while a slot is held there, stops the child as the user's Esc does, which `fx ask` cannot press. Each is off unless set to an absolute path. A host's owner keeps the hook that does the stop (`Owner.user_stop_hook`): `Runtime.create` writes only that field of its own owner, a hold writes its counter only once both of its variables are absolute paths, and the libfx artifacts leave the hook and every control out. A normal run writes no process-level variable.
- One file-hold type (`file_hold.Hold`) serves the end, run, next-work and start controls, and #1920's settle control. It owns the marker and release protocol (write `<held>.<n>`, then wait for `<release>` or `<release>.<n>`, for at most a minute), which for the start control is the protocol it had before; the start control keeps its own cancel flag and its own variables. One test hold type serves the inline tests. All 31 tests this PR adds to `tool_host.zig` build their host through one `StopFixture`; 4 of them are the quit tests, which set `torn_down` because the quit has already torn the host down.
- A test control is off unless every path it needs is set, not empty, and absolute. The old end and start holds on `main` had the same fault: an empty or relative release path made fx panic ("reached unreachable code") when the hold was reached, and an empty or relative marker path wrote the marker into the directory fx runs in, then waited up to a minute when the release did not exist. The shared helper fixes both for the end, run, next-work, settle, start and user-stop controls. Unit tests set each of the eleven variables (`FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_END_*`, `_RUN_*`, `_NEXT_*`, `_SETTLE_*`, `_START_*` and `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_USER_STOP`) to a relative path and to an empty string, and the hold ignores it.
- Two older tests are repaired here. Each read the registry once after `waitUntilQuiet`, while the host clears the busy mark a moment before the slot writes the close: `stop ends a subagent's turn without a report and drops what waits for it` and `an idle subagent closes at once, and its name then starts a new one`. On clean `main` (`bdc749963`) they failed in 360 runs under 12 parallel loops: 2 and 1 times in one measurement, 0 and 4 in a second one by the same method. They wait for the slot's end now (`waitForSlotEnd`). The count comes from a Linux sandbox with a local `build.zig` edit that adds a `-Dtest-filter` step: `zig build test-one -Dtest-filter=core.subagent`, then 12 parallel loops of 30 runs each of the built test binary (`$bin --cache-dir=./.zig-cache --seed=0x$i`), counting the `FAIL` lines of each run. Three more tests of that shape, the parent's close test, the user's close test and `trace children show each subagent's work phase, last outcome, and closing`, were repaired on `main` by #2003 (`7aec1f109`, with `waitUntilClosed`). This PR takes `main`'s version of them, byte for byte. On `0a317f81a`, the head of this branch, the three together with #2075's six unit tests passed 100 of 100 runs of one built test binary (a build filtered to those nine, with the same local `build.zig` edit). On `7cab1507a`, an earlier head, they passed 300 of 300 runs each, and they still passed with a 40 ms delay before `settleClose`, which was a sandbox-only edit and is not in this PR (those builds were filtered to each test).

## Contains #1920

This PR contains one other PR of this work: #1920 (`fazxes/nudge-parent-after-child-ends`, head `d571b6a21`, which holds `main`'s #2059 and #2075 and fixes the order in which the main agent's `wait` is nudged and the busy flag is cleared). It came in with its own signed merge commit, so the base stays `main` and the diff also shows its files until it lands. It merges first. `main` holds #1919, #2014 and #1942, and #2069, which repairs the time limit of the `TLA+ MCP models and drivers` job; this branch contains `main` at `54a36f011`, so all of them are in it, and so is #2075.

#1920 adds two test-only variables, registered in `scripts/cli_shape_registry.json` with job `test`: `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_SETTLE_HELD` and `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_SETTLE_RELEASE` hold the host after it has told the owner of a work's end and before it clears the child's busy flag and settles a close, so a test can start the main agent's `wait` in that gap every time. Each is off unless set to an absolute path.

On `0a317f81a`, the head of this branch, I ran #1920's tests together with this PR's, and none of them failed (Zig 0.17.1, a Linux sandbox). The unit tests are the 47 tests that this branch adds to `main`, which include those of #1920, 6 tests of `main` that its diff shows as removed and added again, and the 18 that #2059 adds: 71 named tests, each with an OK line in the output of the built test binary (the filtered build selects 98, with unnamed blocks), and 20 of 20 runs of that binary pass. The build is filtered with a local `build.zig` edit, not in this PR, that adds a test filter, and the binary is built once and run in a loop. That includes the three close tests of #2003 (see above) and #1920's probe, `a user's turn on a closing subagent writes the close before it nudges main's wait`, which holds the registry so the close write cannot finish, waits for the child's closing entry to carry its `settling` mark, and checks that the wait is not nudged before the close is written. #2075's six unit tests and #2003's three each have an OK line and pass 100 of 100 runs of one built binary, and #2075's E2E test (`a message to a subagent whose close is not written yet is refused`) passes 3 of 3 runs. The E2E tests of #1920 (two in `gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`, one in `tui-host-switch.test.ts`) and the one of #1942 that is on `main` now (`main's stop ends a subagent's open question`) each passed 3 of 3 runs. The stop-message driver passed 3 of 3 runs on the Linux binary (34 tests each), and #2059's main-mail driver once (9 tests). `sh tests/tla/subagent/check.sh` exits 0 with 57 `ok` lines for 57 `.cfg` files: 47 on `main` at `54a36f011`, 3 for #1920's WaitNudge and 7 for this PR's mutations; the list of verdict lines has one line for each file. On the macOS arm64 binary built from this head in the sandbox and run on this Mac, the 33 walks of the driver passed once and the 9 walks this PR adds passed 10 of 10 runs each (90 runs); the driver's TLC step does not run on the Mac, so TLC checked the kept traces afterwards in the sandbox and accepted all 123. None of the walks ends in `child_closing`: the driver waits for the child's closed line before it goes on. A full `zig build test --summary all` on this head passes 11935 of 11974 tests (27 skipped, 12 failed). On plain `main` at `54a36f011` it passes 11888 of 11927 with the same 27 and 12; the 12 failures are 8 test names (4 of them fail in two test binaries), and the names are the same on both. `acp.test.ts` as a whole file was run on `55e4ce0d5`, an earlier head, and not on this one: it had 205 passing and 1 failing test, `an attached folder whose rule file cannot be read is reported in the note, not in the instructions`, which fails the same way, 3 of 3 runs, on plain `main` at `8f013d250`. This round changed no line of that file.

Files, by whose they are. Only #1920's: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/tui-host-switch.test.ts`, `tests/tla/subagent/WaitNudge.tla` and its three `wait-nudge*.cfg`. Shared with #1920: `scripts/cli_shape_registry.json`, `src/core/subagent/end_test_controls.zig`, `src/core/subagent/start_test_controls.zig`, `src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig`, `tests/tla/README.md` and `tests/tla/subagent/check.sh`. All other files are this PR's: `src/core/subagent/file_hold.zig`, `src/core/subagent/managed_owner.zig`, the stop-message driver, `StopMessage.tla`, `StopMessageTrace.tla` and the `stop-message*.cfg` configs.

What each merge resolved:
- #1920 conflicted in five files. `end_test_controls.zig` keeps this PR's holds on `file_hold.Hold`. #1920's settle hold is a fourth `Hold`, `settle_hold`, beside `stopped_hold`, `run_hold` and `next_hold`. #1920's `holdFiles`, `usableHoldFiles`, `holdOnFiles` and `HoldFiles` are gone. Its three unit tests all stay: `a test build holds a stopped work's end only through its hook` is this PR's version of it, which reads `stopped_hold.count`; `a test build holds the host before it settles an ended work only through its hook` reads `settle_hold.count`; and `a hold is armed only when both of its paths are absolute` asserts through `file_hold.usablePath`, without the `.held` and `.release` checks of the removed `HoldFiles` type. `start_test_controls.zig` keeps this PR's version. In `tool_host.zig` the closing branch of `endUserWork` is the same code on both sides (drop what waits, clear the busy mark, return) and takes #1920's comment, whose last line adds that the owner's `wait` is nudged after the close; `endUserWork` has #1920's defer order and `finishTurnWork` returns `posted`; `startNextPendingLocked` is this PR's, which counts the messages it starts. `scripts/cli_shape_registry.json` keeps the entries of both, and `tests/tla/README.md` keeps this PR's `subagent/` row with #1920's `WaitNudge.tla` sentences added to it.
- #1919 conflicted in one block of `managed_owner.zig`. This PR had inserted `Owner.armNext` before `closeTree`, and #1919 had reworded `closeTree`'s doc comment to say the tree is also closed by a switch to another session. Both stay: `armNext`, then `closeTree` with #1919's comment.
- `main` (`1b006e531`, with #2003) conflicted in six blocks of `tool_host.zig`, all in test code. #2003 repaired three close tests with `waitUntilClosed`, the cause this PR repaired with `waitForSlotEnd`. The three tests, `waitUntilQuiet` and `waitUntilClosed` are `main`'s, byte for byte. `waitForSlotEnd` stays for the two older tests that only this PR repairs and for this PR's own tests. Counted by script on `55e4ce0d5`, 22 tests in `tool_host.zig` call it: those two older tests and 20 of the 31 tests this PR adds to that file. The helpers that conflicted by adjacency keep `waitForSlotEnd`, `waitUntilQuiet`, `waitUntilClosed` and `waitForBlockedOnUser`, in that order.
- A later merge of `main` (`6ddd5790a`) had no conflict. #2007 added compiled Python caches under `scripts/` and #2011 removed them, so none are tracked. Net of those, `main` changed since then the size ceilings in `scripts/pgso/`, one line of `AGENTS.md`, and the empty-reply fix in two TUI E2E files, one of which (`tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`) this PR also changes, in a different test. `main` changed nothing under `src/`.
- `main` (`c36d7b3d4`, with #2059) comes in through the new head of #1920, which holds it, and a merge of `origin/main` into this branch is then empty. The merge of that head conflicted in one block, the `subagent/` row of `tests/tla/README.md`: this PR's edits to the row and #2059's MainMail sentence are in different sentences of one long line, and the merged row keeps both, whole. `tests/tla/subagent/check.sh` merged without a conflict, and its list of verdict lines has 55 lines for 55 `.cfg` files, with none missing and none doubled.
- The new head of #1920 (`c06f4d875a9d`, which holds `main` at `8f013d250`) conflicted in two files. In `managed_owner.zig`, `main`'s #1937 added `UserWaiting` and `userWaits` before `Owner.start`, and this PR had changed `start`'s signature (the `unstarted` count). Both stay: `UserWaiting`, `userWaits`, then this PR's doc comment and the two-argument `start`. In `tests/e2e/acp.test.ts`, #1919's session-switch tests and `main`'s prompt-usage tests were added after the same test; both sets stay whole. The new head of #1919 (`fbf6b71fd800`) then merged without a conflict, and so did `main` at `4790dbf20`. `main` holds #2014, so the note that #2014 fixes the crash on a session switch is gone from this body: its fix is in this branch.
- `main` at `83f79696d` (with #1919, whose merge is the tip of `main`, and #2069, which repairs the time limit of the `TLA+ MCP models and drivers` job) came in through the new head of #1920, `c0e26af52389`, which holds it. There was no conflict, and `git show --remerge-diff` of both merge commits is empty. This branch has one merge base with `main` now; before, it had two, #1919's head and an older `main`.
- `main` at `54a36f011` (with #2075, which keeps a closing subagent on the host's closing list until its close is written) came in through the new head of #1920, `d571b6a21`. That merge, `af688a32c`, conflicted in five files, and `git show --remerge-diff` of it is 272 lines, all in them. In `tool_host.zig`, one block of `closeChild`: this PR's note of what a user's close dropped, then #2075's `.{ .id = owned }` entry. In `StopMessage.tla`, both sides' additions stay: this PR's phases `ended` and `installed`, its variables `startq`, `kept` and `stoppedQ`, its actions `Rearm`, `Fail` and `Hook` and its planted bugs, and #2075's phase `writing`, `Marked`, `QueuesMarked`, the action `WriteClose`, the op `write_close`, the bug `unmark_early` and the invariant `ClosingHoldsNothing`. The two models combine as follows: `EndStopped` of a closing child goes to `writing` and leaves what the slot holds as it was, `DoStop` and `DoClose` leave out `writing`, and `WriteClose` leaves those variables unchanged. `StopMessageTrace.tla` keeps both sides' op descriptions. In the stop-message driver, the walk keeps this PR's polling of the end hook and its note of whether the child was closing, then #2075's wait for the close to be written. In `tests/tla/README.md` the sentence that counts the planted bugs is counted again from the configs ("Fifteen" in the merge commit, "Sixteen" after the next commit). The next commit adds `ClosingHoldsNoKept`, `close_leaves_kept` and its config. #2075 changes how a closing child is listed until its close is written. This PR's stop and close tests, its walks and #2075's six unit tests all pass on the merged tree (see "Contains #1920" for the counts); I did not run a case of a message that starts a work in the gap before a close write, on either side.

## Not in this change

- If the subagent registry cannot be loaded or saved when a waiting or kept message would start the next work, the message is dropped with a trace line only and main is not told (`dropStart` in `startNextPendingLocked`). This is the same on `main` and needs its own change.
- The session-write and ACP prompt test controls (`src/core/session/write_test_controls.zig`, `src/acp/prompt_test_controls.zig`) and the close control that `main`'s #2075 added (`src/core/subagent/close_test_controls.zig`) have the same fault on `main`: a relative or empty path crashes fx at the control and leaves a marker file in the workspace. They need their own change.
- In the interactive app, a subagent's run is handed to the main loop before its cancel is checked (`postAndWait` in `src/core/app/app_agents_runtime.zig`). If the main loop takes the run in that moment, or a stop lands after the run is taken and before the child's worker takes its prompt, the turn begins and is cancelled within about 50 ms (`waitForCompletion`), so one model request can go out. In the first case the stop has already counted the work's messages as dropped. This is the same on `main` and needs its own change.

title: Add /loop to rerun a prompt on an interval
body:
## What and why

fx had no way to rerun a prompt on a schedule. Typing `/loop 1h <prompt>` matched no builtin, so the text fell through to any skill named `loop` in a shared skill root. A skill written for another agent harness armed a `sleep` loop whose output fx never reads, because the shell tool returns output only when the agent calls `interact`. That loop fired 21 hourly ticks and ran its prompt 0 times, with no error.

This branch adds a builtin `/loop` slash command to the interactive TUI. It reruns a prompt in the same conversation on a fixed interval until you remove it, the conversation changes, or fx exits. A builtin is matched before any prompt path, so a skill named `loop` no longer receives `/loop` and stays reachable as `$loop`.

This is a new slash command, so it needs a maintainer's approval per `.fx/skills/fx-cli-shape/SKILL.md` before merge.

## How

- `/loop <interval> <prompt>` arms a loop. `/loop` lists every loop with its interval, next run, runs, and failures. `/loop pause <id|all>` keeps a loop without running it, `/loop resume <id|all>` restarts any paused loop, and `/loop remove <id|all>` deletes a loop. The list says whether a loop is "paused by you" or "paused after 3 failed runs". `remove` matches the verb `/mcp`, `/skills`, and `/workspace` use to delete an item. The interval floor is 1m, the ceiling is 365d, a conversation holds at most 10 loops, and a prompt holds at most 4,000 bytes.
- Typing `/loop ` opens a menu with interval starters (`10m`, `1h`, `1d`), then `pause`, `resume`, and `remove`, each with the loops it applies to plus `all`. Each verb appears only when a loop can take it, and choosing a verb or an interval types a space and waits for the rest. Enter with the menu open after `/loop ` lists loops instead of submitting the highlighted interval, which still needs a prompt; built-in commands keep picking their completion on Enter.
- On each pass of the 8 ms UI loop, a due loop starts only when its agent is idle, using the same busy check as `/compact`, so a message you just sent goes first. A draft in the composer does not hold a run back. The first run starts as soon as the loop is armed, and `/loop resume` runs the loop at once. Later runs are due one interval after the previous one finishes, and missed intervals collapse into one run.
- Each run is queued on the worker's non-steering queue as the user's own request, opens with a `loop <id> · every <interval> · <prompt>` notice, and shows its prompt as a normal user card. A builtin command in a loop prompt, such as `/status`, reaches the model as text and does not run.
- A run that ends `failed`, or that cannot be queued, counts toward a pause after 3 consecutive failures, with a notice for each. A provider error, such as a rejected request, an expired sign-in, or exhausted credits, does not end the turn: fx shows its own prompt and the loop holds at that run until you act, then carries on.
- `/clear`, `/new`, `/reset`, `/resume`, and `/fork` end every loop, and the new conversation says which ones ended. Loop state lives on the conversation's `Agent` in memory only: nothing is written to the session log, so older fx versions can still open these sessions.
- The footer shows `1 loop` or `N loops` while the agent on screen holds loops.

The branch is one commit per task, `314988ac4..a27692fc0`. It touches 15 production files, adding about 1,140 lines including tests. Eight test files only change the pinned slash command count from 40 to 41.

## Verification

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `zig fmt --check src/` | pass |
| `zig test src/core/loops/loops.zig` | 21/21 passed |
| `zig build test --summary all` on `f58a02b8e` (merged with `main` `8256ef8d3`) | exit 0; the main test step ran 11205 pass, 2 skipped |
| `zig build` | pass |
| `scripts/check-agents-boundary.sh`, `python3 -m scripts.check_cli_shape`, `scripts/check-public-surface.sh` | pass |
| `bun test ci-shards.test.ts` | 11 pass |
| `bun test tui-slash-commands.test.ts -t loop` | 7 pass, including the arm-runs-at-once, `/loop` menu, and pause-then-resume tests |
| `bun test tui-slash-menu.test.ts` | 43 pass |
| `bun test` on `tui-slash-commands`, `tui-slash-menu`, `tui-startup`, `prompt-history`, `tui-input-navigation`, `tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle`, `tui-render-stress`, `tui-resize` | 269 pass, 3 fail. All 3 fail the same way on an unmodified `8b86172cd` build: `tui-resize` "a long assistant stream keeps every row and the collapsed group in order", and the API-key-gated `tui-slash-commands` "/settings opens the settings catalog" and "unknown and removed commands show errors" |
| `./zig-out/bin/fx` against a real provider | Two real `1m` runs with the marker and the reply, a draft that survived the second run, `/loop remove all`, `/quit` exit 0 with empty stderr, and `fx -c` showing no restored loops. On `9a48cf1e8`, `/loop 1h` ran at once and listed `next in 59m  runs 1`. On `19e35e0a8`, `/loop ` showed the interval starters and Tab on `10m` left `/loop 10m` waiting for the prompt. On `5effa653c`, arm, `/loop pause 1`, the list row `paused by you · /loop resume 1`, `/loop resume 1` running at once, and `/loop remove 1`, with exit 0 and empty stderr |

Review: ship, 0 findings applied, 2 deferred (nits).

Not yet checked by hand: the Enter race, `/loop` on a subagent's screen, a loop on a second instance with `/close`, and a run that waits for approval in `ask` mode.

## Risk and rollback

If a run started in the wrong conversation or a loop would not stop, revert the merge commit. Nothing persists, so a revert leaves no state behind. Until a release ships the revert, `/loop remove all` deletes every loop in a session.

## Docs

The fx.sh slash-commands page (`apps/marketing/content/docs/using-fx/slash-commands/index.mdx` in `vercel-labs/fx-web`) needs:

- In **Sessions and shell**, after `/compact`, add the row `/loop [<interval> <prompt>|pause <id|all>|resume <id|all>|remove <id|all>]`: "Run a prompt now, then again on an interval until you remove it. With no argument, list the loops in this conversation. See Repeat a prompt."
- After that table, add a **Repeat a prompt** section: the run-now-then-every-interval behavior, the `1m` to `365d` interval range, idle start, fixed delay, the 10-loop limit, the `/loop ` menu, `/loop pause`, the pause after 3 failed runs, `/loop resume`, `/loop remove`, provider errors holding the loop, and the commands that end loops.

Companion pull request: [vercel-labs/fx-web#315](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx-web/pull/315); merge it after this one merges and ships.

title: Keep a subagent's profile settings across restarts and resumes
body:
## Summary

- A subagent keeps the tools, MCP servers and permission mode its profile set when it started, through a restart, a resume in another repository, and an edit of the profile file. What the profile left out still follows the agent that started the subagent, live.
- An edit to a profile no longer reaches a subagent whose settings fx saved, even after a restart. That includes an edit that makes the profile stricter, such as removing a tool or changing its mode to `ask`. To give a subagent the new profile, close it and start it again. The profile's prompt is the exception, below.
- A mode chosen on a subagent's own screen still wins over its saved mode. Configured deny rules, the MCP servers that are connected, and the permission check on each call still apply as they are now.
- A session's saved profile is trusted the way its saved permission rules are. fx reads it back when its parsed content is what fx would write: the same keys in the same order, values fx can write, and a mode only on a user's own profile. The same content in another JSON spelling, with spaces or `\u` escapes, reads the same, and fx writes it back in its own form. Anything else is ignored, including a repeated key inside the block, a repeated `started_with` key, or a repeated key in a field fx does not read. Someone who can edit a session's log can now also change what a subagent saved in it may do. This was a choice.
- Spawn data that does not parse for another reason does not get that far. A repeated key in a field the child's own load reads (`agent`, `fingerprint`, `profile`, `report`, `by` or `purpose`) fails the load of the child list, and a log line cut short makes fx refuse the session. Both fail before the block is read, and the fallback to the profile's name does not cover them.
- A profile's prompt (`prompt.md`) and its `prompt` setting, which says whether the prompt is added to fx's own or replaces it, are not saved. fx reads both again by the profile's name from the folder of the source the subagent started in: `~/.fx/agents` for a user's profile, and `.fx/agents` in the repository fx runs in for a repository's. So after a restart or resume, an edit to either still reaches a subagent that exists, and a resume in another repository gives a repository profile's subagent that repository's prompt for the same name. A profile of the same name in the other folder, such as one the user saves later, neither takes the prompt away nor supplies its own. When the profile no longer loads from that folder, the subagent runs without a prompt, and the debug trace records it. When only `prompt.md` is gone, it has none. A built-in profile has no prompt.
- A subagent saved with only its profile's name loads that profile by name, as before, and is not saved later, so an edit still reaches it.
- When a subagent saved with only a name can't load its profile, the failure the main agent sees is `profile_unavailable: <reason>; Restore the profile, or close this subagent and start a new one, which loses its conversation`, instead of `admission: AdmissionFailed`. The reason names the profile, and the report ends with the usual sentence about earlier tool calls. It no longer advises keeping that subagent.
- A profile whose saved settings take more than 3072 bytes still starts a subagent. fx saves nothing for it, the subagent reads its profile by name, and the debug trace names the subagent, the profile and the size.
- A saved profile that fx can't read back, such as an unknown version, an unknown key, a mode on a repository's profile, or a repeated key inside the block, is ignored. The subagent reads its profile by name, and the debug trace names the subagent and says the saved profile was unreadable.
- A saved profile takes 24 bytes for fx's own `agent` profile and 129 bytes for a user profile with a mode, four tools and one MCP server. `main` saves none. The spawn line's data limit is 4096 bytes.
- v0.0.16, the latest release, opens sessions with saved profiles and ignores the new field. It has no profiles and drops the profile name as well, so after v0.0.16 sends a message to such a subagent, this build runs it with no profile and every tool, as v0.0.16 already does to sessions that `main` writes.
- `/fork` copies a subagent's saved profile with it.

Not in this change: the main agent's own profile on resume. It is still read again by name, so a resume in another repository gives it that repository's profile of the same name, and when the profile does not load, fx continues as `main` with a notice. This stays as it is: it is the user's own session, and fx restores it by name as the docs promise.

Not in this change: a new subagent's model and effort. fx holds them in memory until the subagent's first turn starts and saves them in its own preferences then (D34), so a subagent lost before that turn keeps its profile's tools, MCP servers and mode, but not its model and effort.

Docs: https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx-web/pull/302

title: Tell the model what to do after a refused subagent call
body:
## Summary

- A refused subagent call that used to reach the model as a bare code now carries one or two sentences that say what happened and what to try next. The `error_code` and the decision to refuse are unchanged. For example, `child_busy` was
  `{"ok":false,"result":null,"error_code":"child_busy"}` and is now
  `{"ok":false,"result":"The subagent is busy, and instructions can only be set while it is idle. Send the message again without instructions, or wait for its report and then send it with them.","error_code":"child_busy"}`.
- Instructions sent to a busy subagent, which is one working or waiting for an approval or the user's answer: the model is told that instructions can only be set while the subagent is idle, and to send the message without them or wait for its report and send them then.
- Wording change made when `main`'s #1937 landed. The first sentence of the `child_busy` refusal said the subagent was working. The refusal covers the phases `running` and `awaiting_approval`, and #1937 makes `status` name a subagent that waits on the user "waiting for an approval" or "waiting for the user's answer", so "working" was false for it. "busy" is true of every phase the refusal covers, and it is the word the tool already uses for that state. Before: `The subagent is working, and instructions can only be set while it is idle. Send the message again without instructions, or wait for its report and then send it with them.` Now: `The subagent is busy, and instructions can only be set while it is idle. Send the message again without instructions, or wait for its report and then send it with them.`
- `model`, `effort`, or `profile` sent to a subagent that exists: the model is told they are fixed when a subagent is created, and to send the message without them or close the subagent and start a new one, which loses its conversation.
- `stop`, `close`, or `status` naming a subagent that is not open: the model is told that no open subagent has that name, and sees the open names (the first eight, then a count of the rest).
- A bad `agent` name: the model gets the real name rule. `stop` or `close` of `parent` is told that `parent` works only with `message`.
- A call that fails validation gets the rule it broke: `message`, `instructions`, `report`, `model`, `effort`, `profile`, and a message to `parent` with other fields.
- A subagent that is closing, a full queue, a missing or unreachable parent, a call id reused with other content, and a turn the message could not reach get sentences of their own. A full parent queue says the parent has 64 messages from its subagents waiting, because the cap counts the messages of all its subagents.
- A message that would start a subagent past the 256 a session holds open is told the session is at its limit, and to close a subagent it is done with or message one that exists. It was a bare `host_failure`, and the code is the same.
- Any other failure that stops a subagent call in fx's host is told that fx hit an internal error, and to check `status`, try again, and do the work itself if it fails again.
- The transcript row of a refused call reads as before. Two other places now show the sentence. The full transcript (Ctrl+O) shows it in the raw result. ACP clients get the raw result as `tool_call_update` content. ACP shows only the first 200 bytes of the body, and `error_code` comes last, so a refusal longer than 200 bytes loses part or all of its `error_code` there. These are always longer: `child_busy` (218 bytes), `override_after_create` (264) and `host_failure` for an internal error (214). The not-open refusal is longer when the names in it are long, and never when no subagent is open. Refusals that already carried text on `main` are unchanged and are cut as they were when they pass 200 bytes, such as `unknown_model`, `ambiguous_model`, `feedback_capacity` and the decoder's `unknown_field` correction for a field that an action does not take (224 bytes or more). Refusals that had no text of their own were 51 to 64 bytes on `main`, so ACP showed their codes. Nothing in this repository, the SDK or the Mac app (`fxd-zig`) parses that cut text.

## How

- The new file `src/core/subagent/refusal.zig` holds one table: a union with one variant for each refusal code and cause (for example `invalid_agent` for a bad name and for `stop` of `parent`), and an exhaustive `switch` that gives each its sentence, so a refusal with no sentence does not compile. The host (`tool_host.zig`), the decoder (`src/tools/agent/subagent.zig`) and the provider's catch-all (`tool_runtime.zig`) build their refusal bodies from it. A test scans those three files for a code written as a string at a call site. Results that already carried their own text (`feedback_capacity`, `close_not_saved`, the model and profile failures, the decoder's corrections) stay where they are built.
- `model_contract.zig` gives `stop` or `close` of `parent` its own validation error, so it gets its own advice. The code stays `invalid_agent`.
- The not-open refusal reads the open names under the host's locks. The 256 limit is mapped where the host adds a subagent.
- Merged with `main` at `54a36f011`. `main`'s #2075 changed the type of the host's list of subagents being closed from ids to entries, and the test `every refusal the host returns tells the model what happened and what to do next` now builds that entry for its `child_closing` case.

## Testing

- `refusal.zig`: `every refusal carries one or two short sentences and its code` (every variant and cause has a sample, and its body is one short line with its code); `the host, the decoder and the provider name no code outside Refusal unless it carries its own text` (the scan); `a refusal says what to do next for the case it names` (exact sentences, including the open names); `each validation failure and each turned-away message maps to a refusal with its own code`; `a subagent at work and one waiting for an approval get the same refusal for instructions` (the phases `running` and `awaiting_approval` both get the one `child_busy` body).
- `tool_host.zig`: `every refusal the host returns tells the model what happened and what to do next` (16 scenarios on the real host runtime); `a refusal reaches the model as its code with the sentence that says what to do next` (exact bodies); `a name no subagent bears, with no subagent ever started, says there are none open`; `a message that would start a subagent past the session's limit says what to close, and closing one lifts it` (the refusal, a message to an existing subagent that still goes through, and a close that frees a place); `a parent queue that one subagent filled refuses another that sent nothing, and the sentence says whose messages it counts` (two senders on a real worker queue).
- `src/tools/agent/subagent.zig`: `every call the decoder refuses tells the model what is wrong and what to do next`.
- `tool_presentation.zig`: `a refusal's sentence for the model leaves its row's label as its code made it`.
- `model_contract.zig`: the existing `minimal request validation owns each action's intent` now expects the new error for `parent`.
- E2E, `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`: `a refused subagent call tells main what to do next in the result it reads` runs `fx ask` against the fake gateway and pins three exact bodies: instructions to a working subagent, `stop` of an unknown name, and a bad `agent` name.
- Run on `origin/main` at `09e5d4cd0`, the base of the first push, with only the tests added, the host and decoder walks and the E2E failed with the bare body. The limit test fails without its mapping, and the two-sender test fails with the old sentence. The other new tests were not run on `main`.
- On head `42f16eaf2`, with Zig 0.17.1 in a sandbox: `zig fmt --check src/` passes, and so does `zig build` after removing `.zig-cache` and `zig-out`. The 13 tests named above ran 20 times as one built test binary, and every run printed an OK line for each of them and no failure. The E2E test ran 5 times with no failure. The full `zig build test --summary all` passed 11900 of 11939 tests, with 12 failures in 8 tests that are not in subagent code, and no test binary failed to compile. The same 8 tests fail the same way on `main` at `54a36f011` in the same sandbox, where 11888 of 11927 passed. The difference of 12 is the 12 tests this change adds; a second run of the same tree counted one test fewer in its total.
- The wording was compared on three models before it was chosen. For `override_after_create`, the next call retried without the refused field or closed the subagent in 14 of 36 refusals with the bare code and in 25 of 36 with the sentence. Ending the turn to report the refusal to the user rose from 3 to 8 of 36 (3 to 7 of 12 on one model, 0 to 1 of 12 on another, none on the third). For `child_busy`, where models already waited, the next call was a retry, a wait, a status or a stop in 20 of 33 refusals with the bare code and in 19 of 31 with the sentence, measured with the sentence as it read before the wording change above.

Not in this change: the `shell` tool's `invalid_action_fields` error lists the fields to fix and carries no sentence. It is a different tool with a different shape, so it needs its own fix.

Not run on the built binary, though a model call can reach them: `no_parent` for a parent that cannot take the message, `host_failure` for an internal error, `child_cancelled` (only in a race while fx shuts down), `state_unavailable` (while fx shuts down, or after fx could not save the end of the subagent's last work), and `host_unavailable` (only if the host goes away between the offer of the tool and the call). Unit tests drive `child_cancelled`, `state_unavailable` and `no_parent` on the real host runtime, and the table's own test builds the body of each of the five and checks its code and the shape of its text, not its exact words.

Not run on the built binary, and no model call reaches them. For `invalid_json`, fx answers arguments that are not JSON before the decoder runs: on the binary such a call gets fx's own `tool_execution_failed`. For `caller_unavailable` for a caller that does not own the subagents and for `wait_unavailable`, this is by the code: every agent calls its own host and its own worker. For `caller_unavailable` for a caller that could not be identified it is by the code too: every place that offers the tool sets the caller's id with the host, and every subagent turn has its id. Unit tests drive `invalid_json` through the decoder and the not-owner and `wait` refusals through the host; the table's own test builds the body of the unidentified caller's refusal. For `child_unavailable` for a finished subagent and `child_not_persistent` this rests on the code and no run has tried to disprove it: a message finds a subagent only by `findPersistent`, which skips one-off subagents, and a persistent subagent goes to idle, never to finished.

title: Keep a held Backspace from closing an agent after it clears the list search
body:
## Summary

- Holding Backspace to clear the agent list's search no longer goes on to arm and close the highlighted agent once the search is empty. The presses that follow in the same run do nothing.
- Forward Delete follows the same rule for its own run, since it also takes text out of the search.
- Pressing any other key in the list, or closing the list, ends the run, even a key the list does nothing with, such as Ctrl+A or End. An arrow key and then two Backspace presses close an agent as before. Only a key fx does not use at all, such as F1, and the reports a terminal sends between key repeats leave the run going.
- Pressing Backspace twice right after a Backspace run emptied the search no longer closes an agent until another key is pressed in between.
- On a list nothing was searched in, Backspace still arms on the first press and closes on the second, held or not.
- A press the run leaves alone is written to the debug trace as `agents_menu_close_ignored`.

## Contains #1928

This branch contains #1928's head (`fazxes/show-subagent-purpose-in-list`, merged in with a merge commit), which carries `main`'s #2024, and its base stays `main`. Until #1928 lands, the diff here also shows #1928's ten files. Merge #1928 first. The two conflicted in `tests/tla/drivers/agents_menu/lib.ts`, and the merge keeps both sides there.

- This branch added the close key's run to the model's driver in that file (`run` and `pressed` in its state, the `CloseKey` type, and the steps that hold or repeat a close key), right above the comment on `SEARCH_LETTERS`. #1928 reworded that comment to say a search letter can be in an agent's name, title, or purpose. The result has the driver's close-key code and then #1928's comment.
- #1928's change to `AgentsMenu.tla` is a comment too, since the model leaves open which agents a text matches. The two meet only at the search box: the run starts when a close key is pressed while the search holds text, whichever rows match.
- One test, added with this merge, covers a search that only a subagent's purpose holds, cleared by a held Backspace: `a search that matches a subagent only by what it is for, cleared by a held Backspace and then some, closes nothing: the agent stays open and working`. The list returns to two rows with the auditor still highlighted and working, nothing is armed, and the four presses after the search emptied are left alone. On #1928's head `92e2421f5` alone it fails in 3 of 3 runs, at the expectation of two rows: `bun test tui-host-switch.test.ts -t 'matches a subagent only by what it is for'` in `tests/e2e`, with this branch's test file over that head's copy.

## Not in this change

- A held Esc in the list clears the search and then leaves the list. It acts on no row, so it needs no run rule.
- The other menus do not have the same pattern: `/resume`, the model picker, help, settings, skills, `/launch` and the MCP menu take the composer as their query, and act on a row only with Enter, Tab or the right arrow, so a held Backspace never reaches a row there.
