title: Retry sign-outs that the provider did not confirm
body:
## Summary

- When Codex, Grok, or Vercel doesn't confirm a sign-out, fx keeps its tokens where the login was saved, in a private profile file or, for a Vercel login on macOS, the Keychain, and the warning says fx will try again later.
- `fx logout` and `fx login` for a provider revoke that provider's kept sign-outs, and each TUI start revokes all of them in the background.
- fx deletes a kept sign-out once the provider confirms it, and after 30 days without sending it.
- A sign-out interrupted by a crash or a kill during the request stays kept and is revoked later.
- When a retry can't help, such as an issuer without a revocation endpoint, or the tokens can't be kept, nothing is kept and the warning promises nothing.
- Logouts started at the same time still revoke a login once.

The warning for a sign-out the provider didn't confirm, before and after:

```
fx logout: local Codex session removed, but remote revocation could not be confirmed
fx logout: local Codex session removed, but remote revocation could not be confirmed; fx will try again later
```

```
Warning: signed out locally, but the remote session could not be revoked.
Warning: signed out locally, but the remote session could not be revoked. fx will try again later.
```

When a failure can't be fixed by trying again, such as a provider with no revocation endpoint, nothing is kept and the old warning is shown.

## Design

- The tokens are kept before the revocation is sent and forgotten once the provider confirms it, so a crash or a kill during the request still leaves them for a retry.
- They are kept where the login was, with the same secrecy: a private file next to the Codex or Grok login, and the Keychain for an fx login on macOS. A marker file that holds no token tells a TUI start that something is kept, so a start with nothing kept reads no Keychain item.
- Each kept sign-out is leased to the fx that is sending it, until its request limit ends. Logouts started together, or a TUI start beside a logout, would otherwise send one token twice. A lease whose process is gone no longer holds.
- The retries run where fx already talks to the provider: fx login and fx logout for that provider, and TUI start on a worker. A timer or a background process would be new machinery, and retrying inside the logout would hold it and fail the same way while the provider is down.
- A warning alone gave no next step. OAuth token revocation (RFC 7009, section 2.2.1) tells a client that gets a 503 to assume the token still exists and retry later, and revoking a token twice is harmless.

Before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  logout["fx logout or /logout"] --> delete["Delete the saved login"] --> revoke["Revoke at the provider"]
  revoke -- "refused or no answer" --> drop["Warn; the token is dropped"]
```

After:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  logout["fx logout or /logout"] --> keep["Keep the tokens"] --> delete["Delete the saved login"] --> revoke["Revoke at the provider"]
  revoke -- "confirmed" --> forget["Forget the kept tokens"]
  revoke -- "refused, no answer, or killed" --> warn["Warn: fx will try again later"]
  later["Next fx login, fx logout, or TUI start"] --> retry["Revoke the kept tokens"] --> forget
  retry -- "older than 30 days" --> forget
```

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#304

title: List each subagent's usage in fx ask JSON
body:
Stacked on #1921. This PR's base is that PR's branch, `fazxes/sum-ask-usage-across-turns`, because it changes the same result sites and extends the same tests. It retargets to `main` once #1921 merges.

## Summary

- `fx ask --json` adds a `subagents` field that lists each subagent that did work in the request, in the order each first ran, with its `name`, session `id`, and `usage`.
- Each entry's `usage` has the same fields and null rules as the result's `usage`, so a subagent whose model reported no counts has null counts instead of no entry.
- The counts cover the request alone: a subagent reused after `--resume` shows only what it used in the new request, and a subagent stopped mid-turn shows the replies it finished.
- A request that ends in an error still lists the subagents that worked.
- A request in which no subagent worked prints the same JSON as before, with no `subagents` key.
- `usage` stays main-agent only and does not include subagent usage.
- `fx ask --help` describes the field. It says `fx session <session_id>/<name>` reads a listed subagent and prints the same `id`.

## How

- The subagent host keeps an in-memory ledger of what each subagent used (`src/core/subagent/usage_ledger.zig`). Only `fx ask`'s runtime turns it on (`fx ask`, and `fx pr --create`, which runs its prompt through it), so the interactive app and ACP keep nothing.
- `agent_adapter` notes a subagent in the ledger when its turn opens, and adds each reply's usage as it arrives. `fx ask` copies the ledger into its result once the run is over, and the JSON writer prints that copy as `subagents`.
- Why not each subagent's saved `usage`: that setting is the subagent's total over its whole life, so after `--resume` it also holds the subagent's earlier requests. One request's share would need every subagent's saved total read before the request and again after it. The ledger starts empty with the host, so it holds this request's usage and nothing else.

## Before and after

One run: main delegates to a subagent named `reviewer`, which answers. Main's three requests report 700 input tokens in all, and the subagent's reply reports 7000. Only the two fields this change concerns are shown; the rest of the result is the same in both. On the base, the #1921 branch:

```json
{
  "usage": { "input_tokens": 700, "output_tokens": 7, "cache_read_tokens": 70 }
}
```

With this change, the same run:

```json
{
  "usage": { "input_tokens": 700, "output_tokens": 7, "cache_read_tokens": 70 },
  "subagents": [
    {
      "name": "reviewer",
      "id": "_6QrItP4DnSR",
      "usage": { "input_tokens": 7000, "output_tokens": 70, "cache_read_tokens": 700 }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Testing

- `src/core/subagent/usage_ledger.zig`: `a ledger that is off keeps nothing`; `a ledger lists children in the order they first ran and adds each reply to its own child`; `a snapshot is a copy that later usage does not change`; `a ledger frees what it holds when an allocation fails`.
- `src/core/cli/cli_ask.zig`: `ask JSON lists each subagent with its own usage in the shape of the result's usage`; `ask JSON has no subagents field when no subagent worked`; and the existing `ask JSON usage sums every main turn of the run, however the last turn ends`, which now also checks the list and is named `ask JSON usage sums every main turn and subagents lists the work, however the last turn ends`.
- E2E, `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`, each against the fake gateway: `fx ask --json subagents lists each subagent in the order it first ran`; `fx ask --json lists a subagent that reported no token counts with null counts`; `fx ask --json lists the subagents that worked when the run ends in an error`; `fx ask --json has no subagents field when no subagent ran`; `fx ask --json shows a reused subagent's usage for this run only`; `fx ask --json shows a stopped subagent's usage for the replies it finished`; `fx ask --json lists a subagent stopped before any reply finished with null counts`.
- The help snapshot in `tests/e2e/cli.test.ts` has the new line.
- The two #1921 E2E tests `fx ask --json usage sums the turn that sends work and the turn its report starts` and `fx ask --json usage sums three main turns` now also check `subagents`. On the base, those two, the new E2E tests except `fx ask --json has no subagents field when no subagent ran`, and the help snapshot fail; on this branch they all pass.

Not in this change: when main closes a subagent and later starts another with the same name, the result lists both. `fx session <session_id>/<name>` then reads the newer one, and no command reads the older one, whose session stays on disk. The help line does not say this yet.

Not in this change: a saved request that stops for a permission it cannot ask for reports an empty `session_id`, on the base too, although its session is saved. Its listed subagents are then read through the session that `fx sessions` shows.

Not in this change: a `subagents` field on the ACP `session/prompt` response. ACP's `usage` stays main-only, as it is in #1921. The field needs a choice that is not made here: ACP has no place for it in the response schema outside `_meta`, and an ACP session's subagents outlive a prompt, so which prompt counts a subagent's usage is open.

## Docs

The `fx ask` page and the design reference change in vercel-labs/fx-web#305. Merge it after this change ships.

title: Give the model feedback after a malformed tool call
body:
## Summary

- When a model reply ends with Gemini's `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL`, fx sends the request again at once, with tools available, and tells the model that its tool call could not be read and did not run. Before, fx waited 1 to 30 seconds and sent the same request again, with no limit.
- The transcript shows "The model's tool call could not be read (provider reason: MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL). Asking it to try again."
- A second malformed reply in the same step asks the model for smaller calls with short arguments.
- A third malformed reply in a row ends the turn as failed, with a notice that names the provider reason. A later step starts the count again.
- A failed reply that started a provider web search resends with tools on and tells the model the search may have run. Before, the resend went with tools off, and Gemini answered each one with `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL`.
- The tool rows of a failed reply that started a web search settle as calls that did not run.
- A malformed reply to a resend with tools off stops the turn for review instead of resending it.

title: Show in status that a subagent waits for the user
body:
## Summary

Contains #1942 (`fazxes/turn-cancel-ends-open-question`, head `965c21eb2`), merged in with a merge commit; the base is `main`. Until #1942 lands, the diff here also shows its five files. Merge #1942 first. The change that lets main's stop end an open question is #1942's and is not this PR's; the message of commit `4ab6ba3bc` still describes it.

Files, by `git diff --name-only`: #1942 changes `src/core/agent/worker_runtime.zig`, `src/core/app/app_agents_runtime.zig`, `src/core/shared/testing_event.zig`, `src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig` and `tests/e2e/tui-host-switch.test.ts`. This PR changes `src/core/agent/worker_runtime.zig`, `src/core/subagent/managed_owner.zig`, `src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig` and `tests/e2e/tui-host-switch.test.ts`. Both change `worker_runtime.zig`, `tool_host.zig` and `tui-host-switch.test.ts`. Only #1942 changes `app_agents_runtime.zig` and `testing_event.zig`. Only this PR changes `managed_owner.zig`.

- `status` says a subagent is "waiting for an approval" while it waits for the user to answer a permission prompt, and "waiting for the user's answer" while it waits for the answer to a question: one it asked, one an MCP server asked, or the out-of-credits picker. It said "working". The picker was left out before and is counted now.
- Main's list of subagents says the same, dated as the bullet on main's list below says.
- A turn the user typed on the subagent's screen shows its wait the same way.
- In the app, the label in `status` ends when the user answers, declines, or presses Esc, when main stops or closes the subagent, and when fx quits. A stop ends a question's label because of #1942. In ACP and `fx ask` it does not end that way: see "Not in this change".
- Main's list of subagents is built once per turn in the app and in `fx ask`. A subagent that waits when the turn starts is listed as waiting `when this turn started`, and the row stays so until the turn ends, also when the wait ends before that. `status` gives the current state. A wait that begins during the turn shows in the list from the next turn. In ACP the list is built for each request, and its rows have no such words.
- In `fx ask` a subagent whose permission request needs an approval has nobody to answer it. Its row already read "waiting for an approval"; in a turn that starts while it waits, it now reads "waiting for an approval when this turn started". This was driven on the macOS arm64 binaries with the fake gateway, by a local script that is not in the repository: `fx ask --json` starts two subagents, one whose shell call waits for an approval and one that finishes, and the finished one's report starts main's next turn, whose request carries the list. The binary of `main` at `3fd4905af` gave `- alpha: waiting for an approval. For: ALPHA_TASK`, and the binary of `c319b76ba` gave `- alpha: waiting for an approval when this turn started. For: ALPHA_TASK`.

## How

- Each worker counts the waits of its running turn: `permission_waits` around the permission wait loop and `question_waits` around the question wait loop (`src/core/agent/worker_runtime.zig`). Every source of a question counts, the out-of-credits picker among them. `userWait()` reads the two atomics with no lock: an approval wins over a question, and null means no wait.
- `tool_host.zig` reads those workers in `userWaitsLocked` (the owner's works and the turns the user typed on a subagent's screen), and `childStateLocked` makes `awaiting_approval` or `awaiting_answer` of it while the subagent is busy, so a turn's end clears a wait. `status` prints that state. ACP and `fx ask` keep an approval in the registry as `awaiting_approval`, which `childStateLocked` already returned first.
- Main's list uses `ChildState.noteLabel(kind)`. `NoteKind` is `kept` for a turn id other than 0, which the app (`agent.worker.activeTurnId()`) and `fx ask` (`ctx.active_turn_id`) pass, and `fresh` for 0, which ACP passes. Only a waiting row of a kept list says "when this turn started". Neither the start nor the end of an approval or question wait reaches main during its turn, so a kept list shows each row as it was when the turn started. Only a waiting row says so, because it is the row main could act on wrongly: main could tell the user to answer a prompt that is already answered. A row that reads `working` while the subagent has begun to wait is the same as on `main`, and `status` shows the wait. `team_head` and `team_guidance` are unchanged, and `status` never carries the words.

## Testing

Unit tests, 21, each named once:
- `src/core/agent/worker_runtime.zig`: `a turn that waits for a permission answer says so until the wait ends, however it ends`; `a turn that waits for a question's answer says so until the wait ends, however it ends`; `an MCP server's question and the out-of-credits picker are waits for the user`; `a permission request and a question that wait together are both counted`.
- `src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig`, 17: `status says a subagent waits for an approval, and not once the user allows it`; `status says a subagent waits for an approval, and not once the user declines it`; `status says a subagent waits for an approval, and not once the user presses Esc on its screen`; `status says a subagent waits for an approval, and not once main stops it`; `status says a subagent waits for an approval, and not once main closes it`; `status says a subagent waits for an approval, and not once the user closes it`; `status says a subagent waits for an approval, and not once fx quits`; `status says a subagent waits for the user's answer, and not once the user answers`; `status says a subagent waits for the user's answer, and not once the user presses Esc on its screen`; `status says a subagent waits for the user's answer, and not once main stops it`; `status says a subagent waits for the user's answer, and not once main closes it`; `status says a subagent waits for the user's answer, and not once the user closes it`; `status says a subagent waits for the user's answer, and not once fx quits`; `only the subagent that waits for the user says so`; `a turn the user typed on a hosted subagent's screen shows its wait too`; `a row of a kept team note that waits says when the wait was true, and one of a fresh note does not`; `a kept team note says a subagent waited when the turn started after the wait ends, and the next turn's note does not`.

End to end, 5 tests in `tests/e2e/tui-host-switch.test.ts`: `main's status says a subagent waits for an approval, and not once it is answered`; `main's status says a subagent waits for the user's answer, and not once it is answered`; `main's status says a subagent waits for the user's answer while the out-of-credits picker is open`; `main's status says working for a subagent whose request waits for a sign-in, and main is told only the user can continue it`; `main's list of subagents says a wait began when the turn started, also once the wait is over, and the next turn's list says working`.

With the out-of-credits exception put back in `worker_runtime.zig` and the kept list's label left unmarked, on the tree of `c319b76ba`, 3 unit tests fail (`an MCP server's question and the out-of-credits picker are waits for the user`; `a kept team note says a subagent waited when the turn started after the wait ends, and the next turn's note does not`; `a row of a kept team note that waits says when the wait was true, and one of a fresh note does not`) and 2 E2E tests fail (the picker reads `payer: working`; the list's row lacks "when this turn started"). The sign-in test passes either way, because it pins what main is told.

Counts at `c319b76ba`, Debug, on Linux x86_64 unless stated:
- A filtered build of 62 unit tests, which holds the 21 above, ran 100 times with 0 failures. The count comes from a Linux sandbox with a local `build.zig` edit, not in this PR, that adds a comma-separated `-Dtest-filter` option to the `test` step: `zig build test -Dtest-filter='<the test names, comma separated>'`, then `for i in $(seq 100); do "$bin" || echo FAIL; done` on the built test binary.
- The five E2E tests ran 20 times each: 100 pass (`cd tests/e2e && FX_SOUND=0 bun test tui-host-switch.test.ts -t '<the five names>' --rerun-each 20`, after `zig build`). On the macOS arm64 build of `c319b76ba` they ran 10 times each: 50 pass (`FXC_LOCAL=1 FX_SOUND=0`, `--rerun-each 10`). macOS CI does not run `tui-host-switch.test.ts`, so the macOS runs are the only ones.

## Not in this change

- `fx sessions --live` still says working for a waiting subagent. It reads each session's log, which has no wait state, so a label there needs a new field in a public output.
- A request that failed and waits for the user, other than out of credits, still reads as `working` in `status`: an expired sign-in, a content filter, a message too long after one compaction, a crash loop. Main is told in its own message that only the user can continue it, and the app's agent list marks these `needs you`. A label for them in `status` changes the text main reads, so it is left. The sign-in case is driven on the binary in `tui-host-switch.test.ts`.
- A subagent in ACP or `fx ask` cannot ask a question: its tool context is not interactive, and only the app lets a subagent ask. Its permission request can wait, as above. #1722 (head `acb47e16e`) also edits `worker_runtime.zig` and `managed_owner.zig`, in other places than this PR; `git merge-tree` of this PR at `c319b76ba` and #1722 at `acb47e16e` reports no conflict in them.
- In `fx ask` and ACP, main's stop does not end a subagent's wait for an approval. `stopTurn` (`src/core/subagent/managed_owner.zig`) interrupts a turn that is not hosted and leaves its approval waiting; only the app hosts a child. This PR does not change `stopTurn`. In `fx ask`, with alpha's approval open for 2 s, main's stop left `status` at `alpha: waiting for an approval, in Running echo HI for 2s, reports final. For: ALPHA_TASK`, and `fx ask` was still running 60 s after main's fifth request. A close dropped alpha from `status`, and `fx ask` was still running then too. The macOS arm64 binaries of `main` at `3fd4905af` and of `c319b76ba` gave the same: two runs of each for the stop, one for the close, by a local script that is not in the repository. ACP was not driven here.
- Main is not told when a subagent starts to wait for an approval or a question during main's turn. Its row in the list kept for that turn reads as it did when the turn started, for example `working`, until the next turn, as on `main`; `status` shows the wait. A note to main when such a wait starts would be new text for main and a new way to deliver it, so it is left.
- A turn the user typed on a subagent's screen: the host marks the subagent busy (`started_by = .user`), so `status` says `working`, while the list kept for main's turn still says what it said when the turn started, for example `idle`. That is the same on `main` and unchanged here.

title: Keep a session's subagents running when ACP loads or resumes it again
body:
## Summary

- Loading or resuming the session that is already active no longer stops its working subagents. They go on, and a report that arrives afterward runs as a turn of the session's next prompt, as after `session/cancel`. Before, the reload stopped each one as interrupted and its report said that fx stopped it. The prompt that was running is still cancelled.
- A kept subagent runs beside everything a client can send, so what it reads of the session is set under `subagent_authority_mutex` and read under it once, when its turn starts:
  - The mode, the permission mode, the hook config and the MCP host: set by the reload in one locked block.
  - The model route, the credential and the model catalog: `session/set_config_option` (provider, model, effort, Fast, Ultrafast) writes them under the lock, and a subagent takes a copy under it when each of its turns starts and reads only the copy, its capability lookups included. A switch frees nothing a working subagent reads. It does not move a subagent that already exists to the new provider or model: that subagent keeps the ones it was created with, on the turn it is in and on its later turns, and a subagent created after the switch takes the new ones (run on `00cb07f35` with Zig 0.17.0, Linux Debug: 3 of 3 and 2 of 2). The credential refresh a subagent makes publishes under the same lock, and the web search runtime, which borrows the key and the model, is pointed at the new ones before the old are freed. The parent's own turns, its prompt turn and each report turn ([#2045](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/pull/2045), on `main`), copy the key, account and team under the same lock when they start, and send the copy. What they still read from the session is under "Not in this change".
  - The project context: the next prompt gathers it again and frees the snapshot, so a subagent holds a copy.
  - The catalog refresh that a load or a `session/set_config_option` reply makes is skipped while a subagent works. A provider switch replaces the catalog under the lock, which is safe because a subagent reads its own copy.
  - The reload's cancel sets the cancel flag and ends a kept subagent's pending requests to the client, such as an MCP question, cancelled, as `session/cancel` does. Both are atomic or under their own lock.
- A session with no working subagent swaps its MCP host for the new one, as before. A session with one keeps its host, because the subagent's tool context holds it, and takes the new server list in place. A server whose config is the same keeps running with its calls. A removed or changed one stops and ends its calls cancelled. After that, the working subagent's later MCP calls are refused on every server until its next work. The refusal of `toolbox run`, `toolbox open` (of a tool and of a server) and `toolbox search` now says the session's MCP servers changed.
- A subagent that waits on a permission request when the reload runs is stopped, as a reload always stopped it: in ACP its request reaches no client. Its work ends interrupted and its report says so. The other subagents go on.
- A reload that cannot take the new MCP servers names the cause in its error.
- Closing stdin while a kept subagent runs a shell command now exits. A reload makes that state ordinary, because it no longer stops the subagent. Before #2005's change, macOS builds of `74e62aa4b` with edits not yet committed aborted in 9 of 500 runs that reloaded and then closed stdin, and in the other 491 the process was still running 8 s after stdin close, when the script killed it; the 7 aborts of the build that printed a stack were the assertion that no operation is in flight (`managed_execution.Runtime.deinit`). The fix is [#2005](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/pull/2005), now on `main`; the test for closing stdin after `session/load` is this branch's own.
- A load that names another `cwd` reopens the session as before, and still stops its subagents.
- The MCP fixture server can hold a call until a file exists, for the tests.

### Two choices

- A provider switch replaces the model catalog while a subagent works. That is safe because a subagent reads only its own copy, and skipping the replacement would leave the client with the old provider's model list in the reply to `session/set_config_option`. The E2E test `ACP session/set_config_option switches the provider while a subagent waits at a model step, and the subagent finishes on the route it began with` holds a subagent at a model step during the switch.
- The catalog refresh that a load or an option reply makes is skipped while a subagent works, and the trace shows `event=model_catalog_refresh_skipped`. A subagent reads its own copy of the catalog, so a refresh frees nothing it reads and the skip is not needed for memory safety. It is kept as it is, so that a load or an option reply that only refreshes the list does not replace the catalog while a subagent works. A provider switch is different: it must replace the catalog, as the first choice says. Removing the skip would let a refresh run while a subagent works, a case no test here runs, and this change does not need it. Four E2E tests check the skip for `session/load` through the trace line: the three `ACP session/load with ... ends a subagent's call on that server cancelled, and its later calls are refused as stale` tests (a removed and an added server, a server changed in place, the only server removed), and `ACP session/load gives a session with no MCP servers its first ones while a subagent works, and the next work uses them`. No test checks the skip for an option reply, which calls the same function.

### Contains `main`

This branch contains `origin/main` by four merges, at `c36d7b3d4`, `dd6f896ca`, `83f79696d` and `c9d7bbffb`. `main` now holds [#2014](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/pull/2014) and [#2005](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/pull/2005), so the diff no longer shows their files. #2005 stops the subagents before the executions they run commands through are torn down, so `fx acp` exits when stdin closes while a subagent runs a shell command; before it, `main` hung there with no reload at all. #2014 makes `Owner.deinit` join every slot's thread before it frees any slot.

`main` also holds [#2045](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/pull/2045), the source of `TurnSignIn`, which copies a turn's sign-in; this branch takes that copy under the lock. This branch and #2045 each added `const secret = @import("../core/auth/secret.zig");` to `src/acp/prompt.zig`, 27 lines apart. Git merges the two without a conflict, and the merged file declares the name twice and does not compile. The first merge commit drops the second one. The second merge conflicts in `src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig`, where `main` and this branch each add functions after `closeTree`: `main`'s usage ledger functions and this branch's `interruptApprovalWaits`. The merge keeps both. The third merge brings [#1919](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/pull/1919) and merges without a conflict; see below. The fourth merge brings [#1872](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/pull/1872), which removed the `permission_rules` argument from `Catalog.snapshotAccessView` and `Catalog.snapshotToolNames`; the text merge is clean, and the last commit of this branch drops the argument from the three calls in its reload test in `src/core/mcp_host/model.zig`. [#2059](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/pull/2059), also on `main`, makes a queued mail turn wait until the finished turn is committed; only the app's two thread starters enable it, so ACP turns are unchanged by it.

[#1919](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/pull/1919), now on `main`, stops a session's subagents when the client switches to another session (`session/new`, `session/load` or `session/resume` of another id, `session/close`) or loads the active session under another `cwd`; this branch keeps them when the active session is loaded again under the same `cwd`. `src/acp/sessions.zig` chooses by the session id and by whether the request names another workspace (`workspace_binding.prepare` gives null for no `cwd` and for the current one). A switch calls `stopSubagentsForSwitch`: it closes the tree, joins the host, then drops the queued mail. A load under another `cwd` calls `stopSubagentsForReopen`: it joins the host without closing the tree and drops only the reports the log still owes. The same-`cwd` reload calls neither, nor `closeTree`, `disableSubagentHost` or a drop. #1919's 8 E2E tests and this branch's 14 reload tests pass together: 22 tests, 5 runs, 110 of 110.

### Queued mail across a load of the active session under the same `cwd`

The load does not touch the worker's queue, so mail queued for the session stays queued and runs once, in order, as turns after the next prompt.

| Mail | After this change |
|---|---|
| Report with a work id | Stays queued and runs once. Working subagents go on and queue their later reports too. |
| Child message (`message` to the parent) | Stays queued and runs once, before the reports. |
| Note a child's quiet command raised | Takes the child message's path, because `Runtime.noteChildQuiet` posts it as a message from the child. Read from the code, not run: no test queues one across a load. |

A queued report and a child message are pinned by an E2E test.

Same as before, and pinned by tests: an idle subagent keeps its conversation across a reload, and the turn's list names it. A session whose subagent host did not build when it opened gets one on a reload.

### Not in this change

- A kept subagent that asks for an approval after the reload waits until a cancel, as a working subagent does after `session/cancel`. [#1722](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/pull/1722) makes a subagent's request end with its prompt.
- `fx acp` on `main` still ends with SIGSEGV when a shell command that its turn left running writes output after the turn has ended. This needs no subagent, no stdin close and no reload, and it happens on Linux and on macOS. It is a separate fault. Neither #2005 nor this branch removes it, and #2005's text has the counts.
- A subagent that waits on a permission request when the reload runs is stopped, as before. #1722 lets a reload leave such a subagent running; remove `interruptApprovalWaits` then.
- A catalog refresh that a load or an option reply skips while a subagent works is not run again when the subagent ends. A refresh that was due stays due and runs at the next load, new session or option reply that finds no subagent working, and until then those replies list the catalog fx already has. Whether to run it when the last subagent ends is a product choice this change leaves as it is.
- A subagent's refresh that publishes a new credential frees the key, team and account in the session. The parent's model steps no longer read them: since #2045 on `main`, each prompt turn and each report turn sends its own copy, and this change takes that copy under the lock. The parent still reads them live in two places, read from the code and not reached in a run: the tool context's key, account and team that the permission reviewer's request sends (`AcpContext.toolContext` in `src/acp/prompt.zig`, `Context.admissionAutoClassifier` in `src/core/tooling/tool_runtime.zig`), and the start of the session title task, which copies them with no lock. The title read is on `main`; this change touches neither read. In 15 runs with a fake issuer, made before #2045 on `00cb07f35` and on `main` `3fd4905af` (Zig 0.17.0, Linux Debug), the subagent's 401 came after half a second (6 and 5 runs) or after 31 seconds (2 and 2). In every run the server-side refresh skipped as verified recently and did not publish while a parent's turn ran, so no free was reached. This change neither adds nor removes the reviewer or title reads, and keeps subagents working beside later turns in more cases.
- A subagent turn that starts while the next prompt gathers the project context copies the empty snapshot that the gather leaves until it stores the new one, because the gather runs outside the lock. That one turn runs without the project's rule files from the session start, and the subagent's next turn copies them again. This is read from the code, not run. `main` has the same window with no lock, after `session/cancel`. There, a subagent turn that is already running when the gather starts reads the freed snapshot, which this change removes.

## Testing

Run on `1f4edc30e` with Zig 0.17.1, Linux x86_64 Debug, unless it says macOS.

- `zig fmt --check src/` and `zig build`: exit 0, no output. `check_deprecated.py --review src/`: 20 deprecated and 556 to review, the same as on `main` `c9d7bbffb`; none new.
- Full `zig build test --summary all`, once: 11899 of 11938 passed, 27 skipped, 12 failed, none crashed, and no compile error in any test binary. Plain `main` `c9d7bbffb` gives 11895 of 11934 with the same 12 failed. The 8 failing test names are the same on both trees: tests of read-only folders and permissions that the sandbox user cannot meet.
- Unit tests this change adds or changes, with those of #2005, #2014, #2045 and #2059: 30 named tests, each line ends in OK. The filtered test binary (57 tests), run 20 times: 20 of 20.
- The two-thread test of the lock (`ACP turn sign-in is one whole credential while a refresh publishes beside it`): 20 runs each way, on the same tree with and without the two lock lines.
  - Without the lock: the Debug binary fails 20 of 20, and ThreadSanitizer (ReleaseSafe) reports a data race in 20 of 20. The race is on a field of the server state that one thread reads while the other replaces it; the frames are not symbolized.
  - With the lock: the Debug binary passes 20 of 20, and ThreadSanitizer exits 0 in 20 of 20 with no report. #2045's own unit test passes both ways.
  - The Debug failure without the lock, first run (the two lock lines are removed in this copy, so the line numbers are two lower than in the file). The capture faults inside the copy of the key while the publishing thread replaces it:

```
5/26 acp.prompt.test.ACP turn sign-in is one whole credential while a refresh publishes beside it...Segmentation fault at address 0x7f541c8a1e88
compiler_rt/memcpy.zig:162:17: 0x1a4231c in copyFixedLength (compiler_rt)
/vercel/zig-0.17.1/lib/std/mem/Allocator.zig:482:5: 0x110f90f in dupe__func_98 (std.zig)
    @memcpy(new_buf, m);
src/acp/prompt.zig:1083:39: 0x12b7b9d in capture (main.zig)
        const api_key = try alloc.dupe(u8, session.api_key);
src/acp/prompt.zig:6232:45: 0x12b8147 in runCapturer (main.zig)
            var sign_in = TurnSignIn.capture(alloc, self.state, &self.state.active_session.?) catch {
```

- E2E, 5 runs each: the 14 reload tests, the 3 stdin tests, the 3 switch tests and #2045's `ACP report turn sends the sign-in its first turn refreshed`: every run passed. The name pattern of the reload tests also matches three of #1919's tests, so 24 tests ran in all. The 8 tests of #1919 and the 14 reload tests alone, in one run each time: 22 tests, 5 runs, 110 of 110. The whole `acp.test.ts`, once: 225 pass, 13 skip, 1 fail, an attached-folder test that also fails on plain `main` `c9d7bbffb` in this sandbox (user `ubuntu`, uid 1000), where the file gives 211 pass, 13 skip, 1 fail.
- Reload, then close stdin while a subagent runs a shell command, 500 runs each way: Linux Debug 500 of 500 exit 0 within 2 s, and the macOS binary of this head 500 of 500; with no reload, 500 of 500 on both. No run printed to stderr. The same loop on plain `main` `c36d7b3d4`, before #2005 was merged, with no reload: 40 of 40 runs still running 8 s after stdin close, which the script killed.
- ThreadSanitizer (ReleaseSafe), 3 runs each: the same 24 E2E tests passed with no report; a report fails the test.

Not run on this head: the macOS unit tests and platform E2E (CI runs them), and the whole `acp.test.ts` under ThreadSanitizer.

title: Leave a subagent idle and usable when its work cannot start
body:
## Summary

Contains #1929 (head `0a317f81a`), which itself contains #1920. `main` holds #1919, #2014, #1942, #2059 and #2075, and this branch contains `main` at `7f76e8e52`, so they are in it. The merge of #1929's new head into this branch had no conflict, and `git show --remerge-diff` of it is empty. The base is `main`, so the diff also shows the files of #1929 and #1920 until they land. Merge #1929 first: it added the `unstarted` count to `Owner.start`'s signature and to `endUserWork`'s call of it, and this change builds on both. At `111e1b926`, this PR's own change is `scripts/cli_shape_registry.json`, `src/core/subagent/managed_owner.zig`, `src/core/subagent/start_test_controls.zig`, `src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig`, `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`, and `tests/tla/session_manager/` (`README.md`, `Subagents.tla`, `mutants.py`), and `src/core/subagent/refusal.zig`, which is `main`'s and gets one line. That is nine files, and the first five are also files of #1929.

- When fx has saved a message's work and cannot start the subagent's thread, it now ends that work as failed and answers the main agent that the start failed and the subagent is idle. Before, the answer was a generic host failure (`host_failure`), and the subagent stayed marked running with nothing running it, so every later message to it was refused (`state_unavailable`).
- When fx cannot start the thread and cannot record the end of that work either, the answer now says what the main agent can do. It reads, with the name and the cause filled in: `<agent> did not start: <cause>. Your message did not run, and fx could not reset <agent>: it refuses messages until fx restarts, and a close of it cannot be saved either. Send the work to a subagent with another name, and tell the user that <agent> needs an fx restart.` Before, it ended after "cannot be saved either." and named no next step.
- `start_failed` carries its own sentence, with the subagent's name and the cause, so it is in the list of such codes (with `close_not_saved` and `profile_unavailable`) in `main`'s test of refusal codes in `src/core/subagent/refusal.zig`.
- A message that waited for the user's turn and cannot start when that turn ends is now reported to the main agent as failed, with the cause, instead of vanishing.
- The same holds when fx runs out of memory marking the subagent busy, which also leaked the copy of its id.
- Opening the work of a turn the parent did not start (the user's turn on the subagent's screen, or one its own subagent woke) had the same fault: the work was saved first, and a later step that failed left an active work in the log with nothing behind it. The log entry is now the last step that can fail.

## How

- `Owner.start` (`managed_owner.zig`) runs after its caller has saved the work. Under `Owner.mutex` it creates the slot, copies the child id and appends the slot to `self.slots`. When the thread cannot start, it returns `error.ThreadSpawnFailed`, and its three `errdefer`s pop the slot from `self.slots`, free the id copy and destroy the slot before the mutex is released. They touch neither the registry nor the runtime's busy list, so the saved work is still active when `start` returns.
- `Owner.endUnstarted` ends that saved work. It holds the registry store's lock (`state_store.acquireLock()`, not `Owner.mutex`) while it loads the registry, finishes the child's active work as `failed` with the failure `start_failed` and the error's name, and saves the registry. Finishing clears the child's active work, so the child is idle and takes its next message. A report is owed only when the caller asks for one, the tree is not closed, and the child's report rule makes a failed work reportable. When the work cannot be ended it returns null and writes a trace line naming the child, the work and the stage. At the stages `state_load`, `work_id`, `state_finish` and `state_save` the registry could not be read or nothing was written, so the child stays marked running until fx restarts, and a close of it cannot be saved either (`close_not_saved`), because a close is written only for an idle child. A new host over the same registry recovers the work (`recoverInterrupted`), and the child then takes messages and closes. At `child_missing`, `no_active_work` and `other_active_work` there is no such work to end: the child is gone, has no active work, or runs another one. The two callers hold the admission lock from the save of the work to this call, so for them a null is one of the first four.
- Two callers use it, both under `Runtime.admission_mutex`. `admitAndStartManagedWork`, for a `message` call that starts a work, passes `owes_report = false` because the call carries the failure: `message` answers with the error code `start_failed`. The wording is `startFailedResult`'s when the work was ended ("<agent> did not start: <cause>. Your message did not run. <agent> is idle, so send the message again if it is still needed.") and `startFailedStuckResult`'s when `endUnstarted` returned null ("<agent> did not start: <cause>. Your message did not run, and fx could not reset <agent>: it refuses messages until fx restarts, and a close of it cannot be saved either. Send the work to a subagent with another name, and tell the user that <agent> needs an fx restart."). `startPendingAfterTurn`, for a waiting message that cannot start when the user's turn or a child's report ends, passes `owes_report = true`; when it gets null there, no report is posted: the message is dropped with a trace line.
- `WorkEnd.start_failure` is a static cause string from `startCauseText`: `fx could not start a thread for it`, `fx ran out of memory`, `fx is closing`, or the error's name. Only `endUserWork` sets it, for a waiting message that could not start. `Runtime.reportOutput` reads it and words the report as "The subagent could not start the work your message made: <cause>. It never ran. Send the message again if it is still needed." in place of a reply. That text does not say the subagent is idle: the report's `next` note says so, from `idleAfterEnd`, which reads the waiting messages, the open turn and any close after the text is built. It is null for every other end.
- `openTurnWorkLocked`, which opens the work of a turn the parent did not start, now appends the turn work and sets the busy mark first, and saves the log entry (`startTurnWorkInLog`) last, only when the work opens at once (`open_now`). A failure of that save pops the turn work and clears the busy mark if this call set it. Before, the entry was saved first, so a later failure left an active work in the log with nothing behind it.
- `markBusyLocked` copies the child id before it appends the copy to `busy`. The copy is now freed by an `errdefer` when the append fails; before, it leaked there. When the mark is cleared normally, `clearBusyLocked` frees it.
- `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_START_FAIL=<n>` is a decimal count, not a path or a hold. `start_test_controls.spawnFails` reads it, and `Owner.start` calls it after the slot is appended and before the thread would spawn; the first n such starts in the process return `error.ThreadSpawnFailed`. A value that `std.fmt.parseInt(u32, value, 10)` cannot read is ignored; that parser also takes a leading `+` and `_` between digits, so `+1` and `1_0` count as 1 and 10. Every fx binary except libfx reads the variable, the shipped `fx` binary included, as the other test controls do; it is registered as internal. In a libfx build `spawnFails` returns false at compile time, before the variable is read, and the `libfx.node` built from this commit does not contain its name. In unit-test builds the variable is never read; tests set `test_fail_spawn` instead.

## Tests

- A start that fails after its work is saved, and a sweep that fails each allocation of a message's start in turn, check that the subagent is working or idle and takes the next message.
- The same sweep over the opening of a user's turn work (`a user's turn whose work fails to open at any allocation leaves its subagent idle or working, then takes the next message`). On `111e1b926` it passed in 100 of 100 runs. With the save of the log entry moved back before the steps that can fail, as it was before this change (a sandbox-only edit of `8b2ab4ea5`, measured before `main` came in, 20 runs), it failed in 20 of 20, each at allocation 11 of the sweep's numbering, which starts at 0. That number belongs to this build and tree: an earlier tree failed at a different one.
- Two messages wait for the user's turn, the allocation that joins them fails so that the second still waits as the first starts, and every start fails: each report's idle flag is checked against its text. The first report is built while the second waits, so its flag is clear and its text does not call the subagent idle; the second report's flag is set.
- The parent's close, and the user's close, each landing after a failed start is ended and before its report is built: the report does not say the subagent is idle, and the next message to the name starts a new subagent. After the user's close its answer names the close ("The user closed the earlier reviewer, so this one starts with no history."); after the parent's close it is the plain "Sent to reviewer, ..." answer. These two tests run code in that window through `start_test_controls.test_failed_start_ended`, a variable that only inline tests set; it is absent from non-test builds and from libfx, and no environment variable sets it. The refusal of a resend by `child_closing` while the close is still pending is read from the code (`admitManagedWork`) and is not run by these tests.
- A message makes a new subagent, its start fails, and the allocation at each index of the call fails too (`a message whose start failed and whose end was not recorded says the subagent refuses messages until fx restarts`). At every index where the end of the failed start is not recorded, the answer is the `startFailedStuckResult` text above, the next message gets `state_unavailable`, a close gets `close_not_saved`, and a new host over the same registry takes a message and closes. On `8b2ab4ea5` the sweep has 27 failing indices, and 12 of them leave the end unrecorded. At each of those indices the sweep also checks, after the answer, what the failed close write leaves behind: the child is not on the host's closing list (`main`'s #2075 keeps a closing child listed until its close is written and takes it off when the write fails), the app has nothing to drop (`hasClosed()` is false), the trace does not call the child closing, a second close gives `close_not_saved` again, and a message gives `state_unavailable`, not `child_closing`. These checks are in their own commit; they pin where this change meets #2075. The sweep also checks the advice in the answer: with the stuck child present, a message to another name (`helper`) starts a new subagent, its work runs and a report for it reaches the owner, and `status` lists both names. It does not pin what `status` calls the stuck child (see "Not in this change"). Another test checks that the answer fits a 64-letter name with the longest cause `startCauseText` gives for the errors `Owner.start` returns, and a 100-character cause, in the buffer `start_failed_result_bytes`, and that the shorter text used when it does not fit says the same things without the names.
- A `message` whose start failed says the subagent is idle only while the busy mark is clear, nothing waits, no turn work is open and no close is under way, and `idleAfterEnd` agrees, for a child the call made and for one it left idle.
- Runs on `111e1b926` (Zig 0.17.1, Linux, Debug), with a local `build.zig` edit, not in this PR, that adds a test filter (`zig build test-one -Dtest-filter=<name>` builds the test binary once, and the binary is then run in a loop): each of the filters `a start that fails after its work is saved`, `a message that waited for the user's turn`, `a message whose start fails at any allocation`, `a user's turn whose work fails to open`, `a subagent whose` and `a message whose start failed and whose end was not recorded` passed in 100 of 100 runs. By the test names in `src/`, those filters select 1, 1, 1, 1, 7 and 1 named tests; the last is the sweep with the checks above. The 65 tests that this branch adds to `main` and the 18 that #2059 adds (83 named tests; 110 tests selected, with unnamed blocks) each print an OK line in the output of the built test binary, and 20 of 20 runs of that binary pass; the buffer test is one of them. #2075's six unit tests and #2003's three each print an OK line and pass 100 of 100 runs of one built binary, and #2075's E2E test (`a message to a subagent whose close is not written yet is refused`) passes 3 of 3 runs. The E2E `a subagent whose start failed is idle and takes the next message` passed in 3 of 3 runs, and so did the E2E tests of #1920 and #1942 (four in all), `main`'s E2E `a refused subagent call tells main what to do next in the result it reads`, and ACP's `ACP refuses a subagent profile that only the directory fx acp started in has`. The stop-message driver passed 3 of 3 runs (34 tests each), #2059's main-mail driver passed once (9 tests), `sh tests/tla/subagent/check.sh` exits 0 with 57 `ok` lines for 57 `.cfg` files (the 47 of `main`, 3 for #1920, 7 for #1929), and `sh tests/tla/session_manager/check.sh Subagents` exits 0. A full `zig build test --summary all` on this head passes 12126 of 12171 tests (32 skipped, 13 failed); on plain `main` at `7f76e8e52` it passes 12066 of 12111 with the same 32 and 13. The 13 failures are 9 test names (4 of them fail in two test binaries), the names are the same on both, and one of them, `core.workspace.capture_store.test.capture store: the object copy stops at the deadline, and a failed copy leaves the ref alone`, is `main`'s own. `main`'s test of refusal codes, `the host, the decoder and the provider name no code outside Refusal unless it carries its own text`, passes on this head; without the allow-list entry it failed, on the tree before that commit (`c1078467a`, this branch merged with `main` at `1ed36dddc`).
- Earlier runs, on `8b2ab4ea5` before `main` and #1929's new head came in, with a local `build.zig` edit, not in this PR, that adds a test filter (`zig build test-one -Dtest-filter=<name>` builds the test binary once, and the binary is then run in a loop, Debug, Linux): each of the filters `a start that fails after its work is saved`, `a subagent whose`, `a message that waited for the user's turn`, `a message whose start fails at any allocation`, `a user's turn whose work fails to open`, `each report of a waiting message that could not start`, `the parent's close that lands after a failed start is ended`, `the user's close that lands after a failed start is ended`, `a message whose start failed says its subagent is idle only while`, `a message whose start failed and whose end was not recorded` and `a test build holds a work's start` passed in 100 of 100 runs, and so did `core.subagent`, which selects named tests and unnamed blocks. With the report text as it was before this change (a sandbox-only edit of `8b2ab4ea5`, 20 runs each), `each report of a waiting message that could not start` and the two close tests failed in 20 of 20 runs each, on a report whose idle flag was clear and whose text said the subagent is idle; `a message whose start failed says its subagent is idle only while` passed in 20 of 20, as it pins what already held. With the not-ended answer as it was before this change (a sandbox-only edit, 20 runs), `a message whose start failed and whose end was not recorded` failed in 20 of 20. The E2E `a subagent whose start failed is idle and takes the next message` passed in 20 of 20 runs. `zig build libfx-napi -Dnapi-surface=core` exits 0, and the `libfx.node` it builds does not contain `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_START_FAIL`, which the `fx` binary does.
- A deterministic E2E runs the start failure through `fx ask`. `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_START_FAIL` is a test control and is registered as internal in the CLI shape registry. Only tests set it, and the shipped `fx` binary reads it.
- `Subagents.tla` has the failed start, and a planted mutant that leaves the work unfinished is caught by `NoIndeterminate`.

## Not in this change

- `status` and the idle note call the stuck subagent idle. With the child stuck, `status` says `reviewer: idle, reports final. For: first`, and the answer to a message that starts another subagent ends with `Idle subagents, each with its own context:` followed by `- reviewer: first` and `Give related work to the one whose context fits instead of a new name.` So that answer can point the main agent back to the subagent that refuses messages. I saw both in the sweep's unit test, at the indices where the end is unrecorded; the test does not pin them.
- A message to the stuck subagent then gets `state_unavailable`, whose text is `fx could not reach the subagent's turn, so the message was not sent. Call status, then send it again.` That advice cannot work until fx restarts, because `status` still says idle. The sentence is `main`'s, and it serves the other causes of `state_unavailable` too.
- Both come from `Runtime.childStateLocked` on `main`, which reads a child that the registry holds as running, with no slot running it, as idle: any child that is not on the host's busy list reads as idle unless it is interrupted, finished or waiting for an approval. `status`, the idle note (`idleOthers`) and the roster all use it. It needs its own change.
- A work's end that cannot be written to the registry (`Owner.finish` returns an error): the slot stays unpublished and later messages get `state_unavailable`. It needs a different fix, on the finish side of the slot.
- A waiting message that the end hook cannot install as the next work, because the registry cannot be loaded or saved, is dropped with a trace line and the main agent is not told. No work was saved, so nothing is stuck, but a report for it needs a way to name a work the registry never had.
- A waiting message whose start fails and whose end cannot be recorded gets no report: it is dropped with a trace line, the subagent then refuses messages (`state_unavailable`) until fx restarts, and a close of it cannot be saved (`close_not_saved`). In a scratch sweep of each allocation of `endUserWork` with one waiting message whose start fails (not in this PR), 13 of 39 indices leave it so on `8b2ab4ea5`.
- Making the close of a subagent whose work no slot runs succeed needs a change in `settleClose`: a close is written only for an idle child.
- The report of a failed start does not say that the user's close is under way when one lands at that moment; main learns of the close from the answer to its next message.

title: Read question options and read_tool_result requests sent as JSON text
body:
## Summary

- Some models write a list or object argument as JSON text, such as `"options":"[{\"label\":\"Yes\"},{\"label\":\"No\"}]"`. ask_user_question already read its `questions` batch from text but refused each question's `options`, and read_tool_result refused its `request` wrapper, so the call failed.
- ask_user_question now reads each question's `options` from JSON text, and the question opens with those options.
- read_tool_result now reads its `request` wrapper from JSON text. Its row label and the link to the row whose output it reads use the same `requestObject`, so the row says what the call reads, as it does for an object.
- `fx ask --json` names the question of an ask_user_question call whose `questions` is JSON text.
- Text of the wrong kind, an array or object encoded twice, and text nested deeper than 64 levels are refused with the same message as before.
- web_search's `allowed_domains` and `blocked_domains` stay as they are: the local web_search runtime is never ready in fx today, so the call never searches.

## Testing

- `tests/e2e/tui-decision-prompts.test.ts`: a question whose options are JSON text opens in the TUI with both options, and the chosen answer reaches the model.
- `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`: in the TUI, read_tool_result with `request` as JSON text reads the shell command's saved output and its row shows `output for "READ_TEXT_MATCH"`; `fx ask --json` names the question of a batch sent as JSON text. All three fail on main.
- Inline tests in `ask_user_question.zig`, `read_tool_result.zig`, `read_tool_result_presentation.zig`, and `cli_ask.zig` cover each refusal, the 64-level limit, and the default row label for request text too large to read.
- Fuzz: the `ask_questions_text` target also sends its bytes as one question's options, and the new `read_tool_result_request_text` target checks that decode and the row read the same request. Both ran for 300 seconds with no failure.

title: Speed up fx doctor and group its report
body:
## Summary

- `fx doctor` checks that each saved session file exists instead of reading and hashing it. On a profile with 352 saved sessions, one of them a 128 MB log with about 38,000 saved files, and about 16,000 sessions an older fx saved, plain `fx doctor` ran for more than 14 minutes on `main` before it was stopped, and finishes in about 7 s with this change.
- The saved-session checks, including the scan of sessions an older fx saved, stop at doctor's time limit, and the report says how many sessions it did not check to the end.
- `fx doctor --deep` reads and hashes every saved file of each session it checks, with no time limit.
- The session checks run while doctor waits on the provider, MCP, and gh checks.
- A saved file that several log lines name counts once in the damage check.
- On a terminal, doctor shows what it is checking on stderr, cut to fit one row, and clears those lines before the report.
- The text report starts with what doctor ran with, groups each check under a heading with aligned name and detail columns, and ends with a totals line. It uses color only on a terminal and respects `NO_COLOR`.
- On a terminal, a long value, check detail, or fix wraps at a space and goes on under its own column. Output to a pipe or file keeps one line per check.
- The text report shows the number of configured MCP servers instead of one `[doctor] mcp_server=` row per server, and no longer prints `auth_refreshable`. Each checked server keeps its own check line, and `--json` keeps all of these fields.
- The text report escapes control characters in the workspace path, as it already did for check details.

## Docs

- vercel-labs/fx-web#319 updates the troubleshooting page and the CLI table.

title: End a question that a turn cancel finds open
body:
## Summary

- Main's stop of a subagent cancels a question that subagent is waiting on: its own `ask_user_question`, or the out-of-credits picker after a failed request. Before, the question stayed open and the subagent stayed blocked until the user answered it, although stop said its turn ended.
- Main's stop of a turn the user typed on a subagent's screen does the same.
- While a run's cancel flag is set (main's stop, the user's close, or shutdown), the run's slot thread repeats the turn cancel every 50 ms in `waitForCompletion`. That repeat now ends a question too.
- Esc and Ctrl+C on a question, main's own turns, ACP, and `fx ask` do not reach the new code. Closing a subagent ends the same way.

The stop of an `ask_user_question` is driven end to end by an E2E test. The out-of-credits case is covered by a worker-level test only.

The tests wait for the asking thread with one shared helper, `setInTime` in `src/core/shared/testing_event.zig`, which the tests in `worker_runtime.zig`, `tool_host.zig` and `app_agents_runtime.zig` call. Its three tests run in `zig build test` through those files, so `src/main.zig` does not change.

## What each caller saw with a question open

| Caller | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main's `stop` of a subagent (`stopTurn`, hosted slot) | `stop` said the turn ended, but the question stayed on screen and main's later `status` calls kept saying the subagent was working. | The question closes, the turn ends cancelled, and `status` says idle. |
| Main's `stop` of a turn the user typed on a subagent's screen (`stopTurnWorkLocked`) | The question stayed open and the turn stayed blocked. | The question closes. |
| The run's slot thread, repeating the cancel while the run's cancel flag is set (`waitForCompletion`) | The repeat declined a permission request but left the question. | The repeat also ends the question. |
| Close of a subagent, by main or the user | The question was released when the app dropped the subagent's worker (`requestShutdown`). | The close's turn cancel ends the question first; the drop still follows. |
| Esc or Ctrl+C on a question, on main's or a subagent's screen | The question prompt answers the question itself. | Unchanged. It does not call `requestTurnCancel`. |
| Esc on main while it waits for a subagent | It cancels main's own worker only. | Unchanged. |
| ACP `session/cancel` | ACP never calls `requestTurnCancel`. It offers no `ask_user_question`, and an MCP server's question goes to the client as an elicitation request. | Unchanged. |
| `fx ask`, SIGINT | `fx ask` never calls `requestTurnCancel`. On a terminal it puts an MCP server's question to the user itself, and SIGINT sets its own cancel flag. | Unchanged. |

The other things a turn can wait on the user for: a permission request is declined by a cancel already, including one that waits on a file review, which a test now covers. An MCP server's question was already cancelled within about 20 ms by the app's own watcher, and a worker test now covers it. A request's sign-in wait is a flag wait that already wakes on the cancel flag. The out-of-credits question after a failed request is the case this fixes.

Not in this change: plain `requestCancel` and `requestInteractiveCancel` still do not end a question or a permission request. Their callers answer the prompt themselves (Esc and Ctrl+C on a question), shut the worker down next (`stopSet`, `stopChildren`), are commands that an open question prompt takes the input from (`/new`, `/clear`, `/resume`), cancel a submitted prompt that is still pending, or have no worker question to end (ACP, `fx ask`).

title: Show Token Pass features only on teams that have Token Pass
body:
## Summary

- At startup, fx asks the AI Gateway credits endpoint whether the team has Token Pass, once per run and team, and saves the answer for each team in `~/.fx/token-pass.json` so the next run knows it at once. An fx login is saved under its account, an API key under a hash of the key, and a Vercel OIDC token under the team and project its claims name.
- On a team without Token Pass, the model picker, the default model, Fast mode, and fx's own helper requests work as they did before Token Pass support. fx shows no Token Pass headings, tags, or notices, except when AI Gateway itself returns a Token Pass error.
- On a team with Token Pass, the model picker lists the Token Pass models first, under "Token Pass" and "All Models" headings.
- On a team with Token Pass, the picker no longer shows Fast mode for Token Pass models, and choosing one sets standard speed without the speed step.
- On a team with Token Pass, a new session starts on `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` at standard speed when no model was chosen, in the interactive app, `fx ask`, and ACP. The model is not saved as the user's choice, and a resumed session keeps its model.
- Without a saved answer, the app's first prompt, `fx ask`'s prompt, and ACP's `initialize` reply wait up to two seconds for the check. A model the user picks before the answer arrives keeps its place.
- fx takes the Token Pass models from AI Gateway's model list, which marks each model a team's pass pays for with `token_pass: true`, and keeps no list of its own. The picker group and tag, the hidden Fast mode, the speed step, and the `/fast` warning follow those marks.
- A model list with Token Pass marks also tells fx the team has Token Pass until AI Gateway answers otherwise in this run, in the interactive app, `fx ask`, and ACP. The start model and the picker do not wait for the credits check, and a failed check does not hide Token Pass.
- Auto mode reviews, session titles, the vision fallback, and compaction retries move to fx's Token Pass models only on a team with Token Pass, and only when the model list marks both the session's model and that model.
- The `/fast on` warning for a Token Pass model shows only on a team with Token Pass.
- The "Token Pass covers this model" notice after a model switch is removed.
- The hint for an API key scoped to Token Pass points at the Token Pass group in `/models` instead of listing models.
- A `token_pass` object whose balance AI Gateway could not read still counts as an active Token Pass. `/credits` and `fx credits` leave out the amount, and `fx credits --json` returns `"remaining": null`.
- Replaces the quiet startup check from #1961 and its switch to the Token Pass default once the agent is idle with this check, in the interactive app. The check keeps #1961's "Token Pass is active, so fx uses deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash. Change it with /model." line, now written once this run's check has finished and AI Gateway or the model list's marks said in this run that the team has Token Pass, while fx still has the session on the Token Pass default; a saved answer alone never writes it, and a model the user chooses never gets it, and #1961's sign-in offer line, team line, and credential epoch for `/credits` replies stay as they are.

## Design

**Startup check.** The credits endpoint answers for every team (vercel/ai-gateway#5510): a `token_pass` object for an active pass, `null` for none. The catalog's marks appear only for a team with a pass, so they cannot say "no", and a response that Token Pass served comes too late to pick the first model or the picker layout. So fx sends the `/credits` request in the background when the credential is known, through the same lookup `/credits` uses. In the interactive app it waits while an fx login needs renewal, as `/credits` does, and asks once the renewal is done. `fx ask` and ACP skip the request when the login has no token yet and keep the saved answer.

**Saved answer.** Without it, every run would start on the built-in default and change after the check, or wait for the check on every start. The file holds only hashed names (`token_pass.identity`: the first 16 bytes of a SHA-256 of the credential kind, its subject, and the team), so it holds no key or account ID. It keeps the 16 newest teams, which bounds its size (16 KiB at most) for a user who rotates keys. fx opens it only as an existing regular file, so a FIFO or device in its place cannot stall startup. A Vercel OIDC token renews often, so fx names it by its `owner_id` and `project_id` claims, which stay the same; a token without them is asked about for one run only.

**#1961.** #1961 asked AI Gateway the same question with a quiet `/credits` lookup after the catalog loaded, only in the interactive app and only when no model was chosen, and moved the session to the Token Pass default once the agent was idle. Two checks would send two requests and could switch the model twice, so this branch keeps one. It keeps this check because it also covers `fx ask` and ACP, saves the answer for the team so the next start knows it at once, and sets the start model before the first prompt instead of during the session. The quiet lookup mode of `credits_lookup` goes with #1961's check, since nothing else used it. #1961's Token Pass default tests now expect one check on every AI Gateway start; a chosen model and a resumed session still keep their model and get no line.

**Catalog marks.** vercel/ai-gateway#5675 marks the models a team's pass pays for in `/coding-agent/v1/models`, only for a team with an active pass, so fx reads them from the catalog it already loads and drops its own list, which went stale each time Vercel added a model. A catalog without marks shows no Token Pass group: AI Gateway then says the pass pays for none of its models, as for a BYOK-only team or a catalog loaded without sign-in. The marks also count as an answer for the team, under one rule that `token_pass_team` holds: an answer AI Gateway gives in this run (the credits check, `/credits`, a token-pass response, a no-pass 403) wins; until then, a catalog with marks says the team has Token Pass, over an answer saved from an earlier run. The app, `fx ask`, and ACP save the marks' answer under that rule, so a credits reply and a catalog that disagree cannot flip the saved answer between runs. `fx ask` loads the catalog before it picks the start model when it has no answer, and before it picks the title model; the turn reuses that catalog. ACP takes the marks from the catalog it loads during `initialize`. This follows the approach of #1956, without its fallback to a list in fx.

**Two-second wait.** Only when fx has no saved answer, so the first run on a team with Token Pass starts on the Token Pass default. A request that fails or is slow lets the prompt go after at most two seconds on the built-in default, and the trace logs it.

**Start model.** It changes only on a fresh main-agent AI Gateway session whose model nothing chose (`--model`, `FX_MODEL`, and a saved model all win), and only between the two start models. A pick with `/model` or the picker settles it for the run, so a late answer never moves the user's model.

**Process-wide team state for helper requests.** Permission reviews, titles, and the vision tool run on worker threads, and `fx ask` and ACP load the catalog through the capability resolver rather than the model cache. A process has one AI Gateway credential at a time, so `token_pass_team` holds whether the team has Token Pass and which models its catalog marks, behind a mutex, in a fixed buffer that any thread copies without allocating. The model cache publishes the marks of each catalog it loads, of which only AI Gateway's carry any, the resolver publishes AI Gateway catalogs only, and a credential or provider change clears them. The marks never set the answer by themselves; the owners do, under the rule above.

Before: every AI Gateway user got the Token Pass picker, notice, and helper models, and fx learned about the team only from `/credits` or a served response, for one run.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  start[fx starts] --> picker[Picker: Token Pass headings for everyone]
  start --> model[Default model: grok-4.7]
  credits["/credits or a token-pass response"] --> status[In-memory status for this run]
  status --> helpers[Token Pass helper models]
```

After: one answer per team, and the models its catalog marks, decide the picker, the start model, and the helper models.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  start[fx starts] --> saved["Saved answer for the team (token-pass.json)"]
  start --> check["Credits check in the background"]
  catalog["Model list with token_pass marks"] --> marks[Team's Token Pass models]
  catalog --> status
  saved --> status[Team status]
  check --> status
  check --> file[Save a changed answer]
  credits["/credits, a token-pass response, a no-pass 403"] --> status
  status --> picker["Picker: headings, no Fast mode on marked models"]
  marks --> picker
  status --> model["Start model: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, or grok-4.7"]
  status --> team["token_pass_team for helper requests"]
  marks --> team
```

Before and after, in the picker for a team with Token Pass and one without:

```text
Before, every team                       After, team with Token Pass        After, team without Token Pass
Token Pass  2                            Token Pass  2                      moonshotai/kimi-k3    1M context  Fast mode
  moonshotai/kimi-k3  Fast mode            moonshotai/kimi-k3                 deepseek/deepseek...  1M context  Fast mode
  deepseek/deepseek…  Fast mode            deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash       provider/fast-model   128K context  Fast mode
All Models  1                            All Models  1
  provider/fast-model  Fast mode           provider/fast-model  Fast mode
```

The notice after a switch to a Token Pass model is gone:

```text
Before: Token Pass covers this model: https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass
After:  (nothing)
```

`fx credits --json` when AI Gateway cannot read the balance:

```json
{"kind":"credits","balance":"12.50","used":"1.25","plan":null,"token_pass":{"remaining":null,"resets_at":"2026-12-05T08:00:00.000Z"}}
```

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#307

title: Load an ACP session's subagent profiles from its workspace
body:
## Summary

- In ACP, a subagent starts in the profile its session's workspace has, the directory a client gives as `cwd` in `session/new`, `session/load` or `session/resume`, not the one in the directory `fx acp` started in. A profile of the same name in `~/.fx/agents` still comes first, and `main` is always fx's own, as in the terminal app.
- A profile other than `main` that only the session's workspace has now works. One that only the directory `fx acp` started in has is refused with `profile_unavailable`, which names the profile, instead of starting in a profile from another directory; for `main` or `agent`, fx's own is used instead.
- A subagent saved with only its profile's name reloads that profile by name: `~/.fx/agents` first, then the session's workspace, then fx's own profiles; `main` is always fx's own. A resumed subagent whose settings were saved from a repository's profile reads its prompt from the profile of that name in the session's workspace, and runs without a profile prompt when that profile is missing or does not load.
- A subagent that an earlier build started in a repository's profile, and whose settings that build saved, keeps the tools and MCP servers it started with, which came from the directory `fx acp` started in when the session's `cwd` differed. Its prompt is now read from the profile of that name in the session's workspace, and it runs without a profile prompt when that profile is missing or does not load. Closing it and starting it again loads its profile as for a new subagent.
- In ACP, the current directory the model is told is the session's workspace root, where its commands already run, not the directory `fx acp` started in. The terminal app and `fx ask` are unchanged, since their workspace is the directory they start in.

Not in this change: ACP does not send the model the list of profiles, so listing them is separate work.

Not in this change: ACP reads its startup settings once at `initialize` from the directory `fx acp` started in. That includes project permission rules, the step limit and tool placement, so a session bound to another workspace keeps those. `workspace_binding.zig` states this for connection settings and permission policy, and changing which rules apply to a session is a permission decision.

Docs: https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx-web/pull/308

#1931 is on `main`, and the base of this PR is `main`.

title: Leave a fast variant out of the model picker when Fast mode runs it
body:
## What changes

The AI Gateway catalog lists a model such as `provider/model-fast` next to `provider/model`. When `provider/model` also offers Fast mode, the model picker shows two rows that run the same model: `provider/model-fast` labeled **Fast**, and `provider/model` labeled **Fast mode**. It is unclear which one to choose.

A catalog entry can now name the model whose Fast mode runs it in a `fast_variant_of` field. With that field:

- The Models menu leaves the entry out when the named model is in the catalog and offers Fast mode. To run it, choose the named model and pick **fast** in the speed step.
- The entry no longer takes one of the highlight slots at the top of the picker.
- The entry stays in the catalog, so `/model <id>`, `--model`, `FX_MODEL`, `fx models`, and a saved selection still work. ACP and CLI model lists are unchanged.

The entry stays in the menu when the named model is missing from the catalog or has no Fast mode, because its row is then the only way to run it. A `fast_variant_of` that is not a string, is empty, or names the entry itself is ignored.

The catalog does not send `fast_variant_of` yet, so the picker is unchanged until it does. `isGlmFastVariant` stays for now, because it keeps GLM fast models out of the highlights without the field. It can go once the catalog sends the field.

## How it works

- `src/builtins/gateway.zig` reads `fast_variant_of` into `ModelCatalogEntry`.
- `model_catalog.foldsIntoFastMode` decides whether an entry is left out, and `hydrateMenuSnapshot` in `src/core/app/model_cache_runtime.zig` applies it when it builds the menu rows. The cached catalog keeps every entry, which is why a session that names the model still resolves its capabilities.

## Verification

Built with Zig 0.17.0 on macOS arm64.

- `zig fmt --check src/`: passed.
- `zig build`: passed.
- `cd tests/e2e && FX_SOUND=0 bun test tui-slash-menu.test.ts`: 44 passed, 0 failed. The new test, "model picker leaves out a fast variant that Fast mode on a listed model runs", drives `./zig-out/bin/fx` in tmux against a fake gateway. It checks that the menu lists three of four models, that the kept variant reads **Fast**, that `/model <left-out id>` still switches to that model and saves it, and that stderr is empty.
- `zig build test`: the four new unit tests pass. 16 other tests failed on my machine, none in the files this change touches. 15 are `command_runner` and `command_effect` tests that pass with an empty `HOME`, because my shell profile writes to stderr. The last one, in `assistant_stream`, runs `zig` from `PATH`, which is an older Zig on my machine. CI is the check for the complete suite.
- `scripts/check-public-surface.sh`: passed.

## Docs

- https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/models, "Fast mode": after the paragraph that starts "The model picker labels a model **Fast**", add "The picker leaves out a model that always runs fast when Fast mode on another listed model runs it. Choose that model and pick **fast** in the speed step, or pass the full ID to `/model`, `--model`, or `FX_MODEL`."

title: Show failed and stopped on a subagent's row and footer
body:
## Summary

- A subagent that is not working says `failed` in the agent list when its last turn failed, and `stopped` when its last turn was stopped or cancelled, whether you stopped it, the agent that started it did, or fx quit. After a turn that completed, its row still says `idle`.
- The footer on a subagent's own screen says `failed` or `stopped` in place of `done` after such a turn, and `done` after one that completed.
- A new turn says `working`, and a later turn that completes clears the mark. A turn you type on the subagent's own screen counts, and the report to the main agent names the same end.
