- A restored subagent keeps it after a restart that resumes the session, and in a `/fork` copy. A turn that fx cut short by quitting reads `stopped`.
- A failed or stopped row sorts and counts as an idle one does (it has idle's urgency and tone), so it takes the place an idle row would, and nothing new asks for you. Instances and main keep their states.
- A subagent's record in `/trace` takes its state from the same function as its row, so it says `failed` or `stopped` there too. The comment that lists the states a record can say names them. Two E2E tests in `tui-command-permissions.test.ts` read that field, through one helper, and they assert only `idle` or `finished` for subagents whose work completed and `needs_you` for one that waits for the user, so they do not change; no driver, script, Mac app or the fx-web trace viewer reads it, and the docs name the field without listing its values. Unlike `fx sessions --live`, whose `state` is JSON output with a fixed set that tools read, a trace is a diagnostic report whose record also carries `last_outcome`.

## How it decides

The row and the footer read one field on the subagent, `last_end`. The app sets it when the subagent's own turn ends, through `workOutcome`. `endRun`, which ends a turn the main agent started, and the end of a turn you typed take their outcome from the same function, so in the app there is one mapping from a turn's end to its outcome. A unit test walks every end with and without a hand-off, and a second one in `main.zig` checks the row and the work's outcome for each.

The host's `last_outcome` would give the same answer in the usual case, because the host also registers a turn you type on the subagent's screen: after a completed turn from the main agent and a failed one that you typed, the row, the footer and the report to the main agent all say `failed` for that second turn (an E2E test checks the three). The agent list is built each time it is drawn, and the footer's label goes into each frame's render input, so the agent's own turn is the better source. Reading the host's record there would mean calling `listChildren` on every frame, which takes the host's locks, clones the registry (the host keeps it in memory) and copies each child's strings again. `last_end` is one field on the subagent, set when its turn ends, and the row and the footer read it as it is. A one-off child takes no typed turns, so its row and the host's record cannot differ there.

On a restore, `last_end` is seeded from the host's saved record when the app lists the restored subagents, which a resumed session and a `/fork` copy both read.

The interrupted outcome gets `stopped`. A clean quit in the middle of a turn is recorded as cancelled and reported to the main agent as "fx quit before it finished.": a unit test in `tool_host.zig` checks that text, and an E2E test checks that such a subagent reads `stopped` after a resume. A crash is recorded as interrupted and reported as "fx stopped before it finished."; a unit test checks that it reads `stopped`. A paused turn also reads `stopped`, and an interrupted turn that was handed off reads `done`, as the host already counts it.

## Contains #1928 and #1933

This branch contains the heads of #1928 (`fazxes/show-subagent-purpose-in-list`) and #1933 (`fazxes/held-backspace-keeps-list-row-open`, which contains #1928 as well), each merged in with a merge commit and both carrying `main`'s #2024, and its base stays `main`. Until they land, the diff here also shows their files. Merge #1928 first, then #1933, then this one. The three change the same agent list, and this PR carries what each meeting needed.

The diff against `main` is 40 files (`git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD | tail -1`; `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` lists them), by whose work they are:
- #1928 only (4): `execution.zig`, `managed_owner.zig`, `render_input.zig`, `sessions.test.ts`.
- #1933 only (19): `app_input_runtime.zig`, `binary-to-spec.ts`, and 17 files in `tests/tla/agents_menu/spec/` (`TraceAgentsMenu.cfg`, `TraceAgentsMenu.tla`, and the 15 `agents-menu*.cfg`).
- This PR only (7): `trace_report.zig`, `RowOrder.tla`, `TraceRowOrder.tla`, `row-order.cfg` and its three mutation configs.
- #1928 and #1933 (1): `AgentsMenu.tla`.
- #1928 and this PR (2): `tool_host.zig`, `agents_menu_presentation.zig`.
- #1933 and this PR (4): `src/main.zig`, `tests/tla/README.md`, `tests/tla/agents_menu/check.sh`, `mutations.json`.
- All three (3): `app_agents_runtime.zig`, `tests/e2e/tui-host-switch.test.ts`, `tests/tla/drivers/agents_menu/lib.ts`.

What the merges resolved:
- `main`'s #2024: a working subagent's row keeps its title instead of showing its current call, and the field that held the call is gone. It conflicted with #1928 in `titleOf`. #1928's head resolves it as the title, else what a subagent is for, else `untitled`, and changes its test of that order so that it no longer expects a call to come first. #1933 and this branch take that through their merges without a conflict.
- #1928, `tool_host.zig`: `ChildListing` and the literal `listChildren` builds keep both `purpose` and `last_outcome`.
- #1928's resume test, "after a resume, a restored subagent with no title shows what it is for in the agent list, and the search finds it by that text", quits fx while the auditor's turn is held, and it expected the restored row to say `idle`. A turn that fx's quit cut short reads `stopped`, so it now expects `stopped`, with a comment that says why. Git showed no conflict in that file.
- #1928, after a quit and a resume, a subagent whose first turn the quit cut short has no title yet, so its row shows what it is for and says `stopped`, and a search by that text finds it. A unit test checks that row at 80, 48, 40 and 34 columns with wide characters in the purpose.
- #1933, `app_agents_runtime.zig`: both branches added declarations in the same place before `AgentsMenu`: `LastEnd`, `workOutcome` and `completionOf` here, `CloseKey` there. All four are kept.
- #1933, `tests/tla/README.md`: both changed the `agents_menu/` row. It carries both texts, with its two counts taken from the merged files: twelve planted mutations of the agent list model (eleven on `main`, one from #1933) and five of `RowOrder` (two on `main`, three here).
- `check.sh`, `mutations.json`, `lib.ts`, `main.zig` and the E2E file merged without a conflict, and each side's lines are kept. `check.sh` has 21 configs here against 17 on `main` (`grep -c -E '^MC' tests/tla/agents_menu/check.sh`: 3 added here, 1 by #1933), and the spec has 17 mutation configs against 13: 12 `agents-menu-mutation-*.cfg` and 5 `row-order-mutation-*.cfg` here, 11 and 2 on `main` (`ls tests/tla/agents_menu/spec/agents-menu-mutation-*.cfg | wc -l`, and the same for `row-order-mutation-*.cfg`).
- One test added with this merge covers where this PR and #1933 meet (see Testing).
- #1902 has landed on main, and this branch contains it.

## Testing

New unit tests:

`src/core/app/app_agents_runtime.zig`
- `a subagent's last work reads as done, failed, or stopped, as its parent's report words it`: each outcome of the record gives its mark, and the footer's words are the marks' tags.
- `a failed or stopped row asks no more of the user than an idle one and sorts with it`: label, urgency, tone and busyness.
- `an agent's state says how its last turn ended only when nothing else claims the row`: a request for the user and a turn going outrank the mark.
- `a subagent's footer name says how its last turn ended once no turn is going`: `done`, `failed` and `stopped`, and the bare name while a turn goes.
- `a turn's end becomes its work's outcome in one place, which the row and the parent's work both take`: each end of a turn, with and without a hand-off.

`src/main.zig`
- `a subagent's footer says how its last turn ended until its next turn starts`
- `the agent list says failed or stopped on a subagent row whose last turn ended so, and the row sorts as an idle one does`
- `a subagent's record in /trace says failed or stopped as its row does`: the record's state and the list's row agree for a failed, a stopped and a completed subagent.
- `an instance's row keeps its states whatever its turns did`
- `a turn's end gives a subagent's row and its parent's work one outcome, for every end and hand-off`

`src/ui/footer/agents_menu_presentation.zig`
- `a failed or stopped subagent's state fits the state column, wide and narrow`: 80, 48 and 40 columns.
- `a stopped row that shows what its subagent is for keeps the state column, wide and narrow`: 80, 48, 40 and 34 columns, with wide characters in the purpose.

New E2E tests, in `tests/e2e/tui-host-switch.test.ts`, run against the fake gateway in tmux:
- `the agent list says failed on a subagent whose last turn failed and stopped on one the user stopped, and idle on one that completed`: two identical invalid `shell` calls make fx stop one subagent's tool loop, so its turn fails.
- `the footer on a subagent's own screen says failed or stopped after such a turn, and done after one that completed`
- `a subagent's next turn says working, and a later turn that completes clears its failed or stopped state`
- `a turn the user types on a subagent's screen decides its row and footer, and the report to main says the same`
- `after a restart and a resume, a restored subagent says failed or stopped as it did, one cut short by fx quitting says stopped, and the footer on its screen too`
- `a /fork copies each subagent with how its last turn ended, so the fork's list says failed, stopped, and idle as the source's did`
- `a failed or stopped row that a search finds keeps its label when a held Backspace clears the search and goes on, and nothing closes`: added with the merge of #1933. It searches for `broken`, which failed, and then for `cut`, which the user stopped, holds Backspace for the letters and four presses more each time, and compares the list with the list as it opened: the same four rows in the same order, each with its label, nothing armed, and the four extra presses of each run left alone, which it reads from fx's trace log.

Changed tests:
- `src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig`: `stop ends a subagent's turn without a report and drops what waits for it` also checks that the listing carries `last_outcome` as cancelled.
- `tests/e2e/tui-host-switch.test.ts`: #1928's `after a resume, a restored subagent with no title shows what it is for in the agent list, and the search finds it by that text` expects `stopped` where it expected `idle`.
- `tests/e2e/tui-host-switch.test.ts`: the team helper `withEndedSubagents` takes an option to write fx's trace log, which the new test reads; the six tests above do not use it.

Model: `RowOrder.tla` in `tests/tla/agents_menu` now models how a turn ends and a restart, with three new properties and a mutation config for each. CI does not run it. `sh tests/tla/agents_menu/check.sh` checks it, and each new mutation config is expected to be rejected by its property.

Checks, all at `c30d72d42` unless a line names another commit:
- The 13 unit tests above pass in `zig build test`: the exact-SHA `Build & Test`, run `43670939748`.
- The E2E tests above, with the two `/trace` tests that read a subagent record's state (`TUI trace names each subagent, its task, its state, and its turns` and `TUI trace shows a subagent whose model request failed`), pass in `E2E (deterministic)`, run `43670939748`. It runs `tests/e2e/tui-host-switch.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/tui-command-permissions.test.ts`.
- `sh tests/tla/agents_menu/check.sh` exits 0 and prints 21 `ok` lines.
- Each of these fails without the change. To repeat one, check out the commit, run `zig build`, copy this branch's `tests/e2e/tui-host-switch.test.ts` over its copy, and run `bun test tui-host-switch.test.ts -t '<test name>'` in `tests/e2e`:
  - the six new row and footer tests fail on `f0ca39670`, the `main` this work started from;
  - the test of a failed or stopped row and a held Backspace fails on `deb54269e`, which has the labels but not #1933's rule for a held key;
  - #1928's resume test fails on this head with `idle` back in the line that now says `stopped`.
- With `traceRows` made to write `"idle"` where it writes `@tagName(stateOf(app, child))`, `zig build test` fails the `/trace` unit test.

## Not in this change

- `fx sessions --live` prints a state for each subagent of a running session from `LiveState` (`working`, `idle`, `unknown`). That says whether a turn or a work item is open, it covers root sessions too, and its values are public JSON, so a new value would change a contract. It still says `idle` for a failed subagent. If the end should show there, it needs a separate field.
- The ACP and headless host decides how a run ends in its own code (`managed_owner.zig` and `finalRunOutcome` in `agent_adapter.zig`) and records a stop as cancelled or interrupted. Both read `stopped`, and those hosts have no agent list or footer, so there is no mark to disagree with.
- Instances and main keep their states. No new mark, column, reorder or reason text.

Docs: https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx-web/pull/309

title: Say that createFxAgent sessions emit no delegation events
body:
## Summary

- The SDK README, the observer hooks note, and the `FxHookEvent` declaration now say that a session made by `createFxAgent()` or `createFxEngine()` is not offered the subagent tool, so it never emits `delegation` events, and that ACP sessions that set `_meta.fx.hooks` do.

Not in this change: the `delegation` phase mapping, which reports a child that was interrupted or lost as `failed`, because changing it widens an SDK contract; and subagents on libfx sessions, because that is a feature.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#310

title: Test the history-debt hold on an anchor a recovery leaves unflagged
body:
## Summary

- Follow-up to #1923. The six history-debt tests from #1877 reach the hold by clearing the catch-up flag by hand, so nothing showed that a real sequence still reaches that state after #1889.
- A recovery from an invalid origin still leaves a stable anchor with history behind its viewport and no catch-up flag. A new test builds that anchor from that sequence, the one #1889's "a source rewrite over a receipt that owed nothing flags nothing" uses, and expects the next rewritten frame to hold: no rows, no scroll, no append, and history unchanged.
- Without #1877's rebase check, that frame scrolls rows that nothing writes, and the new test fails along with the six. All 267 `ui.transcript.runtime_tests` tests pass.
- The comment on `unflagHistoryDebtForTest` now says such an anchor still occurs. Tests only; no runtime code changes.

title: End a tty command when the user cancels it
body:
## Summary

- Cancelling a turn with Escape while a tty shell command runs now ends the command. Since #1918, any cancel during a tty command interrupted the turn but left the command running until fx exited, with or without steering.
- On main, the Escape tests with tty fail with "timed out waiting for interrupted command exit"; with this change they pass, with and without a pending steer.
- Adds tests for the steering yield grace when its test value is empty, negative, or not a number, and for a parent agent's steering asking a subagent's running command to yield while a subagent's report does not.

title: Hold hidden agents' work while a scrollback handoff is pending
body:
## Summary

- fx no longer crashes when a hidden agent has work while a session switch is still writing the previous transcript into scrollback. A hidden agent is main while a subagent is shown, another fx instance, or a subagent that is not on screen.
- Their events and paced text wait until the handoff's rows are written, usually a pass or a few, and are handled then, all of them and in order.
- A subagent run handed to a hidden agent in that time waits in the queue, as it already waits while that agent's turn is going.
- A subagent that its hidden parent closes in that time is dropped once the handoff ends, even when it is the one on screen.
- Quitting fx while a handoff is pending, as when the terminal window closes during a session switch, no longer crashes, and every agent's session is still closed.
- If a turn starts on the agent on screen during the handoff, such as one a subagent's report starts, the handoff gives way until that turn ends. Hidden agents keep working, and a turn that waits on one of them can finish.
- When a handoff gives way after it already pushed rows into scrollback, fx clears the screen and the scrollback and prints the transcript again, as after a resize, so no row shows twice once the switch hands the rows off again.
- The trace logs `hidden_tick_deferred`, `child_run_held reason=scrollback_handoff_pending`, `closed_drop_deferred`, `session_scrollback_handoff_cancel` with its reason, such as `shutdown` or `agent_busy`, and `scrollback_handoff_reset`.

An answer to a question or approval that a subagent lent to the instance's prompt still goes to it at once. It comes from a key press, and key presses wait while a session switch is pending.

title: Keep turns before a compaction through a resize until the next turn ends
body:
## Summary

- A resize right after resuming a session whose newest compaction came after its last turn keeps the conversation on screen and in terminal scrollback. Before, the resize removed every turn from before that compaction.
- The same holds after `/compact`: until the next turn ends, a resize prints the turns before the compaction again.
- Once the next turn ends, those turns leave memory as they scroll into terminal history, as before.

title: Read request wrappers sent as JSON text like objects
body:
## Summary

- Models sometimes wrap a call's arguments in a `request` field, and some write that wrapper as JSON text, such as `{"request":"{\"action\":\"run\",\"command\":\"ls\"}"}`. fx unwrapped a wrapper that is an object for shell, and replayed a wrapped read_tool_result call with its top-level arguments, but a text wrapper got neither: a shell call got a correction and never ran, and history replayed the read as it was sent.
- A shell call whose wrapper is JSON text now runs. It is stored and admitted with its top-level arguments, so permission rules and reviews see the real command, and a deny rule stops it as it stops a flat call.
- History now replays a read_tool_result call whose wrapper was JSON text with its top-level arguments.
- Admission's reload check, the shell wait label, and `fx ask --json`'s shell action read a text wrapper like an object. A shell grant no longer applies to a reload call whose wrapper is text.
- Shell's correction path reads a text wrapper with the 64-level limit, so deeper text is refused without being read.
- `unwrapRequest` moves from the read_tool_result row to `tool_args`, and every reader of a request wrapper uses it. subagent's wrapper is unchanged.

## Testing

- `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`: a shell call whose wrapper is JSON text runs its command; a text wrapper beside another field still gets the correction with its `retry_with`, and 300-level text gets one without; the TUI read_tool_result test now also checks that history replays the read with top-level arguments. The run and replay tests fail on main.
- `tests/e2e/permission-errors.test.ts`: a deny rule on the command stops a shell call whose wrapper is JSON text, with `tool_permission_denied` and no file written.
- The full `tests/e2e/tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`, whose shell calls go through the changed intake, passes.
- Inline tests cover each reader. Fuzz: the new `request_wrapper_text` target checks that history replay and shell intake unwrap exactly the wrappers `tool_args` reads; it ran 300 seconds with no failure. The intake, admission, and wait-label tests also pass under ThreadSanitizer (`-Dsanitize-thread=true`), run with a local test filter in `build.zig` that is not part of this change.

## Code move

`requestObject` moves from `src/core/tooling/read_tool_result_presentation.zig` to `src/core/tooling/tool_args.zig` as `unwrapRequest`, with the same contract, so every reader of a `request` wrapper uses one function instead of its own object-only check.

Before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  decode["src/tools/session/read_tool_result.zig"] --> row["src/core/tooling/read_tool_result_presentation.zig (requestObject)"]
  intake["src/core/agent/runtime/orchestrator.zig (object only)"]
  admission["src/core/tooling/tool_admission.zig (object only)"]
  wait["src/core/agent/runtime/tool_presentation.zig (object only)"]
  ask["src/core/cli/cli_ask.zig (object only)"]
```

After:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  decode["src/tools/session/read_tool_result.zig"] --> args["src/core/tooling/tool_args.zig (unwrapRequest)"]
  row["src/core/tooling/read_tool_result_presentation.zig"] --> args
  intake["src/core/agent/runtime/orchestrator.zig"] --> args
  admission["src/core/tooling/tool_admission.zig"] --> args
  wait["src/core/agent/runtime/tool_presentation.zig"] --> args
  ask["src/core/cli/cli_ask.zig"] --> args
```

title: Read MCP protocol fields that a server writes with JSON escapes
body:
## Summary

A server can write a protocol field name with a JSON escape. `is\u0045rror` is `isError` once decoded, and `std.json`, which core and the ACP projection use, reads it that way. The MCP engine skipped such a name, as if the server had left the field out. A tool result marked `isError` was reported as `completed`, and the model was told `"isError":false`. An escaped `resultType`, `requestState`, `nextCursor`, `ttlMs` or `id` was dropped the same way (an escaped `id` turned a server request into a notification).

`wire.objectFields` now compares an escaped name by its decoded text, through `spells`, a private function of `wire.zig` that decodes the key against the asked name as it goes and allocates nothing. `wire.sameString` is the same decoder for two tokens; `mrtr.zig` uses it to compare two `inputRequests` keys. A surrogate pair equals the character in UTF-8. A lone surrogate, an invalid escape and invalid UTF-8 match only the same bytes.

## Duplicate names

A name that the engine asks for, written twice, is refused with `DuplicateField`, however each copy is spelled. That is what `std.json` does for a field it reads, so the engine and core no longer disagree about a duplicate of such a name. The engine refuses only duplicates of the names it asks for: a repeated key it never asks for, or one inside a nested value it only skips, is still accepted where `std.json.Value` would refuse it. Before, `{"mode":"form","m\u006fde":"url"}` was read as one `mode`. Two `inputRequests` keys that are one name once decoded now make the round `Malformed`, where the retry used to send both keys back (`mrtr.zig:54`).

A response line that repeats a name the engine reads has no readable id, because `responseId` reads the line with the same decoder. Since #2010, such a line is handled like any line the engine refuses and cannot attach to a call: the call it was meant for ends about 30 seconds later as "the server's answer was malformed" and is cancelled, instead of waiting for its operation timeout. The refused-line e2e test in `mcp-stdio.test.ts` has a variant for it (a `result` written twice, the second copy as `r\u0065sult`, the id first).

## What changes for consent (an escaped `mode`, `url` or `elicitationId`)

An escaped `mode`, `url` or `elicitationId` now behaves like the plain spelling. Before, fx refused the request or skipped the field. A server can already send the plain spelling, so this gives a server no new power. Consent and the capability gate still apply: a form-only client given a URL question is still refused with "the server asked for input fx can't give." A URL written with an escape still fails closed through `plainString`, so the URL the user sees cannot differ from the one the engine read.

The e2e test `ACP asks about a URL or a form the same way whether the server writes a key plain or with an escape` is new: `main` has no test for it. It requires each escaped case to come out as its plain case does, in 17 cases. Two of them are for a 2025 server that asks a client that takes forms only for a URL, with `mode` plain and escaped: nothing is asked and the call ends with "MCP protocol error -32042: URL elicitation required" in both. The four cases where the question is held no longer pass on any throw: they wait 6 seconds, and require that the wait ran out, that the server was called once and never cancelled, and that the trace has no refusal of the question or of its answer.

## Tests

- Engine tests in `wire.zig`, `tools.zig` and `mrtr.zig`: a test for each field above, a table for `sameString` (the same table as the one in #1914), look-alike names (`x` and `id` with an escaped NUL between them, a dotless i, an astral suffix), names that hold a backslash or a quote, bad escapes, a 20,000-member object with a 100,000-escape name, and 1,500 levels of nesting.
- Fuzz target `mcp_object_fields`, in `src/core/mcp_host/wire_tests.zig` because the engine imports only `std`: the engine's read of an object's names must equal `std.json`'s typed read, including `DuplicateField`. For every pair of keys it generates, `wire.sameString` must be true exactly when `std.json` decodes both keys to the same text. Keys are written with `\u` escapes in either hex case, surrogate pairs, and the short escapes `\/`, `\"`, `\\` and `\n`. 24 saved inputs, ten of them for the pair law.
- `tests/tla/mcp/FieldRead.tla`: one read of one field, with the rules `AgreeOrRefused`, `DupRefused` and `ReportedAsSaid`, 5 planted bugs, and two findings configs. `check.sh` requires `FieldRead.findings` to violate `AgreeOrRefused` and `FieldRead.findings.isError` to violate `ReportedAsSaid`.
- Driver: `u01-field-names` (120 reads against a `JSON.parse` oracle, each trace checked by TLC), its control against the raw-read model, and `u12-escaped-iserror`, `-resulttype`, `-requeststate` and `-nextcursor`.

### Mutation check

20 planted bugs in a copy of `src/mcp`, each caught by the engine tests:

| Planted bug | Caught by |
|---|---|
| `objectFields`: an escaped name matches nothing again | several tests, among them `a name written with escapes is read as the name it spells` |
| `objectFields`: the last piece of an escaped key is matched | `a key whose last escaped piece is a field name does not match it`, and others |
| `objectFields`: a decoded duplicate is not refused | `a name seen twice is a duplicate, however either one is written` |
| `objectFields`: the key's raw token starts at the comma | several tests |
| `spells`: the asked name is read for escapes | `an asked name that holds a backslash or a quote is matched by the key that spells it` |
| `mrtr.zig:54`: the raw compare is back | `two input request keys that are one name once decoded make the round malformed` |
| `tools.zig`: an absent `isError` is read as true | `a tool result's isError written with an escape is still the server's isError` |
| 13 decoder bugs (surrogate shift, lone surrogates, hex case, short escape, UTF-8 forms, a prefix match, a non-string read as a string) | `sameString is JSON's equality of two string tokens` |

The first run caught 16 of 20. Two mutants did not compile, and two survived because no test asked for a name holding a backslash or for an absent `isError`. Both tests were added and all 20 are caught. Each was planted by hand in a copy of the file and run with `zig test src/mcp/mcp.zig -lc -OReleaseSafe`.

Nine more bugs in `sameString` and its decoder (it never decodes, an upper-case hex digit, the `\/`, `\n` and `\\` escapes, the `\"` escape, a surrogate pair that drops its low half, a prefix that matches, only the first code point compared) are each caught by `zig build fuzz -Dfuzz-target=mcp_object_fields`, the replay of the saved inputs. With the old target and its 14 inputs, six of the nine were not caught.

### Where each check ran

All of it on the head of this pull request, after the merge of `main`, on Linux x86_64 (a ReleaseSafe `fx` for the e2e files), with the keys unset and `FX_SOUND=0`.

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Engine tests, the whole root | `zig test src/mcp/mcp.zig -lc -OReleaseSafe`, and again without `-OReleaseSafe` | 288 tests pass in both |
| Main root, the groups of this change | `core.mcp.` and `core.mcp_host.` | 307 tests run, 0 failed |
| Fuzz replay | `zig build fuzz -Dfuzz-target=mcp_object_fields` | 24 saved inputs, exit 0 |
| ACP | `bun test acp.test.ts -t "ACP asks about a URL or a form the same way"` | pass, 17 cases in 30 s |
| MCP stdio | `bun test mcp-stdio.test.ts` | 136 pass, 0 fail |
| TLA+, engine half of the CI job | `sh tests/tla/mcp/check.sh`, then `bun tests/tla/drivers/mcp/driver.ts` | both exit 0; `FieldRead.findings` and `FieldRead.findings.isError` are "violated, as required" |
| TLA+, host half of the CI job | `bun test ./tests/tla/drivers/mcp_host/` | 55 pass, 12 skip themselves, 0 fail |

### Planted bugs for the tests changed in the review round

| Planted bug | Caught by |
|---|---|
| 9 bugs in `sameString` and its decoder, one at a time | the replay of the saved inputs, 9 of 9 (3 of 9 with the old target and its 14 inputs) |
| `objectFields` skips an escaped key again, and a `-32042` entry with no readable `mode` is asked as a form | the ACP case `a 2025 URL question to a client that takes forms only, mode escaped`; the plain case passes |
| `answerElicitation` panics | the four held ACP cases, on the process check |
| `objectFields` accepts a repeated name when the later copy is escaped | the refused-line e2e test, which fails with the variant in it |

Each is planted by hand in a copy of the tree, with the same commands as above.

## Not changed

These read raw names or strings in the same way and are left for their owners:

- `src/mcp/protocol/elicitation.zig:119,128,300` compare raw keys. #1914 fixes them with its own private decoder, and this PR does not touch that file. There is one decoder rule: whichever of #1914 and #1953 lands second removes the private `Decoder` and its duplicate tests from `elicitation.zig`, and uses `wire.sameString` instead.
- `src/mcp/protocol/http_headers.zig:130-186` has its own raw matches for `properties`, `type` and `x-mcp-header` in a tool's schema. The server controls the schema, and an escaped key only drops a header the server asked for.
- About 20 value-side `plainString` sites read a string value written with an escape as no value and refuse it (an escaped `method`, `mode` value or `resultType` value, and auth fields). They fail closed.

## Docs

None.

title: End a cancelled provider switch at once
body:
## Summary

A sign-in refresh is never cut off once its token request is sent (#1897). As a side effect, a provider switch cancelled with Esc or Ctrl+C during such a refresh stayed pending until the issuer answered, up to the request's 15 second deadline. Until then fx refused new prompts and switches with "Provider preparation is still in progress".

- The cancel now ends the switch at once: fx shows "Provider preparation cancelled." and accepts the next prompt or switch right away.
- The auth runtime keeps a cancelled preparation that still runs until it ends, so its refresh still saves the new login. A new refresh of the same login waits for the first one under the sign-in's lock and uses its result.
- A full shutdown waits for a kept preparation; quitting never waits and leaves it to end with the process, as before.
- A kept refresh can hold the login's lock until the issuer answers. A logout or a team change takes that lock on the input loop, so while such a refresh runs (from a cancelled switch, or from a prompt that stopped waiting) they refuse at once with "A sign-in refresh is still finishing. Try again in a moment." instead of freezing the terminal.

## Tests

- Unit tests in `auth_runtime.zig`: an fx login refresh held during a provider preparation, cancelled, ends the switch at once, reports a refresh still finishing until it ends, and still saves the renewed login; a cancelled preparation that already finished is freed at once; exit leaves a kept preparation running.
- E2E in `tui-auth-source-selection.test.ts`: with the issuer holding the refresh, Ctrl+C after `/logout` shows the cancel notice within 1.5 s, `/logout vercel` is refused at once while the refresh still runs, and the login file holds the renewed token once the issuer answers.
- The new tests fail on `main`, and the E2E test fails without the logout refusal.

title: Renew a rejected login during a turn's compaction
body:
## Summary

When the gateway rejected a turn's summary request with 401, the automatic compaction failed and the turn failed with it, even when another fx process had renewed the shared login or one refresh would have worked. `/compact` and agent turns already renew a rejected login once; a turn's own compaction did not.

- The turn's compaction now renews the login once through the same rule (`credential_renewal.renewRejected`): it sends the stored login when another process renewed it, or forces one refresh while the store still holds the rejected token.
- The rest of the turn sends the renewed login, so the next request does not hit a second 401.
- In ACP, the host's reload frees the credential the turn borrowed. The compaction keeps the credential it reloaded even when it cannot renew it, as an agent turn does, and the turn takes it as soon as the compaction returns, so neither the compactor's fallback summary nor the turn ever sends the freed bytes.

## Tests

- `gateway_flow.zig`: a context overflow, then a 401 on the summary request, for both a login another fx renewed and one that needs a forced refresh. The summary and the rest of the turn send the renewed token.
- `text_completion.zig`: when the forced refresh gives nothing, the 401 stands and the caller sends its own copy of the stored login.
- `acp.test.ts`: the renewal flow over ACP against a gateway that accepts only the current token; and, with the issuer down and every summary rejected, the fallback summary still goes out with the stored login.
- The new tests fail on `main`. Without the turn taking the renewed credential, the Zig test sends the old token after the compaction and the ACP turn ends `refused`; before the stored login is kept, the ACP fallback summary does not reach the gateway on Linux and carries freed bytes on macOS.

title: Take Token Pass models from the catalog when it marks them
body:
Stacked on #1945.

## What changes

fx decides which models Token Pass pays for from a list in its own source. A model that joins or leaves Token Pass, or one that a team's settings keep off the pass, stays wrong in the picker until the next fx release.

A catalog entry can now carry `token_pass: true`. When any entry does, the catalog decides which models are Token Pass models:

- The picker's **Token Pass** group and the **Token Pass** tag list the marked models. Models that fx's own list also names keep their order, and a model that only the catalog marks follows them.
- The speed step starts on **normal** for a marked model.
- The "Token Pass covers this model" notice and the Fast mode warning after a switch follow the marked models.

When no entry is marked, fx marks the models in its own list, so the picker is unchanged for a catalog without the field. Before the catalog loads, fx's own list answers for AI Gateway models.

The calls that fx makes on its own, such as permission reviews, session titles, the vision fallback, and the compaction fallback, still choose from fx's list. They pick a model without reading the catalog, and which Token Pass model suits each call is fx's choice.

The catalog does not send `token_pass` yet, so this change has no visible effect until it does.

## How it works

- `src/builtins/gateway.zig` reads `token_pass` into `ModelCatalogEntry`. After it parses a catalog, `model_catalog.markBuiltInTokenPassModels` marks fx's own list when no entry is marked.
- The flag reaches `Capabilities.token_pass` through `GatewayMetadata`. The menu, the speed step, and the notices read it there in place of `token_pass.isFeaturedModel`.
- `vercel_model_policy.capabilitiesForModel` sets the flag from fx's list for a model that has no catalog entry yet.

## Verification

Built with Zig 0.17.0 on macOS arm64.

- `zig fmt --check src/`: passed.
- `zig build`: passed.
- `zig build test`: passed, run with an empty `HOME` and Zig 0.17.0 first on `PATH`.
- `cd tests/e2e && FX_SOUND=0 bun test tui-slash-menu.test.ts`: 45 passed, 0 failed. The new test, "model picker takes Token Pass models from the catalog when it marks them", drives `./zig-out/bin/fx` in tmux against a fake gateway whose catalog marks one model and leaves a model from fx's own list unmarked. It checks that only the marked model sits under **Token Pass**, that switching to it prints the Token Pass notice, that switching to the unmarked model does not, and that stderr is empty. The existing test "model picker keeps Token Pass models on Token Pass credit" covers a catalog without the field.
- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test acp.test.ts auto-mode-reliability.test.ts cli.test.ts -t "Token Pass"`: 3 passed, 0 failed.
- `scripts/check-public-surface.sh`: passed.

## Docs

- https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/models, "Token Pass models": after the sentence that starts "The model picker lists the featured models first", add "When your team has Token Pass, the picker takes these models from the AI Gateway catalog, so the group shows the models your team's pass pays for."

title: Show Still running for a shell command that returned before it ended
body:
## Summary

- A shell command that is still running when its call returns, because steering moved it to the background or its yield time ran out, now shows `Still running <command>` in its tool row instead of `Ran <command>`.
- The same row reads `Still running` after the session is resumed, for captured and tty commands.
- Commands that finish before the call returns still show `Ran`, `Exited <code>`, or their other final status.

title: Send SDK host tools the argument types their schemas name
body:
## Summary

- Some models write a number, boolean, array, or object argument as JSON text, such as `"40"` for an integer. fx sends such an argument to an MCP server as the type the tool's schema names, but a tool that an SDK app registers itself got the model's text, so its `execute` saw `"40"` where its `inputSchema` says integer.
- Host tool calls now go through one provider on both backends. It repairs the arguments against the tool's `inputSchema` with `repairArgumentTypes`, the function MCP calls use, and then calls the native `libfx/tool_call` path or the WebAssembly host.
- Values the schema accepts as written, text that is not exactly a value of the schema's type, and tools with no matching schema get the model's own bytes. The session and the `tool_call` update still record the arguments as the model wrote them, as for MCP.
- MCP tools that an app adds with `createMcpAdapter` are host tools to fx, so they get the same repair.
- `sdk/README.md` says what `execute` receives.

## Testing

- `sdk/tests/test-host-tools.mjs`: a second host tool, `count`, with integer, boolean, array, and string fields, gets `{limit: 40, exact: true, tags: ["a", "b"], label: "40"}` when the model writes all four as text. It fails on main on both backends and passes on both here (`node sdk/tests/test-host-tools.mjs native` and `node --experimental-wasm-jspi sdk/tests/test-host-tools.mjs wasm`).
- An inline test in `src/acp/prompt.zig` covers the repaired case and each case that sends the model's own bytes: text that is not an integer, a field with no single type, an unknown tool, and arguments that are not an object.
- `node sdk/tests/test-core-browser.mjs` passes all eight browser cases, including the host tool case, against the core and terminal WebAssembly builds.
- The `mcp_argument_repair` fuzz target ran 300 seconds with no failure. The 25 host tool tests also pass under ThreadSanitizer, run with a local test filter.

title: Pin that a 2026 MCP server's -32602 on a call keeps its session
body:
## Summary

- A comment on the TUI rejected-arguments test in `tests/e2e/mcp-stdio.test.ts` said that a `-32602` from a 2026 server on `tools/call` makes fx negotiate the protocol again. fx does not: it lists the tools again (`suggestsChangedList` in `src/mcp/protocol/tools.zig`) and keeps the 2026 session, so the next call reaches the same server process without an `initialize`.
- The claim came from a TUI run against the 2026 fixture without `expectedElicitation: "both"`. The TUI declares form and URL elicitation, so that fixture refused `server/discover` itself, and fx fell back to `initialize` as designed. Every 2026 TUI test in the file already sets the option.
- New tests in the 2026 suite pin the real behavior, and the comment now says what fx does and points at them. No product code changes.

## Testing

- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test mcp-stdio.test.ts -t "refuses a call.s arguments with -32602"`: the first call sends `limit: "forty"`, which the fixture's `typed_arguments` mode refuses with `-32602`. A valid retry gets `TYPED_ARGUMENTS_OK`, and a second refusal gets the server's own `-32602` text. In both cases the wire log has two `tools/call` in one process and no `initialize`, and no result says "unavailable".
- The TUI rejected-arguments test passes with its corrected comment.

title: Show the model the details an MCP server gives with a failed tool call
body:
## Summary

A server can explain a refused call in the `data` of its error, such as which arguments broke its schema. The engine read it and the host dropped it, so the model saw only the code and the message and had to guess at the fix. The model now gets the data after the message, bounded. The host never holds more than 16 KiB of the data's compact text, even for the moment it cuts it.

## What the model sees

- **It fits:** the data's compact JSON text, up to 8 KiB, after `; data=`. An error without data gives the model the same bytes as before.
- **It is longer:** one JSON string. It holds the longest prefix whose quotes and escapes fit in 8 KiB, cut where a character ends, then a marker that names the length, such as ` ... [data truncated: 300013 bytes, cap is 8192]`. The literal is at most 8 KiB plus the marker, and the marker is at most 64 bytes. Data longer than 16 KiB is cut without being read.
- **Where it is stated:** the comment on `data_cap` in `src/core/mcp_host/runtime.zig`, the rules `Bounded`, `KeepsMost` and `CutOnBoundary` in `tests/tla/mcp_host/ErrorData.tla`, and the law of the `mcp_error_data` fuzz target all say the same bound.

## Why the bound is judged on the compact text

Core writes the data again before the model sees it, and `std.json` writes `1e-300` (6 bytes) as 302 bytes. A few hundred such numbers, well under 8 KiB as the server wrote them, would pass core's 128 KiB metadata limit. The whole call would then fail and the model would lose even the message. The host writes the compact text itself, with the same `std.json`, so core's round trip changes nothing, and `sanitizeModelText` leaves text with no NUL byte and valid UTF-8 as it is. A cut is a string, which core writes back the same way.

## What is left out

The model gets what it got before for these:

- **Data the host cannot read** (not UTF-8, not JSON, a repeated key, or nested past 128 levels): the trace has one line with the reason and a length, and no data. `std.json` keeps the nesting of what it writes in a stack of 256 levels and the engine reads up to about 2,000, so passing deeper data on to core would crash fx. An object with a repeated key is valid JSON, but `std.json` refuses it by default, so it is left out as unreadable.
- **A `null` data**, which says nothing, and **the data of a `-32042`**: its URLs are the user's to answer through the questions the host already asks, and its words stay byte for byte (`tests/tla/mcp_host/UrlRetry.tla`). These two leave no trace line.

## What the compact text changes

The model sees the data as `std.json` writes it with no spaces, which is also how core's own round trip writes it. So a number may be written differently: `0.1000000000000000055511151231257827` becomes `0.1`, and `12345678901234567890.5` becomes `12345678901234567000`. This is not changed here.

## How much the host holds

Data up to 16 KiB is parsed, and the compact text of a small number can be 47 times as long as the number (`5e-324` is 6 bytes and `std.json` writes it as 327). The host writes the compact text twice into writers that keep nothing of it: once into a discarding writer, to learn its length for the marker, and once into a 16 KiB buffer that fills and stops. The cut reads that buffer. The scratch holds the parse tree and at most 16 KiB of text, where it held 765,183 bytes of text for 16,383 bytes of `5e-324`. `HeldBounded` in `ErrorData.tla` says this: `held` counts the compact text at the moment of the cut, at most `2 * Cap`.

## A change in `tool_result.zig`, needed by this one

The cause line for a rejected call (#1840) reads the text after the message, and that text now ends with `; data=...`. A zod-style server that also sent data lost its cause line, because the reading takes everything from the first `[` to the last `]`, and a server's data could add a field to a Go-style one. The cause line now reads only the message: `withoutData` takes the first `; data=` whose rest is one JSON value, or the start of one when the text was cut, so the data can never put a label before the real one. The first version looked at the last 8 labels, which data with 8 or more labels could use to add a field to the line or remove one (1,273 of 300,000 random data values did). It also failed on a cut text. The trace report reads a 4 KiB head of a text longer than 8 KiB, and a text cut by `max_tool_result_bytes` ends with a marker, and neither ends in a whole JSON value. The cause line is now the message's for the whole text, for every head of it that holds the message and the label, and for a text with the marker. The reader finds that marker by the same constants `tool_result_limits.zig` writes it with, so the two cannot drift apart. This holds for every message that does not itself contain `; data=`. If a server writes that label in its own message (for example `; data="`), its data can make fx cut the message at that label, so the cause line can lose its fields; it never gets a word of the data, because the cut is always inside the server's own message. The commit message of the earlier commit has the same claim in its first form, and stays as it is.

## The cause line when the result cap stores the error text

A project whose `.fx.json` sets `max_tool_result_bytes` below the error text (about 8.5 KiB or less) still sees the cause on the status line, such as `arguments rejected: limit is a string, the schema wants a number`, because it is now read from the first 4 KiB of the text that the result store keeps in the model's preview block. The same holds when the server's message alone is over the cap: before this change the line showed the block's tag. `result_store.storedPreview` reads the block that `formatStoredResultOutput` writes, and the two share the text that ends the preview.

For every other protocol error code, the status line shows the server's message, as it does when the server gives no data, and never the data: only the model gets the data. `protocolErrorWithoutData` in `tool_result.zig` cuts it, with the same search that `invalidParamsCause` uses (which now calls it), and `failureStatusDetail` uses it when there is no cause to name, after it has read the stored block.

## Tests

- 30 new unit tests in `runtime.zig` (14), `model.zig` (5), `tool_result.zig` (5), `json_depth.zig` (1), `tool_presentation.zig` (4) and `result_store.zig` (1), with no test-only seam in the code. They cover the bound on every escape class, a cap exactly after escaping, characters of two to four bytes across the cap, the float growth above, nesting, bytes that are not UTF-8, a `-32042`, 200 calls with 300 KB of data each, what the model got for hostile data (16 KiB of `5e-324` gives 8,240 bytes, 10,000 levels in 20 KB give a string of 8,239, 129 levels are left out), what the scratch holds (an allocator that counts its peak: the parse tree and no more than two caps of text), and the cause line for data with 8 and with 800 labels, for the first 4096 bytes of a text over 8 KiB, and for texts the result cap cut. The three in `tool_presentation.zig` give the cause for a stored text (a zod message and a plain one, each with data and a head cut at 4 KiB, and a zod message alone over the cap), show no block tag for a head cut inside the zod list or for words that are not a protocol error, the fourth in `tool_presentation.zig` and the new one in `tool_result.zig` check that a `-32603` error shows its message and no data, whole, as a stored block and with a head cut inside the data, and that the helper keeps a message that holds its own `; data=`; and the one in `result_store.zig` reads back every preview that `formatStoredResultOutput` writes, including one that holds the end tag itself.
- 9 e2e tests in `mcp-stdio.test.ts`, with the fixture options `FX_MCP_PROTOCOL_ERROR_CODE`, `_DATA`, `_DATA_BYTES`, `_DATA_RAW` and `_FAULT` in `mcp-legacy-stdio.mjs`. One sends data that forges the cause line (a zod-like list and 8 labels, past 8 KiB) after a zod message and after a plain one. It requires that no word of the data is in a trace of every scope, on standard error or on the screen, and that in the report `/trace` writes it is only in the failed call's result, which is the model's text, and in no other field: the cause is the message's. The old test watched only the `mcp` and `tools` scopes and standard error. The ninth sets `max_tool_result_bytes` to 2000 in the workspace's `.fx.json`, in a saved TUI session under tmux, and refuses a call with a zod message and data, a plain message and data, and a zod message alone, each over the cap. It requires that the model got a preview block, that the screen shows the cause and no block tag, and that no word of the data is on the screen or in a log. Both the no-leak test and this one have a `-32603` case: the screen shows `MCP protocol error -32603: Internal error` and no `data=`, at the default cap and at 2000.
- Fuzz target `mcp_error_data`: 33 saved inputs. Its law no longer calls the code it checks: data that fits is kept as the same JSON with no spaces (both texts parsed and compared), and a cut is a prefix of the data's text with its spaces removed. Fuzz target `mcp_invalid_params_cause` has a data law (for a message that holds no `; data=` of its own: the cause of the message with any data after it, and of every head that holds the message and the label, is the cause of the message) and 5 saved inputs, two of them the 8-label and the 4 KiB-head case. Iterations: 25,000 and 20,000.
- `ErrorData.tla`: smoke and stress configs (221 and 577 distinct states, up from 111 and 283), nine planted bugs, and a findings config for the code before this change. `error-data.test.ts` runs 19 real `fx ask` cases against the model through its trace wrapper, and the model of the old host rejects the same trace.
- Planted bugs, each caught (the e2e test too fails with the base `withoutData`): the base `withoutData` (4 unit tests and the fuzz replay fail); a cut text refused as data (4 tests); the cut marker left on (1 test); the base `boundErrorData` that holds the compact text whole (the bound test, and only it); three bugs in `compactText` (spaces, a dropped last byte, strings as arrays) against the fuzz law of `mcp_error_data`; `HeldBounded` against the model's whole-text plant. Each was planted by hand in a copy of the tree and run with the commands below. For the stored text: `failureStatusDetail` reading the block as before (3 unit tests fail, and the e2e test fails on the screen with `<tool_result_preview handle=...` where the cause should be), `protocolErrorWithoutData` returning the text unchanged (8 tests), the fallback of `failureStatusDetail` not using it (1 test, and both e2e tests fail on the screen), the helper reading only `-32602`'s words (2), `invalidParamsCause` cutting by its own search (6), `storedPreview` returning nothing (4 tests), ending the preview at the first end tag (1), starting it two bytes after the tag (4) and keeping the line break before the end tag (2).

## Where the checks ran

All of it on the final head, on Linux x86_64, with the keys unset and `FX_SOUND=0`. No check needed macOS.

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Zig tests of the files this changes | the groups `core.mcp.`, `core.mcp_host.`, `core.shared.json_depth.` and `core.app.trace_report.` of the unit-test binary | 398 tests pass |
| Fuzz replay | `zig build fuzz -Dfuzz-target=mcp_invalid_params_cause`, and `-Dfuzz-target=mcp_error_data` | exit 0 |
| Fuzzer | `python3 -m scripts.fuzz_nightly run --target T --budget-seconds 180` for both targets | `mcp_error_data`: 2 rounds ok; `mcp_invalid_params_cause`: 3 rounds ok; no failure (180 s each) |

The same binary run with every capability dropped passes all 1,750. |

## Not changed here

- A successful tool result whose `structuredContent` is nested 256 levels deep used to panic inside `render`. #1989 fixed that, and this change guards only the error `data` path.

- Where a rewritten number or a repeated key matters (see above), the data is as `std.json` reads it, as core's own round trip would read it.

## Docs

title: Offer Token Pass at login and default Token Pass teams to DeepSeek
body:
## Summary

- Stop printing the `Preparing <provider>.` line when fx starts preparing a provider.
- Print the Vercel team line without the `auth:` label after login or a team change.
- Show a dim `Get $150 of tokens for $30 with Vercel Token Pass.` line under the team line, with the name linked to https://vercel.com/get/token-pass, unless fx already knows the team has Token Pass.
- In the interactive terminal, check Token Pass in the background after the model catalog loads, when the user has no saved AI Gateway model and no `FX_MODEL`, `--model`, or `--provider`.
- Switch that run to `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` once the main agent is idle when the team has an active Token Pass, without saving it as the user's model, and say so in the transcript.
- Show the result of `/credits` when it runs while the background check is still in flight.
- Keep a resumed session on the model it saved, even when settings name no model.
- Leave `fx ask` and ACP hosts on their own model selection.


## Design

- fx learns that a team has Token Pass only from `/credits` or from a reply that Token Pass served, and a user on the built-in default model gets neither. The startup check reuses the `/credits` background lookup, in a quiet mode that prints nothing, instead of adding a second request path.
- The switch applies only while the main agent still runs AI Gateway's built-in default, and the no-chosen-model rule reuses `ModelOrigin.of`, which `fx status` already uses.
- The lookup carries a per-credential epoch, so a reply that started before a login or team change cannot mark the new team as having Token Pass.
- The offer line is a new optional `detail` on notices, which renders dim on its own indented rows. A separate notice would add a blank row and its own bullet.



Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#320

title: Count both new auth runtime fields
body:
## Summary

`main` does not compile: `src/core/auth/auth_runtime.zig` fails the field-count check in `Runtime.initIntoWithMode` ("update Runtime.initInto for the changed field set").

Two pull requests each added one field to the auth runtime and each raised the count from 36 to 37: `kept_sign_out_retry_task` (retry unconfirmed sign-outs) and `cancelled_provider_preparations` (#1954). Each passed CI against its own base, and together the runtime has 38 fields. Both fields are already initialized in `initIntoWithMode`; only the count was stale, so this sets it to 38.

## Tests

title: End 204 and 304 responses at the header block in web_fetch
body:
## Summary

- `web_fetch` treats a 204 or 304 response as complete at the end of its header block, as RFC 9112 section 6.3 specifies, and ignores any bytes the server sends after it.
- A 204 or 304 followed by stray bytes no longer fails with `UnexpectedBodyForBodylessResponse`. That check saw the bytes only when they arrived in the same read as the head, so the result depended on how the response was split across reads.
- Reading on after the head to look for those bytes would break real 204 endpoints, such as `https://www.google.com/generate_204`, which close TLS without close_notify, and would wait on servers that ignore `Connection: close`. fx sends one request per connection with `Connection: close`, so no later response follows on it.

## Testing

- The nightly fuzz target `http_response` found the split dependence ([run 43267564765](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/actions/runs/43267564765), seed `0xa70f6b22`). Its input is saved as `tests/fuzz/corpus/http_response/split-after-304-head`: replaying it fails on main with `UnexpectedBodyForBodylessResponse` and passes with this change.
- The new test "web_fetch bodyless response ends at its head however the bytes after it are split" fails on main and passes here. `zig build fuzz -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe -Dfuzz-target=http_response --fuzz=200K` finds nothing, also with the CI seed.
- Against `https://www.google.com/generate_204` and `https://connectivitycheck.gstatic.com/generate_204`, `web_fetch` returns status 204 with an empty body.

title: Hold the worker's reply until the parent's turn ends in a recovery test
body:
## Summary

- The test "ask continues and persists a healthy parent when its child's session is gone" holds the worker's model reply until the parent's first turn has finished, so the worker's report always starts the seed run's second turn. Before, the report could join the first turn when the parent was slow, as `tests/tla/subagent/MainMail.tla` `JoinsOpenTurn` allows, and the saved history then had one turn too few.
- The test reads the end of that turn from fx's `worker` trace, the way `tests/tla/drivers/subagent/main-mail.test.ts` does.

title: Continue a waiting request with a login another fx session saved
body:
## Summary

- When fx sessions share a login that stops working, each session's request waits for a sign-in and opens its own. Signing in from one session now continues the others within about a second, instead of at their next try, up to 3 minutes later.
- A session that continues this way closes the sign-in it opened for the request and says "Signed in from another fx session. Continuing with that login." A sign-in the user opened for another provider stays open.
- While a request waits for a sign-in, fx reads the stored login about once a second without calling the issuer. A stored login that still holds the token the provider refused counts as none, and so does the login this session's own sign-in saved before its team is chosen: that sign-in still continues the request with the team picked.

## Testing

- `tests/e2e/tui-auth-source-selection.test.ts` "a sign-in finished in one session continues another session waiting for it": two sessions on one login, both waiting for a sign-in, and only the first session's code is approved. Without this change, the second session still shows its own sign-in 10 seconds later (`Sign-in expired · waiting 10s · next try in 2m 50s`) and the test fails; with it, the second session continues with the new login, its own sign-in closes, and only two device codes are requested.
- "a team picked during a sign-in wait sends the waiting request with that team" now waits on the team picker before choosing: the request is not sent during that wait, and it goes out only on the team picked. The whole file passes, 230 tests.
- Unit tests cover the stored read (`.stored` finds only a login other than the refused one and never calls the issuer), the sign-in remembering the token it saved, the wait's once-a-second check in `request_recovery.zig`, and the turn loop resending with the other login in `gateway_flow.zig`.

## Docs

vercel-labs/fx-web#313 updates the troubleshooting page.

title: Bug: Shell commands fail on NixOS with Nushell because /bin/bash is missing
body:
## Problem

fx 0.0.16 cannot run default shell commands on NixOS when the account's login shell is Nushell. It tries `/bin/bash`, but NixOS provides Bash at `/run/current-system/sw/bin/bash` instead.

fx reads the login shell from the account's passwd entry, not `$SHELL`. Setting `$SHELL` to Bash does not fix this. This is a gap in the fallback added by #121, not a request for native Nushell support.

## Reproduce

Use a NixOS account with Nushell as its configured login shell and Bash installed.

1. From Bash, check the setup:

   ```bash
   getent passwd "$(id -un)" | cut -d: -f7
   command -v bash
   test ! -e /bin/bash && printf '/bin/bash is absent\n'
   ```

   Expected: `/run/current-system/sw/bin/nu`, `/run/current-system/sw/bin/bash`, and `/bin/bash is absent`.

2. Start fx with a configured model. Ask it to run `printf 'shell-ok\n'` using the shell tool without an explicit shell override:

   ```json
   {"action":"run","command":"printf 'shell-ok\n'"}
   ```

3. Repeat with `"profile":"clean"`.

## Actual result

Both calls fail before the command runs:

```json
{"state":"lost","error":"FileNotFound","exit_code":null,"output_delta":""}
```

A terminal call with `"tty":true` also fails with `shell_unavailable`. Explicitly selecting `/run/current-system/sw/bin/bash` works.

## Expected result

fx finds the installed Bash executable, prints `shell-ok`, and exits with code 0. Users should not need to change their login shell or create `/bin/bash`.

title: Find fallback shells beside the configured login shell
body:
## Changes

Fixes #1966.

When the platform fallback shell (`/bin/bash` on Linux or `/bin/zsh` on macOS) is missing, look for the same shell beside the configured login shell.

- Use the configured login-shell directory without resolving its symlink. Require an executable regular file, including a symlink to one.
- Copy discovered paths wherever they must outlive the resolver's buffer.
- Cover default precedence, invalid candidates, symlinks, buffer bounds, and execution-profile path ownership.

The branch contains one signed commit on upstream `3b76573b06fd`. The diff remains limited to `shell_resolver.zig` and its `native_session.zig` caller.

## Impact

NixOS accounts configured with Nushell can use captured user commands, captured clean commands, and persistent terminals through an installed sibling Bash, such as `/run/current-system/sw/bin/bash`.

Supported login shells, explicit shell overrides, and existing platform defaults retain their behavior. Fallback discovery does not search `PATH`, add settings, or hardcode NixOS paths in production code. This does not add native Nushell support.

## Verification

Tested on NixOS x86_64 with Zig 0.17.1 at `8fe7e923d7e9`:

- Build, formatting, and static checks passed.
- All 38 shell-resolver tests passed with `/bin/bash` hidden.
- Six checks using the freshly built `./zig-out/bin/fx` passed: user commands, clean commands, and persistent terminals, with and without `/bin/bash`.

Required CI, including macOS arm64, awaits maintainer approval. This remains draft until those checks and the final ship check pass. Before merge, the SSH signing key needs GitHub registration and a maintainer must add `type: bug`.

## Docs

On https://fx.sh/docs/capabilities/tools, under **Background commands**, add the following after the paragraph beginning “The `shell` tool uses `run` to start a command”:

> When your account's login shell is neither Bash nor Zsh, fx uses `/bin/zsh` on macOS or `/bin/bash` on Linux. If that path is missing, fx tries an executable file with the same name in the directory of your configured login-shell path, without resolving that login shell's symlink. Symlinks to executable regular files are accepted. Fallback discovery does not search `PATH`.

title: Cycle the reasoning effort with Ctrl+T
body:
## Summary

`ctrl+t` cycles the current model's reasoning effort: `default`, then each level the model lists, then back to `default`. This matches [opencode's `ctrl+t`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/f6e0c2d0833ffe772035f221fed923e1cd5fb408/packages/tui/src/model-preference.ts#L67-L75).

- Each press saves the level as `/effort` does. The status line shows it; the transcript and the draft are untouched.
- A level the model doesn't offer goes to `default`. A model without levels gets the `/effort` notice.
- The key does nothing while a prompt, picker, menu, or `/effort ` or `/model ` query owns the keyboard. Over the open `/effort` menu, it closes the menu and steps.

## Tests

- Unit tests for the cycle, the decoder, routing, blocked surfaces, and the no-levels notice.
- E2E in `tui-effort-menu.test.ts`: the full cycle, saved settings, the draft, the effort sent with the next request, and a model without levels.
- Ran `./zig-out/bin/fx` against a fake gateway: `default` → `none` → `low` → `medium` → `high` → `default`, and the next request carried the selected effort.

## Docs

Companion PR: vercel-labs/fx-web#321

- https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/keyboard-shortcuts, "Control fx": add after `ctrl+p`:

  ```md
  | `ctrl+t` | Cycle the current model's [reasoning effort](/docs/configure-fx/models#reasoning-effort) from `default` through each of its levels and back to `default`. |
  ```

- https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/models, "Reasoning effort": add after the `/effort high` example:

  ```md
  Press ctrl+t to cycle the reasoning effort without a menu: from `default` through each of the model's levels, lowest first for AI Gateway models, then back to `default`. The status line shows the level in use, and no level at `default`.
  ```

title: Count the auth runtime's new field in its init check
body:
## Summary

- `main` compiles again: the auth runtime's field-count check now expects the 38 fields that `initIntoWithMode` sets, including `cancelled_provider_preparations`.

title: Read a Keychain login without waiting for the fx login lock
body:
## Summary

With the macOS Keychain backend, `oauth_session.load()` took the fx login lock for every read, because a read can also move a valid profile file into the Keychain. While another fx process held the lock, such as through a refresh's token request, a read waited up to the request's deadline plus slack (about 17 s). Readers include the model list and title fetches, a `/usage` renewal, the fx login source check, and `fx status`. The profile file backend never locks for a read.

- A Keychain read now tries the lock once (`loadKeychainProfile`). When the lock is free, it reads and migrates as before.
- When another process holds the lock, it reads the file and the Keychain as they are and leaves the migration to a later load (`loadKeychainUnlocked`). A valid file still wins, as under the lock.
- Writers replace the file in one rename and the Keychain item in one call, so an unlocked read gets the login from before or after a write. A refresh still takes the lock with its wait and reads the login again inside it.

## Tests

- `oauth_session.zig`, with the fake Keychain: while another holder has the lock, a read returns at once with the file's login and does not migrate it; once the lock is free, the next read migrates the file. While the lock is held, a Keychain-only login is returned as stored.
- With the old wait put back, the first test fails on its time check.

title: Wait for the hosted shell's pid before checking that it ends
body:
## Summary

`sessions.test.ts` "a hosted terminal ends with an app crash, and the resumed app reports it ended" failed now and then in CI, at `expect(alive(shellPid)).toBe(false)`.

The test read the terminal record right after the turn was saved. The shell tool call uses `yield_time_ms: 0`, so it returns before the shell has started, and the record can still hold `pid: null`. `Number(null)` is 0, and `process.kill(0, 0)` signals the test's own process group, which is always alive. So the check passed before the kill and could never pass after it.

- The crash test now waits for the record to hold the shell's pid before it kills the app.
- `alive()` in that test and `processAlive()` in `tui-terminal-tool.test.ts` refuse a pid that is not positive, so a missing pid fails at once instead of looking alive.
- The ask exit test in `tui-terminal-tool.test.ts` lets fx exit before the shell pid is recorded, so it now checks `processAlive` only when a pid was recorded; its loop already waits for the command by name.
- The terminal budget test in `tui-terminal-tool.test.ts` turned every record's pid into a number the same way. It now waits only for real pids. A terminal still starting when fx exits has no shell pid to check (the store writes `pid: null` until the child starts), and its command is still found by name through `processesMatching`. Requiring a pid for every record could fail when fx exits before the last shell starts. A small `pidOf` helper reads a record's pid for `recordedPid` and the budget test.
- The crash test in `sessions.test.ts` keeps its own short wait for the pid: that file reads records through its own `terminalRecords(fixture, id)`, and the two test files share no helper module today.

## Tests

- In a sandbox, the old crash test failed 1 of 8 runs, and in the failing run the pid it checked was 0. The new test passed 15 of 15 runs, and 5 of 5 on the current `main`.
- `tui-terminal-tool.test.ts`: 19 of 19 pass, and the ask exit and budget tests 3 runs of 3. `sessions.test.ts -t terminal`: 3 of 3 pass.
