title: Pin compaction of a tool argument larger than the window
body:
## Summary

- A tool call's arguments stay in the conversation, so a call whose argument is larger than the model's whole context window leaves only compaction. No test covered that path.
- The compaction request must clip the argument to fit (`fittingTranscript` in `src/core/compactor/summarize.zig`). Because the open turn itself no longer fits, the compaction folds the turn's own call into the summary, so the streamed turn no longer matches its rebuild and is written again once. That is the path `tests/tla/session/TurnStream.tla` allows in `SupersedeExplained`.
- Two new tests in `tests/e2e/compaction-policy.test.ts` pin it, and a new reader, `logLinesAfterCompaction` in `tests/e2e/saved-sessions.ts`, accepts that one supersede and still refuses any other. No product code changes.

## Testing

- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test compaction-policy.test.ts`: all 9 tests pass. In the two new ones, the model writes a 1 MB file with `write_file` against `fixture/compaction` (128k-token window), once with the first compaction request refused with HTTP 400 `context_length_exceeded`. Each turn ends with the final reply after one compaction. The accepted compaction request is about a quarter of the argument's size and keeps its start and end around the "bytes left out here" note, and the next model request no longer carries the argument.
- The existing tests in the file keep the strict `logLines` reader and pass.
- A check with four planted session logs: `logLinesAfterCompaction` refuses a supersede without a compaction, a second supersede after one compaction, and a supersede after a compaction in an earlier turn, and accepts a supersede after a compaction in its own turn.

title: Wait for the stop notice that ends the empty-reply TUI test's turn
body:
## Summary

- "two empty replies that stop for another reason show the stop and its reason instead of Done." in `tests/e2e/tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` now waits for "Continue with a follow-up prompt if needed.", the notice that ends the turn. Before, it waited for "The model stopped without a reply (provider reason: UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL).", which the first empty reply also prints before fx asks the model to continue. A quick stable composer check then let the test read the screen while the second request was still on "Thinking".
- It failed and then passed on retry in 2 of the last 300 CI runs: on #1949 (run 43364088932) and in run 43314931849. A local copy that delays the second reply by 1.5 seconds fails the old test every time with the same message and passes with this change.
- Test only. No product code changes.

title: Hold fake subagent answers until the parent's turn is saved
body:
## Summary

- A subagent's report that arrives while the parent's turn still runs joins that turn, as `postMail` in `src/core/agent/worker_runtime.zig` intends. Four E2E fakes answered the child at once but checked for the parent's receipt as its own step, so a fast child made the receipt and its request disappear:
  - "ask continues and persists a healthy parent when its child's session is gone" in `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`, which failed twice, with its retry, on macOS arm64 for #1957 (run 43373286161) with `["PARENT_SEED_SENTINEL", "PARENT_CONTINUATION_SAVED"]` saved.
  - "fx ask runs a subagent as a v2 child with its own log, recorded in the parent's log" in `tests/e2e/sessions.test.ts`.
  - "subagent requests preserve connection and %s model capabilities" and "persistent child capabilities stay bound when the parent changes providers" in `tests/e2e/configured-providers.test.ts`.
- `tests/e2e/saved-sessions.ts` gets `committedRootTurns` and `waitForRootTurnCommitted`, built on `rootSessionIds` and `logLines`. Each fake now answers its child only once the parent's log holds a new `turn_committed` line, so the report always starts the next turn. The resumed run in the persistent test waits for a turn past the ones it starts with.
- A local copy of each test that adds a `sleep 1` shell call after the subagent call in the parent's first step, so the report surely lands in that turn, fails 3 of 3 runs on `main` with the receipt missing and passes 3 of 3 with this change, for all six cases.
- Test only. No product code changes.

title: Never start a new session id with a dash
body:
## Summary

- New session ids, and the ids of new subagent children, never start with `-`. Before, one id in 4096 started with `--`, and `fx session <id>` and `fx session recover <id>` refused it as an unknown flag and exited 2. For example `fx session --abcdefghij --json` printed `{"kind":"session","error":"unknown flag --abcdefghij","code":"InvalidSessionDetailArgs"}`.
- Existing ids are unchanged. An id that starts with a single `-` still works as an operand, and `--id <id>` still takes any id.
- This is why "fx ask runs a subagent as a v2 child with its own log, recorded in the parent's log" in `tests/e2e/sessions.test.ts` failed once on #1949 (run 43364088932): `fx session <child-id> --json` exited 2, not 1, which only a child id that starts with `--` does.

title: Close the terminal a cancelled tty start created
body:
## Summary

- Cancelling a tty command just after its terminal launched now ends that command, instead of leaving it running unseen until fx exits.
- The cancelled request still reports as cancelled, and the terminal's record shows it closed.

title: Keep a subagent's always approval for the session
body:
## Summary

- A subagent's "don't ask again" answer, option 2 on its prompt, now keeps its grant for the session. Before, it kept nothing: the subagent's next call, its siblings, and main were all asked again, and `/permissions` showed `Session grants none`.
- Now the same subagent, its siblings, and main run the same command, file change, or MCP tool with no prompt, even when main is in `ask` mode, and main does so in the turn that is already running: its next check reads the grant, and so does a command it starts later, for the `fx mcp call` that command makes. The grant goes to the instance at the top of the subagent's tree, as main's own does.
- A second instance, started with `/launch` or `--instances`, is another session and still asks. A one-time answer, option 1, keeps nothing, as before.
- No prompt text changes. "For this session" was already the words, and it is now true. This replaces #1926, which changed only the words.

## What changed

The tool path kept a grant only when a turn had no live authority, and every subagent turn in the app has one. The condition now keeps the grant for every "always" answer. The grant is written to the instance's list as the answer is given, on the worker thread of the agent that answered, so that agent's next call in the same turn finds it. `/permissions` lists it.

A turn of main used to check and run its calls against its own list: the one it began with plus its own answers. Each check, file-change check and tool call now reads that list followed by a copy of the instance's list (`mergeLiveGrants`), taken when the check or the call begins, so an approval a subagent gives while main's turn runs is used at main's next check or call. A tool call takes the copy in `requestForExecution` and carries it in its request, because `executeToolCallAuthorized` sets the execution's list from `request.session_grants` and overwrites any list set on the context. A command's own `fx mcp call` is checked as part of its tool call, against that list. Main's own answer is also written to the instance's list at once, and the event the main loop handles for the same answer adds no second row. A copy that cannot be made leaves the turn's own list, so the call asks.

The path for calls that run together stores a grant for any caller, but it forms a group only when a turn has no live authority, so a subagent's turn never reached it. It stored nothing before and its behaviour is unchanged.

## How the list is protected

The instance's list of session approvals (`Agent.session_grants`) is guarded by the permission authority lock. Its writers already held that lock, and every agent's worker is now one of them. Its readers did not, and a reader could keep a slice that a growing list had freed. Every reader now takes the lock and copies what it keeps:

| Reader | Thread | Copy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main's permission checks, file-change checks and tool calls | the instance's worker | `mergeLiveGrants`, for a call through `requestForExecution`, into an arena that ends with the check or the call |
| The start of a turn | main loop | `copyGrants`, freed with the turn's snapshot |
| The queued-prompt sync | main loop | `copyGrants`, freed on return |
| The status line and `/permissions` | main loop | `liveGrantCount`, and `liveGrants` into the panel's arena |
| The trace report | main loop | `copyGrants`, into the report's arena |
| A subagent's resolve | the subagent's worker | already copied under the lock |

- `copyGrants`, `copyGrantsAfter` and `liveGrants` in `app_permission_runtime.zig` are the only functions that copy the list, and `liveGrantCount` the only one that counts it. `main.zig` and the other callers call them and take no lock of their own. The list itself comes only from `grantsLocked`, for the resolver, which already holds the lock. `viewOf` returns the mode and no longer a copy of the list's header. A tool context no longer holds main's approvals; the three calls that read them take a copy for the call.
- Lock order: a reader holds the authority lock while it copies and is called with no lock held. `liveGrantCount` and `liveGrants` also take the shell snapshot's own lock (`Owner.mutex` in `shell_snapshot.zig`) inside it, to tell whether a command grant still applies. `copyGrants`, `copyGrantsAfter` and the writers take no other lock. Nothing takes the two the other way round: `shell_snapshot.zig` never takes the authority lock. The early write holds the authority lock alone and lets go before it queues the event. The resolver takes the lock around other locks and calls none of the readers.
- This also closes a pair that already exists on `main`: an instance's own worker reads the list with no lock while the main loop writes it.

## What the grant covers

These are the cost of keeping it:

- A grant can cover more than the one action. A command's grant covers that exact command. A file change's grant inside the workspace covers editing, reading, globbing, and grepping files across the whole workspace.
- A grant skips the prompt for everything it covers, and in `auto` mode the automatic safety check of a command or an MCP tool it covers, for main as well as for the subagent that asked. In `auto` mode, a call that main's turn already refused after a safety caution stays refused for the rest of that turn, even when a later approval covers it; main's next turn runs it with no safety check. A file change inside the workspace is not checked in `auto` mode with or without a grant.
- A prompt that another agent already has open stays open. The grant applies to later requests.
- A grant given while a check of main's is already running applies from main's next check: the copy is taken when the check begins.
- A command's own `fx mcp call` is checked against the approvals as they stood when its tool call began, for main and for a subagent alike (a subagent's run resolves its list when its call begins). An approval given while the command already runs applies from the next tool call, and a `/permissions reset` while it runs does not reach it either. The first is run on the binary by `a subagent's always approval given while main's command runs does not reach that command's fx mcp call, which asks, and main's next command's call does not`, the second by `/permissions reset while main's command runs does not reach that command's fx mcp call, and main's next command's call asks`; the subagent half is read from `tool_runtime.zig`, where a call with a live authority takes `authority.grants`.
- Profile tool limits and rules that deny still win over a grant.
- `/permissions reset` clears the instance's list. Main's running turn then asks again for what only that list held, such as an approval a subagent gave. The approvals the turn's own answers made stay in its own list until the turn ends, so main runs those again with no prompt. `/new` and `/clear`, typed while main's turn runs, stop the turn and its subagents and drop queued prompts before the list is cleared; `/fork` and `/resume` wait until the turn ends, and the session they open starts with no approvals. Quitting frees the list after every worker is joined.
- The list has no cap. It grows by one for each command, outside root, or other request that a person approves with option 2, and by four for the first file change approved in the workspace. Main's permission check, file-change check, and tool call each take one copy, 1 + 2n allocations for n approvals, under the authority lock, and a command's nested `fx mcp call` takes none; the test `a merge of approvals makes one copy of the instance's list: a slice and two strings for each` asserts it for n = 1, 20 and 200. Each copy goes into an arena that ends with the check or the call, so a turn keeps none (`a check and an execution free their copy of the approvals when they return, so the turn's arena does not grow with them`).

A subagent whose profile lacks the tool is still refused, and a rule that denies still wins, for the subagent and for main (`an approval in the instance's list never makes a tool that main's turn does not offer available`, and the admission test below). An outside root covers only that root (the admission test). A second instance still asks (`a subagent's always approval stays in its instance: another instance's subagent still asks`). A subagent of a subagent (main, lead, inner) uses the grant at every level (`a nested subagent's always approval is kept: its parent subagent and main are not asked again`, `a lead subagent's always approval reaches the subagent it starts: inner is not asked`).

## Tests

Unit tests, 18, each named once:
- `src/core/agent/runtime/tests/tool_flow.zig`, 7: `a subagent's always approval of an ordinary call stores the session grant`; `a subagent's always approval of a file change stores the session grant`; `a subagent's always approval of a command stores the session grant`; `a subagent's always approval of an image path stores the session grant` (the orchestrator stores that one in a branch of its own); `a subagent's one-time approval stores no session grant`; `a subagent's one-time approval of an image path stores no session grant`; `a subagent's always approvals of two calls in one step store the session grants`.
- `src/core/subagent/authority.zig`: `a session approval lets an asked action run, and never a tool the child lacks or a denied one`.
- `src/core/app/app_agent_runtime.zig`, 4: `a merge of approvals makes one copy of the instance's list: a slice and two strings for each`; `the request an execution runs under holds the call's approvals, then the instance's, so a command's own check reads both`; `a check and an execution free their copy of the approvals when they return, so the turn's arena does not grow with them` (50 checks and 50 executions, with no approvals and with 200, against a turn arena that cannot grow past 256 KB; with the copy put back in the turn's arena it fails with `OutOfMemory`); `an approval in the instance's list never makes a tool that main's turn does not offer available`.
- `src/core/tooling/tool_runtime.zig`, 2: `a command's fx mcp call is checked against the approvals its tool call began with` (a real shell call through `executeToolCallAuthorized`, whose command's `fx mcp call` goes over the bridge: allowed with the approval in the request, and refused without it, with another tool's approval, with a deny rule, and for a tool the agent is not offered; the MCP tool runs once); `in auto mode a command's fx mcp call skips the safety check for the approved tool only` (the checks are counted: none for the approved tool, one for another tool and one for the same tool without the approval; the `auto` case of a command's `fx mcp call` is covered by this unit test only, and the end-to-end tests of that path run in `ask` mode). Neither fails on `83e1194e7`, where the defect was between them and the app: the first pins what the nested check reads, the second and the app's test above pin the other half, and the end-to-end tests below fail there.
- `src/core/tooling/tool_admission.zig`: `a session approval merged into a turn's list lets its command run with no prompt, and another command, a deny rule, and another root still win` (it also runs the command in `auto` mode, with a safety check that cannot run, and the command is allowed with no prompt).
- `src/main.zig`, 3: `a subagent's always approval reaches its instance's list at once, for main and its siblings only` (main's own answer is written at once too, and the event adds no second row); `main's check reads the approvals its instance holds when it checks, and no other instance's` (a turn whose own list lacks the approval, as a prompt that waits has); `subagents' workers and main's worker add approvals while main's worker and main's thread read them` (the threaded test).

End to end, 19 tests in `tests/e2e/tui-host-instances.test.ts`:
- Kept: `a subagent's always approval of a command is kept: it is not asked again, nor is its sibling or main`; `a subagent's always approval of a file change is kept: it is not asked again, nor is its sibling or main`; `a subagent's always approval of an MCP tool is kept: it is not asked again, nor is its sibling or main`; `a nested subagent's always approval is kept: its parent subagent and main are not asked again`; `a subagent's always approval stays in its instance: another instance's subagent still asks`; `a subagent's one-time approval is not kept: its next run, and main's, ask again`.
- Main's running turn: `a subagent's always approval of a command reaches main's running turn: main runs it later in that turn with no prompt`; `a subagent's always approval of a file change reaches main's running turn: main writes later in that turn with no prompt`; `a subagent's always approval of an MCP tool reaches main's running turn: main calls it later in that turn with no prompt`; `in auto mode a subagent's always approval of a command lets main run it later in its running turn with no safety check, and another command still gets one` (it counts the safety checks that reach the fake gateway: exactly one, for the other command); `a prompt typed in main's running turn is taken into it, and runs a command a subagent was just given always for with no prompt`.
- A command's own `fx mcp call` in main's running turn: `a subagent's always approval of an MCP tool reaches main's running turn: main's command calls it with fx mcp call later in that turn with no prompt`; `a subagent's always approval given while main's command runs does not reach that command's fx mcp call, which asks, and main's next command's call does not`; `/permissions reset while main's command runs does not reach that command's fx mcp call, and main's next command's call asks`.
- Running agents: `main's always approval reaches a subagent that is running, which runs the same command with no prompt`; `a subagent's always approval reaches a sibling that is running, which runs the same command with no prompt`; `a lead subagent's always approval reaches the subagent it starts: inner is not asked`.
- Reset: `/permissions reset in main's running turn clears an approval a subagent gave: main's later check asks`; `/permissions reset in main's running turn keeps the approvals the turn's own answers made: main runs its command again with no prompt`.

On the source of `c87a13a96` with these 16 tests (`git checkout c87a13a96 -- src`, `zig build`, then `cd tests/e2e && FX_SOUND=0 bun test tui-host-instances.test.ts -t '<the 16 names>' --rerun-each 2`, Debug, Linux), four fail in both runs: the command, the MCP tool, the typed prompt and the `auto`-mode test, each at main's running turn. The other 12 pass there, the two reset tests among them, because they pin what a reset does and not what a subagent's approval reaches.

On the source of `83e1194e7` with the three nested-call tests (`git checkout 83e1194e7 -- src`, `zig build`, then `cd tests/e2e && FX_SOUND=0 bun test tui-host-instances.test.ts -t '<the three names>' --rerun-each 1`, Debug, Linux, the test file of `87f22e9a2`), all three fail. In the first, both commands' calls of the tool ask in main's turn, where none should. In the second, main's next command's call asks, where it should not. In the third, the first command's call waits at a prompt.

Counts, all Debug and Linux x86_64 unless stated. The counts at `2f616df85` use Zig 0.17.1. Those at `70cd3ce91` and `83e1194e7` were taken with Zig 0.17.0, before `main` moved to 0.17.1:
- At `2f616df85`, the head after merging `main` at `c36d7b3d4`: each of the 19 E2E tests ran 20 times, 380 pass, 0 fail, and each test passed exactly 20 times (`cd tests/e2e && FX_SOUND=0 bun test tui-host-instances.test.ts -t '<the 19 names>' --rerun-each 20`, after `zig build`). On the macOS arm64 build of that commit each ran 5 times (`FXC_LOCAL=1`, `--rerun-each 5`): 95 pass, 0 fail.
- At `70cd3ce91`, on the macOS arm64 build, the same tests ran 5 times in five passes (`FXC_LOCAL=1`, `--rerun-each 5`): 94 pass and 1 fail in the first, and 95 pass in each of the other four. The failure was `a subagent's always approval reaches a sibling that is running, which runs the same command with no prompt`, which showed `HTTP 501` on main's first request, before any approval. It is not attributed. fx shows the status it receives and never makes up a 501, and the test's fake gateway answers none, so the answer did not come from fx or from that gateway. The gateway is `Bun.serve({ port: 0 })` and fx is pointed at `127.0.0.1` on its port; on the Mac the passes ran on, a second `Bun.serve` on `127.0.0.1` with the same port bound and then answered the requests sent there with its own status, and whether that happened is not known. The last three passes kept fx's trace and the gateway's request log: 285 tests, no 501, no failure. That test also ran 30 times on the same build with 30 passes.
- At `2f616df85` the 18 unit tests, in a filtered build of 45 tests (the 18 and the 27 unnamed `test_0` blocks that Zig always includes), ran 100 times with 0 failures, and every run printed the `OK` line of each of the 18 names. The copy test also ran 20 times in a ReleaseSafe build on Linux x86_64 at `83e1194e7` (`zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe -Dtest-filter='a check and an execution free their copy'`): 0 failures. Its result on macOS arm64 ReleaseSafe is CI's: the job `macOS arm64 unit tests` (`zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe`) passes at `83e1194e7`. The counts come from a Linux sandbox with a local `build.zig` edit, not in this PR, that adds a `-Dtest-filter` option to the `test` step, with one filter per line: `zig build test -Dtest-filter="$(cat names.txt)"` with the 18 names in `names.txt`, then `for i in $(seq 100); do "$bin" || echo FAIL; done` on the built test binary that holds them.
- The threaded test, built with `zig build test -Dsanitize-thread=true -Dtest-filter=<its name>` and run 20 times at `2f616df85`: 0 failing runs, 0 reports. With the lock removed from `copyGrantsAfter` it reported a data race in 5 of 5 runs at `70cd3ce91`, one of them with an allocation-size error from a torn length.
- On a ThreadSanitizer build of fx (`zig build -Dsanitize-thread=true`) at `2f616df85`, the 19 E2E tests pass once each (19 pass, 0 fail) and write no report (`TSAN_OPTIONS=log_path=/tmp/tsan-e2e/report:exitcode=0:halt_on_error=0`, then 0 files in `/tmp/tsan-e2e`).
- The unit test `a command's fx mcp call is checked against the approvals its tool call began with` runs a real shell command, and under ThreadSanitizer (`zig build test -Dsanitize-thread=true -Dtest-filter=<its name>` at `2f616df85`, Debug, Linux x86_64, Zig 0.17.1) it reports one `thread leak` at exit and no race, as it did at `70cd3ce91`. At `70cd3ce91` the leaked thread was symbolized: it is the shell snapshot's capture thread, created at `src/core/terminal/shell_snapshot.zig:686` (`startCaptureLocked`, from `acquire`, from `executeWithSnapshot`). `src/core/terminal/shell_snapshot.zig` is unchanged on `main` since `3fd4905af`; the stack of the `2f616df85` run was not symbolized, because its sandbox has no symbolizer. `main` at `3fd4905af` reports the same for any test that runs a command through the snapshot: its test `user profile commands reuse one startup-file snapshot` reports it with the same stack, and so does this test added to `main`'s code. The nightly ThreadSanitizer job (`.github/workflows/tsan.yml`) runs with `exitcode=0` and `continue-on-error: true`, so a report does not fail it.

## Not in this change

- ACP and `fx ask` never offer a subagent's permission request to the client or the user: the child waits on it in its own worker (`requestChildPermission`, `src/core/subagent/execution.zig`) and nothing there answers it, and `src/acp` builds `session/request_permission`, with "Allow for this session", only for main's own prompts (`src/acp/prompt.zig`). A child's approval therefore never exists there, and `propagate_grant = discardGrant` (`src/core/subagent/agent_adapter.zig`) is not reached.
- `fx ask` offers only once or deny, with no session choice.
- A prompt of main that waits for its turn with a list taken earlier reads the instance's list at its check too. No end-to-end test holds that window, and one unit test covers the check (`main's check reads the approvals its instance holds when it checks, and no other instance's`).

## Docs

https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx-web/pull/300

title: Support Workflow dashboard replay for durable Libfx sessions
body:
Libfx saves raw `{}` as Workflow run input, so dashboard replay fails in Workflow's format decoder. Save a session descriptor with Workflow's codec and handle standard replay deliveries by copying the first saved prompt, context, settings, and image bytes into a fresh session.

Validate the source, parent, agent, and store before execution. Later prompts and prior tool results are not copied; tools can run again. Older raw-JSON runs still require starting a new session. Vercel needs a separate private replay queue route. App-supplied in-process Worlds retain their own standard Workflow handler; automatic replay registration is limited to Worlds Libfx constructs.

The adapter build pins @workflow/core at 5.2.1 and overrides its devalue and nanoid dependencies to 5.9.3 and 5.1.16. This addresses GHSA-j22f-vq7h-c4qm, GHSA-xwg4-73v4-xw9w, and GHSA-28wg-ghj8-5hjv before the adapters are bundled. npm audit no longer flags either dependency; other existing advisories remain.

Validation:
- Five focused replay and ownership tests pass: same/latest deployment, duplicate deliveries, images, first-prompt semantics, invalid descriptors, routing across stores, the real local queue, and preservation of an application's existing handler.
- Core suites passed: memory 55, local 58, app-built World 60, and queue 105. Native durable suites passed on memory 61, local 58, and app-built World 55; the local/World/queue core suites and native World suite were rerun after the final changes.
- Built fresh native addons and WebAssembly surfaces and exercised the real engine. After the security patches, a cancelled Vercel run replayed on its original deployment and a new deployment. Both stored encrypted arguments and produced LIBFX_REPLAY_VERIFIED with successful turn-end events. The model transport was a deterministic fixture; execution used the actual native engine, Workflow World, and Vercel Queues.
- Durable state model checks, all 10 required local model drivers, and all 55 native durable tests against Vercel storage passed. The remote Vercel model driver remains in progress.
- The regenerated package passes its size guard. Only the overall package budgets increase to accommodate Workflow's bundled codec; WebAssembly, engine, and platform-addon budgets stay unchanged.
- Independent final code review reports no remaining high-confidence findings at f51ec6ec. Required CI is running for that commit. The broad local Zig suite has 15 shell-command failures caused by existing shell profile startup errors; the same stderr reproduces outside Libfx. No user shell files were changed.

Docs: https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx-web/pull/316 documents the second replay route, first-prompt replay semantics, and the shared in-process World limitation.

title: Report out of memory in the Still running label check
body:
## Summary

- When memory runs out while fx reads a shell result, the row of a command that still runs no longer falls back to `Ran`. The error is reported as other allocation failures are.
- A shell result that is not JSON still gives no `Still running` decision, as before.

title: Read subagent request wrappers sent as JSON text like objects
body:
## Summary

- Models sometimes wrap a subagent call's arguments in a `request` field, and some write that wrapper as JSON text, such as `{"request":"{\"action\":\"message\",\"agent\":\"worker\",\"message\":\"...\"}"}`. fx unwrapped an object wrapper of a `run` or `message` call at intake and in history replay, but kept a text wrapper as sent. Subagent decode reads an object wrapper of any action but never a text one, so every text-wrapped call got the "request must be an object" correction and never ran, and its row named no action.
- Subagent intake (`normalized_subagent_request_arguments` in `src/core/agent/runtime/orchestrator.zig`) now reads the wrapper through `tool_args.unwrapRequest`, as shell intake and read_tool_result replay already do. An object wrapper is unwrapped for `run` and `message`, as before. A text wrapper is unwrapped whatever it asks for, so a text-wrapped `run`, `message`, `wait`, `status`, `stop`, or `close` is admitted, reviewed, and stored with its top-level arguments, and decode judges its fields.
- History replay reads a text wrapper of `run` and `message` the same way, the only calls it summarizes. A session saved before this change replays an old text-wrapped call with its top-level arguments next to the correction it got then, as read_tool_result replay does.
- The subagent rows (`subagentAction` and `subagentRoster` in `src/core/tooling/tool_presentation.zig`) read a text wrapper the same way, so a row names the action that runs.
- A wrapper beside another field, text that is not an object, and text nested past the 64-level limit still reach subagent decode as sent. Decode still accepts only an object wrapper, so a call that skips intake cannot run in a form admission did not see unwrapped.

## Testing

- `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`: a subagent message whose wrapper is JSON text reaches the worker, the parent's result carries no correction, the saved call has top-level arguments, and a following text-wrapped `status` call reports the worker. It fails on main with the "request must be an object" correction.
- The subagent tests in that file pass: 45 with `-t '^(?!.*subagent failure retains its cause).*(subagent|worker|child|delegat|JSON text)'`, which leaves out one test that times out only in the fx-cloud sandbox, on main too. And `tests/e2e/tui-host-switch.test.ts`, whose TUI rows show wrapped subagent calls, passes with real tmux (52).
- Inline tests cover intake with text-wrapped `message`, `run`, `wait`, and action-less calls (unwrapped; `message` and `run` to the same bytes as the object form), and non-object text, 70-level text, an extra field, and object-wrapped other actions (kept as sent), plus the rows. The `request_wrapper_text` fuzz target now also checks that subagent intake unwraps exactly the text wrappers `tool_args` reads and that replay unwraps only `run` and `message`; it ran with no failure. The changed code's tests also pass under ThreadSanitizer, run with a local test filter.

title: Let CI runs on main finish instead of cancelling them
body:
## Summary

- A push to `main` no longer cancels the CI run already in progress on `main`. The newer push waits, and GitHub keeps only the newest waiting run.
- Pull requests still cancel their older CI runs when a new commit arrives.

title: Stop steered background commands when a turn is cancelled
body:
## Summary

- Pressing Escape twice to cancel a turn now stops every shell command that steering moved to the background during that turn, for both captured and tty commands.
- Cancelling a subagent's turn does the same for that subagent's steered commands.
- Each stop works like the shell `stop` action: graceful first, then forced if the command still runs.
- Commands the model started in the background itself (`yield_time_ms` 0), commands from earlier turns, and commands of turns that end normally or because steering ended them keep running.
- A shell call with `yield_time_ms` 0 no longer carries a steering notice, since steering never moved its command.
- ACP and `fx ask` turns are unchanged.

## Docs

`using-fx/working-with-fx`, Steering section. Replace the shell command bullet:

> While a shell command is running, fx moves the command to the background and continues with your follow-up. The command keeps running, and fx can still check on it or stop it.

with:

> While a shell command is running, fx moves the command to the background and continues with your follow-up. The command keeps running, and fx can still check on it or stop it. If you then press `escape` twice to interrupt that turn, fx stops the commands it moved to the background during it.

title: Ask AI Gateway to cache libfx requests
body:
## Summary

- libfx requests on the native and WebAssembly backends ask AI Gateway to cache their stable start, as fx CLI requests do.
- Later turns of a libfx session read that start from the cache instead of paying for it as new input again.
- Claude, OpenAI, and Amazon Nova requests from libfx mark their stable start in each model family's own cache syntax.

## Before and after

A three-turn `createFxAgent` session on `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`, about 3,260 input tokens per request:

| Backend | Input read from the cache, turns 2 and 3, on main | With this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native | 0 and 0 | 3,258 and 3,278 |
| WebAssembly | 0 and 0 | 3,278 and 3,298 |

title: Close quietly when a closed window refuses a frame
body:
## Summary

When the window closes, fx usually sees its input end first and closes as SIGHUP does: it saves the request in flight marked clean and leaves the turn open, so the next launch resumes it (`tests/tla/recovery/Resume.tla` `Close`). Sometimes a frame write comes first. That write fails with EIO, and so does the cleanup write `recoverPartialFrame` sends after it. The renderer then returned `TerminalSyncRecoveryFailed`, which `app_entry_runtime` treats as an unexpected error: fx printed `fx: terminal sync recovery failed`, exited with status 1, and skipped `closeOnHangup`.

- `terminal_diff.recoverPartialFrame` returns `TerminalOutputClosed` when the cleanup write fails because the terminal is gone: `InputOutput` (EIO, a closed window or a tty that hung up), `BrokenPipe` (EPIPE), or `NotOpenForWriting` (EBADF). Any other cleanup failure still returns `TerminalSyncRecoveryFailed`. The trace line for a failed cleanup now names the write error.
- `app_entry_runtime` handles `TerminalOutputClosed` as it does `TerminalInputClosed`: `closeOnHangup` before the terminal is released, then the process-exit shutdown, with nothing on stderr.

## How it was found

The TUI's reopened-recovery tests, run under a ThreadSanitizer build, close the window while a request is held open. The extra slowdown lets a frame write reach the closed terminal before the input loop sees it close. On `main`, 2 of 40 and 3 of 40 runs failed with `fx: terminal sync recovery failed` in the first session's stderr. Without ThreadSanitizer the input side wins the race, so the normal build rarely shows it.

## Testing

- New unit tests: `flushFrame` returns `TerminalOutputClosed` for each of the three write errors, and the app entry closes for `TerminalOutputClosed` with `hangup-close` before `terminal-release` and an empty stderr. Both fail on `main` and pass with this change.
- The same ThreadSanitizer run, 80 times with this change: 80 pass, no `terminal sync recovery failed`, no race reports.
- macOS: `./zig-out/bin/fx` in tmux, closing the window after typing in the composer, exits with an empty stderr. The reopened-recovery and hang-up-before-SIGHUP TUI tests pass 9 of 9 on the macOS build.

title: Wait for a slow terminal backend before a terminal test frees it
body:
## Summary

- When fx exits, `SupportedRegistry.closeAllForExit` in `src/core/terminal/native_session.zig` gives terminal backend threads `exit_join_ms` (500 ms). A backend that is still draining stays allocated on purpose, and `Runtime.deinit` in `src/core/terminal/client.zig` logs "terminal backend left allocated: threads still draining".
- Under load, "closing owned terminals for exit leaves no orphan and records them ended" can miss that budget. `std.testing.allocator` then reports the kept session id from `generateTerminalSessionId` and its 120-byte record as leaks, and the test binary aborts.
- `LiveTerminalFixture.deinit` now ends its terminals and waits up to 10 s for such a backend through a new `joinDrainingBackendsBefore`, then frees it. fx's own exit path and its 500 ms budget are unchanged, and the test still checks that the exit close stays under 1.5 s.
- The registry for hosts other than macOS and Linux gets the same `joinDrainingBackendsBefore`, reporting nothing left to drain as its `closeAllForExit` does, so the test build for those hosts fails no more than on `main`.
- A local copy that makes the exit join report "still draining" whenever less than 1 s is left gives the same leak on `main` in 5 of 5 runs, and passes 5 of 5 with this change.

title: Stop deeply nested MCP server JSON from crashing fx
body:
## Summary

An MCP server could crash fx by sending JSON nested about 257 levels deep. fx wrote a server's tool result and a listed tool again with `std.json.Stringify`, and an elicitation form goes through the same writers. In Debug and ReleaseSafe builds it keeps 256 levels of nesting in a fixed stack and aborts past it (`index out of bounds: index 32, len 32`), while the engine hands the host a message up to 2,584 levels deep. The host now checks that JSON where it turns it into a value, with one limit of 128 levels.

## What crashed

I proved it with the built fx through `fx ask` and through ACP, on the Debug build and on the ReleaseSafe build that fx ships. Both builds gave the same result at every place, 198 runs each. The value's depth is counted from the root the host checks.

- **A tool call's result**, from 257 levels: `structuredContent`, a content item's `_meta`, a content item's `annotations`.
- **A listed tool**, from 258 levels, when fx connects and before any call: the tool's `_meta`, `annotations` and `icons`.
- **An elicitation form** crashes nothing in the built fx, because it never gets that deep: every form passes `mrtr.parseRequestJsonForWire` first, which refuses JSON deeper than 32 levels (`src/core/mcp/mrtr.zig`). The form check below is a second layer that no server reaches, and the Zig tests call `parseRequest` directly. Without the check, a form 257 or 258 levels deep aborts in the ACP projection (`_meta`) and in the requested schema's writer. The commit message says a form crashed fx at those depths. That is not true for the built fx, and the message stays as it is.

`fx ask` exits 134 (SIGABRT). In ACP the panic prints, the process stays up, and the session never answers.

Not reached: a result's own `_meta` (the host drops it), a tool's `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` (already refused per tool past 64 levels), and an error's `data` (the host drops it, and #1960 bounds it to 128 levels).

## What fx does now

`src/core/mcp/server_json_depth.zig` holds `max_server_json_depth = 128` and `within`, which walks the value with its own stack of at most 128 frames, never recurses, and stops at the first level past the limit. A value nested 100,000 levels costs no more than one nested 129. The limit is below the 256-level stack with room for the levels a writer adds around a value (none adds more than 2, and the comment allows 4). `tests/tla/mcp/WireDepth.tla` `NoWriterOverflow` states it: whatever an entry point accepts, every writer behind it can write.

Four places call it:

- `parseCallOutcome` checks the `result`. Past the limit the call ends with a tool error: "MCP protocol failure: the server's reply is nested deeper than fx accepts (128 levels)". The four-line arm that says so is in `tool_result.zig`.
- `parseTool` checks the tool object after its schemas, so a schema past 64 levels is still refused as a schema. A tool past the limit is left out and its server's other tools stay.
- `parseRequest` checks the whole form, `_meta` and requested schema both. It is refused with `LimitExceeded`, as a form over any other limit is. As said above, no server reaches this check through fx, because the 32-level limit comes first.
- `parseProtocolError` leaves out an error's `data` past the limit and keeps the code and the message. #1960 also bounds `data`, so this is a second layer: one rule at every place the host turns server JSON into a value, even if that cap changes.

`src/core/shared/json_depth.zig` also exists: it limits the raw text of a provider's JSON to 64 levels, before it is parsed. The new file is named `server_json_depth.zig` so the two are not mixed up, and each header says how it differs.

Each refusal writes one trace line with the code, the limit and the place, and no server text: `MCP server JSON refused code=NestingTooDeep limit=128 at=<result|tool|form|data>`.

## Tests

- Zig tests in `tools.zig`, `elicitation.zig` and `server_json_depth.zig`: each entry point at 127, 128, 129, 256 and 300 levels, in arrays, objects and mixed nesting, through each field above; nesting inside a string, a shallow result that holds one 1 MiB string, a successful result's bytes unchanged, an error's `data` at 128 and 129, and the exact trace lines with no server text. `server_json_depth_testing.zig` builds the nested texts and values, and only tests import it.
- 16 e2e tests in `mcp-stdio.test.ts` and 5 in `acp.test.ts`, with the options `FX_MCP_DEEP_SITE`, `_DEPTH`, `_SHAPE` and `_FAULT` in `mcp-legacy-stdio.mjs`: each place at 127 and 128 (unchanged) and past the limit (refused, fx stays up, the model gets the words, the server's other tool still works), a deep error `data` that reaches the model with its message (no refusal is traced, because the host drops `data`), a reply cut inside the nesting, and a result nested 3,000 levels deep, past the engine's own limit (below).
- Fuzz target `mcp_json_depth` with 84 saved inputs, registered at 100,000 iterations: whatever the site, shape and depth, an entry point refuses past 128 levels, keeps up to it, and never aborts.
- `WireDepth.tla`, with a findings config for the code before this change and six planted bugs: the limit removed, the limit above the stack less a writer's wrapper, a writer with a larger wrapper, one entry point that skips the check, and the limit off by one each way. `wire-depth.test.ts` runs 28 real `fx ask` cases against it through a trace wrapper, and the model of the host before the limit rejects the same trace. The u01 and u12 scenarios pin the engine's own limit: a message decodes up to 2,584 levels and not 2,585.
- Planted bugs, each caught by named tests: the limit set to 127 or to 129, the form check removed (the writer then aborts, as it did), and the test helper that builds a nested value making one level too few. To repeat one, change `max_server_json_depth` in `server_json_depth.zig`, or replace `server_json_depth.require(parsed.value, .form) catch return error.LimitExceeded;` in `elicitation.zig` with `_ = server_json_depth;`, and run `zig build test`.

The failing tests were written first and recorded failing on the code before the change: the e2e tests with SIGABRT, the Zig tests by assertion or abort, the driver `REJECTED`, the fuzz replay by assertion.

## Where each check ran

All of it on the head of this pull request after the merge of `main` that carries #2069, with the keys unset and `FX_SOUND=0`. The Zig tests, the models and the fuzz replays ran on Linux x86_64, and the e2e tests ran against a ReleaseSafe build made there.

- Zig, the group `core.mcp.` of unit tests (`zig build test` runs them with the rest): 157 tests, 0 failed. They include the 28 tests of `tools.zig`, the 26 of `elicitation.zig` (27 with a scratch probe), the 5 of `server_json_depth.zig` and the 16 of `tool_result.zig`. The four planted bugs above each fail named tests, for example the limit at 127 fails 9 and the limit at 129 fails 9.
- e2e: `bun test mcp-stdio.test.ts`, the whole file: 136 pass, 0 fail. `bun test acp.test.ts -t "nested"`: 5 pass.
- The new e2e test, `a result nested past the engine's own limit ends the call after the grace…`: 30.1 seconds, passes. On the head before the merge of #2010 (`2d349ad0c`) it fails at its 60 second limit. With the engine's grace planted at 1 second (`Timeouts.refused_ms` in `src/mcp/core/request.zig`) it fails after 1.2 seconds.
- TLA+: `sh tests/tla/mcp/check.sh` exits 0, with `WireDepth.findings` and `Request.findings` violated as required, in one `tlc_verdicts` block. `bun test ./tests/tla/drivers/mcp_host/wire-depth.test.ts`: 3 pass. `bun tests/tla/drivers/mcp/driver.ts`: every scenario passes, among them the u01 and u12 cases at 2,584 and 2,585 levels.
- Fuzz replays: `zig build fuzz -Dfuzz-target=mcp_json_depth` and `-Dfuzz-target=mcp_request_grace`, both exit 0.
- `zig fmt --check src/` and `scripts/check-public-surface.sh` exit 0, and `bun test ci-shards.test.ts` passes (11 tests) with the new weight of `mcp-stdio.test.ts`.

## Notes for the merge

- **Shared driver code:** `tests/tla/drivers/mcp_host/tlc.ts` and `trace.ts` gain an optional `specDir`, so a trace check can use a model that is not in `tests/tla/mcp_host/`. `WireDepth.tla` is in `tests/tla/mcp/`, with its findings verdict in a `tlc_verdicts` block at the end of `tests/tla/mcp/check.sh`. #1914 and #1953 add findings blocks to the same file: this branch already has `Request`'s findings line and `WireDepth`'s in one `tlc_verdicts` block after the merge of #2010, and whichever of the others lands next adds its line to that block.
- **Near other PRs:** #830 edits `tool_result.zig` at lines 23 to 29, nine lines from the new arm. #823 edits the import block at the top of `elicitation.zig`, where one import is added. #1960 and #1815 do not touch these hunks. The legacy fixture, `u12-engine.ts` and `trace.ts` are text conflicts only.

## Not changed here

- **A reply past the engine's own limit** (2,585 levels or more) is dropped by the engine before the host sees it. Since #2010, a message with no readable id ends its call after the engine's grace for an unreadable line (30 seconds), as "the server's answer was malformed", and the call is cancelled on the server. A new e2e test pins that with a result nested 3,000 levels deep and its id first, as a real server writes it: the call ends after about 30 seconds, the model gets the malformed words and not the depth limit's, and no depth refusal is traced. The test fails on this branch before the merge of #2010, where the call waits for the 60 seconds the test allows.
- **A tool dropped at connect** is reported only by a trace line (`MCP tool left out … err=NestingTooDeep`), as every dropped tool is.
- **A refused form** is declined silently on every surface. The TUI form prompt and `fx ask` log "MCP question not answered … err=LimitExceeded" and answer nothing, and ACP does the same. No surface gives the user words, and a notice would be a new feature in `runtime.zig` or `model.zig`. The depth case adds its own trace line, pinned by a test.
- The toolbox and ACP writers of the model's own arguments (`toolbox.zig`, `prompt.zig`) take model text, not a server's JSON.

## Not verified

- The TUI. It uses the same host path as `fx ask` and ACP, and I did not run it.
- A form past the limit end to end: no client can send one through fx, because of the 32-level limit that comes first.
- ReleaseFast and ReleaseSmall, which have no 256-level stack.

## Docs

The fx.sh protocol page states the schema limit of 64 levels. A one-sentence change for the new limit is in vercel-labs/fx-web#318, a draft that goes out when this ships.

title: Send a smaller compaction request after a too-long refusal
body:
## Summary

- fx fits a compaction request to the model's window with its own token estimate. A provider that counts more tokens refuses the request as too long. The compactor then sent the same text to the fallback model, the compaction failed, and the turn ended with `ModelFailed`.
- The compactor's caller now reports that refusal as an overflow. It uses the check the agent's own request already uses to recover (`isContextOverflow`), which moves from the orchestrator to `stream_provider.zig`, next to `Failure`.
- The compactor then writes the turns out again within three quarters of the refused request, as the agent's own request recovers, and asks again, at most three times. When none fits, it fails with `ModelFailed` as before, so its callers see the same errors.
- When the conversation's model refuses as too long and the fallback model fails for another reason, the compactor still tries the smaller request. A fallback that answers still wins.
- A refusal for another reason is not retried smaller. An overflow on the request after the conversation still falls back to the turns written out.
- Every compaction gets this: the one during a turn, the overflow recovery, and `/compact`.

## Testing

- `tests/e2e/compaction-policy.test.ts`: a fake gateway refuses every compaction request over 200 KB, in OpenAI's and in Anthropic's wording. On main both turns end with `ModelFailed`. Now a smaller request fits, and the turn ends with its reply. Two bound cases: a refusal as too long every time ends the turn after 8 compaction requests (four rounds, each on the conversation's model and the fallback), and a refusal for another reason after 2, as on main. 13 of 13 pass in the file.
- `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`: "HTTP 413 during compaction preserves the completed local tool without replay" now expects the smaller requests: a 413 counts as too large, as it does for the agent's own request, so the compaction asks four rounds of two before the turn fails. The tool still runs once.
- Inline tests in `summarize.zig`, `model.zig`, and `stream_provider.zig` cover each wording, the three-quarter step, the bound, a refusal that is not an overflow, the fallback, and the request after the conversation. 600 of 602 focused unit tests pass (2 skipped), and the same tests pass under ThreadSanitizer, both run with a local test filter over the compactor, overflow, and fallback tests.
- Six planted bugs, one for each rule, each make a test fail.
- `scripts/check-compactor-boundary.sh`, `zig fmt --check`, and `scripts/check-public-surface.sh` pass.

## Docs

None: the manual does not describe how compaction recovers from a refused request.

title: Surface log errors while waiting for a committed root turn
body:
## Summary

`committedRootTurns` in `tests/e2e/saved-sessions.ts` caught every error and returned 0. A broken complete line in a session log, or a superseded turn that the `logLines` assertion rejects, therefore showed up only as a 10 s timeout ("no root session committed more than N turns") in the tests that use `waitForRootTurnCommitted`. A direct call, as in the configured-providers resume test, could also read 0 and let the next wait pass at once.

The helper now skips only what fx has not written yet:

- a missing store, session folder, or log (`ENOENT`)
- a session whose first line is still being written (the log reader already leaves out an incomplete last line, so no `SyntaxError` has to be caught)

Every other error is thrown with its own message. Child sessions are still left out by the role on their first line.

## Callers checked

- `configured-providers.test.ts`: the three `subagent requests preserve connection` cases and `persistent child capabilities stay bound when the parent changes providers`, which also calls `committedRootTurns` directly
- `gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`: `ask continues and persists a healthy parent when its child's session is gone`
- `sessions.test.ts`: `fx ask runs a subagent as a v2 child with its own log, recorded in the parent's log`

## Testing

- New `sessions.test.ts` case, with no fx process: no store, a folder with no log, and a partial first line count as 0; a child's turns and a partial last line are left out; a broken complete line rejects with `SyntaxError`, and a superseded turn rejects with the assertion that names it, not the timeout. With the old helper the case fails: `Received message: "no root session committed more than 0 turns"`.
- The caller tests above, 5 runs each: all pass.
- `configured-providers.test.ts` in full: 116 pass, 0 fail.

title: Stop the MCP task limit test from hanging the unit tests
body:
## Summary

A full `zig build test` run could hang for many minutes in `src/mcp/io/process.zig`, with a thread blocked reading the stderr of a bare `cat` while the test binary still held that cat's stdin.

The cause is the test "a start whose tasks can't all run closes each of the server's pipes once". It starts `exec cat >/dev/null` where only one, two, or three tasks can run, and expects the start to fail with `ConcurrencyUnavailable`. The shell points cat's stdout at `/dev/null`, so the stdout reader reads EOF at once and frees its task slot. On a busy machine that happens before the spawn asks for the next task, so every task runs and the start succeeds. The check then failed with `expected error.ConcurrencyUnavailable, found null` and returned before `p.deinit()`. Cat kept its stdin open, its readers and exit watcher kept running, and `defer threaded.deinit()` waited for them forever.

This is a test bug. The product spawn and its error paths close every pipe, and the pipes are made with CLOEXEC, so no descriptor leaks into other children.

## Changes

- The server is now `exec cat`, which keeps stdout and stderr open until its stdin closes, so no task the start runs can end and free its slot.
- Each limit runs in `startWithTaskLimit`, which defers `p.deinit()` before `threaded.deinit()`. A failed check now fails the test instead of hanging it.

## Testing

- Stress run of the file's tests on Linux, 16 at a time with 4 busy loops: before, 2 of 619 runs hung in this test with the message above; after, 640 of 640 passed.
- With a 200 ms sleep put into the spawn before the stderr reader and the exit watcher start: the old test hangs until `timeout 60` kills it; the new test passes; the new test with the old server fails at once with `TestExpectedEqual`.
- `zig fmt --check src/`

title: Read v1 sessions an older release left readable by others
body:
## Summary

`fx session recover <id>` printed `record is corrupt; run fx doctor for recovery guidance` (exit 1) for a healthy v1 session when an older release left its files readable by others: folders 0755, files 0644, which is also what a plain `cp -r` of `tests/fixtures/v1-sessions` gives. The same sessions failed `fx sessions convert` (`unreadable: the conversion failed (PrivateStatePermissionsUnsupported)`), and `fx session <id>` refused one with a saved tool result. D61 in `tests/tla/session_manager/system-design.md` says these sessions convert, and D64 says a healthy v1 session answers that no recovery is needed.

Root cause: three checks on v1's read path required private modes before anything looked at the session's health.

- `v1_conversion.lockOpened` took v1's `session.lock` with `io_mod.acquireTimedAdvisoryLock`, which refuses a lock file that is not 0600.
- `SessionChildCapability.initLegacySubagentControl`, which `kindOf` uses, required the v1 `subagent/` folder to be 0700.
- The read-only capability v1's readers open on the session folder (`restoreExecutionResultBodies` for `fx session <id>`, `recoverableState` for salvage) required 0700.

`session_adapter.commandError` then mapped the leftover `PrivateStatePermissionsUnsupported` to `InvalidSessionFormat`, which the CLI prints as a corrupt record.

The existing D61 test changes only folder modes, not file modes, and on Linux its `setPermissions` on an `O_PATH` handle makes it skip, so nothing covered a lock file others can read.

## Changes

- `io.zig`: `acquireTimedAdvisoryLockOnOlderFile` takes an existing lock file that only its owner can write, keeps its mode, and still creates a missing one private. `acquireTimedAdvisoryLock` is unchanged for every other caller.
- `session_child_store.zig`: the read-only legacy `subagent/` route and a new `SessionChildCapability.initOlderReadOnly` accept a folder only its owner can write. Writable routes and `init` still require 0700.
- `v1_conversion.zig`, `session_log.zig`, `session_store.zig`: v1's lock and read-only capability use those.
- `session_adapter.zig`: `commandError` maps `PrivateStatePermissionsUnsupported` to `DurablePathUnsafe`, so a v1 file others can write reads as unsafe storage, not a corrupt record.

Recover still refuses a healthy session, as D64 says, with `SessionRecoveryNotNeeded` and exit 1: `recovery was refused because the session has a valid commit boundary; resume it normally`.

## Verification

- New E2E `recover answers that a whole v1 family an old fx left readable by others needs none, and the family still converts` in `tests/e2e/session-recovery.test.ts`. It fails on `origin/main` (`Expected: "SessionRecoveryNotNeeded"`, `Received: "InvalidSessionFormat"`) and passes with this change.
- New unit tests: the older-file lock in `io.zig`; readable v1 family and damaged readable v1 salvage, and a lock others can write, in `session_adapter.zig`.
- Every v1 fixture kind, copied with 0755/0644 modes, through `fx session`, `fx session recover` and `fx sessions convert` on the built binary: all show, all answer `SessionRecoveryNotNeeded`, all convert. Also run with the macOS arm64 binary.
- `zig fmt --check src/`, `python3 -m scripts.check_cli_shape` (`CLI shape: ok`), `zig build test` (only the known sandbox-only failures).
- `tests/tla/session_manager/check.sh`: SessionLog, TurnLifecycle, WriterLock, ResumeSnapshot, Fork, ForkChildren, Subagents, Catalog, Lifecycle, Wiring and MoveSideFiles found no error. V1Conversion, which models salvage, found no error in 28 minutes (14.2M distinct states) but did not finish, and PromptImages did not run. The models do not cover file modes, so this change leaves them as they are.

## Docs

No page change needed. `using-fx/cli`, `using-fx/sessions` and `using-fx/troubleshooting` describe `fx session recover` and stay correct.

title: Stop steered commands after the cancelled turn ends
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1984. When the user cancels a turn, fx stops the shell commands that steering moved to the background during it. Those stops ran one after another before fx reported the turn, so a command that ignores SIGTERM made the turn end about 3 s later in a terminal (about 1.2 s for a captured command), and each further such command added the same again, with nothing on screen.

- Turn finalization now asks whether the user cancelled the turn before it reports the turn, and stops the commands after the report and the post-turn checkpoint. The answer cannot wait until after the report: a prompt typed once the turn is reported can join its ending as steering, which no longer reads as a cancel. The deps hook is split in two for this (`turn_ends_by_explicit_cancel` and `stop_steering_detached_commands`). `worker_runtime` still knows nothing about the shell.
- The stops of one cancel run as tasks of one `std.Io.Group` that the cancel awaits, so the 2 s waits of stubborn commands overlap. At most 8 run at once: each holds one terminal client request at a time, and the client runs at most 32 requests for all agents and refuses the rest. Each task gives each stop its own arena over the thread-safe `lifecycle_allocator`. `Group.async` runs a task on the caller when it cannot start one, which covers the single-threaded WebAssembly builds. Each stop keeps its `debug_trace` lines, and a new `steering-detached command stops done turn_id=N count=M` line marks the end.
- The two shell unit tests of steered stops share one `SteeringCancelTest` helper instead of copying their setup.

The worker still runs the stops before it takes the next prompt, so a prompt sent right after Escape waits for them. The graceful closes do not overlap: the terminal client runs every write, resize, signal and close of all terminals in one admission order (`OrderedMutations`, `operation.requiresOrderedMutation`), so each tty command that ignores SIGTERM still adds its 800 ms graceful close, and each further group of 8 adds another 2 s wait. Making the closes overlap would mean changing that order for every terminal mutation, which belongs in its own change to the terminal client.

## Before and after

Steered tty commands that ignore TERM, HUP and INT, then Escape, then a new prompt, on the Linux sandbox. Time from Escape to the next model request:

| Commands | `main` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | 5525 ms | 3513 ms |
| 12 | | 13993 ms |
| 20 | | 22914 ms |

On `main` the stops run one after another, about 2.9 s each. With no cap on parallel stops, an earlier head of this branch took 11849 ms for 12 and 18358 ms for 20; the cap of 8 costs about 2 s for each further group of 8, which keeps the stops within the terminal client's limits. The new E2E test fails on `main` (`Expected: < 4588.8`, `Received: 5525`) and passes on this branch. In every run on this branch, all commands were stopped, fx exited with status 0, and stderr was empty.

## Testing

- `zig fmt --check src/`
- `zig build test`: new unit tests for the order (the cancel check before the report, the stops after the finish event), for a completed turn that asks nothing, for two steered commands stopped together, and for more steered commands than run at once, also with an async limit of none, where every task runs on the caller.
- `zig build fx-core-wasm -Dwasm-surface=core -Doptimize=ReleaseSmall` and `zig build fx-term-wasm -Dwasm-surface=term -Doptimize=ReleaseSmall`
- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`: 95 pass, 0 fail. New tests:
  - `Escape stops steered commands that ignore SIGTERM together, after the turn ends`
  - `a parent's stop of a subagent turn stops the command its steering moved to the background`: a parent's message moves the subagent's running command to the background, and the parent's `stop` of that turn stops it.
- Ctrl+C twice while the stops still run: fx exits with status 0 in about 0.8 s, stderr is empty, and both commands are gone.

title: Fix two gateway client tests that fail on slow macOS runners
body:
## Summary

Two kinds of `src/gateway/client.zig` tests fail on slow macOS arm64 runners for every branch.

- **Stuck-lookup tests (six).** They cancel an unpooled open stuck in its lookup, then release the lookup. The open's job still calls `client.request` after the cancel, and a connect to loopback can finish before the cancel stops it, so the test server sees a connection that fx then closes. The tests expected no connection at all, and "Esc during a stuck lookup ends an unpooled gateway request at once" failed with `expected .none, found .closed`. They now check that no connection is left open through a new `UnpooledOpenFixture.expectNoneLeftOpen`. A connection fx already closed counts the same as none, which `lateConnection` already allows, and a connection left open still fails the test.
- **"delivery certainty becomes possibly sent before response head".** It gave its request a 20 ms deadline. When the connect and send take longer, the deadline ends before the send, and fx rightly reports the request as definitely unsent (`expected .possibly_sent, found .definitely_unsent`). The deadline is now 250 ms and the server holds the response head for 1000 ms, so the request is sent first and the deadline still ends before the head arrives.

## Testing

- `zig fmt --check src/`
- `zig build test --summary all` on Linux x86_64: only the sandbox's known permission-dependent failures, none in `gateway.client`.
- Unit tests in CI on Linux and macOS arm64.
