title: Send turn progress, model calls, and compactions to fx acp clients
body:
## Summary

- `fx acp` sends a running turn's progress (its phase, token counts, and the provider that served it) as `_sh.fx/session/turn_progress` to clients that list `sh.fx/turnProgress`, once per change.
- It sends one `_sh.fx/session/model_call` for each model call that ends, with its purpose, outcome, provider, model, finish or failure, tokens, end time, and duration, to clients that list `sh.fx/modelCalls`.
- The `session/prompt` response's `usage` takes ACP's unstable names (`thoughtTokens`, `cachedReadTokens`, `cachedWriteTokens`) and adds `totalTokens`. When the provider reports no counts it carries fx's estimate, and when no count is known it is left out instead of being an empty object.
- `sh.fx/usage` in the response's `_meta` gives the turn's duration, its thinking time, and whether its counts are exact, for clients that list it.
- Clients that set ACP's `session.compaction` capability get a `compaction_update` with `in_progress` and then `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled` for each compaction, and a load replays each saved compaction as one `completed` update.
- Plain ACP clients get none of these messages.
- The SDK reads the new `usage` names and keeps its own result fields.

- Remove `Session.visitHistoryCycle`, which nothing outside tests called after #2013; its tests now read cycles through `CycleReader`, the path Ctrl+O uses.

title: Read the compaction race tests' log through the compaction-aware reader
body:
## Summary

- `listedRecords` in `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` read the session log raw, because a compaction in the middle of a turn makes fx write the turn again as superseded, and `logLines` refuses every supersede. A raw read also accepts a supersede that no compaction explains, so the three tests that call it could not notice one.
- It now reads the log through `logLinesAfterCompaction`, which accepts a supersede only when a compaction in the same turn explains it, once per compaction. The comment says why. The three tests are "a compaction commit while a subagent finishes lists each record once", "fx killed while a compaction's write holds its records resumes the session", and "fx told to quit while a compaction's write is held and a subagent's waits behind it exits without a panic".
- Only this helper changes, in one file. fx itself does not change.

## Checks

All runs were in a fresh Linux sandbox after `zig build`, with `-t` filters on the three tests.

- Unchanged logs: the three tests pass, 15 of 15 repeats (5 each). The real logs of two of the tests hold one compaction and one supersede. The killed test's log holds neither, because its compaction never lands.
- A supersede planted in a turn with no compaction, appended to the log a test reads: with the raw read from `main`, all three tests still pass. With this change, all three fail on the compaction expectation in `logLinesAfterCompaction`.
- A second supersede after one compaction in a turn, and a compaction of an earlier turn followed by a supersede in a later one, give the same result: 3 of 3 pass with the raw read and 3 of 3 fail with this change.
- Control: the designed pattern planted, one compaction and then one supersede, passes all three tests. The plants therefore fail because of their shape and not because something was appended.
- The strict `logLines` still refuses the real log of the two tests that hold a supersede. They fail at the superseded check in `tests/e2e/saved-sessions.ts`, and the killed test passes. So the change is needed.
- A half-written last line, as after a kill: the new read skips it and the three tests pass, while the raw read throws a JSON parse error in all three.

## For review

- Another raw reader has the same effect, but I think not the same reason. The steering test in `tests/e2e/tui-compaction-activity.test.ts`, "auto: steering sent during a turn stays user text through compaction", finds one compacted line in a raw read of a log that holds the same supersede. The strict `logLines` refuses its log and `logLinesAfterCompaction` accepts it, in one run each. The raw read was ported unchanged from an older raw read, so I left it. Switching it is a one-line follow-up if you want it.
- The other raw readers of compaction lines in `tests/e2e` compare bytes, count text, or run after a manual compaction between turns, where fx writes no supersede. The drivers in `tests/tla/drivers/` also read session logs raw. I did not look at them.

title: Name what a long read_tool_result request reads in its row
body:
## Summary

- The row of a `read_tool_result` call says what the call does: Searching, Opening, Reloading or Reading. For a request the model wrote as JSON text, the row parsed the text into a 4096-byte stack buffer, and the parse needs more room than the text. On `main` a request text of 2,240 bytes (a query of 2,208 characters) already got the tool's default "Reading", and 2,239 bytes still got its real verb. The code comment said 4 KiB.
- The row now scans the text in place. It reads only `search`, `handle` and `query` at the top of the text and skips every other value with `std.json.Scanner`. It allocates nothing, its work is linear in the text, and its memory is fixed.
- Nesting past 64 levels (`json_depth`, checked first), text that is not one object, text with anything after its object, and a repeat of a field the row reads name nothing, as a parse of the text refuses them. The code comment says this, and corrects the old "4096 bytes" claim.
- A handle written with escapes decodes into 1 KiB on the stack, and a longer one keeps the tool's default label. A handle without escapes is read in the text, whatever its length. No real handle comes near the bound: a replay handle is at most 128 bytes.
- The `read_tool_result_request_text` fuzz target now requires the label of the text to equal the label of the object it holds, in place of accepting a null label for text "that does not fit the buffer".

## Known gap

A parse of a request text fails on a repeated key at any depth, because `std.json` treats a duplicate as an error by default, and decode then refuses the call. The row can see a repeat of the three fields it reads, and then names nothing, as the parse does. It cannot see a repeat of another field, top level or nested, without memory in proportion to the number of fields. Such a text gets the label of what it reads, though decode refuses the call. For example `{"handle":"t5","x":1,"x":2}` gives "Opening". This is the one way the row reads a text differently from a full parse, and the fuzz target allows it only when the full parse fails with `DuplicateField`. A test pins it.

## Checks

All runs were in a fresh sandbox. Run numbers are the build run's.

- Failing first on `origin/main` (run 2): the two new unit tests fail, "a request text longer than 4 KiB" and the comparison of about 70 hostile and edge texts with a full parse. The other 27 tests of the filter pass.
- The same tests on this change (run 12, 32 of 32), and in ReleaseSafe (run 16, 32 of 32). The fuzz target's seeds are among them.
- The real binary: a model call with a `read_tool_result` request of JSON text over 4 KiB (a 5,000-character query). With the two Zig files put back to `main`, the row reads "Read printf ... " and the new test fails on the `Searched` check (run 13). With the change, it passes 3 of 3, beside the existing short-query test (run 14, 6 of 6).
- The existing TUI test of saved-output rows, which sends object requests, passes 3 of 3 (run 15).
- Fuzz (run 17): the saved inputs replay clean, then six rounds of 250,000 new inputs in ReleaseSafe, 1.5 million in all, found no failing input. Texts reach 16 KiB.
- Mutation check (run 18): twelve planted bugs in the scanner, one at a time, each makes a test fail: no depth check, no check after the object, a repeated handle, query or search allowed, an empty query counted, search not read first, the handle not trimmed, escapes not decoded, the room off by one, the room unchecked for a plain handle, a non-string handle read. A first pass missed two, a repeated `search` and an empty query written as text, so two cases were added.

Edge and hostile texts, each compared with a full parse (the rest of the list is in the test):

- text just under, at and over the old limit, and 1 MiB, for a query, a range, a record, an image handle and a history search
- text that is not one object (an array, a number, a string, `null`, an empty text), long or short; text after the object; an unterminated string; a trailing comma; invalid escapes and a lone surrogate
- nesting at 64 levels is read, and 65 levels is refused, short and padded past 4 KiB
- a repeat of `handle`, `query` or `search`; keys and handles written with escapes; a handle with escapes at its room and one byte past it
- a long unknown field, 3,000 keys, quotes and brackets inside strings, 6,000 bytes of white space around the object

### Cost

The scan costs, in ReleaseSafe, 7.6 µs for a 4 KiB text, 116 µs for 64 KiB, 1.9 ms for 1 MiB and 7.9 ms for 4 MiB. A first measurement gave 9 µs, 2.3 ms and 9.2 ms. That is 59% to 127% of the time the caller already spends parsing the whole call before the hook runs (`toolCallPresentation` parses it into an arena), so it adds about one more pass over a long text and allocates nothing. Debug is about four times slower.

## For review

- The `PresentationFn` contract is unchanged: the hook still takes no allocator. A heap parse with a cap, or a bigger stack buffer, were the other options considered.
- The scanner's nesting list is a plain 512-byte buffer. `std.ArrayList` grows it by a cache line (128 bytes on the targets fx builds for), and a larger one would make the scan find no label and fail the 64-level test.
- `displayTarget` and `requestedHandle` are unchanged: they take an allocator and already read long text.

title: Document how isContextOverflow matches refusal text
body:
## Summary

- Adds a doc comment above `isContextOverflow` that names a known, rare case. No code changes.
- The function matches its phrases anywhere in the provider's detail. It has to, because most families send no code for a context overflow. Only OpenAI-style bodies carry `code: "context_length_exceeded"`. Gateway, Anthropic and xAI send only text, and a Gateway multi-attempt body holds it only under `providerAttempts[].error`.
- A refusal for another cause that quotes one of the phrases therefore counts as an overflow. The main request compacts once and retries, and the compactor sends up to three smaller requests.

## Why a comment and not a change

I measured the case before deciding. The refusals below are constructed: no fixture in the repository quotes user or tool text in a refusal, so I could not find a recorded one. All runs used the built binary against a mock gateway, in a sandbox. The probe edits are not part of this PR.

| Refusal | Requests |
|---|---|
| Compaction request refused with HTTP 400, text names "prompt is too long", "maximum context length" or "input is too long" | 8 each |
| Same, for another cause with no such phrase (invalid tool schema) | 2 |
| Same, a real overflow | 8 |
| Main request, headless, refused once, with a phrase | 2 agent requests, 2 summary requests, 1 compaction, then it recovers |
| Main request, headless, same refusal without a phrase | 1 agent request, no compaction, "API request failed · HTTP 400 · invalid_request_error: invalid tool schema" |
| TUI, with an earlier tool-call turn, phrase in every refusal | 6 requests, "Still too long after compacting · press Esc and shorten your message" |
| TUI, same turn, no phrase | 3 requests, "The provider rejected this request · press Esc" |

So a false positive costs 6 extra compaction requests, and on the main request it shows the wrong status text. Public reports say some servers, such as vLLM, echo a bad request value in a 400, but I found no realistic refusal that quotes one of these phrases.

Options I considered and left out:

- **Match only structured codes.** Gateway, Anthropic and xAI send no overflow code in the repository's fixtures, and vLLM's public error reports show `code` as the number 400. Real overflows would be missed.
- **Match only `error.message`.** A Gateway multi-attempt body has the text only under `providerAttempts[].error`, and a message that echoes a request value would still match.
- **Stop the compactor's smaller retries when the detail repeats.** A real overflow from Gateway or Bedrock carries no token counts, so every size gets the same detail. This would cut retries the design wants.
- **Guard the main request with fx's own token estimate.** It needs a threshold and does not help the compactor, whose requests are already fitted to the window.

## Checks

- `git diff origin/main --numstat`: 7 insertions and 0 deletions in `src/core/agent/stream_provider.zig`. Every changed line is a `///` line.
- `zig fmt --check src/core/agent/stream_provider.zig`: exit 0. No added line is over 80 characters or holds a double hyphen.
- `fx-cloud run zig build`: exit 0, in a sandbox.
- Each claim in the comment was checked against the code and the fixtures: the match at `stream_provider.zig` `containsIgnoreCase(detail, needle)`, the OpenAI-style and Gateway fixtures in `gateway_flow.zig`, the multi-attempt body in `vercel_failure_diagnostics.zig`, `max_smaller_requests = 3` in `summarize.zig`, and the `.too_long` step in `recovery.zig`.

title: Show failed tool calls quietly
body:
## Summary

- A failed call that is not a command shows as one dim row, such as `Couldn't read nope.zig`, without the error text.
- A failed command keeps its first error line on its row, and a failed subagent call keeps its reason.
- A failed call that ends the turn shows its reason on its row.
- The group header no longer counts failed calls that are not commands, except that a collapsed group counts a failure its turn ended on, since no row shows it.
- Under a named theme that sets red, the failure mark and the reasons use that red. Under fx's own themes they are dim.
- The model still gets the whole error, and Ctrl+O still shows it.

Before:

```
● Read a file · 1 failed
├ Read app.zig
└ Couldn't edit main.zig · old_string not found in file
```

After, while the turn goes on:

```
● Read a file
├ Read app.zig
└ Couldn't edit main.zig
```

title: Bug: Codex subagent accepts an unsupported model override and fails with HTTP 400
body:
### Issue details

On fx `0.0.17`, the `subagent` tool accepts an explicit `gpt-5.4-mini` override when using Codex with a ChatGPT account. The child then fails at the provider instead of fx rejecting the unsupported model before launching it.

The parent originally selected this model during ordinary delegation. I reproduced the failure with a fresh child and a no-tools prompt.

#### Environment

- fx `0.0.17`
- Linux, Fedora 44
- Provider: `codex`, authenticated with a ChatGPT account
- Parent model: `gpt-6-astra`

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Start fx with Codex and a working parent model.
2. Run `fx models`. In this account's catalog, `gpt-5.4-mini` is absent.
3. Have the parent invoke the `subagent` tool with these arguments:

```json
{
  "action": "message",
  "agent": "model-validation-check",
  "model": "gpt-5.4-mini",
  "message": "Model-validation smoke test only. Do not use tools or change anything. Reply with exactly OK."
}
```

4. Wait for the child's result.

#### Actual behavior

The tool returns `ok: true` and says the child is working. The child then fails with a provider rejection.

The original failure displayed:

```text
system: API request failed · HTTP 400 · model_not_found: The 'gpt-5.4-mini' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.
```

The fresh reproduction recorded these fields in the child's `model_call` event:

```json
{
  "purpose": "turn",
  "outcome": "failed",
  "provider": "codex",
  "model": "gpt-5.4-mini",
  "failure": "invalid_request",
  "after_tool_step_count": 0
}
```

`fx models` exited with code 0 and listed eight Codex subscription models, none named `gpt-5.4-mini`. As a control, a new subagent explicitly using catalog-listed `gpt-5.6-luna` completed a read-only task successfully.

#### Expected behavior

Reject an unsupported subagent model override before sending a completion request, using the active provider's catalog when available. Return an actionable tool error so the parent can select an available model or omit the override to inherit its own model. Do not silently switch providers or models.

#### Workaround

I added local instructions requiring `fx models` before explicit subagent model selection and parent-model inheritance when availability cannot be confirmed. This is an instruction-level workaround, not runtime validation.

Related: #1144 describes model-validation behavior with custom providers. This report concerns Codex subscription authentication and an upstream rejection. I have not verified whether they share an implementation cause.

### Trace

No full trace attached. The excerpt above contains only the relevant reproduction fields.

### Sensitive information

- [x] I reviewed the information above and removed secrets and other sensitive data.

title: Keep related tool calls on one row
body:
## Summary

- A shell session's run, input, and stop share one row, such as `● Stopped echo, sleep · 3 calls ✓`. A group with only that row takes the row's mark, as other one-row groups do.
- Input to a session joins only the run with the same command, so it never joins another session's run.
- Calls to the same MCP tool share one row that counts them, such as `Ran MCP <tool> ×3`. An MCP call that failed, was denied, or was cancelled keeps its own row.
- A command that returns while it keeps running stays on the row it joined instead of moving to a row of its own. That row reads `Still running` with all of its steps, as a row of running commands reads `Running`.
- A command that ran after one still running keeps its own row, so the row of the one still running never reads `Ran` or gets a check mark.
- A running read, search, edit, or write whose target has not arrived yet waits in its tool's row instead of showing on a row that later folds away.
- An edit or write whose status already names its file shows on its own row unless that file already has one.

Stacked on #2038.

title: Stop false hangs in the nightly fuzz runs
body:
## Summary

- Build each fuzz target with one `--fuzz=1` pass under its own 15-minute limit before the timed rounds, so the 600-second round limit measures fuzzing alone. Round 1 used to compile the instrumented binary too, which took up to about 400 seconds for some targets: `agents_menu_selection` reached 464 seconds in round 1 while it fuzzed for about 20.
- Report a build that runs out of time as a build error instead of a hang.
- Fuzz `toolbox_menu` for 60,000 iterations per round instead of 500,000. Its fuzzing alone took up to 426 seconds per round, and with the build it passed the limit (#2015).
- Fuzz `switch_order` for 1,200,000 iterations per round instead of 4,000,000. Its rounds took up to 217 seconds of fuzzing.
- Keep the iterations of every other target. Without the build, their longest nightly round took 251 seconds (`responses_stream`).

title: Name a toolbox call while its arguments stream in
body:
## Summary

- A toolbox call's row names what it runs, searches, or opens as soon as that name has streamed in, such as `Running glob_files` or `Running MCP <tool>`, instead of a bare `Using` until every argument arrives.
- The early label comes from the same presentation as the finished call's, so a skill opened by its location reads as the skill's name.
- A search with no words yet, which may list one server's tools, and a value with an escape in it still read `Using` until the arguments are complete.
- The streaming scanner the subagent row used now takes the key and depths it looks at, and both calls share it.

Before, while a `run` call's arguments stream in:

```
● Using
```

After:

```
● Running glob_files
```

title: Start a new tool group after a message sent mid-turn
body:
## Summary

- A message the user sends while a turn runs joins that turn, so the calls after it share the turn's tool group. Their rows were drawn in that group, above the message that asked for them.
- A group's rows after a user message now start a new group at their own place, under the message.
- Saved steering resumes as a user message, so the rows stay in the same places after resume.

Before, after a failed request left the first turn open:

```
┃ Edit the readme.
● Read a file
├ Read README.md · 2 parts
└ Couldn't edit README.md
┃ Read it again.
  Done.
```

After:

```
┃ Edit the readme.
● Read a file
├ Read README.md
└ Couldn't edit README.md
┃ Read it again.
● Read README.md
  Done.
```

title: Show an edit's whole file as a diff to fx acp clients
body:
Stacked on #2032.

`fx acp` sent an edit's tool call as text only, so a client could not show what changed. This uses ACP v1's `diff` tool call content, with the file's whole text before and after.

- A `session/request_permission` for a `write_file` or `edit_file` call shows the prepared change in `toolCall.content`. The core passes it on a new optional `FileApprovalRequest.change`, borrowed from the prepared mutation for the prompt call only; owned copies leave it out.
- A committed edit's completed `tool_call_update` carries the `diff`, then its text result. `oldText` is `null` for a new file. ACP keeps the committed handoff's diff per call and sends it in the deferred completed update, because an update's content replaces the call's.
- A failed or denied edit ends with text only.
- When either side is over 1 MiB or isn't UTF-8, the call keeps only its text, and fx logs why.

## Tests

- `AcpToolDiffs.tla`: two base configs pass (50,170 and 188,560 states), the `Today` config fails `Complete`, and all six mutants are caught.
- `tests/tla/drivers/acp/tool_diffs/driver.ts` runs `fx acp` through a new file then an edit, two edits of one file in one step, an approved and a denied edit, and a write over 1 MiB, and checks each diff against the files on disk: 4/4 accepted. On #2032 the rules model rejects the three plans that show a diff, and the `Today` model accepts all four.
- Two new `acp.test.ts` tests; the diff one fails on #2032.

title: Send the current sign-in on ACP report turns
body:
Over ACP, a subagent report that waited for its parent's turn to end could fail on the report turn's first model call. With a small request, the call got `HTTP 400: 400 Bad Request` and the prompt ended with `stopReason: refused`. With a large request, the send failed with `WriteFailed`, which fx treats as a lost connection and retries, so the thread looked hung. A turn the user started afterwards worked.

Reported in Slack: https://vercel.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C0ARX59MRNZ/p1794777287588279

## Cause

`handlePrompt` in `src/acp/prompt.zig` built the turn's job with slices it borrowed from the server: `api_key` from the session, `account_id` from the session, and `gateway_team` from the server state. `runReportTurns` starts each report turn from a copy of that job, so every report turn sent the same borrowed slices.

When a step refreshes the credential, `server.adoptServerCredential` zeroes and frees the server's `api_key` and frees its `account_id` and `gateway_team`, then publishes the new ones. The running turn keeps working because the agent loop sends its own copy of the refreshed token. A report turn that starts afterwards still sends the first turn's job, which by then points at the zeroed token and freed team and account bytes.

A step only refreshes when the last credential load is older than `request_path_verified_window_ms` (30 s, in `src/core/auth/auth_runtime.zig`). Before that, the request path skips the reload. So a report turn failed only when the parent turn kept running for more than about 30 s after it started, which matches the 16 s pass and 38 s fail in the report. A turn the user starts reads the server's current credential, so it worked.

The three errors in the report are this one fault. A zeroed bearer token gets a 400 from the edge. With a large body, the server answers and closes before fx finishes writing, so the write fails instead. Once the retry's own refresh replaces the token, the freed `gateway_team` bytes stay in the request, so it gets 401 even after a forced refresh.

## Change

Each ACP turn now copies its sign-in (token, source, account, and team) from the server when it starts, in a small `TurnSignIn` owner in `src/acp/prompt.zig`. The first turn and every report turn use their own copy, so publishing a refreshed credential no longer frees bytes a job holds, and a report turn sends the credential that is current when it starts, as a user-started turn does. Nothing changes in the protocol, the session format, or how credentials are stored.

## Tests

- New E2E test in `tests/e2e/acp.test.ts`, "ACP report turn sends the sign-in its first turn refreshed". The fake Codex server answers the parent's first request with 401, so fx refreshes the login and publishes it during the turn. A subagent's report then starts the next turn. Before this change the report turn failed with `InvalidChatGptSubscriptionAccount`, because the account id it sent was freed memory. With the change it sends the refreshed token and ends with `end_turn`.
- New unit test in `src/acp/prompt.zig`, "ACP turn sign-in outlives a refreshed credential the server publishes".

## Repro

`acp_repro.py` is a small ACP client that starts a subagent, keeps the parent turn running, and reports each turn's model calls. Each run uses `fx acp --auto` with `anthropic/claude-fable-5.2` at low effort, signed in with fx login, on macOS arm64.

| Prompt | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parent sleeps 40 s after `subagent wait` | Report turn: `HTTP 400`, `stopReason: refused` | Report turn completed, `end_turn` |
| Same, with about 750 KB of filler | Report turn: 10 attempts over 200 s, every one `WriteFailed` in under 250 ms, shown as "Connection lost" retries until the client cancelled | Report turn completed, `end_turn` |
| Subagent left open, parent ends at once | Passed in the original report | Passed |
| Parent idle when the report arrives 66 s later | Passed in the original report | Passed |

In the passing runs after the change, the trace shows the parent turn refreshing the credential after the report was queued and before the report turn started, which is the condition that failed before.

title: Read $${ in MCP config as a literal ${
body:
## Summary

- In ~/.fx/mcp.json and project .mcp.json, $${VAR} now reaches the server as ${VAR} instead of being expanded by fx.
- A server that expands its own variables can now receive its placeholder. For example, mcp-remote expands ${TOKEN} in --header 'name:${TOKEN}' from its own env block, so the secret stays out of the process arguments.
- Before this change fx expanded that placeholder from its own environment and skipped the server when the variable was unset, with no way to escape it. $${VAR} and \${VAR} failed the same way.
- A $$ that isn't followed by { stays as written, so values such as passwords that contain $$ don't change.
- ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} behave as before.

## Verification

- zig fmt --check src/core/mcp/project_config.zig passes.
- New cases in "workspace template expansion is explicit bounded and deterministic" cover $${SET}, $${MISSING} with surrounding text, an escape next to an expansion, a lone $$, and a trailing $${. They fail without the change, and all 27 tests in project_config.zig pass with it.
- The zig skill's check_deprecated.py reports nothing for the changed file.
- zig build succeeds.
- With ./zig-out/bin/fx and a temporary FX_HOME, fx mcp add --env BYPASS=<token> index -- npx --yes mcp-remote@0.16.6 <url> --header 'x-vercel-protection-bypass:$${BYPASS}' followed by fx mcp show index reports "status ready, 51 tools" and exits 0 with nothing on stderr. The running mcp-remote process received --header x-vercel-protection-bypass:${BYPASS}. The released fx skips the same server written with ${BYPASS}.

## Docs

- https://fx.sh/docs/capabilities/mcp/protocol, "Project configuration limits": after "After approval, `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` expand in commands, arguments, environment values, and HTTP header values.", add "Write `$${VAR}` to pass a literal `${VAR}` to the server, for example to a server that expands its own variables."

title: Show the newest names on a row that lists several
body:
## Summary

- A row that names several commands shows the newest ones, oldest first, after a count of the older ones, such as `Running +3, head, ls, sleep`. Before, it named the first three and counted the rest as `+N more`, so the command still running was the one left out.
- A command that runs again moves to the newest place, and so does a session's input or stop.
- Read and search rows, and the folders one search looked in, follow the same order, such as `Read +2, c.zig`.
- A narrow row leaves out its oldest names first, so the newest one stays in view.
- One command's own steps, such as `make && npm test && cargo build`, still show from the first.

Before, while the sixth command runs:

```
● Running printf, cat, wc +3 more
```

After:

```
● Running +3, head, ls, sleep
```

title: Send a shell call's command result as sh.fx/commandResult
body:
Stacked on #2044.

`fx acp` put a shell call's command result in a `command_result` field at the root of its `tool_call_update`. ACP reserves the root of its types, and sh.fx's own rule puts fx's additions in `_meta` under an `sh.fx/` key.

- The result is now `_meta["sh.fx/commandResult"]` on the update that ends the call, with camelCase names (`exitCode`, `timedOut`, `durationMs`, `stdoutBytes`, ...), sent only to a client that lists `sh.fx/commandResult`. fx lists it for every client.
- Unknown values, such as the exit code of a command a signal stopped, are left out, and so are `terminationIndeterminate` and `outputIncomplete` when false. `outputFile`, `stdoutFile` and `stderrFile` are names in the session's store, not paths.
- The root `command_result` field is gone. Nothing in the tree reads it: the SDK doesn't, and the E2E `command_result` reads are `fx ask --json` output, which keeps its snake_case names.
- `sh-fx.md` documents the key under "Details on standard messages", adds it to "Keys fx used before sh.fx", and the schema gains `CommandResult`.

Also fixes the shared TLC runner (`tests/tla/drivers/lib/tlc.ts`): it read the state count from the first `distinct states found` match, which on a run long enough to print progress lines is a progress line with commas. This change's model is the first whose base runs print one.

## Tests

- `AcpTurnEvents.tla` gains a shell call per turn, a `CommandMeta` constant for fx acp before this change, and a `StandardOnly` invariant. The three base configs pass (738,737, 3,313 and 91,321 states), `AcpTurnEventsToday` still fails `Complete`, the new `AcpTurnEventsRootField` fails `StandardOnly`, and all 11 mutants are caught, four of them new.
- The `turn_events` driver runs a shell call in its third turn and checks the camelCase fields it reads: 5/5 accepted. On #2044 the rules model rejects all five plans, and `--model root-field` accepts all five.

title: Refuse a v1 session folder others can write
body:
## Summary

A v1 session that others could write got answers that disagreed, and one sent the user in a loop: `fx session <id>` said the session was corrupt and to run `fx session recover`, which said no recovery was needed, while `fx sessions convert` converted it and removed the v1 folder.

fx now refuses a v1 member folder when others can write the folder itself, a file or folder directly in it (`session.json`, `events.jsonl`, `permissions.json`, the lock file, `subagent/`, side folders), or a file or folder directly in its `subagent/` folder (`children.json`, the relationship index, child markers). Every command gives the same reason: what others can write, the subagent when it is a subagent's folder, and the fix.

```
others can write <its folder | NAME in its folder>, so its files may not be the ones fx saved; make it private with `chmod -R go-w ~/.fx/sessions/<id>`
```

| Command | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `fx session <id>` | shown, or for a session with a saved result `is corrupt; run fx session recover <id>` | `fx session: session <id> can't be read safely: <reason>`, exit 1, JSON code `DurablePathUnsafe` |
| `fx session recover <id>` | `SessionRecoveryNotNeeded` | `fx session: session <id> can't be recovered safely: <reason>`, exit 1, JSON code `DurablePathUnsafe` |
| `fx sessions convert` | converted, v1 folder removed | `<id>: unreadable: <reason>`, exit 1, folder kept |
| `fx ask --resume <id>` | converted and continued | one line, `fx ask: the session can't be converted: <reason>`, no model request; JSON keeps `"error":"InvalidSessionFormat"` |
| `fx doctor` | nothing | `session <id> saved by an older fx can't be converted: <reason>` |

For a subagent's own folder the reason starts `its subagent <child id>: `. A name read from the folder is written terminal-safe, as `fx doctor` writes names, and a name too long for the reason is left out ("something in its folder"), not cut. The fix names the folder once as `~/.fx/sessions/<id>` (`"$FX_HOME"/sessions/<id>` when `FX_HOME` is set), which needs no quoting: a session id holds only letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`. A symlinked or FIFO v1 folder is reported as unsafe storage by `fx session <id>` too, without a reason. A folder readable by others only (0755) behaves as before. When v2 already holds a session and its v1 folder comes back writable, `fx sessions convert` keeps the folder and reports nothing.

## Rule

D61 in `tests/tla/session_manager/system-design.md` takes v1 folders an old release left readable by others because "others could only read them". A folder or file others can write fails that reason: those files carry no digest, so fx could not tell a change from what it saved. #1998 applied it to the lock file and `subagent/`; this applies it to the member folder, what is directly in it, and what is directly in its `subagent/` folder, in `v1_conversion.openMemberDir`, which show, recover, conversion and doctor all go through. D61 states the limits: files deeper in side folders are not checked by mode (salvage checks a saved result against the digest its handle names, D74, and conversion copies them as they are), only mode bits are read, not access control lists, and a group that holds only the owner counts as others, as for all of fx's private state.

## Changes

- `shared/io.zig`: `othersCanWrite`, the write-bit rule, used by the older-file lock check, `session_child_store.verifyOwnerWritableDirectory` (now pub) and `openMemberDir`.
- `v1_conversion.zig`: `openMemberDir` refuses a member as above; `recordUnsafe` writes the reason, with the member's role (`MemberRole`), for `kindOfRecorded`, `kindProblem` and each member `lockFamily` locks. `Problem.capacity` is 1024, enough for the reason without its entry name for any id.
- `session_adapter.zig`: conversion reports a refused member unreadable with that reason; doctor shows it; `readV1Session` and salvage record it, and pass `PrivateStatePermissionsUnsupported`, `DurablePathUnsafe` and `SessionPathUnsafe` through as unsafe storage; `convertAll` checks whether v2 holds a session before it reports its v1 folder.
- `cli_surface.zig`: `fx session <id>` and `fx session recover` print the reason with the `DurablePathUnsafe` code.
- `cli_ask.zig`: text-mode `fx ask --resume` prints the reason once.
- `system-design.md`: D61.

## Verification

- E2E in `tests/e2e/session-recovery.test.ts`: `a v1 session folder others can write is refused as unsafe by show, recover, convert and resume, and stays` (show, recover and text-mode ask messages, and the writable leftover of a converted session) and `a v1 subagent folder or session file others can write is refused with its path and the fix, and stays`. Both pass with the two #1998 recovery tests (4 pass), also run without capabilities (`setpriv --inh-caps=-all --ambient-caps=-all --bounding-set=-all --no-new-privs`).
- Unit tests: the folder at 0757 and 0775, then 0755 converts; a family whose root `subagent/` folder is 0777; a family whose subagent's folder is 0757; `subagent/children.json` at 0646; `events.jsonl` at 0646; a 0666 entry whose name holds `ESC]0;...BEL ESC[31m` (no raw ESC or BEL in the reason); a 255-byte name of control bytes (left out, not cut); a converted session whose v1 folder comes back at 0757, converted twice.
- Hands-on with the Linux builds of 3398c57b and of this head, and with the macOS arm64 binary on a Mac, each case in its own HOME with every gateway URL at `127.0.0.1:9`: `side` at 0757, 0775 and 0755, a 0757 subagent folder, `events.jsonl` at 0646, `children.json` at 0646 with one child id changed (3398c57b converted the family without that child; now it is refused), a 0666 entry named with escape sequences (3398c57b put raw ESC bytes on stdout and stderr; now none), and a writable leftover. On the Mac, the printed `chmod -R go-w` commands, run as typed, make the family convert.
- `zig fmt --check src/`, `python3 -m scripts.check_cli_shape` (`CLI shape: ok`), `zig build test` without capabilities (only the `command_effect` printf failure and the four Linux aborts that #2053 fixes).

## Docs

No page change needed: no fx.sh docs page describes v1 folder modes or these messages.

title: Retry a steered command stop the terminal client refuses
body:
## Summary

When the user cancels a turn, fx stops the shell commands that steering moved to the background in it (#1984, #1999). The terminal client runs at most 32 requests across agents and refuses the rest at once with a retryable failure. A refused stop was not tried again, so a tty command kept running after Escape. Main had the same gap before #1999.

- A steered stop that the busy terminal client refuses (`capacity_exceeded`, marked `retryable`) now runs again after 50 ms, and the wait doubles up to 800 ms, for at most 6 runs: about 1.5 s for one stop. A command whose graceful and forced stops are both refused every time takes about 3.1 s. Only this cancel path retries; the model's own `stop` calls are unchanged. Other failures, also retryable ones such as a `session_lost` wait after the host disconnects, end the stop at once, and the `stopped ... ended=false` line names their code (`failure=session_lost`).
- Each retry writes `steering-detached command stop refused session_id=... attempt=N reason=terminal_busy retry_in_ms=...`, and a final give-up writes `steering-detached command stop gave up session_id=... reason=terminal_busy dropped=background_command_stop`. A graceful stop that never ran logs `graceful stop of steering-detached command never ran ... reason=terminal_busy next=force`, not that it left the command running.
- The turn-end release of the agent's terminal write lease, which runs in the same finalization, retries a busy refusal the same bounded way. It logs `terminal lease release refused ...` for each retry and `terminal lease release gave up ... dropped=agent_write_lease_release` for a give-up. The release runs before the turn is reported, as before, because the next prompt may need to write to the terminal. So with a full client, each held lease can add up to about 1.56 s before the user sees the turn end.
- The close of a tty command whose run was never published (`closeTtyBestEffort`) retries a busy refusal the same way. A give-up, or another failure, logs `dropped=unpublished_tty_close`; before, a refusal was freed unread and the command kept running with no record.
- A busy refusal of the refresh before the stop counts too. The tty observer maps `capacity_exceeded` to `TerminalCapacityExceeded` only when the failure itself says `retryable`, which the client's admission refusal does. The host's own store and monitor limits also use `capacity_exceeded` but are not retryable, and they still map to `TerminalObservationFailed`. The shell failure for `TerminalCapacityExceeded` says `"retryable":true`.
- `joinExitDrainForTest` on the terminal client is now `pub`, so the shell tests can free its backend.

The retry waits do not read a shutdown flag. #2055 moves the stops into a group the shell runtime owns, with a cancel flag for process exit; whichever of the two merges second checks that flag before each wait.

One rule decides what a busy refusal is: `StructuredError.isBusyRefusal` in `src/core/terminal/contracts.zig`, true only for `capacity_exceeded` marked `retryable`. The tty observer, the lease release, the unpublished tty close and the steered stop all use it. The stop reads a shell failure as busy only when it is the retryable `TerminalCapacityExceeded`, which the observer gives only for such a refusal. When the graceful stop does not end the command, its log line names the cause (`graceful stop did not end ... failure=session_lost next=force`), and so does a forced stop that fails.

## Tests

- `only a retryable capacity failure is a busy refusal` (contracts): the helper itself, for a client refusal, a host limit, a retryable `session_lost`, and `session_not_found`.

- `a turn cancel stops a steered tty command while the terminal client is full`: a real tty command through the shell tool and an in-process terminal client, every client slot filled with waits, one more request checked as refused and retryable, the slots freed 300 ms into the cancel. The command still stops.
- `a turn cancel gives up a steered tty stop the full terminal client keeps refusing`: the client stays full; the cancel gives up after at least 3.1 s and the command still runs.
- `a turn-end lease release runs again while the terminal client is full`: the release succeeds after the slots free up, and gives up with `TerminalLeaseCleanupFailed` while they stay full.
- `a stop failure counts as busy only for a retryable capacity refusal`: cloned terminal failures and shell failures with `retryable` true and false, a retryable `session_lost`, a string flag, and bodies that are not a failure object or not JSON. It also checks the code each one reports.
- `an unpublished tty close runs again while the terminal client is full`: the close succeeds after the slots free up, and the terminal is closed.
- `only a capacity refusal marked retryable maps to the retryable error` (managed_observer).
- With one attempt, as before this change, the four tty tests fail (`TestUnexpectedResult` three times and `TerminalLeaseCleanupFailed`).
- `zig build test --summary all` in a Linux sandbox: 11591 of 11632 passed. The 12 failures and 4 crashes are the known sandbox-only ones that fail on main too (api_tests D29/D39/D49, session_adapter D45/D61/D89, web_fetch_artifacts D44/D49, command_effect printf, change_tracker undo x2, storage read-only).
- `FX_SOUND=0 bun test tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts -t steer`: 19 pass, 0 fail, including the Escape stop tests with tty=true and tty=false.

title: Run the v1 folder-mode session tests on Linux
body:
## Summary

Four tests in `src/core/session/session_adapter.zig` never ran on Linux:

- `a v1 session's hosted terminal folders an old fx left readable by others convert, private (D45)`
- `a v1 profile an old release left readable by others converts (D61)`
- `a new session never takes an id v1's folder could not be checked for (D61)`
- `a turn the store cannot start keeps its prompt images inline and does not fail the prompt (D89)`

Each opened a folder without `.iterate` and then changed its mode. On Linux such a handle is `O_PATH`, and `fchmod` on it fails with `BADF`. A Debug build aborts (`programmer bug caused syscall error: BADF` in `setPermissions`), and a ReleaseSafe build, as CI runs, took the `catch return error.SkipZigTest` path. D89 had the same cause.

## Changes

- Open those folders with `.iterate = true`, and use `try` for the mode change, so a failed chmod fails the test instead of skipping it. The `readableByOthers` helper from #1998 gets the same `try`.
- The two tests that need a refused write (D61 "never takes an id" and D89) skip only when the process writes into the locked folder anyway, as root or a process with `CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE` does (`writesWhateverTheMode`). CI runners and a normal user on macOS do not.
- New test `a v1 family whose subagent folder others can write: recover refuses it as unsafe, conversion as unreadable, and every member keeps its v1 folder (D61)`: a 0777 v1 `subagent/` makes `commandError(recover(...))` return `DurablePathUnsafe`, conversion fails with `InvalidSessionFormat`, and every member keeps its v1 folder.
  Both errors are the same on `main` and with #2051. #2051 changes only the reason conversion gives (it names the folder and the `chmod -R go-w` fix), so that assertion lives in #2051.

No product code changes.

## Verification

`zig build test --summary all` in a Linux x86_64 sandbox (Debug), which runs with every capability:

- `origin/main`: D45, both D61 tests and D89 `terminated with signal ABRT` (BADF in `setPermissions`).
- This branch: `11586/11625 tests passed (27 skipped, 12 failed)`, 0 crashed. D45 and the readable-profile D61 test run and pass, and so does the new subagent test. The two refused-write tests skip, because this sandbox writes into a 0500 folder. The 12 failures are the known sandbox-only ones (api_tests D29/D39/D49, storage read-only, web_fetch_artifacts D44/D49, command_effect printf, change_tracker undo x2).

`zig fmt --check src/` passes.

title: Share one pid check across the E2E tests
body:
## Summary

Twelve E2E files checked whether a process runs with `process.kill(pid, 0)`, each through its own helper (`processAlive`, `isProcessAlive`, `isRunning`, `processExists`, a local `alive`) or inline. Two pids pass those checks without checking anything:

- Signal 0 to pid 0 or a negative pid reaches a whole process group, which is always alive, so an alive check passes and a gone check never does. This is how #1971's flaky crash test failed: it read `Number(null)` from a terminal record.
- A pid that is not a number, such as `Number("")` from a pid file read too early, makes `process.kill` throw as if the process had ended, so a gone check passes.

`tests/e2e/process-alive.ts` now holds one `processAlive` that throws on any pid that is not a positive safe integer. Files with their own named helper (`isProcessAlive`, `isRunning`, `processExists`, `processAlive`) import it under that name, so their call sites stay as they are. The one local `alive` closure, in a `sessions.test.ts` test, is removed, and its three calls use `processAlive`. The inline wait loops and `expect(() => process.kill(pid, 0)).toThrow()` checks now call it. No `process.kill(pid, 0)` is left in `tests/e2e` outside the helper.

The three TLA+ drivers that check pids are left as they are: drivers load E2E helpers from the checkout under test (`targetModule`), which may predate this file, and their pids come from processes they started or recorded.

## Tests

In a sandbox, every changed file: `mcp-stdio` 116/0, `mcp-verbs` 27/0, `tui-command-permissions` 58/0, `tui-file-picker` 23/0, `tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle` 97/0, `tui-host-switch` 52/0, `tui-resume` 90/0, `tui-terminal-tool` 19/0. `acp` 180/1, `gateway-stream-lifecycle` 335/1 and `sessions` 93/30 fail only their file-permission and fault-grid tests, which fail the same way on `main` in that sandbox; `tui-interrupt-recovery` 9/2 fails only the two tests that build a preload library with `cc`, which the sandbox lacks. No test hit the new guard.

title: Name the file of a saved write or edit call
body:
## Summary

- After resume, a failed write or edit row names its file, such as `Couldn't edit README.md`, as the live row did. Before, it read `Couldn't edit file`.
- A live write or edit that fx refuses before it can resolve the path, such as one outside the workspace, now names its file too, instead of `file`.
- A write or edit the user denies names its file, such as `Denied marker-denied.txt`, instead of `Denied file`.
- A call with no display target now takes the path from its arguments: relative to the workspace when it is inside it, and terminal-safe.

Before, after `--resume`:

```
└ Couldn't edit file
```

After:

```
└ Couldn't edit README.md
```

title: Keep fx mcp call working until its command ends
body:
## Summary

- `fx mcp call` keeps working in a command after the shell call that started it returns, such as at its 30-second wait limit or when steering arrives.
- A call from a command that no shell call follows waits, and runs once the agent follows the command with `interact`, with that call's permission check and access.
- An `interact` that serves one of the command's calls does not return at its wait limit, at the quiet limit, or on steering until that call ends.
- Cancelling the shell call that follows a command cancels the MCP calls it runs for that command.
- A command's `fx mcp call` token ends when the command ends.
- A result that returns a running command that has used `fx mcp call` tells the agent to follow it with `interact`.
- `fx mcp call --help` and the bridge's refusal messages say that a call works while its command runs.

title: Start the Worlds of one local folder one at a time
body:
## Summary

libfx creates a World for each agent and starts it when the agent first needs it. Agents on one `local()` folder that took their first prompts together started their Worlds at the same time. On a new folder, world-local's start creates `version.txt` and then writes it, so a start that read the file between the two found it empty, failed with `Invalid version file content: ""`, and failed that agent's prompt. This is how `agents with different names each run only their own sessions' turns` failed the SDK Bun job on #2043.

- The Worlds `local()` creates for one folder now start one at a time in a process: each start waits until the one before it on that folder has finished or failed.
- A start that fails does not stop the next World on that folder from starting.
- Two names of one folder, such as a path through a symlink, share one queue, even before the folder exists.
- Every other World starts on its own, as before: one an app builds through a `world()` factory, whose start may wait on a service with no time limit, one an app passes to `world()`, and `vercel()`'s. A start that never ends holds only its own agent.

world-local picks the folder of a `local()` without a `dir` once per process, which libfx cannot see, so those Worlds share a queue of their own, apart from a `local({ dir })` that names the same folder. Two processes that start on one new folder at the same time can still race inside world-local.

## Tests

- New, on `local`: `agents that start their Worlds on one store at once start them one at a time`. Four agents on one new folder take a first prompt at the same time, and each World's start waits 20 ms first. On `main` 4 starts run at once; with this change 1 does.
- New, on `local`: `Worlds on one folder named through a symlink start one at a time`. One agent uses `<dir>/sessions` and one `<dir>-link/sessions`, before that folder exists. On `main` both starts run at once; with this change 1 does.
- New, on `local`: `a World whose durability names no start turn starts while another start on its store hangs`. The first World's start never settles. With a queue for every World, the other agent was still waiting after 3 s; with this change it starts and runs a turn.
- New, on `local`: `a World that fails to start leaves the next World on its store free to start`.
- A script, not committed, that starts 32 agents on one new `local()` folder at once: on `main`, 7 of 1000 rounds failed on Bun 1.4.2 with `Invalid version file content: ""`. With this change, 0 of 300 rounds failed on Bun 1.4.2 and 0 of 100 on Node 24.
- The four commands of the `Test durable sessions on Bun` step, on Bun 1.4.2 in a Linux sandbox: 6 of 6 runs passed with this change, and 27 of 27 with the first version of this PR.
- On Node 24: `test-durable-core.mjs` on memory, local, world and queue, and `test-durable.mjs` on memory, local and world with the native addon, all passed.
- `tests/tla/sdk/check.sh`, then `drive-agents.mjs --walks 60 --seed 11`, which runs two agents of one process on one world-local folder, and `drive-tenants.mjs --walks 60 --seed 11`: every step was one the model allows.

title: Start a mail turn only after the finished turn is committed
body:
## Summary

A subagent's report or message that arrives right after the parent's turn ends could start the next turn before the loop saved the first one. The session log then held `superseded` and `turn_interrupted` lines for both turns, and a fork before the rewritten prompt could offer a subagent that the prompt itself had started. This is what failed the macOS `/fork` tests on hosted runners about one run in six.

The worker now has an opt-in commit gate: mail that missed a finished turn waits for the main loop to commit that turn, up to five seconds.

## Cause

- The agent's worker thread finishes turn N and pushes a `finish_prompt` event. The main loop commits it to the session a pass later (about 25 ms in the traces).
- A report that missed the turn waits as a continuation, and an idle worker starts it at once.
- The new turn's first write reaches the session while turn N is still open, so the adapter writes `superseded` and `turn_interrupted` for it (`streamedPrefix` in `src/core/session/session_adapter.zig` calls that mismatch a bug). The late commit then supersedes the new turn too.
- User-typed prompts already avoid this with the turn-start hold. Mail did not.
- With the supersede, `forkChildren` takes the children at the end of the turn before a fork point, and a rewritten prompt moves that point past the subagent its own turn spawned. That fits the CI failure `expected 1 subagent, got 2`. I did not reproduce that failure end to end.

## Change

- `src/core/agent/worker_runtime.zig`: `enableCommitGate`, `acknowledgeFinishCommitted` and a check in the wait loops. Only the continuation at the head of the queue is held. Prompts a user typed and queued compaction are not. The hold ends at the acknowledgement, at a stop of the worker, or `commit_gate_limit_ms` (5000) after the finish was pushed; the limit logs `commit_gate_expired` and forgets the count. The trace also has `commit_gate_held` and `commit_gate_released`. `acknowledgeFinishDropped(reason)` lowers the count for a finish the app drops unsaved, and `discardEvents` releases the finishes it frees; each drop logs `commit_gate_finish_dropped` with its reason.
- `src/core/app/app_process_runtime.zig`: the two thread starters opt in.
- `src/core/app/app_worker_runtime.zig`: the runtime that owns the pacer's deferral gets `clearPacer`, `deferFinish` and `acknowledgeDroppedFinish`. `input_interrupt_runtime.zig`, `input_question_runtime.zig`, `input_approval_runtime.zig`, `app_session_runtime.zig` and `app_callbacks.zig` call them in place of `pacer.clear` and `pacer.deferFinish`.
- `src/core/app/app_session_runtime.zig`: `appendFinishedPrompt` acknowledges in a `defer`, so a failed commit still acknowledges. The visual-epoch path acknowledges only a committed turn, because an uncommitted one stays with the pacer and comes back through `appendFinishedPrompt`.
- Test fakes: `FakePacer.deferFinish` in `app_callbacks.zig` and the pacer in the session-transition test in `app_session_runtime.zig` are `pub`. `clearPacer` and `deferFinish` call them from `app_worker_runtime.zig`, and Zig refuses a call to a method that is private to another file. A filtered test build does not analyze those fakes, so only a full test build shows it.
- `src/main.zig`: tests only. No state was added to `App`; the gate's state is on the worker, which owns the queue it guards.
- `tests/tla/subagent/MainMail.tla`: new rules `CommitBeforeNextTurn` and `GateNeverStuck`, a `Commits` constant, a `Drop` action for a finish the loop drops unsaved, and configs for the design and three planted defects.

## Dropped finishes

The gate counts every finish the worker pushes, so a finish the app frees without saving must be acknowledged too, or the count stays raised and a later report waits for it. I searched for every such place:

| Drop | Where | Acknowledged as |
|---|---|---|
| Cancel of a turn or of compaction | `input_interrupt_runtime.zig`, 2 sites | `cancel`, `cancel_compaction` |
| Cancel of a question | `input_question_runtime.zig` | `cancel_question` |
| Cancel of an approval | `input_approval_runtime.zig` | `cancel_approval` |
| Live session switch, the pacer's turn | `beginLiveSessionCancellation` | `session_switch` |
| Live session switch, events still queued | `WorkerRuntime.discardEvents` | `events_discarded` |
| A newer finish replaces the pacer's | `deferFinish` | `pacer_replaced` |
| The drain does not save after an earlier save failure | `preserveFinishedAfterDrainFailure` and the drain's finish handler | `not_persisted` |

Not acknowledged, on purpose: `pacer.deinit` and `ScreenSlot.deinit` on quit or when an agent closes, because its worker stops there; `discardPendingText`, which keeps the turn; and a visual-epoch append that did not commit, which stays with the pacer.

## libfx and other hosts

The gate is off unless a host calls `enableCommitGate`. Only the app's two thread starters do. libfx, ACP and `fx ask` take their turns through `takeQueuedPromptForTurn`, `takeQueuedPrompt` and `beginDirectProcessing`, never call it, and never count a finish. The cooperative host returns before it would. The SDK suites that cover the worker pass (below).

## Evidence

Sandbox runs, Linux. The failing-first runs and the final runs use the same tests, `tests/e2e/sessions.test.ts` with the two `/fork forks without the subagents` tests.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `origin/main` 35f755353, quiet | 8 of 24 runs failed (8 of 48 executions) |
| `origin/main` f4d94b8ac, quiet | 3 of 24 runs failed (3 of 48), with CI's `superseded` failure via `ownChildLines` |
| This branch, quiet | 40 of 40 runs pass (80 of 80 executions), on `6a7c7fce3` and again on `2f8c97565` built with Zig 0.17.1 |
| This branch, six busy loops on the two CPUs the tests use | 30 of 30 runs pass (60 of 60), on `6a7c7fce3` and again on `2f8c97565` built with Zig 0.17.1 |
| All seven `/fork` tests, quiet | 15 of 15 runs pass (105 of 105), on `6a7c7fce3` |
| `/fork asks once and copies the subagents`, under load | 15 of 15 runs pass, on `6a7c7fce3` |
| Real binary with the worker trace on, 12 runs | 4 holds, each released by the commit after 24 to 25 ms, no expiry, 12 of 12 pass |
| New worker tests, 7 | pass; with the gate switched off, the three I ran that need it fail |
| Drop tests, 9 | pass: a dropped finish does not hold a later report after a cancel (through the real `cancelActiveOperation`), after a session switch (the real `beginLiveSessionCancellation` and `discardEvents`), when a newer finish replaces the pacer's, and in the not-persisted branches, including the one inside the drain's finish handler; the worker logs each drop with its reason |
| Drop tests without the fix | with `acknowledgeFinishDropped` a no-op, the 6 that need it fail; with `discardEvents` not releasing, the discard and session-switch tests fail; with the call sites back on `pacer.clear`, the cancel and session-switch tests fail; with the acknowledgement removed from the drain's finish handler, its test fails (`expected 1, found 0`) |
| New session test through `appendFinishedPrompt` | passes: no `superseded` or `turn_interrupted` line, and the fork before turn N's prompt offers no subagent; with the gate switched off it fails, and the control test shows both lines |
| Full unfiltered `zig build test --summary all`, Zig 0.17.1 (CI's version, checked against the published sha256), on `2f8c97565` | every test binary compiles. The main target ran 11,379 tests: 11,351 passed, 20 skipped, 4 failed, 4 crashed. The same 12 tests fail or crash on the base `f4d94b8ac` in the same sandbox, and none is unique to this branch: file-mode and undo-permission tests, a shell `printf` test, and four `session_adapter` tests that abort with `BADF` |

title: Read quoted-pairs only inside quotes in the challenge fuzz law
body:
## Summary

Three small follow-ups to #1815, from its review notes. No behavior changes.

1. **The `mcp_challenge` fuzz law** (`src/core/mcp_host/wire_tests.zig`). The law checks that a challenge names a step-up only when the header spells `insufficient_scope`. It took every backslash out of the header to do that, inside quotes or not. The parser reads a backslash and the byte after it as one byte only inside a quoted string (RFC 9110 section 5.6.4), so the law accepted a step-up for two headers that the parser reads as none: `Bearer error="insuffic\\ient_scope"` (an escaped backslash, so the value is `insuffic\ient_scope`) and `Bearer error=insuffic\ient_scope` (unquoted, so the backslash is part of the value). A parser that dropped the wrong backslash would have passed the fuzz target. The law is now `spellsStepUp`, which reads escapes only inside a quoted string.
2. **A comment in `tests/e2e/mcp-auth.test.ts`** said what the sign-in used to do. It now says what the test checks: that a refused sign-in ends with the server's words and saves nothing.
3. **`expireLogins` in `src/core/mcp_host/runtime.zig`** now says in a comment what #1815 documents in its description. At the 45 second wait, a retry that the server would accept but that is still pending is refused, because the engine keeps the first 401 until a request that carries the token is answered, and fx saves no login the server refused and has not accepted since. The person can sign in again. The behavior is unchanged.

## Tests

- `the step-up law reads escapes only inside a quoted string` (`wire_tests.zig`) checks `spellsStepUp` on the plain and quoted name, a quoted-pair that spells it, the header the fuzzer found in #1815's CI (`mcp_challenge-b20002adaa6b`), a quoted string with no end, and then the cases that must not spell it: an escaped backslash in quotes, an unquoted backslash, a backslash before a byte the name does not have there, and another error.
- `an error written with escapes is read as the word it spells` (`discovery.zig`) gains the same two headers, which the parser reads as no step-up, with the value `insuffic\ient_scope`. These pin the parser; they pass before and after.
- Two saved inputs for the fuzz target, one per header (`mcp_challenge-007de39cced5`, `mcp_challenge-f31ecf917abd`). The saved reproducer still passes.

The law test was recorded failing before the change: with the old body (every backslash removed) in `spellsStepUp`, it fails on the escaped backslash in quotes and passes with the new body. The parser tests and saved inputs cannot fail on the old law, because the parser was already right.

## Where each check ran

- macOS arm64, API keys unset: `the step-up law reads escapes` (24 tests in the `src/main.zig` root, all pass), `an error written with escapes` (6 tests, all pass), the whole `src/mcp/mcp.zig` root (249 tests), the fuzz replay of `mcp_challenge` (25 tests over the saved inputs), `zig fmt --check src/`, and `scripts/check-public-surface.sh`.
- macOS arm64, a ReleaseSafe build of this tree, API keys unset: `tests/e2e/mcp-auth.test.ts` whole (103 pass).
- Linux x86_64: `scripts.fuzz_nightly` on `mcp_challenge` for a 300 second budget, two rounds, both ok.

## Notes for the merge

Open pull requests touch these files, but none has a hunk near these lines: #2028, #2026, #1735, #1709 and #1872 edit `mcp-auth.test.ts`; #2026, #2010, #1960 and #1753 edit `runtime.zig`; #2010, #1953 and #1914 edit `wire_tests.zig`. A merge conflict with #1953 or #1914 would be only where tests are appended to the same file.

## Docs

No docs change. The comments and tests describe behavior that #1815 already documents on the MCP pages.

title: Show fx mcp call rows again after a resume
body:
## Summary

- Show the MCP rows of the calls a command made through `fx mcp call` again after `--resume`, in the command's group: one `Ran MCP <tool> ×N` row for the calls that worked, and a row of its own for each call that failed or was cancelled.
- Save each such call as an `mcp_bridge_call` item in the session log when it ends, with only its shell call's id, its request id, the tool's name, and its outcome. Its arguments and result are never saved.
- Show a resumed call's row in Ctrl+O with no arguments or result.
- Older fx versions skip the new item and read these sessions as before.

## Limits

- A turn interrupted while its command runs shows the call's row after a resume, but not the command's row when the command saved no output. A resume does not show that command's row on main either.

title: Send the agent loop's events through one TurnEvent and emit
body:
Stacked on #2050.

The agent loop reported a turn to its front ends through `push_event` and eleven narrower `push_*` sinks. `fx acp` handled two of the 28 worker event kinds before #2032, and no front end saw one ordered, typed stream. This gives the loop one `TurnEvent` and one `AgentRuntimeDeps.emit`, and gives each front end one adapter. Nothing a user sees changes.

- `TurnEvent` (`src/core/agent/runtime/turn_event.zig`) holds today's `WorkerEvent` as its `worker` case, plus text, reasoning, a notice with its plain-text fallback, context and session notices, and HTTP errors. Tool lifecycle, diffs, route recovery status, and command output ends use their existing `WorkerEvent` kinds.
- `emit` lends its event: the payload is valid only during the call, the loop frees what it allocated once `emit` returns, and a front end copies what it keeps. Before, `push_event` and `push_diff_block` took the loop's payload and freed it, while the other sinks borrowed theirs.
- Notices that depended on whether a front end set the interactive or session sink now carry both forms, and each front end picks one, so the loop no longer asks which sinks a front end has.
- The TUI, `fx acp`, `fx ask`, subagent turns, and the runtime's test fixtures each set `emit_event`. `fx acp` maps every kind with no catch-all arm. The `push_*` sinks are gone.

The commits move one piece at a time: the union and `emit` with a forwarding shim to the old sinks, the loop's calls, then each front end, then the shim and the sinks. Each commit builds.

## Tests

- `tests/tla/agent_runtime/TurnEvents.tla` models what one front end is told: every event, in the loop's order, for a front end that writes at once and for the TUI, whose screen thread shows its queue later, and each lent payload read only while it lives and freed once, by the loop. Both design configs pass, `turn-events-today.cfg` (the old ownership) fails `LoopFrees`, and all five planted mutations are caught.
- `tests/tla/drivers/agent_runtime/turn_events.ts` runs a turn of text, a `read_file` call, and an `edit_file` call through `fx acp` and `fx ask`, and has TLC check the order each showed. Both are accepted on this branch and on #2050, and it rejects a run with two events swapped and one with the last missing. CI runs it with `--self-check`.
- The E2E files for `fx acp`, `fx ask`, subagents, and the TUI's streaming, tools, compaction, model calls, and permissions give the same results as #2050.

fx-core.wasm grows by 2,710 bytes; the budget is raised to 2,482,000.

title: Read a refused shell request as the model's mistake
body:
## Summary

- When the shell refuses a request before running anything, such as one that sets both a profile and a shell, the call is the model's mistake, not a failed command.
- When the model's next call runs the same steps, the refused calls get no row and no failure count, and the fixed call says which try it was, such as `Ran ls, fx help · 3rd try`. The group's header no longer adds `· 1 failed` for them.
- A refused call the model does not fix reads `Couldn't run ls, fx help`, without the whole command or the reason, like any call the model got wrong. The header counts no command and no failure for it, except that a collapsed group counts it when the turn ended on it. Ctrl+O still shows the error.
- A command that ran and failed is unchanged, and still reads `×3 · passed on the 3rd run` when a later run passes.

Before, two refused requests and then the fixed one:

```
├ Failed ls -l zig-out/bin/fx 2>/dev/null && ./zig-out/bin/fx help 2>&1 | head -60 · 2 invalid fields
└ Ran ls, fx help ×2 · passed on the 2nd run
```

After:

```
└ Ran ls, fx help · 3rd try
```

title: Keep a cancelled command's row when a session resumes
body:
## Summary

- When the user cancels a turn while a command runs, a resume shows the command's row again, also when the command printed nothing before the cancel. Before, the saved turn kept the row only through the command's saved output, so a command with none came back as just `▪ Cancelled · What can fx do differently?`, and the `fx mcp call` rows in its group showed alone.
- Such a turn now saves a `cancelled_command` item, `{"call_id":…}`, right before its `interruption`. The `interruption` keeps the same bytes, a command that saved output gets no item, and an older fx skips the item (D100 in `tests/tla/session_manager/system-design.md`).
- The resumed row reads as the live row, with the command's short name. Before, a command that had printed came back with its full line, such as `Cancelled echo CANCEL_PRINTED; touch .cancel-ready; sleep 60` for the live `Cancelled echo, touch, sleep`.
- The notice under a cancelled command names no command, live and after a resume: `▪ Cancelled · What can fx do differently?`, as a cancelled turn's notice reads. It used to repeat the command's full line, such as the fx binary's path and the JSON arguments of an `fx mcp call` command, while the row above already names the command by its short name. Ctrl+O still shows the full line. Other tools keep their notices, such as an MCP call's `▪ Cancelled mcp_fixture_echo · What can fx do differently?`, and only the compact view changes: the model, ACP, `fx ask`, and the saved session get the same text as before.

Before, after `--resume last` for a turn cancelled in its second command:

```
● Ran echo FIRST_STEP_DONE ✓
▪ Cancelled · What can fx do differently?
```

After, the same as live:

```
● Ran a command ✓ · 1 cancelled
├ Ran echo FIRST_STEP_DONE
└ Cancelled touch, sleep
▪ Cancelled · What can fx do differently?
```

The notice under a cancelled `fx mcp call` command, before:

```
▪ Cancelled "/path/to/fx" mcp call mcp_fixture_echo... · What
▪ Cancelled mcp_fixture_echo · What can fx do differently?
```

After:

```
▪ Cancelled · What can fx do differently?
▪ Cancelled mcp_fixture_echo · What can fx do differently?
```

title: Keep cut secrets out of traces
body:
## Summary

- `/trace` no longer keeps part of a key, token, or URL credential where it cuts a tool call's arguments or result. The kept text ends before that secret.
- The kept end of a failed tool call's arguments and result starts after a secret that its cut falls inside, including a long quoted value such as a private key, whose key the kept end no longer holds.
- A long run of text with no space or punctuation stays up to the cut, unless a key or token starts near the cut.
- A subagent's task, an auto-mode review's command and reasoning, an interrupted turn's tool arguments, the provider's gateway error text, and a shell alias's target follow the same rule.
- The debug log's tail in the trace leaves out the partial line its read starts inside.
- The trace masks a secret that fx's display cut short and marked with `...` or `…`.

title: Run the MCP engine and host TLA+ checks as two parallel CI jobs
body:
## Summary

Splits the `TLA+ MCP models and drivers` job into two jobs that run in parallel:

| Job | Runs |
|---|---|
| `TLA+ MCP engine models and driver` (`tla-mcp`) | `python3 tests/tla/mcp/run.py check`, then `bun tests/tla/drivers/mcp/driver.ts` |
| `TLA+ MCP host models and drivers` (`tla-mcp-host`) | `bun test ./tests/tla/drivers/mcp_host/` |

## Why

The job ran those three commands one after another in one step. On `main` it took about 25 minutes before #1815, then 37m37s at `0cbd30b93` and 37m54s at `7e2508110`, and at `b9324912c` it reached its 40 minute limit and was cancelled after 40m17s. #2061 was cancelled the same way. `Build & Test` has `tla-mcp` in its `needs`, so a cancelled run fails the required check and blocks a merge.

## What changes

- `tla-mcp` keeps its id and now runs the engine models and the engine driver. `tla-mcp-host` is new and runs the host drivers, whose `models.test.ts` checks the host models with TLC.
- Both jobs start from the same `build` artifact, set up Zig, Bun and tmux as before, download `tla2tools.jar` v1.7.4 and check its sha256, keep the step gate `needs.ci-need.outputs.mcp == 'true'` and `timeout-minutes: 40`, and have their own cache key (`ci-tla-mcp`, `ci-tla-mcp-host`).
- `Build & Test` (`zig`) now lists both jobs in `needs`, and its check counts ten results instead of nine. A missing, skipped or failed job fails it, as before.
- The text that named the job or gave its time now names both jobs: the comment above `ci-need` in `ci.yml`, the header of `scripts/detect-ci-need.sh`, `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `tests/tla/README.md`. The detector's rules are unchanged, and its tests pass. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is on the detector's MCP list, so this pull request runs both jobs.
- No required status check names the job, and `publish-libfx.yml` waits for the whole `CI` run, so nothing else refers to it by name.

## Verification

- `actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml` reports three findings, and `main`'s file gives the same three: an unused variable in a shell step at line 132, and two `steps.zig` references at the end of the file. None is in these lines.
- A parse of the workflow shows both jobs with `needs: [build, ci-need]`, the same step gate, 40 minute limits and separate cache keys, and `zig` with ten entries in `needs`.
- `jq -e 'length == 10 and all(.[]; . == "success")'` passes for ten successes, and fails for nine results and for ten with one failure.
- `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_detect_ci_need`: 15 tests pass.
- CI on `1441a824d`: `TLA+ MCP engine models and driver` took 20m28s and `TLA+ MCP host models and drivers` 16m46s. They started within a second of each other, so the two together take 20m28s of wall time where one job took about 38 minutes. `Build & Test` started after both, and its log lists ten `success` results.

title: Admit a subagent whose parent has more than 256 permission rules
body:
## Summary

- A subagent now starts when its parent's folder has more than 256 permission rules. When fx admits a subagent, `captureAdmission` copies the parent's rules into it, and it returned `TooManyAdmissionItems` once there were more than 256. The `subagent` tool then reported `Subagent failed: admission: AdmissionFailed` before the child reached a model.
- A parent can run with that many rules. A client that serves several hundred MCP tools and writes one rule for each tool is an example: the parent works, but it can start no subagent. This is the same reason #1104 lifted the cap on the MCP tool names a child inherits.
- The child still receives every rule, so a deny on the parent still applies to the child. Tool names and grants keep their count cap.

## Verification

- `zig build test` with Zig 0.17.1 on macOS arm64: 11,832 of 11,842 passed and 9 were skipped. The one failure, `streamed presentation preserves ANSI OSC 8 code fence and table spans`, fails the same way on unpatched v0.0.17 on the same machine. It was not rerun on unpatched `main`.

- `./zig-out/bin/fx acp`, with a scripted model on a loopback gateway and a parent in `auto` mode that starts a subagent which writes a file:
  - 256, 300 and 1,200 rules for the folder: the subagent's work completed and the file was written, with empty stderr.
  - 300 rules plus `"write_file": "deny"`: the subagent was admitted and the file was not written.
  - The v0.0.17 release binary: 256 rules completed, and 300 rules failed at admission.
- Not run: the end-to-end suites and Linux, which CI covers.
