title: Show the finished turn behind an open prompt once mail waits for its commit
body:
## Summary

- A subagent's report or message that waits for an agent's finished turn, which an open prompt keeps in the pacer, now starts its turn at once, however long after the turn ended it comes: 0 s, 6 s and 10 s after with an approval open, and 0 s and 6 s after with a question open, in every measured run. Text the user typed while the turn ran, which the turn did not take in, waits for the turn's commit like mail and is treated the same way. Before, mail that came at once waited out the commit gate's five second limit, and mail that came five seconds or more after the turn ended found the limit already passed. Either way the mail's turn started before the finished turn was saved, and the session log got `superseded` and `turn_interrupted` lines for both turns.
- Change to the limit of the commit gate (#2059): its five seconds now count from the first time the worker holds mail for a commit, not from the moment the turn's finish was pushed. The limit is still five seconds, and a hold still ends at it. Before, a person who left a prompt open for more than five seconds and then got a subagent's report found the limit already passed, so the report started at once, before the commit and before the loop could flush. In the trace, `waited_ms` of `commit_gate_released` and `commit_gate_expired` is now how long the mail was held, and no longer how long ago the finish was pushed.
- Visible change: today the reply behind an open prompt shows when the prompt closes, or above the prompt when a waiting report's or message's turn starts at the five second limit. With this change it shows above the prompt as soon as a report or message waits for it, with its summary line, once, and the prompt stays. This is what fx showed before the commit gate, when the report's turn started at once and flushed it. While no report, message or typed text waits for the turn's commit, nothing changes and the reply still waits for the prompt to close.
- If the text cannot be shown, fx logs it once, keeps the finished turn in the pacer and does not try again until the hold ends; the five second limit then ends the hold as it does today. If the commit itself fails, the finish is acknowledged as on `main`, the hold ends and the mail's turn starts.

## How

- The commit gate holds a report until the main loop commits the finished turn. An open prompt keeps the loop from ticking the pacer, so the turn is never committed, and the report's turn start, which is what flushes the pacer, waits for the commit. Only the limit ended that wait.
- `WorkerRuntime.commitGateWaitsForCommit` says, under the worker's lock, that the gate holds a continuation for a commit. A continuation is mail, and also text the user typed into the running turn that missed it (`finishProcessing` makes it one, and the gate already holds it), so the flush runs for typed text too. A prompt typed after the turn ended is an ordinary prompt: the gate does not hold it and the flush leaves the pacer alone.
- `commitGateRemainingMsLocked` starts the limit (`commit_gate_since_ms`) the first time it finds mail to hold in a spell, and logs `commit_gate_held` there. `noteFinishPushedLocked` only counts the finish now. The limit is checked on every take of work as before, so a hold ends at most five seconds after it began. A hold ends when its commit releases it or at its limit, and both clear the mark that says the hold was logged, so the next hold starts its own clock. One unit test pins each end, and an end-to-end test pins the release end with a second report that comes more than the limit after the first hold began.
- `noteCommitGateFlushFailed` marks a failed flush only while a finish is unacknowledged. A flush whose commit fails has acknowledged it already (`appendFinishedPrompt` acknowledges in a `defer`), so the count may be zero by then; the mark would outlive that hold, and nothing clears a mark at zero. Both the mark and the count are on the worker, not on `App`.
- `Runtime.flushPacerForHeldMail` in `app_worker_runtime.zig` runs in the paused branch of `tickAgentInContext`. When the pacer of the agent in context holds a finished turn and the worker holds mail for it, it calls `pacer.flushPresentationAtBoundary`, the call `workerBridgeDrainAssistantText` makes when the next turn starts. That shows the text, commits the turn through `appendFinishedPrompt`, and its `defer` acknowledges the finish, which releases the held mail. `src/main.zig` takes that one call line, and the hidden agent test, which posts, takes and frees the worker's mail with `c_allocator` as production does.
- Threads: the loop thread owns the pacer, the transcript and the session, and it does the flush. The worker thread only waits and sees the count drop. The reads of the worker's state take its lock for a few instructions, only on passes where a prompt pauses the pacer.
- Hidden agents go through the same function: `tickChildren` already visits a hidden agent whose pacer holds a finished turn, so no visit is new. While a scrollback handoff is pending, `tickChildren` skips every hidden agent, so none is flushed then. A test pins both.
- Which prompt keeps the pacer still, and whether the flush is right there:

  | Prompt | Flush |
  |---|---|
  | A subagent's approval or question shown on the agent's screen | Right, and the case of the end-to-end tests. The finished turn only shows and commits, as the report's turn start would show and commit it. |
  | An agent's own approval, question or out-of-credits question | A running turn opens it, and that turn's start already flushed the pacer. There is no finished turn to flush. |
  | The sign-in picker's key entry | Right for the same reason, and pinned by the hidden agent test. Not driven on the binary. |

- `@hasDecl(@TypeOf(agent.worker), "commitGateWaitsForCommit")` is the only new probe, as `acknowledgeDroppedFinish` uses one. Both methods are `pub`, and the tests run against the real worker, so a private method would turn the flush off and fail them.
- `tests/tla/subagent/MainMail.tla` needs no change. The model has no clock: its `Commit` step is allowed at any time while a commit is owed, and `Expire` is a step that can happen at any time while one is owed, so a later start of the limit is inside what it already allows. The flush only makes the commit happen sooner. `sh tests/tla/subagent/check.sh` exits 0 with 47 ok lines on `main` and on this branch, and the three planted defects (`no-gate`, `stuck-gate`, `drop-unacknowledged`) still fail as required.

## Testing

Zig 0.17.1 (`zig version`) in a Linux x86_64 sandbox, unless a row says macOS. On this head each test also checks that `commit_gate_released` says `reason=committed`. On `c746cc686` all six pass 3 of 3 on Linux: the two new tests pin what that head already did.

For #2076, measured with its own end-to-end tests before this change gained its late-report tests, 3 runs each, on `main` `50af72932`, on this change alone, on #2076 alone (at `d2705e88c`), and on a hand merge of the two. `A1` are this change's two end-to-end tests. `B2` are #2076's. "Both faults" are the three tests of an earlier attempt, which need both changes.

| Test | `main` | This change | #2076 alone | Both |

| A1 approval open | 0 of 3 | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 | 3 of 3 |
| A1 question open | 0 of 3 | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 | 3 of 3 |
| B2 approval answered | 0 of 3 | 0 of 3 | 3 of 3 | 3 of 3 |

## Not in this change

- The report's request still lacks the finished turn when the report was posted before the commit. The pane and the session are right after this change, but the history the mail's turn starts with is not. #2076 fixes that.
- The commit gate's limit counts from the first hold. A loop that stays busy past the limit after the turn's finish still makes the gate give up with no prompt open, and the flush cannot help there, because the finish has not reached the pacer. That belongs to the gate's limit and is left to its owner (W85).
- A hold that ends without a release (the held mail leaves the queue) leaves later mail in the same spell on the same clock, as the push clock did before.
- No end-to-end test drives typed text that missed the turn. A line typed while the turn runs interrupts the model request and joins the turn (`steering_admission` with `interrupt_model=true`, then `prompt_steering_consumed`); it misses the turn only inside the turn's closing step, after steering is closed, a window of a few milliseconds that a keyboard cannot hit twice the same way. A worker test and an app test cover it.
- A queued user prompt and `/compact` take their history when they are queued, as before (W80).
- The sign-in key entry is not driven on the binary. A unit test covers it.

title: Keep a closing subagent closing until its close is written
body:
## Summary

A subagent that its parent or the user closed could, for a moment before its close was written, be listed again, shown as not closing in `/trace`, and take a message. A message in that moment froze fx: its call and the slot that writes the close waited for each other, and every call that takes `admission_mutex` stopped behind them, the main loop's too. The subagent now stays closing until its close is written.

## Cause

`settleClose` (`src/core/subagent/tool_host.zig:2119` on `origin/main`) removed the child from `closing` under `admission_mutex` (`:2125`), released the lock, and only then took the registry's lock (`:2132`) and wrote the close (`:2134`). In between the child was neither closing nor gone:

- `listChildren` (`:418`) listed it. The app's `syncChildList` (`src/core/app/app_agents_runtime.zig`) adds an agent for every listed child it does not hold, and the app had already taken the child as closed, so the agent would come back and no later close would drop it.
- `traceChildren` (`:484`) said `closing = false`.
- A message was admitted. `admitAndStartManagedWork` (`:2402`) holds `admission_mutex` across `managed.start` (`:2421`), which waits for the ending slot (`managed_owner.zig:399`). The admitted message made the child busy in the registry again, so the slot's close failed with `ChildBusy`, and `closeNotWritten` waited for `admission_mutex`. Neither went on.
- A second close answered `stopped=true`, wrote the close itself, and the first writer then failed with `ChildUnavailable`.

## Change

- `Runtime.closing` holds an entry per closing child, with a `settling` mark. `settleClose` marks the entry and writes the close outside `admission_mutex`, as before. A final admission-locked step, `finishClose`, removes the entry; it replaces `closeNotWritten`. A second settle of a close that is being written leaves it to the thread that has it. A write that fails removes the entry and the child's unseen mark, so the child is listed again and the app keeps its agent, as before. No lock is nested.
- A message to the child in that time is refused with `child_closing`, and a second close answers that it is already closing.
- `src/core/subagent/close_test_controls.zig` holds a close's write for the tests, as the start and end controls do for theirs: an inline hook in test builds, and `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_CLOSE_HELD` and `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_CLOSE_RELEASE` for the E2E test. A build that sets neither reads one environment variable per close, and the libfx artifacts leave it out.
- `scripts/cli_shape_registry.json` lists the two new variables as internal controls of the test job, which `python3 -m scripts.check_cli_shape` in `Build & Test` requires. It is a JSON-only commit, `5e646070f`; the evidence below was measured on the code before it, which it does not change.
- `tests/tla/subagent/StopMessage.tla` splits a closing subagent's end into the work end and `WriteClose`, with a `writing` phase that refuses messages as `closing` does. `ClosingHoldsNothing` is the new rule, and the planted `unmark_early` defect breaks it. `StopMessageTrace.tla` and the `stop-message.test.ts` driver replay the close's write, taken from fx's `closed` trace line, and a planted trace without it is rejected.

## Evidence

Every run was in a sandbox with the official Zig 0.17.1 (checked against the published sha256), on base `4790dbf20`. `origin/main` is `50af72932` now; this diff applies to it cleanly (`git apply --check`), and I did not rebuild there.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| The 6 new unit tests on unchanged `origin/main` with the hold only | 4 fail: the listing and the trace, the message (blocked, so it fails after its 5 s bound), the second close, and the failed write while held. 2 pass: the sanity test and the back-off test. The run ends in 6 s |
| The same 6 tests with the change | all pass |
| Mutations, each on the change | back-off check removed: the back-off test fails. The failed write's unseen cleanup removed, or its entry kept: the failed-write test fails |
| The 6 new tests, 500 runs each | 500 of 500 quiet and 500 of 500 under CPU load |
| 17 close tests, the new ones and the existing ones, 200 runs | quiet 200 of 200. Under load 199 of 200: the failure is the existing "an idle subagent closes at once" test, which fails 5 of 1500 runs under load on unchanged `origin/main` and 4 of 1500 with the change |
| E2E "a message to a subagent whose close is not written yet is refused" (real binary) | on unchanged `origin/main` with the hold only: 0 of 3 pass, the message call hangs until the 60 s limit. With the change: 20 of 20 quiet, 15 of 15 under load |
| `tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`, `-t subagent` | 38 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail |
| `tests/tla/subagent/check.sh`, no arguments, `fx-cloud run` | exit 0, 47 `ok` lines, including `stop-message`, `stop-message-deep` and `stop-message-mutation-unmark-early` (`ClosingHoldsNothing` violated, as required) |
| Subagent drivers | `stop-message.test.ts` 25 pass, with 40 random walks added 65 pass; `quiet-relay.test.ts` 6; `main-mail.test.ts` 9; `driver.ts --self-check` exit 0 |
| libfx: addon and Wasm builds, SDK native and Wasm suites | all exit 0 |
| Full unfiltered `zig build test --summary all`, change against unchanged `origin/main` | main target 11536 against 11530 passed, the same 20 skipped, 4 failed, 4 crashed, 2 leaks. The 12 failing or crashing tests have the same names on both sides, all known sandbox limits |

## Limits

- I did not drive the App's agent-list reappearance: it needs a real subagent host inside the App fixture. The first unit test checks what `syncChildList` depends on, that a child the app took with `takeClosed` is not listed before it is gone.
- The failed-write test passes on unchanged `origin/main` except for its assertion that the child stays closing while the write is held; the failed write's own outcome is behavior this change keeps. The back-off test passes there too, since the mark is gone by then.
- I did not measure how often a real user reaches the window. It is as long as the registry lock takes to be acquired, so it is short.
- No crash and restart check: the registry write and its log lines are unchanged.
- "an idle subagent closes at once" is a flaky test before this change; this PR leaves it alone.

title: Give mail queued behind a finished turn the turn the loop commits after it
body:
## Summary

- A subagent's report or message that is posted after an agent finished a turn, and before the main loop committed that turn, now starts with that turn in its history, except when a prompt the user typed waits ahead of the mail, or the mail joins that prompt's turn while steering is open: then the turn is still missing, as on `main` (see "Not in this change"). Before, the mail's own turn went to the model without the user's prompt and the finished turn's answer. This showed when a subagent's approval or question was answered while the report waited, and when the prompt stayed open: the report 0 s, 6 s or 10 s after main's turn ended with an approval open, 0 s or 6 s after with a question open, and a second report 6 s after the report's turn ended. In each case the report's request lacked the user's prompt and the finished turn's answer.
- Only the mail's own turn ran without the finished turn. The loop committed that turn to the session right after, so the saved session log has it, which the end-to-end tests read, and a second report's request carries it and the report's turn before it. Nothing was lost from the session.
- The change is in the worker's queue and in what `appendFinishedPrompt` and the visual epoch commit hand to the worker after they commit a turn. The pane checks of #2074's tests (the first turn shows once above the open prompt, and nothing is shown twice) pass on this head. A prompt the user typed after the turn ended owes nothing and is not changed (a test pins it).
- When the commit gate gives up (its five second limit, which counts from the first time it holds the mail), the mail still starts without the turn, as before, and the trace now names how many turns it started without.

## How

- The worker keeps one history for its whole queue (`queued_history`). The first prompt posted into an empty queue gives it, and later prompts' own histories are dropped (`enqueuePromptLocked`). When a turn ends, the worker adds the turn to that history, and to what each queued prompt derives from it, but only when the queue is not empty then (`propagateHistoryTurnToQueue`). Mail that is posted after the turn ends takes the history the loop has, which lacks a turn the loop has not committed.
- `WorkerRuntime.queued_history_owed` counts the finished turns an empty queue's history was taken without: the unacknowledged finishes when it adopted a continuation's history. Each acknowledgement lowers it, and `acknowledgeFinishCommittedTurn` adds a committed turn to the queue through the same propagation while it is above zero. It is read and written only under `worker_mutex`.
- `appendFinishedPrompt` and `appendFinishedPromptForVisualEpoch` (`app_session_runtime.zig`) pass the turn they committed, its snapshot files and the history limit. When the append fails nothing was committed, and the plain acknowledgement runs as before. The snapshot files are reference counted, so each queued prompt keeps them until it ends, as for mail that was queued when the turn ended.
- Each turn goes into the queue's history at most once: at its end when the queue is not empty then, or at its commit when the queue was empty then and mail took the history before the commit. The count is above zero only in the second case. When a typed prompt took the empty queue's history first, the count is zero and the turn does not go in (see "Not in this change").
- A finish that is dropped unsaved (`cancel`, `cancel_approval`, `cancel_question`, `cancel_compaction`, `session_switch`, `pacer_replaced`, `not_persisted`, and `discardEvents`) lowers the count and adds nothing, so the history matches the session, which never saved that turn. A session switch clears the count with the queue (`clearQueuedPromptsLocked`).
- The count is set when a post adopts a base and means something only while the queue holds that base: the other calls that empty the queue leave it as it was, the next post sets it again, and a commit with no queued prompt adds nothing. A test empties a queue with five calls (a discard, a take, a removal, a drop of messages, a clear) while a turn is owed, and checks that the next message gets the turn once, whether the loop commits after that post or before it.
- A turn that cannot be added (an allocation failure) is logged with `dropped=turn_in_queued_history`. The gate giving up logs `queued mail starts without finished turns turns=N`. Both go to the trace.
- With #2074 on `main` the loop commits the finished turn while a prompt is open, and the report's turn starts then. The end-to-end tests below need this change as well: on `main`, which has #2074, they fail at the check of the request, all but the one with no prompt open.
- `src/main.zig` takes tests only, and no state is added to `App`. The hidden agent test commits a turn in the agent's own tick, and posts, takes and frees the worker's mail with `c_allocator`, as production does.
- `tests/tla/subagent/MainMail.tla` needs no change: it models when mail may start, not what history it starts with. No file under `tests/tla` changes.

## Testing

Zig 0.17.1 (`zig version`) in a Linux x86_64 sandbox, unless a row says macOS. The head is `775e93ae0`, which merges `main` `0bd01d376`. `build.zig` has no `test-one` step, so the unit binary comes from a local edit that is not part of this change: a `test-filter` option passed as the `.filters` of `exe_tests`, and a `test-one` step that runs `exe_tests`.

| What | Command or method | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Format | `zig fmt --check src/` | exit 0 |
| Unit tests: 18 new, 22 near them (the gate, the drops, the history, the handoff), and the 27 unnamed `test` blocks that every filtered build runs | loop over the built test binary, each run needs exit 0 and 67 `OK` lines, and the first run needs the `OK` line of each new test; the binary is built with one filter for each of the 18 new tests (listed below) and the filters `the commit gate`, `a worker held by the commit gate`, `a finish the app dropped`, `an acknowledged drop`, `discarded events release`, `a report that missed a finished turn`, `a finished turn the pacer replaces or clears`, `a finished turn the loop does not save after` and `scrollback handoff` | Debug 20 of 20, ReleaseSafe 20 of 20 |
| The same under ThreadSanitizer | `-Doptimize=ReleaseSafe -Dsanitize-thread=true`, 20 runs | 20 of 20, 0 reports, 67 `OK` lines per run |
| End-to-end, Linux | `cd tests/e2e && FX_SOUND=0 bun test tui-host-switch.test.ts -t "<name>"` for each of the 9 tests below, 20 rounds each | 20 of 20 for each |
| End-to-end, macOS arm64 binary | `fx-cloud macos-build`, then `FXC_LOCAL=1 FX_SOUND=0`, 10 rounds each, one at a time | 10 of 10 for each |
| ThreadSanitizer on `fx` | `-Dsanitize-thread=true`, 20 rounds of each of the 9 end-to-end tests, in two sandboxes | 180 of 180 flows pass. Every report is one race: `enableSubagentHostV2` writes what `childRole` reads through `prepareChildRun` (`app_session_runtime.zig`, `app_agent_runtime.zig`). `main` `0bd01d376` has the same race: the same two functions are reported there in the test with no prompt open, which passes on `main`. Neither function is in this change. |
| TLA+ | `sh tests/tla/subagent/check.sh` | exit 0 and 48 ok lines on `main` `0bd01d376`, and the same on this head. `no-gate`, `stuck-gate` and `drop-unacknowledged` still fail as required. |
| Full `zig build test --summary all` | once on plain `main` `0bd01d376`, and once on this head | the same 9 tests fail on both (13 failed in the build summary), and no test binary fails to compile: tests of read-only files and folders that deny writes, one `printf` test, and one capture store deadline test, which do not hold in this sandbox. 12,184 of 12,229 tests pass on `main` and 12,202 of 12,247 on this head, 18 more: the new unit tests. |

| The path without a prompt that #2059 fixed | `cd tests/e2e && FX_SOUND=0 bun test sessions.test.ts -t "/fork" --rerun-each=50`, in two sandboxes | 800 of 800: 100 runs of each of the 8 tests whose name contains `/fork`: `/fork asks nothing when no subagent existed at the fork point`; `/fork asks once and copies the subagents made before the fork point, with their history up to it`; `/fork forks without the subagents when the answer is Esc`; `/fork forks without the subagents when the answer is n`; `/fork gives the fork the source's workspace_capture refs without waiting for them`; `/fork starts a session before a chosen prompt and leaves the source as it was`; `/fork stops a subagent waiting on a long shell command and ends that command`; `/fork switches to the fork while a subagent of the source is still working` |

The 18 new unit tests, whose names are the first 18 filters:

- `mail posted behind a turn the pacer holds gets that turn when the loop commits it`
- `mail posted behind a finish the loop has not applied yet gets that turn when the loop commits it`
- `a message posted behind a finished turn gets that turn like a report`
- `two reports behind a finished turn share one history that has the turn once`
- `a turn the loop drops unsaved never reaches mail queued behind it, whichever reason drops it`
- `a session switch retires the queue and what it was owed`
- `a cancelled turn's commit reaches mail queued behind it like any turn`
- `a commit that failed leaves mail queued behind it with the history it has`
- `a gate that expires logs the turns its mail starts without, and a late commit adds nothing`
- `a turn added at its end to a queue that was not empty is not added again at its commit`
- `turns the loop commits one after the other reach the mail in the order it commits them`
- `a prompt a user typed owes nothing: its history is the one it was typed with`
- `a committed turn's snapshot files stay with the mail queued behind it`
- `appendFinishedPrompt gives the worker the turn it committed, with its snapshot files and the history limit`
- `appendFinishedPrompt acknowledges a turn it could not commit without the turn`
- `a visual epoch commit acknowledges with its turn, and one that did not commit acknowledges nothing`
- `a hidden agent's turn that its own tick commits reaches the report queued behind it`
- `a queue emptied while a turn is owed gives the next mail the turn once, whichever call emptied it`

Each break below was applied alone to this head and run against the unit tests built as above:

| Break | Tests that fail |
|---|---|
| No count when an empty queue takes its history | 11 tests: the hidden agent test, the held turn test, the unapplied finish test, the message test, the two reports test, the drops test, the five calls test, the cancelled turn test, the expiry test, the order test, the snapshot files test |
| A prompt a user typed is counted too | 1 test: the typed prompt test |
| An acknowledgement does not lower the count | 6 tests: the held turn test, the two reports test, the drops test, the five calls test, the failed commit test, the order test |
| A commit adds its turn without asking the count | 2 tests: the test of a turn added at its end, the typed prompt test |
| The expiry keeps the count | 1 test: the expiry test |
| The expiry does not log the turns missed | 1 test: the expiry test |
| `appendFinishedPrompt` never gives the worker the turn | 2 tests: the hidden agent test, the app test of the committed turn |
| The turn goes in without its snapshot files | 1 test: the snapshot files test |
| A retired queue keeps its count | 1 test: the session switch test |
| The visual epoch path gives no turn | 1 test: the visual epoch test |
| The turn is added with another allocator than the worker's | 3 tests (the tests abort): #2074's hidden agent flush test, #2059's test of a report behind a missed finish, the hidden agent test |

The 9 end-to-end tests. The first six are #2074's tests, which now also check what the report's request carries: the user's prompt, the first turn's tool calls and its answer, and for the second report the report's turn before it. The first two release the helper's report as soon as main's turn ended, with an approval and with a question open; the next three release it 6 s and 10 s after with the approval still open, and 6 s after with the question open; the sixth has a scout whose report comes 6 s after the report's turn ended, a second report more than the limit after the first hold began. The seventh has a subagent still at work and no prompt open. The last two leave an approval or a question open when main's turn ends, and answer it once the worker holds the report. Baselines: 3 runs each, with this head's test file on `main`.

| Test (the `-t` filter is the whole name) | `main` `0bd01d376`: Linux, macOS (3 runs each) | This head: Linux (20), macOS (10) |
|---|---|---|
| `a report for main starts its next turn while a subagent's approval stays open` | 0 of 3, 0 of 3 | 20 of 20, 10 of 10 |
| `a report for main starts its next turn while a subagent's question stays open` | 0 of 3, 0 of 3 | 20 of 20, 10 of 10 |
| `a report 6 s late for main starts its next turn while a subagent's approval stays open` | 0 of 3, 0 of 3 | 20 of 20, 10 of 10 |
| `a report 10 s late for main starts its next turn while a subagent's approval stays open` | 0 of 3, 0 of 3 | 20 of 20, 10 of 10 |
| `a report 6 s late for main starts its next turn while a subagent's question stays open` | 0 of 3, 0 of 3 | 20 of 20, 10 of 10 |
| `a second report more than the limit after the first hold starts its turn while a subagent's approval stays open` | 0 of 3, 0 of 3 | 20 of 20, 10 of 10 |
| `a report for main starts its next turn while no prompt is open, and carries the first turn` | 3 of 3, 3 of 3 | 20 of 20, 10 of 10 |
| `a report that waited for main's turn while a subagent's approval was open carries that turn once the prompt is answered` | 0 of 3, 0 of 3 | 20 of 20, 10 of 10 |
| `a report that waited for main's turn while a subagent's question was open carries that turn once the prompt is answered` | 0 of 3, 0 of 3 | 20 of 20, 10 of 10 |

Every failure on `main`, on Linux and on macOS, is at the first check of the report's request (`expect(userTexts(body).some((entry) => entry.includes("SWITCH_USER"))).toBe(true)`): the request lacks the user's prompt. The test with no prompt open passes on `main` as well. It is a control for the path without a prompt, not a test of this change: a test that fails there needs a loop that is still behind when the report is posted, which depends on the machine's speed (see below).

## Not in this change

- A prompt the user typed, and `/compact`, take their history when they are queued, as before (W80). A typed prompt that is queued inside the short window before an earlier finished turn commits changes what mail behind it gets. With T the earlier turn and P the typed prompt, four orders, each run as a unit probe on the worker (the probes are not tests of this change):
  - P waits in the queue ahead of the mail, and T commits before P starts: the mail's history lacks T, as on `main` (run).
  - The mail joins P's running turn while steering is open: the mail's history lacks T, as on `main` (run).
  - The mail is posted after steering closed, and T commits before P ends: the mail gets T, then P; on `main` it lacks T (run).
  - As the third, but T commits after P ends: the mail gets P, then T, out of order; on `main` it lacks T (run).
- A loop that stays busy for longer than the commit gate's five second limit, which counts from the first time the gate holds the mail, still makes the gate give up with no prompt open, and then the mail starts without the turn, with the trace line above. This belongs to the gate's limit (W85).
- No end-to-end test drives a loop that is still applying a long answer when the report is posted. Whether the loop is still behind depends on the machine's speed, so such a test can pass on `main` and prove nothing. The unit test for mail posted behind a finish that its events still hold pins that case without timing.

title: Give replayed ACP messages the same id on every load
body:
Stacked on #2065.

`session/load` gave every replayed message a new random `messageId` on each load, even though the variable was named `stable_message_id`. A client could not match a message across loads, and `sh.fx/forkBefore` had no stable id to name a prompt by.

Each replayed message now gets `turn-{n}-{k}`: its turn's number in the session log and its place among that turn's replayed messages. A turn's prompt, with its images, is `turn-{n}-0`, then each tool step's text and the final reply count up. The session manager never reuses a turn number, and a fork continues after the turns it copies, so an id names one saved message. Live messages keep their random ids, since live text splits at each model request and a replay splits at each saved tool step.

- `src/acp/sessions.zig`: `ReplayIds` gives each message of one replayed turn its id. The v2 visitor takes the log's turn number through a new `appendNumbered`; an in-memory or WASM history uses each turn's place. A conversion notice, which belongs to no turn, keeps a random id.
- `src/core/session/session_adapter.zig`: `visitHistory` passes the turn number to a visitor that declares `appendNumbered`, and every other visitor keeps `append`.
- `tests/tla/acp/AcpFollow.tla`: the id rule gets its own `IdRules` flag, apart from the following rules, and `StableIds` checks replayed messages only. `AcpFollowIds.cfg` shows fx with this change and without following, and a new planted bug takes ids from the replay's order.
- `tests/tla/drivers/acp/follow/driver.ts`: runs the real `fx acp` on one connection through new sessions, prompts, restarts and loads, and has TLC check each run against `AcpFollow` through `AcpFollowTrace.tla`. `check.sh --ci` runs it.

Verification:

- `sh tests/tla/acp/check.sh --ci`: exit 0. The AcpFollow configs give their expected verdicts, follow's planted bugs are killed 11/11, and every ACP driver passes.
- The follow driver accepts both plans here and rejects both with the model of fx before this change. On #2065's head it is the reverse.
- New E2E test: two loads in two new processes give the same five ids, and a live reply keeps a random id. It fails on #2065's head.
- `acp.test.ts`, `sessions.test.ts` and `ultrafast-fake-gateway.test.ts` match #2065's head, apart from the new test and the random `/fork` failure in `sessions.test.ts`, which fails at the same rate on both builds when they alternate in one sandbox.
- `zig build test`: only the failures that a root sandbox always gives.
- macOS: two turns, then two loads in new `fx acp` processes, gave the same ids.

title: Show a command's steps past its here-document, and the error it reported
body:
## Summary

Two command rows told the story wrong:

- **A command with a here-document showed its whole text.** The short form lexed the document's body as shell words, so an apostrophe in it, such as `core's`, stopped the lex, and the row fell back to the full command. The body is now taken out before the lex, so the row shows the steps, such as `Ran cat, wc`. A command whose lines core folded into one still ends the document's step at its delimiter.
- **A failed command's reason could be a line of code it printed.** The reason was the first output line that held "error" or "fail" anywhere, even inside a name such as `terminal_action_field_error_code`. Now it is, in order:
  1. the first line that reports an error or a failure, such as `Error: timed out` or `main.c:3: error: bad type`, where the word stands alone;
  2. else the last line where one of the command's programs, or its shell, speaks, such as `sed: 1: ...` or `ls: missing-file: No such file or directory`;
  3. else the first line that names an error or a failure as a word;
  4. else the last line, as before.

Before:

```
● Ran cat > notes.md <<'EOF' The model's notes EOF wc -l notes.md ✓
● Exited 1 printf, ls · const error_code = 1;
```

After:

```
● Ran cat, wc ✓
● Exited 1 printf, ls · ls: missing-file: No such file or directory
```

## Tests

- Unit tests cover the short form of a here-document with an apostrophe, two documents on one line, `<<-`, a here-string, a shift in `$(( ))`, `<<` in quotes and comments, and a folded command. They also cover the reason order on real output shapes, including a command that printed code before `sed` failed.
- Two new story tests in `tests/e2e/tui-tool-story.test.ts` fail on main and pass here: the here-document row, live and after `--resume last`, and the reason of a command that printed code before `ls` failed.

title: Answer session/set_config_option during a turn in fx acp
body:
Stacked on #2077.

`fx acp` refused `session/set_config_option` while the session's turn ran, with `-32600` "Prompt already in progress". The TUI's model and effort pickers work during a turn and apply from the next one ("Next turn will use ..."), and `session/set_mode` already worked that way. The refusal also hid a lifetime bug: the running turn borrowed `session.model` and the credential slices, which a model or provider change frees.

Now the request is answered at once, and the change applies from the next turn:

- `src/acp/prompt.zig`: a turn copies its model, provider, credential, Fast, Ultrafast and effort into `TurnSettings` when it starts. The job, the agent config, the tool context, the capability callbacks, the title task and the journal's progress record read the copy. The key is zeroed when the turn frees it.
- `src/acp/server.zig`: a per-session `settings_mutex`, held by `session/set_config_option` for its changes, by a turn while it picks its credential and copies its settings, and by the turn's credential renewal while it publishes. Lock order: `settings_mutex`, then `catalog_mutex`, then `session_write_mutex`. A renewed credential reaches the session only while the session still has the turn's provider; otherwise the turn keeps it, and a trace line says why. `session/set_config_option` leaves the requests a running turn holds.
- `src/acp/sessions.zig`: the turn-end usage update reads the turn's model, and a `session/load` of an open session reads its credential under the settings lock, so it no longer races the turn's renewal.
- `tests/tla/acp/AcpConfigTurn.tla`: the rules, with a config for fx acp before them, and five planted bugs (`drivers/acp/config_turn/check-spec.ts`). `drivers/acp/config_turn/driver.ts` holds a turn at the fake Gateway, changes the model, and has TLC check each run against the model.

Verification:

- `sh tests/tla/acp/check.sh --ci`: exit 0. `MCAcpConfigTurn` passes, `AcpConfigTurnToday` fails `AnswersDuringTurn` as it must, and every ACP driver passes. check-spec kills 5/5 planted bugs.
- The config_turn driver accepts both plans here and rejects both with the model of fx before this change; on #2077's head it is the reverse.
- E2E: the new test "a model change during a turn applies from the next turn" and the updated hold test pass, and both fail on #2077's head. `acp.test.ts`, `sessions.test.ts`, `ultrafast-fake-gateway.test.ts` and `configured-providers.test.ts` otherwise match #2077's head.
- `zig build test`: only the failures of a sandbox that doesn't enforce file permission bits; the new unit test keeps a renewed credential out of a session that changed provider.
- macOS: a model change during a held turn was answered at once, the turn's second request kept the old model, and the next turn used the new one.

title: Make a stop or close right after a subagent's work ended act on the right work
body:
## Summary

A subagent's slot records the end of a work and asks the host what follows, then goes on a few instructions later: it starts the next work or publishes that it is done. In that gap `Owner.stop` and `Owner.closeByUser` still saw a running slot, so a parent's stop or close, or the user's close, that landed there got a wrong answer and could be lost:

| In the gap | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parent `stop`, nothing next | "Stopped reviewer: its turn ended." | "reviewer was not working." |
| Parent `close`, nothing next | "Closed reviewer, ending its turn." | "Closed reviewer. A later message to reviewer starts a new one." |
| User close, nothing next | `stopped=true` for work that had ended | `stopped=false` |
| Parent `stop`, a message waiting | The slot cleared the stop, the next turn ran, its report arrived | The stop takes effect on the next work, which starts stopped: no turn, no report |
| Parent `close`, a message waiting | The closed child ran its next turn and a report for it reached the parent | The next work starts stopped, the close is written once it ends, no report |
| User close, a message waiting | The closed child ran its next turn | The next work starts stopped and reports the user's close, as a user's close of running work does |
| Parent `stop` while the user began a turn on the child's screen | The stop took the ended slot's answer and never reached the user's turn | The stop ends the user's turn |

The registry, report counts, `takeClosed`, the wording outside the gap and the session log in the normal case do not change.

## Change

- `managed_owner.zig`: `Slot.ended` is set under `Owner.mutex` once a work's end is recorded. `Owner.stop` returns null and `Owner.closeByUser` returns false while it is set. New `Owner.markNext` spends the ended work's stop flags (cancel, stopped by parent or user, closed by user, settled feedback) when the host chooses a next work; the slot no longer does it after the hook, so a stop or close that arrives between the choice and the next start stays. The slot still resets the live metrics itself as it goes on: `markNext` must not touch them, because the term WebAssembly surface reaches the host's hook but never runs a slot, and `live_metrics.zig` uses 64-bit atomics that wasm32 does not compile (the second commit; the first commit failed `SDK build (WASM)` on `fx-term-wasm`). The `EndHook` comment states that the hook calls `markNext` before it returns true.
- `tool_host.zig`: `nextOrIdleLocked` calls `markNext` after `startNextPendingLocked` returns true, under `admission_mutex`, where it already calls `markEnding` for the idle case.
- Locks: nothing is added, nested or reordered. `markNext` takes only `Owner.mutex`, the existing order stays `admission_mutex`, then `Owner.mutex`, then the registry lock, and `startNextPendingLocked` has released the registry lock before `markNext` runs. #2075's settling contract is untouched. The new state lives in `managed_owner.zig`.
- `publish_test_controls.zig` holds the slot in the gap for tests, as the start, end and close controls do for theirs: an inline hook for unit tests, and `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_PUBLISH_HELD` and `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_PUBLISH_RELEASE` for E2E. Both variables are registered in `scripts/cli_shape_registry.json`. The libfx artifacts leave the seam out; other builds read one environment variable per work end.
- `StopMessage.tla`: the gap is two phases (`gap_idle`, `gap_next`) that a work's own end and a stopped work's end can enter, and `Publish` leaves. A new rule, `GapStopHonest`, says a stop or close that answers it ended a turn, or closed the subagent, leaves it ending, closing or gone. The planted `gap_blind` bug, where a stop or close in the gap answers but acts on nothing, must break it. Calls that send a message wait for the gap to pass, as one to a starting turn does. `check.sh`, the design configs and the README list the rule and the mutation. No trace line changes, so the trace spec and the `stop-message` driver stay as they are.

## Evidence

Everything ran in a sandbox on the official Zig 0.17.1, checked against its published sha256. Heavy work did not run on the Mac. The numbers below were measured on the head, `0aa1669c2`; the first commit's loops and unit runs gave the same results.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Nine new unit tests on `main` with only the hold applied | all 9 fail, by assertion, and the whole run ends in 0.15 s (no hang) |
| The same tests with the change | 9 of 9 pass |
| Two new E2E tests (idle stop, idle close) on `main` with only the hold | 0 of 3 runs pass; each test fails by assertion in about 0.1 s |
| The same E2E tests with the change | 20 of 20 quiet and 15 of 15 under load |
| Six tests that close or stop right after `waitUntilQuiet` (the idle close test and five `stop ends a ...` tests), 1500 runs under load pinned to two CPUs, `main` | 32 failed runs: "stop ends a subagent's turn without a report and drops what waits for it" 23 times, "an idle subagent closes at once, and its name then starts a new one" 9 times |
| The same 1500 runs with the change | 0 failed runs |
| The idle close test alone, 1500 runs under load, with the change | 0 failed runs (`main` earlier: 8 of 1500) |
| The 9 new tests and the 7 existing tests that match their filters, 500 runs quiet and 500 under load | 0 failed runs in each |
| `tests/tla/subagent/check.sh`, no arguments, `fx-cloud run` | exit 0, 48 `ok` lines; `stop-message` and `stop-message-deep` pass with `GapStopHonest`; `stop-message-mutation-gap-blind` violates it, as required |
| Subagent drivers | `stop-message` 25 pass (65 with 40 random walks, seed 1717), `quiet-relay` 6, `main-mail` 9, `driver.ts --self-check` exit 0 |
| E2E `gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts -t subagent` | 40 pass, 0 fail |
| Every build surface `ci.yml` builds: `zig build fx-core-wasm -Dwasm-surface=core -Doptimize=ReleaseSmall`, `zig build fx-term-wasm -Dwasm-surface=term -Doptimize=ReleaseSmall`, and `libfx-napi -Dnapi-surface=core -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe` for linux-x64, linux-arm64, darwin-x64 and darwin-arm64 | all 6 exit 0. `fx-term-wasm` failed on the first commit with `atomic.zig:25: expected 32-bit integer type or smaller` through `markNext`; it exits 0 now |
| libfx SDK suites on the head | `test:node-napi` and 5 native suites exit 0; 4 Wasm suites exit 0 |
| Full unfiltered `zig build test --summary all` | with the change: 11896 of 11935 passed (27 skipped, 12 failed), main target 11627 passed, 22 skipped, 4 failed. `main`: 11887 of 11926, main target 11618 passed. The 9 extra tests are the new ones. The names of the failing tests are identical on both sides (sandbox permission and file-mode tests that run as root) |
| `python3 -m scripts.check_cli_shape` | exit 1 with the two new variables named before the registry change, exit 0 after |
| `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_macos_signing ... scripts.tests.test_check_cli_shape` (the line from `ci.yml`) | 107 tests OK |
| `python3 -m unittest discover -s .fx/skills/zig/scripts` | 67 tests OK (sandbox, Zig 0.17.1) |
| `scripts/check-public-surface.sh` | exit 0 |

The base I measured on is `54a36f011`. `origin/main` has since moved; the one change it made under these paths is `src/core/subagent/authority.zig`, and `git merge-tree` finds no conflict.

Tests that call `waitUntilQuiet` and then stop or close:

- Now exact: the idle close test, "stop ends a subagent's turn without a report and drops what waits for it" (its second stop), "the parent's stop ends a turn the user started on the child's screen" and "the parent's stop ends a question that waits in a turn the user typed on a hosted subagent's screen".
- Need nothing: the tests that stop or close while the work is running or blocked on the user, the trace and closing tests, and the user-close status test, whose assertions do not read the stopped answer.

## Not covered

- A stop or close between the recorded end and the end hook's admission step, which is a few instructions earlier than the gap this fixes and is not held by the seam. If the ended turn left unread messages, a stop there answers "not working" but those messages still start the next turn, and a close there drops them with no log line and no count. Both were already so.
- The waiting-message rows are proven by the unit fixture, whose run takes the cancel flag as the real one does, and not end to end with a real model request. The E2E tests cover the idle stop and close.
- `GapStopHonest` compares a stop's answer with the phase right after it. It would not catch a defect that takes a stop and undoes it later.
- A user stop on the child's screen that arrives after `markNext` now stays on the next work, where the slot cleared it after the hook before. The app only reaches `noteUserStop` for a turn in flight, so this is probably not reachable.
- The hosted child's own worker is not exercised for the user-close row; the hosted unit tests cover the parent's stop and close.
