title: Move /help, /settings, /resume, /effort, and /agents onto the shared menu style
body:
`/help`, `/settings`, `/resume`, `/effort`, and `/agents` now follow the shared menu style from #1972 and #2028.

`/help` and `/effort` draw through `menu_frame`. `/settings`, `/resume`, and `/agents` keep their own layouts, with the settings' option strips and model choices, the session pages, and the agent tree, but use the frame's title and message rows. In all five menus:

- The title has no count and shows only the active tab, as `< All >`. `/effort` names its model after the title, as `effort · <model>`.
- The list holds five rows and a `↓ N more` row, and keeps its height while a filter narrows it.
- Only the selected row is bright. `/settings` keeps every option on its row with the value in use bright. `/agents` no longer brightens a waiting state.
- Columns sit six cells apart, two on a narrow terminal.
- Empty and no-match states are gray messages that end with a period, and the hint row names only keys that act, so `/resume` with no sessions shows `tab scope     esc close`.
- `/agents` closes on Esc with `esc close` and keeps `↑↓ preview`. Its Delete key reads `delete remove`, and the second-press warning reads `press delete again to remove this subagent`, so `close` names only closing the menu.

A paged `/resume` shows `↓ N more` for the loaded sessions below the window, and `↓ load more` once the window reaches the last of them. `/resume` and `/agents` move their window by the rows they show, as the slash menu does.

On a terminal too short for the title, every menu gives its rows to the list, so `/effort` shows a level and the `↓ N more` row rather than its title and a level.

The `/settings` labels, such as `Status line context`, and the tab names keep their capitals. They move to lowercase with the tool labels in a later change.

## Tests

- `zig build test` passes.
- These e2e files pass locally: `tui-effort-menu`, `tui-host-instances`, `tui-host-switch`, `tui-slash-menu`, `tui-startup`, `tui-input-navigation`, `prompt-history`, `sessions`, `tui-resume`, `tui-resume-brutal`, `tui-render-stress`, `tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle`, `tui-slash-commands`, and `tui-resize`. In `tui-resize`, the long assistant stream test fails locally with or without this change.
- The e2e tests read the new titles and count rows with `catalogMenuItemCount`. They find the help catalog by its `commands   <` title, since the slash menu's title is also `commands`. `tui-resume-brutal` finds the next page by the selection, since the picker no longer shows a total.
- Checked by hand in tmux with the built binary: all five menus, an empty `/resume`, and a `/help` search with no match.

Stacked on #2028.

title: Show a failed command's reason by its message alone
body:
## Summary

- A failed command's row ends with one line of its output that says why. That line often starts with words that say who spoke and where, such as `ls: missing-file:` or `src/main.ts:14:15 - error TS2554:`, so the row was long and the message came last or was cut.
- The reason is now the message alone, at most 40 columns:
  - the text after an `error` or `fatal` label and its code, such as `error: `, `error[E0308]: ` or `error TS2554: `, where the label starts the line or follows `: ` or ` - `, so `connection error: timeout` inside a message stays;
  - then without each leading word that has no space and ends in `: `, such as `ls: `, `missing-file: ` or `ValueError: `, while the text after it has a space, so `undefined: foo` and `KeyError: 'key'` stay whole;
  - a line with no such words, such as ` FAIL  quits on click`, is unchanged.
- Ctrl+O still shows the whole output. Other tools' reasons are unchanged.

Before:

```
└ Exited 2 sh build.sh · src/main.ts:14:15 - error TS2554: Expected 1 arguments, but got 3.
● Exited 1 printf, ls · ls: missing-file: No such file or directory
● Exited 128 git status · fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
```

After:

```
└ Exited 2 sh build.sh · Expected 1 arguments, but got 3.
● Exited 1 printf, ls · No such file or directory
● Exited 128 git status · not a git repository (or any of the par…
```

## Tests

- A unit test covers the message rules on real output shapes (ls, zig, TypeScript, go, cargo, Python, git, test runners, a CJK line) and the 40-column cut on a row.
- Three story tests in `tests/e2e/tui-tool-story.test.ts` now expect the message alone: the failing build, the hostile output at a narrow width, and the command that printed code before `ls` failed. All three fail on main and pass here.

title: Keep a streaming subagent call in the row it will join
body:
## Summary

- While a `subagent` call's arguments stream, its status is a bare verb such as `Managing`, and its row is not known yet. It showed on a row of its own, and when its action or agent arrived, that row went away and the call joined a row above it.
- A running read, search, edit, or command already waits in the row it will most likely join. A subagent call whose status is a bare verb now does the same: it waits in the latest subagent row, so the group only grows.
- A second message to an agent that already has a row showed the same way while its message streamed: its status already read `Managing reviewer`, but its arguments did not parse yet. A running subagent call whose status is one verb and one name now takes that name as its agent, as a running MCP call takes its tool from `Running MCP <tool>`. So it joins that agent's row at once, and a first message to a new agent shows on a new row at the end.
- A retry after a failed message to an agent joins the failed message's row, so while its arguments stream it waits there too, not on a new row at the end.
- A running subagent whose status says more, such as `Subagent working · inspect auth`, keeps its own row.

Before, while the second call streams:

```
● Used subagents
├ Checked subagents
└ Managing
```

then, when it arrives:

```
● Checked subagents
```

After, the group shows `● Checked subagents` the whole time.

## Tests

- A unit test covers a call with no action after a status row, one after a message row with a read between them, a second message to the same agent and to a new agent, with and without partial arguments in the record, and a retry after a failed message.
- A new E2E test in `tests/e2e/tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` holds the second call's stream after `{"act` and checks every frame. It fails on main, where a frame shows the `Managing` row, and passes here.
- A new story test in `tests/e2e/tui-tool-story.test.ts` messages a subagent, reads a file, then holds a second message to the same agent after its agent name. It checks that the group's rows never go down and that one row names the agent. It fails on main and passes here. The story fixture gains an optional `response` for a step that needs its own reply.

title: Keep the end of long command output
body:
A running command kept only the first `max_output_bytes` of its undelivered output, 64 KiB by default, and dropped every later byte. The shell result's start-and-end view was then built from those first 64 KiB, so its end was the 64 KiB mark and not the real end. When a build or test run printed more than that, the last lines, usually the error, were missing from the model's first view and from the command's row. The full output was still behind `full_output_handle`, so the model had to read it again to find the failure.

Now the buffer keeps the first half of the limit as a head and the newest bytes as a rolling tail, with a `[... N bytes truncated ...]` line between them, as the command runner's own preview does. Both cuts land on UTF-8 boundaries, and `output_truncated` stays true while bytes are missing.

Delivery ranges now count bytes as the command printed them, dropped bytes included. An observation of a running command that ends in the head, in the dropped middle, or in the tail leaves exactly the later output for the next one, with no repeats. Terminal sessions keep their cursor as before; only the buffer of their undelivered output changes in the same way.

## Example

A script prints 1,000 lines of about 99 bytes each, then `FINAL_STEP_FAILED_MARKER`, and exits 1.

Before, the result ends at the 64 KiB cut, and the row shows a line from the middle of the output:

```text
● Exited 1 ./long-build.sh · step 0661 compiled module xxxx…
```

After, the result ends with the real last line, and the row shows it:

```text
● Exited 1 ./long-build.sh · FINAL_STEP_FAILED_MARKER
```

## Tests

- Unit tests in `src/core/execution/managed_execution.zig`: output under the limit is unchanged; output over the limit keeps the exact head and the newest tail for every chunk size; both cuts keep whole UTF-8 sequences; deliveries that end in the head, the gap, or the tail keep exactly the later output; a seeded random mix of output, delivery, and cancel checks that no byte repeats or goes missing; and a terminal session keeps its head and tail through restore, refresh, and delivery.
- `tests/e2e/tui-command-permissions.test.ts`, "TUI and the model see the last line of command output past the output limit": fails on main, where the result ends at `step 0661`, and passes with this change.
- `tests/evals/long-command-output.test.ts`, which calls a real model and runs only on request: a build prints about 100 KB and fails on its last line. The model must run it once, quote that line, and make no `read_tool_result` call, so the eval passes only when the first shell result holds the end of the output. On main the model reads the stored output again, and the eval fails.

title: Let fx acp keep a client's turns after it disconnects
body:
Stacked on #2086.

When the client of `fx acp` closes its input, fx cancels every running turn and saves it as interrupted. That is right for an editor that starts `fx acp` as its child, but fx's own apps want quitting the app to stop no chat.

## What changes

- New capability `sh.fx/keepTurnOnDisconnect`. A client that lists it in `clientCapabilities._meta` keeps its running turns after its input ends: they finish and are saved, its queued prompts still run, and fx exits once nothing runs or waits. Other clients keep today's behavior.
- Once the input ends, fx never waits for the client. A pending request ends with a no-client result and later ones are refused: a permission request is denied, and a host tool or an MCP server's question gets an error result, so the turn goes on.
- This also fixes a hang: a queued prompt that asked for permission after stdin closed waited forever, and fx never exited.
- Writes continue after the input ends, so a client that closed only its input still reads updates. After a write fails with a broken pipe, notifications are dropped and requests fail instead of failing the turn.
- A host tool request whose write failed is no longer left registered against the session's request limit.
- A session whose host keeps its journal (`sh.fx/journal`) can't save without that host, so its turn stops at its next journal flush.

## Tests

- `tests/e2e/acp.test.ts`, four new tests, all of which fail on #2086:
  - a client that lists sh.fx/keepTurnOnDisconnect keeps its running turn after it disconnects
  - a kept turn denies a permission its gone client can't answer
  - a kept turn's queued prompt still runs after its client disconnects
  - fx exits when a queued prompt asks a gone client for permission
- Unit tests for the writer after a closed client, a pending request when the input ends, the denied permission, and the capability's parsing.
- `tests/tla/acp/AcpDisconnect.tla` models kept and plain clients. Its two configs for today's behavior violate `KeptTurnsComplete` and `NeverWaitsForGoneClient`, and `drivers/acp/disconnect/check-spec.ts` catches four planted bugs.
- `tests/tla/drivers/acp/disconnect/driver.ts` runs five plans against the real `fx acp` and reads how each turn ended from the responses fx writes after stdin closes. The rules model accepts all five here and rejects four on #2086; the model of today's behavior does the reverse. `check.sh --ci` runs it.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#340.

fx-core.wasm grows by 3,647 bytes; the budget is raised to 2,488,000.

title: Hold the persistent resume test's child until its parent saved the turn
body:
## Summary

"saved ask resume continues one chat-created persistent child" failed once in CI with `Expected: 8, Received: 7` at its request count. The cause is a race in the test on behavior that is designed: a subagent's report that arrives while the parent's turn still runs joins that turn (`postMail` in `src/core/agent/worker_runtime.zig`). The parent's request after the receipt then carries the report, and a run makes three requests instead of four. The fake gateway answered the child at once, so a slow runner could let the report win that race. Test only; no product code changes.

## Change

- The fake child answers only once the parent's log holds a new `turn_committed` line (`waitForRootTurnCommitted` in `tests/e2e/saved-sessions.ts`), so the report always starts the parent's next turn. #1976 did the same for four other fakes.
- The resumed run's child waits for a turn past the ones the first run committed (`committedBefore`, read from the log between the runs).
- A wait that fails is kept and answered with a 500 response, so fx sees a failed request and `runFx` ends it normally; the test throws the kept error after the run. Thrown out of the gateway's handler, which has no error handling, the error would fail the test at once and leave fx running (the second commit).

## Evidence

CI history, read with `gh run view --log-failed` and a `timeout` on each call, over every failed `ci.yml` run (600) and `macos.yml` run (171) from 2026-09-02 to 2026-11-17:

- `Expected: 8` with `Received: 7` for this test appears once: `ci.yml` run 43513441299 on 2026-11-13, Linux E2E shard 4/4, at the first count check. The file's retry passed this test, so the retry hid it; the job failed for another test that failed on both attempts. In the same minute two other tests of that shard failed on the first attempt and one test took 32 s, so the runner was stalled.
- Three other failed runs list this test for other causes: a macOS path assertion in an older version of the test (2026-10-24) and two runs of a branch that was removing v1 sessions (2026-10-17). They are not this failure.
- Not on macOS in any failed run, as far as these logs show.
- Hidden by a retry: in the E2E jobs of the last 220 commits (about three days, 1,537 jobs), `gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` passed only on retry twice, and neither time for this test. Older passing runs were not searched.

Reproduction, Zig 0.17.1 in a sandbox, six busy loops pinned to the test's two CPUs:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Test on `main`, 300 runs under load | 300 of 300 pass (the race needs a stall, as in CI) |
| Test on `main` with a one second shell call after the subagent call in the parent's first step of both runs, so the report surely lands in that turn (kept out of this PR) | 10 of 10 fail on the base I started from and 5 of 5 on the latest `main`, with `Expected: 8, Received: 6`; the trace shows `mail=report delivery=joined` in both runs |
| Same hold with this change (both commits) | 20 of 20 quiet and 20 of 20 under load pass, all with 8 requests and `delivery=waits` in both runs |
| This change alone (both commits) | 100 of 100 quiet and 300 of 300 under load pass; the subagent tests of the file (`-t subagent`) pass: 50 pass and 2 skip |
| The hold made impossible in a sandbox copy (`committedBefore = 1000000`), first commit | the test fails after 10 s with "no root session committed more than 1000000 turns", and the first run's `fx ask` stays alive: still running 100 s later |
| The same impossible hold, second commit | the test fails with the same error after 15 s, the bound of `runFx`, and no `fx ask` process is left, at once or 10, 30 and 60 s later |

Both orders leave a consistent saved session. In the joined order each run commits one turn, with `child_finished` inside it and 2 turns saved in all; in the waiting order the receipt's turn is committed first and the report starts a second one, 4 turns in all. Neither order has a superseded line, and both final outputs name the child's result. #2059's commit gate is opt-in for the terminal app, so `fx ask` does not have it; here it does not matter, because `postMail` joins an open turn or waits for the next one, which `tests/tla/subagent/MainMail.tla` models for `fx ask`.

Standing checks. The full build and the build surfaces ran on the first commit; the second commit changes only the same test file, so they cannot differ. The script checks ran again on the second:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Full unfiltered `zig build test --summary all`, Zig 0.17.1 | 12123 of 12168 passed (32 skipped, 13 failed), identical to `main`, with the same failing test names (sandbox permission and file-mode tests that run as root) |
| `fx-core-wasm`, `fx-term-wasm`, and `libfx-napi` for linux-x64, linux-arm64, darwin-x64 and darwin-arm64, as `ci.yml` builds them | all 6 exit 0 |
| `python3 -m scripts.check_cli_shape` | exit 0 (no new `FX_*` variable), on both commits |
| `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests...` line from `ci.yml` | 107 tests OK, on both commits |
| `python3 -m unittest discover -s .fx/skills/zig/scripts` | 67 tests OK (sandbox, Zig 0.17.1) |
| `scripts/check-public-surface.sh` | exit 0 |

The change touches no Zig file, so the Zig builds cannot differ from `main`'s. They ran because the rule asks for them. I ran no TLA checks, because nothing under `src/core/subagent/` or `src/core/session/` changed.

## Not covered

- The race itself needs a stalled runner, so the hold is what shows it; the plain test passed on `main` in 300 runs.
- Other tests have the same shape: a fake child that answers at once, with an exact request count or a branch that expects the report to start the parent's next turn. I left them alone and did not search CI history for them: `gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` at lines 10168 (`toBe(6)`), 10456 (`toHaveLength(5)`), 10728 (`toBe(8)`, used by the tests at 10806 and 10808), 10810 (`toBe(withEffect ? 8 : 4)`), 10901 (`toBe(12)`) and 10273 (no count, but its report branch can answer the wrong request), and `ultrafast-fake-gateway.test.ts` at lines 876 and 913.
- The first three timeouts of the test (15 + 15 + 10 s) already add up to more than its 30 s limit; this change does not alter that.

title: Color the whole program name in highlighted shell commands
body:
Command rows such as `Ran agent-browser --version` highlight only `agent` and leave `-browser` dim. The shell highlighter ends every word at the first `-` or `.`. That is right for argument words like `build-20260918`, but it splits program names such as `agent-browser`, `docker-compose`, and `python3.12`.

A word in command position now keeps `-` and `.`, so the whole program name takes the command color. Argument words still stop at the first dash, so flags, dated paths, and names passed as arguments color as before.

## Before

![Before: the command rows highlight only "agent" in agent-browser and agent-desktop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/380f9433-3c05-45a4-b2fa-01c3dc878f12)

## After

![After: the command rows highlight agent-browser and agent-desktop in full](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0442135-52fb-4552-ac43-54da4059cb39)

## Verification

- Added `command words keep dashes and dots in program names` to `src/core/agent/presentation/code_highlight.zig`.
- `zig fmt --check src/` passes.
- `zig build test` passes 11,930 tests. The one failure, `streamed presentation preserves ANSI OSC 8 code fence and table spans`, compiles a nested test with the `zig` on `PATH`, which is 0.16 on this machine. Running that nested command with Zig 0.17.1 passes. Its fixture renders a `zig` fence, which this change doesn't touch.
- Built `./zig-out/bin/fx` with `-Doptimize=ReleaseFast` and ran it on macOS 27.2 in a session that runs `agent-browser --version` and `agent-desktop --version`. The before screenshot is the released 0.0.17 in the same session.

title: Wait for the saved interrupted turn in cancel tests
body:
Two tests in `tests/e2e/tui-resume.test.ts` cancel a running command, wait for the `event=interrupt_persisted` trace line, and then read the saved session log for the command's replay:

- "cancelled cap-crossing command keeps grouped rows stable and Ctrl-O opens its artifact" waits at line 2388 and reads `commandReplays` at line 2407 (line 2389 before this change).
- "cancelled below-cap command exposes its TERM tail only through Ctrl-O" waits at line 2604 and reads at line 2615 (line 2596 before this change).

That trace line does not mean the turn is on disk. The agent worker writes it in `traceInterruptedPersistence` (`src/core/agent/runtime/interruption.zig`, lines 178 and 212), before `finalization.finish` at lines 185 and 219. `finish` hands the turn to the app thread as a `finish_prompt` event (`src/core/agent/runtime/finalization.zig`, line 218), and the app thread saves it when it handles that event (`src/core/app/app_worker_runtime.zig`, line 1500, through `persistFinishedPrompt` at line 492). In sandbox runs the save landed 11 to 29 ms after the trace line. A read in that gap found no replay, so the `replays` length check failed in some runs on `main`: 8 of 42 in one sandbox, and 0 of 54 in another, where a branch with more work before the save lost it more often.

The replay itself is never late: it is written in the same batch as the interrupted turn, with the `tool_call` item that names its blob, the `interruption` item that holds `command_replay_ref`, and the `turn_interrupted` record last.

Each test now waits, with the test's own timeout and a message that names the session, until the log holds that `turn_interrupted` record before it reads the replay. Every existing assertion stays. Product code is unchanged.

The other tests in the file that wait for `event=interrupt_persisted` read the saved log only after a follow-up turn finishes or after `/quit` ends the session, so they do not race.

## Tests

- Both tests, 42 runs each, one Bun process per run: 42 of 42 pass on a build of this branch and 42 of 42 pass with this test file on a build of #2095.
- The whole `tui-resume.test.ts` file once on each build: 93 pass, 0 fail.

title: Accept schema 12 tool results when loading a saved session
body:
**Summary**
---
- Sessions saved with a runtime context write tool results with execution schema 12, but the reader accepted only 10 and 11. A saved session that had run a tool could not be loaded again, and in the browser terminal on fx.sh, resuming such a session dropped the conversation.
- The reader now accepts schema 12. A regression test writes a schema 12 tool result and reads it back.

title: Ship five named themes with light and dark variants, and add /theme
body:
**Summary**
---
- Five named themes ship inside the binary: `phosphor`, `breadbin`, `dotmatrix`, `beige`, and `geist`. They work without theme files, including in the WebAssembly terminal. Each has a dark and a light file, and fx loads the one that matches the terminal's mode, again when the mode changes while fx runs. A file in `~/.fx/themes` with the same name still replaces a named theme.
- `/theme` lists the themes with a short description, applies the chosen one at once, and saves the `theme` setting. It warns when `FX_THEME` will override that setting at startup.
- New theme slots: `accent`, `heading`, `quote`, `list_marker`, `rule`, `type`, `constant`, `punctuation`, `diff_added_word`, `diff_removed_word`, and `agent_1` to `agent_6`. fx's own themes keep their exact output. The unused `approval_button_active` slot is gone.
- Diffs highlight the changed part of a line. Switching themes recolors what is already on screen, and tool summaries use the theme's colors instead of fixed grays.
- `scripts/themes/audit.py` checks the named themes, and `scripts/tests/test_themes.py` fails when a theme drops below a contrast floor or `geist` uses a color outside the Geist palette.

**Working on the colors**
---
The JSON files in `src/core/shared/themes/` are the source of truth, one `<name>-dark.json` and one `<name>-light.json` per theme. To change a color:

1. Edit the JSON file.
2. Run `python3 scripts/themes/audit.py` (or `audit.py <name>`). It measures every color on four common terminal backgrounds per mode, flags pairs that collapse under deuteranopia, and checks that `geist` uses only Geist tokens. `audit.py --fit '#RRGGBB' read dark` suggests the nearest color, same hue, that meets a role's target.
3. Run `zig build`, then `./zig-out/bin/fx` and `/theme <name>`.

The header of `audit.py` describes the rules the themes follow: gray structure with color only where it means something, the selected row in the theme's accent, the usual code green and red for diffs in every theme, and Geist tokens only in `geist`. It also documents the exceptions, such as `geist` on dark keeping Geist's own 900 text step below the contrast target.

**For review**
---
- The token that pushed this branch can't edit workflows, so CI does not run the new test yet. Please add `scripts.tests.test_themes` to the `Test CI and release scripts` step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
- `tui-resize.test.ts` "a long assistant stream keeps every row and the collapsed group in order" fails locally on this branch and on its base, #2028, without these changes.

**Docs**
---
vercel-labs/fx-web#343 updates the themes docs page and adds a `/themes` page with a live terminal.

Stacked on #2028.

title: Count the messages a stop or close drops between two works of a subagent
body:
## Summary

#2087 made a stop or close that lands right after a subagent's work ended act on the right work. Two things about the messages main sent are left, and this change fixes them for the parent's stop and close:

- Nobody is told what was dropped. A stop or close of the work the host has just chosen, or of the messages the ended turn never took, drops those messages, and the answer says nothing of them (`Stopped reviewer: its turn ended.`). Main thinks its message ran or still waits. `StopMessage.tla` calls this `NoSilentLoss`.
- A stop or close that lands after the slot recorded a work's end and before the host's end hook runs finds `Slot.ended` set and does nothing, as #2087 intends for the work that ended. But the hook then queues the messages the ended turn never took as the next work, so a stopped subagent runs them. Tests of that window on `main` show the kept message run as a second turn after the stop (the work ran twice, expected once).

This change counts what the parent's stop or close drops in both windows and tells the parent in the answer, except between the attach of a hosted work's worker and the begin of its turn, where a stop or close still counts nothing, as on `main` (see "Not in this change", the stop or close before a hosted turn begins). The hook does not queue what a stop or close counted. The user's close and stop are as on `main`: they count what waits at the host, and the user's stop what the app's own queue dropped, and nothing more (see "Not in this change", the counts for the user's close and stop).

`Slot.ended` and `Owner.markNext` stay. The answers #2087 gave for a stop or close with no message waiting are unchanged word for word. Every answer that changes is an existing builder branch (`stopChild`, `closeNamed`); no sentence is new. All are `ok: true` results, not refusals, so #1932's refusal rule and the ACP result shape do not apply to them.

| Window, caller | `main` `51f69c14c` (read from the builders with a count of 0, and from #2087's own test for the first row) | This change (asserted by the tests) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Next work chosen, parent `stop`, one message waiting | `Stopped reviewer: its turn ended.` | `Stopped reviewer: its turn ended, and the message waiting for it was dropped.` |
| The same with two messages (joined as one work) | `Stopped reviewer: its turn ended.` | `Stopped reviewer: its turn ended, and the 2 messages waiting for it were dropped.` |
| Next work chosen, parent `close` | `Closed reviewer, ending its turn. A later message to reviewer starts a new one.` | `Closed reviewer, ending its turn. The message waiting for it was dropped. A later message to reviewer starts a new one.` |
| After the end is recorded, before the hook, parent `stop`, a message the turn never took | `reviewer was not working.` and the hook runs the message | `reviewer was not working; the message waiting for it was dropped.` and nothing runs |
| The same window, parent `close` | `Closed reviewer. A later message to reviewer starts a new one.` | `Closed reviewer. The message waiting for it was dropped. A later message to reviewer starts a new one.` |

Only the count changes in these rows. `reviewer was not working.`, `Closed reviewer. A later message to reviewer starts a new one.`, `Stopped reviewer: its turn ended.` for a work with no message waiting, and the user's `closed it before it finished` report stay as #2087 has them. His 9 unit tests and 2 end-to-end tests pass with one expectation changed, in `expectStopStopsNextWork` (used by `a stop right after a subagent's work ended stops the turn its waiting message starts` and its hosted twin). It asserted `Stopped reviewer: its turn ended.` for a stop of an installed work with one message waiting. It now asserts the whole sentence, `Stopped reviewer: its turn ended, and the message waiting for it was dropped.`, because that answer now names the message. His close expectation (`expectCloseEndsNextWork`) is unchanged and still passes: it checks `Closed reviewer, ending its turn.`, the first sentence of the longer answer in the table, and `the parent's close that lands as the next work is installed drops it, and it never begins` pins its first two sentences, `Closed reviewer, ending its turn. The message waiting for it was dropped.`

A table test puts one subagent in each of 26 windows of its slot, on the plain path and on the hosted path the app's children use, has each stop and close act there alone and two in a row, and checks, in each cell, that the number of accounts main reads equals the number of messages whose turn never began: each count (a stop's or close's answer, a report's `dropped=N`, a user note still held) plus each message whose own work's report says it failed or was cancelled, with no count beside the report of a work that failed (656 cells; see Testing). The answers do not name the messages they count, so this is a sum per cell; `StopMessage.tla` checks each message. The user's close and stop rows of that table describe `Runtime.closeChild` and `Runtime.userStopped` and are driven by tests, not by a key press.

Rules (`RULES.md`): R3.8, never drop queued work silently: a parent's stop or close no longer drops queued messages without a word (the answer counts them, and each kept message the hook does not queue is traced); R7.1: the tests fail before the change, as Testing shows; R7.2: `StopMessage.tla` is updated, and a planted bug breaks each of its new rules (`CountedOnce`, that main is told of each message once, among them); R7.4: no test is skipped, deleted or loosened, see Testing; R6.3 and R8.2: the parent's stop and close only, the user's counts are left out (see "Not in this change").

## How

- `managed_owner.zig` (+87 −4). Three fields on `Slot`: `unstarted` (how many of main's messages the chosen work carries, until a worker attaches), `leftovers_counted` (how many kept messages the parent's stop or close counted, or the host holds), `kept_dropped` (the parent's stop or close counted the kept messages, so the hook must not queue them). `markNext(child_id, messages)` and `start(child_id, unstarted)` take the count. `takeDropped` counts and clears what the slot holds, the chosen work and the kept messages, for the parent's stop and close, which set the slot's cancel, so the work starts stopped; `handOverLeftovers` is the hook's question, answered false once a stop counted the kept messages. `slotMain` zeroes `unstarted` where it records a work's end, beside `Slot.ended` and under the owner's lock: every end is recorded there, whichever way `runOne` returned, so a work that ends before its worker attaches (a failed bind to its agent, `Owner.cancel`) takes its count with it, its report having told main it failed or was cancelled, and a stop or close in the gap counts none of its messages again; `markNext` sets the count again for the next work. `detachWorker` marks the unread messages of a turn the parent stopped as counted, and `freeLeftovers` and the worker's attach reset the fields. `Owner.stop` and `closeByUser` still return null (`closeByUser` false) while `Slot.ended` is set (his check stays); `closeByUser`, `noteUserStop` and `userStopped` are as `main` has them.
- `tool_host.zig` (production +40 −19). `startNextPendingLocked` and `absorbPendingLocked` return how many messages the chosen work carries (1 plus the ones joined), and `nextOrIdleLocked` and the start path pass it to `markNext` and `start`. `stopChild` and, for the parent, `closeChild` add `takeDropped`, which counts the work the host chose, whose cancel their `Owner.stop` has just set, and the messages the slot kept from the ended turn, which it marks dropped so that the hook does not queue them. `queueLeftoversLocked` asks `handOverLeftovers`, and logs `dropped ... reason=stopped` for each kept message it does not queue.
- Locks: nothing is added or reordered. `takeDropped` and `handOverLeftovers` take `Owner.mutex` only, from code that holds `admission_mutex` (the order `admission_mutex`, then `Owner.mutex`, #2087 documents).
- `end_test_controls.zig` (+23): one hook, `test_hold_run`, set only by inline tests. It exists only when `builtin.is_test`, and is compiled out of every other build and of libfx. It is called twice per work in `slotMain`: after the turn ended and before the end is recorded, and after the end is recorded and before the host's hook runs. No environment variable, registry row or file control is added. The windows that need #2087's hold, the next work chosen, use `PublishHold` as it is.
- `StopMessage.tla`: a work's messages are `read` when its turn begins, not when the host chooses it. ## Not in this change

- Counts for the user's close and stop. `main` keeps no count of the messages a user's close or stop drops from a running turn's queue, the ones the slot kept, or the work the host chose, and this change adds none. A count there must not sit beside the report of a work that failed (the user's close after a failed bind, before the end is recorded) and must not repeat a parent's stop's (the user's close, then the parent's stop of the same running turn); the table pins both. The 37 cells of the table where a user's close or stop drops a message that no count names, alone or before another action that does not count it (a second close by the user or the parent), are marked `(as on main: R2)` in their names, and each is asserted to break R2; Testing lists them. A `/close` of the subagent tree (`closeTree`) and a quit drop such messages with no count too, as on `main`; the table does not run them. A parent's stop before or after either one counts what it drops. All of these break `RULES.md` R3.8 (never drop queued work silently) as `main` does, and the change that adds the counts fixes that and takes them as its failing list.
- A user's stop on a subagent's screen in the moment after the parent's close of its running turn, before the turn has ended, counts a message the close already counted: main reads the close's `The message waiting for it was dropped.` and then `The user stopped it, and 1 of your messages waiting for it were dropped.` The same happens on `main`; neither count is this change's. A fix belongs with the user's counts.
- The user's stop of a subagent whose next work is installed and has no worker yet. `Runtime.userStopped` there neither ends that work nor counts its messages, as on `main`. No key press reaches it today: the app calls it only while the child's run is in flight or the user's own turn runs (`noteUserStop` in `src/core/app/app_agents_runtime.zig`), and both have ended by then. Whether such a stop should end the next work is a product choice, so it is left as #2087 has it.
- If the subagent registry cannot be loaded or saved when a waiting or kept message would start the next work, the message is dropped with a trace line only and main is not told (`dropStart` in `startNextPendingLocked`). This is the same on `main` and needs its own change.
- Four walks of a failed turn (a stop or close after a turn that failed leaving a message, and the message after it) are not added. They need a control that holds a failed turn's slot, which this change does not add; the table's `recorded_kept_failed_first` and `gap_next_failed_first` cells hold one in the unit tests (`fail_first`).
- In the interactive app, a subagent's run is handed to the main loop before its cancel is checked (`postAndWait` in `src/core/app/app_agents_runtime.zig`). If the main loop takes the run in that moment, or a stop lands after the run is taken and before the child's worker takes its prompt, the turn begins and is cancelled within about 50 ms (`waitForCompletion`), so one model request can go out. In the first case the stop has already counted the work's messages as dropped, as this change counts them. The table's hosted cells mirror the run's check in the fixture's hosted `run` (`postAndWait`, `src/core/app/app_agents_runtime.zig:715`), so they do not reach this race. This is the same on `main` and needs its own change. Read, not run, on this head.
- A parent's stop or close between the attach of a hosted work's worker and the begin of its turn counts nothing. `Slot.unstarted` is zeroed where the worker attaches, and a hosted turn whose cancel is set before the main loop takes it is withdrawn (`postAndWait`, `src/core/app/app_agents_runtime.zig:715`), so the work's messages never run and the answer says only `Stopped reviewer: its turn ended.` (a close: `Closed reviewer, ending its turn. A later message to reviewer starts a new one.`). The table holds the window twice. In `attached_not_begun` the work is the first of a `message` call: main's answer began `Sent to reviewer, which works on it now.`, and main then stops that work, so it knows which work it stopped. In `next_attached_not_begun` the host chose the work from a waiting message, and main's answer to it began `reviewer is busy, so the message waits and starts its next turn.`: a stop there tells main nothing about that message, and that is the silent loss. On the hosted path the 22 cells of those two windows in which a parent's stop or close acts are asserted silent and marked `(as on main: R2)`; they hold on `main` `51f69c14c`'s production too: the table run there (this head's tests on `main`'s production) fails 246 of its 656 cells, every one silent, and none of the marked cells is among them, so they are silent on `main` as well (a marked cell that is not silent fails as `wrongly_marked`). This change cannot fix it, because the host does not learn when a hosted turn begins, and `RULES.md` R8.2 keeps it out. The case of a work that carries several joined messages follows from the code (the count is zeroed at the attach whatever it holds) and is not run: the table has no joined-messages variant of these windows. The `next_attached_not_begun` cells are the failing-first cells for the change that fixes it.
- `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_PUBLISH_HELD` and `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_PUBLISH_RELEASE` (#2087) with a relative path: run on #1920's head `a3a9aa588`, with both set to relative paths fx panicked in an `assert` at the hold, 3 of 3 runs of the relative-path end-to-end test with those two added; a later review narrowed it to the RELEASE path (a relative marker path only writes a file), which I did not run. This change does not touch `publish_test_controls.zig`, and its walks set absolute paths.

title: Check the trace cut laws against cuts that leave out a split secret
body:
## Summary

- The `trace_cuts` fuzz target and the seeded cut test check the cut that leaves out a split secret. The UTF-8 cut loses at most three bytes on each side, and the secret-safe cut keeps no more than it. What a short head leaves out holds no whitespace. The kept tail starts where `text_utils.secretSafeSuffixStart` moves the UTF-8 start, and in a value with no secret that `maskSecrets` finds, no URL, and no `Bearer ` token, what the tail loses holds no whitespace. Where the value holds a secret, the tail may step past it whole; the `text_utils` tests pin those cases.
- The old laws said the kept head and tail lose at most three bytes. That was false after the cut began to leave out a split run of secret bytes, so the head check failed on a plain word cut in two.
- `split-letter-run-at-head-cut` is the input from the nightly fuzz run 44038897562. `split-letter-run-before-two-byte-text` is the input from the fuzz run on #1814 (run 44138426681). Both join the `trace_cuts` corpus, so `zig build test` replays them on every pull request.
- On `main`, replaying either input fails at `tool_call_metrics.zig:739`. On this branch, both pass.

Fixes #2088.

title: Keep a command's last character whole when its double quote never closes
body:
## Summary

- A shell command whose double quote never closes keeps its last character whole in its transcript row, such as the `é` in `echo "café`. Before, a color escape could land inside that character, and the row showed a broken character: `main` shows `Exited 1 echo "caf��`, and this branch shows `Exited 1 echo "café · unmatched "`.
- A command whose double quote closes is highlighted as before.
- The input that failed the nightly fuzz run joins the `tool_story_rows` corpus, so `zig build test` replays it on every pull request.

Fixes #2089.

title: Keep a turn's recap count after the window drops its earlier rows
body:
## Summary

- A finished turn's recap, such as `Explored 10 files`, keeps its count after a compaction, whether the compaction ran between turns or inside the turn, and also after a resize. Before, the count could fall, for example to `Explored 2 files`.
- The transcript window keeps a turn's entries, back to its prompt, for as long as the turn's summary stays, and drops them together with the summary. A turn that one or more compactions split keeps its earlier parts until its summary leaves, when the cycle that holds the summary closes.
- A failed allocation right after a turn's summary is added no longer frees the summary line twice.

title: Make the deadline kill test able to see a missing kill of what a check started outside its group
body:
## Summary

"a check killed at the deadline takes with it what it started in a group of its own" could not see a missing kill of what a check started outside its group. With that kill removed from `killTree` in a sandbox copy, the test still passed in 98 of 100 quiet runs.

The cause is the kernel, not fx. When a stopped process sits in a group that its parent's death orphans, the kernel sends it SIGHUP and SIGCONT. The test's perl server moves to its own group and ignores SIGTERM, and fx's stop path stops it and then kills the check's group, which holds its parent. The server did not ignore SIGHUP, so the kernel's hangup ended it, which is fx's job. #2012 fixed the same blind spot in the test of the process forker.

## Change

The perl server in this test now ignores SIGHUP before it moves to its own group, and the comment says why. Test only; no product code changes.

## Evidence

Everything ran in sandboxes on Zig 0.17.1 with a `timeout` on each run, six busy loops pinned to the test's two CPUs for the load runs, and a check after every run that no perl, sleep or shell the tests start was left. "Outside kill removed" means the `signalOutsideProcessGroupChecked` call and its log line deleted from `killTree` in a sandbox copy.

The gap on unchanged `main`:

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Unchanged test, nothing planted, 100 quiet and 100 under load | 100 of 100 pass in each |
| Unchanged test, outside kill removed, 100 quiet | 98 of 100 pass |
| Same, 100 under load (and 30 in a second run) | 5 of 100 pass (and 2 of 30). My reading, not proven: under load the server's SIGSTOP has often not landed when the check dies, so the group holds no stopped process for the kernel to hang up |

The cause, still on unchanged `main`, with the outside kill removed and SIGHUP ignored in the test's server (sandbox copy): the test fails in 100 of 100 quiet runs and 100 of 100 runs under load.

With this change:

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Outside kill removed, 100 quiet and 100 under load | the test fails in 100 of 100 runs of each |
| Group-only kill (`killTree` returns after `killGroup`), 50 quiet and 50 under load | fails in 50 of 50 runs of each |
| Unchanged stop path, 300 quiet and 300 under load | 300 of 300 pass in each; slowest run 148 ms quiet and 282 ms under load; largest memory 11,568 KB |
| Processes after a run, failed or not | in every single-test run above none was left, and memory did not grow |
| Whole `doctor_probes` file, nothing planted | passes |
| Whole file, outside kill removed | 2 tests fail: this one and the forker test |
| Whole file, group-only kill | the same 2 tests fail |
| Whole file, no group kill (`killGroup` removed from `killTree`) | "a child still running at the deadline is killed with its group and its waiter joined" fails, and "an ending signal during the fan-out..." then hangs until the 60 s `timeout` ended it. This test does not catch that one. |
| Full unfiltered `zig build test --summary all` | 12223 of 12268 passed (32 skipped, 13 failed), identical to `main` at `5707c6ad6`, with the same 9 failing test names (the tests that fail on `main` in the sandbox, most of them read-only or permission tests that run as root) |
| `fx-core-wasm`, `fx-term-wasm`, and `libfx-napi` for linux-x64, linux-arm64, darwin-x64 and darwin-arm64, as `ci.yml` builds them | all 6 exit 0 |
| `python3 -m scripts.check_cli_shape`, the `ci.yml` unittest line, `scripts/check-public-surface.sh`, `zig fmt --check` | exit 0, 107 tests OK, exit 0, clean |

## Other tests that stop a process group

- The forker test (`stopping a check that keeps starting processes in groups of their own leaves none of them`) already ignores SIGHUP, since #2012. On unchanged `main` it is the only test that fails when the outside kill is removed, so the file as a whole saw that kill before this change; this test alone did not.
- Neither test shares a helper: each has its own perl script string, so nothing else here has this blind spot.
- "a child still running at the deadline is killed with its group and its waiter joined" and "an ending signal during the fan-out stops what started, starts nothing more, and is returned" use a shell and `sleep` in the check's own group, so no hangup can end them early. The first fails when the group kill is removed. The second then hangs instead of failing.
- "a waiter blocked by a process that left the group is cancelled after the grace and still reaps" does not test a kill: fx kills nothing there, and the escaped process is ended by the test.
- When the forker test fails, its perl processes stay for their 30 s sleep (I saw 18 to 26 after a run). With the group kill removed and the test binary restarted by the build runner, the forker kept starting processes: about 8,000 in the sandbox, 5 GB, before I ended it (I read this live from the sandbox's process list and `free`; it is not in a saved log). A bound on that test, such as a limit on processes, is worth its own change.
- The tests of `process_tree.zig` use fake signals or kill nothing, and `native_session.zig` has no test that starts a process in a group of its own, so neither has this blind spot.
- One candidate outside these files: the test "finishing a detached session leaves cleanup to its supervisor" in `command_runner.zig` starts a python process in a group of its own that does not ignore SIGHUP. I did not trace whether its cleanup stops that process before it kills the parent shell; if it does, it has the same blind spot, and `signal.signal(signal.SIGHUP, signal.SIG_IGN)` before `setpgid` would fix it. I left it out of this PR.

title: Skip the tests that need enforced file permissions where they are not enforced
body:
## Summary

A user that holds `CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE`, such as the one in the cloud sandbox, or root, reads and writes through a mode that removes permissions. Tests that remove permissions with `chmod` and expect fx to be refused then fail or run into their limit. This is the follow-up to #2022, which moved the probe `ignoresFileModes()` to `tests/e2e/file-modes.ts`.

Seven tests and the 27 tests of the fault grid need the kernel to enforce the mode. Each now uses `test.skipIf(ignoresFileModes())`, as #2022 did. No trigger changes, and no Zig file changes.

## Which tests remove permissions, and which need enforcement

I searched `tests/` on `main` for every `chmodSync` and every file created with a mode below 0o600: 30 permission-removing calls in 12 files. Each test ran alone with `bun test <file> -t <name>` and a `timeout`, once as the sandbox's user with every capability (`CapEff 000001ffffffffff`, "kept"), and once as the same user with every capability dropped (`setpriv`, `CapEff 0`, "dropped"), which enforces modes as CI's runner does.

| Test | Kept, before | Dropped, before | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gateway-stream-lifecycle`: OS filesystem access denial reaches the next gateway request | fails: the glob answers `no matches` instead of a denial | passes | skip |
| `sessions`: a read-only session folder fails cleanly and resumes once writable | fails: the resume exits 0 where 1 is expected | passes | skip |
| `sessions`: the app refuses a damaged session, a busy one and a read-only one | fails after 33 s ("timed out waiting for the app to exit") and leaves an `fx` app and its tmux session running | passes in 6 s | skip |
| `sessions`: ACP refuses a damaged or read-only session and leaves its log as it was | fails: the load succeeds, so the reply holds no error | passes | skip |
| `sessions`: the 3 new-session and 24 session fault grid tests | all 27 fail: the read-only row enters the session (`Expected: false Received: true`), 184 s | all 27 pass, 396 s | skip |
| `acp`: an attached folder whose rule file cannot be read is reported in the note | fails: `ACP_UNREADABLE_RULE` reaches the instructions | passes | skip; replaces an early return that covered only uid 0 |
| `session-recovery`: committed-history corruption (unreadable) | fails: exit 0 where 1 is expected | passes | skip for this case only; `malformed` and `oversized` still run |
| `tests/tla/drivers/session_manager/prompt-images`: an image the session cannot save stays inline | fails: the second image is saved, so one more image is noted | passes | skip |

Tests that remove permissions and are not changed:

- `mcp-auth` (3 tests), `cli` (`fx logout fails when the saved login cannot be deleted`) and `tui-auth-source-selection` (6 tests) pass in both modes. fx itself reads the mode bits there (`requireWritableInDir` in `src/core/auth/session_presence.zig` refuses a login file that is not exactly 0o600, or a folder without 0o200), so the trigger works for every user. With the `chmod` removed on a sandbox copy, all 10 fail in both modes.
- `sessions`: `fx sessions --live ...`, `plain doctor ...`, and `prompt-history`: `read-only prompt-history bootstrap ...` pass in both modes and also pass with the `chmod` removed, so the permission is not what they depend on.
- `oauth-keychain-migration`: `Vercel sign-in checks a read-only legacy file ...` runs only on macOS (`process.platform !== "darwin"` skips it), so I could not run it here. It uses the same mode check as the 10 tests above.
- `tui-startup` and the subagent failure test of `gateway-stream-lifecycle` already use the probe (#2022).
- `conversion/formats.test.ts` sets 0o400 back on a blob after a planted change and runs `chmod -R go-rwx` on a fixture, which tightens a mode and needs no enforcement.

## Checks

- With the capabilities kept, after the change: the 7 tests and the 27 grid tests skip, in 1 run and again in 5 of 5 repeats; the two tests #2022 guarded still skip.
- With them dropped, after the change: the same tests run and pass, as before: 5 of 5 repeats of each, and 27 of 27 grid tests in 385 s. The whole `session-recovery.test.ts` passes 36 of 36 dropped, and kept it passes 35 and skips the `unreadable` case.
- The other tests of the changed files are not touched.
- `python3 -m scripts.check_cli_shape` and the `python3 -m unittest ...` line from `ci.yml`: ok, 107 tests.

## CI

On the head of this branch, CI run 44216963071 (Linux E2E shards) shows the guarded tests running and passing, not skipped, because CI's runner enforces file modes:

- Shard 2/4: `acp: model-independent > an attached folder whose rule file cannot be read is reported in the note, not in the instructions`.
- Shard 3/4: `OS filesystem access denial reaches the next gateway request`, `a read-only session folder fails cleanly and resumes once writable`, `the app refuses a damaged session, a busy one and a read-only one, and says which`, `ACP refuses a damaged or read-only session and leaves its log as it was`, and all 27 `fault grid:` tests.
- Shard 4/4: `committed-history corruption (malformed)`, `(oversized)` and `(unreadable)`.

No guarded test has a `(skip)` line in those logs. The second macOS run, 44216978682, also passed; the `FAILURE` of the `macOS arm64` aggregator comes from the first macOS run, which the label call cancelled.

## For review

- `ignoresFileModes()` prints nothing. The guarded tests show as skipped in Bun's output. #2022's subagent test adds its own `console.warn`; I did not add one to each test.
- The grid tests and the app and ACP refusal tests skip as a whole, so where modes are not enforced their other rows (damaged, busy, full disk) skip too. They run in CI. Splitting the read-only row out of a test would change its structure, so I did not.
- `prompt-images.test.ts` is a TLA driver that no CI job runs, so CI does not show it.

## Zig tests that set permissions (not changed here)

Full unfiltered `zig build test --summary all` on `main` in the same sandbox: with the capabilities kept, 12239 of 12284 pass, 32 skipped, 13 failed (9 distinct tests). With them dropped, 12259 pass, 24 skipped, 1 failed. The one that still fails, `planner native printf forms match shell-visible execution`, is not about permissions. The other 8 fail only when the capabilities are kept:

| Test | Kept | Pattern |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api`: a read-only session folder fails with AccessDenied | fails | `setFilePermissions` 0o400, no guard |
| `api`: a blob is read-only and its path opens to its bytes | fails | the store's 0o400 blob, no guard |
| `api`: a lost or damaged blob damages its session | fails | the store's 0o400 blob, no guard |
| `storage`: a read-only file is written through its own handle and opens read-only only | fails | the store's 0o400 file, no guard |
| `web_fetch_artifacts`: a v2 download is a blob the model opens by path | fails | the store's 0o400 blob, no guard |
| `capture_store`: the object copy stops at the deadline | fails | `chmod` 0o500; guard is uid 0 or a failed `chmod` |
| `change_tracker`: undo refuses a file whose directory denies writes | fails | `chmod` 0o500; skips only when the `chmod` fails |
| `change_tracker`: undoLast reports unavailable when a new file cannot be deleted | fails | `chmod` 0o500; skips only when the `chmod` fails |

These skip when the capabilities are kept, with their own probes (`writesWhateverTheMode` in `session_adapter.zig`, or a failed `chmod`): `a turn the store cannot start keeps its prompt images inline`, `a new session never takes an id v1's folder could not be checked for`, `fx sessions convert says a v1 subagent's own subagent stays with a parent it can't read`, and `capture retention: a store that cannot be pruned stops eviction`. `oauth_session`: `OAuth refresh preflight honors file authority` and `change_tracker`: `a locked directory plus a failing write never leaves a half-replaced file` pass in both modes. None of them shares the TypeScript probe, so I left them for their own change.

title: Add RULES.md for repository rules
body:
## Summary

- Add RULES.md, a numbered list of rules that every change to fx keeps, each with a way to check it.
- Agents read RULES.md before any change, cite its rule IDs, and follow it over AGENTS.md when the two disagree.
- A pull request that changes RULES.md asks @fazxes for review.

title: Run shell commands in Vercel Sandboxes from placement rules
body:
## Summary

- Add the `experimental.sandbox_execution` setting. It is off by default and is read only from the user profile.
- Choose where each shell command runs from rules in `~/.fx/sandbox/config.json`: on this machine, in the repository's workspace sandbox, or in a new isolated sandbox. Rules match command patterns and folders; the model cannot pick a placement.
- Sync the repository into its workspace sandbox before each placed command, uploading only changed files, and fall back to a full sync when the sandbox copy does not match.
- Copy files the command changed back to the local checkout. A file that also changed locally during the command keeps the local version.
- Stream output from sandbox commands and support background runs, `wait`, and stop. Stopping kills the command in the sandbox.
- Run isolated commands in a new sandbox with no credentials and the profile's network policy, copy new and changed files to a run folder, and delete the sandbox afterwards.
- Delete isolated sandboxes left behind by an fx process that exited without cleaning up, on the next start.
- Build sandbox snapshots from setup scripts in the user's folder and reuse them until a script changes. An optional warm script runs once per new workspace sandbox.
- Pass named environment variables to workspace sandbox commands, never to isolated ones.
- Let `read_file` read a file that exists only in the workspace sandbox, and say so in the result.
- End sandbox command output with `fx:` lines that say where the command ran and which files moved.
- Refuse a placed command instead of running it locally when the sandbox cannot start, the Vercel login is missing, or the config file is invalid.
- Refuse `tty=true` commands that a rule places in a sandbox.
- Keep permission grants separate per placement and isolated profile, so a local approval does not cover a sandbox run or the other way around.

title: Count the last failed command in a group header's failure count
body:
## Summary

A group header's failure count left out the last command when that command failed too, so the count did not match the rows below it:

```
before:  ● Ran commands ✗ · 1 failed
         ├ Ran printf ok
         ├ Exited 1 ls missing-one · No such file or directory
         └ Exited 1 cat missing-two · No such file or directory

after:   ● Ran commands ✗ · 2 failed
```

The `✗` mark stands for the last command, and the count only took in the failures before it. The added failure comes from the group's last command row, the same row the earlier count leaves out, and only when that row ran and failed. So a command that still runs after a failed one, or a request the shell refused before running it, never makes one failure count twice (`● Ran commands ✗ · 1 failed` while `sh b.sh` runs after a failed `sh a.sh`). Now, when the header shows a count, the count takes in the last command's failure too, so it matches the failed rows. A group where only the last command failed still shows the mark alone (`● Ran commands ✗`), and a group whose last command passed is unchanged (`● Ran commands ✓ · 1 failed`).

## Tests

- Unit: "a command that failed before the last one still counts in the header" now also covers a group whose earlier and last commands both failed. It fails without the change.
- Unit: "a header counts each failed command once while a later command runs or was refused" covers a running command after a failed one (`1 failed`, expanded and collapsed) and a refused request that ends the turn after a failed command (`1 failed` expanded, `2 failed` collapsed). It fails when the added failure comes from the last finished command instead of the last row.
- E2E: "a header's failure count takes in the last command, also after resume" in `tests/e2e/tui-tool-story.test.ts`. It fails on a `main` build (`● Ran commands ✗ · 1 failed`) and passes with the change, live and after `--resume last`.
- `tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle` 98/98, `tui-tool-story` 14/14, `tui-terminal-tool` 19/19, `tui-command-permissions` 63/63 and `tui-resume` 93/93 pass in the sandbox.

title: Say that a terminal session has ended instead of holding input to it
body:
## Summary

- In auto mode, input typed into a terminal session that has exited, closed, or gone missing now fails with a message saying the session is no longer running and nothing was sent, instead of a "Safety review evidence incomplete" hold.
- That input no longer goes to the safety review, since it cannot reach the session.
- Input to a session that is still starting, or that belongs to someone else, is still held as before.

title: Keep a resumed subagent report on its own line
body:
A subagent's report that joins a running turn shows live as a line of its own after the turn's tool group. After `fx --resume last`, the same report became the last row of that group.

Before, after `fx --resume last`:

```
● Started a subagent, read a file
├ Messaged reviewer
├ Read main.ts
└ reviewer finished
```

After, the same as live:

```
● Started a subagent, read a file
├ Messaged reviewer
└ Read main.ts

● reviewer finished
```

## Cause

Live, the report's turn is drawn by `writeUserPromptCardWithSpacingAndSkillTokens` in `src/main.zig` as a tool row whose detail has no presentation group. The main agent's calls carry one, so the compact projection in `src/ui/transcript/tool_group_projection.zig` never puts the report in their group. On resume, `appendUserTurn` in `src/core/app/app_session_runtime.zig` draws the report the same way, but no resumed row carries a presentation group. The projection then grouped every tool row next to the report with it.

## Fix

- `ToolDetailRecord` gets a `subagent_report` mark. A report's call has no id, and main's own `subagent` call can have the same `{}` arguments, so only this mark tells a report row from a call main made.
- `TranscriptRuntime.attachSubagentReportDetail` attaches a report row's detail with the mark. The live path (`src/main.zig`, which session replay into the live transcript also uses) and the resume projection (`src/core/app/app_session_runtime.zig`) call it. `cloneToolDetailForSnapshot` keeps the mark.
- In the compact projection, a run of rows without a presentation group now ends where marked report rows start and end. Reports next to each other still share a group, as they do live. Live rows are unchanged: their presentation groups already keep reports apart.
- The group header's count of subagent updates reads the mark too, so a call main sent with `{}` arguments no longer counts as one.

A failed call main sent with `{}` arguments stays in its group on resume, as it does live:

```
● Read files
├ Read a.ts, b.ts
└ Failed subagent · action is required
```

## Tests

- `tool_group_projection.zig`: "a resumed subagent report keeps its own line after main's calls" checks rows without presentation groups: main's calls, two reports, then another call. Without the split, all five rows fold into one group.
- `tool_group_projection.zig`: "a resumed subagent call main sent with empty arguments stays in its group" checks a read, a failed `{}` subagent call, and a read. It fails when a report is matched by its `{}` arguments.
- `runtime.zig`: "only a subagent report's detail carries the report mark". `store.zig`: "a snapshot copy of a tool detail keeps its subagent report mark".
- `tui-tool-story.test.ts`: "a report that joins a turn after its calls keeps a line of its own, also after resume" messages a subagent, holds main's read until the report has joined the turn, and checks the report line live and after `fx --resume last`. It fails on a build without the fix at the resume check. `startStoryGateway` now lets the child's reply wait.

title: Show a parent's steer on the subagent's screen
body:
## Summary

- A message the parent agent sends into a working subagent's turn now shows on that subagent's screen when the subagent reads it, the same way as a message you type there.
- When a subagent's screen is shown again from a saved session, a parent's steer shows only the parent's words, without the `parent-agent feedback, not new user authority:` label that the model reads.

title: Let fx acp record a socket in each session lock it leads
body:
Stacked on #2096.

A session's lock picks the one fx process that runs it, but nothing says where that process is, so another process can only learn that the session is busy. This is the first step toward several clients on one session: a leader that others can find.

## What changes

- A native `fx acp` serves a Unix socket while it runs, one per process, in a new `0700` folder `fx-leader-<16 hex>` under `TMPDIR`, or under `/tmp` when the path would pass macOS's 103-byte limit or `TMPDIR` is unset or relative. It removes the socket and folder at a normal exit.
- When a session becomes live, the session manager writes one JSON line into the session's `lock` file, `{"socket":...,"pid":...}`, and empties it before it releases the lock. A killed process leaves its line; the next holder replaces or empties it. A process that can't make its socket runs without one and leaves the lock empty.
- The socket answers `initialize` with the stdio result plus `_meta["sh.fx/leader"]`: the pid and the sessions the process leads. Other requests get `-32601`. Attaching to a session over the socket comes next.
- Each reply has a 1 s write deadline, so a client that stops reading can't hold up exit. A socket option call on a connection whose peer already left counts as a closed connection: Zig's `posix.setsockopt` treats macOS's `EINVAL` there as unreachable, which crashed `fx acp` on macOS during testing.
- The SDK's in-process transport and WASM don't serve a socket.

## Tests

- `tests/e2e/acp.test.ts`, six new tests; the five about the record fail on #2096:
  - a session's lock names the socket of the fx acp that leads it
  - the leader socket answers only initialize
  - fx acp empties its session locks and removes its leader socket when it exits
  - after fx acp is killed, the next fx acp that loads the session records its own socket
  - a TMPDIR too long for a socket path puts the socket under /tmp
  - the leader socket keeps serving after clients leave before their answer
- Unit tests for the record write and clear, a dead holder's record, a failed write reported through `diag`, the socket path limit, the record line, the socket's answers, and a client that never reads.
- `tests/tla/acp/AcpLeader.tla` models processes, the lock, the record and a reader. `MCAcpLeader.cfg` passes; `AcpLeaderToday.cfg` (no record) violates `RecordFollowsLock`; `drivers/acp/leader/check-spec.ts` catches five planted bugs.
- `tests/tla/drivers/acp/leader/driver.ts` runs four plans against the real `fx acp`, reading the lock file, connecting and asking. The rules model accepts all four here and rejects three on #2096; the model without a record does the reverse. `check.sh --ci` runs it.
- Checked by hand on macOS arm64: the socket under macOS's `TMPDIR`, its answers, 20 clients that leave before their answer, and a clean exit.

Docs: vercel-labs/fx-web#346.

fx-core.wasm grows by 1,256 bytes; the budget is raised to 2,490,000.

title: Remove the test-only beginFreshPersistedSession wrapper
body:
## Summary

- No user-facing change: the session runtime's tests call `beginFresh` directly, and the public wrapper that only those tests used is gone.

title: List each safety review send in the trace
body:
## Summary

A held auto-mode review now shows each request fx sent to the safety reviewer in `/trace`, with the request's result and how long it took.

Before this, a review record had one total time and one reason. A hold reported as `transport_timed_out` after 15.6 seconds could not be explained from the trace: the reviewer allows 30 seconds and one retry, so the record could not show which request failed, how, or whether the retry ran.

## Changes

- `auto_classifier.zig`: `ReviewRequest` takes an optional `AttemptLog`. The send loop adds one entry for each request: `answered`, `malformed`, `timed_out`, `transient_failure`, `permanent_failure`, `call_failed`, or `cancelled`, with its elapsed time. A review and its confirming second review share the log, which keeps at most 6 entries.
- `tool_admission.zig`: every automatic review gets a log, and `recordAutoReview` passes its entries on. The conversion between the reviewer's and the trace's result types is an exhaustive switch, so the two lists cannot drift apart silently.
- `auto_review_metrics.zig` / `diagnostics.zig`: each stored review keeps its requests in a fixed buffer, like its other fields.
- `trace_report.zig`: `auto_review` and `held_auto_review` records write an `attempts` array when the review sent at least one request. A reused hold, or a review held before any request, writes no array.

## Testing

- Unit: "a review logs each send so /trace can show a retried timeout" (a timed-out request, then an answer), "a review keeps its sends in order, up to the limit", and "a review record lists each send to the reviewer".
- E2E with the built binary in tmux, through `/trace`: a new test where the reviewer answers 503 once and then clears, which records `transient_failure` then `answered` and runs the command; and the existing "reviewer could not give" test now checks that its 400 records one `permanent_failure` with no retry.
- `bun test ./auto-mode-reliability.test.ts`: 48 pass, 0 fail.
- `zig fmt --check src/` and `zig build` pass.
