title: Show a streaming call's row only once it names its target
body:
## Summary

While a read-like call's arguments stream in, its row showed a bare verb, such as `● Searching` or `● Reading`, until the whole call arrived. The row said nothing, then jumped to its real text:

```
before:  ● Reading          (while the arguments stream)
         ● Read a.md        (when the call ends)

after:   ● Reading a.md     (as soon as the path has streamed in)
         ● Read a.md
```

Two parts:

- **Core names the target early.** `ProvisionalToolStatuses` already names a streaming toolbox or subagent call once its name streams in. A builtin read-like call (`read_file`, `glob_files`, `grep_files`, `web_fetch`, `web_search`) now does the same with its own label value, such as a read's `path` or a search's `pattern`, read from the partial arguments with the same scanner (`streamedLabelValue`). A value with an escape in it, and the kinds that are not a plain top-level string, wait for the call. Calls that are not eligible for streaming rows (shell, edit, write) are unchanged.
- **The compact view shows no bare verb.** A streaming call whose status is a bare verb waits in the row it will join, as before. With no such row, it now has no row at all until its status names a target or the call starts, and the header does not count it. A group whose only calls name nothing yet shows nothing. Only a call whose arguments still stream counts: the transcript runtime marks a tool detail `streaming` when a provisional start creates it, and every other start clears the mark, so a call that has started keeps its row whatever its status says.

Ctrl+O, ACP and `fx ask` keep the provisional lifecycle as it was; they only get the named status sooner.

## Tests

- Unit (core): "a streaming builtin call's row names its target once that value arrives, and keeps it": a bare row first, the named row once the value is a whole string, no more publishes after that, and a value with an escape waits.
- Unit (projection): "a running call that names nothing yet shows no row until it does": a lone bare read is hidden, a named one shows, a started call keeps its row, and a bare search and command after a finished read add no row and nothing to the header.
- Unit (runtime): "a provisional call's detail is streaming until the call starts".
- The full unit suite passes in the sandbox except its 13 known environment failures (read-only files and blobs, `printf` parity, the capture deadline, `change_tracker` undo); "recorded tool finality stays independent of a live turn with the same number" and "rewrite publication cancellation follows accepted export without losing finalized rows" pass.
- E2E (`tests/e2e/tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`), with the stream held partway through the arguments:
  - "a streaming read shows its file as soon as the path arrives": `● Reading a.md` while held; `main` shows `● Reading`.
  - "a streaming search shows no row until its pattern arrives": no row while held; `main` shows `● Searching`.
  Both fail on a `main` build and pass with the change.
- `tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle` 100/100, `tui-tool-story` 13/13, `tui-terminal-tool` 19/19, `tui-command-permissions` 63/63 and `tui-resume` 93/93 pass in the sandbox.
- `acp`, `gateway-stream-lifecycle`, `mcp-stdio`, `web-search-fake-gateway`, `tui-decision-prompts`, `tui-host-switch`, `tui-permissions` and `tui-auth-source-selection` pass in the sandbox, except one denied-file-access test each in `acp` and `gateway-stream-lifecycle`, which fail the same way on `main` there.

title: Show a toolbox run of a built-in tool as a direct call of it
body:
A toolbox call that runs a built-in tool now reads as a direct call of that tool from start to end: while it streams, when it ends, when it fails, and after a resume. Before, one call could show three verbs: toolbox's "Running web_fetch" while it streamed, the tool's own verbs once it started, and "Couldn't use" when it failed before it started.

This branch merges main at 2484be8bd, which shows a streaming call's row only once it names its target (#2120). A streaming toolbox run now follows the same rule: its row stays hidden until both the tool it runs and that tool's target have streamed in, then reads as the direct call does.

## Before and after

Rows from the E2E test, which streams a toolbox run of `web_fetch` and holds it twice, streams a toolbox run of `web_search`, runs `read_file` through toolbox, then resumes the session. `web_fetch` refuses the address and `web_search` has no provider in the test profile, so both fail before they start. "Before" is main at 2484be8bd.

| Moment | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `web_fetch` run, held after `{"run":"web_fetch",` | `● Running web_fetch` | no row yet |
| `web_fetch` run, held after its `url` | `● Running web_fetch` | `● Fetching http://127.0.0.1/page` |
| `web_fetch` run failed | `├ Couldn't use http://127.0.0.1/page` | `├ Couldn't fetch http://127.0.0.1/page` |
| Streamed `web_search` run failed | `├ Couldn't use zig release notes` | `├ Couldn't search zig release notes` |
| `read_file` run done | `└ Read notes.txt` | `└ Read notes.txt` |
| After resume: group | `● Wrote a file` with `1 file changed` | `● Read a file` with `Explored 1 file` |
| After resume: `web_fetch` | `├ Couldn't run web_fetch` | `├ Couldn't fetch http://127.0.0.1/page` |
| After resume: `web_search` | `├ Couldn't run web_search` | `├ Couldn't search zig release notes` |
| After resume: `read_file` | `└ Ran read_file` | `└ Read notes.txt` |

## Causes

- The streamed row used toolbox's own presentation (`src/tools/capabilities/toolbox.zig` `presentation`: "Running" and the run's name) and named the row `toolbox` to the transcript (`src/core/agent/runtime/tool_presentation.zig` `publish`).
- A run that fails before it starts settles that streamed row. The transcript then saw a `toolbox` record with no arguments, so `failedVerb` in `src/ui/transcript/tool_group_projection.zig` wrote "Couldn't use" with the target of the call fx ran.
- A resumed session described and recorded the saved toolbox call (`src/core/app/app_session_runtime.zig` `writeCompletedToolResult`). `formatToolAction` in `src/core/app/app_agent_runtime.zig` used toolbox's "Ran" and the run's name, and toolbox's activity for a run (a write) made the group read "Wrote a file".

## Changes

- `toolbox.shownBuiltinRun` (`src/core/tooling/toolbox.zig`) gives the call a toolbox run of a built-in tool shows as: the call fx runs for it, of that tool with that tool's arguments under the toolbox call's id. Runs of MCP tools, of toolbox itself, and of names fx doesn't hold return null and keep toolbox's rows.
- The streamed row reads as a direct call of the tool does. It stays hidden until the run's tool and that tool's target are in, so it never reads as a bare verb, then shows the tool's verb and target and names the tool to the transcript. `streamedRunLabelValue` reads the target from the run's own `arguments` while they stream in, and `observeArguments` publishes the row once that value is whole. A run of `write_file`, `edit_file`, `shell`, or `ask_user_question` stays hidden until the call starts, as a direct call of those tools does. Settling a stream that ends early skips rows it never showed.
- `formatToolAction` and `formatPlainAction` (used by fx ask) unwrap the run, which covers rows settled from the toolbox call itself, such as a pending call a cancel stops.
- A resumed session replays the saved call as the tool it ran, so its row, record, and group match the live ones. Saved-output labels for later `read_tool_result` rows still use the saved call, as they do live.

What the model receives, the permission prompt, and ACP output do not change. ACP already titles a run as the tool it runs (`shownCall`), and its tool cards don't show these labels.

## Tests

- E2E: in `tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`, "a toolbox run of a built-in tool reads as a direct call of it, live and after resume" and "a streaming toolbox call's row names what it runs before its arguments end" fail on main at 2484be8bd, where the held rows read `● Running web_fetch` and `● Running glob_files`, and pass with this change on Linux and on a macOS build.
- Unit tests for each label path: `shownBuiltinRun`, `streamedRunLabelValue`, the streamed row frame by frame and its hidden cases, `formatToolAction` in every state, `formatPlainAction`, resume replay records, and the transcript projection of the records core now sends.
- `tui-gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts`, `tui-tool-story.test.ts`, `mcp-stdio.test.ts`, and `tui-resume.test.ts`.

title: Check elicitation string lengths in the escapes fuzz law
body:
## Why

The `mcp_elicitation_escapes` fuzz law checks that the elicitation engine treats two strings as one exactly when `std.json` decodes them alike. It never looked at the length of a string. The gate of the last change to it planted "a string's length counts bytes": one unit test caught it, and the replay of the saved inputs passed.

## Change

In `fuzzEscapedStrings` (`src/core/mcp_host/wire_tests.zig`), for the strings the law already makes, with escapes, surrogate pairs and non-ASCII characters:

- A form has a string field with `minLength` and `maxLength` set to the number of code points `std.json` decodes from the server's string.
- The engine must take that string, and refuse a string one code point longer (`maxLength`) and one shorter (`minLength`).
- The answer the script made must be taken exactly when it decodes to that many code points.

The test and its `tests/fuzz/targets.json` entry are renamed to say that the law now covers length limits too. The law does about half as much work again for each input, so the target runs 150,000 inputs a round and not 1,000,000: a round took 205 s with the new law and 137 s with the old one at 1,000,000, and takes 31 s at 150,000 (`CONTRIBUTING.md` asks for about 30 s). There is no product code and no docs change.

Eight saved inputs in `tests/fuzz/corpus/mcp_elicitation_escapes/` (`length-*`) cover two-, three- and four-byte characters, escaped surrogate pairs in lower and upper case hex, short escapes, twelve mixed characters, and an answer one wide character short, which a byte count accepts.

## Fail first

Each plant is made in a copy of `src/mcp/protocol/elicitation.zig`, at the length check of a string field, and run against the replay of the saved inputs (`zig build fuzz -Dfuzz-target=mcp_elicitation_escapes`):

| Plant | Law of `main` | New law |
|---|---|---|
| none | passes | passes |
| length counts the bytes of the token between its quotes | passes | fails |
| length counts the bytes of the decoded string | passes | fails |
| length counts the UTF-16 units of the decoded string | passes | fails |
| `maxLength` is exclusive | passes | fails |
| `minLength` is exclusive | passes | fails |

The "law of `main`" column runs the old law with the new saved inputs, so the inputs alone do not catch the plants.

## Where the checks ran

On Linux x86_64, in a build sandbox, with the model keys unset and `FX_SOUND=0`:

- The plant runs above, and the replay without a plant (24 saved inputs, exit 0).
- `python3 -m scripts.fuzz_nightly run --target mcp_elicitation_escapes --budget-seconds 150`: 3 rounds ok, at 150,000 inputs a round.
- One round, ReleaseSafe, the second time after the first instrumented build: 205 s (new law) and 137 s (law of `main`) at 1,000,000 inputs, and 31 s (new law) at 150,000.
- The `core.mcp_host.` group of the unit-test binary: 146 tests pass, with and without capabilities.
- `zig fmt --check src/` exits 0.

The law is in `core.mcp_host`, which `zig test src/mcp/mcp.zig` does not reach, so that root is not part of the proof.

title: Leave a subagent idle and usable when its work cannot start
body:
## Summary

Replaces #1939.

- When fx has saved a message's work and cannot start the subagent's thread, it now ends that work as failed and answers the main agent that the start failed and the subagent is idle. Before, the answer was a generic host failure (`host_failure`), and the subagent stayed marked running with nothing running it, so every later message to it was refused (`state_unavailable`).
- When fx cannot start the thread and cannot record the end of that work either, the answer now says what the main agent can do. It reads, with the name and the cause filled in: `<agent> did not start: <cause>. Your message did not run, and fx could not reset <agent>: it refuses messages until fx restarts, and a close of it cannot be saved either. Send the work to a subagent with another name, and tell the user that <agent> needs an fx restart.` Before, it ended after "cannot be saved either." and named no next step.
- `start_failed` carries its own sentence, with the subagent's name and the cause, so it is in the list of such codes (with `close_not_saved` and `profile_unavailable`) in `main`'s test of refusal codes in `src/core/subagent/refusal.zig`. It is an `ok: false` answer, like the other codes in that list.
- A message that waited for the user's turn and cannot start when that turn ends is now reported to the main agent as failed, with the cause, instead of vanishing, as long as fx can save the end of the user's turn, install the message as the subagent's next work and record that its start failed; when one of those saves fails, the message still gets no report, as on `main` (see "Not in this change"). When several waiting messages were joined into that work, the one report says how many it carried, `The subagent could not start the work your N messages made: <cause>. They never ran. Send them again if they are still needed.`; for one message the text is as it was. Before, the report named the first message and said `your message`, and the others were lost without a word, although `RULES.md` R3.8 (never drop queued work silently) and #2102's rule are that main is told what was dropped.
- When fx runs out of memory marking the subagent busy, which also leaked the copy of its id, the start is ended and answered in the same way, unless the end cannot be recorded either (the answer then says the subagent refuses messages) or fx cannot build the answer at all (main then reads a generic tool failure, as on `main`).
- A `message` call that could not keep the child's settings, or could not copy the child's id for its answer, after the registry save had written the work, left the child marked running with no slot behind it: for a new child, every later message to it was refused (`state_unavailable`); for one that already existed, the next message was answered `reviewer is busy, so the message waits and starts its next turn.` and never ran. The call now saves the work last, so such a failure leaves the registry as it was.
- Opening the work of a turn the parent did not start (the user's turn on the subagent's screen, or one its own subagent woke) had the same fault: the work was saved first, and a later step that failed left an active work in the log with nothing behind it. The log entry is now the last step that can fail.

Rules (`RULES.md`): R3.8, never drop queued work silently: a waiting message that cannot start is reported to the main agent as failed, with how many joined messages it carried; R7.1: each new test fails before the change, as Testing shows; R7.2: `Subagents.tla` gains `StartFail` (a start that fails after the work is saved ends it as failed, and the child is idle), and the planted bug that leaves such a work unfinished is caught by `NoIndeterminate`. `Subagents.tla` gets no rule that main is told once: it models the session's subagent records and their states, not counts, and the one number this change adds, the N of the joined-messages report, is pinned by unit tests.

## How

- `Owner.start` (`managed_owner.zig`) runs after its caller has saved the work. Under `Owner.mutex` it creates the slot, copies the child id and appends the slot to `self.slots`. When the thread cannot start, it returns `error.ThreadSpawnFailed`, and its three `errdefer`s pop the slot from `self.slots`, free the id copy and destroy the slot before the mutex is released. They touch neither the registry nor the runtime's busy list, so the saved work is still active when `start` returns.
- `Owner.endUnstarted` ends that saved work. It holds the registry store's lock (`state_store.acquireLock()`, not `Owner.mutex`) while it loads the registry, finishes the child's active work as `failed` with the failure `start_failed` and the error's name, and saves the registry. Finishing clears the child's active work, so the child is idle and takes its next message. A report is owed only when the caller asks for one, the tree is not closed, and the child's report rule makes a failed work reportable. When the work cannot be ended it returns null and writes a trace line naming the child, the work and the stage. At the stages `state_load`, `work_id`, `state_finish` and `state_save` the registry could not be read or nothing was written, so the child stays marked running until fx restarts, and a close of it cannot be saved either (`close_not_saved`), because a close is written only for an idle child. A new host over the same registry recovers the work (`recoverInterrupted`), and the child then takes messages and closes. At `child_missing`, `no_active_work` and `other_active_work` there is no such work to end: the child is gone, has no active work, or runs another one. The two callers hold the admission lock from the save of the work to this call, so for them a null is one of the first four.
- Two callers use it, both under `Runtime.admission_mutex`. `admitAndStartManagedWork`, for a `message` call that starts a work, passes `owes_report = false` because the call carries the failure: `message` answers with the error code `start_failed`. The wording is `startFailedResult`'s when the work was ended (`<agent> did not start: <cause>. Your message did not run. <agent> is idle, so send the message again if it is still needed.`) and `startFailedStuckResult`'s when `endUnstarted` returned null (the text above). `startPendingAfterTurn`, for a waiting message that cannot start when the user's turn or a child's report ends, passes `owes_report = true`; when it gets null there, no report is posted: the message is dropped with a trace line. The work it starts carries the `messages` count that #2102 gives `Owner.start`; the call path starts a work of one message, so it passes 0.
- `WorkEnd.start_failure` is a static cause string from `startCauseText`: `fx could not start a thread for it`, `fx ran out of memory`, `fx is closing`, or the error's name. Only `endUserWork` sets it, for a waiting message that could not start. `Runtime.reportOutput` reads it and words the report as `The subagent could not start the work your message made: <cause>. It never ran. Send the message again if it is still needed.` in place of a reply. That text does not say the subagent is idle: the report's `next` note says so, from `idleAfterEnd`, which reads the waiting messages, the open turn and any close after the text is built. It is null for every other end. `WorkEnd.start_messages` is how many of the parent's messages that work carried, 1 unless waiting messages joined it. `startPendingAfterTurn` takes it from `messages`, the count it starts the slot with (the `unstarted` count of #2102), through `FailedStart.messages` to `endUserWork`, and `startFailedReport(a, cause, messages)` words the report from it. For more than one message it reads `The subagent could not start the work your N messages made: <cause>. They never ran. Send them again if they are still needed.` with N as a number; for one it is the text above, word for word. The count is the messages that are in that work (one, plus the ones `absorbPendingLocked` joined, which includes kept ones the host queued as waiting), so it is exact at that point. The call path (`startSavedWorkLocked`, `managed.start(child_id, 0)`) starts a work of one message, since a `message` call starts a work only when nothing waits, so `startFailedResult`, `startFailedStuckResult` and the answer `Your message did not run` stay as they are. The report's text is built in the report's arena, not in the fixed buffer that the call answers use, so a long cause or a large N has no buffer to overflow.
- `openTurnWorkLocked`, which opens the work of a turn the parent did not start, now appends the turn work and sets the busy mark first, and saves the log entry (`startTurnWorkInLog`) last, only when the work opens at once (`open_now`). A failure of that save pops the turn work and clears the busy mark if this call set it. Before, the entry was saved first, so a later failure left an active work in the log with nothing behind it.
- `admitManagedWork`, for a `message` call that saves a work, now saves the registry last as well: after `ensureManagedChildSession` and `managedAdmissionReady`, both for an existing child and for a new one. Before, a failure of either after the save left a saved active work with no slot. `ensureManagedChildSession` writes nothing to disk: it keeps the child's settings in memory until its first turn. The test `a message whose child's seed cannot be kept leaves its subagent idle or working, then takes the next` fails with the old order in either branch.
- `markBusyLocked` copies the child id before it appends the copy to `busy`. The copy is now freed by an `errdefer` when the append fails; before, it leaked there. When the mark is cleared normally, `clearBusyLocked` frees it.
- `FX_TEST_SUBAGENT_START_FAIL=<n>` is a decimal count, not a path or a hold. `start_test_controls.spawnFails` reads it, and `Owner.start` calls it after the slot is appended and before the thread would spawn; the first n such starts in the process return `error.ThreadSpawnFailed`. A value that `std.fmt.parseInt(u32, value, 10)` cannot read is ignored; that parser also takes a leading `+` and `_` between digits, so `+1` and `1_0` count as 1 and 10. Every fx binary except libfx reads the variable, the shipped `fx` binary included, as the other test controls do; it is registered as internal. In a libfx build `spawnFails` returns false at compile time, before the variable is read. In unit-test builds the variable is never read; tests set `test_fail_spawn` instead.

## Testing

Zig 0.17.1 (`zig version`) in a Linux x86_64 sandbox unless a row says macOS. Tree: `62a6345b2`, which is `main` `2c06393ff` with this change on top; the branch holds one merge of `main` (with the printf repair of #2127), and `git show --remerge-diff` of it is empty. `build.zig` has no `test-one` step, so the unit binary comes from a local edit that is not part of this change: a `test-filter` option split at `|` and passed as the `.filters` of `exe_tests`, and a `test-one` step that runs it. The filter holds this change's 19 tests, #2102's 27 and #2087's 9: 55 named tests, and the build also runs the 23 unnamed `test` blocks that every filtered build runs, 78 tests in all.

| What | Method | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Format, build | `zig fmt --check src/`, `zig build` | exit 0, exit 0 |
| Deprecated declarations | `check_deprecated.py --review` on the four Zig files | exit 0: 0 removed, 0 deprecated, 0 to review |
| Unit tests, Debug | loop over the built test binary, 4 at a time, each needs exit 0; the first run is checked for an `OK` line of each of the 55 named tests | 20 of 20; 55 of 55 `OK` lines |
| Unit tests, ReleaseSafe | the same, 100 runs | 99 of 100; 55 of 55 `OK` lines. The one run that failed is a cell of #2102's table test, which this change does not touch (see the paragraph after the table) |
| Unit tests under ThreadSanitizer | `zig build test-one -Dtest-filter=<the 55 names> -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe -Dsanitize-thread=true`, then the built binary 10 times, 2 at a time | 10 of 10, 0 ThreadSanitizer warnings, 55 of 55 `OK` lines |
| Unit tests, macOS | `zig build install -Dtarget=aarch64-macos` with the same edit plus `installArtifact(exe_tests)`, built in the sandbox and run on this Mac (`FX_SOUND=0`) | 10 of 10; 55 of 55 `OK` lines on the first run (78 tests) |
| End-to-end tests | `FX_SOUND=0 bun test tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts -t "<name>"` for this change's `a subagent whose start failed is idle and takes the next message` and #2087's `a stop right after a subagent's turn ended finds it not working` and `a close right after a subagent's turn ended closes it as an idle one`, 3 runs; and the whole file once on Linux | Linux 3 of 3; macOS arm64 binary (`fx-cloud macos-build`, run on this Mac) 3 of 3. The whole file on Linux (`bun test tests/e2e/gateway-stream-lifecycle.test.ts` from the repository root): 255 pass, 2 skip, 0 fail on this head, 254 pass, 2 skip, 0 fail on `main` `2c06393ff` (+1, this change's test); the whole file was not run on the Mac |
| `check.sh` | `sh tests/tla/subagent/check.sh` | exit 0, one `ok` per config: 57 on `main` `2c06393ff` and 57 on this head (no config is added) |
| `Subagents` model | `sh tests/tla/session_manager/check.sh Subagents`; `python3 tests/tla/session_manager/mutants.py Subagents` | exit 0; 204,097 states generated, 120,297 distinct before and 303,843 / 175,397 after, as the README says; all four planted bugs caught, among them `a failed start leaves the work unfinished` by `NoIndeterminate` |
| Stop-message driver | `cd tests/tla/drivers/subagent && bun test stop-message.test.ts` (this change does not touch it) | Linux 3 runs of 28 of 28; macOS binary 3 runs of 28 of 28 |
| Full `zig build test --summary all` | once on plain `main` `2c06393ff`, once on this head | every test binary compiles on both, and the same 8 tests fail on both (tests of read-only files and folders and one capture-store deadline test, which do not hold in this sandbox; 12 failed in each summary); the `printf` test that failed on both before #2127 passes on both. The unit-test binary runs 12,105 tests on this head (12,074 pass, 27 skipped, 4 fail) and 12,086 on `main` (12,055, 27, 4): +19, this change's 19 tests (counted by script from the diff). The other test binaries are equal (1, 2, 4, 123 and 153 tests). The summary's totals (12,344 of 12,388 on this head, 12,325 of 12,369 on `main`) leave out the test steps a run takes from the cache, so totals compare only between runs with the same cached steps |

The ReleaseSafe loop's failing run is not from this change. #2102's table test, `every message main sends has one account in every window of a subagent's slot, for each stop and close`, fails now and then at its cell `running_unread / user_close then parent_stop` (`TABLE 1 of 656 cells break the rule or could not be driven`). Loops of the same ReleaseSafe build, 4 runs at a time, show it on plain `main` `2c06393ff` (its 36 named tests: 1 failing run of 264) and on this head (2 failing runs of 300); a loop of that one cell alone failed 18 of 6000 times on this head. The cell fails in two ways, and in both the message the user's close dropped has no account. In the first, the turn and its work had ended before the parent's stop came, so the stop answered `reviewer was not working.`; the user's close counts nothing, as the cell `user_close` alone says (marked "as on main: R2"). In the second, the stop met the turn while it ended, answered `Stopped reviewer: its turn ended.` with no count, because the end of the slot dropped the kept message between the stop's two steps, `Owner.stop` and `takeDropped`, which take the slot's lock one after the other. That window is in `main`'s stop and close, and this change has no line in them; it needs its own change.

No test is skipped, deleted or loosened (R7.4). A script found 151 named tests in the four Zig files this change touches on `main` `2c06393ff`: every one is on the head, none missing, and the body of all but two is byte for byte the same. The two are extended, not shortened. In `refusal.zig`, the test of the codes that carry their own text gains `start_failed` in its list. In `start_test_controls.zig`, `a test build holds a work's start and sets the wait limit only through its hooks` gains three assertions (the new hook is null without a test, `spawnFails` is false until a test asks, and true while it does). This change deletes no line of any test.

Waits (R7.3): the tests use no network, credential or model. This change adds 28 calls of `waitUntilQuiet` and 1 of `waitForRuns`, which are `main`'s polling helpers (1 ms polls with a bound), in its 19 tests and in the helpers they share (counted by script over the diff: none is removed), and no sleep of its own: a script found no added line that sleeps.

Each new test, before the change. The first tree is this branch with `managed_owner.zig` and `refusal.zig` taken from the base, and the production part of `tool_host.zig` (everything before `const MailboxFixture`) too; what stays is the tests, the text builders that sit after that line, `start_test_controls.zig` and the one line of `Owner.start` that lets a test make a start fail. Two tests are left out there: `a failed start is ended only for the work it was told of`, which calls `endUnstarted` directly and does not compile without the change, and `a message sent after a waiting message's failed start was ended waits for the next start`, which compiles there and fails at `try expectBodyHas(WindowSend.answer, "is busy")`: nothing calls the hook it sets, so the answer is empty. Linux, Debug, one run of this head's tests (`62a6345b2`) on `main` `2c06393ff`'s production, of the 17 tests that remain (the 13 for a failed start and its report, the 3 of joined messages and the sweep of the child's seed): 16 fail and 1 passes (the `Build Summary` reads `24/40 tests passed (16 failed)`). The statement each fails at comes from a run with a line print before each `try` of the tests, so the line is the last statement the test reached.

| Test | Fails at |
| --- | --- |
| `a start that fails after its work is saved answers that it failed, and ends the work` | `try callTool(... "first" ...)`: the failed start escapes the call as `error.ThreadSpawnFailed` |
| `a subagent whose start failed is idle and takes the next message` | `try expectBodyHas(again, "Sent to reviewer")`: the answer is `state_unavailable` |
| `a subagent whose busy mark failed is idle and takes the next message` | the same statement: the answer is `reviewer is busy, so the message waits...` |
| `a message that waited for the user's turn and could not start is reported as failed` | `expectEqual(@as(usize, 2), fixture.reportCount())`: expected 2, found 1 |
| `each report of a waiting message that could not start says its subagent is idle only when it is` | `try waitUntilQuiet(runtime)` returns an error: the host never goes quiet |
| `the parent's close that lands after a failed start is ended leaves a report that does not call the subagent idle` | `try expectCloseInReportWindow(.parent)` |
| `the user's close that lands after a failed start is ended leaves a report that does not call the subagent idle` | `try expectCloseInReportWindow(.user)` |
| `a message whose start failed says its subagent is idle only while nothing waits for it, runs it or closes it` | `try callTool(... .message = call ...)`: the failed start escapes the call as `error.ThreadSpawnFailed` |
| `a subagent whose waiting message could not start after the user's turn takes the next message` | `try expectBodyHas(again, "Sent to reviewer")` |
| `a message whose start fails at any allocation leaves its subagent idle or working, then takes the next` | `expectAt` of the sweep: reviewer is running with no slot, or the next message was refused |
| `a message whose child's seed cannot be kept leaves its subagent idle or working, then takes the next` | `expectAt` of the sweep: reviewer is running with no slot (on `main`'s order the work is saved before the seed, so a seed that cannot be kept leaves the saved work with no slot) |
| `a message whose start failed and whose end was not recorded says the subagent refuses messages until fx restarts` | `try std.testing.expect(stuck > 0)`: no index leaves the end unrecorded |
| `a user's turn whose work fails to open at any allocation leaves its subagent idle or working, then takes the next message` | `expectAt` of the sweep |
| `the answer for a start whose end was not recorded fits the longest name and cause, and its fallback is still true` (passes) | it tests the two text builders, which the tree keeps |
| `two waiting messages joined into a work that could not start are reported as two` | `expectEqual(@as(usize, 2), fixture.reportCount())`: expected 2, found 1 (the start failure escapes, nothing is reported) |
| `three waiting messages joined into a work that could not start are reported as three` | the same |
| `a stop or close after a failed start of a work of joined messages counts none of them` | `try expectBodyHas(again, "Sent to reviewer")`: the answer is `state_unavailable` |

The tests of joined messages on their own (tree `0e540f703`, which has everything except the lines that carry the count to the report): the two tests of joined messages fail and the third passes (Linux, Debug, one run). `two waiting messages joined ...` fails with `expected this output: The subagent could not start the work your 2 messages made: fx could not start a thread for it. They never ran. Send them again if they are still needed.` and `instead found this: reviewer call-2 <work id> failed The subagent could not start the work your message made: fx could not start a thread for it. It never ran. Send the message again if it is still needed.`; the one for three fails in the same way. The third test, `a stop or close after a failed start of a work of joined messages counts none of them`, pins what already holds there: the failed start leaves no slot, so `Owner.start`'s `errdefer`s have popped and destroyed the slot with its `unstarted` count, and nothing is left for a later stop or close to count or for the next work to count again. After a failed start of a work of two messages the parent's stop answers `reviewer was not working.` with no count, the next message starts a work of its own, the user's close counts 0 and `user_dropped` stays empty. The user's close counts nothing on `main` and in #2102 either, so those assertions on it hold without this change too; they stay for a later change that counts what the user's close or stop drops (#2102 leaves that uncounted, as `main` does), which must not count a work whose start failed. This change reads nothing that #2102 removed: it calls neither `takeKept` nor `closeByUser`. A start whose end cannot be recorded leaves no slot either.

The four allocation sweeps fail each allocation of a call's thread in turn, so their cost is the number of indices they visit, measured with a print after each loop (a sandbox-only edit, three runs, the same numbers every run, on `62a6345b2`): `a message whose start fails at any allocation` 15 indices when the call makes the subagent and 11 when it follows a first message; `a message whose start failed and whose end was not recorded` 27 indices, 12 of which leave the end unrecorded; `a user's turn whose work fails to open` 15 indices; `a message whose child's seed cannot be kept` 11 indices when the call makes the subagent and 10 when it follows one. The first three put their fault allocator in the runtime and its owner (`FaultedHost.install`); the fourth puts it in the allocator of the child registry (`FaultedHost.installChildren`), which `install` leaves alone and where the child's seed is kept and the registry is copied on a save, and keeps the call's own arena off it, so only that allocator's allocations count. Each installs its fault allocator once, before any slot thread of the host exists, and `arm` and `disarm` change only its `fail_at` and `count`, so a slot thread of an earlier work reads no field that the test thread writes: `FaultAllocator.alloc` reads `fail_at`, `count` and `fired` only on the test thread (a thread-id check comes first); the slot threads read `thread` and `len`, which nothing writes after the install, and `children.alloc` itself, which the test thread writes once before the first message. Under ThreadSanitizer 10 runs of the tests give 0 warnings (the ThreadSanitizer row above).

Twenty product lines, each changed alone on the head and run against the 19 tests of this change plus #2102's 27 and #2087's 9 named tests (Debug, one run each, in five sandboxes, on `62a6345b2`; a mutant counts as killed when a test fails or does not run): 19 killed, 1 not.

| Change to one product line | Tests that fail |
| --- | --- |
| The failed start's work is not ended (endUnstarted gives up at once) | 14 tests, among them `a start that fails after its work is saved answers that it failed, and ends the work` |
| The failed start owes no report | 8 tests, among them `a message that waited for the user's turn and could not start is reported as failed` |
| The failed start ends whatever work is active (the expected work id is not checked) | `a failed start is ended only for the work it was told of` |
| The answer for a work that was ended is the stuck one | 3 tests, among them `a start that fails after its work is saved answers that it failed, and ends the work` |
| The call's start failure is told as ended whatever the end did | `a message whose start failed and whose end was not recorded says the subagent refuses messages until fx restarts` |
| The work of a failed start of a call is not ended | 5 tests, among them `a start that fails after its work is saved answers that it failed, and ends the work` |
| A waiting message's failed start owes no report | 8 tests, among them `a message that waited for the user's turn and could not start is reported as failed` |
| A waiting message's failed start report gives no cause | 7 tests, among them `a message that waited for the user's turn and could not start is reported as failed` |
| The report of a waiting message's failed start does not carry its cause | 7 tests, among them `a message that waited for the user's turn and could not start is reported as failed` |
| The window after a failed start's end has no hook | 3 tests, among them `the parent's close that lands after a failed start is ended leaves a report that does not call the subagent idle` |
| The next waiting message does not start after a failed one (busy is cleared) | `a message sent after a waiting message's failed start was ended waits for the next start` |
| A failed start that could not be ended leaves the busy mark set | none |
| The call of a failed start's work stays in the call table | `a message that waited for the user's turn and could not start is reported as failed` |
| The busy mark's id copy leaks when the append fails | `a message whose start fails at any allocation leaves its subagent idle or working, then takes the next`; `a message whose start failed and whose end was not recorded says the subagent refuses messages until fx restarts` |
| A turn work that fails to open clears the busy mark of a child that was already busy | `a user's turn whose work fails to open at any allocation leaves its subagent idle or working, then takes the next message` |
| The end of a failed start's copy of the work id leaks | 6 tests, among them `a start that fails after its work is saved answers that it failed, and ends the work` |
| The report counts one message whatever the work carried | `two waiting messages joined into a work that could not start are reported as two`; `three waiting messages joined into a work that could not start are reported as three` |
| The failed start carries a count of one | `two waiting messages joined into a work that could not start are reported as two`; `three waiting messages joined into a work that could not start are reported as three` |
| The registry save comes before the seed and the answer's copy, for a message to an existing child (`main`'s order) | `a message whose child's seed cannot be kept leaves its subagent idle or working, then takes the next` |
| The same for a message that makes a child | the same test |

Not pinned by any test: the `clearBusyLocked` call in `startPendingAfterTurn` for a waiting message whose failed start cannot be ended (the row `A failed start that could not be ended leaves the busy mark set`). Reaching it needs a waiting message's start to fail and the end of that failed start to fail at one of the stages `state_load`, `work_id`, `state_finish` or `state_save`. The sweeps that reach an unrecorded end do it through a `message` call, not through a waiting message, and the registry then keeps the work running whichever way the busy mark is left, so the one thing the line changes is whether `status` calls that child working. The case itself is under "Not in this change". Every other change is killed by the tests in its row.

Not run: the whole unit suite under ReleaseSafe or ThreadSanitizer (the 55 named tests and the unnamed blocks only), the whole E2E file on the macOS binary, the failing-first tree on the macOS binary, a key press in the app.

## Not in this change

- `status` and the idle note call the stuck subagent idle. With the child stuck, `status` says `reviewer: idle, reports final. For: first`, and the answer to a message that starts another subagent ends with `Idle subagents, each with its own context:` followed by `- reviewer: first` and `Give related work to the one whose context fits instead of a new name.` So that answer can point the main agent back to the subagent that refuses messages. I saw both in the sweep's unit test, at the indices where the end is unrecorded; the test does not pin them.
- A message to the stuck subagent then gets `state_unavailable`; it is refused with a notice, so `RULES.md` R3.8 (never drop queued work silently) holds for it, but the notice's advice is wrong. The text is `fx could not reach the subagent's turn, so the message was not sent. Call status, then send it again.` That advice cannot work until fx restarts, because `status` still says idle. The sentence is `main`'s, and it serves the other causes of `state_unavailable` too.
- Both come from `Runtime.childStateLocked` on `main`, which reads a child that the registry holds as running, with no slot running it, as idle: any child that is not on the host's busy list reads as idle unless it is interrupted, finished or waiting for an approval. `status`, the idle note (`idleOthers`) and the roster all use it. It needs its own change.
- A work's end that cannot be written to the registry (`Owner.finish` returns an error): the slot stays unpublished and later messages get `state_unavailable`. It needs a different fix, on the finish side of the slot.
- A waiting message that the end hook cannot install as the next work, because the registry cannot be loaded or saved, is dropped with a trace line and the main agent is not told, as on `main` (`RULES.md` R3.8). No work was saved, so nothing is stuck, but a report for it needs a way to name a work the registry never had.
- An allocation that fails while the user's own turn on the subagent's screen ends, before a waiting message's start: the end of that turn is not saved, so the registry keeps the user's work open with nothing running it. The waiting message is then dropped with a trace line, never runs, and gets no report. The next message is answered `reviewer is busy, so the message waits and starts its next turn. Its report arrives on its own.`, and it never runs or gets a report either; `status` reads `reviewer: idle, 1 waiting message, ...`. A restart of fx marks the open work interrupted, so the subagent takes messages again, but those two messages stay lost, with no report. A sweep that fails one allocation at a time through the end of the user's turn, with one waiting message whose start fails, finds it at the first 10 of its 39 allocations (indices 0 to 9, before the waiting message's start; measured on `19a2581c0d`); `main` `283323f40` gives the same at the same indices. It needs its own change.
- A waiting message whose start fails and whose end cannot be recorded gets no report: it is dropped with a trace line (`RULES.md` R3.8), the subagent then refuses messages (`state_unavailable`) until fx restarts, and a close of it cannot be saved (`close_not_saved`). In a sweep of each allocation of `endUserWork` with one waiting message whose start fails, 13 of 39 indices leave it so (indices 23 to 35, measured on `19a2581c0d`); that sweep is not part of this change.
- Making the close of a subagent whose work no slot runs succeed needs a change in `settleClose`: a close is written only for an idle child.
- The report of a failed start does not say that the user's close is under way when one lands at that moment; main learns of the close from the answer to its next message.

title: Hold fake children's answers until the parent has saved its turn
body:
## Summary

A fake child that answers at once can finish before its parent has saved the turn that sent its message. The report then joins that turn (`postMail` in `src/core/agent/worker_runtime.zig`) instead of starting the next one. The receipt gets no request of its own, so a request count or a read of the report depends on which side is faster. #2097 fixed this for three persistent-resume tests. This change fixes the other tests of that shape that really failed in CI.

Each of those tests now holds the child's answer until the parent has saved its turn. One helper, `holdChildAnswer` in `tests/e2e/saved-sessions.ts`, does this. A wait that fails is answered with an error response, so fx sees a failed request. runFx's bound is above the 10 s wait in every test but the replay test, so those tests throw the kept error after the run. The replay test's bound equals the wait, so it fails on its exit code check instead. In all five tests runFx ends fx itself, so no fx process is left behind. Nothing in fx changes, and no test is skipped or loosened (R7.3, R7.4, R8.2 in `RULES.md`).

## Which tests

I searched CI for every test of the shape. Only a report that joined the parent's turn counts as this failure.

| Test | Jobs | Dates | CI message |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `an allowed subagent child inherits ultrafast routing` | 2 | 11-13, 11-14 | `parent observed the child` expected, `parent read the report` received |
| `a named v2 subagent continues its history ...` | 1 (main) | 11-17 | `ULTRA_PARENT_1` expected, `ULTRA_REPORT_1` received |
| `subagent replay returns saved success and failure ...` | 5 | 11-12 to 11-14 | length 2 expected, 1 received |
| `subagent HTTP failures retain terminal outcome before output` | 1 | 11-14 | 4 expected, 3 received |
| `subagent failure retains its cause after effects ...` | 1 | 11-13 | `history.some(...)` true expected, false received |

Every job passed on retry, so the failure was hidden. The search covered:

- Failed runs from 2026-09-02 to 11-18: 967 runs, 229 with no log left.
- The "passed only on retry" notes of `ci.yml` runs from 2026-10-29, when reports became turns, to 11-18: 2,223 runs, and 1,638 E2E jobs read.

Failures on older branches (09-07 to 10-24) came from each branch's own change, so they do not count.

The commit-fails variant and the HTTP after-effects variant never failed in CI. They stay in this change because they share the changed code with the tests that did: `runFailedChildAfterEffects` and the HTTP `test.each`.

## Evidence

All runs were in a sandbox with Zig 0.17.1 and `timeout -k`, with every capability dropped (`setpriv`, `CapEff 0`), as in CI. The probe adds a one second shell call to the parent's step, so the child's report arrives while the parent's turn still runs.

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Main with the probe, 5 runs | all 35 test runs fail, with CI's messages |
| Fix with the probe, quiet | 20 of 20 runs pass (7 tests each) |
| Fix with the probe, load | 20 of 20 runs pass |
| Fix without the probe, quiet | 100 of 100 runs pass |
| Fix without the probe, load (6 CPU hogs on 2 CPUs) | 1969 of 1970 runs pass |
| Both whole files | 281 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip |

On main with the probe, the messages are `parent read the report`, `ULTRA_REPORT_1`, length 1, 3 for 4 and 6 for 8 (the HTTP after-effects variant), and true expected for false in both failed-child tests.

A failed hold (made impossible in a sandbox copy, with the same setup):

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| The two ultrafast tests, first commit only | both end by Bun's 20 s limit, with no hold error, and one fx process is alive right after each test (gone within 30 s) |
| The two ultrafast tests, with `629e9f3b82` | both fail at 15 s with `no root session committed more than 1000000 turns`, and no fx process is alive at once or after 30 s |
| The two ultrafast tests, `629e9f3b82`, no probe, quiet | 100 of 100 runs pass |
| The same, load | 300 of 300 runs pass |
| The same, with the probe, quiet and load | 20 of 20 and 20 of 20 runs pass |
| Whole `ultrafast-fake-gateway.test.ts` | 25 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip |

The first table is from the first commit. `629e9f3b82` only gives the two ultrafast tests a runFx bound of 15 s inside their 20 s limit.

Script checks: `python3 -m scripts.check_cli_shape` passes. The unittest line in `ci.yml` runs 107 tests, OK. `scripts/check-public-surface.sh` exits 0. No Zig file changes, so there is no full Zig build.

## One failure I cannot explain

In the load runs, 1 run of 1970 failed. The test was `a named v2 subagent continues its history ...`, round 3. The output held `ULTRA_PARENT_3` and no `ULTRA_REPORT_3`: the parent's own text, and no report turn.

About 6,500 later runs did not show it. They included runs with a trace, runs with a 0 to 40 ms delay after the hold, runs on one CPU with ten hogs, and 810 more runs of the full set. The unchanged test did not show it either in 1,500 runs of that test alone under load. The log of the failed run was lost, so there is no trace.

The cause is unknown. It may be in the test or in fx. It did not come back in 3,000 more loaded runs with fx traces on (2,000 on the first head and 1,000 on the merged head), and the traces showed no sign of a lost report.

## Not in scope

- `ask continues and persists a healthy parent when its child's session is gone` failed in 23 jobs from 11-11 to 11-13, mostly on macOS.
- `an empty reply that stops for another reason gives way to a subagent's report` failed in 2 jobs.
- These tests had no CI failure in the window, so I left them alone: the two `canonical subagent executes through parent MCP adapters` tests, `subagent starts when the parent has more than 256 MCP tools`, and `a subagent recovers from search path failures and completes its batch`.

title: Run printf through the shell when its data starts with --
body:
## Summary

`Build & Test (ReleaseSafe)` fails on `main` and on every PR in "planner native printf forms match shell-visible execution". The CI runner now uses the `ubuntu-26.04` image, where `/usr/bin/printf` is uutils printf 0.10.0. The planner admits `printf '%s' '--help'` for a direct run of `/usr/bin/printf` (`planPrintf` in `src/core/shell_command/command_effect.zig`). uutils reads that `--help` as its own option even after the format, so the direct run printed the uutils help text while the shell printed `--help`. The test found a real gap: on a Linux host with uutils coreutils, fx ran such a command without review and returned output the shell would not give.

## How each printf reads a data argument

Each printf binary against the `dash` builtin, with the value as the first data argument (`printf '%s' VALUE`). Ubuntu 26.04 for uutils and GNU, macOS 27.2 for BSD.

| Data argument | uutils 0.2.2, 0.5.0, 0.10.0 | uutils 0.12.0 | GNU 9.7 | macOS (BSD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--help` | prints its help | prints the value | prints the value | prints the value |
| `--version` | prints its version | prints the value | prints the value | prints the value |
| `--help=x`, `--version=1` | exits 1 with `unexpected value` | prints the value | prints the value | prints the value |
| `--` | drops it and prints nothing for it | prints the value | prints the value | prints the value |
| `--he`, `--hel`, `--h`, `--v`, `--ver`, `--x`, `--foo`, `---` | prints the value | prints the value | prints the value | prints the value |
| `-h`, `-V`, `-x`, `-`, `-leading`, `-hV`, `-e`, `-n`, `-1` | prints the value | prints the value | prints the value | prints the value |

uutils misreads these values only as the first data argument: `printf '%s%s' x --help` prints `x--help` with every binary. In the format position every binary reads `--help`, `--version`, or `--` as an option, and the planner already refuses a format that starts with `-`.

## Fix

`planPrintf` now refuses any data argument that starts with `--` with `unsupported_argument`, so those commands run in the shell after review, as they did before direct runs existed. Every value that a printf reads as an option starts with `--`, and no printf reads a single-dash data argument as one, so `printf '%s' '-h'` and `printf '%s' '-leading'` still run direct. The rule covers every data position and both targets, so it does not depend on the uutils version or its option parser on a given host.

Rules: R6.3, R7.1, R7.4.

## Tests

- "planner admits the reviewed direct command matrix": `printf '%s' '--help'` leaves the matrix, and `printf '%s' '-h'` and `printf '%s' '-V'` join it.
- "planner returns stable reasons for approval-bearing forms": adds `printf '%s' '--help'`, `printf '%s' '--version'`, `printf '%s' '--'`, and `printf -- x`.
- New "planner refuses printf data that the binary reads as an option": `--help`, `--version`, `--help=x`, `--version=1`, `--`, `--he`, `--x`, and `---` as the only, first, and later data argument, on macOS and Linux.
- "planner native printf forms match shell-visible execution" still compares the real shell with the direct binary. The `--help` form, which is no longer direct, gives way to `-h`, `-V`, `-`, and `'-x' '-h'`. Both generated printf matrices add `-h`, `-V`, and `-` to their data classes.

The `command_effect` tests (ReleaseSafe) in the Ubuntu 26.04 sandbox, with each binary installed as `/usr/bin/printf`:

| `/usr/bin/printf` | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| uutils 0.10.0 (the image default, as in CI) | 44 pass, 1 fail: the `printf '%s' '--help'` mismatch | 46 pass |
| uutils 0.5.0 | 44 pass, 1 fail: the same mismatch | 46 pass |
| uutils 0.2.2 | 44 pass, 1 fail: the same mismatch | 46 pass |
| uutils 0.12.0 | 45 pass | 46 pass |
| GNU 9.7 | 45 pass | 46 pass |

- Full `zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe` in the sandbox with uutils 0.10.0: 12314 of 12358 pass. The 12 failures are the known sandbox environment failures: D29, D39, D49, and the storage read-only test in both session manager binaries, both `change_tracker` undo tests, `web_fetch_artifacts`, and the `capture_store` deadline. The printf tests pass.
- The built fx in the sandbox, with `fx ask` in `auto` mode against a fake gateway and a `profile: "clean"` shell call: `printf '%s' '--help'` and `printf '%s' '--'` now get one review and run in the shell (`route=approved_shell`), and return `--help` and `--`. `printf '%s' '-h'` still runs direct (`route=direct_read_only`) with no review and returns `-h`.
- macOS: the rule has no platform branch. A script that makes the same comparisons as the native printf tests, `/bin/sh -lc` against `/usr/bin/printf`, matches in stdout, stderr, and exit status for all 131 forms on macOS 27.2. I did not run the unit tests on macOS.

title: Write fx's interface text in lowercase
body:
fx's interface text is now lowercase, except acronyms such as `MCP`, `API`, and `HTTP`, mixed-case names such as `OpenAI`, file names, and environment variables.

- Tool rows, group headers, turn summaries, and activity read `read runtime.zig`, `ran zig build test`, `• thinking`, and `denied by auto agent`.
- Menus show tabs, headings, settings labels, confirmations, and sign-in steps in lowercase, as `settings   < all >` and `status line context`.
- Notices, approvals, the welcome banner (`run /help for commands`), recovery status, and CLI output and help follow the same rule.

`menu_frame.uiCase` lowers tab names and settings labels when a menu draws them, keeping words with no lowercase letter, so the shared provider and settings catalogs keep their own text.

Rows saved before this change still read `Exited 1 make` or `Timed out`. The matchers that read saved phrases now ignore case, so those rows keep grouping and failing as before. The saved `Untitled session` fallback title is unchanged, since saved sessions record it and `session_adapter` matches it; the session list shows it as `untitled session`.

Text the model reads, protocol values, JSON codes, HTTP headers, the pasted-text and image placeholders, and the browser sign-in page are unchanged.

## Compatibility

ACP `tool_call.title` and libfx titles are lowercase, as `read runtime.zig` and `ran MCP notion.search`. A client that matches title text sees the new wording; one that uses `kind` and `toolCallId` does not change. CLI text output, such as `fx status`, `fx sessions`, `fx mcp`, and `--help`, is lowercase too; JSON output keeps its fields and codes.

## Tests

- `zig build test` passes.
- Checked by hand in tmux with the built binary: a turn with read, grep, edit, and two shell commands; `/settings`, `/resume`, `/mcp`, `/skills`, `/help`, and `/status`; and `fx sessions` and `fx --help`.
- The e2e and SDK terminal expectations are updated for the files already run locally; CI runs the rest.

## Docs

The fx.sh manual pages that show tool rows, menus, or CLI output need their examples in lowercase, such as `● read runtime.zig` in place of `● Read runtime.zig`.

Stacked on #2091.

title: Reject unknown Codex subagent models before launch
body:
Fixes #2039.

## Summary

fx previously started Codex subagents with unrecognized model IDs. The provider
could then reject the completion request with HTTP 400.

Reuse the existing subagent model check for Codex. When the Codex catalog is available and no model matches, return `unknown_model` before starting the subagent. Keep the existing behavior when the catalog is unavailable.

## Verification

- `zig build` passed.
- Two focused ACP tests passed against `./zig-out/bin/fx` using a local fake Codex server. An unknown model ID returns `unknown_model` without sending a completion request, and a catalog-listed ID reaches the server. The regression test failed before the fix.
- `tests/tla/subagent/check.sh` and `tests/tla/session/check.sh` passed on the original checkout.
- An earlier `zig build test --summary failures` run exited 1 because `core.indexer.scan.test.refresh trusts an old unchanged tree and rejects every kind of change` failed without output. The failure has not been checked against the base revision.

## Docs

In the [Choose a model](https://fx.sh/docs/capabilities/subagents#choose-a-model) section, add after the paragraph about looking up model IDs:

> When the Codex model catalog is available, fx checks the requested model before starting the subagent. If no model matches, use `fx models --json` to find a listed model ID, or omit the model to inherit the parent agent's model.

title: Let a second client follow a running fx acp session
body:
Stacked on #2116. Until now, only the connection that opened a session could see it. A second client of the same `fx acp` process, connected to the leader socket from #2116, can now follow a running session.

## What changes

- The leader socket serves full ACP, as stdio does. Each socket connection shares the process's store and session table, so every connection sees the same sessions. `initialize` still adds `_meta["sh.fx/leader"]`.
- `session/load` on a session that another connection has open joins it. fx replays the saved turns, then what the running turn has sent so far, then answers. After the answer, the client gets each update once, in order, filtered by its own capabilities. `session/resume` answers and sends only live updates. There is no new method.
- A running turn keeps a copy of its updates, up to 16 MiB. The turn's save releases the copy inside the same write lock, so a joiner never sees a turn twice. If the copy dropped part of the turn, the replay ends with a notice before the answer.
- A following client only watches. Its `session/prompt`, `session/cancel`, `session/set_mode` and `session/set_config_option` get `-32600`: "This session is open on another connection; only that connection can change it." fx keeps the session's own `systemPrompt` and hooks, and traces the ones it ignores. `session/close` from a follower, or its disconnect, stops only its following. The owner's turn goes on.

## Tests

- `tests/e2e/acp.test.ts`: 4 new tests (load, refusal, close and disconnect, resume) and one leader socket test updated for the full-ACP socket. Each follow test compares the owner's whole message stream with a run of the same steps without a follower. All 5 pass here and fail on #2116's head. They pass on macOS arm64 too.
- `tests/tla/acp/AcpJoin.tla` models the join: saved turns, the running copy and its release, the tail after the save, load, resume, close and follower changes. The base config passes in 65,820 states, the config without joining fails `JoinWorks` as required, and `check-spec.ts` catches all 7 planted bugs, each by its named property.
- `tests/tla/drivers/acp/join/driver.ts` runs 6 plans against the real `fx acp`. The model with joining accepts all 6 here and rejects all 6 on #2116's head. The model without joining gives the opposite verdicts.
- Unit tests in `sessions.zig`, `server.zig` and `leader.zig` cover the audience, the copy, the join order, the refusal and the socket runner.

## Known limits

- fx sends no `current_mode_update` or `config_option_update`, so a follower doesn't learn when the owner changes the mode or a config option. This is older than this change.
- `session_adapter.Store`'s `problem` and `notice` fields have no lock. Two connections that convert v1 sessions at the same time can report each other's problem.
- The owner's `session/close`, or the end of its input, still closes the session for every connection.

title: Handle zero-width command approval previews
body:
Found this while fuzzing and testing the TUI with [bombadil](https://github.com/antithesishq/bombadil).

## Summary

- Treat `CommandDoesNotFit` during inline command-approval measurement as a reason to use the existing review screen.
- Add a regression test for a one-column terminal.

This is a very defensive fix for an edge case.

## Reproduction

1. Open a shell-command approval.
2. Resize the terminal to one column.

Before this change, fx exits 1 with `fx: command does not fit`. With this change, the approval remains pending, and denial completes after restoring the terminal size.

title: Fuzz MCP error data with spaces, and name the error prefix once
body:
## Summary

Two small follow-ups to the error-data change. Neither changes what fx does.

1. The `mcp_error_data` fuzz target only wrote compact JSON, so two bugs in how the host compacts an error's data passed the replay of its saved inputs. The generator now writes whitespace too.
2. In `src/core/mcp/tool_result.zig` the words `MCP protocol error ` were written in one place and read in two, each with its own copy. They are now one constant.

## 1. The fuzz generator writes whitespace

`fuzzErrorData` in `src/core/mcp_host/runtime.zig` built its JSON data with no space anywhere, while its law already compares the kept text with the data's own JSON written with no space outside strings. A wrong total in the cut marker, or keeping the raw text, looked the same as the right code on that data, because the raw text and the compact text were the same bytes.

- The generator now puts spaces, tabs, line breaks, carriage returns, or all four, between the tokens of the data and around `:` and `,`. The strings keep their own spaces.
- The object and the array can hold a second value, so there is a `,` to put space around. The value is `0`, which `std.json` writes as it is.
- Which whitespace goes where comes from bytes the script reads after the ones it read before, so a saved input without them is the compact JSON it was.
- Eight saved inputs, in `tests/fuzz/corpus/mcp_error_data/spaced-*`: a text just under, exactly at and just over the cap (the cap is judged on the compact text, so the raw text is longer than the cap while the kept text fits), a long cut, strings whose escapes double their length, a small object with every kind of gap, and a string alone.
- `iterations` goes from 25,000 to 8,000. One round took 91 s on `main` and 91 s with the new generator, three times the 30 s that `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks for. With 8,000 a round takes 29 s.

### Fail-first

Each plant is one edit in the compaction (`compactText` and `boundErrorData`). The replay is `zig build fuzz -Dfuzz-target=mcp_error_data` over the saved inputs, with no fuzzing. "Main" is the generator and saved inputs of `main`.

| Plant | Replay on main | Replay with this change |
|---|---|---|
| none (control) | pass | pass |
| P1: the kept text is pretty-printed | fails | fails |
| P2: the buffer for the kept text is half the cap | fails | fails |
| P3: the marker names the length of the raw text | passes | fails |
| P4: the raw text is kept, not the compact text | passes | fails |
| P5: the cut is made from the raw text | passes | fails |
| P6: "fits" is judged on the raw length | passes | fails |

P3 and P4 are the two that the earlier review planted and the old replay did not catch. Alone, each saved input fails these plants:

| Saved input | P1 | P2 | P3 | P4 | P5 | P6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `spaced-array-under-the-cap-with-spaces-over` | x | x |  | x |  | x |
| `spaced-object-escapes-over-the-cap` | x | x | x |  | x |  |
| `spaced-object-escapes-under-the-cap-with-spaces-over` | x | x |  | x |  | x |
| `spaced-object-exactly-the-cap` | x | x |  | x |  | x |
| `spaced-object-one-over-the-cap` | x | x | x |  | x |  |
| `spaced-object-small-every-gap` | x |  |  | x |  |  |
| `spaced-object-well-over-the-cap-cut` | x | x | x |  | x |  |
| `spaced-string-alone-small` |  |  |  | x |  |  |

## 2. The error words have one owner

`protocol_error_words` in `tool_result.zig` is written by `write_protocol_diagnostic`, and read by `invalid_params_prefix` and `protocolErrorWithoutData`. No other non-test code in `src/` writes or reads those words: a search of `src/` finds them in this file, and in test text of other files. The constant stays private.

- The tests of the readers in this file build their text from the constant. They held the old words as literals.
- A new test builds the text with the writer for four codes, with and without data, and reads it with both readers: the message without the data for every code, and a cause for -32602 only.
- The other tests whose result depends on the words are in other files (`mcp_host/model.zig`, `agent/runtime/tool_presentation.zig`, `app/trace_report.zig`). They pin what the model and the status line show, so I left them as they are. Tests in `session/result_store.zig` and `mcp_host/mcp_call_client.zig` also use the words, but only as sample text that passes through unchanged.

### Plants

In a scratch copy, with the groups `core.mcp.` (set A) and `core.mcp_host.`, `core.agent.runtime.tool_presentation.`, `core.session.result_store.` and `core.app.trace_report.` (set B), run as two sets so that one test that aborts the binary hides no other:

| Change | Set A | Set B |
|---|---|---|
| none (control) | 165 of 165 pass | 315 of 315 pass |
| Q1: the words in the constant change, nothing else | 165 of 165 pass | 10 fail: tests of other files that hold the old words as literals |
| Q2: Q1, and `protocolErrorWithoutData` reads the old literal | 7 fail, the new test among them | 9 fail |
| Q3: Q1, and `invalid_params_prefix` is the old literal | the binary aborts at the 5th failing reader test, before the new test | 7 fail |
| Q4: Q1, and the writer writes the old literal | 1 fails: the new test | 5 fail |

So with the words changed in the constant only, every test in `core.mcp.` still passes: the readers follow the writer. The ten tests in set B that fail are the ones that hold the old words as literals. Q3 aborts the test binary on a `null` in a reader test, so there the new test is not reached; with the tests of the readers still holding literals (an earlier run of the same plant), the new test failed too.

## Where the checks ran

Linux x86_64, as root, with the model keys unset and `FX_SOUND=0`, on the head of this branch.

- `zig build` exits 0. The groups `core.mcp.`, `core.mcp_host.`, `core.agent.runtime.tool_presentation.`, `core.session.result_store.` and `core.app.trace_report.`: 490 of 490 pass, with the new test and the fuzz test among them.
- Replays: `mcp_error_data` (41 saved inputs) and `mcp_invalid_params_cause` (5) exit 0.
- Round time (ReleaseSafe, after a first run that builds): `main`'s generator at 25,000 runs, 91.4, 90.7 and 92.9 s; this generator at 25,000 runs, 91.2, 92.5 and 92.0 s; this generator at 8,000 runs, 29.3, 29.4 and 29.4 s.
- `python3 -m scripts.fuzz_nightly run --target mcp_error_data --budget-seconds 150`: 6 rounds, all ok.
- `tests/e2e/mcp-stdio.test.ts`, whole, against a ReleaseSafe build made in the same run: 159 pass, 0 fail, in 312 s. It holds the no-leak test and the low-cap test.
- `zig fmt --check src/` and `scripts/check-public-surface.sh` exit 0.

Not run: a TLA+ model or driver. No behavior changes, and no model describes these tests. CI's TLA+ MCP jobs run on these paths anyway.

## Not changed here

`write_protocol_diagnostic` writes the label `; data=` as a literal, while `withoutData` reads it as `data_label`. That is the same shape of problem for another string, so it is not part of this change.

## Docs

None: no user-facing behavior changes.
